# Changelog

All notable changes to Pane are documented here. Written for users, not developers.

Format: [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). Each entry includes the version, date, and what changed.

---

## [Unreleased]

## [1.0.87] - 2026-11-23

### Added
- `.github/FUNDING.yml`, pointing GitHub's Sponsor button at ThreeLaneStudios (#3106).
- `recipes/REVIEW-CHECKLIST.md` gains a 14th checklist item flagging unpinned remote fetches/installs. The "Submit a recipe" issue form (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/recipe-submission.yml`) gains a required "What does this touch, in your own words?" field, pasted verbatim into a recipe's `## What it touches` section rather than composed from the existing `touches-*` fields (#3262).

### Removed
- `.github/workflows/issue-spec-check.yml` and `.github/workflows/issue-triage.yml`, the two issue-opened workflows that auto-labeled and commented on new issues over a missing spec section or a missing `launch-blocking`/`post-launch` label. `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s description of that automation is updated to match. The `launch-blocking`, `post-launch`, `needs-triage`, and `needs-spec-section` labels themselves are unchanged (#443).
- Every place that applied or read the `needs-spec-section` label: `docs-issue-check.yml` no longer applies it, the dormant `issue-triage-ai.yml`/`issue-triage-ai.mjs` pipeline no longer classifies or replies with it, `scripts/spec-audit.sh` drops its label-based query, and the "Submit a recipe" issue form's unused `Spec Section: N/A` field is removed. The label itself is unchanged; Matt deletes it separately (#445).

### Documentation
- `README.md`'s opening bold tagline is replaced with "The open-source app for running AI agents you own." and a new line below it reads "You decide who sees your data, not a big tech company." (#447).
- `README.md`'s Install section points the Linux and Windows notes at #249 and #250 instead of their pre-migration numbers; the build-from-source paragraph now states signed builds come from the release workflow (`.github/workflows/release-publish.yml`) rather than a local script; the "How it's built" section now states where PR history lives since the repo's migration; the "Where it is" section drops the specific user-count sentence; and the opening paragraph's closing sentence now says you choose which AI provider sees your data (#449).
- `docs/adr/0034-paneapp-ai-email-verification-posture.md`'s typo'd-email example used a typo'd address (`mtt@paneapp.ai`) that no longer corresponded to the correct address it was being contrasted with (`admin@paneapp.ai`); it now reads `admn@paneapp.ai` instead of `admin@paneapp.ai`, a dropped-character typo of the correct address (#441).
- `docs/release-runbook.md` states that publishing a release is Matt's manual click alone; agents never publish a draft (#3106).
- `recipes/README.md` no longer hedges `agents/` and `jobs/` as provisional folder names; they are final (#3262).
- `README.md`'s Build from source requirements sentence no longer states a fixed Rust floor ("1.77 or later"); it now points at `rust-toolchain.toml`'s pinned `1.99.1` and notes `rustup` installs it automatically. The sentence's Node.js clause no longer says "20 or later"; it now states the `^20.19`, `^22.12`, `>=24` ranges that `vite` and `@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte` require via their `engines` fields, enforced by this repo's `engine-strict=true`. The pnpm and Tauri CLI parts of the same sentence are unchanged (#451).

### Fixed
- `recipes/RECIPE-TEMPLATE.md`'s `## What it touches` comment cited the wrong checklist item for the touches-matching rule; it now cites the correct item and names both the PR and issue-form submission routes (#3262).
- `pnpm build` failed on a fresh checkout because the prebuild hook's spec-status check pointed at a spec file that no longer exists. The check is removed from `scripts/pre-build.sh`, the same stale reference is removed from `scripts/spec-audit.sh`, and the now-unreferenced `scripts/check-spec-status.sh` is deleted (#3243).
- `scripts/check-spec-first.sh`'s core-behavioral file list matched bare filenames as path prefixes instead of whole filenames, so a deleted or renamed file sharing a core filename's prefix (for example `database.rs.before_composite_pk`) was wrongly classified as a core behavioral change. The bare-filename entries are now end-anchored; the directory-prefix entries are unchanged. The spec-first source-change detector also did not recognize `src-gateway/src/` as a source path, so gateway-only PRs skipped the spec-first discipline check entirely; `src-gateway/src/` is now included in that detector (#3234, #3198). The `spec-skip:` and `spec-covered-by:` marker checks in the same script matched the marker text anywhere in the PR body instead of only at the start of a line, and a stale comment referencing a cross-reference pattern in the spec-first workflow (removed by an earlier refactor) is corrected.
- The CHANGELOG-skip and skip-approval marker checks in `.github/workflows/spec-first.yml`, the gate-4d walkthrough markers in `.github/workflows/visual-smoke-check.yml`, and the §4 test-the-test section checks in `.github/workflows/section-4-enforcement.yml` all matched their marker text anywhere in the PR body instead of only at the start of a line, so a PR description that merely explains or quotes a marker in a sentence could satisfy the check that marker is meant to gate. Every one of these checks is now anchored to the start of a line (optionally after leading whitespace), so only an actual declared marker counts; a genuine marker at the start of a line still matches exactly as before. A stale workflow comment in `spec-first.yml` citing a test file that was never part of this repository's history is also corrected to point at where the real wiring tests live (#3235).
- `svelte-check` flagged type errors in `sheetSnapshotEnvelope.ts`, `SearchableModelSelect.svelte`, `Editor.svelte`, and `ScheduledPanel.svelte`. Causes: a locally narrowed `string` value in `applyBorderEntry` was reassigned into a binding still typed from its original `unknown` destructure; two inline snippet parameters in `SearchableModelSelect.svelte` had no type annotations; `Editor.svelte`'s sheet-title save path handed a promise resolving to a note value where a void-resolving promise was expected; and several casts in `ScheduledPanel.svelte` referenced a shape that shared no field with the value being cast, now matching the fuller shape the file's other casts already use. Each is a type-only fix with no behavior change (#3243).

### Security
- Local-agent creation now enforces the centralized filesystem policy for workspace directories and skeleton files, rejecting symlink escapes and avoiding predictable temporary-file writes. External attachment imports via the native file-picker path (`copy_attachment_from_path`) now require a backend-held native file-selection scope grant before reading the source. Corrected during 1.0.87's promotion: the original wording also claimed a "drop grant" satisfies this gate; drag-and-drop and paste attachment imports go through the separate base64/IPC upload path (`handleFileUpload`/`onUpload` in `src/lib/extensions/Attachment.ts`) and never reach `copy_attachment_from_path` or its scope check at all, so no drop-based grant exists or is needed on that path.
- `@sveltejs/kit` 2.70.4 has an open denial-of-service advisory in its experimental remote-functions form-data parser (GHSA-3r8g-jcqq-3p5j, CVE-2026-128120; pnpm advisory 1247438; high). This is a dated deferral, not a fix: the advisory's first-patched version is 3.1.1, and 2.70.4 is the last 2.x release npm ever published, so there is no 2.x patch to land, and the ruling is no major dependency bump before launch. The real remedy is the SvelteKit 3 migration, moved to the post-launch roadmap (umbrella #3217), which will address this advisory together with the two other open `@sveltejs/kit` alerts in one pass. Exempted for now via a dated `docs/security/dependency-audit-exceptions.yml` entry (review_by 2027-01-15) because this app has no `svelte.config.js` `experimental.remoteFunctions` flag and no `*.remote.js`/`*.remote.ts` files, so the vulnerable parsing path is never reached.
- `vitest` 1.6.1 to 3.2.7 (#3217 bucket 2/3), the exact 3.x patch whose peer range admits this repo's `vite` 7.3.7, not an earlier 3.x that would have forced a second, older `vite` copy back into the tree. The bump alone closes 10 of the 12 Dependabot rows in this cluster: the 2 direct `vitest` advisories and 8 `vite@5.4.21` advisories that existed only because `vitest` 1.x carried its own private, older `vite` dependency, now gone. The remaining 2 (both critical `tinypool` findings, GHSA-85c8-ppgw-ccpr and GHSA-5gmw-xhrv-c9v3) needed a `pnpm.overrides["tinypool"] = ">=2.1.2"` entry added alongside this bump, because `vitest` 3.x still pins `tinypool@^1.1.1` on its own and never crosses the patched floor without it. One test file needed an edit for the vitest 1.x to 3.x mock-typing migration: `src/lib/utils/wikiLinkNavigation.test.ts`'s three `vi.fn<[Args], Ret>()` call sites moved to the single function-type generic form `vi.fn<(args) => Ret>()`. `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` (3507 passed, 1 skipped), and `pnpm check` all pass unchanged from before this bump. Note: `pnpm audit` against the post-bump tree surfaces two new moderate advisories in `@vitest/mocker` (GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9/CVE-2026-84373, GHSA-qxg6-89mg-rqv8/CVE-2026-112949) that only patch at `vitest` 4.x, outside this PR's exact-3.2.7 ruling; both are below the gate's `--audit-level=high` floor so they do not block CI. Per Matt's ruling (no `vitest` 4 before launch), both are accepted and covered by dated exception entries in `docs/security/dependency-audit-exceptions.yml` (review_by 2027-01-15), not left unlisted.
- `zip` 4.6.1 to 9.6.0 in the `pane` crate only (`src-tauri/Cargo.toml`), fixing the one API break Reed's scope found: `zip::write::FileOptions<()>` became `zip::write::SimpleFileOptions`, a change contained entirely inside `attachments.rs`'s own test-fixture helper (`build_test_docx_bytes`). Production code (`ZipArchive::new` / `.by_name("word/document.xml")`) is unchanged across the whole 4.6.1 to 9.6.0 span. This bump is hygiene for `pane`'s own code, not a closure of the matching advisories: `tauri-plugin-updater@2.11.0` keeps its own `zip = "^4"` pin, gated to `cfg(target_os = "windows")`, which this PR cannot move, so `src-tauri/Cargo.lock` now carries two `zip` entries side by side (9.6.0 for `pane`, 4.6.1 for the plugin's Windows-only branch) by design. No direct dependency besides `zip` itself changed (`src-tauri/Cargo.toml`'s diff is one line); `zip` 9.6.0's own new requirements on `windows-sys 0.61.2` and `getrandom 0.4.3` caused Cargo's resolver to unify compatible pointers. 14 transitive crates moved, all benign, no downgrades: colored, dirs-sys, errno, muda, os_pipe, quinn-udp, rustix, rustls-platform-verifier, socket2, stacker, tempfile, tray-icon, uds_windows, winapi-util. `GHSA-q7v9-x93c-xqv3`/`RUSTSEC-2026-0429` stays open and its dated exception entry is re-justified, not removed, because Pane ships no Windows build and the lingering entry is reachable only there.
- Ten dated entries added or re-justified in `docs/security/dependency-audit-exceptions.yml` (review_by 2027-01-15, #3217 bucket 2/3): three `@sveltejs/kit` advisories (GHSA-27mw-82g8-phjj, GHSA-pfhg-q3qv-9q6r, and the medium GHSA-6cf5-gc4q-fm3x that appeared the same day this scope was written) deferred for the same major-version-jump reason as the existing entry above; `glib` (GHSA-wrw7-89jp-8q8g/RUSTSEC-2024-0429), bookkeeping-only since `cargo-audit` already classifies it as a non-blocking `unsound` warning rather than a vulnerability; `deepmerge` (GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4), which has no patched version published upstream; the `zip`/`RUSTSEC-2026-0429` re-justification above; two more `zip` advisories with no RUSTSEC counterpart at all (GHSA-m665-v7pm-7grj, GHSA-8hxf-qr8p-62x4), added as bookkeeping-only entries so every open Dependabot alert in this cluster has somewhere to point, even though `cargo audit --ignore` can never match a bare GHSA id; and the two new `@vitest/mocker` moderates named above (GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9, GHSA-qxg6-89mg-rqv8), accepted per Matt's ruling against a vitest-4 bump before launch. The four entries flagged as possibly stale in an earlier pass (`RUSTSEC-2026-0459` and three more `zip` RUSTSEC ids) were confirmed, via a read-only `cargo audit --ignore` simulation, to still be live findings against the current lockfile and are left untouched; removing them would have reopened four real findings, not cleaned up dead ones. `docs/security/dependency-audit-exceptions.yml` is also added to `reed-gate.yml`'s `CORE_PATHS` (anchored to the exact file), so future edits to the exception manifest alone require the same review this PR itself is already subject to.

### Changed
- `scripts/pre-build.sh`'s `prebuild` hook is checks-only now: architecture invariants, version parity, spec check, and `svelte-check`. The `BUILD_APPROVED_BY` and `ROOT_CAUSE_CONFIRMED` gates, the gateway rebuild plus `launchctl kickstart` restart (#3121), and the auto-commit are deleted, not relocated or made conditional. `cargo test` and `npm test` are also removed from this script; CI and `pnpm test` own them now. The issue-comment check moved to a one-line release-runbook step (#3243).
- `release-publish.yml`'s tag-shape guard now recognizes `vX.Y.Z-dev` instead of `vX.Y.Z-test.N` for tester/dev prereleases; 78 consecutive `-dev` tag pushes (every `-dev` tag since 2026-08-16, roughly three months, not two weeks) had been failing this guard since `-test.N` never matched `-dev`. `-test.N` is dropped outright: it had zero live consumers (last tagged 2026-08-02, pre-1.0) while `-dev` is already the convention every other part of the codebase (`scripts/check-release-source.sh`, `scripts/build.sh`'s own incident comment) assumes. `-dev` tags continue to publish as a GitHub prerelease (`--prerelease`), unchanged from `-test.N`'s behavior (#3239).

### Security
- `docs/security/dependency-audit-exceptions.yml`'s two `zip` bookkeeping entries now carry their real RUSTSEC ids (`RUSTSEC-2026-0545`, `RUSTSEC-2026-0548`) instead of a bare GHSA id, so `cargo audit --ignore` can reference them directly. Same `tauri-plugin-updater` Windows-only-pin reasoning and `review_by` as the sibling entries, unchanged.

### Infrastructure
- `release-publish.yml`'s public-release step no longer auto-publishes a successful run; it now always ends with the release as a draft, published only when a human clicks Publish release in GitHub. The asset-count failure message is reworded to match. `docs/release-runbook.md` is updated to describe the draft-only behavior. A new `notify-discord` job posts the run's outcome (success or failure, and which job failed) to Discord regardless of which upstream job succeeded or failed; the webhook secret is optional and the job skips cleanly without it, never failing the release (#3255).
- The macOS CI release job builds `Pane.app` as a universal (`arm64`+`x86_64`) binary and packages the DMG through `scripts/lib/dmg.sh`'s shared `hdiutil` helpers instead of calling `hdiutil` directly, matching `scripts/build.sh`. The app itself is now notarized and stapled before packaging, not only the DMG, and a committed `.DS_Store` asset gives the shipped DMG the same window layout `scripts/build.sh` already produces. The artifact is named `Pane_X.Y.Z.dmg` (#3247, #3049).
- `scripts/build.sh` no longer reads a local Tauri signing key or `.env` file; it always produces an unsigned, non-notarized dev build and prints an explicit notice saying so. Signed, notarized builds now come exclusively from `release-publish.yml`'s self-hosted runner, where the eight signing secrets live in GitHub only. This supersedes the local-signing-password guard #3237 added three days ago (closing #3226): that guard is no longer needed because the local-signing path it guarded no longer exists (#3239).
- Five job-level `env.PATH` lines on the self-hosted macOS ARM64 runner (`nightly-tests.yml`, two in `release-publish.yml`, `updater-release-assets.yml`, `e2e.yml`) hardcoded a `.cargo/bin` path under a nonexistent developer home directory, a user that does not exist on the runner. This is what made `cargo` resolve to exit 127 on the first real run of the signed release path (tag `v1.0.86-dev`, run 43945879372), before signing or notarization could execute. Fixed identically at all five: the `env.PATH` now keeps only the username-free entries (`/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/bin`, `/bin`, `/usr/sbin`, `/sbin`), and a new first step after checkout writes the real `$HOME/.cargo/bin` to `$GITHUB_PATH` from a `run:` step, where `$HOME` actually expands; GitHub Actions prepends `$GITHUB_PATH` entries to every later step's `PATH` in that job, so step order and precedence match the old hardcoded line exactly (#3244).

### Security
- `picomatch` 4.0.7 has a second, distinct ReDoS advisory (GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf / CVE-2026-112366, ReDoS via single-branch repeated extglob patterns; pnpm advisory 1247710; high) with no patched version available anywhere upstream. Pulled only transitively, via `svelte-check`/`vite`/`vitest` -> `fdir`/`tinyglobby` -> `picomatch`, for build/dev/test tooling only. Exempted via a dated `docs/security/dependency-audit-exceptions.yml` entry (review_by 2027-01-15), added alongside the existing, differently-scoped `picomatch` entry (1115554) rather than merged into it.

### Security
- internal: Workflows that write to GitHub (PR comments) or otherwise mutate repository state now declare an explicit `permissions:` block instead of relying on the repository-wide default; every other workflow declares `contents: read`. `visual-smoke-check.yml`'s Gate 4d comment step now fails loudly instead of silently if it cannot post or delete a comment (#3207).

### Documentation
- internal: CONTRIBUTING.md now points to `docs/dev-hygiene-playbook.md` for the full detail behind its process summary (#3106).

### Added
- `recipes/` — a home for community-submitted recipes, with an `agents/` and a `jobs/` subfolder (names provisional), a `RECIPE-TEMPLATE.md`, a `README.md` explaining how to use and submit a recipe, and a public `REVIEW-CHECKLIST.md`. A "Submit a recipe" issue form (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/recipe-submission.yml`) carries the same fields for non-coders (#3260).

### Infrastructure
- `reed-gate.yml`'s `CORE_PATHS` now includes `recipes/`, so a recipe pull request needs the `reed-reviewed` label before it can merge, same as every other core path. `check-issue-reference` now exempts a pull request whose diff touches only `recipes/` from the issue-reference requirement; any diff touching anything else, from anyone, still needs one. `startup-smoke.yml`'s existing docs-only exclusion now also covers `recipes/`, taking the same fast step-skip path docs-only changes already take (#3260).

## [1.0.86] - 2026-11-16

### Security
- Of the 70 open dependency-vulnerability alerts tracked in #3217, 45 had a patch or minor-version fix available with no breaking-change risk. 44 are fixed here: `@sveltejs/kit` (to 2.70.4), `svelte` (to 5.57.3), `vite` (to 7.3.8), `@sveltejs/adapter-static` (to 3.0.11), and, via `pnpm.overrides`, `cookie`, `esbuild`, `form-data`, `picomatch`, `postcss`, `rollup`, `source-map-js`, and `ws` to their patched floors; separately, `tools/enex-import`'s own `yaml` dependency (that tool keeps an independent `package-lock.json`, not scanned by pnpm) is bumped to 2.8.3. One alert in this batch, a Rust `glib` advisory (GHSA-wrw7-89jp-8q8g), turned out to be unreachable without upgrading Tauri's own pinned GTK stack on Linux, a dependency migration rather than a lockfile fix, so it is deferred for a maintainer ruling instead of being forced into this change.
- `tools/enex-import`'s lockfile had no CI dependency scanning of any kind. It's now a fourth job in the dependency-audit gate, checked with the same manifest-aware `npm audit` pattern the existing cargo-audit and pnpm-audit jobs already use (#3217).

### Removed
- `extensions/chrome-clipper/`, an unmaintained, unshipped browser extension (16 files, one commit since February) that was never a build target, never referenced by any app code, and never covered by the dependency-audit gate. A verification pass found zero references to it anywhere outside its own directory tree-wide; the only hits were its own self-references, the app's pre-rename "Trove" branding elsewhere in the repo, and an unrelated `src/lib/extensions/` editor-namespace collision. Deleting it closes five of #3217's bucket-1 alerts outright (`esbuild`, `@mozilla/readability`, `sharp` x3) since those packages existed only in its own, now-removed `package-lock.json`; a sixth alert sharing the same `esbuild` advisory ID has a second, surviving instance in the root lockfile, fixed separately above in this same change (#3217).

### Changed
- CI's `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` step silently rolled every macOS build and test job from Rust 1.99.1 to the 1.100.0 release (shipped 2026-11-12), which made the app abort on startup inside `tao`'s `did_finish_launching` AppKit delegate callback — `Startup Smoke` and `Rust Tests (macOS)` went red on an unchanged tree. A root `rust-toolchain.toml` now pins the whole repo, including this repo's `release-publish.yml` `src-gateway` release builds, to 1.99.1 until the 1.100.0 startup regression is root-caused; `scripts/smoke-launch.sh` also now prints the `panicked at` line plus three lines of context (previously truncated out of the 50-line stderr tail on every one of the six failures checked) so the next such regression is diagnosable from CI logs alone (#3222).

### Security
- Two known-vulnerable Rust networking crates had a published fix available: `quinn-proto` (0.11.18 to 0.11.19, two advisories) and `quinn-udp` (to the 0.5.16 line, not the newer 0.6 line, which would have pulled in an unrelated `quinn-proto` major bump). `src-tauri/Cargo.lock` needed both; the two trees resolve these crates independently, and `src-gateway/Cargo.lock` needed only the `quinn-udp` fix, having been on an even older, also-vulnerable patch (0.5.14) than `src-tauri`'s, though its `quinn-proto` was already current. `nanoid`, pulled in transitively through `postcss`, is bumped 3.3.11 to 3.3.20 via a `pnpm.overrides` entry, fixing three advisories that were previously carried as dated exceptions; since a patch exists for each, those three exception entries are removed rather than kept. Gateway bumped to 1.0.5 (#3229).
- The gateway's outgoing-message log line in `oc_client.rs`'s `send_request()` printed the full serialized RPC request — including the OC bearer token and device signature on every `connect`/reconnect handshake — in cleartext. A sibling log line one function away had already been redacted for this exact reason; this upstream one hadn't been. Now logs only the RPC method name. A new source-scan test (`no_credential_logging.rs`) guards against this class of leak reappearing anywhere else under `src-gateway/src/`. Gateway bumped to 1.0.4 (#3218).
- Two build scripts (`pre-build.sh`, `build.sh`), across four `echo` sites, echoed the live values of the Apple code-signing identity, Apple ID, and Apple Team ID to build logs. They now only confirm the credentials loaded, never the values (#3218).

### Added
- `LICENSE` (Apache-2.0) and `NOTICE` files at the repo root; Pane is Apache-2.0 licensed, matching `Cargo.toml`/`README.md`, which had drifted to say MIT (#3218).

### Changed
- PR and issue templates reworded for external contributors: the PR template's internal "Reed Gate" section is now generic "Maintainer Gate" language, and the long auto-close rationale under Related Issues is trimmed to one paragraph. Em dashes removed from the two issue-template Spec Section fields (#3218).
- The e2e IPC account-sync recorder's hand-kept command list (`tests/e2e/tauri-mock.ts`) had drifted from the set `require_account_enabled()` actually guards in `sync/commands.rs` — it over-recorded two ungated commands (`get_auth_session`, `is_encryption_ready`). Trimmed to the exact 20-command guarded set, now enforced by a source-derived Rust test so the two lists can't silently diverge again (#3218).
- Three unreferenced, dead `.py` scripts from a one-off March rollback session removed from `src-tauri/src/ai/` (#3218).
- The eleven `*_tests.rs` files directly under `src-tauri/src/ai/` moved into `src-tauri/src/ai/tests/` (with `ai/tests.rs` converted to `ai/tests/mod.rs` to make room) — pure relocation, no behavior change (#3218).
- Settings still showed the whole Account & Sync tab — Auto-sync toggle, Sync Now, status dot, Device Name, Sync History — even with the account feature's default-off setting left off; only the inner sign-in section was hidden (#3195). The tab button and its panel are now both hidden the same way, with no other change to Settings.
- Pane's dependencies had no automated vulnerability scanning at all (#3106). Every pull request and a weekly scheduled run now check both the Rust and the JavaScript dependency trees against the public security-advisory databases; any new, unreviewed finding blocks the check. Fixed now: five patched Rust networking/TLS libraries, and the HTML sanitizer plus the rich-text editor's dependency chain on the JavaScript side (one of those sanitizer findings was rated critical). The remaining known findings — all in either build/test-only tooling that never ships, or deferred to a follow-up fix with real migration risk — are tracked in a reviewed, dated exception list rather than silently ignored; a stale entry on that list fails the check until a human re-reviews it.
- Correction to the above: the `devalue` fix exposed two further problems in the same area, now both fixed together. First, its security override was initially written as pnpm-only syntax (`pnpm.overrides`), which npm never read; the repo was still carrying a second, stray `package-lock.json` for the same package manager, so that lockfile kept installing the vulnerable version even after `pnpm-lock.yaml` was fixed. Second, one CI workflow (the visual-smoke-check job) installed from that npm lockfile instead of pnpm, so a fix landed only in `pnpm-lock.yaml` could stay invisible to it. `package-lock.json` is deleted, the visual-smoke-check job now installs with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` like every other workflow in this repo, and `devalue` resolves to the patched version via the existing `pnpm.overrides` entry alone, the only override Pane's single remaining lockfile needs (#3106).
- The gateway's dependency tree carried two different major versions of `rustls` (0.22 and 0.23) and of `rustls-webpki` (0.102 and 0.103) side by side, because its WebSocket library was pinned to a version that depended on the older line. Nineteen previously-tracked, dated exceptions for that older line — spanning `h2`, `openssl`, `quinn-proto`, `webpki-roots`, `rustls`, and `rustls-webpki` — are now fixed outright rather than exempted: patch-level updates to the first four, and the WebSocket library moved to the newest version that still depends on the current `rustls`/`rustls-webpki` line (one version short of a breaking API change in that library, saved for its own future change). The gateway's own dependency tree now resolves to exactly one version of each (#3106).

### Added
- internal: Seventeen scripts that implement a CI gate or handle a build/signing secret (`pre-build.sh`, `build.sh`, `smoke-launch.sh`, `check-dependency-exceptions.sh`, `check-version-parity.sh`, `check-spec-first.sh`, `check-gateway-version-bump.sh`, `build-crsqlite-universal.sh`, `build-gateway-dmg.sh`, `check-gateway-version-floor.sh`, `check-no-native-confirm.sh`, `check-release-source.sh`, `ci-guards/run-guards.sh`, `sign-dylibs.sh`, `smoke-grep.sh`, `spec-audit.sh`, `verify-upgrade-fixture.sh`) now require the `reed-reviewed` label to change, same as the existing `CORE_PATHS` entries (#3226).

### Changed
- internal: Every existing bare-filename entry in `CORE_PATHS` is now anchored to match only its exact file, not any name that merely starts with it; directory entries are unchanged. The `database.rs` entry's match count drops from 4 to 1 as a result: the 3 extra matches were the dead `.before_*` backup files removed below in the same change, so no live file loses coverage (#3226).

### Removed
- internal: `src-tauri/src/database.rs.before_composite_pk`, `.before_tags_fix`, and `.before_v9.1.2` (unreferenced backup snapshots from past migrations) and `scripts/release.sh` (dead, superseded by `pre-build.sh` plus `build.sh`; never invoked by `package.json`, any workflow, or any other script) are deleted; no behavior change (#3226).

### Security
- internal: `scripts/build.sh` read the updater signing password from a hardcoded literal in the script instead of the environment. It now requires `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` to be exported before running, failing with a distinct message depending on whether the variable is unset or set but empty, so a build can no longer proceed unsigned or wrongly signed without being flagged (#3226).
- The updater's public key in `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` is rotated. The prior build script's hardcoded signing password was committed in plaintext, so it is permanently exposed in git history and the matching private key is retired rather than just the file that carried it. This invalidates auto-update signature verification for every build through 1.0.85; the automatic update check is currently disabled and the update endpoint is already down, so no installed build is affected in practice today. A manual reinstall is the path once auto-update is re-enabled (#3226, a one-time override of the "never change the pubkey" ruling recorded in #3158).

## [1.0.85] - 2026-11-10
### Security
- A tainted chat turn (one that had just read an untrusted web page or attachment) could still schedule, spawn, cancel, pause, or resume a background job for the rest of that turn, even though every other note/project-mutating action was already blocked after untrusted content was read. A scheduled job created this way would later run as its own fresh turn with every write tool available and no taint restriction (#3106). All five job actions are now blocked for the rest of a tainted turn, the same way editing or deleting an existing note already was.
- Pane's self-hosted end-to-end and packaging-regression CI jobs could in principle run a pull request's own code on real Studio hardware before a human reviewed it, once this repository has outside contributors (#3106). The end-to-end job now only runs when someone manually starts it; the packaging-regression job still runs automatically on every pull request, but only for branches from this repository.
- A label named with the right crafted text could have injected a shell command into an internal, Matt-only labeling check (#3106). The check now passes that text through safely instead of interpolating it directly into the script.
- The OpenClaw gateway sync token could be read or written in plaintext through a generic internal settings command instead of always going through the secure keychain storage already used for it elsewhere (#3106). It's now routed through the keychain consistently. An unused, dead settings-save command that had no live caller was also removed.
- The gateway accepted a TCP connection from any reachable address with no network-level check of its own, relying entirely on Tailscale/LAN placement to keep it private (#3106 H1). It now checks the connecting address against an allowlist — defaulting to loopback plus the Tailscale ranges, defined in a gateway config file so it's visible and operator-overridable — and refuses anything outside it before TLS even starts.
- The gateway's pairing code accepted unlimited wrong guesses against the active code with no throttling (#3106 H1). It now locks out after ~10 wrong attempts, for the remainder of that code's own 5-minute window; a fresh code (via the gateway's local CLI) is never blocked by a previous lockout. The code is also widened from 6 to 8 digits.
- The gateway logged the pairing code, the OC bearer token (embedded in the `connect` handshake message), and the authentication challenge nonce in full across seven call sites in five files (#3106 M2). None of the seven log the value anymore.
- A background notification poller started unconditionally on every launch and could make a live network call to Supabase — and rewrite the stored session file — for anyone with a leftover signed-in session, even though no sign-in UI is reachable today (#3195). It, 23 of the 30 account/sync commands behind it, and a push-notification command that reached the same session-refresh path through a second, independent door the poller's own gate didn't cover, now require a default-off `account_enabled` setting that nothing currently turns on; behavior is unchanged for every user (#3195, #3201).

### Changed
- Account sign-in (behind the still-off-by-default account flag) now talks to Supabase directly instead of the ecom wrapper backend that's being shut down, using the same token format the app's token-refresh already used. No functional change for anyone today — the flag is still off by default and nothing in the shipped app reaches this path (#3195).
- Pane now opens straight to Home on every launch — no sign-in screen first. The subscription-check and multi-machine take-over screens that used to sit behind it are gone too, along with the launch and on-focus checks that used to drive them. Account sign-in and sync are still in the app, present and tested but off by default, kept for planned team sharing and the mobile app; nothing in today's build reaches them (#3195).

## [1.0.84] - 2026-11-09
### Fixed
- Hovering the sidebar rail to expand it pushed the rest of the app sideways instead of overlaying it, at **every** window width. The visible symptoms were worst when collapsed: the expanded menu rendered behind the Jobs column at narrow widths, and showed only dots/chevrons with no project labels at medium widths. The hover-expanded sidebar is now the wide state, overlaid — identical classes, labels and DOM as the sidebar at >=1200px, painted over the content at all three width bands and never reflowing its siblings. This required a structural change, not a stacking-order tweak: a new always-in-flow `.sidebar-rail-spacer` element holds the rail's resting width, and `.sidebar` is now unconditionally `position: absolute`. Verified by six committed WebKit screenshots (narrow/medium/wide, at rest and on hover) rather than width or position assertions, which passed three times while the behaviour was wrong (#3190, C65).
- The sidebar rail's resting `40px` width was a literal duplicated between `Sidebar.svelte` and `+page.svelte` (#3188). Both now read a single `--sidebar-rail-width` custom property declared once on `.app`. No behavior change.

## [1.0.83] - 2026-11-07
### Fixed
- The sidebar rail could appear to vanish entirely at narrow window widths on Home — it hadn't; the chat panel's narrow-width rule had no left/width bound and painted over the rail in an identical background color (#3186, C65). The rail is now always visible at every width.
- Hovering the sidebar rail to peek its full width did nothing at narrow or medium window widths — a leftover rule from the long-removed Cmd+B manual-collapse shortcut was unconditionally blocking it (#3186, C65). Hover-expand now works at every width.
- A notification for an image reply dropped the image's alt text entirely instead of showing it, reading as just "Generated 1 image(s) · Agent Name" with nothing describing the image (#3186, C63). The bell preview now shows the alt text, same as the chat bubble already does.

## [1.0.82] - 2026-11-06
### Fixed
- A notification for a note containing an image embed showed a stray `!` left over in the preview text (#3182, C63) — a rule-ordering bug (the plain-link rule ran before the image rule and ate the image's brackets first, stranding the `!`). The image rule now runs first.
- The New job dialog's Agent and Project lists had no height cap at all once in-flow (#3178, C57) — a long enough list grew the whole dialog to match it, pushing the rest of the dialog's fields and its Save button down with it. Both fields now cap at roughly 5 rows and scroll internally instead.
- Narrowing the window closed the chat panel but never reopened it on widening back (#3182, C64) — only the sidebar had that restore behavior before this fix. On Home specifically, the chat panel could disappear entirely at narrow widths, leaving the sessions list looking stranded in an otherwise-empty column. Both are fixed: chat now restores on widen exactly like the sidebar already did, and Home's chat panel no longer depends on the state the narrow-width handler was clobbering.

## [1.0.81] - 2026-11-05
### Fixed
- The New job dialog's Project and Agent fields' dropdown list could open over the preset cards near the top of the dialog, or run off the bottom of the window with no way to scroll to the rest, depending on window size and project-list length (#3178, C57). The list now opens in the normal flow of the dialog, directly under its field, and the dialog's own scrollbar always reaches every item — it no longer floats as a separate overlay that has to guess how much room it has.
- The New job dialog's Project field always showed "Home" first and highlighted, even when you'd typed something that matched a different project — the thing you typed sat second, unhighlighted (#3178, C57). Home still always appears regardless of what you type; it just no longer jumps ahead of an actual match.
- The notification bell showed raw markdown syntax (like `![alt](...)`) instead of plain text for messages containing an image (#3178).

### Security
- An AI-generated image's filename was handed to the model as a full, absolute disk path — including your real username — which could then be echoed back into a chat reply and, from there, into a persisted message or notification body (#3178). The model is now given only a relative reference; nothing about your disk layout leaves the app. Existing messages already containing the absolute form are rewritten automatically, once, the next time Pane starts.

## [1.0.80] - 2026-11-05
### Fixed
- The New job dialog's Project and Agent search fields opened a type-to-search box but never showed a list on click, with nothing typed (#3175, C57). The dialog's own centering CSS (a `transform` on its outer box, present since #3116, unrelated to the recent shared-picker work) was accidentally turning itself into the positioning anchor for the dropdown beneath it, landing the list in the wrong place and clipping it. The dialog now centers itself the same way Settings' own dialogs already do; clicking either field opens the full list immediately.
- Settings → AI → Smart Features showed a "Connected via Provider Connections" status row for OpenRouter, Anthropic, and Venice that just repeated what the Provider field's own description already says, plus a stray extra divider line underneath it (#3175). Removed both — the Provider field's description is the only place that fact needs to live.

## [1.0.79] - 2026-11-05
### Fixed
- The image-model picker (Settings → AI → Image generation) and the New job dialog's Project and Agent fields had each grown their own ad-hoc search box floating above a plain dropdown (#3166, C51/C57) — including, ironically, the image-model picker itself, which had fallen into the exact search-box-above-a-dropdown pattern it was meant to demonstrate the fix for. All three now use the same searchable picker component the AI model pickers elsewhere already use (#3171, C51/C57).
- A job session's reply showed "Generated 1 image(s)" as plain text with no actual image — interactive chat has shown a real thumbnail since 1.0.77 (#3171, C59). Job sessions now render the same thumbnail.
- The New job dialog's footer claimed a new session would be "called "this job"" when the Name field was left empty — a false claim; the session is actually auto-titled from the brief (#3171, C43). It now reads "Runs go to a new session, named after the job." when empty, and still names your typed title, live, as you type it.
- A job session's "Job session · <name>" label could float over the header's right edge or spill past its bottom instead of sitting inside the header row (#3171, C58).

### Security
- Settings → AI now asks for your OpenRouter, Anthropic, or Venice key **once** — in Provider Connections. Smart Features and Semantic Search no longer have their own key fields; they reuse whatever provider you've already connected (#3171, C50). Previously, Semantic Search's OpenRouter key sat in the database in plain text, never in the keychain — a credential-handling gap, not just a repeated-prompt annoyance. On first launch after this update, any key you'd already typed into either section is moved into Provider Connections automatically (or discarded if Provider Connections already had one for that provider) and the old copy is deleted — nothing is left behind, and nothing is silently dropped. Removing a connection's key now fails clearly if Smart Features or Semantic Search still depends on it, instead of quietly going through with an empty key.
- Closed a narrow gap in that same migration: an empty or blank-only saved key could theoretically have been treated as a real, usable connection, discarding a real key in its place (#3171). Not reachable through normal use today — Pane's own Save button already refuses a blank key — closed anyway since this is credential-handling code.

## [1.0.78] - 2026-11-04
### Fixed
- An AI-generated image could land in Home's Assets instead of the project it was actually meant for — either when the agent was in Home chatting about a project note, or when a scheduled job ran inside a project (#3166, C54). The image's destination now follows: the note it's being embedded into, then the job's own project (for background jobs), then the chat's own project, in that order, before ever falling back to Home. A Home-scheduled job's own standalone image (no note involved) is also now correctly recognized as belonging to Home, rather than a bogus internal folder. A pre-existing cross-project write guard is unchanged by this — it already requires a project-scoped chat's note to belong to that same project before any image is generated.
- Clicking a project in the sidebar while already viewing it could make an older wake/job dispatch brief suddenly reappear as a block of raw, unformatted text (#3166, C55). Two separate places that decide which messages to show disagreed about one kind of message; they now agree.
- Opening a job's session from the notification bell or the Jobs card (when it shared a project with whatever you were already viewing) left the chat header showing the old session's name, even though the messages shown were correct (#3166, C58). The header now always names the session you're actually looking at, and job sessions get a small "Job session" label so they're never mistaken for your regular project chat.
- The New job dialog's Project dropdown listed every folder inside every project as if it were its own project (#3166, C56). It now lists projects only.
- Reordering a card within the Cabinet column left that column highlighted green afterward, as if a drop were still in progress (#3166, C52).
- A resized image's card preview could show raw HTML markup instead of a short placeholder (#3166, C53).
### Added
- Search fields on the image-model picker (Settings → AI → Image generation) and on the New job dialog's Project and Agent fields — all three were previously plain, unfiltered dropdowns (#3166, C51/C57).

### Security
- A background job's write tools — editing notes, sheets, job management (cancel/pause/resume), and image generation — now follow the same project-isolation rule a typed chat message in that job's project would (#3167). Previously, a job's writes were never checked against its own project at all, regardless of which project the job belonged to: a job running inside one project could silently write into another. A job created in Home keeps Home's existing cross-project allowance, unchanged — exactly as if the same request had been typed in Home's own chat.

## [1.0.77] - 2026-11-03
### Added
- **Image generation (OpenRouter) — PR 1 of 2 (#3161, §39).** A new `generate_image` tool lets your AI generate an image from a prompt and optionally place it in a note (top, bottom, or after a heading you name) — the brief decides placement, the tool doesn't guess. New Settings → AI → Image generation section (no new key field — reuses your existing OpenRouter connection) with a provider + model picker and a Test button. Generated images are ordinary attachments (Projects/\<name\>/Assets or Home/Assets) embedded as a plain `![alt](Assets/...)` line, the same as any dropped image; a thumbnail now also renders on the assistant's chat message. Cost is shown per call when the provider reports it, never as "$0.00" when it doesn't. A cross-project write guard closes a gap found while building this: a project-scoped agent could not previously be stopped from pointing a (not-yet-existent) write tool at another project's note by name alone — `generate_image` is the first tool built against that corrected guard. `SCHEMA_VERSION` unchanged at 97 — no migration. Venice support and a per-turn image cap land in PR 2. `docs/spec/runtime.md` §39 amended (cross-project guard documented; the draft's "classifier bypass list gains 'image'" instruction was found unnecessary — the list already covers it automatically — and struck rather than implemented).
- **Image generation (Venice) — PR 2 of 2 (#3161, §39).** Venice joins OpenRouter as a second image provider in Settings → AI → Image generation. Venice's sizing is genuinely three shapes, not two — pixel models (`width`/`height`), aspect-ratio-only models, and aspect-ratio-plus-resolution-tier models — told apart automatically from Venice's own model-list metadata, never guessed or hardcoded per model. A new **"Max images per job turn"** setting (default 4) caps how many images a background job can generate in one turn; interactive chat is never capped. A capped-out job turn gets a clear tool error and keeps going — nothing else in the turn is affected. The job's receipt line now shows how many images it generated and the total cost, when every call reported one. `SCHEMA_VERSION` unchanged at 97 — no migration, one new settings key.
- internal: the per-turn image cap lives on the turn's own in-memory state, not a lookup table keyed by session — closing off the exact kind of "forgot to ever clean it up" bug a prior per-session budget tracker (#3122) had.

### Fixed
- Pre-existing: editing and re-saving a note that already had an image embedded in it (dropped in any time before 1.0.76, not through the new AI tool) could silently turn the image into a plain, non-rendering link, losing its connection to the original file (#3163). This has been happening since image embeds were introduced — it predates image generation entirely. 1.0.76 already stopped this from happening to NEW edits; this release repairs the damage on notes that were already affected, automatically, the next time Pane opens. The repair only ever touches a link that: used to be an image, still points at a real image file, and currently isn't rendering as one — a link to a document or anything else you've placed in your Assets folder is left exactly as it was.

## [1.0.76] - 2026-11-03
### Fixed
- A scheduled job whose brief the classifier judged simple could die with `401 Missing Authentication header` instead of running (#3155, C48). The job dispatcher read the API credential from the primary provider BEFORE Smart Routing chose which provider to actually use, then handed that stale key to the provider it switched to — so any job routed to an override provider authenticated with the wrong account's key. The credential is now derived after the provider is resolved, the same ordering interactive chat already used. This blocked every content-machine step classified simple.
- The job-failed notification was titled "Tick stopped after N failures" for every job, whatever its name — a job called "Say hello" reported as "Tick" (#3155, C47). It now names the real job, and a one-off job says "failed" rather than borrowing the recurring-streak wording.
- The back button that returns you from a job session to where you came from followed you out of job sessions entirely, appearing over unrelated chats (#3155, C49b). It now renders only inside a job session, sits at the left edge of the job-brief strip rather than floating over the messages, and its return target clears on any manual navigation. `Cmd+[` still works.
- internal: notification, session and memory timestamps are parsed through one shared helper rather than three hand-rolled copies of the same conversion (#3155, C44). The copies were individually correct after #3154; a fourth site would have been a fourth chance to get it wrong.
- internal: every notification idempotency key now comes from one typed helper (#3155, C45). The last hand-rolled key prefix is gone, so a new notification consumer cannot silently collide with an existing one and suppress its own bell.

### Known issues
- After a chat-created once-job or spawn finishes, its dispatch brief can still render as a visible block in the origin chat, raw markdown included (#3155, C49a). **Not fixed in this release.** Two backend reproductions were written and both pass against the current code, so the leak is almost certainly in rendering rather than in what gets written — a fix was deliberately left out rather than guessed at without a failing test to prove it.

## [1.0.75] - 2026-11-03
### Changed
- **Jobs UX — PR 3 of 3: cleanup (#3151).** Seven items, closing out the sprint before the 1.0.75 bump: (1) notification timestamps that read "now" forever (C44) — four independent `formatRelativeTime` copies (`utils/time.ts`, `NotificationPanel.svelte`, `Settings.svelte`, `SessionRow.svelte`, the last of which had a second affected sibling, `formatCreatedAt`) all parsed SQLite's naive-UTC `datetime('now')` string as local wall-clock time, making the computed age negative in any timezone behind UTC; all four get the same `+ 'Z'`/`.replace(' ', 'T')` fix already used elsewhere in this codebase (`ChatPanel.svelte`, `scheduledPanel.ts`, `jobStatusChip.ts`) — not collapsed into one shared implementation, since each has a genuinely different output vocabulary and unifying them would be a visible format change on at least one surface. (2) `notification_key(firing_id, scope)` (#3149/C45) — a `NotificationScope` enum (`OwnSession`/`Origin`) replaces the bare `agent_message:{id}` own-session key and the caller-side `format!("{}-origin", ...)` suffix with one helper, used at the three call sites that actually implement the own-session/origin pair (the fourth, unrelated OC-pickup call site keeps its own distinct key shape, now expressed as `OwnSession` scope — byte-identical, not a new behavior). (3) #3148/C46's recurring-with-origin test now also asserts the two bells' idem_keys are exactly what the new helper computes from the same firing id, not independently-matching strings. (4) a missing negative control: the archive-sweep status list's `'running'` exclusion had no test pinning it — widening the list to include `'running'` survived all 174 scheduler tests undetected; closed with a `job-running` row added to the existing archive test. (5) `SAFE_URL`'s `pane:` allowlist entry (added in PR 1 for `pane://note/{id}` job-output links) narrowed from a bare `pane:` scheme to the exact `pane://note/` shape. (6) `cancel_job` now stops a running job instead of refusing it (#3132) — `wait_for_running_job_to_stop` sets the SAME per-session cancel flag for OC-runtime jobs that it already set for API-runtime ones, since #3129 gave every runtime a real cancel checkpoint through `run_agent_loop`; the Scheduled panel's Delete-on-a-running-row control (built in #3050 PR 9, already shipped) already performs the wait-then-cancel sequence this closes — no new UI needed, the "stop it first" error already has a working, clickable referent. (7) #3135 docs hygiene — §36.12's ADR-0023 table corrected in place (undated status rows for the retired `sessions.send`/`sessions.create` mechanism), and the one mid-paragraph bracketed superseded-annotation in `runtime.md` converted to the same append-after form every other correction in the file already uses, with the rule stated in a new conventions note. `SCHEMA_VERSION` unchanged at 97 (PR 2's bump; nothing here needed a column). `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.7, §36.12 amended; a new annotation-conventions note added.
- **Jobs UX, one rule for every job kind — PR 1 of 3 (#3151, Matt's 2026-11-02 ruling, live test #4 follow-up).** Every job — once, reminder, recurring, heartbeat, dialog-created, spawn — now gets its own session, titled after the job, the same shape every kind but `reminder` already had. The Reminders session (#3120 PR 2's C5) is retired: `find_or_create_reminders_session` is deleted; a reminder now gets a fresh session per firing like everything else. Existing `origin='reminder'` sessions are migrated once, at launch, idempotently (`ensure_reminders_sessions_renamed_once`, `migrations.rs`) — renamed to "Reminders (old)" and flipped to `origin='user'`. **No new toggle, no new `list_sessions` parameter** — Matt's amendment overrode the scope's own proposal for one: `list_sessions` already excludes `origin IN ('spawn', 'schedule')` unconditionally, in both `include_hidden` branches, which is what makes the Reminders row disappear from the drawer for free the moment its origin stops being the special `'reminder'` value.
- **Job output links.** When a job turn's own tool calls create (or find-existing) a note or sheet, a `[title](pane://note/{id})` reference token is appended to both the job's own-session reply and the origin receipt (#3148's unchanged plain-insert mechanism) — one append site in `run_agent_loop`, never two independently-built copies. Chosen mechanism: a plain markdown link rendered by the chat renderer's existing `<a href>` path (`markdown.ts`'s `SAFE_URL` gained the `pane:` scheme) plus one new branch in `ChatPanel.svelte`'s existing link-click handler — not a second ProseMirror/wikilink renderer. Clicking it opens the note in its OWN project (`ChatSidebar.svelte`'s new `navigateToNoteById`, reusing the existing `open_note` navigation decision verbatim). Home has no notes or sheets — already true today, for free (`create_note`/`create_sheet` with `project_id='workspace'` are refused before any write).
- **Bell and Jobs card → the job session, with a way back.** Both entry points (the notification bell and the Scheduled panel's "Open session" link) now set a one-deep return target before switching in; a new back button in the chat header (and `Cmd+[`) returns to wherever the user was. A second back press is a no-op — the button is absent, not disabled, matching the "visible and wrong" failure mode this sprint's own task named explicitly.
- **Editing a job can no longer change its agent.** The Agent dropdown locks during Edit with a "Change agent = new job" hint (Project stays editable); the backend now refuses the whole edit if the resolved agent differs from the job's existing one — closing a real desync bug (the session stayed bound to the OLD agent while `agent_jobs.agent_id` silently changed), not just a UX gap.
- `SCHEMA_VERSION` unchanged at 96 — no column, no migration. PR 2 of 3 carries the v97 bump (C24, Done-tab archive); PR 3 is cleanup. `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.2/§36.3.3/§36.3.6/§36.8.1/§36.11 and `docs/spec/ui-layout.md` §3.5 amended.
- **Jobs UX — PR 2 of 3: the Done tab's "Show deleted" toggle, "Clear done," auto-archive, and hard delete (#3151/#3136, C24).** `SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped 96 → 97 (`migrate_v97`: `agent_jobs.archived_at TEXT NULL`, mirrors `chat_sessions.hidden_at`'s NULL-vs-timestamp shape — archive hides a row from the panel, it never touches `status`, so the done/failed/cancelled distinction the tab exists to show survives). The Done tab now hides `cancelled` ("Deleted") rows by default — a new **"Show deleted"** toggle reveals them (its own toggle/store key, deliberately separate from the Sessions drawer's unrelated hidden-session toggle). **"Clear done"** archives the full Done-tab dataset (done/failed/cancelled, not `stopped`) in one click. The scheduler tick now runs an **auto-archive sweep** — `RUNTIME_JOB_ARCHIVE_DAYS` (30)'s first-ever use against `agent_jobs` (previously it only gated a session wake-staleness check) — sharing the exact same archive mechanism "Clear done" uses, gated behind a once-per-day interval check so it's a cheap settings read on most ticks, not a table scan, backed by a new index for when it does run. **Delete on a Done card** is a brand-new command, not the existing (soft-cancel) Active-tab Delete relabeled: it hard-deletes the job row AND its own chat session (plus the session's messages and processing bookkeeping rows), guarded server-side to done/failed/cancelled jobs only — closing the orphan-session risk PR 1 introduced once every job got its own session. The app version stays 1.0.74; only the schema version moves. A pre-existing install migrates cleanly through the new `migrate_v97` arm (including a dedicated `old_version == "96"` arm and a real-fixture test against `tests/fixtures/upgrade-from-v96.db`) — no DB nuke required. 16 new backend tests and 9 new/rewritten frontend tests, each guard's mutation confirmed red and reverted (see the PR body for the full list). `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.8/§36.11 amended.

## [1.0.74] - 2026-11-02
### Fixed
- Reminders fired and posted their text into the Reminders session but never raised a notification, regardless of whether that session was on screen (#3147, C40, live test #5). `fire_reminder_job` had zero calls to `emit_agent_message_notification` anywhere in its body. Resolves the reminder's own agent name and project display name, then notifies unless the Reminders session is the one open — same gate every other `emit_agent_message_notification` call site uses. 1 new Rust test, mutation confirmed red (deleted the new emit — reddened to zero rows) and reverted.
- A recurring or heartbeat job notified once, ever — not once per firing. Tick fires three times, Home shows one bell (#3147, C41, live test #5 — Matt's own repro). The own-session notification was keyed `job-turn-{job_id}`, identical on every firing of the same job, so `emit_agent_message_notification`'s own dedup silently skipped every firing after the first. Three timestamp keys were considered and rejected (`next_run_at`: means the NEXT occurrence, would collide across a whole cron period; `last_run_at`: does not exist anywhere in this codebase; `started_at`: real, but second-granular, collides under a fast/mocked two-firings-in-one-test case) in favor of reusing the existing, documented `agent_message:{message_id}` convention — `insert_wake_turn_reply` now returns the message id it mints (previously discarded) instead of inventing a timestamp scheme. 1 new Rust test, mutation confirmed red (reverted the key to `job-turn-{job_id}` — reddened to one row after two firings) and reverted.
- Recurring and heartbeat jobs scheduled with an origin chat (the common case — "remind every 2 minutes" typed in Home) never got a report-back copy in that origin — only `spawn`/chat-created `once` jobs did. The "Morning brief never lands in Home" symptom (#3147, C42, live test #5, Matt's ruling — the fix that matters this sprint). Widened the report-back gate to also cover `recurring`/`heartbeat`, confirmed structurally separate from C39's own wake-on-complete gate (no shared boolean, no fallthrough). A second, hidden fix was required beyond the kind-widen alone: the report-back notification key and the ingest dedup key (`chat_messages_local.oc_message_id`, under a UNIQUE INDEX) were job-id-only — safe only because `once`/`spawn` fire at most once ever. Without fixing this too, a recurring job's report-back would land once, then silently dedup-skip forever starting on its second firing — a pass on the first walk, a regression the next morning. Both keyed on the same per-firing message id C40/C41 introduced. 3 new Rust tests, each mutation confirmed red and reverted, including a standing regression lock proving C39's wake-on-complete guard is untouched. `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.3/§36.7/§36.8.1 amended.
- A recurring or heartbeat job with an origin got its report-back INSERT into that origin (C42, above) but no bell there — only the own-session notification fired, targeted at the job's OWN hidden schedule session, not the origin Matt was actually watching (#3147, C42d, live test #5 FOLLOW-UPS, Matt's live-tested ruling: "three Tick bells," watching Home). Widened the `agent_message_due` gate (separate from C41's own-session gate) from `spawn`/`once` to also cover `recurring`/`heartbeat`, matching report-back's own kind gate. This reinstates a real collision risk a prior pass had correctly flagged and used as the reason NOT to widen: for `recurring`/`heartbeat` with an origin, the own-session bell and this new origin bell now both fire for the same firing, and `emit_agent_message_notification`'s dedup is a global `idem_key` lookup — not session-scoped — so reusing the bare per-firing key for both would silently drop the second. Fixed by suffixing the origin bell's key (`{message_id}-origin`) rather than reusing it verbatim; `once`/`spawn` are unaffected either way, since their own-session bell is already gated off whenever an origin exists. 2 new Rust tests (one for the bell itself, one tracing C38's own-session write and C42's origin write never doubling up in the same place), both with mutations confirmed red and reverted (kind-widen reverted: zero origin bells; key-suffix reverted alone: first origin bell dedup-skips against the own-session bell fired the same tick). `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.3/§36.7/§36.8.1 corrected — the prior §36.8.1 C42 note's claim that recurring/heartbeat should NOT get a second, separate origin notification is superseded, not deleted.
- Composer textarea showed a stray horizontal scrollbar at certain zoom levels — the third C27 diagnosis this scope, and the first one that targets the right element (#3147, C27, live test #5). The two prior attempts (`ad0c074a`/#3139, #3144/#3145) both modified `.app`, the root flex container; neither was ever the cause. The real rule, `.message-input` (`ChatPanel.svelte`), set `overflow-y: auto` but declared no `overflow-x` at all — per the CSS Overflow Module's own coupling rule, that makes `overflow-x` silently compute to `auto` too. Fixed by setting `overflow-x: hidden` explicitly — mechanism-agnostic, closing the whole class of failure. **Unconfirmed mechanism, stated plainly:** two different proxies for native WKWebView `pageZoom` were tried and neither reproduced the ~1px discrepancy specifically; `docs/spec/ui-layout.md` gains a correction note on the `.app` section (both prior attempts targeted the wrong element) and a new subsection for `.message-input`. 1 new Vitest source-text pin, explicitly disclaimed (proves the literal, not the real-WKWebView symptom), mutation confirmed red and reverted. `4d-skip: Matt` — confirmed at Cmd+ zoom on the next live walk.
- Two leftover "schedule" strings in the New job dialog (#3147, C43, live test #5): the Name field's placeholder ("Schedule name") and the footer's fallback summary ("this schedule") didn't match the rest of the dialog's "job" vocabulary (title, submit button, the Edit flow's own sibling summary). Renamed to "Job name" / "this job". No test — a mutation here would prove nothing beyond "the string changed," stated rather than invented.

## [1.0.73] - 2026-11-02
### Fixed
- No session scrolled at all on 1.0.72 — Home, project, and job sessions alike; the message list grew with its content and the composer sat below the window edge (#3144, C27, second attempt). The prior fix (`ad0c074a`, #3139) had moved `.app` (`src/routes/+page.svelte`) from `100vw`/`100vh` to `width: 100%; height: 100%` on a theory its own commit message called "a strong lead, not a confirmed repro" — that theory was never confirmed, and the `%` value it shipped is what broke every session's scroll. A second theory (`app.html`'s `display: contents` wrapper not passing percentage height through in WKWebView) was tested this time and also **not confirmed** — a byte-faithful repro of the exact shipped CSS chain passed clean, 6/6 structural variants, in both Playwright's bundled WebKit and Chromium, including the currently-broken shipped CSS (`docs/audits/2026-11-02-scope-3144-c27-scroll.md`). Changed to `position: fixed; inset: 0`, chosen deliberately to be **mechanism-agnostic**: it depends on neither percentage-of-ancestor resolution nor viewport-unit resolution, so it works regardless of which link in the chain is actually responsible — proven empirically by forcing an ancestor box to collapse to zero height (a stand-in for the real, still-unidentified fault) and confirming `%` reproduces the exact break while `position: fixed; inset: 0` recovers completely. Rejected `100dvh`/`100dvw` (same unit family as the original, still-unconfirmed `vw`/`vh` suspect, under a new name) and giving `app.html`'s wrapper an explicit height (that wrapper is SvelteKit's own default, kept to protect hydration from extension-injected DOM; changing it fights the framework for an unconfirmed benefit). `docs/spec/ui-layout.md` gains a new "App Shell Root Sizing" subsection. The existing jsdom source-text pin (`src/routes/page.c27-app-sizing.test.ts`) is rewritten to assert the new literal and its docstring is demoted further — explicit that a green result here proves nothing about real layout, same house pattern as the first version's own (unheeded) disclaimer. The real verification is a new, **local-only** test, `e2e/tests/tier1/c27-app-sizing-layout.spec.ts`, asserting against a real Tauri build through the real-WKWebView socket bridge (`@srsholmes/tauri-playwright`) that `.app`'s height matches the viewport and that `.messages-area` actually scrolls once overfilled — not added to any CI job: Playwright's bundled WebKit does not reproduce this symptom at all, and `e2e.yml` ("E2E — Playwright (self-hosted)") is `disabled_manually` (Matt, 2026-10-30) regardless. Written and discovered, but NOT yet executed end-to-end: the fixture's `window.__PANE_TEST_MODE__` bypass loses a race against the frontend's synchronous `initAuth()`, so `AuthScreen` never yields to `.app` (0/40 across a 4s poll) — pre-existing #1382, reproduced today, not fixed here. The layout fix therefore rests on Matt's live walk, not on a green test. **`4d-skip: Matt`** — this scope's own live-repro constraint (read-only on GitHub, no access to a zoomed real WKWebView) means this fix is unconfirmed against the real symptom until Matt's next live walk, same caveat class as before, stated up front this time. **C27 goes back to Open on the cleanup list: "live repro required before the next attempt."** `SCHEMA_VERSION` unchanged at 96.

## [1.0.72] - 2026-11-01
### Fixed
- A job turn's reply was only ever written into its origin session via report-back — a job created with no origin (the New job dialog) had no report-back target either, so the reply was computed and persisted nowhere, with no notification (#3139, C38, live test #4 — Matt's exact repro: 174 chars, fired, gone). Widens `insert_wake_turn_reply`'s call site (`ai/scheduler.rs`) from `wake`/`recurring`/`heartbeat` to an unconditional call covering every kind that reaches it; `job.session_id` is never the same column value as `job.origin_session_id` for any covered kind except `wake` (already handled, unaffected), so a job WITH an origin now gets two writes — its own session (new) and the origin via report-back (unchanged) — landing in two distinct sessions, not a double-write to one. **Notification ruling (Matt, decided): one notification per firing, never two.** A job with an origin keeps exactly today's notification (report-back's own); a job with no origin now raises one off its own-session write instead — the case that was silent before. Also fixes the recurring/heartbeat own-session notification title, which used the job's title instead of the agent's name ("Message from Tick" instead of "Message from Brit"). 5 new Rust tests, each with its mutation confirmed red and reverted, including an absence assertion (a with-origin job's notification is proven ZERO on the job's own session, not just one on the origin) to catch a regression into double-notifying. `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.3/§36.8.1/§36.7 amended.
- Recurring/heartbeat jobs scheduled with an origin chat woke that origin with a fresh proactive turn on EVERY firing, not just once — Matt's "six wake rows on Home from the Tick job" repro (#3139, C39, live test #4). `§36.4.5`'s own spec text already scoped wakes to `spawn_job`/chat-originated `once` jobs only; the code's guard checked `wake_origin` + an existing origin, with no `kind` filter. Closed with one added condition at the wake-creation guard (`ai/scheduler.rs`): `kind IN ('spawn', 'once')`. Verified non-breaking for the wake-chain mechanism before building: a `kind == 'wake'` row's own `origin_session_id` is always `NULL` by construction, so it never reached this guard with an origin present either way — the chain's next hop is carried by the fresh `spawn`/`once` row the woken turn itself creates. 4 new Rust tests (2 negative, 2 positive-control), each with its mutation confirmed red and reverted. `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.4.5 amended.
- "Remind me to X" could still produce a plain scheduled job instead of a reminder — the `schedule_job` tool's `kind` property was optional and its enum contained only `"reminder"`, with no legal "this is a normal job" value a model could pass to make `required` meaningful (#3139, C36, live test #4). Added `"job"` to the schema's `kind` enum alongside `"reminder"`, added a pure-passthrough `kind="job"` match arm to `execute_schedule_job` (identical to omitting `kind`), then flipped `required` from `["brief"]` to `["brief", "kind"]`. The pre-existing kind-inference fallback is NOT deleted — a JSON-Schema `required` array is advisory to the model/provider only, never enforced by Rust. Paired with a new system-prompt rule (ABSOLUTE RULES rule 32) telling the model explicitly when to pass `kind="reminder"` vs `kind="job"`; `STATIC_PROMPT_TOKEN_BUDGET` remeasured at 5,719 tokens with the new rule included (no raise needed, still under the existing 5,800 ceiling). Inverted an existing regression test whose own old assertion was the literal opposite of this fix's goal, renamed and widened rather than silently left for CI to catch as a surprise. 3 new Rust tests, each with its mutation confirmed red and reverted. `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.7 amended.
- Chat chips showing a scheduled job's next run time always printed it in UTC, never the viewer's local time (#3139, C37, live test #4). Root cause: the chip's "next" clause was baked into its stored content server-side, in UTC, at creation time — never reformatted client-side at all, unlike the Scheduled panel's own chip text, which is correct because it defers formatting to render time. Fixed by plumbing, not a second formatter: `execute_schedule_job`'s chip text drops the baked "next" clause; `get_job_status` (`ai/scheduler.rs`) now also returns the existing `agent_jobs.next_run_at` column (no migration); `chipDisplayText` (`jobStatusChip.ts`) computes the "next" clause at render time, importing and reusing the Scheduled panel's existing `formatScheduleDateTime` directly — one formatter, two consumers. Old chip rows written before this fix keep their frozen UTC text forever (expected, not a regression). 2 new Rust tests and 3 new Vitest tests, the latter confirmed deterministic under both `TZ=UTC` and `TZ=America/New_York` and confirmed reddening under a non-UTC TZ when the formatter call is swapped for a raw passthrough (the exact "wrong hour" failure mode this closes).
- Cmd+/Cmd- zoom reflowed the chat column, producing a stray scrollbar-shaped artifact and a misaligned composer (#3139, C27, live test #4 — Matt's live re-walk confirms). Root cause (code-grounded, not live-reproduced per this scope's read-only constraint): `.app` (`src/routes/+page.svelte`), the root flex container for the entire UI, was sized with viewport units (`100vw`/`100vh`) — a redundant, independently-derived sizing path for the SAME box `html`/`body` already size correctly via percent; viewport units and percent aren't guaranteed to resolve from the same measurement under a zoomed WKWebView. Changed to `width: 100%; height: 100%`, inheriting cleanly from `html`/`body` instead of re-deriving it a second, possibly-divergent way. 1 new Vitest source-text regression pin, mutation confirmed red and reverted — proves nothing about the real zoom behavior on its own; that confirmation is Matt's live walk (`4d-skip: Matt`).
- "Create schedule" button in the New job dialog renamed to "Create job" (#3139, leftover 1, live test #4). "Save changes" (the Edit flow's own label) is unchanged. 2 new Vitest tests, mutation confirmed red and reverted.
- The composer's pre-send attachment chip for a non-image file was still a bare uppercased-extension box (#3139, leftover 2, live test #4). Direct precedent: C30 (#3128) closed the identical complaint for the post-send in-message attachment chip by adding filename + size alongside the icon, explicitly leaving this pre-send box untouched at the time. Applied the same treatment here, reusing the existing `formatFileSize` helper — no new formatting logic. 1 new Vitest test, mutation confirmed red and reverted.

## [1.0.71] - 2026-11-01
### Changed
- Scheduled/spawned/wake jobs on an OpenClaw-bound agent now dispatch through Pane's own agent loop with Pane's full tool surface, the same path every other runtime's job already used — "Pane is the toolset" (#3129, C28(b), `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.0.1/§36.3.4/§36.11, Reed's scope audit `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-31-scope-3129-c28b.md`). Previously, a job on an OpenClaw-bound agent sent a single trigger message into a separate OC-side session (`sessions.create`/`sessions.send`) and never got Pane's own notes/tasks/schedule tools, a real cancel checkpoint, or the shared tool-call budget every other job turn has — OC did all the thinking on its own side, with its own `'sent'` resting status. `prepare_job_dispatch` was already provider-generic (it resolves `AiProvider::OpenClaw` credentials the same way an interactive OC chat turn does); the fix was deleting the one `if job.runtime_type == "openclaw"` branch in `scheduler_tick` that routed around it, plus fixing a hardcoded `own_turn_is_openclaw: false` that would have silently disabled the #2738 own-turn dedup guard for OC job turns. Retired as dead code once nothing dispatches through the old path: `dispatch_oc_job`/`ensure_oc_session_bootstrapped` (the bootstrap-then-send mechanism and its C9 session-label-collision fix), the `'sent'`→`'done'` background-pickup flip, background pickup's stored-OC-session-key lookup (job sessions are never bootstrap-returned OC sessions once they run through the real loop), and the wake-into-OC-origin skip that silently downgraded a finished spawn's wake-on-complete to report-only whenever its origin session happened to be OpenClaw-bound — a wake is a job like any other now. `agent_jobs.oc_session_key` stays as a vestigial, unread column (dropping a SQLite column is a heavier migration than this PR's own "no bump" rule allows for zero benefit); `SCHEMA_VERSION` is unchanged at 96. The §36.11 invariant "OC's failed status is not evidence" is reworded, not deleted — it still protects OC's own spawns/cron (read back via background pickup, never Pane-dispatched) from being mirrored as a Pane failure; it no longer describes the retired Pane-dispatched-job case, which now settles its terminal status the same way every other runtime's job does. The cancel/pause refuse-only guard on a running OC job (`execute_cancel_job`/`wait_for_running_job_to_stop`) is unchanged by this PR — its original reason ("no cancel checkpoint to flag") no longer applies now that OC jobs run the real loop, but loosening it is new, separately-tested behavior, filed as its own follow-up issue, not bundled here.
- **Behaviour change, Matt's Ruling 3 (2026-10-31):** a recurring/heartbeat job's 3-strike failure ladder is reimplemented on the shared dispatch path, for every runtime — closing Reed's #3133 WARN finding #2. The ladder (`agent_jobs.consecutive_failures`/`last_failed_at`) lived exclusively inside `dispatch_oc_job`, deleted above; the API-runtime path never had it either, so deleting `dispatch_oc_job` had silently removed the mechanism's only implementation entirely, not "narrowed it to API" as the retirement above originally characterized it — a recurring/heartbeat job that hit one transient provider blip went straight to a terminal `'failed'` and stopped recurring, where before (via the now-deleted function) it got two more chances. New `ai::scheduler::settle_recurring_job_outcome`, called instead of `write_job_terminal_status` for `kind IN ('recurring', 'heartbeat')` only (`once`/`spawn`/`wake` keep their unchanged single-firing terminal mapping): a `Failed` outcome under 3 consecutive strikes increments the counter and stays `'pending'` (`next_run_at` was already advanced at claim time — this never re-advances it); the 3rd consecutive strike flips to a terminal `'failed'`; a `Done` outcome anywhere in the streak resets the counter to 0 and clears `last_failed_at`. `last_failed_at` is written only on the FIRST failure of a new streak and left untouched on the 2nd/3rd, so it stays usable as PR 6's `emit_or_update_job_failed_notification` dedupe key (`job_id` + `streak_started_at`) — a per-firing notification now fires for every strike (not just the terminal one), same as the OC-only mechanism originally did. No schema change — the columns already existed; `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 96. 2 restored tests (re-expressed against the shared path, not OC-specific — their deleted ancestors mocked `sessions.send`), plus 2 new tier-check tests (a single failure stays `'pending'` with the counter at 1; `Stopped` bypasses the ladder entirely).
- **Separate finding, not caused by this PR — a standing regression since `d3f74e8f` (#3050 PR 5, Oct 28), closing Reed's #3133 re-audit gap** (`~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-31-reaudit-3133-ladder.md`): since `d3f74e8f`, every recurring or heartbeat job on an API-runtime agent (ollama, anthropic, openrouter, venice — any runtime other than `openclaw`) went terminal after its first firing, because `write_job_terminal_status`'s terminal write ran unconditionally for every `kind`, with no check routing recurring/heartbeat jobs around it, overwriting the `'pending'` status `recompute_recurrence` had just set moments earlier at claim time. OC recurring jobs were unaffected — `dispatch_oc_job`'s own, separate ladder (deleted above) already gave them their two extra chances; the API-runtime path simply never had the mechanism at all. This was not caused by this PR's own deletion of `dispatch_oc_job` above — the bug predates #3129/#3133 by three days and was independently reachable before either existed.
