This PR's shared ladder (`settle_recurring_job_outcome`, above) closes it as an incidental side effect of unifying the dispatch path onto one implementation, not as this PR's stated purpose.
- Scheduled panel: an **Edit** action for Active `once`/`recurring` jobs — Matt's ask, "dial in the content machine without delete-and-recreate" (#3134, C26, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.8). Previously the only way to change a job's brief or schedule was cancel-and-recreate, which lost the job's identity and its session's run history. New `update_job`/`execute_update_job` (`ai/tools.rs`, a bare command sibling to `create_scheduled_job`, never an AI tool — Edit is a UI-only panel action) rewrites the SAME `agent_jobs` row (`id`/`session_id` untouched); `next_run_at` recomputes through a newly-extracted `resolve_kind_and_next_run_at`, the exact same helper `schedule_job` itself calls — one mechanism, not two. Refused while `status = 'running'` with its own textually-separate `WHERE status != 'running'` clause (same SHAPE as `cancel_job`'s guard, deliberately not the same code, so #3132's planned loosening of `cancel_job`'s own guard can land without silently changing Edit's behavior). **Saving an edit to a recurring job unconditionally resets `consecutive_failures`/`last_failed_at`** (Matt's pin: "the old failures were against a different definition") via SQL kept textually identical to `settle_recurring_job_outcome`'s `Done` branch — confirmed safe against PR 6's `job_failed` notification dedupe key (`job_id` + `last_failed_at`): the reset forces the next real failure to mint a fresh `streak_started_at`, so no duplicate notification row is possible. A recurring job whose stored cron doesn't match one of the New-job dialog's 4 known picker shapes (daily/weekdays/weekly/every-4-hours) shows that cron as a raw text field instead of the frequency controls, detected once at dialog-open via the new `cronToFrequency` (`scheduledPanel.ts`) — saving without touching it round-trips the cron byte-for-byte, never re-derived through the picker's own `buildCron()`. `openEditJobModal(row)` (`ScheduledPanel.svelte`) is a sibling to the existing `openNewScheduleModal(preset)`, reusing the same form state; the once-job pre-fill uses the new `toDatetimeLocalValue` (`scheduledPanel.ts`) against local `Date` getters, never `.toISOString()`, so the pre-filled time isn't silently shifted by the local offset. `list_scheduled_jobs` gains `brief`/`cron`/`run_at`/`agent_id` in its one SELECT (all four already existed on `agent_jobs` — no schema change) so the Edit dialog's pre-fill has everything it needs off the panel's existing query. **`SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 96** — C26 is a pure UPDATE path; C24 (the Done tab's archive behavior) is split out to #3136, not touched here. 12 new tests across both layers (backend: rewrites-the-same-row, cron-change recomputes `next_run_at`, refuses a running row, resets the streak unconditionally on a title-only edit, and the dedupe-key interaction test proving a fresh streak after an edit; frontend: the two inverse formatters' own unit tests, Edit-button gating, both pre-fill shapes, the raw-cron fidelity test, submit routing, and the "not a silent third edit mode" guard for New job). Mutations run for each, see the PR report.

### Fixed
- A non-image/audio/video attachment chip in chat rendered with no file-type icon — just filename and size, a bare-looking chip (#3128, C30, icon-parity only). **Click-to-open is explicitly OUT of scope** — no lightbox/open-attachment mechanism exists anywhere in `ChatPanel.svelte` to reuse (images render inline with no lightbox either); building one would be a new feature, not a fix, out of this sweep's light-sweep weight. Added the same uppercased-extension icon convention `pendingAttachments`' own `.preview-file-icon` already uses, matching `AttachmentCard.svelte`'s treatment. 1 new Vitest test asserts a rendered `.attachment-file` chip for a non-media file shows the uppercased extension (e.g. "PDF"). Mutation (removing the icon markup): reddens, confirmed and reverted.
- **Every dialog-created Once job was rejected** (#3128, C29, Matt's correction to Reed's brief — this is a hard bug, not a UI ask). The New job dialog's `<input type="datetime-local">` emits `2026-10-31T10:32` per the HTML spec — no seconds — but `parse_run_at_local` only ever accepted `%H:%M:%S`-suffixed shapes, so every dialog-submitted Once job failed with `run_at '...' must be a local datetime like 2026-11-02T09:00:00: input contains invalid characters`. Fixed in the validator (not the one frontend caller) — it's the same function a hand-typing model hits, and its own pre-existing doc comment already says it exists so "a model that hand-types either common ISO-ish shape is not rejected"; accepting `HH:MM` extends that intent rather than patching one caller. 5 new Rust tests: `parse_run_at_local` accepts the dialog's exact no-seconds string (both `T`- and space-separated), the pre-existing with-seconds shape still works (regression guard), garbage is still rejected; and an end-to-end test through the REAL `execute_schedule_job` using the literal dialog string `2026-10-31T10:32` (not a hand-written one with seconds — the bug was precisely that the two differ), proving a real job gets created. Mutation (reverting to the pre-existing two `%H:%M:%S` formats only): the round-trip test reddens with the exact quoted error, confirmed and reverted.
- The Once picker's date/time popups rendered in the browser's light theme, clashing with the dark UI around them (#3128, C29 dark-calendar half). §8a sibling-parity check (`git log -S'color-scheme' -- ScheduledPanel.svelte`) confirmed this was a plain omission — `Editor.svelte`'s `.pill-date-picker` and `TaskMetadataHeader.svelte`'s date input already set `color-scheme: dark`. Added the same declaration to the Once picker's `datetime-local`/`time` inputs. **The "seconds"/time-field half of C29 is a separate, hard bug — see the next entry, Matt's correction to Reed's brief.** 1 new Vitest source-pin test. Mutation (removing the declaration): reddens, confirmed and reverted.
- The Notifications panel painted BEHIND the chat panel instead of over it (#3128, C25). Root cause: C10 (#3125) raised `.chat-panel`'s own z-index to 1001 to escape in-project toolbar stacking — but `.nt-pop` (`NotificationPanel.svelte`'s own fixed-position root) and `.panel-overlay` (`Sidebar.svelte`'s overlay that gates it — confirmed used only for this one panel, not shared by any other sidebar overlay) were left at their old 30/29. Raised both above 1001 (to 1002), same reasoning as C10's own fix. 1 new Vitest source-pin test asserts both z-indexes are strictly greater than `.chat-panel`'s own. Mutation (reverting both back to 30/29): reddens (30/29 is not greater than 1001), confirmed and reverted.
- internal: near-empty notes/facts could get embedded and surface as false-positive semantic-search matches (#3128, C35). The #3126/#3101 drop of `SEMANTIC_SEARCH_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` from a fixed `0.5` to `0.35` admitted a new similarity band that near-empty content — which tends to produce less distinctive, more centroid-near embedding vectors — is especially likely to land in. Chats already guard with `content.len() >= 20` alongside the emptiness check; notes and facts never did, so a stub body (a lone character, a markdown artifact) passed `!trim().is_empty()` and got embedded with no floor. Added the identical `len() >= 20` floor to the notes and facts sub-passes. Both are true: the 0.35 drop made the band newly admissible; the missing floor is what put degenerate vectors in the table to begin with — fixing the floor closes this specific repro, but doesn't retire the standing 0.35 question Reed flagged earlier. 1 new dedicated Rust test (a 1-char note body and a 1-char fact, both excluded, zero embedding rows); 3 pre-existing tests updated where their fixture content was itself under the new 20-char floor by coincidence (not the behavior under test). Mutation (removing the new clause from both guards): reddens with both stubs embedded, confirmed and reverted.
- internal: "remind me to..." messages could get misclassified as trivially simple, stripping `schedule_job` before the model could call it with `kind="reminder"` (#3128, C34). `classify_message_complexity`'s blanket tool-strip for the simple tier is deliberate and robust (every tool, including every future one, is dropped unconditionally — untouched by this fix); the genuinely hand-maintained, fragile surface is `tool_bypass_patterns()`'s reachability gate — `non_tool_name_bypass_patterns()` had no entry for "remind"/"reminder", the exact vocabulary C23's `kind="reminder"` depends on being reachable, so a message like "remind me to call mom at 5" fell through to the probabilistic classifier instead of bypassing to the full model. Added `"remind"`, `"reminder"` to the list. 2 new Rust tests: direct list-membership check; an end-to-end check that "remind me to call mom at 5" bypasses the classifier (returns false/complex) with no provider configured, rather than attempting a real classifier call. Mutation (removing both entries): the membership test reddens directly; the end-to-end test reddens differently (now attempts the real classifier path), confirmed and reverted. **Self-caught during mandated mutation-testing, reported honestly:** the end-to-end test's FIRST version did not actually prove the bypass — with no real provider mocked, `classify_message_complexity`'s own classifier-model/provider resolution failed and fell back to `false` either way, masking whether the pattern list mattered; separately, the first candidate message ("remind me to call mom at 5") happened to also match an unrelated pre-existing pattern ("all", from `navigate_all_projects`'s tool-name token, as a substring of "c-ALL"). Fixed by mocking a real Ollama classifier returning "YES" and switching to "remind me about dinner" (verified by direct enumeration against the live pattern list to match ONLY "remind"). Re-run with the mutation applied afterward: now reddens correctly.
- A scheduler-authored job/wake dispatch brief rendered as a normal user chat bubble, pixel-identical to something the human typed (#3128, C32). `insert_job_brief_message` (`ai/scheduler.rs`) writes the brief with `role='user'`, `synthetic=1`, `job_id` set; `ChatPanel.svelte`'s 3-branch render chain (continuation divider / schedule chip / normal bubble) had no branch aware of `synthetic` — the chip branch correctly excludes it (`!synthetic`), so it fell through to the default bubble, which reads only `message.role`. Added a 4th branch for `job_id && synthetic && role === 'user'`, rendering a distinct non-bubble `.job-brief` treatment (same "bookkeeping, not a person" family as the continuation divider, visually distinct from the schedule-chip pill). 2 new Vitest tests: the synthetic brief row does NOT get `class="message user"` and instead gets `.job-brief`; a real user message (no job_id, synthetic=0) still gets the normal bubble unchanged (regression guard against an over-wide condition). Mutations (deleting the new branch; widening its condition to match any `role === 'user'`): both reddened, confirmed and reverted.
- A refused Run now gives no visible feedback — the rejection (e.g. "Run now is disabled while a run is already in flight") only reached `console.error`, nothing in the DOM changed (#3128, C31 UI half). `handleRunNow`'s catch block now surfaces the rejection's own message as a visible, row-level error (`data-testid="run-now-error"`), reusing the modal's existing `sp-status`/`sp-status--error` visual language rather than inventing new UI; cleared on the next retry attempt. **Data half of C31 (stale pre-C1 `sent` cards from before #3115's 7-day pickup window) is a one-time manual DB cleanup outside this PR's scope, per Reed's brief — not a code change, not attempted here.** 2 new Vitest tests: a rejected `runJobNow` shows the error inline with the rejection text; a successful call never shows it. Mutation (reverting the catch block to `console.error`-only): reddens, confirmed and reverted.
- `ScheduledPanel.svelte`'s New job dialog dropdowns were still visually cramped despite C12's own PR-3 `min-height: 38px` fix landing in source (#3128, C12/C21). Root cause, confirmed by reading — the 3 `<select class="inp">`s (Project, Agent, Frequency) never got `appearance: none`, so WKWebView's native select chrome ignores `min-height` for the select's own box without it; every other styled `<select>` in this codebase (Settings/Editor/ChatPanel) already sets this. §8a sibling-parity check (`git log -S'appearance' -- ScheduledPanel.svelte`) confirmed a plain omission, never a deliberate removal. Added `select.inp { appearance: none; -webkit-appearance: none; ... }`, same custom-arrow pattern as `Settings.svelte`'s `.select-input`. **C21 widened:** the modal's own `<h3>New schedule</h3>` was never attempted by PR 3 (Matt's ruling at the time named only two strings) — #3128 widens the ruling to cover it; renamed to "New job". PR 3's own regression test asserted the string was absent from `container.textContent` but never opened the modal, passing vacuously; updated to actually open the modal first, closing that blind spot for real. 2 new Vitest tests (`select.inp` declares `appearance: none`; the opened modal's own `<h3>` reads "New job"). Mutations (removing the `appearance` rule; reverting the h3 text): both reddened, confirmed and reverted.
- The model now has a clock — local time + UTC offset, not just today's date (#3128, C33, `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` rule 24's tracked history). Confirmed by grep: zero `Local::now`/timezone injection into any prompt-builder path other than rule 24's own date-only `{current_date}`. The model had no way to reason about "in 20 minutes," "this evening," or "it's late, don't ping them." `build_messages_with_context` (`ai/chat.rs`) now also substitutes `{current_time}` (`chrono::Local::now().format("%H:%M %:z")` — numeric UTC offset only; `iana-time-zone`/`chrono-tz` stay absent from `Cargo.toml`, keeping this dependency-light) into the same rule-24 block. The chip-rendering half (`scheduledPanel.ts`'s local-time getters) was already correct and is untouched. 1 new Rust test asserts the assembled system prompt's rule 24 contains both an `HH:MM` pattern and a numeric UTC-offset pattern, alongside the pre-existing date. Mutation (reverting to the date-only format string): reddens, confirmed and reverted. `STATIC_PROMPT_TOKEN_BUDGET` raised 5,700 → 5,800 (measured 5,693 tokens with C23+C33 both included).
- `schedule_job`'s AI tool schema now declares `kind` (#3128, C23, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.2). `kind="reminder"` (C4/C5, #3120 PR 2) was fully built and tested at the Rust level from the start — `execute_schedule_job` already validated it, `fire_reminder_job` already fired it with zero provider calls — but the tool's own JSON Schema never declared a `kind` property at all, for any value, so a model calling the real tool had no way to discover `kind="reminder"` existed. Added `kind` (type string, enum `["reminder"]`, optional) to the schema; also added a one-sentence steer to the same `ToolDef` description noting a job scheduled onto an OpenClaw-bound agent runs through Pane's dispatch/send path, not Pane's own tool loop — marked `TODO(#3129)` since it becomes false once #3129 (C28(b)) lands. 1 new Rust test reads the live `serde_json::Value` schema (not a regex) and asserts `kind`'s enum contains `"reminder"` and that `kind` stays optional. Mutation (deleting the `kind` property): reddens with `properties.get("kind")` returning `None`, confirmed and reverted. `STATIC_PROMPT_TOKEN_BUDGET` raised 5,600 → 5,700 (measured 5,644 tokens with this change included) — real, intentional growth, same documented convention as prior raises.

  - **#3101's mutation test didn't reach the real production code.** `test_switch_embedding_engine_clears_stale_rows_on_model_change_same_engine` hardcoded a copy of the correct `DELETE FROM embeddings` predicate and ran it against a bare `rusqlite::Connection` — no linkage back to `switch_embedding_engine`'s own call site. Reed's two-line injection is now a permanent regression test (`test_scan_finds_a_site_wrapped_across_two_source_lines`, a synthetic 6-site fixture) asserting 6 sites found and the injected one flagged as missing the constant. Mutation (the same injection, done for real in `chat.rs`'s production area) confirmed the guard now reports 6 and reddens on the missing-constant check — then reverted.

OR model IS NULL OR model != ?`. `semantic_search` additionally skips (logs, never scores) any stored vector whose dimension doesn't match the query vector's — a correctness backstop, since a dimension mismatch is a bug, not a low score — and now logs its top-3 scored candidates on every call regardless of threshold, so a near-miss is diagnosable from terminal output. `search_notes`'s fixed `0.5` similarity cutoff (named `SEMANTIC_SEARCH_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD`) drops to `0.35`, reproducing the issue's own repro ("shipping announcement workflow" against a Release Playbook note, which scored below 0.5 and was dropped) as a hit instead of a miss. 5 new Rust tests, each with its mutation confirmed red (or, for the model-change clear, an inline sanity check proving the OLD engine-only predicate deletes nothing — the bug itself) and reverted: model-change clearing within one engine; dimension-mismatch skip; the 0.35-vs-0.5 threshold band; `embeddings` staying out of `CRR_TABLES`.

- internal: notifications for a Home-bound job or session no longer read "· workspace" — they read "· Home" (#3120 PR 3, C3, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.7, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-30-scope-3120-four-prs.md`). The issue's own citation (`unwrap_or("workspace")` sites in `ai/chat.rs`/`ai/tools.rs`) traces to the internal Home-surface sentinel used for `project_id` DB writes — confirmed by direct read, none of those 5 sites ever produce rendered text. The actual rendered-text bug, independently traced for this PR: `emit_agent_message_notification`'s `body = format!("{} · {}", first_line, project_name)` was fed the raw, unresolved `project_id` column verbatim at all 3 of its call sites in `ai/scheduler.rs` — so a Home-bound job/session's notification literally read "... · workspace" in `NotificationPanel.svelte`'s `{notif.body}`. Fixed with one new function, `resolve_project_display_name` (same fallback shape `list_scheduled_jobs`'s own `COALESCE(p.name, 'Home')` already uses), called at all 3 sites — the stored `project_id` sentinel itself is untouched everywhere else it already is one. 4 new Rust tests, each with its mutation confirmed red and reverted (the sentinel resolving to "Home"; an unknown id falling back to "Home" rather than panicking or leaking the raw id; a real project resolving to its own name; the real `resolve_oc_pickup_notification_context` call site end to end). **Diverges from the issue's own file citation, flagged for Reed's audit as a question, not silently decided** — see the PR body and the spec amendment for the full trace.
- internal: two findings from Reed's 2026-10-30 WARN audit of PR #3124 (#3120 PR 2, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.9.3, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-30-pr-3124-pr2.md`), closing the WARN's blocking item and its should-fix item in one commit.

  **1. (Blocking) The #3123 live-refresh test polled a proxy signal, not the condition it asserted — a genuine race, not a flake.** `test_recurring_job_turn_reply_live_refreshes_open_session_3123` polled `mock.matched_async()`, which only proves the mocked ollama HTTP server RECEIVED the request — it does not wait for the detached dispatch task (spawned via `tauri::async_runtime::spawn`, cooperatively scheduled on the same current-thread `#[tokio::test]` runtime) to then parse the response, write the terminal status, call `insert_wake_turn_reply`, and emit the `pane-chip-changed` "inserted" event — all of which happen strictly AFTER the mock observes the request, with no further `.await` point in the test to let that task finish before synchronously reading `events`. Reed read CI's own job log directly, could not reproduce it in 21 local runs (consistent with a narrow, CI-load-dependent window), and explicitly ruled it out as one of the three named artifacts rather than absorbing it. Matt's ruling: poll the condition the test actually asserts. Fixed by polling `events` itself (via the file's existing `poll_until` helper, 25ms interval / 20s ceiling, no fixed `sleep`) until it contains an "inserted" row for the job's own `job_id` — the same pattern `test_recurring_job_turn_reply_is_persisted_3123`/`test_heartbeat_job_turn_reply_is_persisted_3123` already use correctly (polling the real DB row, not a weaker proxy). Mutation (disabling the production `emit_chip_changed` call inside `insert_wake_turn_reply`'s `is_session_open` gate): the test now correctly times out and panics with its own poll message after 20s, instead of racily passing — confirmed red, reverted. 12 serialized reruns of the fixed test: 12/12 pass, 0 flakes.

  **2. (Should-fix) C16's filename escaper missed `]` and newline, breaking the announcement's own bracket structure.** `escape_attachment_label_text` entity-escaped `&`/`<`/`>` — correctly blocking the forged `<<<EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT...>>>` delimiter attack #3117 established — but did not escape `]` or a raw newline, so a hostile filename could still close the `[Attached: ...]` label's own bracket early or split it across two lines; no existing test covered either case. Now also escapes `]` (entity-style, `&#93;`) and replaces `\n`/`\r` with `_` (sufficient to guarantee the single-line property; no bracket-structural meaning to preserve there the way `<`/`>`/`]` have). One new Rust test: a hostile filename carrying both `]` and a newline in one string, pinned to the announcement staying exactly one well-formed `[Attached: ...]` line (exactly one `[`, exactly one `]`, no raw `\n`/`\r`, the filename's own text surviving neutralized rather than dropped). Mutation (reverting `escape_attachment_label_text` to the `&`/`<`/`>`-only form): reddens with the raw `]`/newline surviving interpolation, breaking the asserted single-line shape — confirmed red, reverted. The `rowid ASC` tiebreak pin (Reed's audit, item 1c) is unchanged — Reed proved it structurally unfalsifiable on SQLite (forced index scans plus the reverse-scan pragma, ties always resolve rowid-ascending); kept as the disclosed-intent pin per Matt's ruling, not touched. (Part of #3120)
- internal: `recurring`/`heartbeat` API-runtime job turns now persist their own reply, closing #3123 (#3120 PR 2, last commit per Matt's instruction, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.8.1, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-30-scope-3120-pr2-recut.md`). C18 (PR 1) closed this gap for `wake` only, via `insert_wake_turn_reply`'s direct-insert mechanism, gated on `job_kind_for_report == "wake"`. The same gap existed for `recurring`/`heartbeat`: neither `run_agent_loop` nor any of its callers ever persisted a job turn's final text anywhere on its own — the interactive path's only writer is the frontend's `ai-stream-chunk` listener, never registered for a scheduler-dispatched `sid`. **Shape 2 ("persist at the scheduler"), per Reed's ruling:** the one-condition gate is widened to also match `recurring`/`heartbeat`, reusing `insert_wake_turn_reply` as-is — both kinds' `session_id` IS their own persistent schedule session (§36.3.6), the same shape wake's `session_id` already has (§36.4.5), so no new mechanism is needed. Shape 1 (persisting inside `run_agent_loop` itself) was rejected — it would touch the interactive streaming path for no additional benefit, raising this PR's audit risk for a problem that doesn't require touching it. `spawn`/`once` are deliberately excluded — those kinds have a meaningful `origin_session_id` and already go through the separate report-back/ingest path. Scope: the API-runtime closure only; OC-runtime recurring/heartbeat jobs go through `dispatch_oc_job`/§36.6 pickup instead, untouched. **§36.8.1's prose corrected** — it claimed recurring/heartbeat jobs write to their own schedule session, true in intent but false in code until this commit; the "open question" note PR 1 left against this exact discrepancy is resolved and replaced with a fix(runtime) note, PR 1's own trace kept for the record. 3 new Rust tests: a recurring job's turn and a heartbeat job's turn each persist a real, visible assistant-role row in their own session (not `origin_session_id`); a live-refresh (`pane-chip-changed`) regression pin for an open recurring-job session, same shape C18's own wake test already uses. Mutation (reverting the widened condition to `wake`-only) confirmed red across all three. Full `ai::scheduler` module suite re-run clean (148 passed, +3, 0 failed; the pre-existing wake test, C18, stays green unmodified — confirmed the widening didn't disturb it). (Part of #3120, closes #3123)
- internal: wake-dedup repair fixture widened to cover N>2 duplicates and the same-timestamp tiebreak, test-only (#3120 PR 2, PR 1 WARN #1 carry-forward, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-30-scope-3120-pr2-recut.md`). `ensure_agent_jobs_wake_dedup_index`'s repair query (`migrations.rs`) was already correct for any N and for the same-timestamp `rowid ASC` tiebreak — the committed fixture (PR 1) pinned only two duplicates, narrower than the behavior it was proving. Zero production diff. Two new tests: (1) three pending wake rows, three distinct `created_at` values — mutation (swapping `rn = 1` for `rn <= 2`) confirmed red, and more directly than predicted: the `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` itself fails with a `UNIQUE constraint failed` error (two rows would survive the repair, not one), rather than merely failing a count assertion. (2) two pending wake rows with an IDENTICAL `created_at` (a fixed literal, not two independent `datetime('now')` calls) — asserts the lower-rowid (first-inserted) row survives. **Honestly reported, not glossed over:** the predicted mutation for test (2) (dropping `, rowid ASC` from the `ORDER BY`) was tried against both this fixture and a minimal standalone repro (including with `PRAGMA reverse_unordered_selects = ON`, to try to force a reversed scan order) and did NOT redden in this run's SQLite build — a plain, index-free table scan already returns rows in rowid order here, so the explicit tiebreak coincides with the default order whether written or not. The test is kept as a correctness/intent pin (it still asserts the documented behavior and will catch other regressions), but the specific single-clause-removal mutation Reed's brief predicted could not be reproduced as red in this environment — flagged as a question for Reed's audit rather than silently claiming a result that wasn't actually observed. - Scheduled panel: Done cards no longer show a Delete button (#3120 PR 2, C11, Matt's ruling, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.8, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-30-scope-3120-pr2-recut.md`). - internal: two OpenClaw jobs that happen to share a title no longer collide on OC's own session-label uniqueness constraint (#3120 PR 2, C9, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.4, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-30-scope-3120-pr2-recut.md`). `ensure_oc_session_bootstrapped`'s `sessions.create` call previously sent `title: job.title` verbatim — two different jobs with the same title (two "Check-in" heartbeats, two identically-named schedules) each bootstrap independently on their own first firing, and the SECOND one's `sessions.create` would collide with OC's own per-account session-label uniqueness check. Fixed by appending a short (first-8-char) slice of the job's own UUID to the title; stable across every firing of the SAME job, so a legitimate retry of one job's own failed bootstrap reproduces the identical label rather than becoming a new collision source. 1 new Rust test: two same-titled jobs, each with its own expected (title+short-id) `sessions.create` body mocked for success, plus a catch-all mock returning OC's real-world 409 "label already in use" for any OTHER body (the shape BOTH jobs' calls would have produced pre-fix, since they'd be byte-identical) — asserts both jobs reach `status = 'sent'` with DIFFERENT `oc_session_key`s and the catch-all mock's `.expect(0)` is never hit. Mutation (reverting to `job.title` alone): job 2's bootstrap falls through to the catch-all 409 mock, `status` for that job ends up `"failed"`. Full `ai::scheduler` module suite re-run clean (145 passed, +1, 0 failed). (Part of #3120)
- internal: a `once` OpenClaw job's reply, once ingested by background pickup, now flips its status from `sent` to `done` (#3120 PR 2, C1, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.6, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-30-scope-3120-pr2-recut.md`). Before this fix, nothing in `run_oc_background_pickup`'s ingest path ever wrote `'done'` for an OC job — a `once` job's card stayed stuck on the Scheduled panel's Active tab forever (`sent` matches none of §36.3.8's Done-tab filter values), even after its reply had genuinely landed and was visible in the chat. Scoped to `kind = 'once' AND status = 'sent'` (a `recurring`/`heartbeat` job already returns to `pending` at send time per §36.3.4 Ruling 1 and never rests at `done`); fires `pane-chip-changed` with `status: "done"` on a successful flip so an open Scheduled panel updates live. 2 new Rust tests: the once-job flip itself, and a regression guard confirming a recurring job's reply ingest never flips to `done`. Mutation (removing the `UPDATE agent_jobs SET status = 'done' ...` block): the once-job test reddens with `status` still `"sent"`. **Not done in this PR, flagged plainly:** any `once` OC job already stuck at `status = 'sent'` on an existing install predates this fix and is not retroactively repaired by it — that's a one-time direct-SQL data cleanup against the live production database, which this author does not have access to and must not touch; see the spec amendment for the illustrative (not yet run) statement. (Part of #3120)
- internal: job turns now get the same smart-routing cost optimization interactive turns already have (#3120 PR 2, C6, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.3, `docs/spec/smart-routing.md` §27.6.1, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-30-scope-3120-pr2-recut.md`). `prepare_job_dispatch` (`ai/scheduler.rs`) previously used an API agent's configured model/provider verbatim for every job/wake/recurring/heartbeat turn, with no smart-routing classifier call at all — `resolve_model_for_message` (the exact function `ai_chat_stream` already calls for interactive turns) is now called for job dispatch too, BEFORE the existing `apply_budget` pass (so budgeting sees the context window of the EFFECTIVE model smart routing selected, not the agent's configured one — a simple-tier model can have a different window than the primary model it replaces). `primary_provider` stays the agent's real configured provider (used by downstream fallback/retry logic); only `provider_for_streaming`/`model` become the smart-routing-resolved values, mirroring the `effective_provider`/`provider` split `ai_chat_stream` already makes. When smart routing is unconfigured, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged (classifier/simple-tier failure falls through to the agent's own model, same as before this fix). 2 new Rust tests: one dispatches an unreachable primary-provider endpoint (`prepare_job_dispatch` never actually dials it — it only resolves which model to use) alongside a real mocked classifier call, asserting the job dispatches on the simple-tier model with the classifier mock's `.expect(1)` proving the gate actually ran; one regression pin confirms smart-routing-disabled job dispatch is unaffected. Mutation (reverting to `dispatch_cfg.model`/`dispatch_cfg.provider` verbatim): the classifier mock's `.expect(1)` panics with "received 0" and the model assertion reddens. Full `ai::scheduler` module suite re-run clean (142 passed, +2, 0 failed). (Part of #3120)
- internal: a new `reminder` schedule-job kind fires with zero provider calls, and reuses one shared session per agent (#3120 PR 2, C4/C5, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.2/§36.3.6, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-30-scope-3120-pr2-recut.md`). **C4:** `scheduler_tick`'s claim loop intercepts `kind == "reminder"` ahead of BOTH the OC-trigger send (§36.3.4) and the API-runtime `run_agent_loop` dispatch (§36.3.3) — a reminder's brief IS its own text, posted verbatim via a new `fire_reminder_job`, which reuses the exact `insert_wake_turn_reply` mechanism a wake turn's own reply already uses ("write one assistant message directly into a session, emit the live-refresh chip iff open"), settling `status = 'done'` synchronously within the same tick — no async round trip. `execute_schedule_job` (`ai/tools.rs`) gains a `kind="reminder"` override requiring `run_at`, never `cron` (the inverse restriction of the existing `kind="heartbeat"` override, which requires cron) — a reminder is always one-off. **C5:** a `reminder` job's session is the one exception to `create_job`'s "fresh session every job" rule — new `find_or_create_reminders_session` looks up the calling agent's existing `origin = 'reminder'` session (scoped by `agent_id` alone, titled "Reminders") and reuses it; a second, third, Nth reminder for the same agent all land in that one session, never a new one per firing. 5 new Rust tests, each with its mutation confirmed red and reverted: removing the `scheduler_tick` short-circuit trips two independent `.expect(0)` mockito guards (an OC agent's `sessions.create`/`sessions.send` endpoints, proving zero HTTP calls); reverting `create_job`'s session-reuse branch to the unconditional `create_session_internal` call makes two reminders for the same agent land in different sessions; dropping the `kind="reminder"` cron-rejection match arm lets a cron+reminder request silently succeed. (Part of #3120)
- internal: non-image attachments (pdf/docx/txt/csv/...) are now announced to the model instead of silently invisible (#3120 PR 2, C16, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.9.3, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-30-scope-3120-pr2-recut.md`). Two sites in `ai/chat.rs`'s vision-enrichment loop (inside `ai_chat_stream`) combined to make this happen: a bare `continue` on `!mime_type.starts_with("image/")` added nothing to the per-message `content_parts` for a non-image attachment, and separately the `content_parts.len() > 1` gate deciding whether `msg.content_blocks` gets set at all was then never tripped for a non-image-only attachment — two effects of one gap, confirmed still present on main at both sites before this fix. A non-image attachment now gets a `[Attached: <filename> (id <uuid>, <size> bytes) — read with read_attachment]` text entry pushed into `content_parts` (new `build_attachment_announcement_text` helper), which alone satisfies the existing `len() > 1` gate — no separate change was needed at that second site once the first one actually produces output (confirmed, not assumed, by a test that pins the real gate expression). The filename is attacker-controllable the same way `read_attachment`'s own `source` attribute was (Matt's 2026-10-29 ruling on #3117) — entity-escaped (`&`/`<`/`>`, new `escape_attachment_label_text`) before interpolation, a second site carrying attacker-controlled filename text into model-visible output held to the same discipline. 4 new Rust tests (`ai::chat::c16_non_image_attachment_tests`), each with its mutation confirmed red and reverted: dropping the escaping leaves a raw `<script>` substring in the announcement; skipping the `content_parts` push leaves `content_blocks` at `None`. (Part of #3120)
- internal: wake and job turns actually see context, and the chat live-refreshes when they report back (#3120 PR 1, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.4.5/§36.3/§36.7.1/§36.8.1, four-PR re-cut of the cleanup-sprint issue). **C17 — wake/job turns load real session history, budgeted:** `prepare_job_dispatch` built every job/wake turn from the brief alone (the issue's own `Iteration 1 with 2 messages` log line); it now loads the dispatch target's real prior messages (the calling chat for a spawn/once job with an origin, else its own session — correct for a wake row either way, since `create_wake_job` always makes `session_id = origin_session_id`) and runs the combined set through `context_budget::apply_budget`, the same pass every interactive turn already gets — landed together, since history without a budget pass is a regression the old brief-only array never exposed. **C22 — one wake per sibling-completion batch:** a captain fanning out N `spawn_job` children produced N independent wake rows on N independent completions; fixed with a SQLite partial unique index (`idx_agent_jobs_one_pending_wake_per_session`) plus an upsert in `create_wake_job` that merges later siblings' briefs into the first pending row instead of inserting a second one — not gated behind a `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump (created idempotently at fresh-install time and unconditionally on every launch for already-migrated installs). **C18 — live refresh on wake/report-back:** a job/wake turn's reply landing in a session the user had OPEN previously showed nothing until the user navigated away and back; report-back into an open origin session and a wake turn's own reply (via new `insert_wake_turn_reply`) both now emit the existing `pane-chip-changed` `status:"inserted"` signal `ChatPanel.svelte` already re-fetches on — zero frontend changes needed. **Found and flagged, not fixed in this PR:** tracing the wake-reply path turned up that recurring/heartbeat jobs' own-session reply persistence, described in §36.8.1's existing prose, has no actual implementation anywhere in the codebase — surfaced for Reed/Matt rather than silently assumed working. 10 new Rust tests (`ai::scheduler::scheduler_v2_tests`, `migrations::tests`), each with its mutation run and reverted; 2 pre-existing tests updated for the new behavior (`migration_tests::test_all_indexes_exist`'s index count 69→70; `ai::tools::spawn_wake_chain_fix_tests_3107::test_wake_chain_climbs_and_caps_without_ever_reaching_9` needed the same claim-before-run status flip real dispatch always does, which its own direct-call harness skipped). Rust: base `f58cdc83` 2821/0/9 → head **2829/0/9** (+8, exactly the new tests). Vitest unchanged at 3264/1 skipped (no frontend files touched — C18 reused an existing listener). Analyzer (`check-turn-origin`) → `{"violations": [], "constructions_scanned": 2}`, unchanged. G1–G8 guards and spec-first gate both pass (G1–G6's report-only violations are all pre-existing, none in this diff). `SCHEMA_VERSION` unchanged at 96 (the C22 index is a deliberately non-version-gated idempotent `CREATE INDEX`). `src-gateway/` untouched; `Cargo.lock` unmoved; `crsqlite.dylib` unchanged at 1,631,456 bytes. (Part of #3120)
- internal: C22's index creation can no longer brick wake dispatch on a DB with pre-existing duplicate pending wakes (#3120 PR 1, Reed's 2026-10-30 FAIL audit of PR #3122, defect 1, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.4.5). `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` only guards against the index already existing BY NAME — a session with more than one pending `wake` row at the moment the index is (re-)created fails the `CREATE` itself (`UNIQUE constraint failed: agent_jobs.session_id`), a startup failure propagated through `run_migrations`'s `?`; from that point on, `create_wake_job`'s own `ON CONFLICT` upsert has no matching partial index to target and hard-errors on EVERY wake creation, for every session, forever — confirmed by Reed in raw SQLite and by mutation-testing the real upsert path. Matt's ruling: repair, then index. `ensure_agent_jobs_wake_dedup_index` now repairs before indexing — for every session with more than one pending wake, the oldest (by `created_at`) is kept and every other pending wake for that session is set to `status = 'cancelled'`, never deleted (history stays), before the `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` runs; a `cancelled` row can't conflict with the partial index afterward since its own `WHERE` clause only matches `status = 'pending'`. New fixture test seeds two pending wakes on one session (newer-row-first, so the test can't pass on insertion order) and proves the repair, the surviving index, and a clean `create_wake_job` upsert immediately after. Mutation (remove the repair `UPDATE`): the test's `run_migrations` call fails with the exact `UNIQUE constraint failed` error Reed reproduced. `SCHEMA_VERSION` unchanged at 96 — the repair lives inside the existing, already-unconditional `ensure_agent_jobs_wake_dedup_index`, no new migration arm. (Part of #3120)
- internal: C17's budget half is no longer defeated by a cache collision between sessions (#3120 PR 1, Reed's 2026-10-30 FAIL audit of PR #3122, defect 2, `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §27.2/§27.6/§27.8). `BudgetState.window` was one app-wide `Mutex<Option<WindowState>>` shared by every interactive session AND (new as of C17b, this same PR) every scheduler job dispatch, with continuity keyed only on the §27.5 `{system_prompt, tools_json, spatial_context, compaction_summary}` prefix hash — no session identifier anywhere in it. Job dispatch's own system prompt is invariant (`default_system_prompt()`), so a second job on a DIFFERENT session inherited the first job's §27.6 append-only bookkeeping (`target_message_count = previous_included_count + new_message_count`, a branch that does zero budget-fitting arithmetic) — Reed's probe measured a 476% context overflow this way, meaning C17 shipped the exact regression its own budget half was paired to close. Matt's ruling: session-keyed window. `window` is now a `HashMap<String, WindowState>`; the prefix-hash stability check happens inside each session's own entry. `apply_budget` gained a `session_id: &str` parameter; both call sites now pass the session they already hold — `ai_chat_stream` passes `session_id_str`, `prepare_job_dispatch` passes `history_session_id` (the same target whose history C17a just loaded). **Not job-only:** this closes the identical pre-existing collision two ordinary chat sessions with the same prompt/view state already had in `chat.rs` alone — confirmed reachable before this PR (two idle sessions, same agent, nothing open, both pass an empty `db_context` and an unchanged system prompt, landing on the same unkeyed slot) — so this is the real fix for the shared mechanism, not a job-dispatch-only patch. New test reproduces Reed's probe by name (two job dispatches, different sessions, identical invariant system prompt): job B gets its own fresh budget-fitting scan instead of inheriting job A's bookkeeping. Mutation (collapse the map key to one shared constant string): reddens with "got 40/40 included" — the exact all-messages-inherited shape of the real overflow. Rust (`cd src-tauri && PANE_TEST_ROOT=/tmp/pane-test-root-stia-head-full cargo test --lib -- --skip tests::test_backup:: --test-threads=1`): prior disclosed head (`744be044`) 2829/0/9 → this head **2831/0/9** (+2, exactly this PR's 2 new tests across both defects; `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert` failed once under full-suite load, confirmed the known load-sensitive artifact by passing clean in isolation, not a product failure). Vitest unchanged at 3264 passed/1 skipped (zero frontend files in this diff). (Part of #3120)

## [1.0.69] - 2026-10-30
### Added
- Captain & Crew UI — the New Session flow gets a sheet, and sessions get a visible, editable crew (#3050 PR 10, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.17.4, **last PR of the sprint**). PR 5 landed the `crew_agent_ids` column, the `spawn_job` crew gate, self-spawn refusal, and "no crew ⇒ `spawn_job` not offered" — but nothing wrote the column and nothing on the frontend could read it (Reed's scope audit: zero `UPDATE`s, zero frontend-visible `Session.crew_agent_ids`); this PR owns both the read and the write.
  - **New Session sheet** (`NewSessionSheet.svelte`) replaces the old 280px split-control popover (`AgentPickerPopover.svelte`, now deleted — `AgentPickerRows.svelte` stays, still used by the New Project dialog) at **both** its call sites — the session header's "New Session" button and the Home drawer's "New Session" button both open the exact same 620px sheet with a scrim (Matt's Ruling 1: "one component; no second layout"). Captain list grouped by provider, search filters both the captain list and the crew pool unconditionally (Ruling 3 — the design README's "past about 12 agents" was prose, not a real threshold: there is no agent-count gate anywhere in this build), DEFAULT agent pre-selected, Start always enabled. Crew (optional): every other API agent, tap to add, hidden entirely (not just visually) when the captain is an OpenClaw agent and replaced by a one-line "brings its own crew from the gateway" note — OpenClaw agents bring their own crew and are never themselves crewable. Chip area caps at the design's real pinned value, `max-height:102px` (not a computed "three rows"). Footer reads back the exact choice: "Astro · works alone", "Astro + 2 crew", or "Brit Freed · own crew" — three distinct strings, not a generic template.
  - **Drawer rows and the session header** now show the crew: a 22px captain chip with a 1px teal ring (1.5px gap) followed by up to three 18px unringed crew chips, then a "+N" overflow chip with the full crew list in the tooltip. The header's crew cluster is a button that opens the new edit-crew popover; "+ Crew" renders muted when there's no crew yet; an OpenClaw captain's header shows plain, non-clickable "own crew" text.
  - **Edit-crew popover** (`EditCrewPopover.svelte`, new) — captain shown locked ("Captain · can't be changed", no toggle affordance of any kind), crew chips toggle add/remove against the full API-agent-minus-captain pool, "Applies to the next job `<Captain>` hands off. Running jobs keep their agent.", Save crew. That guarantee is structural, not a new runtime check: no code path in this codebase has ever `UPDATE`d `agent_jobs.agent_id`, and `execute_spawn_job` already re-reads `crew_agent_ids` fresh from the DB on every dispatch — so the moment the write path below exists, the very next handoff picks up an edit for free.
  - **Settings → Agents** gains a helper line ("Any agent can be a captain (runs a session) or crew (takes jobs from a captain)"), and the "Main" badge on the default agent is renamed to **DEFAULT CAPTAIN** (Matt's Ruling 2) — read from one new shared constant (`DEFAULT_CAPTAIN_LABEL`, `$lib/constants.ts`) so the Settings badge and the sheet's own captain-list chip can never drift apart by hardcoding the string twice.
  - **Backend:** `Session` gains `crew_agent_ids: Option<String>` (raw JSON text, matching this file's existing `tool_calls`/`tool_results` convention — parsed once on the frontend, `parseCrewAgentIds`). `list_sessions` and `load_session_by_id` (which `switch_session`/`get_active_session` already called) now share one `SESSION_SELECT_COLUMNS` constant and one `session_from_row` mapper, closing the #3104-shaped "two queries over the same data drift" risk Reed's scope audit named — there is now exactly one column list to extend, not several to keep in sync. Two new commands: `create_session_with_crew` (additive sibling of `create_session` — zero signature change on the original 6-call-site command; forces `crew_agent_ids = NULL` for an OpenClaw captain even if the caller sends one) and `update_session_crew` (the first-ever production `UPDATE chat_sessions SET crew_agent_ids` — touches nothing else, in particular never `agent_jobs`).
  - 5 new Rust tests (`ai::chat::crew_rw_tests_3050_pr10`) plus 15+ new/updated Vitest files across the New Session sheet, drawer rows, header, edit popover, and Settings — every guard mutation-run and reverted (OC-captain crew suppression, empty-crew→NULL normalization, the shared-column-list drift proof, the running-job-untouched proof, the three-exact-footer-strings proof, the no-threshold search proof). (Part of #3050)
- `read_attachment` — agents can now read the text content of a file dropped into chat: md/txt/csv/json as UTF-8, PDF's text layer (new `pdf-extract` dependency, pure Rust, MIT), and docx's `document.xml` text, paragraphs joined by newline (`zip` + `quick-xml`, both already resolved transitively — zero new dependencies there) (#3050 PR 9, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.9.3, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-29-scope-3050-pr9-attachments.md`). Resolved by `attachment_id` or by `filename` (scoped to the session's project, or the Home `"__global__"` scope for a Home chat — the same sentinel every Home attachment write already uses); an ambiguous filename (more than one attachment with that name in the project) returns every match (id, size, created-at) instead of silently picking one. Capped at **60,000 characters, char-indexed** (`.chars().take(n)`, #3111's own precedent — not byte-indexed, which can panic or miscount on multi-byte UTF-8 content straddling the boundary), with a trailing `[truncated: N of M characters]` marker. Extracted text enters the model inside the same §4.6.1 untrusted-content delimiters `web_fetch` uses (`ai::web::wrap_untrusted`, factored out of `wrap_external_content` and reused verbatim rather than reimplemented — `source="attachment:{filename}"`) and sets the same §4.6.3 taint: `MUTATE_EXISTING_TOOLS` is withheld for the rest of the turn after a successful read, exactly as after a web fetch — "a dropped PDF is external content." The taint mechanism (`web_tainted`/`check_web_taint`) is renamed to `external_content_tainted`/`check_external_content_taint` for honesty: it was always generic over the bool and tool name, but the old name specifically said "web," which became a mild lie once a local file read also trips it; the refusal text moved from "after web content was fetched" to "after untrusted external content was read." **Images are deferred** (Matt's ruling: the spec's cited "`ModelInfo` capability from #3075" doesn't exist — #3075 added Venice TEE/E2EE fields, nothing about vision, and no provider's model-list endpoint carries a live modality signal cheaply enough to gate this honestly today; separately, `content_blocks` — the wire shape an image part needs — is read by `openrouter.rs` only, never `anthropic.rs`/`ollama.rs`) — an image attachment still stores and attaches normally everywhere else; `read_attachment` on one returns exactly `"Image attachment; image reading isn't available yet."`, no hardcoded model list, no silent drop. `read_attachment`'s own "Tools used" line always shows `read_attachment(<filename>)`, never the extracted content, success or failure alike. Offered to API runtimes only — the web-tool allowlist's sibling, zero new gating mechanism (OC agents have their own file access, §36.0.1). 20 new Rust tests across `attachments.rs`/`ai/chat.rs`/`ai/tools.rs`, each with its mutation confirmed red and reverted (byte-indexed truncation panicking/miscounting on a multi-byte-straddling fixture; a `LIMIT 1` ambiguity-lookup silently hiding the second match; a wrong XML tag silently emptying docx extraction; a stubbed-out PDF extractor; a missing taint-set leaving the next-iteration `edit_note` wrongly permitted; `read_attachment` pushed unconditionally outside the `web_tools_offered` guard). (Part of #3050)
- internal: chat composer gains the file-picker upload path, closing the one real gap between chat's attachment flow and notes' three upload paths (#3050 PR 9, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.9.2). `ChatPanel.svelte` gets a new toolbar button (`handleAttachFilePicker`, placed beside the message textarea) that mirrors `Editor.svelte::handleToolbarAttachFile` almost verbatim: `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog`'s `open({multiple: true})`, then `api.copyAttachmentFromPath` per selected path — same native `fs::copy` path notes' own picker already uses (1 GB cap, no 50 MB client-side base64 cap, since it bypasses the `FileReader` pipeline entirely). Zero new Cargo/capability/plugin work — both prerequisites (`tauri-plugin-dialog`, `dialog:default` capability) were already present for notes. Cancelling the native dialog (`open()` resolving `null`) is a no-op. 3 new Vitest tests (mutation: swapped the handler for a no-op — all three reddened, confirmed and reverted).
- internal: Home attachment storage redirected to `~/Pane/Home/Assets/`, step 1 of chat attachments (#3050 PR 9, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.9.2, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-29-scope-3050-pr9-attachments.md`). A new `PaneRoot::Home` variant (`filesystem_policy.rs`) plus `attachments.rs::home_attachment_location()` (parallel to the existing `project_attachment_location()`) give the Home chat sentinel (`project_id == "__global__"`) its own fixed `Home/Assets/{id}.{ext}` tree — `attachment_location()` now checks for that sentinel BEFORE falling through to the legacy `.pane/attachments/__global__/` leaf every prior Home attachment used. **No migration**: a file already written at the old legacy path keeps resolving there forever — `attachment_location_candidates()`'s existing historical-fallback chain (the same mechanism that absorbed #1775's `.pane/attachments → Projects/{name}/Assets` migration) already tries the legacy leaf as a candidate after the new preferred Home location, so this needed zero changes to the read-side resolver, only the write-time one. Four pre-existing tests that asserted the OLD legacy write-time path for `"__global__"` are updated to assert the new Home path (per Reed's scope audit §2: "must be updated, not just left to rot"); a new test seeds a real file at the OLD legacy path on disk and proves `resolve_attachment_path_by_id` (the real production read path, not a test mimic) still finds it. **Regression catch (Reed's scope audit, "Blast radius"):** the file watcher's `Assets/`-subdir skip-check (`watcher.rs::should_skip`, fixed for #1824 to recognize only `Projects/{name}/Assets/`) did not recognize the new `Home/Assets/` tree at all — a `.md`/`.txt` dropped into Home chat would have been picked up by the recursive watcher and double-ingested as a phantom note. New sibling `is_home_assets_subdir()` check, OR'd into `should_skip` — simpler than the Projects case since "Home" is a reserved top-level name, never a user-nameable project slot, so there's no #1824-style name-collision ambiguity to resolve. 6 new/updated Rust tests, each with its mutation (reverting the new redirect branch, the watcher's new OR-disjunct, or the candidate chain's legacy fallback — all confirmed red, see PR report). (Part of #3050)
- Home now has a Scheduled panel — a fixed 352px column on the left, every job except spawns across every project, at every window width (#3050 PR 8, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.8/§36.3.6/§36.2.2). Always docked, no toggle, no overlay — when the left nav rail opens, the chat column narrows; the panel never moves or resizes (same flex-row-sibling mechanism `SessionsDrawer.svelte` already established, mirrored onto the left). Two tabs driven by `status` (Active: pending/running/sent/paused; Done: done/failed/stopped/cancelled), one flat sorted list in Active (failed-and-missed first, then by next run, paused last), a fifth row state ("Active" — a healthy, waiting schedule gets a neutral pill with a green dot) alongside running/missed/failed/paused. Inline Run now (disabled mid-run), Pause/Resume, and Delete (asks for confirmation, keeps the session's history — it's `cancel_job` under a different label, never a hard delete) are always visible. Clicking a row opens that schedule's session through the exact same frontend path a notification's click-to-open already uses (`switch_session`, PR 6's origin-guarded `demote_and_promote` — the active chat is never demoted). Preset cards (New schedule, Check-in, Morning brief, Weekly review, Custom) create a job through the SAME path the `schedule_job` AI tool uses — same confirmation chip, same session, same status flips, not reimplemented; "Check-in" is the heartbeat preset (a recurring job whose brief defaults to the check-in text — not a per-agent setting), and a second Check-in for an agent that already has one gets a friendly refusal, not a raw SQL error. One-off jobs show an "Once" tag. New backend commands: `list_scheduled_jobs` (the panel's one query — every `agent_jobs` row except `kind='spawn'`, LEFT JOIN projects with a "Home" fallback), `run_job_now` (makes a pending/paused row eligible for the next real scheduler tick, never bypassing `claim_due_jobs`), and thin pass-through wrappers for pause/resume/delete/create so the panel and the AI tools can never silently diverge. Settings → AI gained a "Concurrent jobs" row beside the overall job ceiling (`ai_settings.job_concurrency` already existed and was already read by the scheduler — only the UI row is new). Times render in 24-hour `HH:MM` (Matt's override of the design sheet's 12-hour rendering, matching the chips' existing precedent). **`agent_jobs.status = 'stopped'` is now actually written** (Matt's ruling): a job-bound turn the user stops via the Stop button used to fall through to `'done'`, indistinguishable from a real success — `JobOutcome` gained a third variant, and the Done tab's `stopped` filter arm, specced since before this panel existed, now actually matches a row. (Part of #3050)
- internal: background OpenClaw pickup replaces the frontend's focus-gated poll (#3050 PR 7, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.6, `docs/audits/2026-10-29-scope-3050-pr7-background-pickup.md`). §30.11.4's three-gate 60s poll (session open + app focused + OC-bound, `ChatSidebar.svelte`'s `eligible` boolean, ~160 lines) is deleted — superseded by `ai::scheduler::run_oc_background_pickup`, called from `scheduler_tick` as its own independent step. Every OC-bound session (interactive and job sessions alike, open or not, focused or not — Pane being open is the only requirement) is now pulled on the scheduler's own tick, up to 20 sessions per tick via a process-lifetime rotating page counter (so sessions ranked 21+ are reached within a bounded number of ticks instead of starving forever behind a pure recency sort), each pull spawned concurrently with a 10s timeout wrapper. A job session's real OC session key (the `dashboard:...` string OC returned at bootstrap, `agent_jobs.oc_session_key`) is now used verbatim instead of the derived `pane-{session_id}` formula, which targeted a session OC never created. The eligibility query gains an `OR agent_jobs.updated_at` clause so a long-lived recurring/heartbeat job (whose `chat_sessions.last_active_at` is frozen at creation) doesn't silently drop out of pickup 7 days after creation. A message ingested into a session that isn't the one currently open now raises the previously-unwired `agent_message` notification (§36.7's second trigger — PR 6 only ever wired the report-back half); into the open session, it appends and fires a new `pane-oc-message-ingested` event instead, since nothing told the open chat a row had landed once the frontend stopped driving its own reload. Echo suppression moves into the backend as per-session state (Matt's ruling): no `suppress_ingest` parameter crosses the Tauri boundary anymore — `ai::chat::TurnInFlightGuard` (RAII) marks a session's turn in flight at dispatch time and clears on `Drop`, including on a panic/crash, so a crashed loop can never leave pickup stuck off for that session. 20 new Rust tests plus the deletion of 11 Vitest tests covering the removed mechanism (replaced by backend-side coverage); every guard mutation-confirmed red (see PR report). (Part of #3050)

- internal: Reed's PR #3115 audit §7 gap closed — `pane-oc-message-ingested` (§36.6, #3050 PR 7) shipped with a real listener (`ChatSidebar.svelte`) but no frontend pin, the mirror image of PR 6's own emit-with-no-listener miss. New `ChatSidebar.ocMessageIngested.test.ts` (3 tests, `listenersByEvent` capture-and-fire pattern already established by `ChatPanel.chipListener.test.ts`): the listener registers on mount; an event for the OPEN session reloads its transcript (`api.getChatMessages`, proxying the non-exported `loadMessages`); an event for a DIFFERENT session does not. Mutation (removing the listener registration block) reddens all three, confirmed live and restored. Also closed the matching spec/code divergence the same audit named (the sixth found this sprint by direct count, not the seventh): `RUNTIME_OC_PICKUP_WINDOW_DAYS`/`RUNTIME_OC_PICKUP_SESSIONS_PER_TICK` were promised in `runtime_constants.rs`'s own header comment and already correct in `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.10A's table, but the code used an inline `chrono::Duration::days(7)` and a private, differently-named `scheduler.rs::OC_PICKUP_SESSIONS_PER_TICK` instead — both now real `runtime_constants.rs` consts (1 site each replaced; the pre-existing `OC_PICKUP_SESSIONS_PER_TICK` identifier at 6 other call/doc sites now resolves to the imported, correctly-named constant). Separately, `OC_PICKUP_TICK_COUNTER`'s rotating-page cursor now seeds from a random `u64` (`rand::random::<u64>()`, the same crate/pattern `ai::chat::compute_backoff_interval_ms`'s jitter already uses) instead of a fixed 0 on first access — Matt's one-line bar for the restart-starves-the-tail gap (a full `ai_settings`-persisted cursor was explicitly out of scope; left for a later PR, not built here). `test_rotation_25_eligible_20_this_tick_5_next_not_a_reroll` (pre-existing, #3050 PR 7) hard-coded that the FIRST of two consecutive ticks takes the 20-page — true only when the counter starts at 0 — and had to be loosened to assert the pair is a 20/5 split in either order, still disjoint, still reddening on the same originally-named mutation (remove the rotation counter entirely). Rust 2767/0/9 (lib, unchanged total; the known base failure resolved to a pass, not relabeled — the `crsql_internal_sync_bit` artifact didn't reproduce in this isolated target dir this run); Vitest 3151/1 skipped (+3, exactly the new tests). (Part of #3050)

- internal: composer Send/Stop toggle (#3050 PR 6, Ruling 4's composer sentence, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.2.3). The composer was Enter-only before this PR — zero buttons while idle, Stop popping in and out of an otherwise-empty composer while streaming (the live-test's "floating button" note: not a CSS positioning bug, a UX one — a single button that appears/disappears in an otherwise-empty composer reads as detached chrome). `ChatPanel.svelte`'s `.input-area` now renders ONE button in that slot, toggling on `isStreaming`: idle → "Send" (new; `onclick={sendMessage}`, same function the pre-existing Enter-to-send `handleKeyDown` path already calls — parity, not a second send mechanism; disabled when there's nothing to send, same guard `sendMessage()`'s own early-return already enforces), streaming → "Stop" (unchanged from PR 3). Shared `.composer-action-btn` base CSS; `.send-btn`/`.stop-turn-btn` swap color only. Five Vitest tests (mutation: confirmed red, see PR report): Send shows when idle (new); Stop shows when streaming (regression pin); clicking Send submits the composer's text; Send is disabled when empty; clicking Stop still calls `onStop` (regression pin). Full Vitest suite re-run clean (3145 passed). (Part of #3050)

- internal: Stop now aborts the in-flight provider stream, not only the between-iteration cancel checks (#3050 PR 6, Ruling 4, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.2.3). Root cause (live test #1, Reed's audit): `run_agent_loop`'s two existing checkpoints (top-of-iteration, before-each-tool-call) are unreachable while a response is streaming — for an OC turn, that's the ENTIRE turn, so `[STOP-TURN] cancel flag set` fired while the turn ran to completion anyway. `stream_openrouter`/`stream_openrouter_inner` (`ai/openrouter.rs`) gain a `cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>` parameter, checked once per received SSE chunk; on a hit, the loop `break`s (dropping the still-unconsumed `reqwest` response body — how `reqwest` aborts an in-flight HTTP request) and returns `Err(("Cancelled by Stop", full_text accumulated so far))` — the SAME `(error, partial_text)` channel a mid-stream network error already used, reused unchanged. **Free win:** this function also serves plain `OpenRouter` and `Venice` dispatch, so Stop-mid-stream is fixed for those providers too, not only OC (`Anthropic`/`Ollama` have their own separate streaming loops with the same latent gap — untouched, named as a fast-follow candidate). All 16 production call sites in `ai/chat.rs` (main dispatch match, smart-route retry branch, primary-provider fallback branch) thread the turn's own real per-session `cancel` handle through — never a fresh `Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false))`. `run_agent_loop`'s `Err((e, stream_partial))` arm checks `cancel` BEFORE the OC-reconnect-retry branch (by the flag, never by string-matching `e`) — a Stop must never reconnect a stream the user asked to end, and must render "Stopped by you after N tool calls," never the provider-error copy. Two tests, each with its mutation (confirmed red, see PR report): a direct `stream_openrouter` test with a two-chunk, real-delay mock body proves chunk 2 is never consumed once `cancel` flips in the gap (mutation: remove the in-loop check → reddens, full text returned); an end-to-end `run_agent_loop` OC-path test proves `JobOutcome::Done` (never `Failed`), partial text preserved, text-after-cancel absent, and the mock's `.expect(1)` proves no reconnect attempt fired (mutation: revert one call site to a fresh `AtomicBool` → reddens only that test, isolating the missed site). (Part of #3050)

- internal: click-to-open for `agent_message`/`job_failed` notifications (#3050 PR 6, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.7). `NotificationPanel.svelte`'s click router gains its first `target_kind = 'session'` arm — opens the project (or Home) and lands on `target_id` as the active session. Safe for a job-origin (hidden spawn/schedule) session because `switchSession`'s backend guard (the prior commit's Ruling 2) resolves and returns it WITHOUT promoting it or demoting the project's real active session — no dead click, no destructive click. `navigateTo` (`navigation.ts`) gains a `sessionId` override: when present, thread resolution routes through `api.switchSession(sessionId)` instead of the default `getActiveSession(projectId)` ("open this exact session," not "open whatever this project's active session happens to be") — a general mechanism, reusable by a future caller, not a one-off hack in the panel. Two Vitest tests: `sessionId` present routes through `switchSession`, never `getActiveSession` (mutation: revert STEP 3 to always call `getActiveSession` → reddens); `sessionId` absent is unchanged (regression pin). `userReachableViews.derived.test.ts`'s `'kanban'` citation-count test updated from 2 to 3 real call sites (a genuinely new, correct reachable path, not a bug). (Part of #3050)

- internal: `agent_message`/`job_failed` notifications and the new `pane-chip-changed` live-refresh event (#3050 PR 6, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.7/§36.7.1, `docs/audits/2026-10-29-scope-3050-pr6-notifications.md`). Two new notification `type` string values (NOT a Rust enum — see Ruling 5 below), reusing the existing `notifications` table/`process_notification` surface as-is: `agent_message` fires when a job session's report-back (§36.8) or an OC background-pickup message lands in a session that is not open; `job_failed` fires per Ruling 1's streak rule below. New `ai::chat::is_session_open`/`set_viewing_session` — the "is the user currently looking at this session" predicate didn't exist anywhere before this PR (`is_active` is a per-surface "last shown" pointer, not "on screen right now"); a process-wide `OnceLock<Mutex<Option<String>>>` tracker (same shape as the existing `CANCEL_FLAGS`), written by the frontend on every navigate/switch and chat-view teardown.

  **Ruling 1 (Matt, 2026-10-29) — `job_failed`: one notification per failure streak, updated in place.** First failure creates the row ("Tick failed · 1 of 3 — {error}"); each further failure in the same streak updates that same row ("2 of 3", then the 3-strike flip's "Tick stopped after 3 failures"); a success ends the streak, the next failure starts a new row. Keyed on `job_id` + the streak's first `last_failed_at` — `agent_jobs.last_failed_at` is now written ONLY on a streak's first failure (left unchanged on subsequent failures in the same streak) and cleared to `NULL` on success, so the `idem_key` stays stable across a streak's calls. New `notifications.rs::emit_or_update_job_failed_notification` — a real UPSERT (SELECT-then-UPDATE-or-INSERT), unlike every other notification type's plain dedup-skip. `once`/`spawn` jobs use the same function with a singleton key (no streak concept — the one failure IS the terminal exit). Three tests: three consecutive failures → one row, three updates; failure/success/failure → two rows; different `streak_started_at` values always yield different `idem_key`s (mutation: drop `streak_started_at` from the key → the two-row test collapses to one).

  **`pane-chip-changed`** — a second, deliberately separate event from `pane-notification` (§36.7.1): `pane-data-changed`'s `entity_type`/`reason` enums are both closed by existing tests and don't fit a chat-message chip's shape. Payload `{ job_id, session_id, status: "inserted" | "sent" | "done" | "failed" }`. Emitted from `insert_schedule_confirmation_message` (covers both `schedule_job` and `spawn_job`'s chips — one shared insert function) and at every `sent`/`done`/`failed` status write in `ai::scheduler` (OC once/spawn terminal, OC recurring/heartbeat per-failure AND the 3-strike flip, API-runtime terminal). Four tests, each with its own mutation (drop that specific emit call → only that sub-case reddens): insert via `schedule_job`; insert via `spawn_job`; a terminal status flip; a mid-recurring-failure (non-terminal) flip.

  **Ruling 5 (Matt, 2026-10-29) — fixed the docs, didn't build an enum.** `docs/INVARIANTS.md` §19 and `notifications.md` §19.2 both asserted a `NotificationType` Rust enum that has never existed (`grep -rn "NotificationType" src-tauri/src/` — zero hits; every existing type, `task_due` through this PR's two new ones, is a plain `&str`). Both documents corrected to describe the actual pattern (named `&str` constants, `refresh_event.rs`'s precedent) — fifth spec/code divergence this sprint, same discipline as §36.11/Ruling 1: the prose gets corrected, not left to mislead the next reader. No enum built.

  **Dead-click risk, closed by the prior commit:** the panel's new `target_kind='session'` click arm resolves/displays a job-origin session via the SAME `switch_session` command normal sessions use — safe because `demote_and_promote` (prior commit, Ruling 2) already no-ops the demote/promote mutation for `origin IN ('spawn', 'schedule')` targets. (Part of #3050)

### Fixed
- internal: two gaps Matt wanted closed before merging #3117 (#3050 PR 9), per Reed's PASS audit of PR #3117 (`~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-29-pr-3117-attachments.md` §2/§5): "The delimiter gap sits inside the containment mechanism itself; we don't merge a known hole in it, and a fix between PRs is the in-between we don't do."

  **1. `read_attachment`'s §4.6.1 `source` attribute no longer carries raw, unsanitized filename text.** The prior shape built `source="attachment:{filename}"` with zero escaping — `wrap_untrusted` does none of its own, by design (every caller must hand it an already-safe string) — so a filename containing a quote, a literal `>>>`, or a forged `<<<END_EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT>>>`/`<<<EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT source="...">>>` pair could break out of the attribute, a prompt-injection surface sitting inside the very mechanism meant to contain untrusted text. **Chosen fix (the preferred of Matt's two options): the attribute now carries the attachment's own UUID** (`source="attachment:{attachment_id}"`) — structurally safe, no user input reaches it, nothing to escape, no attribute shape to keep revisiting as the delimiter convention evolves — and the filename moves INSIDE the untrusted block, labeled `Filename: {filename}` ahead of the content: still visible to the model, just as contained data rather than trusted metadata. New shared helper `ai::web::wrap_read_attachment_content` is now the one production call site (`ai/chat.rs`'s read_attachment branch) AND the one the regression test drives directly — no inline-mirrored reconstruction. New `test_read_attachment_forged_delimiter_filename_stays_inside_block` proves a crafted filename containing exactly that forged pair lands strictly between the real (UUID-keyed) open delimiter and the real (final) close delimiter; mutation (reverting the helper to key the attribute on `filename` again) reddens it immediately, reproducing the break-out verbatim in the failure output. **`web_fetch`'s own `source` (the URL) checked for the same shape and found NOT exposed, no code change needed:** it is always `url::Url::parse(..).to_string()` (`net_guard::parse_and_check_scheme`, re-run on every redirect hop including a malicious server's own `Location` header), and the WHATWG URL Standard's path/query/fragment percent-encode sets (implemented by the `url` crate) always percent-encode `"`/`<`/`>` and strip bare CR/LF before parsing — pinned directly by new `test_url_crate_percent_encodes_delimiter_chars_before_reaching_wrap_untrusted` (no mutation: this pins third-party `url`-crate behavior, not a first-party conditional — there is no branch of ours to flip red/green here, said plainly rather than inventing one). A second new test, `test_wrap_untrusted_does_no_escaping_of_its_own`, pins that `wrap_untrusted` itself remains a dumb, zero-escaping formatter — both callers are responsible for handing it an already-safe `source` — so a future "helpful" escaping pass inside it can't silently double-escape either caller without showing as a diff here.

  **2. `read_attachment` by `attachment_id` is now scoped to the session's project — same shape as PR 4's `list_jobs(scope='all')` leak.** `resolve_attachment_for_read` took `session_project_id` but only applied it to the `filename` branch; the by-id branch resolved globally with no project check at all, so a session in project A could read project B's attachment by id if it ever learned the UUID. Pause/Delete on a **running** row in the Home Scheduled panel used to be a flat, disabled refusal — the API-runtime job dispatch's own cancel flag was a permanently-false throwaway, never wired to anything the loop actually read ("this job turn simply can never be cancelled," the exact comment this PR deletes). - internal: CI's `rust-tests` was red on PR #3114 (`feat/3050-pr6-notifications`), both heads, both runs, five `ai::scheduler::scheduler_v2_tests` tests — `test_scheduler_tick_dispatches_missed_oc_job_exactly_once`, `test_spawn_finish_wakes_origin_with_one_proactive_turn`, `test_spawn_job_report_back_lands_in_origin_session_attributed_and_tagged`, `test_wake_false_report_only_no_wake_row`, `test_wake_row_propagates_chain_depth_and_root` — plus one latent case, `test_oc_bound_origin_skips_wake`, found while fixing the other five (Reed's diagnosis, `docs/audits/2026-10-29-diagnose-3114-scheduler-flakes.md`). **Root cause: a test synchronization defect, not a production race.** All six (PR 5, unchanged by PR 6's own diff — `git diff 565c4f7e..8309e5e68c -- src-tauri/src/ai/scheduler.rs` shows zero changed lines inside any of their bodies) raced a detached `tauri::async_runtime::spawn`'d dispatch task using a fixed `tokio::time::sleep(200/300ms)` as a stand-in for "the spawned task finished," instead of an actual completion signal — a margin that was already thin on `main` and that PR 6's new, synchronous `emit_chip_changed` calls inline in the same dispatch hot path narrowed further, tipping it on CI's hardware (consistently, not flakily — same 5 names, same assertion shapes, both audited heads). All five failing assertions are "zero/absent" shapes (a mock never hit, a DB row never written, a `SELECT` returning `QueryReturnedNoRows`) — the signature of waiting too little, never of a wrong value. `test_oc_bound_origin_skips_wake` wasn't failing, but only because its own assertion is an absence check (`wake_count == 0`) that a too-short wait satisfies for the wrong reason (nothing had run yet, not "wake was correctly skipped") — the same defect shape, just not yet caught by a positive assertion.

  **Fix: all six fixed sleeps replaced with a shared bounded poll-retry helper**, `poll_until(condition, timeout_msg)` — polls the real condition (mockito's `mock.matched_async()`, or the actual DB row/count the test cares about) every **25ms** up to a **20s** ceiling, returning the instant it's true instead of waiting out a guessed duration regardless; on timeout it panics with the test's own original assertion message, so a genuinely-broken test still fails the same way it always did, just without a false negative from CI-host jitter. 25ms keeps the common case (well under the old 200/300ms margins) resolving in a handful of polls, not a perceptible slowdown. **The 20s ceiling was tuned against live CI evidence, not guessed once and left:** a first attempt at 5s (an order-of-magnitude reasoned purely from the assertion shapes) was pushed, watched, and caught its OWN timeout panic on a live CI run — `test_scheduler_tick_dispatches_missed_oc_job_exactly_once` hit the 5s ceiling and failed on the retrigger run, not any of the other five. That run's own full-suite timing (165.75s CI vs. 114.8s local for the identical 2758 tests) showed CI running at best ~1.4x local speed on average — but this is the cluster's first test to touch `tauri::async_runtime`/mockito at all, so it also absorbs whatever one-time runtime/thread-pool/socket warm-up cost exists on a loaded shared runner, a cold-start spike a flat local-to-CI multiplier doesn't capture. 20s is still bounded (a genuinely broken dispatch fails in well under a minute, never hangs) while giving roughly 4x the headroom the empirically-wrong 5s figure had. For the two absence-assertion tests (`test_wake_false_report_only_no_wake_row`, `test_oc_bound_origin_skips_wake`), the poll waits on the test's own positive completion signal (the report-back row) FIRST, so the "zero wake rows" check that follows means what it says instead of passing on a technicality. Zero production code touched — `git diff --name-only` for this commit shows only `src-tauri/src/ai/scheduler.rs` (test module only) and `CHANGELOG.md`. Verified: all 52 `scheduler_v2_tests` pass locally (`--test-threads=1`); full Rust suite **2747 passed, 0 failed** (unchanged); full Vitest suite **3159 passed, 1 skipped** (unchanged); analyzer (`check-turn-origin`) → `{"violations": [], "constructions_scanned": 2}` (unchanged — no `TurnOrigin` constructions); `src-gateway/` untouched; `SCHEMA_VERSION` unchanged at 96, no migration; `crsqlite.dylib` unchanged at 1,631,456 bytes; no lockfile touched. Demonstrated on CI directly (not just locally — these tests pass locally and fail on CI, which is the whole reason a local-only green run isn't evidence here): see PR #3114 for the three consecutive CI run IDs. (Part of #3050)
