## [1.0.68] - 2026-10-28
### Fixed
- internal: `jobStatusChip.ts:56`'s merged `case 'done': case 'sent':` switch arm rendered a `sent` job (Pane's own transport call succeeded) identically to a `done` job (OC actually replied, via §36.6 pickup) — "done in 0s" for a job that had only just been sent, never actually completed. **Split the two cases:** `'sent'` now renders `' · sent'` (no elapsed-time claim — Pane cannot know how long OC will take to reply); `'done'` keeps the existing `elapsedSeconds`-based "done in Xs" text, unchanged. Also wired `get_job_status`'s existing read to include `agent_jobs.last_error` (new field on the already-returned JSON, no new column), and `chipStatusSuffix`'s `'pending'` arm now renders `' · last run failed'` when `last_error` is non-NULL — the frontend half of Ruling 3's recurring/heartbeat failure visibility above; no new live-refresh mechanism needed since the chip's existing 5-second poll (`ChatPanel.svelte`) already re-reads every non-terminal `job_id` in view, and `'pending'` is non-terminal by construction. **Deferred, named explicitly, not built here:** chat's own lack of a live-refresh-on-new-message mechanism (item 4a) — `pane-data-changed`'s `entity_type` enum is spec-closed at five values and chat messages aren't one; building a sixth value or inventing a second event here would duplicate work PR 6 already owns. Four tests, each named with its mutation: `sent` renders `' · sent'`, never "done in Ns" (mutation: revert to the merged switch arm → reddens, reproducing the exact historical bug — confirmed live, see PR report); `done` with real timing is unchanged by the split (regression pin); a pending job with `last_error` renders `' · last run failed'` (mutation: drop the `last_error` check → reddens, confirmed live); a pending job with no `last_error` stays empty. (Part of #3050)

- internal: live-test #1b — five early pre-flight `return;` sites in `ai::scheduler::dispatch_oc_job` (brief-insert lock failure, gateway-context-resolution lock failure, `resolve_oc_gateway_context` returning `Ok(None)` or `Err`, `build_gateway_client_with_cert` failing) bailed out before the finalize block ever ran, leaving `once`/`spawn` jobs stuck at `status='running'` FOREVER (`claim_job` sets `'running'`; `claim_due_jobs`'s own SELECT only ever re-picks up `'pending'` rows — nothing ever re-selects a stuck `'running'` row). **Matt's ruling: no path may leave a once/spawn job at `running`.** All five sites now produce `Err(String)` into the SAME `dispatch_result` chain the bootstrap/send calls already populated, reaching the one shared finalize block instead of bailing before it. **Mutation run on the shared finalizer itself** (not five separate per-branch mutations): breaking the finalize block's `UPDATE agent_jobs SET status = ?1, ...` write reddened `test_oc_job_missing_gateway_context_does_not_panic` (this PR's newly-folded-in pre-flight-return class) AND the pre-existing `test_oc_job_sessions_create_failure_records_failed_no_send`/`test_oc_job_non_2xx_response_records_failed_with_last_error`/`test_oc_job_network_error_on_send_records_failed_with_last_error` (the already-existing bootstrap/send class) simultaneously — proving the finalize path is genuinely shared/load-bearing across both classes, not two independently-correct paths that happen to look alike. The `Ok(None)`-arm's existing test (`test_oc_job_missing_gateway_context_does_not_panic`) was updated from its old pre-fix assertion (`status == "running"`, "left as-is for manual recovery") to the new unconditional outcome (`status == "failed"`, `last_error` populated) — a deliberate design choice this ruling overrides, not silently left pinning the old bug. One site — a DB lock failing at the very last step, inside the finalize block itself — remains structurally unfixable (if that lock fails, no further `conn.execute` can run either way) and is a named, accepted residual risk requiring actual `Mutex` poisoning. (Part of #3050)

- internal: Ruling 3 (Matt, live-test #1b fix PR) — a `recurring`/`heartbeat` OC job's transport failure (`sessions.create`/`sessions.send`) was recorded NOWHERE: `status` returns to `'pending'` unconditionally (by design, self-heals at the next scheduled firing) and the finalize block skipped these kinds entirely, so a failing heartbeat looked identical to a healthy one from the DB's own state. **Record it, keep recurring:** `ai::scheduler::dispatch_oc_job` now sets `last_error`/`last_failed_at` and increments `consecutive_failures` on a transport failure for these kinds (`next_run_at` was already advancing exactly as a success would — that was never the bug); **a success resets the counter to zero and clears `last_error`**; **only at 3 consecutive failures does `status` flip to a terminal `'failed'`** (a dead gateway shouldn't spam forever; one blip shouldn't kill a heartbeat). New columns `agent_jobs.consecutive_failures` (INTEGER DEFAULT 0) / `agent_jobs.last_failed_at` (TEXT, nullable) — migration v95 → v96 (`migrate_v96`), plus `tests/fixtures/upgrade-from-v95.db` for the upgrade-fixture gate. `docs/spec/runtime.md`'s Ruling 1 text amended (it implied the recompute waits on the send's outcome — it never did, and still doesn't; this amendment documents the failure-policy mechanism Ruling 3 adds on top). **Three tests, each named with its mutation:** one failure → still `'pending'` with `next_run_at` advanced and `last_error` set (mutation: drop the failure-recording write → reddens, failure becomes invisible again); three consecutive failures → `'failed'` (mutation: raise the strike threshold → reddens, stays `'pending'` after the third); success after two failures → counter resets to zero (mutation: drop the success-arm's reset write → reddens, counter stays at 2). (Part of #3050)

- internal: Item 3 (live-test #1b fix PR) — both `ensure_oc_session_bootstrapped` (`sessions.create`) and `dispatch_oc_job`'s send block (`sessions.send`) logged only the HTTP status on a non-2xx response, never the body — exactly the gap that made live-test #1b's own 400 invisible beyond a bare status code until Reed grepped the gateway's raw stderr log by hand. Both sites now read the response body as text ONCE (`Response::text()` consumes the response, so the success-path JSON parse re-parses the same captured text via `serde_json::from_str` rather than a second `.json()` call) and log a `.chars().take(500)` excerpt (never a raw byte slice — a multi-byte UTF-8 character is never split mid-codepoint) with a `" …(truncated)"` marker when the full body exceeds 500 characters, via one new shared `truncated_body_excerpt()` function so the two sites can't drift. **Credentials excluded by construction, not just truncation:** the gateway's bearer token is sent as a request HEADER at both call sites — neither reads or forwards a token through a response body — and OC's own documented response shapes for `sessions.create`/`sessions.send` (sync.md §22C.6.5.2/§22C.6.5.3) carry no credential-shaped field; the 500-char limit is a second, independent backstop against an unexpected body (a proxy error page), not the primary safety argument. Three tests on the pure function: over-500-chars truncates to exactly 500 with the marker (mutation: drop `.take(500)` → reddens); at-or-under-500 logs in full with no marker (mutation: always set the marker → reddens); a 600-character multi-byte-UTF-8 body truncates by character count, never splitting a codepoint (mutation: byte-index instead of char-index → would panic/mangle). (Part of #3050)

- internal (`src-gateway/`): live-test #1b — `sessions.create` returned HTTP 400 on every call, because `src-gateway/src/routes/sessions.rs::create()` forwarded Pane's `title` and `context_hint` verbatim into OC's `sessions.create` RPC params; OC's real schema (`docs/spec/sync.md` §22C.6.5.2, already correctly captured before this fix) has no such fields — only `key`/`agentId`/`label`/`model`/`parentSessionKey`/`task`/`message`. OC's own error was explicit: `INVALID_REQUEST: unexpected property 'context_hint'` (`title` was equally invalid but never reached, since the request's non-`preserve_order` `serde_json::Map` serializes keys alphabetically and OC's ajv-style validator reports only the first bad property it finds). **The spec was never wrong here — the gateway's handler diverged from its own cited spec section.** New `build_oc_create_params()` pure function: `title` → OC's `label` (omitted, not sent as `null`, when absent); `context_hint` dropped entirely (no OC equivalent). **Test against the documented schema, not today's three fields by hand:** `test_build_oc_create_params_only_emits_schema_fields` asserts every key the gateway emits is a member of a `OC_SESSIONS_CREATE_SCHEMA_FIELDS` allowlist sourced from §22C.6.5.2's own field list — a future invented field fails this test without needing its name added anywhere first (confirmed live: temporarily adding a `context_hint` field back into the helper reddens this exact test, reverted after confirming). A `debug_assert!` in the production function itself gives the same check a second, runtime backstop. Two regression tests pin the exact shape (`title` present → `{"agentId", "label"}` only; `title` absent → no `label` key at all, never `null`). `docs/spec/sync.md` §22C.6.5.2 gained a dated divergence note — the schema/mapping text itself needed no change. **Touches `src-gateway/` — the Studio gateway (currently PID 43669, pre-fix) must be rebuilt via `scripts/build-gateway-dmg.sh` and restarted before this is live-verified; merged is not deployed.** (Part of #3050)

## [1.0.67] - 2026-10-28
### Fixed
- internal: live-test #1 Bug 1(a) — `ai::scheduler::dispatch_oc_job` read `sessions.send`'s HTTP status only to log it; the finalize write was unconditional on `send_result` itself, so a non-2xx response OR a network error on the send both finalized identically to a 200 (`status = 'sent'`). Now branches on the actual result: 2xx → `'sent'` (unchanged); non-2xx or network error → `'failed'` with `last_error` set to the status code or network-error string, for `once`/`spawn` kinds (`recurring`/`heartbeat` kinds are unaffected — their own `next_run_at` recompute already happens at claim time, Ruling 1, and self-heals at the next scheduled firing regardless of this firing's send outcome). (Part of #3050)

  **The test that enshrined the bug as intended behavior was rewritten, not deleted.** `test_oc_job_non_2xx_response_still_records_sent_never_failed` asserted a mocked `500` on `sessions.send` should still record `'sent'`, citing §36.11's "OC's failed status on Pane-triggered sends is not evidence." That invariant is about OC's OWN downstream run status, read back later via §36.6 pickup — never about Pane's own transport result for its own HTTP call. Rewritten to `test_oc_job_non_2xx_response_records_failed_with_last_error`, asserting the opposite (`status == "failed"`, `last_error` names the status code), plus a new `test_oc_job_network_error_on_send_records_failed_with_last_error` sharing the same mutation. `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.3.4/§36.8.2/§36.11 wording corrected in the same PR so the invariant can't be misread this way again.

- internal: live-test #1 Bug 1(b) — a never-before-dispatched OC job's `sessions.send` failed with a 502 because Pane never registered the job's OC session before sending to it (confirmed by live-test #1b's own gateway log: OC answered cleanly with `INVALID_REQUEST`/"session not found" — a correct rejection of a session Pane never created, not an OC-side failure). `ai::scheduler::dispatch_oc_job` now calls the gateway's existing `POST /v1/sessions` (`sessions.create` — already whitelisted per `docs/spec/sync.md` §22C.6.5.2, so no ADR-0015 change; confirmed by a zero-match grep that nothing in `src-tauri/` had ever called it before) before a job's first send, and stores OC's own returned canonical key on the job row (`agent_jobs.oc_session_key`, migration v94 → v95, `migrate_v95`). A later firing of the same job (the recurring-job repeat-send case) finds the key already stored and skips the bootstrap call entirely — "sends only," one HTTP call. **Idempotency shape chosen deliberately, not the gateway's own idempotency**: the gateway's `CreateSessionRequest` has no `key` field to request a specific one with, so OC mints a fresh key on every `sessions.create` call — calling it twice for the same job would register two different OC sessions under one job id, which is wrong, not merely redundant. Pane tracking its own "already bootstrapped" state via the new column is the only shape that also satisfies "sends only" on the second firing. (Part of #3050)

Three pre-existing tests (`test_oc_job_dispatch_is_one_sessions_send_status_sent_no_loop`, `test_oc_recurring_job_recomputes_next_run_at_at_send_time`, `test_scheduler_tick_dispatches_missed_oc_job_exactly_once`) updated to pre-seed `oc_session_key` so they continue isolating what they were already testing (the 2xx send path, recurrence, tick dispatch) from bootstrap behavior.

- internal: live-test #1 Bug 2 — a `schedule_job` confirmation chip went missing (no error, no chip, survived quit/reopen). Root cause, traced end to end: `ai::chat::ai_chat_stream`'s own `session_id: None` fallback carried an inline, incomplete copy of `get_active_session`'s resolution — the lookup half only, no create-on-miss half — so a surface with no `is_active = 1` row yet (an early/first message to Home) resolved via `.unwrap_or(project_id_ctx)` to the literal, non-existent string `"workspace"` instead of a real session id. That fabricated id then flowed into `agent_jobs.origin_session_id`/`chat_messages_local.thread_id`, and the chip insert succeeded silently (no FK on `chat_messages_local.thread_id`) into a thread nothing ever renders. **Root-cause fix:** extracted `get_or_create_active_session_id` out of `get_active_session`, reused by both — one resolution, not two independently-maintained half-copies. `ai_chat_stream` now surfaces a real error on a genuine resolution failure, never a sentinel string. **Frontend investigated, not changed:** confirmed by evidence (not assumed) that `ChatSidebar.svelte`'s `'workspace'`/`'temp'` filter is still correct — `'workspace'` is a live, intentional error-fallback sentinel (`navigation.ts::navigateToSafe`'s catch-block recovery), not a stale assumption; `'temp'` is dead-but-harmless. Documented in place with the grep evidence rather than guessed at build time. **Defense-in-depth (guard chosen over an FK, named why):** `ai::scheduler::insert_schedule_confirmation_message`/`insert_job_brief_message` now refuse an unknown `thread_id` via a new `require_known_thread_id` guard before the INSERT. An FK on `chat_messages_local.thread_id` was considered and rejected for THIS PR: the table is not CRR (so cr-sqlite's FK-rejection doesn't block it), but SQLite has no `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT` — retrofitting a real FK onto an existing, populated table (FTS5 triggers, possible legacy rows) means a full table rebuild, real risk for real installs' historical data for a narrow bug a cheaper guard already closes; the guard also gives a clear, specific error instead of a raw constraint-violation exception. Accepted tradeoff, named explicitly: this guards the two synthetic-message writers in this module, not every `chat_messages_local` INSERT site in the tree. (Part of #3050)

An end-to-end regression test reproduces Reed's own named repro condition (`schedule_job` dispatched with a `sessionId` resolved via `get_or_create_active_session_id` for a surface with no prior active session) and pins the chip's `thread_id` against a REAL, existing `chat_sessions` row — not just "a row exists," the weaker assertion that let the original bug ship. `docs/spec/sessions.md` §30.2.6's "`get_active_session(surface)` never returns nothing" invariant gained a correction note naming exactly where `ai_chat_stream` violated it and how the fix closes the gap for good (one shared resolver, not two).

New `GatewayError::OcRpcError { code, message }` variant preserves OC's own `code`; `IntoResponse` maps `code == "INVALID_REQUEST"` to **400** (not 404 — Stia's call, named: a direct mapping to OC's own semantic category rather than Pane re-interpreting it into a category OC never asserted) and falls back to the pre-existing blanket 502 for any other, not-yet-named code. `docs/spec/sync.md` §22C.12.2's OC-error-mapping table gained the new row. Own commit, separable from the `src-tauri/` bootstrap fix above — different crate, Reed audits both. ## [1.0.66] - 2026-10-28
### Fixed
- internal: Spawn, depth, wake-on-complete, captain/crew, live chip status, and #3104's shared chat_messages_local projection (Part of #3050, harness PR 5 of 9 — the biggest PR of the sprint and the last before bump/build/live test #1, closes #3104, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.4 + §36.4.5 + §36.8 + §36.17, build brief `docs/audits/2026-10-28-scope-3050-pr5-spawn-wake-crew.md`).

  **Schema — one new column, nothing else.** Migration v93 → v94 (`migrate_v94`): `chat_sessions.crew_agent_ids` (nullable `TEXT`, JSON array of `ai_agents.id`; `NULL` = no crew). `parent_job_id`/`root_job_id`/`chain_depth`/`wake_origin`/`origin_message_id` all already existed on `agent_jobs` since PR 2's own v93 migration but were never populated — `create_job`'s `NewJobParams`/`INSERT` thread them through for the first time here. `agent_jobs.kind` gains a new free-text domain value, `'wake'` (no DDL, same documented-domain convention `chat_sessions.origin` already uses). `runtime_constants.rs` gains `RUNTIME_MAX_SPAWN_DEPTH = 2`, `RUNTIME_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH = 8`, `RUNTIME_JOB_ARCHIVE_DAYS = 30` — named in that file's own module doc comment since PR 2, now real consts. `tests/fixtures/upgrade-from-v93.db` built (`scripts/build-v93-fixture.sh`) for `smoke-upgrade-db`'s own current-1 requirement.

  **Captain/crew (§36.17) — Matt's ruling, replacing §36.4.1's old "any active Pane agent" targeting rule.** A session has a crew: the set of agents its captain may spawn onto. Default is no crew, and no crew means `spawn_job` is not offered. Two independent checks: **offer-time** (`get_pane_tools_for_runtime` gains `has_crew: bool`, both production call sites — `ai_chat_stream`, `prepare_job_dispatch` — resolve it via a new `ai::tools::session_has_crew` helper keyed on the turn's own running session) and **dispatch-time**, two sub-checks inside `execute_spawn_job` itself, independent of the offer-time filter: (a) re-derives "does the calling session have a crew at all," refusing a `NULL`/empty crew; (b) "is this specific target agent a crew member" — a per-argument question the offer-time check cannot answer. **Inheritance**: a spawned session (`origin='spawn'`) inherits its captain's crew verbatim, read from the calling session at `create_job` time — the only choice that makes a depth-2 chain reachable at all (otherwise a spawn session's own crew defaults to `NULL`, `spawn_job` is never offered inside it, and the depth cap is unreachable by construction). Schedule sessions never inherit (`NULL` regardless). Picker UI is a later PR (PR 10); no dev-only Tauri command was needed this session since the live test seeds crews directly via SQL/a future dev command — flagged for Stria/Brit to add before the live test if Matt wants to set crews through the UI layer rather than SQL.

  **`spawn_job(agent, brief, title?, wake?)` (§36.4.1).** New `ToolDef` + `ai/tools.rs::execute_spawn_job`, wired into `execute_single_tool`. Creates an `agent_jobs` row (`kind='spawn'`, `origin_session_id` = calling session, `agent_id` = the crew-checked target, `project_id` = calling session's own project), the job session (crew-inherited per above), returns the tool result `"Spawned <agent> on '<title>'. You'll get the result in this chat when it's done."` immediately — the calling turn does not wait. Refuses an `openclaw`-runtime target (`"spawn_job cannot target an OpenClaw-bound agent."`). `origin_message_id` stays `NULL` — not resolvable from this tool call's own params today (no per-tool-call message id is threaded into dispatch context yet); stated as a documented gap, same one `schedule_job` already carries, not fabricated.

  **Depth cap vs. chain cap — two separate counters, never conflated (§36.17.2).** This was the single biggest risk the build brief named for this PR. **Depth** (`RUNTIME_MAX_SPAWN_DEPTH = 2`): concurrent nesting within one turn-chain — a spawn calling a spawn, same moment. NOT a stored counter: checked at DISPATCH time only, from the presence/absence of `parent_job_id` on the CALLING job's own row (threaded via two new `context_clone` keys, `"ownJobId"`/`"parentJobId"`, absent by construction on an interactive turn — which is exactly what makes depth always "fresh" for a human-typed call). **Chain** (`RUNTIME_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH = 8`): sequential wake-chaining over time — a job finishes, wakes its origin, the origin spawns the next one, repeat. An existing column (`chain_depth`), newly populated; checked at OFFER time only, via a new `chain_capped: bool` fourth parameter on `get_pane_tools_for_runtime` (withholding BOTH `spawn_job` and `schedule_job` when capped). **The critical mutation pair, run together, each isolating one mechanism:** scenario 1 (target IS a crew member, calling turn is itself depth-2) must still refuse — only the depth check can be responsible; scenario 2 (calling turn is fresh depth-1, target is NOT a crew member) must still refuse — only the crew check can be responsible. Each scenario's own mutation (deleting only that one mechanism) was run and confirmed to redden ONLY that scenario's own dedicated test, never the other — proving the two checks are genuinely independent, not one implemented as a special case of the other.

  **Report-back (§36.8.1), via the scheduler's post-completion hook, never the ingest path itself.** `run_agent_loop`'s return type grew from a bare tool-call count (`u32`) to `AgentLoopResult { tool_calls_used, final_text, outcome: JobOutcome }` — a real, audited signature change across all 11 call sites in `ai/chat.rs` (`JobOutcome::Failed` set at the one hard-failure site, the reconnect-retry-budget-exhausted branch; every other exit — Stopped/Ceiling/NoProgressTimeout — counts as `Done`). `ai::scheduler::scheduler_tick`'s spawned closure, after `run_agent_loop` returns, now (for `kind IN ('spawn', 'once')` jobs with an `origin_session_id`): resolves the origin session's own bound agent, builds the attribution line `"**{job agent name}** (job {job identifier}) reported:\n\n{final text}"` ("job identifier" is `agent_jobs.id`, a UUID — the spec's illustrative `#123` was never a literal format this PR matches, stated explicitly), and writes it via `ingest_external_messages_impl` (now `pub(crate)` for this exact caller). `ExternalMessage` gains `job_id: Option<String>` (threaded into `insert_external_message`'s INSERT; every existing constructor — the OC pull adapter, 2 test helpers — updated to pass `None`) and now populates `model` (the job's own dispatch model) for report-back specifically — the field the new Svelte chip discriminator (below) keys on. **§30.11.5's binding check passes with NO exception**: `source_agent_id` is set to the origin session's own bound `agent_id`, the exact value the check would read and compare against itself anyway.

  **Wake-on-complete (§36.4.5) — reuses `claim_due_jobs`'s claim-before-run, never a second dispatch path.** New `ai::scheduler::create_wake_job`: an ordinary new `agent_jobs` row, `kind='wake'`, `session_id = origin_session_id` (the turn runs DIRECTLY in the real chat session — zero new Svelte needed for the reply itself), `origin_session_id = NULL` on the wake row's own record (nowhere further to report back to), `chain_depth` = the finished job's own `chain_depth + 1`, `root_job_id` propagated (never re-self-referenced). Claimed by the exact same `claim_due_jobs` path every other job uses — confirmed `claim_due_jobs`'s missed-run-collapse recompute is gated to `kind IN ('recurring', 'heartbeat')` only, `'wake'` falls through unchanged, same as `'once'`/`'spawn'` today. Gated on ALL of: `wake_origin = 1` (default; `spawn_job`'s optional `wake: false` sets `0`), an origin session that still exists, NOT OC-bound (`resolve_runtime_config_for_session(...).runtime_type == "openclaw"` — the exact call `prepare_job_dispatch` already makes), and NOT stale past `RUNTIME_JOB_ARCHIVE_DAYS` (`last_active_at` — a stated, honest proxy; no real `archived_at`/`is_archived` column exists anywhere in this codebase). Any failed check degrades to report-only; report-back already happened unconditionally. **The chain-shared ceiling is two real code changes**, both in code this PR already had to touch: (1) the post-completion `tool_calls_used` bookkeeping write now `UPDATE agent_jobs SET tool_calls_used = tool_calls_used + ?1 WHERE id = {root_job_id}` — accumulates onto the chain's ROOT row instead of overwriting the finishing job's own row (a non-chained job's `root_job_id` always self-references per `create_job`, so this is a no-op change for the overwhelming majority of jobs — the "quietest regression" class the build brief's own blast-radius table called out, pinned by a dedicated non-chained-job test); (2) `prepare_job_dispatch`'s ceiling computation now reads the root's own `tool_calls_used` and subtracts it from the configured ceiling before handing out `ceiling_remaining`, so the Nth job in a chain starts with whatever budget the chain has left, not a fresh 200 every time.

  **#3104 — the shared `chat_messages_local` projection, three PRs' worth of the same bug, closed with one named mechanism.** Reed's scope audit reconciled the real count directly: 18 occurrences of `FROM chat_messages_local` in `ai/chat.rs`, of which exactly **5** are full-row-projection sites (the whole defect class — `maybe_compact_thread`'s 3 branches, `load_chat_messages`'s 2); the other 13 are narrow `COUNT(*)`/single-column/test-hardcoded reads that never carried bookkeeping columns and structurally shouldn't. **Mechanism: a named column-list constant + a shared row-mapper fragment, NOT a query builder** — the two query families genuinely differ (`maybe_compact_thread` maps into a function-local `MessageRow` struct; `load_chat_messages` builds a `serde_json::json!` object with a `LEFT JOIN` the other family doesn't have), so forcing both into one builder would be the wrong abstraction for a real structural difference. New: `ai::tools::CHAT_MESSAGE_BOOKKEEPING_COLUMNS: &str = "synthetic, continued, job_id"` + `ai::chat::map_bookkeeping_columns(row, offset)`. All 5 sites refactored to append the constant to their own SELECT and call the shared mapper at the matching offset instead of 3 hand-written `row.get(...)` calls each. **`job_id` stays in the constant and mapper even at sites that don't read it yet — UNIFORM, not minimal** (Matt's ruling: `synthetic`/`continued` also started dead at some sites and got used one PR later). **The refactor's own regression pin**: all 6 pre-existing PR-3/PR-4 mutation-anchor tests (`fetch_site_pinning_tests_3050_pr3` ×3 for `synthetic`/`continued`, `job_id_site_pinning_tests_3050_pr4` ×3 for `job_id`) re-run UNCHANGED after the refactor and still pass — proof the refactor preserved every site's exact output, not a new test standing in for that proof. **The `JOB_ID_FETCH_CAPTURE_3050_PR4` `#[cfg(test)]` seam survives**, unified around the new shared mapper rather than duplicated a 4th/5th time (per Reed's scope: "consolidate rather than duplicate" — done, stated here as instructed).

  **Memory-extraction exclusion (§36.4.3), the real gap, not a theoretical one.** Confirmed by direct read: `enqueue_extraction` (`ai/extraction_worker.rs`) is the real, single enqueue site (called from the frontend-invoked `ai_enqueue_extraction` after every turn's SSE `done` event) — job/spawn-session turns were enqueued for extraction COMPLETELY UNFILTERED before this PR; `list_sessions`'s own `origin NOT IN ('spawn', 'schedule')` filter is a different mechanism extraction never goes through. Fixed at the queue: `enqueue_extraction` now looks up the thread's own `chat_sessions.origin` and skips `'spawn'` sessions (returns `Ok(())`, no insert). `'schedule'` is deliberately NOT excluded — §36.4.3 only names spawn transcripts; schedule sessions are visible, named, Scheduled-panel sessions, extracted like any other. The report-back message itself (always `origin='user'`) is never touched by this check.

  **`ChatPanel.svelte` — the chip-vs-normal-bubble discriminator, Reed's own find, fixed in this PR per his scope.** PR 4's chip-render condition (`message.job_id && !message.synthetic`) would ALSO catch the new report-back message (both carry `job_id` set, `synthetic=0`) — a real, concrete conflict Reed's scope audit found by reading both the Svelte and the spec's own report-back framing side by side, not a hypothetical. Fixed with a third clause, `&& !message.model`, using a field that already exists on both sides: `insert_schedule_confirmation_message` never sets `model` (always `NULL` for a Pane-templated chip); report-back's `ExternalMessage.model` now carries the job's own dispatch model (set above). A report-back message therefore falls through to the existing `{:else}` normal-bubble branch automatically, picking up its sender name/avatar/save-to-memory button — it IS the agent speaking, full attribution, per §36.8.1's own framing, never a chip. One condition clause, zero new render paths. **4d-skip, not `4d: PASS`** — this PR touches Svelte (the chip condition + the live-status polling below); Matt walks both the chip's own rendering and the report-back-renders-as-a-normal-bubble behavior at the live test. The DATA reaching here (every `model`/`job_id`/`synthetic` value) is already pinned end to end by real Rust tests (the schedule-family chip round trip from PR 4; this PR's own report-back-lands-in-origin-session test).

  **Matt's addition, not in Reed's scope — "chips show live status."** The spawn chip AND PR 4's schedule chip now read `agent_jobs.status`/`finished_at`/`started_at` by the `job_id` already on the message, and re-render — "running" → "done in 48s" — as the scheduler marks the job done. No new columns. New `#[tauri::command] ai::scheduler::get_job_status(job_id)`, a plain `SELECT` by id returning `Ok(None)` for an unknown id rather than erroring. New `src/lib/jobStatusChip.ts`: pure, side-effect-free formatting functions (`chipStatusSuffix`, `chipDisplayText`, `elapsedSeconds`, `isTerminalJobStatus`), fully unit-tested (14 Vitest tests, including the named test "job exits → the chip row reflects done" with its own before/after re-render assertion). `ChatPanel.svelte` polls `get_job_status` every 5s for every visible, non-terminal chip's `job_id` (derived reactively from `visibleMessages`), stops polling a `job_id` once its status is terminal, tears the interval down entirely once none remain.

  **Tests, every one named with its mutation, every mutation actually run and reverted (not claimed):**
  - Spawn from project chat → job session on the same project, bound to the target agent, `origin_session_id` set (`origin_message_id` asserted `None` — the documented gap, not fabricated). Mutation: deleted the `origin_session_id` assignment → red (`None` where the test asserts `Some("session-1")`); restored.
  - Spawn targeting an OC agent → refused, no row. Mutation: deleted the `runtime_type == "openclaw"` check → red; restored.
  - Depth 3 → refused. Mutation: deleted the depth-cap check → red (a depth-3 row got created); restored. Confirmed independent: the non-crew test stayed green under this same mutation.
  - Spawn onto an agent not in the crew → refused. Mutation: deleted the crew-membership check → red; restored. Confirmed independent: the depth-3 test stayed green under this same mutation.
  - No crew → `spawn_job` absent from the offered set (+ the positive case: crew present → offered). Mutation: deleted the `has_crew` offer-time filter → red (the full tool list, `spawn_job` included, came back); restored.
  - **The depth-vs-crew distinguishing pair**, run together in one test, both scenarios must refuse.
  - Spawned project agent calling `create_note` on another project → refused by the EXISTING scope check. **No mutation — stated explicitly, not invented**, per Matt's own endorsed OC-no-loop precedent from PR 4: there is no new gate here, the test's job is to catch a future regression in job-turn context plumbing.
  - Extraction queue skips `origin='spawn'`, accepts `origin='user'` and `origin='schedule'`. Mutation: deleted the `origin='spawn'` check → red (the spawn-session message got queued); restored.
  - Report-back lands in the origin session, attributed/tagged correctly, `agent_jobs.status` settles to `'done'` — proven end to end through a REAL `scheduler_tick` → `run_agent_loop` dispatch (a mocked Ollama provider), not a direct call to the ingest function.
  - Spawn → finish → one real, second proactive turn on the origin session with the synthetic wake message — TWO real `scheduler_tick` dispatches in one test (the first creates the wake row; the second claims and dispatches it). Mutation: deleted the `create_wake_job` call → red (zero wake rows); restored.
  - `wake: false` → report only, zero wake rows (report-back still happens). Mutation: deleted the `wake_origin` gate → red; restored.
  - OC-bound origin → zero wake rows, report-back still happens (provider-neutral). Mutation: deleted the OC-bound check → red; restored.
  - `chain_depth` ≥ 8 withholds BOTH `spawn_job` and `schedule_job` at offer time (+ the positive case at `chain_depth = 7`). Mutation: deleted the `chain_capped` filter → red; restored.
  - A wake row's own `chain_depth`/`root_job_id` propagate correctly (`chain_depth + 1`, root inherited, never re-self-referenced) — the companion test proving the VALUE the chain-cap gate above depends on.
  - Ceiling shared across the chain: a chained job's ceiling is reduced by the root's already-spent total; a non-chained job keeps the FULL ceiling (the blast-radius table's own "quietest regression" pin, tested as its own assertion, not assumed from the chained case). Mutation: deleted the chain-sharing subtraction → red (`200` instead of the expected `10`); restored.
  - `get_job_status`: known job_id resolves the three fields; unknown job_id returns `Ok(None)`.
  - 14 Vitest tests for the chip-status pure-function module (`jobStatusChip.test.ts`), including the named "job exits → chip reflects done" re-render assertion.
  - Updated for the new tool/field counts: sheet registry (`get_pane_tools()` 42→43, +`spawn_job`), `MUTATE_EXISTING_TOOLS`/`project_scoped_tools()` symmetric difference (7→8, `spawn_job` project-scoped-write but not taint-withheld, same ADR-0064 D4 axis as the rest of the schedule family), the static system-prompt token budget (5,250→5,450 tokens, a deliberate reviewed raise for `spawn_job`'s new `ToolDef`, measured at 5,340 with ~5% headroom, same convention the existing comment there uses).

  **Out of scope, confirmed not built:** the picker UI for setting a session's crew (PR 10 — a dev-only path is the only way to set one this session); a second dispatch-time re-derivation of the chain cap (only offer-time, per the build brief's own scope — Reed's blast-radius table named this as the one withholding rule this PR does not also re-derive at dispatch time, confirmed structurally safe for the stated reason).

  **Verified.** Full details — base/head SHAs, invocation names, exact pass/fail counts both sides, both smokes, the analyzer, `crsqlite.dylib` byte count, lockfile confirmation — reported in this PR's own completion report (`Part of #3050`); summarized here: clean base `5be86ce2` (origin/main, #3105 merged) re-run in its own clean worktree; this branch's head re-run in the same isolated fashion every prior PR in this sprint has used. No `Cargo.lock`/`package-lock.json` changes (checked via `git status --short` immediately before every `git add`). `src-tauri/resources/crsqlite.dylib` confirmed 1,631,456 bytes, untouched. `pnpm-lock.yaml`/`package-lock.json` unmodified by the frontend `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` run needed to materialize `node_modules` for Vitest verification.

- internal: fix(runtime): thread chain position through spawn/schedule/wake; refuse self-spawn — closes the wake-loop gap Reed's audit found in the PR 5 entry above: a self-crewed (or A→B→A-crewed) agent could spawn → wake → spawn → wake indefinitely, zero refusals, because both `RUNTIME_MAX_SPAWN_DEPTH` and `RUNTIME_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` were correctly implemented but structurally unreachable on that one path (Part of #3050, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.4.1 + §36.4.5 + §36.17.2 + new §36.17.3, audit `docs/audits/2026-10-28-pr-3107-spawn-wake-crew.md`).

  **The three unconditional resets, fixed by symbol.** `ai::tools::execute_spawn_job` and `ai::tools::execute_schedule_job` used to set `root_job_id: None, chain_depth: 0` on EVERY call, discarding the calling turn's real chain position — now both read the calling job's own row (via `context["ownJobId"]`) and carry `chain_depth`/`root_job_id` forward verbatim; a fresh root (`chain_depth = 0`, self-referencing `root_job_id`) only when the calling turn has no job at all (a genuine interactive call). `ai::scheduler::create_wake_job` used to hardcode `parent_job_id = NULL` on every wake row — now it's the id of the job that just finished and triggered the wake (provenance). **A fresh root is distinguished from an inherited one purely by whether `context["ownJobId"]` is present** — absent means a genuinely fresh interactive turn (fresh root); present means a job turn (spawn, schedule, or wake), which always inherits.

  **The nesting-depth cap's own signal had to be narrowed, or the fix would have broken it.** Threading `parent_job_id` onto wake rows (needed for provenance) meant a wake row's own `parent_job_id` is now always non-`NULL`, same as a genuinely nested spawn's. Left unguarded, `execute_spawn_job`'s existing "nesting depth" check (`parent_job_id` presence on the calling row) would have fired on the FIRST wake-mediated re-spawn of every single cycle, making `RUNTIME_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` (8) structurally unreachable — the opposite of this fix's intent. Fixed by scoping the nesting signal to the calling row's own `kind == "spawn"` (a genuine spawn-of-a-spawn, same dispatch stack); a `kind == "wake"` calling row is always depth-1-fresh for NESTING purposes, while its `chain_depth` still climbs independently every hop.

  **Self-spawn refused (Matt's ruling): crew is API agents minus the captain.** `execute_spawn_job` now refuses a target that IS the calling session's own bound agent, with the tool error `"spawn_job: <agent> is this session's own agent — an agent cannot spawn itself."` — a SECOND guard, not a substitute for the propagation fix above: an A→B→A cycle (two distinct agents, never naming the same one twice in a row) loops identically without ever tripping this check.

  **Four new tests, every one with its own mutation, every mutation actually run and reverted:**
  - A job turn re-calls `spawn_job`, through the REAL dispatch cycle (depth-1 spawn → depth-2 same-turn re-spawn, allowed → depth-3 attempt, refused, zero new rows). Mutation: deleted the `calling_depth + 1 > RUNTIME_MAX_SPAWN_DEPTH` check → red (`left: 3, right: 2` — a third row got created); restored.
  - A real spawn→wake→spawn→wake cycle, driven through `execute_spawn_job`/`create_wake_job` (not a hand-seeded row): `chain_depth` climbs by exactly 1 every hop; the 8th wake created lands at `chain_depth = 8` and has `spawn_job` withheld, ending the chain with a report — it never reaches a 9th wake. Mutation: reverted the chain-position inheritance (forced `root_job_id: None, chain_depth: 0` unconditionally, the exact pre-fix code) → red (the loop ran all 8 hops without ever hitting the cap, `chain_depth` pinned at 0/1 the entire time — reproducing Reed's 12-iteration live probe exactly); restored.
  - The shared ceiling across TWO REAL chain links (not hand-seeded root ids): a `spawn_job` call made from inside a wake turn inherits the ORIGINAL chain root, so usage from both links (120 + 50) accumulates onto the one root row (170), not two independently-fresh budgets. Mutation: reverted `root_job_id` inheritance only (kept `chain_depth` inheritance, isolating the one field) → red (`left: "..." right: "..."` — link 2 self-referenced a fresh root instead of inheriting link 1's); restored.
  - Self-spawn → refused, no row: a captain whose own crew lists itself (nothing upstream of the crew check refuses that configuration) is refused with a clear error naming self-spawn. Mutation: deleted the self-spawn check block → red (`left: 1, right: 0` — a row got created); restored.

  **Pre-existing fixture fixed, not worked around.** `item_e_agent_event_resolution_tests::test_every_write_tool_fires_an_event_on_success`'s own `spawn_job` registry-walk fixture bound its calling session's own agent AS its only crew member and then spawned that same agent onto itself — a genuine new failure surfaced by the self-spawn guard (not the known `crsql_internal_sync_bit` artifact, not absorbed into it). Fixed the fixture, not the guard: added a second, distinct agent as the crew target so the registry walk still exercises a real, non-self dispatch.

  **Full suite, named invocation:** `PANE_TEST_ROOT=/tmp/stia-3107-test-root CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/stia-3107-target cargo test -p pane --lib -- --test-threads=1 --skip tests::test_backup::` → **2705 passed, 0 failed, 9 ignored, 11 filtered → 2705 total** (this PR's own head was 2701; +4 for the tests above). The known `crsql_internal_sync_bit` artifact (`test_upgrade_from_v85_fixture_migrates_cleanly_to_v86`) and the load-sensitive `wrong_cert_integration_tests` both re-ran clean in isolation — zero failures anywhere in this run, nothing relabeled or absorbed. Both smokes (`scripts/smoke-launch.sh fresh`/`upgrade`) PASS. Analyzer (`check-turn-origin`) → `{"violations": [], "constructions_scanned": 2}`, unchanged from the PR 5 baseline (this fix touches no `TurnOrigin` construction site). Spec-first gate PASS. `crsqlite.dylib` confirmed 1,631,456 bytes, byte-identical. No `Cargo.lock`/`package-lock.json` changes.

- internal: Proactive-turn tool policy + the schedule family — `delete_note`/`move_note`/`move_folder` are withheld from scheduled/background turns, navigation tools no-op in them, and agents can now schedule, list, cancel, pause, and resume jobs as a Pane tool call (Part of #3050, harness PR 4 of 9, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.5 + §36.3.7, build brief `docs/audits/2026-10-28-scope-3050-pr4-toolpolicy.md`).

  **`ToolPolicy`, two independent gates.** A new `ToolPolicy { proactive: bool }` struct (`ai/chat.rs`, next to `TurnOrigin`; `ToolPolicy::from_turn_origin`) is derived once per dispatch and applied at TWO points, per §36.16's forward-compat note. **Offer-time:** `ai::tools::get_pane_tools_for_runtime` gains a `proactive: bool` parameter, filtering a new `PROACTIVE_WITHHELD_TOOLS: [&str; 3] = ["delete_note", "move_note", "move_folder"]` const (same shape/file as `WEB_TOOL_RUNTIME_ALLOWLIST`) when `true`. Both production call sites updated: `ai_chat_stream` passes `false` (one of the two sanctioned `TurnOrigin::User` constructors — known statically, no read needed); `scheduler::prepare_job_dispatch` passes `true` (only ever called from `scheduler_tick`, the other sanctioned `TurnOrigin::Job` constructor). **Dispatch-time:** a new `check_proactive_tool_policy(tool_policy, requested_name)` — a fourth gate inside `run_agent_loop`'s tool-call loop, same placement/shape as `check_tool_offered` → `check_args_parsed` → `check_web_taint`. Deliberately does NOT consult `offered_tool_names` — it re-derives the refusal fresh from `turn_origin` directly, exactly the way `check_web_taint` re-derives from the live taint flag rather than the (already-fixed) offer list. **Proven non-decorative, not just claimed:** a test seeds `offered_tool_names` WITH `delete_note` despite `TurnOrigin::Job` (simulating a future offer-filter bug), so only the dispatch gate — not `check_tool_offered` — can be refusing it; deleting the dispatch-gate call site (leaving the offer-time filter untouched) turns that test red (`Deleted "Target Note"` — the note was actually removed), confirmed and restored.

  **Navigation no-op.** One `NAV_TOOLS` wrapper (`navigate`, `show_view`, and the six `navigate_home`/.../`set_filter` names), placed immediately after the dispatch gate and before all three structurally-separate navigate-family branches that follow it in the loop — sufficient with zero handler changes, since none of the three branches ever runs for a proactive turn once this wrapper `continue`s first. Mutation-proven via a real-loop test with an `app.listen("ai-stream-chunk", ...)` event-capture counter (not just the returned value): deleting the wrapper turns the test red — the `navigate_home` block ran and the final `done:true` payload carried a non-null `navigate` field (`{"tab":"all","view":"home"}`).

  **Web taint, confirmed unchanged.** A real-loop test drives `web_fetch` then `edit_note` under `TurnOrigin::Job`, with the thread's own brief message carrying a non-empty `job_id` (mirroring `insert_job_brief_message`'s shape) — `edit_note` is not in `PROACTIVE_WITHHELD_TOOLS` (edits are versioned/recoverable, §36.5.1), so only `check_web_taint`, not the new proactive gate, can be what refuses it; it does, byte-unchanged note body, same mechanism as every interactive-turn taint test, no new gate involved.

  **The schedule family — five new tools** (`ai/tools.rs::get_pane_tools()`): `schedule_job` (`brief`, `run_at` ISO-local **or** `cron`, `title`/`agent`/`project_id` all optional — `agent` defaults to the calling session's own dispatch agent, `project_id` defaults to the session's own project or Home's `'workspace'`), `list_jobs` (`scope`: `'project'` default | `'all'`), `cancel_job`/`pause_job`/`resume_job` (`job_id`). Per **Ruling 2** (already recorded in the spec, tool code landing now): offered to OC-bound sessions too — the tool runs in Pane (writes an `agent_jobs` row) either way; OC never gets a loop. `schedule_job`'s description says so explicitly: "use this for ANY schedule requested in Pane — never OpenClaw cron." `schedule_job`/`cancel_job`/`pause_job`/`resume_job` are `ToolAccess::Write` (so `project_scoped_tools()` — derived, not a second hand-typed list — gates them automatically); `list_jobs` is `ToolAccess::Read`.

  **Dispatch, reusing what exists.** All five route through `execute_single_tool`'s own `match` (not a loop-level branch like `web_fetch`/`navigate` — every schedule-family operation is a plain synchronous DB read/write, the same shape `create_note`/`edit_note`/`delete_note` already have), so they get `check_home_only_tool_permission`/`check_cross_project_write_permission` for free. `schedule_job` calls the EXISTING `ai::scheduler::create_job` (built, unused, in PR 2/3) — not a duplicate. New `check_cross_project_write_permission` arms: `schedule_job` (optional `project_id` — absent is never a refusal, present-and-mismatched is, same wording as every other arm); `cancel_job`/`pause_job`/`resume_job` (resolves the target job's own `project_id` from `agent_jobs`, same resolve-then-compare shape `note_project_id`/`folder_project_id` already use). **Mutation-proven:** deleting the `schedule_job` arm (falls through to the permissive `_ => Ok(())` default) turns the cross-project test red — the job was actually created on the other project, confirmed and restored; same mutation shape run against `cancel_job`/`pause_job`/`resume_job`'s refusal test (a flagged addition, not in the task's named list, logically required by the same standing rule).

  **`list_jobs(scope='all')` is Home-only — Matt's new ruling, a gap Reed's scope audit found.** `list_jobs` is `ToolAccess::Read`, outside `project_scoped_tools()`'s reach by design, and this codebase's standing rule is "reads aren't project-gated" — but a job row is a new kind of read that rule wasn't written for (it's another project's content, not the calling session's own). A bespoke check inside `execute_list_jobs` itself: `scope == "all" && session_project_id.is_some()` refuses, same message shape as a cross-project `schedule_job`; `scope == "all"` from Home sees every row; `scope == "project"` (default) scopes to the calling session's own project from anywhere. **Mutation-proven:** dropping the check turns the test red (a project-bound session's `scope='all'` call that should be refused instead succeeds), confirmed and restored.

  **The OC-no-loop guarantee is structural, not a gate — stated explicitly, no fake mutation (per the task's own agreed exception).** `schedule_job`'s handler's only side effects are `create_session_internal` (its own sync transaction) and one `agent_jobs` INSERT (`create_job`) — no `app_handle`, no `tauri::async_runtime::spawn`, no call to `run_agent_loop`/`scheduler_tick` anywhere in its body. Asserted mechanically, not by source inspection alone: a test calls `schedule_job` from an OC-bound session and asserts `agent_jobs.status == 'pending'` and `started_at IS NULL` immediately after the tool call returns, before any `scheduler_tick` invocation in the test — a timing-independent proof that dispatch and loop-start are two separate events.

  **The chip.** `ai/scheduler.rs::insert_schedule_confirmation_message` — a sibling of `insert_job_brief_message`'s plain-INSERT shape, **deliberately NOT `insert_external_message`** (that function's `session.agent_id == msg.source_agent_id` binding check and `oc_message_id` dedup key are OC-ingestion-specific invariants that don't apply to a Pane-authored line reporting on a tool call that just ran inside the SAME session). Targets `origin_session_id` (the chat the tool was called FROM — threaded through via two new, additive context keys below — never the job's own new session, so a Home agent scheduling onto a project still writes the chip into the Home chat it was called from) with `synthetic = 0` (must render, the inverse of the job brief's own `synthetic = 1`). `agent_jobs`/`NewJobParams`/`create_job` gain `origin_session_id` (nullable, independent of the job's own `project_id`/`session_id`). New `ai::scheduler::parse_run_at_local` boundary function (ISO-local `run_at` → UTC, same local-time convention `cron` fields use — the third and only other such boundary, alongside `format_stored_datetime`/`parse_stored_datetime`).

- internal: Auto-continue — Pane's API-runtime turns now continue themselves past `max_tool_iterations` instead of stopping and asking the user to "continue" (Part of #3050, harness PR 3 of 9, `docs/spec/runtime.md` §36.2, build brief `docs/audits/2026-10-27-scope-3050-pr3-autocontinue.md`).

  **The mechanism.** `max_tool_iterations` is now a CHECKPOINT interval, not a brake (Ruling 4, Matt 2026-10-27): hitting it in `run_agent_loop` no longer ends the turn. If the model's last iteration still produced tool calls (the loop's own signal, never a model self-report), the dispatch is an API runtime (`API_RUNTIME_ALLOWLIST` — `anthropic`/`openrouter`/`ollama`/`venice`, never `openclaw`, §36.0.1), and the cumulative tool-call ceiling has budget left, the loop appends a `continued=1` progress-divider assistant message ("Continuing — N tool calls so far.") plus a synthetic `synthetic=1` `"Continue."` user message (`insert_continuation_messages`, mirrors #3102's own `insert_job_brief_message` INSERT shape), re-runs the context-budget check (`maybe_compact_thread` — the same function `ai_chat_stream`'s own pre-dispatch path already calls, not a second divergent one; required per Ruling 4, not cosmetic), resets the per-segment iteration counter, and keeps going. **Implemented as an in-place `continue` of `run_agent_loop`'s own `loop { .. }`, not a second async call or recursion** — `all_tool_calls` never resets across a continuation, so it already IS the cumulative "ceiling decremented by calls used so far" counter the spec asks for, with no second mutable field needed to keep in sync with it.

  **`AgentLoopInputs` gains the two fields PR 1 (#3059) deliberately left out:** `continue_policy: Option<ContinuePolicy>` (`ceiling_remaining: u32`, falling back to `RUNTIME_DEFAULT_JOB_CEILING`=200 when `None` — never to "no ceiling") and `cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>`. Both production call sites (`ai_chat_stream`, `scheduler::prepare_job_dispatch`/`scheduler_tick`) now read `job_ceiling_tool_calls` from `ai_settings` the same read-time-fallback shape `max_tool_iterations` already uses, clamped `.max(max_tool_iterations)` — **Ruling 4's `ceiling ≥ checkpoint` rule, enforced by CLAMPING, not validating/rejecting** (Stia's explicit choice, stated per the task): setting them equal reproduces the pre-PR-3 stop-at-N behaviour and is the documented escape hatch.

  **Exit kinds.** `AgentExitKind::IterationCap` is **retired** (Matt's Ruling 2): Reed's scope audit proved it unreachable on every real path once every API-runtime turn auto-continues (a real cap-hit either continues or exits `Ceiling`; OC-bound turns never produce non-empty `tool_calls` through this loop at all, so they never reach the cap check either). Two new variants land with §36.2.1's exact copy: `Stopped { tool_calls_used }` ("Stopped by you after N tool calls.") and `Ceiling { ceiling }` ("Reached your job ceiling of N tool calls. Raise it in Settings → AI, or ask me to continue."). `Stopped` is a dedicated, immediate post-loop branch — no extra summarization call, since the user explicitly asked the turn to stop right now; `Ceiling` goes through the same summary pass `IterationCap` used to. Every existing test that referenced `IterationCap` by name was updated against `Ceiling` (the variant that now actually reaches that code path), not deleted — `test_ceiling_message_differs_from_no_progress_message` (renamed from `test_iteration_cap_message_differs_from_no_progress_message`), `test_summary_failure_ceiling_produces_visible_stop_message`, `test_summary_failure_with_zero_completed_tools_still_produces_message`, plus four more interim-text/post-loop-simulation tests, all re-pinned against `Ceiling`'s actual copy (which does not name completed tools, unlike the old `IterationCap`/`NoProgressTimeout` wording — asserted explicitly, not silently dropped). `test_all_done_emit_sites_include_agent_attribution`'s hardcoded site count went 3→4 (the new `Stopped` emit site).

  **Stop (§36.2.3).** New `CANCEL_FLAGS: OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<String, Arc<AtomicBool>>>>` (`ai/chat.rs`) — same shape as the existing `IMAGE_CACHE`, the closest precedent in this codebase for a per-key process-wide registry (Reed's scope audit §3.2: no existing per-session cancel registry to extend). `reset_cancel_flag` OVERWRITES the session's entry with a fresh `false` flag at the start of every new turn dispatch (`ai_chat_stream`), self-healing regardless of whether a prior turn's own cleanup ran; the SAME `Arc` clones forward onto every continuation of one turn, so Stop reaches a continuation mid-flight, not just the first segment. New `#[tauri::command] stop_turn(session_id)` sets the flag (inserting a fresh `true` one if no turn has dispatched yet, rather than no-op'ing). **Two check sites**, both pre-existing structural sites per Reed's scope audit — no restructuring needed: top of every outer-loop iteration (checked before the cap/ceiling checks, per §36.2.1's exit-priority table: Stopped outranks Ceiling/No-progress), and inside the `for tool_call in &tool_calls` batch loop, before every call past the FIRST (§36.2.3's own wording — "a tool call already in flight completes, its result is saved" — the first call in a just-returned batch is the one the provider round trip already paid for; only the second-and-later calls in the SAME batch, never yet dispatched, are what the mid-batch check exists to stop). The existing `tool_calls.iter().zip(tool_results_for_provider.iter())` message build already truncates correctly for a batch broken early; a new re-slice of `tool_calls` itself (keyed off `tool_results_log.len()`, the ground truth for "how many calls actually concluded") keeps `all_tool_calls`/the assistant message's own `tool_calls` field from reporting calls that were never dispatched.

  **Bookkeeping, Ruling 5 (Reed's two corrections):** `scheduler_tick` now awaits `run_agent_loop`'s return value (changed from `()` to `u32`, the cumulative tool-call count) and writes it to `agent_jobs.tool_calls_used` at job-turn exit — PR 2 (#3102) added the column; nothing in production wrote it (confirmed: the only three `UPDATE agent_jobs` statements were claim/missed-recompute/OC-sent, none touching this column). `load_chat_messages` and `maybe_compact_thread`'s three message-fetch queries now `SELECT synthetic, continued` — both columns existed since migration v93 but nothing selected them, so neither the progress divider nor the hidden-synthetic-row behaviour could ever reach the UI regardless of what was written. `maybe_compact_thread`'s own compaction-summary text (`conversation_text`) now filters OUT `synthetic`/`continued` rows — a "Continue." bookkeeping message or a progress divider must never be summarized as if it were real conversation content.

  **Frontend.** `Settings.svelte`: "Max tool iterations" relabeled "Checkpoint every N tool calls" (same `ai_settings.max_tool_iterations` key, label text only); new "Overall job ceiling" row (`job_ceiling_tool_calls`, default 200), clamped both directions in `handleAbBlur` so the UI can never save an impossible `ceiling < checkpoint` pair even transiently. `ChatPanel.svelte` gets a new `onStop` prop and a Stop button, shown only while `isStreaming` — **no Stop affordance existed in the frontend before this PR** (confirmed in Reed's scope audit §3.4); `ChatSidebar.svelte`'s `handleStopTurn()` invokes `stop_turn` keyed on `activeChatThreadId`. `ChatMessage` (`types.ts`) gains optional `synthetic`/`continued` booleans; `synthetic=1` rows are filtered out of all four message-assembly chains in `ChatSidebar.svelte` so a "Continue." row never renders as a chat bubble; `continued=1` rows render as a distinct divider (the row's own stored text, no sender name, no save-to-memory button) in `ChatPanel.svelte` instead of a normal assistant bubble.

  **Tests, all four required (§36.2.4), driving the real `run_agent_loop` through `tauri::test::mock_app()`'s `AppHandle<MockRuntime>` against a REAL migrated in-memory DB** (not PR 1's `new_empty_for_test()` — the checkpoint path does real `INSERT`s and a real `maybe_compact_thread` call, both needing live tables), new module `ai::chat::auto_continue_tests_3050_pr3`:
  - **Ceiling** (verbatim): fake model that ALWAYS returns a tool call (including on the post-loop summary request — its tool_calls are never read at that site, so this is harmless and is what makes a ceiling bug observable rather than masked), `max_tool_iterations=5`, `job_ceiling_tool_calls=12` → exactly 12 tool calls, 2 `continued=1` rows, 2 `synthetic=1` rows, exit `Ceiling`. **Mutation-proven:** replacing the top-of-loop `if all_tool_calls.len() as u32 >= ceiling` guard with `if false && ...` turns this red — `left: 15, right: 12` (the checkpoint's own, separate `budget_remains` check still eventually fires, but three calls late).
  - **Stop** (verbatim): cancel set from inside the mock's own response callback for request 7 (simulating Stop landing while call 7 is in flight) → exit `Stopped`, exactly 7 tool calls, exactly 7 mock dispatches (no 8th — `Stopped` has no post-loop summary call, unlike `Ceiling`), 0 continuation rows. **Mutation-proven:** replacing the top-of-loop `if cancel.load(Ordering::Relaxed)` guard with `if false && ...` turns this red — `left: 200, right: 7` (the loop ran to the default ceiling instead of stopping).

  **The scheduler tick.** `ai::scheduler::start_scheduler_tick` is spawned once from `lib.rs`'s `.setup()` via `tauri::async_runtime::spawn`, same shape as the existing `ai::extraction_worker::start_extraction_worker` block it sits next to — never a `#[tauri::command]`, never on the main thread. It runs one launch pass immediately, then calls the SAME `scheduler_tick` function every `RUNTIME_TICK_SECS` (60, new `ai/runtime_constants.rs`) — one function, two call sites, never two differently-shaped "run due jobs" implementations. **Claim-before-run:** `claim_job` is a single conditional `UPDATE agent_jobs SET status='running' ... WHERE id=? AND status='pending'`, checked via the affected-row count. Reed's scope audit confirmed this app shares ONE `rusqlite::Connection` behind one `Arc<Mutex<DbConn>>` — no `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` needed; two ticks racing serialize on the Rust mutex, not a SQLite-level lock. **Proven directly:** two real OS threads racing `claim_job` against one shared `Mutex`-guarded connection and one seeded `pending` row — exactly one wins (`test_two_threads_cannot_both_claim_one_row`). `claim_due_jobs` claims up to `ai_settings.job_concurrency` (default `RUNTIME_DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY=2`) due rows in one lock acquisition, releasing the lock before any dispatch work (HTTP calls, `run_agent_loop`) begins. **Missed-run collapse:** for `recurring`/`heartbeat` jobs, `next_run_at` is recomputed and `status` returned to `'pending'` immediately at claim time (not after the dispatched turn finishes — no `job_id`/completion-tracking field exists on `AgentLoopInputs` until §36.2's auto-continue PR), via a new minimal 5-field cron parser (`next_cron_occurrence`, no external crate — adding one would touch `Cargo.lock`) supporting `*`, exact values, comma lists, and `*/step` (covers every §36.10A preset: daily 9am, every 4h, weekly Mon 9am). `missed_count` increments by exactly ONE per collapse event, never per missed interval: a hard-coded hourly cron 3 days overdue produces one claim, one dispatched brief, `missed_count=1`, `next_run_at` strictly in the future — not ~72 runs (`test_missed_run_collapses_to_one_catch_up_not_72`, plus the same assertion through a real `scheduler_tick` call in `test_scheduler_tick_dispatches_missed_oc_job_exactly_once`). An on-time tick (due a minute ago) does not increment `missed_count` (`test_on_time_recurring_claim_does_not_increment_missed_count`).

  **Ruling 1 (Matt, 2026-10-27) — the OC recurring-job gap Reed's scope audit found, resolved, not silently assumed.** As the spec's §36.3.4 originally read, a recurring/heartbeat OC job could never actually recur: Pane records `'sent'` and never observes OC's own completion, so `next_run_at` was never recomputed for the `'sent'` terminal state — it would fire once and go permanently dormant. **Fixed:** `next_run_at` is recomputed at SEND time (generalized in this PR to claim time, for both OC and API jobs, since no completion-tracking wiring exists yet either way), the same clock-only rule §36.3.5's missed-run collapse already uses — Pane depends only on its own clock, never on observing OC. `test_oc_recurring_job_recomputes_next_run_at_at_send_time` proves a recurring OC job lands back at `status='pending'` with a future `next_run_at` after its send, not stuck at `'sent'` forever.

Job sessions call it directly with `origin IN ('spawn', 'schedule')` and `promote=false`, which never touches `is_active` for any other session on the surface (`test_create_session_internal_promote_false_never_activates`). **§36.11's invariant — "a spawn session is never a surface"** — is now mechanically enforced in `list_sessions` itself: both branches (`include_hidden` true or false) add `AND origin NOT IN ('spawn', 'schedule')`, so neither origin is ever returned regardless of what the caller asks for. A new `create_job` (`ai::scheduler`) creates the `agent_jobs` row and its job session together — no production surface calls it yet (`schedule_job`/`spawn_job` are PR 4/5), so this PR's own tests call it directly, same as every other "tool not built yet" PR in this sprint.

- internal: Split `ai/commands.rs` (46,056 lines) into five responsibility-scoped modules — `chat.rs`, `ingest.rs`, `scheduler.rs`, `connections.rs` (new), and `tools.rs` (existing, absorbing tool dispatch/execution) — plus three shared functions (`get_internal_provider`, `call_llm`, `call_llm_from_config`, and `normalize_api_endpoint`, found during the real move to also be provider-shared rather than chat-only) into the existing `provider.rs` (Fixes #3097, build brief `docs/audits/2026-10-27-scope-3097-module-split.md`). **Zero behavior change — functions moved, bodies didn't.** Every top-level item (fns, structs, enums, consts, statics, impls, and all 81 `#[cfg(test)]` modules) was bucketed by verified call-graph membership (grep, not naming guesses) and moved verbatim; cross-module calls got `use`-path updates and the minimum `pub(crate)` visibility bump needed to stay callable, nothing else. **Proof, mechanical and reproducible:** a disposable `syn`-based body-diff tool (not merged into `scripts/section-4-analyzer` — Reed's call, one-time 46k-line move, not a standing gate) matched every item by qualified name across base and after regardless of file, comparing body text byte-for-byte (visibility-insensitive) — `docs/architecture-cheat-sheet.md`'s own PR note: **1118 moved clean, 68 renamed (one generic grab-bag `mod tests` split into 14 purpose-named modules, each co-located with the bucket of the code it tests — the one deviation from pure move/use-path/visibility, fully disclosed with a 1:1 body-identical proof per rename), 15 flagged (all test-infrastructure golden-string source-scan path strings, pointing at the file the scanned code now lives in — zero logic changes)**, full breakdown and reproducible invocation in `BODY_DIFF_REPORT_3097.md` (worktree root, attached to the PR). **Absorbing dispatch into the existing `ai/tools.rs`** (rather than a second tools-named module) ends a real, pre-existing import cycle: `commands.rs` referenced `ai::tools` 56 times, `tools.rs` referenced back once (`MAX_COLUMNS_PER_CALL`/`MAX_ROWS_PER_CALL`) — both constants move with their dispatch code, so the reverse import is deleted outright, not just avoided from getting worse. **`connections.rs` is a genuine fifth module**, not a junk drawer: connection management, API-key storage (Brave/Venice/SearXNG), and model probing/listing across every provider — ~22 functions that fit none of the other four cleanly. Nothing fit nowhere; no sixth module, no stub, no leftover `commands.rs`. **Module-graph honesty, not the clean star Reed's pre-build audit predicted:** `chat`/`ingest`/`scheduler`/`tools`/`connections` each call into `provider.rs` (a true hub — nothing calls back into it); `ingest` also calls one-directionally into `connections` (`fetch_oc_agent_model`/`ai_configure_and_save`, used by `sync_initial_import`) and `tools` (the shared `atomic_write`/`policy_error` file-write-safety cluster, used by all four of `chat`/`ingest`/`scheduler`/`tools`). **Two bidirectional edges exist, found during the real move, not predicted by the pre-build audit:** `chat` ⇄ `tools` (`chat` calls into `tools` for dispatch/resolution helpers in production; `tools`' own test modules — several co-located there because they test tool-execution end-to-end including the loop's gate checks — call `chat`'s gate functions like `check_web_taint`/`check_args_parsed`/`build_messages_with_context` directly; this one is test-code-only, confirmed by grep: zero production call sites), and `chat` ⇄ `scheduler` (**a real production-code edge both directions**: `chat::call_ai_no_stream` reads `scheduler::{SYNTHESIS_MAX_TOKENS, SYNTHESIS_TEMPERATURE}` as shared LLM-call tuning constants; `scheduler` calls `chat::{is_compaction_summary, resolve_default_agent_dispatch_tuple, AI_TOOL_CALL_MAX_TOKENS, AI_TOOL_CALL_TEMPERATURE}`). Neither forms an actual runtime call cycle (A calls B calls A) — these are shared constants/utility-function uses, not mutually-recursive call chains, and Rust's module system has no init-order constraint that makes a bidirectional `use` a problem; the build is clean and every test passes. But this is a genuine deviation from "acyclic, confirmed" and from Reed's star-topology prediction, flagged here rather than silently left uncorrected in this changelog — worth Matt's explicit call on whether the shared constants/functions belong in `provider.rs` instead (follow-up, not attempted in this PR given the risk of re-opening already-green verification this late). `scripts/section-4-analyzer check-turn-origin` (bare-name allowlist, doesn't care which file a constructor sits in) confirmed clean on the split tree: 1 construction (`ai_chat_stream`), 0 violations — matching the pre-split baseline exactly. Reed's mutation audit (`docs/audits/2026-10-21-pr-3058-no-progress-timeout.md`) proved deleting either production reset site left every test green. **The extraction, mechanically:** `ai_chat_stream` now builds one `AgentLoopInputs<R>` struct (deliberately not yet carrying `continue_policy`/`job_id`/`cancel` — §36.2/§36.3 add those in later PRs) and spawns `run_agent_loop(inputs)`; the ~1670-line loop body moved verbatim, zero logic changes. Making it compile for `R = MockRuntime` needed more than the task's two named functions: `stream_anthropic` and `stream_ollama` were generified (matching `stream_openrouter`'s existing `<R: tauri::Runtime>` shape, ADR-0067 D2/D5) as asked, but that alone wasn't sufficient — `execute_single_tool` (and transitively `execute_set_status` → `notes::update_note_internal` → `notifications::check_due_dates_for_task` → `emit_due_notification` → `process_notification`) also took a concrete `AppHandle` and had to be generified the same mechanical way to let the loop's tool-execution path compile under a mock runtime too. Every existing concrete call site still infers `R = Wry` with zero edits. **The new test** (`real_loop_integration_tests_3059`) drives the real `run_agent_loop::<MockRuntime>` through 6 iterations via a mocked Ollama endpoint (the one provider arm whose connection target, `endpoint`, is a plain field rather than a hardcoded production URL) — 5 iterations each gate-refused by `check_tool_offered` (deliberately empty `offered_tool_names`; per the loop's own comment, a gate refusal still counts as a finished tool call and still fires the real reset) with a real, bounded 250ms delay induced via `mockito::Mock::with_chunked_body`'s documented chunk-sleep seam, then a 6th tool-call-free iteration ending cleanly — total elapsed (~1.3s) exceeds a shrunk `idle_timeout_seconds` of 1 (the field is a plain loop input, not clamped by the loop itself), while no single iteration ever does, proving the fixed reset wiring without a real 120+-second wait. **Both required mutation proofs ran and are documented in the PR's `## §4 test-the-test` section**, including the honest result that deleting reset-1-of-2 alone stays green (matching that reset site's own doc comment: today's control flow always reaches reset 2 first) — only reset-2-of-2's deletion is independently load-bearing, and that is what the new test actually proves red. **Deleted** the old mirror (`no_progress_timeout_tests_3053::test_multi_iteration_job_past_old_120s_is_not_cut_off`, plus its now-orphaned `backdated_instant`/`pre_fix_wall_clock_check` helpers) once the replacement was green; `ai/timeout_tests.rs` (settings-resolution coverage only, confirmed to hold zero references to the deleted test) was correctly left untouched. **`TurnOrigin`** (`enum { User, Job }`) is introduced as a field on `AgentLoopInputs`, constructed once, in `ai_chat_stream`, as `TurnOrigin::User` — the only other sanctioned site, the scheduler tick (§36.3), doesn't exist until PR 2. **Ships alongside it:** a second rule in `scripts/section-4-analyzer` (`check-turn-origin`, a new CLI subcommand) — a `syn` visitor of a genuinely different shape than the existing one (finds every enum-variant construction expression in the whole tree first, then asks which function encloses it, rather than checking one known function for a known call), gated by a name-based allowlist that fails closed on any unlisted enclosing function. Found and fixed a real bug in its own design while writing its fixture tests: `syn`'s `Pat::Path` is literally typed as `ExprPath` (no separate pattern-visitor method exists for it), so a `match` arm on the same variant name would have been misflagged as a construction without an explicit `visit_pat` override that skips pattern subtrees entirely — caught by the rule's own fixture tests before it ever ran against real code, not after. `#[cfg(test)]`-gated construction (including this PR's own test fixture) is exempt by design, not by oversight — code that never ships in a release binary cannot produce a turn nobody typed. Scanning the real `src-tauri/src/`+`src-gateway/src/` tree today finds exactly 1 construction (the new `ai_chat_stream` site) and 0 violations. New CI job (`turn-origin-ast-check`) runs on every PR, unlike the two existing §4 jobs, since a violation could land in a file this PR never otherwise touches. 13 new fixture tests (analyzer logic ~130 lines, tests ~280 lines — the task's own "~100 lines" estimate explicitly excluded the test suite). **No functional change; full retest ahead of it** — baseline (`origin/main` @ `354b398d`, scratch worktree, `PANE_TEST_ROOT`, `--skip tests::test_backup::`, `--test-threads=1`) **2618 passed, 1 failed, 9 ignored, 11 filtered**; this branch, same invocation, **2618 passed, 1 failed, 9 ignored, 11 filtered** — identical counts (the one deleted test and one added test cancel out). - **Model picker search ignored Venice's tag data, and the "Enter custom model name..." box appeared even on providers whose list is already authoritative (Fixes #3083).**

  **Reed's scope audit (`docs/audits/2026-10-26-scope-3083-picker-ux.md`) read the code right and the issue wrong.** It traced `filteredModels()` correctly — matching only `name`/`provider`/`id` — and concluded "no action needed" because that's the issue's premise, not its defect. The actual ask: tags (`tier_label`, `supports_tee_attestation`, `supports_e2ee`) should count as search terms, and the custom-entry box should not render on providers whose list is already the full truth. Both are now built, using the audit's correct code findings as the starting point.

  **Tag-aware search.** `filteredModels()` (`SearchableModelSelect.svelte`) now also matches a model when the typed text is a substring of `tier_label` (Venice's raw privacy-tier string) or of the row's own rendered capability-tag text — `"TEE"` for `supports_tee_attestation`, `"E2EE not supported in Pane"` for `supports_e2ee`. Matching the *rendered label*, not the raw flag name, is deliberate — it keeps "what's searchable" identical to "what the row visibly shows." `supports_function_calling` is excluded on purpose: #2988 PR2 ruled it renders no picker tag in this PR (reserved for a future tool-eligibility filter), and making an invisible capability searchable would let a user find something Pane never shows them. **The absent-flag guarantee holds for search exactly as it already does for rendering** — `if (m.supports_tee_attestation)` is false for both `undefined` and `false`, so a model with no capability data structurally cannot surface under a `TEE` search (the #3060 failure mode, one layer below rendering, per #3083's own framing). Name/provider/id matching is unchanged; tag matching is additive.

  **Custom-model entry box gated by namespace.** The "Enter custom model name..." action (unconditional since #2894, inherited by all 21 `SearchableModelSelect` call sites: Settings.svelte ×7, AgentCreateOverlay.svelte ×1, Onboarding.svelte ×13) now renders only when the picker's `provider` prop is in a single named, documented allowlist (`OPEN_NAMESPACE_PROVIDERS`, currently `{'openrouter'}`) — shown for OpenRouter (an open, constantly-growing third-party catalog Pane's own list can legitimately lag behind), hidden for Venice/Anthropic/Ollama (each returns its own complete, authoritative live list, so a typed name absent from it is almost certainly a typo, not a real unlisted model — the Venice `TEE` case the issue named). An unknown or omitted `provider` defaults **closed** — fail-safe, not fail-open. Every one of the 21 call sites now threads its own already-existing provider-tracking variable through as the new `provider` prop (`internalProvider`, `ssProvider`, `sfProvider`, `connectProvider`, `selectedRuntimeType`, `agent.runtime_type` — no new state invented, no magic strings beyond the one allowlist constant). All 21 call sites were checked directly; none assumed the box must always be present beyond the existing design (the box is a convenience affordance, never the only way to set a model — every call site falls back to a plain read-only string for an out-of-list value).

  **Tests, in the component's existing DOM-render harness** (`SearchableModelSelect.test.ts` already renders via `@testing-library/svelte` — unlike `Settings.svelte`, no extraction to a separate predicate module was needed, confirmed by Reed's audit §4 and re-verified here): 5 new tag-search tests (TEE-flag match, E2EE-label match, raw `tier_label` match, the #3075 absent-flag guarantee holding under search, and the pre-existing name/provider/id rule still matching unchanged), Reed's 2 named pinning tests (search-scope false-positive guard; a custom/typed selection structurally never carries a capability tag), and 5 custom-box-gating tests (shown for OpenRouter, hidden for each of Venice/Anthropic/Ollama, and the fail-closed default when `provider` is omitted). 5 pre-existing tests that asserted the custom button's presence without specifying a provider were updated to pass `provider: 'openrouter'` (the box's visibility is no longer unconditional, so these generic-dropdown-behavior tests needed an explicit reason to expect it). `Settings.test.ts`'s source-level regex for the Agents-tab model-edit picker was updated for the new `provider={agent.runtime_type ?? undefined}` line.

  **Spec:** `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §28.5 gains the TEE/E2EE capability-tag description (closing a gap #3075 left — it shipped the flags with zero coverage in this file, only in `smart-routing.md` §27.6 and `onboarding.md` §6.4 for an unrelated line), a new §28.5a (search scope, including the `supports_function_calling` exclusion and its reasoning), and a new §28.5b (the custom-entry namespace gate and its reasoning). No merged PR had specced either of these — this PR's own spec edit is the coverage, not a `spec-covered-by:` reference. `src/lib/components/Settings.svelte` and `Onboarding.svelte` are both touched (provider-threading only, no behavioral changes to either file otherwise), which puts this PR on `scripts/check-spec-first.sh`'s strict `CORE_BEHAVIORAL` path — satisfied by the real `docs/spec/` edit above, not a skip.

This branch: **3120 passed, 1 skipped** (+12, exactly the new tests — 5 tag-search + 2 pinning + 5 gating — zero regressions). `svelte-check`: exactly the same 2 pre-existing errors (`sheetSnapshotEnvelope.ts:242`, `Editor.svelte:2125`) and no new error.
