- **`switch_embedding_engine` froze the whole UI for the duration of a semantic-search re-index, and `/embeddings` was called once per item instead of in batches (Fixes #3082).**

  **Root cause, found in git history and Reed's #2988-era audit trail, not guessed:** `switch_embedding_engine` is a plain `#[tauri::command] pub fn` (not `async fn`), so it ran the entire `run_embedding_pipeline` call — settings writes, stale-row clearing, credential building, and every embed+store call for every note/fact/chat — in-line on Tauri's main/event-loop thread. A synchronous command is never implicitly routed to a blocking pool; Reed's own #2988 scope had assumed otherwise and retracted it in a follow-up audit (`docs/audits/2026-10-26-scope-3082-embed-blocking.md`) after re-reading the actual Tauri dispatch model. Matt reproduced it live on 1.0.64: 178 notes, 375 facts, 226 chats re-indexed with the window frozen for the whole run. The sibling command that runs the same pipeline, `run_integrity_check`, was already correct — it drops its DB lock and hands the pipeline to `std::thread::spawn` before returning — and is untouched by this fix, confirmed by a direct re-read of its body at this PR's base commit.

  **The fix: `async fn` + `spawn_blocking`, the #1921/R7 shape, plus #1296's `State<DbState>` pattern.** `switch_embedding_engine` is now `pub async fn`; its validation (pure, no I/O) stays synchronous, and the entire settings/clear/credential/pipeline/terminal-status sequence moves inside one `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || { ... })` closure, with the `JoinError` (thread panic) surfaced via `.await.map_err(...)?` and an `embeddings://status` error emit — the exact shape `create_backup` established for #1921. `db.0.clone()` (an `Arc<Mutex<DbConn>>`) is cloned before `spawn_blocking` and the lock is acquired only inside the closure, at the same three brief sites the pre-existing code already used (settings persist, credential-build-failure path, terminal status write) — the pipeline itself still runs against its own separate `rusqlite::Connection`, as before, never holding the main mutex.

  **Moving the pipeline off the main thread makes a second, concurrent switch reachable for the first time** (the old main-thread block serialized every call by construction). Matt's ruling: reject it, don't queue or interleave it. A new `EmbeddingSwitchGuard` (`AtomicBool` + RAII `Drop`, identical shape to `backup.rs`'s `BackupGuard`) is acquired as the first statement in the command, before `spawn_blocking` starts, and returns `Err("a re-index is already running")` if a switch is already in flight. No cancellation is built here — Matt: *"that comes later with the harness Stop plumbing."*

  **`/embeddings` is now batched, 25 items per call (configurable, never hardcoded).** `resolve_embeddings_batch_size` (`ai/commands.rs`) follows the exact precedence/logging discipline `resolve_embeddings_max_tokens` already established in this file: read `ai_settings.embeddings_batch_size`, clamp to a sane 1–100 range, fall through to a named, logged default (`EMBEDDINGS_BATCH_SIZE_DEFAULT = 25`) — chosen because it exactly matches the pipeline's existing per-25-item progress-throttle cadence, so one full batch lines up with one progress tick with zero new cadence bookkeeping. `build_http_embed_batch_fn` (`lib.rs`) is a new, separate constructor mirroring all three engine arms (OpenRouter/Ollama/Venice) of the existing `build_http_embed_fn`, sending an array `input` and parsing the full `data[]`/`embeddings[]` response array; `build_http_embed_fn` itself is untouched (still used, unbatched, by query-time semantic search and both already-correct pipeline callers above).

  **Batch-with-fallback error attribution — the subtlest risk, handled explicitly.** A provider's `/embeddings` endpoint returns one HTTP response per request; there is no partial success within a single call, so a batch alone cannot identify which item was bad. `run_embedding_pipeline`'s inner loop (one shared implementation, `run_embedding_pipeline_impl`, backs both the pre-existing unbatched entry point and the new `run_embedding_pipeline_batched` — not two parallel copies of the pipeline) buffers up to `batch_size` pending items per sub-pass and, on any non-auth batch failure (HTTP error, JSON error, or a returned vector count that doesn't match the request — never positionally zipped against an unexpected shape), falls back to the exact pre-existing per-item `embed_with_token_retry` loop **for that one batch only**. One bad item in a batch of 25 is attributed to that item alone; the other 24 are stored normally either way. An auth failure (401/403) still aborts the whole pipeline immediately, never retried per-item. The unbatched path (`run_integrity_check`, the startup pipeline) is unchanged byte-for-byte — it delegates to the same shared implementation with `batch = None`, verified by every pre-existing pipeline test passing unmodified.

  **Tests, through the real pipeline functions, never raw `INSERT` for the embeddings operation itself** (fixture tables — `notes`/`ai_memory`/`chat_messages_local` — are seeded via direct `INSERT`, the same established convention every pre-existing test in `embeddings.rs`'s own test module already uses; this diverges from the stricter "real command" bar for fixture seeding specifically, flagged here rather than silently): the async/`spawn_blocking` shape is pinned via a golden-string source scan (UI responsiveness itself can't be exercised in-suite — the same technique this file's `switch_embedding_engine_tests` module already uses for its other `AppHandle`-constrained gate, since `tauri::test::mock_app()`'s `AppHandle<MockRuntime>` cannot satisfy a command's concrete `AppHandle<Wry>` parameter); `EmbeddingSwitchGuard` is exercised directly (single acquire/release, overlapping-thread rejection with the exact message, release-then-reacquire); `resolve_embeddings_batch_size` is tested for default/configured/clamped/unparseable; `run_embedding_pipeline_batched` is tested for identical `(notes, facts, chats, failed)` counts against the unbatched path over a 60-item corpus, batch-size-driven call counts (25 vs 10), progress firing at the same per-25 cadence, a length-mismatch response falling back without mis-attribution, an auth error aborting immediately, and — the direct regression test for the issue's stated risk — one poisoned item inside a 25-item batch landing in `failed_count` alone while the other 24 store successfully. Two new mockito-backed tests exercise the real, production `build_http_embed_batch_fn` end-to-end for the Venice arm (array in, array out, HTTP-error propagation), the one engine whose base URL is test-overridable (same `test_set_venice_embed_base` mechanism the existing single-item Venice tests use). **No Venice key exists on this host; every HTTP assertion above is mock-verified at the boundary, not a live account.**

  **Spec:** `docs/spec/memory-pipeline.md` §5.9.3 gains the corrected main-thread rule (stated precisely, per #3084's lesson that a spec paragraph misdescribing *why* a test exists is how the next person deletes it) and the reject-guard contract; §5.9.5 gains the batching + batch-with-fallback behavior. No prior merged PR specced this blocking/batching behavior — this PR's own spec edit is the coverage, not a backward `spec-covered-by:` reference.

  **Base verification:** this PR's branch was cut from `origin/main` @ `9ffd0eb6` (#3084's merge commit). Reed's scope audit for this issue was written against an earlier fetch of `origin/main` and cited several `file:line` locations that have since shifted by #3084's `ai/commands.rs` changes (+174/−2 lines) — `switch_embedding_engine` (27716→27739), `run_integrity_check` (27566→27590, matching this PR's own base-commit re-read), `get_embeddings_counts` (28009→28032), `fetch_embedding_models` (27945→27968), `resolve_embeddings_max_tokens` ("27696-27712"→27722) all moved by the same ~+23-line offset; every citation was re-verified by direct `grep -n`/re-read against this PR's actual base commit before editing, not trusted from the audit doc.

  **Counts** (worktree `/tmp/pane-worktrees/3082-async-reindex`, `PANE_TEST_ROOT` scratch root, `--test-threads=1`, `--skip tests::test_backup::`): baseline (own re-run against unmodified `origin/main` @ `9ffd0eb6`, separate worktree + `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`) **2600 passed, 2 failed, 8 ignored, 11 filtered**; this branch **2618 passed, 2 failed, 8 ignored, 11 filtered** (+18, exactly the new tests, zero regressions). Both failures are identical on both runs and pre-existing, confirmed not to be the same thing: `ai::commands::tombstoning_tests::test_upgrade_from_v85_fixture_migrates_cleanly_to_v86` (`no such function: crsql_internal_sync_bit`, cr-sqlite not loaded in test mode) and `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert` (a TCP-bind-class flake under full-suite contention) — two distinct pre-existing failures, not mislabeled as one (the #3078 mislabeling mistake). Frontend: **not re-run** — zero `src/` files touched by this PR; the task brief's given main baseline (3108 passed / 1 skipped) is inherited, not independently re-verified here. **Both smokes run for real** against a debug binary built with a separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` and copied (never symlinked) into `src-tauri/target/debug/pane`: `smoke-fresh-db` — PASS (ready signal). `smoke-upgrade-db` — PASS against the real v91→v92 fixture (ready signal). `src-tauri/resources/crsqlite.dylib` confirmed 1,631,456 bytes, untouched. - **Venice chat 400s on `cache_control`, and Venice (and OC) HTTP errors misclassified as gateway connection failures (Fixes #3081).**

  **Defect 1 — the 400.** Pane added an Anthropic-style `cache_control` marker to the system message and second-to-last message on every OpenAI-shaped-path request, unconditionally — OC, OpenRouter, and Venice alike. Some Venice backends reject it: `abliteration-abliterated-model-large-flash` 400s with `Text content parts may only include type and text`; GLM and Qwen on the same endpoint tolerate it. Venice caches server-side regardless, so the marker bought nothing there even on a model that accepted it. **Fix:** a new shared helper, `apply_anthropic_cache_control` (`openrouter.rs`), gated on `RequestOrigin::Venice` — never on `base_url`, per ADR-0065 D1 (Matt's explicit instruction: branch on the provider enum, the type that already carries the distinction, not a URL string that breaks on a custom endpoint or a self-hosted Venice). **Both application sites fixed**, confirmed by direct read, not assumption: `chat_with_tools_inner` and `stream_openrouter_inner` each carried an identical, independently-maintained copy of this exact marker logic; both now call the one helper. **Searched for a third site** (`grep -rn cache_control` across `src-tauri/src` and `src`): four more hits exist in `anthropic.rs`, but that file is the dedicated Anthropic-direct provider path — confirmed by tracing every `AiProvider::Venice` dispatch site in `commands.rs` that Venice *always* routes through `openrouter.rs`'s OpenAI-shaped functions and never reaches `anthropic.rs`, so those four sites are unreachable from Venice and correctly untouched. One comment-only mention in `commands.rs` (no code) was left as-is.

  **Defect 2 — the misclassification, and a real bug one layer deeper than the issue described.** Investigating "Venice 400 classified as `gateway_connection_failed`" found that `classify_gateway_error`'s existing generic 4xx-to-`gateway_provider_error` catch-all (ADR-0067 D4, §4A.2.5 — already provider-agnostic, not OC-specific despite its section title) looked correct against every existing test fixture, all of which used a synthetic error-string shape like `"API error (400): Bad Request"`. The actual string `chat_with_tools_inner`/`stream_openrouter_inner` build is `format!("API error ({}): {}", status, msg)` where `status: reqwest::StatusCode` — and `StatusCode`'s `Display` impl writes the canonical reason phrase after the number (`"400 Bad Request"`, confirmed empirically against this reqwest version), not a bare `"400"`. `parse_api_error_status` took the *entire* span between `"api error ("` and the next `')'` and parsed that whole span as the number, which only succeeds when that span is a bare number — never, in production. **Every 4xx this branch was meant to catch has been silently falling through to `gateway_connection_failed` since ADR-0067 D4 shipped (Sep 22) — OC's own "Multiple agents are configured..." 400, the one this branch was originally written for, included, not just Venice's.** That also meant OC's deterministic 400 was wrongly eligible for the §22C.12.4 reconnect retry loop the whole time. **Fix:** `parse_api_error_status` now takes only the leading run of ASCII digits after the marker, not the full span to `')'`. Separately, `test_reconnect_loop_source_shape_stays_openclaw_only` confirms by direct source inspection that the §22C.12.4 reconnect loop itself is gated on `AiProvider::OpenClaw` and can never be entered by a Venice dispatch regardless of classification — a second, independent reason a Venice 4xx was never actually retried even before this fix, on top of now classifying correctly.

  **Tests, through real production entry points, mocked at the HTTP boundary (mockito) — never raw simulation of the logic:** `ai::openrouter::cache_control_tests` (5 tests) exercise the real `OpenRouterProvider::chat_with_tools` dispatch against a mocked Venice/OpenRouter server, proving no `cache_control` reaches the wire on Venice and that it still does on OpenRouter (regression guard), plus direct unit coverage of the shared helper for Venice/OpenRouter/OpenClaw. `ai::reconnect_tests` and `ai::commands::tests` gained real-`reqwest::StatusCode`-built fixtures (not hand-typed guesses at `Display` output) proving the root-cause fix repairs both Venice's 400 and OC's original 400 case, that `gateway_provider_error` stays absent from `should_chat_retry`'s retryable set, and that a genuine connection failure (no HTTP response at all) still classifies `gateway_unreachable`/retries normally. **No Venice API key exists on this host — every Venice-path assertion above is mock-verified against the real dispatch code, not a live account.** Still needs Matt's live pass against the real Venice endpoint with `abliteration-abliterated-model-large-flash` to confirm the 400 is gone and the UI shows Venice's own message instead of "couldn't connect to your gateway."

  **Spec:** `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.3.4 (Venice Runtime Request Shape) gains a "No `cache_control`" subsection and a corrected error-copy table (the pre-existing table specified bespoke Venice copy for 401/403/other-4xx that was never actually built — the shared `gateway_auth_failed`/`gateway_provider_error` mechanism is what ships; the 401/403 mismatch, showing gateway-pairing language to a non-gateway runtime, is flagged as pre-existing drift and left as a follow-up, out of #3081's scope). §26.3/§26.4/§26.7/§26.9 (Prompt Caching) gain a Venice row and a correction to the previously-universal "unknown `cache_control` fields are ignored by providers that don't support them" claim, which this issue disproves for at least one Venice model. §4A.2.5 gains a note that its classification was already provider-agnostic, not OC-only, and that #3081 locks that in with tests rather than changing its scope.

  **Counts** (worktree `/tmp/pane-worktrees/3081-venice-cache-control`, `PANE_TEST_ROOT` scratch root, `--test-threads=1`, `--skip tests::test_backup::`): baseline (own re-run against unmodified `origin/main` @ `16ae9fe2`, separate worktree + `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`) **2589 passed, 1 failed, 8 ignored, 11 filtered**; this branch **2601 passed, 1 failed, 8 ignored, 11 filtered** (+12, exactly the new tests, zero regressions). The 1 failure on both runs is the identical pre-existing fixture failure (`ai::commands::tombstoning_tests::test_upgrade_from_v85_fixture_migrates_cleanly_to_v86`, `no such function: crsql_internal_sync_bit` — cr-sqlite not loaded in test mode, unrelated to this change, not chased). Frontend `pnpm test`: **3108 passed, 1 skipped** — identical to main's documented baseline; no `src/` files touched by this PR. **Both smokes run for real** against the debug binary: `smoke-fresh-db` — PASS (ready signal, `smoke-grep.sh` 0 violations). `smoke-upgrade-db` — PASS against the real v91→v92 fixture (ready signal, `smoke-grep.sh` 0 violations, 2 allowlisted pre-existing `[CRITICAL]` lines unrelated to this change). `src-tauri/resources/crsqlite.dylib` confirmed 1,631,456 bytes before and after, not symlinked or touched. No `Cargo.lock`/`package-lock.json` changes.

- **`notes_fts` search index rebuilt with the native FTS5 command, not on every launch (Fixes #3072).**

  **Root cause, found in git history, not guessed:** `notes_fts` is an external-content FTS5 table (`content='notes'`) whose triggers have correctly indexed the full `notes.body` since #486 (`9df638a4`, Apr 2026). But a leftover block from the design #486 replaced — `305afa11`'s Mar 2026 standalone-table rebuild — kept running on **every single launch**: `DELETE FROM notes_fts` followed by a non-transactional, per-row disk-read `INSERT` loop. Any reader landing in the gap between the `DELETE` and the loop finishing saw the index empty while `notes` was full and reported "malformed" — which self-healed on the next launch (same block ran again), which is why this was reported four times (#2352, #2566, #2610) and fixed zero times.

  **The fix:** the startup thread now runs the FTS5-native `'integrity-check'` first — cheap, and (critically) only compares the index against `notes` when invoked with `rank=1` (`INSERT INTO notes_fts(notes_fts, rank) VALUES('integrity-check', 1)`; without `rank=1` an external-content table's integrity-check only validates its own internal structure and would never notice index/content drift, confirmed empirically against a deliberately-drifted fixture). Only if that reports a problem does the native `'rebuild'` run (reusing `migrations.rs`'s existing `rebuild_fts_indexes`, not a forked copy), wrapped in one explicit transaction together with a status write so no reader ever observes a partial index. `verify_backup_integrity` (`backup.rs`) gets the same `rank=1` check on the staged copy before a Migration/Manual/Daily/Weekly/PreRestore backup is published — skipped gracefully (not an error) if `notes_fts` doesn't exist on that DB at all. Neither check touches `BackupPacing::FullSpeed` or the migration backup's file-copy step — #3064's 11-minute-launch fix is untouched.

  **"Empty is not zero":** a new `ai_settings` key pair, `notes_fts_rebuild_status` (`"ok"` / `"failed"`) + `notes_fts_rebuild_at`, is written on every attempt — absence of the key means this logic never ran at all (older binary, crash before reaching it), distinct from `"ok"` (confirmed healthy, via a clean check or a successful repair) and `"failed"` (a rebuild was required and did not complete; logged with a stable `[FTS-REBUILD-FAILED]` prefix). The status write and the rebuild attempt commit together — a committed `"failed"` status is itself the correct durable outcome, not something to roll back.

  **The watcher gap stays as-is, deliberately, per Matt's ruling:** the removed block was also the only code path that noticed an external edit to an already-tracked note's `.md` file made while Pane was closed. Verified directly against the code (not just Reed's scope note): `watcher.rs::process_new_file` explicitly skips any file path already present in `notes`, `run_startup_reconciliation` has zero call sites (dead code), and its companion `reimport_file_to_db` targets a `content` column `notes` doesn't have (agent-system-file-specific, already broken, out of scope). There is no "few lines reusing the running watcher's import" available — reconciling modified tracked files needs new mtime tracking (none exists for ordinary notes today) and a locking-safe call path (`update_note_internal` re-locks `DbState`, which would deadlock if called from inside this already-locked startup thread). Conclusion: **own PR**, not this one.

  **Tests, through real commands (`create_note_internal`), never raw `INSERT`** (drift is simulated by deleting a `notes_fts` row directly — a test harness breaking the fixture on purpose, not a stand-in for a user action): a clean index is not rebuilt and is marked `"ok"`; a drifted index is fully repaired (not just the broken row) and marked `"ok"`; a forced rebuild failure is marked `"failed"`, never left absent; a DB that never ran the gate has no status key at all. `backup.rs` gets a focused test proving `verify_backup_integrity` now fails on `notes_fts` drift that `PRAGMA integrity_check` alone passes.

  **Both smokes run for real, against the debug build:** `smoke-fresh-db` — PASS, `[FTS] notes_fts integrity-check passed — no rebuild needed` (no rebuild on a healthy DB). `smoke-upgrade-db` (real v91→v92 fixture) — PASS; the fixture's `notes_fts` turned out to already be genuinely drifted (a fixture-generation artifact, not a #3072 bug), so this run is a live, unstaged demonstration of the whole mechanism working: `[BACKUP] notes_fts integrity-check failed ... retrying` → `[FTS] notes_fts integrity-check FAILED — drift detected, rebuilding` → `[FTS] notes_fts rebuild succeeded`, migration completes, ready signal fires, `smoke-grep.sh` reports zero severity violations on both runs.

  **Counts (worktree `/tmp/pane-worktrees/3072-native-fts-rebuild`, `PANE_TEST_ROOT` scratch root, `--test-threads=1`):** `cargo test --lib -- --skip tests::test_backup:: --test-threads=1`: **2587 passed, 3 failed, 8 ignored, 11 filtered out**. All 3 failures confirmed pre-existing by reproducing identically on an unmodified `origin/main` checkout in isolation: `ai::commands::tombstoning_tests::test_upgrade_from_v85_fixture_migrates_cleanly_to_v86` (pre-existing `crsql_internal_sync_bit` missing-function fixture failure, test mode has no cr-sqlite loaded — not a #3072 regression); `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert` (passes in isolation on both branches — a TCP-bind-class flake under full-suite contention); `notes::item2874_trash_lifecycle_tests::test_empty_trash_leaves_unmovable_item_in_trash_and_reports_the_count` (real macOS Finder/AppleScript timeout, reproduces identically on baseline in isolation). Zero failures attributable to this change. No frontend files touched by this PR.

- **An agent's model can be changed after creation (Fixes #3074).**

  Previously the model was fixed at agent creation: the Settings → Agents row showed it as read-only text, and the inline edit affordance only ever sent `name`. The backend already supported the change — `update_agent` accepts and persists `model`, and dispatch re-reads `ai_agents.model` on every turn — so this wires up the missing UI.

  A second inline pencil sits beside the model text, mirroring the existing rename affordance. Selecting a model saves immediately (a dropdown cannot blur-save the way a text input does), matching the Smart Routing and Extraction model pickers in the same screen. The picker reuses `SearchableModelSelect`, so a Venice agent also shows its "TEE" / "E2EE not supported in Pane" capability tags here.

  **The picker only appears for `anthropic`, `openrouter`, `venice` and `ollama` agents.** Two exclusions, both deliberate: OpenClaw agents keep read-only model text because `write_back_agent_model_if_changed` (ADR-0063 D9) reverts a manual edit to whatever the gateway resolved after the next successful stream — a picker there would appear to work, then silently undo itself. Legacy agents with no pinned runtime are excluded for the same reason their model is already hidden elsewhere. `runtime_type` itself remains immutable; the save payload carries only `agent_id` and `model`.

  Known gap, tracked separately as #3076: nothing in dispatch checks `supportsFunctionCalling`, so an agent can be switched onto a model that cannot call tools without warning.
- **Venice model capabilities carried through deserialization, and honest "TEE"/"E2EE not supported in Pane" picker labels (Fixes #2988).**

  **The bug, in one line:** `fetch_venice_models`'s `VeniceModelSpec` declared only `privacy`; Venice's `model_spec.capabilities.{supportsTeeAttestation,supportsE2EE,supportsFunctionCalling}` object had no matching Rust field, so serde silently dropped it on every `/models` fetch — the picker had no way to tell the truth about a model's TEE/E2EE/tool-calling capabilities.

  **The fix:** a new `VeniceModelCapabilities` struct (`ai/commands.rs`, inside `fetch_venice_models`) with the three flags nested exactly where Venice's live OpenAPI schema puts them, threaded through to three new `Option<bool>` fields on `ModelInfo` (`ai/provider.rs`): `supports_tee_attestation`, `supports_e2ee`, `supports_function_calling`. The other 8 non-Venice `ModelInfo` construction sites (Anthropic, OpenRouter ×2, Ollama ×2, the Venice *embeddings* lister, OpenClaw ×2) get `None` for all three — mechanical, no real values, since only the Venice chat-model lister has this data.

  **The absent-flag ruling, stated explicitly and pinned by test (Matt's call):** `capabilities` can be legitimately absent from Venice's response for non-text model types, and even when present, Pane's struct must not assume server-side conformance to the schema's own `required` array. Both shapes — the whole object missing, or one flag missing within a present object — collapse to `None`. **`None` renders identically to `false` in the picker; it must never read as "supported."** No `unwrap_or(true)`/`unwrap_or_default()` anywhere in the new code path — this is the exact #3060 failure mode one layer down, which is why #2988 exists.

  **Picker labels (`SearchableModelSelect.svelte`), copy fixed per Matt's ruling, not revisited:** `"TEE"` when `supports_tee_attestation`; `"E2EE not supported in Pane"` (never a "Private" badge) when `supports_e2ee` — Pane sends zero of Venice's E2EE handshake (no `X-Venice-TEE-*` headers anywhere in the codebase), so even though Matt's live test (`e2ee-glm-5-3-p`, plain request, tools worked) proved TEE-backed tool calls work fine, it proved nothing about E2EE itself. The two tags render from **two independent `{#if}` blocks**, not an else-chain — Venice's schema requires `supportsE2EE` models to also have `supportsTeeAttestation`, so a model can legitimately show both tags at once; an else-chain would silently hide one. `supports_function_calling` is carried through the struct but **not rendered as a tag in this PR** — reserved for a future per-model tool-eligibility filter per Matt's ruling.

Lock diff confirmed via `git diff --numstat -- src-tauri/Cargo.lock`: `1  1` — the single `[[package]] name = "pane"` version line, no dependency churn, per the §8a carve-out (#3056/#3062). `scripts/check-version-parity.sh` confirms all four agree at `1.0.63`. This is the version-bump PR that unblocks the 1.0.63 DMG build, Matt's install check, and Xavier's release.
- **Bumped to 1.0.62 with the lock, and gated app `Cargo.lock` version parity in CI (Relates to #3056).** Root cause in one line: #3048's bump raised `package.json`/`src-tauri/Cargo.toml`/`src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` to 1.0.61 but the standing no-lock-changes-in-PRs rule reverted the matching `Cargo.lock` line with no documented exception, and nothing in CI noticed — the app's lock sat on `1.0.60` while the three manifests said `1.0.61`. **This PR:** bumps all four files together to `1.0.62` (the lock's own diff is the single `[[package]] name = "pane"` version line, confirmed via `git diff --numstat`: `1  1`, no dependency churn); extends `scripts/check-version-parity.sh` to check `src-tauri/Cargo.lock` against the three manifests, reusing the gateway's existing name-keyed awk parser (now shared via `scripts/lib/cargo-lock-version.sh`) rather than writing a second one, so the two lock-parsing paths can't diverge — `scripts/check-gateway-version-bump.sh` is unchanged in behavior, just sources the shared helper; and writes the standing rule's first documented carve-out (`docs/REVIEW-CHECKLIST.md` §8a) so a release-bump PR's required lock diff is never again mistaken for an out-of-scope stray change. `docs/SPAWN-CHECKLISTS.md` §C.6 and `docs/release-runbook.md` updated to point at the carve-out and require the lock in the same PR as the bump. No trigger change needed — CI's existing `version-parity` job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) already runs on every PR to `main` with no path filter, since the manifests can drift from the lock on any version-bump PR, not only ones touching `src-tauri/`.

### Added
- **PR B of 2 on #2723 — on a migrating launch, the window opens first and shows real progress instead of a blank screen. (Relates to #2723)**

  **The behaviour change, in one line:** a migrating launch used to leave the window completely unpainted — Tauri's declarative window (`tauri.conf.json`, no `WebviewWindowBuilder`, no `"visible": false`) can't paint until `.run()` starts pumping the native event loop, and `.setup()` (which runs *before* `.run()`) used to block on the full DB init, including PR A's now-fast-but-still-present backup and the schema migration itself — until this PR, that was a silent, multi-second-to-multi-minute gap with zero feedback. Now the window paints immediately and shows "Updating Pane… don't quit" with live progress while the real work runs in the background; every other (non-migrating) launch is provably unchanged.

  **How the window gets up before DB init, and how ordering is guaranteed.** A cheap, read-only pre-check (`database::is_migration_pending`) decides, before any work starts, which of two paths this launch takes. **Fast path (no migration pending — the overwhelming majority of launches):** `complete_db_dependent_startup` runs inline, on the setup thread, byte-for-byte what this code always did — no new thread, same `?` propagation on a hard failure. **Window-first path (migration pending):** `.setup()` records `StartupStatus::MigrationRequired`, emits `startup://migration-required`, and returns immediately without touching the DB; `complete_db_dependent_startup` — the *same function* the fast path calls inline — then runs on a `std::thread::spawn`'d background thread, generalizing issue #353's already-shipped daily-backup-to-background-thread pattern (commit `0880f573`) to the one case that can actually block the window. **Ordering guarantee** (Reed's explicit requirement — `set_schema_version` must complete before any dependent setup block runs, on both paths): held structurally, not by convention. `database::init_database_with_progress(...)?` cannot return a `Connection` without `migrations::run_migrations_with_progress`'s `set_schema_version` having already run to completion on every reachable match arm; `startup::mount_db_state_then(app, conn, on_db_ready)` is a two-line function — `manager.manage(DbState::new(conn))`, then `on_db_ready(manager)` — so the dependent-block closure cannot run before `conn` is mounted, by ordinary sequential execution within one function body that both paths call identically. Proved by execution, not just read: `startup::test_schema_version_committed_before_db_state_is_managed` copies the real `tests/fixtures/upgrade-from-v91.db` fixture, runs the real `run_migrations` on it, then calls `mount_db_state_then` against `tauri::test::mock_app()` with a spy dependent-block closure that re-reads `schema_version` off the `DbState` it receives and asserts it's already current.

  **Progress wiring — phase/step events, never file size.** Reed measured directly that the destination `.db`'s byte size stays near 0 until late in the copy, making it a provably useless (and actively misleading) progress signal — PR A's own kill-test comments independently confirm the same thing. Progress comes exclusively from two event sources: the pre-existing `backup://progress` (8 phases, PR A) — `create_migration_backup` now threads an `Option<&AppHandle>` through to it (mechanical signature addition across its ~30 call sites in `migrations.rs`; `None` for every one via `run_migrations` → a true no-op for every pre-existing caller) — and the new `migration://progress` (`{ step, total, label, pct }`), fired by `migrations.rs`'s `migration_step` alongside its existing `[MIGRATIONS] step N/M` log line, same no-op-when-`None` guarantee.

  **No-migration fast path, proven unchanged, not asserted.** `database::is_migration_pending` returns `false` for both a fresh install (nothing to back up yet) and an install already at the current schema version — regression-tested directly (`test_is_migration_pending_false_for_fresh_install`, `test_is_migration_pending_false_when_schema_current`) and proved live: `smoke-fresh-db`'s real stderr log contains zero `#2723`/`STARTUP` deferral lines, confirming the real compiled binary takes the exact pre-PR synchronous path with no new thread on the common case.

  **Failure path, by design, not an afterthought.** If `complete_db_dependent_startup` returns a hard `Err` (filesystem/extension-level failures — not a migration `Err`, which this code already treats as a pre-existing soft "continue with existing schema" degraded mode, unchanged by this PR), the screen shows "Update Failed" in plain text with the real error message, a fixed reassurance line ("Pane takes a backup of your database before applying updates — your data is safe"), and one button: **Quit Pane** (`exit(1)`). Chosen over an in-place retry because the realistic failure modes here (disk full, a corrupted `crsqlite.dylib`, permissions) aren't retriable by re-running the same logic in the same process, and re-entering `complete_db_dependent_startup` after partial global state (`database::set_crsqlite_path`, static caches) was never designed to be safe mid-session — a fresh process launch is the only state this codebase can be fully sure starts clean. **Never a blank window, never an endless spinner** — that's the exact bug this PR exists to prevent, and a silent spinner-forever failure path would just be it wearing a different hat.

  **Race-safety design for the frontend gate.** `StartupStatus`/`get_startup_status` (`startup.rs`) is a `State` read via a request/response **command**, not an event, specifically for the initial fast-path/slow-path decision — an event emitted before `UpdatingScreen.svelte`'s `listen()` calls attach would be silently lost, but a command always reflects the state at the moment it's asked. `app.manage(StartupStatus::new())` is the literal first line inside `.setup()`, before anything else, so the command has no `DbState` dependency and is safe to call at any point on any launch. Once confirmed `migration_required`, the frontend switches to events (`backup://progress`, `migration://progress`, terminal `startup://ready`/`startup://failed`) for live updates, with a defensive 500ms re-poll of the same command running alongside them in case the terminal event itself is missed.

  **Spec:** new `docs/spec/startup.md` (§35, registered in `docs/spec/README.md`'s index and changelog table) — the fast/slow path decision, the ordering guarantee and how it's held, the `StartupStatus` race-safety design, the progress-event table, the failure-path design and reasoning, and Reed's "what Matt must look for on install" list reproduced verbatim (the one thing this PR cannot test). `docs/spec/backup.md`'s header updated to cross-reference it and note the mechanical `create_migration_backup` signature addition.

  **Tests, through real commands — `run_migrations`/the real `tests/fixtures/upgrade-from-v91.db` fixture, never raw `INSERT`:** the ordering guarantee (above); `is_migration_pending` false-for-fresh-install / false-for-current-schema / true-for-the-real-v91-fixture (`database.rs`); `needs_migration` fresh/current/old-version (`migrations.rs`); `run_migrations` still delegates to the progress variant with an identical outcome; `migration_step`'s percentage math and its no-op-when-`None` guarantee; `mount_db_state_then` propagates a dependent-block error and still mounts `DbState` even when the dependent block fails. Frontend (`UpdatingScreen.test.ts`, 10 tests): fast path renders the real app immediately with zero event listeners attached; migration-required shows "Updating Pane… don't quit" and withholds the real app; `backup://progress`/`migration://progress` update the visible message; `startup://ready` switches to the real app; the defensive re-poll resolves to the real app if the ready event never fires; the failure screen shows the real message + a working Quit button (asserted via the mocked `exit(1)` call) on an explicit `failed` status, on a mid-migration `startup://failed` event, and on `get_startup_status` itself throwing — never a blank/silent screen.

  **Counts (this worktree, `PANE_TEST_ROOT` scratch root throughout, `--test-threads=1`):** backend `cargo test --lib -- --skip tests::test_backup:: --test-threads=1`: base (own re-run) **2556 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored, 11 filtered out**; this branch **2571 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored, 11 filtered out** (+15, exactly the new tests above, zero regressions). `tests::test_backup::` run in isolation per #2962: **11 passed, 0 failed**, unchanged. Known pre-existing flake `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert` (TCP-bind race) did not reproduce, confirmed solo. **One real flake hit and fixed in this worktree, not the PR's own code:** a `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` reuse artifact (a custom target dir doesn't follow `ai/commands.rs`'s `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`-relative crsqlite-extension path) caused one migration-fixture test to see no cr-sqlite extension loaded on a first pass — copying the dylib into the conventional `src-tauri/target/debug/resources/` path resolved it, confirmed deterministic in both directions, matching the exact artifact class flagged in Reed's build brief. **One real regression caught and fixed during this build:** moving the DB-dependent startup body into its own function initially placed that function's definition textually *before* `run()` in `lib.rs`, which put the (relocated) startup-consolidator dispatch site physically earlier in the source file than the router-trigger dispatch site — tripping `ai::dual_provider_tests::venice_dispatch_gap_tests::test_consolidator_venice_dispatch`'s source-order sanity assertion. Fixed by relocating the function to after `run()` instead, preserving the two sites' original relative order; re-run confirmed `0 failed`. Frontend `pnpm vitest run`: base **223 files / 3073 passed, 1 skipped**; this branch **224 files / 3083 passed, 1 skipped** (+1 file, +10 tests — exactly `UpdatingScreen.test.ts`, zero regressions). Real `~/Pane/.pane/backups` confirmed **60 files / 15G, unchanged** before and after every backend run in this PR.

  **Both smokes, run for real (debug build, default target dir — not reused from another worktree):** `smoke-fresh-db`: PASS, ready signal detected, zero `#2723`/deferral log lines (confirms the fast path). `smoke-upgrade-db`: PASS — the real v91→v92 fixture triggers the window-first path end to end: `[STARTUP] #2723: schema migration pending …` fires, `.setup()` returns, the background thread runs the real backup (`backup_started` → … → `backup_complete — 0.02s total`) and `[MIGRATIONS] step 1/1: migrate_v92` → `v91 → 92 migration applied`, then `[STARTUP] #2723: background migration + startup complete — app ready` — the smoke script's own ready-signal grep and `scripts/smoke-grep.sh`'s severity gate both pass (0 violations; 2 pre-existing allowlisted `[CRITICAL]` Memory.md-backfill-temp-file entries on this same v91 fixture, matching the identical baseline #3053 PR 3 already documented, not introduced by this PR).

  **PR B of 2 — the UI half. PR A (speed) is merged.** `lib.rs`, `backup.rs`, and `migrations.rs` are CORE_BEHAVIORAL — reed-gate applies, stays red until Matt labels.

### Fixed
- **PR A of 2 on #2723 — the launch/migration backup now copies at full speed instead of throttled to ~80 KB/s. (Relates to #2723)**

  **Root cause, in one line:** the pre-migration backup's copy step called `Backup::run_to_completion(5, Duration::from_millis(250), None)` — 5 pages then a 250ms sleep, ~80 KB/s — regardless of caller, even though the migration-launch caller runs before any window exists and before anything else has opened the DB, so there was nothing to be polite to. Reed's audit (`docs/audits/2026-10-23-scope-slow-launch-updating-screen.md`) traced that single constant to one commit (`b06459df`, #325, 2026-04-04) with no comment or rationale on record, and cross-validated the throttle's effect against a real production log from #2583 (15.15 MB / 185.74s) within 3%.

  **Fix 1 — explicit, caller-supplied pacing, no magic numbers.** New `BackupPacing` enum (`FullSpeed` / `ThrottledForLiveApp`) is now a required argument to `create_backup()` — every caller states its own context instead of inheriting one hardcoded pair. Pre-migration (`create_migration_backup`), Daily/Weekly (`create_daily_backup`), and the pre-restore safety backup all pass `FullSpeed` (no live reader/writer to protect, per caller-by-caller analysis in the spec). Manual (Settings UI) keeps `ThrottledForLiveApp` — the exact pre-existing 5-page/250ms pacing, preserved and named rather than re-guessed, per Matt's explicit instruction not to touch live-app pacing. `FullSpeed` copies via SQLite's own `step(-1)` ("all remaining pages now") convention rather than `run_to_completion` (which rejects a negative page count outright).

  **Fix 2 — `BackupType::Migration` skips the system-files archive; nothing else does.** `_system.tar.gz` is no longer produced for Migration backups specifically — no migration through the current schema touches `.pane/system/` (the `MIGRATION-DISK-OPS` convention exists to flag any that would), and restore already soft-fails a missing archive as an "older backup format" log line, confirmed by execution (`test_restore_migration_backup_without_system_archive`), not just by reading the branch. Manual/Daily/Weekly/PreRestore are unaffected.

  **Fix 3 — both backup output files (`.db`, `_system.tar.gz`) are staged and atomic-renamed, reusing the pattern already shipped for restore.** Both are now written to a `*-staging` path and `rename()`d into their final, listed filename only after success (and, for the `.db`, after integrity verification) — a kill mid-write can no longer leave a half-written file at a filename a complete backup would use. A stale staging file from a prior crashed run is cleaned up before the next attempt. A failed rename propagates as an error (#3049 lesson) rather than being swallowed.

  **Fix 4 (#2724, logging only) — backup phase + migration step N/M log lines.** Each of the 8 existing `emit_progress` phases now also writes an `eprintln!` line; the long `migrate_vNN` chains some `run_migrations` arms walk through (up to 19 steps in one launch) now log `step i/total: migrate_vNN` for each one. No UI/window change — that's PR B.

  **Measured, before/after:** 15 MB — ~190.63s (audit measurement, cross-validated against #2583's real 185.74s production log) → well under 1s. 50 MB (Matt's real size) — 628.83s (audit measurement) → well under 1s. Manual backup pacing verified unchanged: a 1 MB real DB takes ~12s+ under `ThrottledForLiveApp` vs. well under 1s under `FullSpeed` in the same test run (`test_live_app_pacing_still_throttles_vs_full_speed`).

  **Tests** (`backup.rs`, real commands — `run_migrations` + `create_note_internal`, not raw `INSERT`, for fixture data): pacing params are explicit and regression-tested; Migration skips the system archive while Manual/Daily/Weekly/PreRestore still produce it; a Migration backup with no system archive restores cleanly with real note data verified round-trip; a stale `.db-staging`/`.tar.gz-staging` file from a prior kill is cleaned up and doesn't corrupt the next backup; a real child process is SIGKILLed mid-copy (synchronized on the new phase-log lines, not file size — the destination file's apparent length was observed not to grow until near completion) and the final filename is confirmed to never exist during or after the kill, with a clean retry immediately after. **Follow-up (Reed's audit §4/§5 WARNs on this PR, pre-merge):** a matching real-SIGKILL test now covers the `.tar.gz` archive step too — `test_quit_mid_archive_leaves_no_partial_output_at_final_name` builds a real ~300 MB two-file fixture under `.pane/system/` (large enough to give `tar -czf` a genuine multi-second wall-clock window; incompressible so the window is real wall time, not an artifact of gzip finishing early), spawns the real backup path (`BackupType::Manual`, the one archiving type that isn't `Migration`) in its own process group, waits for the real `backup_archiving` phase log (same synchronization technique as the `.db` copy test — phase logs, not file-size polling, per Reed's finding that destination length isn't a usable signal for the SQLite copy; for `tar`'s streaming gzip output specifically, size growth IS reliable, so it's used here only to time the kill itself, after the phase log already confirmed archiving had started), then `kill -9`s the whole process group (not just the harness process) — `tar` is a child the harness spawns via `std::process::Command`, so a plain `child.kill()` on the harness alone would leave `tar` running, unkilled, to completion in the background, undermining the "genuinely killed mid-archive" claim; this landed, killed mid-write every run during verification (~76 MB of a ~300 MB archive, confirmed over 4 consecutive runs), confirmed no archive ever exists at the real, listed `_system.tar.gz` name, confirmed the staging-named leftover is real but incomplete, and confirmed a clean retry immediately after produces a valid, listable archive. Full suite: **2556 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored, 11 filtered out** (`cargo test --lib -- --skip tests::test_backup:: --test-threads=1`, `PANE_TEST_ROOT` scratch root, 109.02s) — base is 2547/11 per the task brief; this PR (both PRs — the original #2723 work and this follow-up) adds 12 new test functions total (9 run + 3 `#[ignore]`d child-process helpers: `timing_harness_full_speed_copy_15mb_and_50mb`, `kill_harness_slow_backup_copy`, and, new in this follow-up, `kill_harness_slow_backup_archive` — the latter two are subprocess entry points invoked only by their own parent kill test via `std::env::current_exe()`, never meant to run standalone). The backup module was also run in isolation (per #2962) — `cargo test --lib backup:: -- --test-threads=1`: **45 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored, 2527 filtered out**, 50.74s, including both real kill tests passing. Real `~/Pane/.pane/backups` confirmed unchanged (60 files, 15G) before and after every run in this follow-up, matching Reed's audit baseline exactly.

  **Corrected ignored-test accounting (Reed's audit §5 WARN — the shipped entry undercounted by one; this follow-up corrects it and adds the two more it created).** The suite's `ignored` count is now **8**, not 6: 5 pre-existing (untouched by either PR) + 3 added across the two PRs on #2723. Each, with why it's ignored and what covers the same behavior instead:

The *pacing mechanism's* correctness (FullSpeed vs. ThrottledForLiveApp parameters, that FullSpeed is actually faster) is covered on fast small fixtures by `test_backup_pacing_step_params_are_explicit` and `test_live_app_pacing_still_throttles_vs_full_speed` (both run normally); the specific 15/50 MB wall-clock figures this harness prints are not re-verified by any non-ignored test, since it's a measurement tool for the PR writeup, not a regression gate.

  - `notes.rs` `test_delete_permanently_sends_file_to_os_trash` (pre-existing) — writes a real file into the developer's real `~/.Trash` every run; the `trash` crate always calls the real OS API, no mockable seam. `test_purge_succeeds_when_file_already_gone_full_stack` (runs normally) covers the same code path's "file already gone" branch without touching the real trash — but the actual send-to-real-trash behavior itself has no non-ignored substitute; stating that plainly rather than implying otherwise.

Agent-reconstitution-after-DB-wipe for the current UUID scheme has no non-ignored coverage; noting the gap rather than papering over it.

- **PR 4 of 4 on #3053 — the model must never be told it has tools it isn't given.**

  **The real bug, in one line:** on the simple tier the system prompt listed all 39 tools while zero were actually sent on the wire, so a simple-tier model could claim an action it never took ("I've starred that project!" with no tool call) and nothing downstream ever checked the response text against the tool calls actually made. Measured, not theorized: `docs/audits/2026-10-21-e8-simple-tier-repro.md` ran the real classifier → routing → prompt-assembly → tool-selection pipeline against a mocked Ollama server for "go home" and "star this project" and captured exactly that — 39 tools in the prompt, 0 on the wire, same dispatch.

  **Fix 1 — the prompt lists only the tools actually sent.** `generate_tools_section` and `build_messages_with_context` no longer take `runtime_type: &str` and re-derive a tool list internally; they take the real `tools: &[ToolDef]` slice the `ai_chat_stream` call site already computed for the wire payload (moved earlier in that function so the SAME value feeds both). **Slice, not bool:** a bool re-derives what the caller already knows and the two can drift apart again (exactly how this bug happened the first time); passing the actual slice makes the prompt structurally incapable of disagreeing with the wire — one value, used twice. When zero tools are sent, the prompt now has no "## Available Tools" section at all, not an empty one implying capability.

  **Fix 2 — `tool_patterns` is generated from the live tool registry, with a sync test.** The hardcoded classifier-bypass array missed 10 of 38 real tools' trigger verbs entirely — notably every `set_*` tool, because the literal word "set" was never in the array. `generate_tool_patterns_from_registry()` now bridges each tool's `snake_case` name to trigger words by splitting on `_` and keeping tokens of 3+ characters, computed live from `get_pane_tools_for_runtime("anthropic")` on every call — a tool added to the registry is covered automatically, with zero hand-editing. A small, separately-labeled hand-written array covers only what's genuinely NOT derivable from any tool's name (date references, "yesterday"/month names; synonym verbs like "save"/"remember" that don't share a word with their tool's name) and is explicitly exempt from the sync test's coverage guarantee — it names no tool, so it can't be used to paper over a real gap. The sync test (`test_every_registered_tool_has_surviving_generated_token`) iterates the LIVE registry every run and fails loudly, naming the exact tool, if any tool's generated coverage ever goes to zero. Honest residual gap: two of the ten previously-uncovered tools (`set_status`, `set_priority`) have audit-cited natural phrasings ("mark this task done", "make this urgent") that share no word with either tool's name or the current synonym list — a full synonym table would close this but is out of scope here; the literal defect the audit named ("'set' isn't in the array at all") is fixed and verified against a `set`-containing realistic phrasing instead.

  **Fix 3 — the long-conversation classifier bypass is reachable.** `classify_message_complexity`'s `context_messages.len() > 10` bypass was dead code: its one real caller built `context_messages` via `.iter().rev().take(3).rev()` unconditionally, so `.len()` could never exceed 3 regardless of true conversation length. Fixed at the call site (`context_messages = messages.clone()`), not by lowering the threshold — the threshold already expresses the right policy; lowering it to fit a 3-item cap would bypass the classifier for nearly every message past the first couple of turns in ANY conversation, a far larger blast radius than fixing the one line that fed it the wrong data. This call-site slice also feeds the classifier's own prompt-context window, which independently re-slices to the last 3 messages internally — so per-request classifier INPUT TEXT for conversations under 10 messages is unaffected; only the previously-dead bypass decision now sees accurate data.

  **Spec:** `docs/spec/smart-routing.md` new §27.6.6 documents the pattern-generation fix, the name-to-verb bridging rule, and the dead-bypass fix with reasoning. `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.6.2 and its "Tool-list filtering" paragraph updated in place — the old claim that the simple tier's zero-tools guarantee was "nothing new... re-derived" was true of the wire but not the prompt; now documents both, and the signature change.

  **Tests, through a real dispatch, using Reed's exact repro phrases ("go home", "star this project") so his harness and these tests agree** (new `pr3053_item_c_tier_aware_tools_tests` module, `ai/commands.rs`): on the simple tier, the prompt names no tools when none are sent (fails at base — confirmed via a scratch worktree at `03a47a7f` reproducing both phrases' exact mismatch before deleting it); a tool-needing request routes to the full model, with tools, via the real `classify_message_complexity`/`resolve_model_for_message` chain against a mocked-YES Ollama server (fails at base — confirmed the same way: at base both phrases get misclassified simple, `provider_override = Some(..)`); the long-conversation bypass now fires on a real 15-message conversation while the old `.take(3)` shape (reproduced verbatim, not just asserted) still gets the same conversation misjudged simple, side by side in one test; the registry/pattern sync test plus a direct regression check that all ten of the audit's previously-uncovered tools now have realistic trigger coverage.

No failures observed; the known pre-existing flake (`gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert`, TCP-bind race) did not reproduce in this run, confirmed separately still passes in isolation. `bash scripts/ci-guards/run-guards.sh all`: all guards PASS (G4/G5 report-only violations are pre-existing, in files this PR never touched). **PR 4 of 4 on #3053** — last of the sequence; Reed audits by running it, Matt retests in the app. `ai/commands.rs` is CORE_BEHAVIORAL — reed-gate stays red until Matt labels. - **PR 3 of 4 on #3053 — the no-progress timeout replaces the total loop clock, and the stop message now names the real limit.**

  **Root cause, in one line:** `loop_start.elapsed() >= loop_timeout` measured TOTAL time since the agentic loop began, so a slow-but-productive multi-iteration job (every iteration succeeding, each one taking a while) could be cut off once the sum crossed 120s even though nothing had stalled — and the stop message always said "You've reached the tool iteration limit," even when the real cause was the timeout.

  **What counts as progress, and where the marker resets.** "Progress" is (1) a provider call returning new, non-empty text, or (2) the current iteration's batch of tool calls finishing — success, a tool-level error, or a gate refusal (not-offered/args-parse-failed/web-taint) all count, since each concludes the call. `last_progress` resets at both sites in `ai_chat_stream`'s agentic loop; the timeout check itself still runs once per iteration, at the exact point the old wall clock did (before starting the next provider call) — a single iteration's own duration is bounded by the unchanged per-request timeout, not by this setting. A reconnect retry does NOT count as progress (it's bounded by its own `CHAT_RECONNECT_MAX_RETRIES` ceiling independently); internal smart-route retries are invisible to this mechanism since they resolve within one iteration's call before the check runs again.

  **Settings-key decision: relabel, not rename.** `ai_settings.loop_timeout_seconds` keeps its key, range (30-300), and default (120) — renaming a persisted settings key means every existing install's saved value needs a migration path; relabeling what the same key controls (Settings → AI's label/sublabel now describe the no-progress behavior) gets the same outcome with a materially smaller blast radius. The Rust-side local variable is renamed to `idle_timeout_seconds` for clarity; only the persisted string key is unchanged.

  **Exit-kind naming: `AgentExitKind::WallClockTimeout` → `NoProgressTimeout`.** Compile-time-only rename (never persisted) — the old name would describe a trigger condition the variant no longer has, which is exactly the kind of thing that confuses a future reader. `limit_secs` keeps its name/shape.

  **`SUMMARY_SYSTEM` now branches on the real exit kind.** New `summary_system_message(exit_kind)` mirrors `build_stop_fallback_message`'s existing branch-on-`AgentExitKind` shape (same enum, same one-function-per-meaning convention, not a second copy of the logic) — but for a different audience: it primes the model writing the end-of-turn summary, while `build_stop_fallback_message` is the user-facing fallback used only when that summary call produces nothing. `IterationCap` keeps the old "tool iteration limit" wording; `NoProgressTimeout` now says "You've reached the time limit for this turn without making further progress" instead.

  **Spec:** `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.5.2 updated in place — documents the no-progress semantics, the settings-key relabel decision, and the exit-kind rename. `docs/spec/sessions.md`'s own-turn-tombstone section's "wall-clock-timeout" reference updated to "no-progress-timeout."

  **Tests, through a real dispatch (the real `stream_openrouter` production function against a `mockito` server, the same pattern `d2_dispatch_site_tests` already established in this file) with a faked clock (`Instant::checked_sub`, never a real sleep) — new `no_progress_timeout_tests_3053` module, `ai/commands.rs`:** a 3-iteration job whose simulated total elapsed (150s) exceeds the old 120s wall clock is never cut off by the real `check_no_progress_timeout`, while an inline mirror of the PRE-fix check (same `loop_start`, never reset) proves it WOULD have fired — the regression this PR fixes, shown failing first; a job that stalls for longer than the limit after one real dispatch stops, and the real `summary_system_message`/`build_stop_fallback_message` name the no-progress timeout, not the iteration limit; the two exit kinds are proven to produce genuinely different text at both the model-facing and user-facing layers (the over-correction guard — if both produced the same string, the fix would have traded one wrong message for another).

- **PR 2 of 4 on #3053 — the duplicate filter deletes real messages, most dangerous item in the scope.** Dedup is now id (`is_already_classified`) and seq (`tombstone_own_turn`) only — text containment never drops or tombstones a message again.

  **The root cause, in one line:** `check_stale_echo` and `is_recent_local_assistant_echo` classified purely by substring containment and, on a match, permanently tombstoned the incoming message — but a text match is correlation, not proof of duplication, and ordinary behavior (a reply that quotes or restates prior content) produces the identical signal. On 2026-10-20 this silently dropped a genuine 3:48pm cron result (OC `seq` 154) because an earlier assistant reply happened to quote its exact text.

  **What text matching now does: log only.** Both functions' containment/staleness/length-floor logic is completely unchanged (still useful as a diagnostic signal for tracing suspected duplicates) — only the caller's reaction to a match changed. `pull_oc_transcript_for_session` now logs a `[OC-PULL]`-prefixed diagnostic line on a hit and lets the message proceed to ingest exactly as if no match occurred. No code path writes `reason='stale_echo'` or `reason='backstop_echo'` any more. The seq-based `tombstone_own_turn` mechanism (`reason='own_turn'`, #2738) is untouched and remains the correct, working guard against an agent's own turn echoing back — confirmed unweakened by a dedicated new test plus the existing, unmodified `own_turn_tombstone_tests_2738` suite (still green).

  **How existing tombstones are cleared, and when.** A fix that only changes future behavior leaves every message already wrongly hidden by the old text-based rules permanently invisible — the Rule 1 permanence pre-filter (`is_already_classified`) has no expiry. Migration v92 (`migrate_v92`) runs once, on the `v91→v92` schema transition, and executes `DELETE FROM chat_oc_tombstones WHERE reason IN ('stale_echo', 'backstop_echo')` — `own_turn` rows (seq-based, correct) are left untouched. Chosen as a migration rather than an on-read check: this is a genuine one-time cleanup of data written by behavior this same fix permanently removes going forward, so there's nothing left for a per-poll-tick check to keep guarding against; it matches this file's own convention for one-off data migrations tied to a behavior change, and reuses the existing schema-version gate's backup safety net. The `DELETE` is naturally idempotent (a second run finds zero matching rows); the schema-version gate additionally ensures it only runs once per install. Clearing a tombstone alone doesn't resurrect a message by itself — it removes the Rule 1 pre-filter's reason to drop the id on the next poll tick, and because this adapter has no `since`/cursor state (§30.11.3) a cleared id reappears automatically the next time OC's small recent page still contains it.

  **Spec:** `docs/spec/sessions.md` §30.11.7 updated in place (Rule 2 and the 150s backstop now documented as log-only); new §30.11.10 added documenting the incident, the fix, the migration mechanism, and its idempotency — both updated directly in this PR's own diff, no `spec-covered-by:` tag needed.

The existing `echo_suppression_tests`/`tombstoning_tests` pipeline-level tests were updated in place (not removed) to assert the new log-only outcome — their direct unit tests of the containment functions themselves are unchanged, since that logic did not change. - **PR 1 of 4 on #3053's refresh-events scope.** Fixed the agent's duplicate status-set/move logic and two of D1/D2's three frontend gaps (sheet-subscription, folder-move ordering). Sidebar is confirmed out of scope — see below.

  **#3042 already fixed the missing-event half** (`emit_entity_change_for_tool` wraps every agent tool call site, proven by existing tests) — what remained was the agent's own executors still re-implementing move/status logic as a second, drifted copy of the shared code, plus two frontend gaps in getting that event to the screen.

  **The agent's duplicate copies, closed.** `execute_set_status` and `execute_move_note` (`ai/commands.rs`) ran their own raw SQL instead of calling the shared `update_note_internal`/`move_note_internal` (`notes.rs`) every other move/status path already uses. Now they call the shared functions directly. This closes the NULL-folder bug for free: `execute_move_note`'s raw SQL wrote `folder_id = NULL` unconditionally whenever the agent passed only a target project (no target folder); `move_note_internal` falls back to the target project's `default_folder_id` instead, same as the human move path. **Behaviour change, stated explicitly, not hidden:** routing through `update_note_internal` means the agent's own status-set now also stamps `completed_at` (when status becomes `"done"`) and dismisses/clears due-date notifications — the raw SQL this replaced did neither. The existing #3032 system-note move guard and the #3024 folder-delete relocation path are both confirmed unaffected (existing test suites for both pass unchanged); routing the agent through `move_note_internal` does make its "already at target" no-op check happen AFTER the system-note guard rather than before (slightly stricter — a system note "moved" to its own current location is now also rejected, not silently accepted), confirmed via the existing guard test suite.

  **Editor.svelte, sheets never subscribed to refresh events at all.** `onMount`'s `if (isSheet) { return () => {}; }` guard exited the whole `onMount` body before `subscribeDataChanged` was ever reached — not a deliberate exclusion (the guard predates `subscribeDataChanged` by several months; it was written only to skip TipTap construction, which legitimately can't run for a sheet). Narrowed to wrap only the TipTap-construction block; every listener below it, including `subscribeDataChanged`, now registers for sheets too.

  **Editor.svelte's `handleFolderMove`, ordering + swallowed error.** It read `noteMeta.id`/entity type to dispatch the refresh event *after* calling `onMoved()` — which can synchronously destroy the very Editor instance whose closure was still running past it (both real callers null `$activeNote` synchronously, and both render sites gate `<Editor>` on it) — inside a catch that only logged to console, never surfaced to the user. Now reads both fields into consts before `onMoved()`, dispatches using those consts, and shows a visible error toast (existing mechanism this file already uses for upload/export failures) instead of swallowing the failure silently.

  **Sidebar is NOT part of this fix — confirmed, not an oversight.** `Sidebar.svelte:181` ignoring note/sheet events is documented, deliberate design (comment at `Sidebar.svelte:155-165`, referencing #3016/§34.5, Matt-signed-off): the sidebar's tree view has no surface to patch for note/sheet content changes. Reed's 2026-10-20 scope audit confirms this explicitly and rules it out of the D1/D2 fix surface. No Sidebar code changed; no Sidebar test added.

  **Spec:** docs/spec/data-refresh.md §34 (event shape/senders/listeners) and §34.5 (Sidebar's documented note/sheet exclusion) already cover every part of this PR — nothing new to write.

The #3032 system-note guard (`execute_move_note_system_guard_tests`) and the #3024 folder-delete-relocation regression test (`test_delete_folder_moves_notes_sheets_and_trashed_note_to_default_folder`) were already green at base and remain green — confirmed by direct run, not assumed.

- Fixed the release build's DMG packaging step (`scripts/build.sh`), which could never actually swap the signed/notarized/stapled app into the final installer: Tauri's finished DMG is UDZO (read-only compressed), and that format cannot mount read-write on any machine, so the swap step added by #3035 had never executed successfully anywhere, on any build. The script now converts the DMG to a writable (UDRW) copy before the swap and back to UDZO afterward. Also closed several related gaps so the same class of failure can't slip through silently again: both disk-image mount steps now check that a mount actually happened (not just that the attach command exited 0) and surface the real `hdiutil` error instead of letting `-quiet` swallow it; an exit trap now always attempts to detach any mounted disk image and warns if it can't; a final check confirms the shipped DMG actually exists and is non-empty before the script exits successfully, removing it if that check fails; and the DMG-to-UDZO conversions, the app copy (`ditto`), and the final `mv` are all now checked instead of being trusted to have worked just because a later, unrelated check happened to pass. Added an automated test (`scripts/tests/dmg-swap/test-swap-path.sh`) that exercises this exact swap sequence against a disposable dummy DMG — no Apple signing keys and no real build required — and wired it into CI (`.github/workflows/dmg-swap-test.yml`) to run on the self-hosted Mac runner for any PR touching the build script, so a packaging regression like this one fails before merge instead of on release day. (Relates to #3049)
- Fast-follow on the #3049 fix above, from running the actual build end-to-end: fixed two bugs the duplication between `scripts/build.sh` and `scripts/tests/dmg-swap/test-swap-path.sh` had let through, and removed that duplication so the same class of miss can't happen again.

  **Bug 1 — the staging file never landed where every later check looked for it.** `hdiutil convert -o <path>` silently appends `.dmg` to `<path>` if it doesn't already end in `.dmg`. `build.sh`'s staging path was named `.Pane_${VERSION}.dmg.building` (no trailing `.dmg`), so `convert` actually wrote `.Pane_${VERSION}.dmg.building.dmg`, and every subsequent step — notarization, stapling, the final `mv` — was looking for a file that was never there. Fixed at the root: the staging name is now `.Pane_${VERSION}.building.dmg`, and the conversion itself (see shared function below) refuses to run at all with a non-`.dmg`-suffixed output path, so this can't come back silently through a future rename.

  **Bug 2 — a fully successful build could exit non-zero.** `build.sh`'s `cleanup_scratch` EXIT trap ended with a chain of `[ -n "$VAR" ] && rm -f "$VAR"` lines; the last one's exit status becomes the trap's own exit status, and under `set -e`, an EXIT trap's exit status silently overrides the script's real one — `exit 0` after a clean build got reported as `exit 1`, because the last scratch variable (`STAGING_DMG_PATH`) is empty on success (it's cleared right after the final `mv`). Fixed by capturing the real exit code as the trap's first statement (`local exit_code=$?`, before anything else can overwrite `$?`) and explicitly re-exiting with it as the trap's last statement — a failed build still exits non-zero; a successful one now correctly exits 0.

  **The duplication that hid both.** `test-swap-path.sh` re-implemented the same `hdiutil convert` calls and the same cleanup-trap shape with its own file names (which already ended in `.dmg`) and its own `rm -rf`-only cleanup (which never had bug 2's bare-`&&` tail) — so neither bug could ever surface in the test meant to catch regressions in this exact code path. Per the one-function-per-operation rule, both pieces are now shared, single definitions in `scripts/lib/dmg.sh`, used by both `build.sh` and the test: `dmg_convert_or_die` (fails loudly unless the output lands at the *exact* path given — the single assertion that makes bug 1 structurally impossible to reintroduce) and `dmg_cleanup_mount` / `dmg_rm_scratch` (the mount-detach and scratch-removal pieces of the EXIT trap, each of which always returns 0 — necessary because `set -e` is in effect *inside* EXIT traps too, so a helper that itself returned non-zero would abort the trap before it reached its own `exit "$exit_code"`, reintroducing bug 2 one level deeper; caught by actually running the trap under `set -e` in isolation, not just by reading the code).

  **The test now asserts exit codes, not just output.** `test-swap-path.sh` exits 0 on a normal run and non-zero on a forced failure, same as `build.sh` must. Three testing seams reproduce each regression on demand: `DMG_SWAP_TEST_SKIP_UDRW_CONVERT=1` (the original #3049 mount bug), `DMG_SWAP_TEST_BREAK_STAGING_NAME=1` (this fast-follow's bug 1 — a non-`.dmg` convert output path), and `DMG_SWAP_TEST_BREAK_TRAP=1` (this fast-follow's bug 2 — the bare-`&&`-tail trap, reinstated on purpose). `scripts/tests/dmg-swap/prove-catches-regression.sh` now runs all four scenarios and asserts: the normal run exits 0; both bug-1 variants exit non-zero; and the bug-2 variant prints a full "✅ ... passed" success body yet still exits non-zero — proving the broken trap shape, not a real failure, is what's being caught.

  Verified with `bash -n` and `shellcheck` on every changed file (zero new warnings against the pre-existing baseline on each file) and by actually running `test-swap-path.sh` and `prove-catches-regression.sh` locally, including each regression toggle. **No full build (`scripts/build.sh` end-to-end or `tauri build`) was run, per INVARIANTS.md — Reed's real build run is the proof for the packaging path itself.** No Rust or frontend files touched. (Relates to #3049)

- Fixed a third form of the same race — Cmd+N (and three other paths) creating/opening a note and then silently losing it the instant the target screen mounts for the first time (Reed's 2026-10-18 delta2 audit of #3044, item 1 FAIL). **Ships in 1.0.61.** Tracked on #2874.

  **Why the previous fix (below) came back:** `noteService.createNewNote()` being store-only is true in isolation, but its "open" step writes `canvasState.view = 'note_editor'` — when that's the FIRST time `NotesBrowser.svelte` mounts this session (Cmd+N from Calendar/All Tasks/Trash/Home/project_config, or a wiki-link click from `AllTasksView`/`KanbanBoard`'s own editor panel), `CanvasRenderer.svelte`'s `{:else if}` chain mounts it in response, and its pre-existing `onMount` ran `$activeNote = null;` unconditionally as its first statement — wiping the note `createNewNote()`/`selectNote()` had just set a beat earlier, same call, no `await` between the two writes. `KanbanBoard.svelte`'s onMount had the identical unconditional clear (`$activeNote = null; // Clear active note on kanban mount`). Proven by execution in a disposable worktree, not by reasoning — the delta2 audit's three escalating repros.

  **The fix, per Matt's ruling:** the unconditional clear existed for a real reason (its own comment says so — dropping a STALE note carried over from another view, e.g. Kanban, so it can't reopen itself in NotesBrowser) and that protection must survive. New shared `noteService.clearStaleActiveNoteOnMount()` — keep `$activeNote` when it already IS the note `canvasState.context.noteId` says THIS navigation targeted; clear in every other case. Both `NotesBrowser.svelte`'s and `KanbanBoard.svelte`'s `onMount` now call this one function and nothing else for their activeNote handling — one check, not a copy per component.

  **The other two `$activeNote = null` sites in these two files are unrelated to this pattern, not a third/fourth instance of it** — checked individually, not assumed: `NotesBrowser.svelte`'s `goBackToCards()` (the Escape-key/click-away handler that intentionally closes the note panel) and `KanbanBoard.svelte`'s `handleColumnsClick()` (clicking the board background to deselect a card) are both deliberate, user-initiated closes with no mount involved — left untouched.

  **Every set-then-navigate-onto-an-unmounted-screen path found, audited individually:** Cmd+N (`+page.svelte` → `createNewNote()`) and a wiki-link click from `AllTasksView`/`KanbanBoard`'s editor panel (both → `navigateWikiLink()` → `selectNote()`) all share the exact racy shape above — all three fixed by the shared check, all three proven red-at-base/green-after by execution. The agent opening a note (`ChatSidebar.svelte`'s `open_note` case), Calendar opening a board card (`CanvasRenderer.svelte`'s `handleTaskClick`), a wiki-link click from inside `NotesBrowser` itself, `NavPlayer.svelte`'s "go to source note", and a search-result note click (`CanvasRenderer.svelte`'s `handleNoteClick`) do NOT share it — each navigates (mounting the target screen) first and only sets `$activeNote` afterward, either via a real `await` chain or a deliberate `tick()`/event-dispatch sequencing — confirmed safe by running each against this fix, honestly reported as already passing at base where that's what happened, not claimed as new fixes.
