- Fixed Cmd+N (and the New Note button) silently doing nothing from most of the app's screens (Reed's 2026-10-17 delta1 audit of #3044, WARN 2) — one shared `noteService.createNewNote()` function, no `window.__paneNewNote` global, ever. **Ships in 1.0.61.** Tracked on #2874.

  **Why the previous fix came back:** that fix (below) routed Cmd+N through `window.__paneNewNote`, a global `NotesBrowser.svelte` registered to its own `handleNewNote` on mount and cleared on unmount. `CanvasRenderer.svelte`'s render tree is a plain `{:else if}` chain — navigating to ANY view besides `notes_browser`/`note_editor` unmounts `NotesBrowser` and clears the global. Since the fix routed creation exclusively through it, Cmd+N became a silent no-op — zero note, zero error, zero UI feedback — from precisely the "common case" (any other screen) the original bug report named, untested.

  **The fix:** Matt's ruling — move the New Note button's own creation code into ONE shared function, and have both the button and Cmd+N call it directly, with nothing in between. `noteService.createNewNote()` reads/writes stores only (`$activeProject`/`$activeNote`/`canvasState`), never a component's local state — it does not care whether any particular component is mounted, which is what makes the race structurally impossible rather than relocated a third time. `window.__paneNewNote` is deleted outright, along with its registration/cleanup in `NotesBrowser.svelte`'s `onMount`/`onDestroy`.

  **Behavior, exactly as ruled:** inside a project (`$activeProject` set), creates the note in that project's own `default_folder_id` — never a "first non-system folder" scan, never a hardcoded `'AI'`/`'Pane System'` name check (both were the leftover island #3044 already removed once from this exact code path; this PR removes them a second time and adds a source-level regression guard against a third) — then opens it, from whichever screen Cmd+N was pressed on. Outside a project (Home, All Tasks, Calendar, Trash, the project list), creates nothing and shows **"Open a project to make a note."** — a visible result instead of the prior silent no-op. Kanban's own, separate, pre-existing Cmd+N (`KanbanBoard.svelte`'s own `window` keydown listener, since #424, creating a task card via a different flow entirely) is untouched and out of scope, confirmed by this PR's zero-line diff to that file.

  **Also corrected — a mechanism-claim drift found in the same audit (WARN, same class as #3046's wrong CHANGELOG count):** the prior entry below described wiki-link inertness in language that could be read as "the render pass stopped linkifying unresolvable links." It never did, and this PR didn't change that: `Editor.svelte`'s render-pass regex and `WikiLink.ts`'s live-node `renderHTML` are both unconditional — every `[[Title]]` becomes the identical clickable-looking span whether or not a note with that title exists, with zero existence check anywhere in rendering. Inertness is achieved ENTIRELY at click time, inside `navigateWikiLink()` — correctly implemented and tested; only the written description of how was imprecise. `docs/spec/ui-layout.md` §3.4's "Missing wiki links are inert" and "Cmd+N creates a note" subsections are both rewritten for accuracy.

  **Tests:** `noteService.createNewNote.test.ts` (new) — the shared function's full contract with ZERO Svelte components mounted anywhere in the file (the core structural claim): project default_folder_id used (not a scan), opens via the activeNote-then-canvasState sequencing `selectNote()` already uses regardless of starting screen, the blocked-outside-a-project path creates nothing and dispatches exactly one `pane-new-note-blocked` event, plus a source-text RED-ON-REVERT guard against `is_system`/`'AI'`/`'Pane System'` creeping back into this function. `NotesBrowser.cmdN-save.test.ts` (rewritten) — real `NotesBrowser`+`Editor` mount, Cmd+N-from-the-notes-browser creates/saves a title and body through a real debounced `api.saveNote` and reopen round-trip (unchanged in substance from the prior fix, now invoking the shared function directly instead of the deleted global), the button's own real DOM click still works, and a grep-backed assertion that no `window.__paneNewNote` reference survives anywhere in the component or its own mount/unmount cycle. `page.cmdN-shared-function.test.ts` (new) — mirrors `+page.svelte`'s real keydown-handler source (same house convention as `page.wiki-link-context.test.ts`) to prove Cmd+N calls the shared function (not the old global) and the kanban early-return is unchanged; "Cmd+N from Home" end to end through the real shared function and a real `pane-new-note-blocked` listener rendering the exact message. `KanbanBoard.cmdN-preexisting.test.ts` (new) — Cmd+N from the board creates and saves via Kanban's own pre-existing, unrelated flow; **named honestly as passing at base, not a fix** (zero lines of this PR touch `KanbanBoard.svelte`). `NotesBrowser.folder-selection.test.ts` (deleted) — covered the exact "first non-system folder, respect $activeFolder" logic Matt's ruling here explicitly supersedes with `default_folder_id`; keeping it would describe dead, superseded behavior.

- Fixed wiki links creating notes on a miss, a link opening in the wrong project, Cmd+N/Cmd+T silently failing to save, and chat free-text phrases being intercepted instead of reaching the agent — plus deleted six confirmed-unreachable screens/components and added a CI check forbidding native `confirm(` (Matt's #3044 round-2 rulings, same branch as the Calendar/ConfirmDialog/Kanban-collapse PR below). **Ships in 1.0.61.** Tracked on #2874.

  **1. Missing wiki links are now inert, not create-on-click:** `Editor.svelte` turns every `[[Title]]` into a clickable span on reopen, and clicking one with no exact-title match used to silently `confirm()` + create it. Matt's ruling: a missing note stays plain and does nothing, both while typing and on reopen. `navigateWikiLink()` (`wikiLinkNavigation.ts`)'s create/confirm branch — and the `projectId`/`folderId`/`createNoteFn`/`confirmFn` parameters it needed — is deleted outright, not gated; an exact match still navigates exactly as before.

  **2. A wiki-link click opened the note in the PREVIOUSLY active project, not its own — proven cause:** `CanvasRenderer.svelte`'s `loadDataForView` resolves `context.projectId` into `$activeProject` for every project-scoped view EXCEPT `note_editor` — the one view note-to-note navigation (wiki links included) actually lands on. `NotesBrowser.svelte` (rendered for both `notes_browser` and `note_editor`) reads `$activeProject` directly for its folder header/list/filtering, so a note's content loaded correctly (`get_note` is id-keyed) while the surrounding chrome kept showing the stale project. Fixed by resolving `$activeProject`/`$activeFolder`/`$activeNotebook` in the `note_editor` case too, mirroring every sibling case in the same switch.

  **3. Cmd+N/Cmd+T silently failed to save a new note's title or content — proven cause:** `+page.svelte` carried its OWN duplicate note-creation code (a legacy notebook-name fallback outside `notes_browser`, a hardcoded `'AI'`/`'Pane System'` folder-name check inside it) instead of calling the New Note button's function. When `NotesBrowser.svelte` wasn't already mounted (any view besides `notes_browser`/`note_editor`/`note_list` — the common case), that code set `$activeNote` to the new note and THEN navigated to bring `NotesBrowser` on screen for the first time — which ran `NotesBrowser`'s own `onMount`, whose first statement nulls `$activeNote` right back out (#2874 item 15 fix #3's stale-carry-over guard), wiping the just-created note before the user could type into it. **Fix:** Cmd+T removed entirely; Cmd+N now calls the exact same function the New Note button calls (`NotesBrowser.svelte` registers it on `window.__paneNewNote` from its own `onMount`, which has therefore already run by the time any creation happens — no race is possible by construction). `+page.svelte`'s duplicate creation code is deleted.

  **4. Chat free-text navigation deleted — every message now reaches the agent:** `ChatSidebar.svelte`'s `handleSendMessage` used to intercept phrases like "go to home"/"show tasks" via a `navMap` lookup + Levenshtein `fuzzyMatch` fallback, plus "go to [project]"/"open [note]" regexes, answering locally with a fabricated "Done — navigated..." assistant reply the agent never produced. Matt's ruling: chat is not a second, parallel command parser. The whole block is deleted; `userReachableScan.ts`'s matching exclusion marker (carved out for this exact block, #3043 item 2) is removed as confirmed-dead in the same commit.

  **5. Six confirmed-unreachable screens/components deleted, each independently proven, not assumed:** `TaskEditModal.svelte` (reachable only via `+page.svelte`'s `handleNewTask`, which had zero callers anywhere in `src/`); `TaskFullPage.svelte` (imported by `CanvasRenderer.svelte` but never actually instantiated — zero `<TaskFullPage` usages); `TaskList.svelte`/the `task_list` view (zero literal `view: 'task_list'` call sites anywhere, user or agent — the backend already rejects it); the `dashboard` view (same basis); `KanbanBoard.svelte`'s `openTaskDetail` (zero callers); `settings/MemorySection.svelte` (zero references anywhere in `src/`, never wired into `Settings.svelte` at all). `note_list` (a pure rendering alias of `notes_browser`) is ALSO deleted, conditional on item 3: its only citation was the now-deleted `handleNewNote`, and the derived user-reachable-views scan (`userReachableScan.ts`), re-run after that deletion, confirmed zero routes remain.

  **6. CI check: no native `confirm(` in `src/`:** the pinned Tauri dialog plugin has no `confirm` command — native `confirm()` never asks the user anything in this WebView, it returns immediately and the calling code carries on as if answered. New `scripts/check-no-native-confirm.sh` (thin `CI — No Native confirm()` workflow, same shape as `check-spec-first.sh`/#3015) scans `src/` for bare/`window.confirm(` calls, excluding comments (`//`, `/* */`, `<!-- -->`) and files that shadow `confirm` locally (`AgentPickerPopover.svelte`'s own zero-arg `confirm()`); `alert()` is explicitly left alone per Matt's ruling — it works. 10 unit tests (`scripts/tests/check-no-native-confirm/run-tests.sh`) prove it catches a planted violation (not vacuous) and doesn't false-positive on any of the comment/shadow shapes found while building it. The three real native-`confirm()` sites this check would otherwise have caught (`TaskEditModal.svelte`/`TaskFullPage.svelte`/`TaskList.svelte`, Reed's named follow-up from the prior #3044 audit) are resolved by item 5's deletions — the check now reports zero violations in `src/`.

  **7. Real render assertion for #3043's unknown-view "no-screen-change" half:** `ChatSidebar.errorCaseNoScreenChange.test.ts` proved the shape of `handleNavigateFromStream`'s `case 'error':` branch via source-text extraction only (the banner half already had a real render assertion). New `ChatSidebar.navErrorScreenUnchanged.test.ts` mounts the real `ChatSidebar`/`ChatPanel` pair, captures the real `onDone` callback `streamManager.startStream` is called with, invokes it with a backend-rejected `navigate` payload, and asserts BY EXECUTION that the error banner renders with the real message AND `canvasState` is byte-identical before/after.

  **Tests, every one through real rendered components or real execution, never a hand-copied restatement:** `CanvasRenderer.crossProjectNoteNav.test.ts` (item 2, confirmed failing pre-fix — `$activeProject` stayed on the stale project); `NotesBrowser.cmdN-save.test.ts` (item 3, confirmed failing pre-fix — `window.__paneNewNote` didn't exist; full round-trip: create → type title → paste body → real debounced `api.saveNote` → reopen via `noteService.selectNote` → both values render back); `wikiLinkNavigation.test.ts` (item 1, rewritten for the inert-on-miss contract); `ChatSidebar.freeTextNav.test.ts` (item 4, confirmed failing pre-fix — `api.sendChatMessage` was never called for "go to home"); `ChatSidebar.navErrorScreenUnchanged.test.ts` (item 7); `scripts/tests/check-no-native-confirm/run-tests.sh` (item 6); `userReachableViews.derived.test.ts`/`userReachableScan.test.ts`/`canvas.showViewParity.test.ts`/`navigationDispatch.test.ts` updated for `note_list`/`task_list`/`dashboard`'s deletion and the dead `navView` exclusion marker's removal. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test --test-threads=1 --skip tests::test_backup::` and `pnpm vitest run` both green (see PR body for exact counts/invocations). `smoke-fresh-db`/`smoke-upgrade-db` both PASS.

No version bump. Out of scope: #3036 PRs 3/5/7/7b (lane 2); #3020/#3022/#3023/#3025/#3030/#3033/#3041 (parked). (Relates to #2874)

- Fixed the Calendar opening the wrong thing, consolidated multiple hand-rolled confirm modals onto the shared `ConfirmDialog`, and made every Kanban column collapsible with persisted state (1.0.60 live-test-failures scope items 6/F and 7/G plus a new Kanban-collapse ruling, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-16-scope-1060-test-failures.md`, plus the scope comment on #2874). **Lane 1 PR 5 — ships in 1.0.61.** Tracked on #2874.

  **Item F — Calendar opened the wrong thing:** `CanvasRenderer.svelte`'s `handleTaskClick` navigated to `view: 'notes_browser'` (the full per-project note browser, "every note") instead of the project's board. Matt's ruling: clicking a task from the Calendar opens that project's **board** (`view: 'kanban'`, the same view `Sidebar.svelte`'s `selectProject` already uses) **with that task's card open** — both halves. Changed the one navigation-target literal; the existing `await navigateTo() -> tick() -> dispatchEvent('pane-select-note')` sequencing (#2874 item 18 fix 1) is unchanged and reused as-is — no new dispatch path added, per the explicit caution about #3043's in-flight `ChatSidebar`/`ChatPanel` navigation rework. `KanbanBoard.svelte` gains a `pane-select-note` listener (the exact same event `NotesBrowser.svelte`/`ChatSidebar.svelte` already dispatch/listen for) with a `pendingSelectTaskId` queue mirroring `NotesBrowser`'s own completion-signal pattern, so a click that arrives before `loadTasks()` resolves still opens the right card once it does, rather than being dropped.

  **Item G — one confirm dialog, not many:** `Trash.svelte`'s hand-rolled Delete Permanently/Empty Trash modal (both shared one state machine) — the one with the near-invisible `rgba(255,255,255,0.05)` background the audit flagged — is replaced with the shared `ConfirmDialog.svelte` (gained an additive `error` prop in #3040, already used in 7 places before this PR). A failed confirm now surfaces its error INSIDE the dialog and keeps it open, instead of a `console.error`-only catch that silently closed it. **Full classification of every `confirm` hit across `src/lib/components/*.svelte` at base, not a crude text match:** converted `Trash.svelte` (required, this item) and `Settings.svelte`'s template-delete modal (found during the sweep, same hand-rolled `.modal-overlay`/`.modal-content` pattern, self-contained, zero overlap with any in-flight PR). Deliberately left, with reasons: `ChatSidebar.svelte`'s Phase-4 delete-confirmation modal (also genuinely hand-rolled) — left because #3043 is actively reworking navigation dispatch in this exact file right now and an unrelated confirm-modal swap would add needless merge-conflict surface to a concurrent PR; `TaskEditModal.svelte`/`TaskFullPage.svelte`/`TaskList.svelte`'s native `window.confirm()` calls for task delete — a structurally different (synchronous, blocking) pattern that would need each component's delete flow restructured to the async `ConfirmDialog` state machine, tripling this PR's scope for three unrelated files; left as a named follow-up, not silently skipped. Everything else matching `confirm` (`AgentPickerModal`/`AgentPickerPopover`/`DefaultAgentPickerModal`'s picker `onConfirm` callbacks, `PromptDialog`'s intentionally-separate input+confirm component, `CalendarView`/`ChatPanel`/`Editor`'s unrelated create/save-confirm actions, assorted comments) is unrelated word-matches, not confirm-modal duplicates — full list and reasoning in the PR body.

  **Kanban — every column collapsible, state persisted:** `KanbanBoard.svelte`'s column-header click was gated to `column.status === 'done' || count > 5` — a non-Done column with 5 or fewer cards couldn't be collapsed at all, and `collapsedColumns` was a plain ephemeral `$state` that reset to Done-only on every mount. **Matt's three rulings, implemented exactly:** (1) every column collapses/expands via its header, no gating; (2) collapse state is persisted per project and survives a restart; (3) Done still defaults collapsed when no state has been saved yet. **Persistence reuses the mechanism `docs/spec/ui-layout.md`'s existing "Column Collapse (Rails)" section already documents and `NotesBrowser.svelte` already implements for its own cabinet/tasks rails — the generic `ai_settings` KV table via the existing `get_ai_setting`/`set_ai_setting` Tauri commands, zero new Rust commands** — not localStorage (that mechanism was explicitly superseded by this SQLite approach per a prior Matt ruling documented in the same spec section). Key format `kanban:{projectId}:{status}:collapsed`, values `'true'`/`'false'`, loaded in a sequence-guarded `$effect` on project change, saved immediately on toggle click.

  **Spec:** both the Calendar→board navigation target and the Kanban collapse/persistence behavior were unspecified before this PR (confirmed: no prior hit for either in any `docs/spec/*.md`). Written up as a new `## 3.3 Kanban Board Layout` section in `docs/spec/ui-layout.md`, following the same route #3040/#3042 both took (Reed-confirmed correct both times) — no `spec-covered-by:` marker needed, since this PR's own diff touches `docs/spec/`. Item G needed no spec addition: adopting the existing, already-specified `ConfirmDialog` contract in two more call sites is not new unspecified behavior.

- Fixed the agent prompt's remaining drift and a real caching bug: removed the daily-log "you SHOULD write to it" instructions, reworded the web-fetch follow-up rule to match what the code actually enforces, fixed the ABSOLUTE RULES numbering, moved the per-turn-variable note header out of the cacheable prefix, fixed the OpenRouter `[CACHE]` log's field names, and added a real token-budget regression test (`~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-16-scope-agent-instructions.md`, PRs 3/5/7/7b plus Matt-rulings item 6). **Lane 2's LAST PR — ships in 1.0.61.** Tracked on #3036.

  **R1 — daily-log instructions removed, backend guard untouched.** The system prompt's "## Daily Logging (IMPORTANT) ... You SHOULD write to the daily log" block (injected whenever a `daily_note_id` resolved) and `execute_list_daily_logs`'s own tool-result hint ("Use append_to_note with the note ID to add entries") both told the agent to do something `append_to_note`'s `note_type="daily"` guard has always refused, unconditionally, for the life of the feature — the instruction was the bug, not the guard. Both removed; `execute_list_daily_logs` now points at `read_note` instead. ABSOLUTE RULE 16 (formerly the non-numeric `15-SYS`) still states the prohibition in the prompt itself, untouched. `docs/spec/memory-pipeline.md` §5.6.4 documents this directly ("the chat agent is not a fifth writer").

  **R3 — rule 30 (formerly 27) reworded to match `check_web_taint`/`MUTATE_EXISTING_TOOLS`, which are byte-for-byte unchanged.** The old wording named only `create_note` as exempt (omitting `create_sheet`, which the code also exempts), didn't connect the restriction to the prompt-injection rationale, and — the same drift class this whole scope exists to fix — never mentioned 6 of the 17 real `MUTATE_EXISTING_TOOLS` entries (the sheet-mutation tools, added across #2339 PR16/#2874 item 35/#2970, after the prose was last hand-updated). New text states the rationale explicitly and says the restriction categorically ("every tool that edits, moves, sets a status or priority on, or deletes an existing note, project, folder, subtask, or sheet is blocked") instead of hand-listing examples, removing the drift surface instead of just widening the hand-list. `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.6.3's own `MUTATE_EXISTING_TOOLS` documentation had the identical under-count and is corrected in the same PR.

  **PR 5 — rule 3 gains a carve-out; rule 20 (formerly 18) is narrowed.** Rule 3 ("ONE ACTION PER REQUEST") previously contradicted rules 13/14 (navigate-after-create), which instruct a second, unrequested tool call as standard practice — new text adds an explicit carve-out for the rulebook's own fixed follow-ups. **Rule 20's narrowing loosens a gate, not a drift fix — flagged for Matt's sign-off before merge, exact proposed wording in the PR body under its own heading, per instruction.** The old wording ("only use tools when the user asks you to DO something — create, edit, open, set, change, add, delete") read literally gives the model no permission to use read-only tools (`search_notes`, `search_memory`, `list_daily_logs`, `read_note`, etc.) proactively to answer a question, directly undercutting rules 26/27 (formerly 24/24a) which already assume that permission exists. New wording scopes the rule to mutating tools specifically and states read-only tools may be used proactively.

  **Rule numbering fixed — two duplicate `4`s, two duplicate `20`s, a non-numeric `15-SYS` and `24a`, and a missing `22` (pre-existing before #3039 removed the old rule 6 without renumbering, confirmed by Reed on `main`) — now sequential `0`-`31`, no duplicates, no gaps.** Every cross-reference to a rule number anywhere in the codebase, tests, and this spec was updated to match (`tools.rs`'s `navigate` doc comment, `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.8.3, and every test assertion/comment in `commands.rs` that quoted a rule's number or exact text) — checked by a repo-wide grep for every old number, not assumed. New §4.5.9A in `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` documents the full renumbering, R1, and the rule 3/20 wording changes.

  **PR 7 — caching: `note_header` moved out of the front of the system prompt, so the static block can be cached.** `db_context`'s note-specific lines ("Currently viewing note: X" plus a content preview) used to be PREPENDED ahead of the per-agent prompt, ABSOLUTE RULES, and the generated tools section — since that text changes on nearly every turn, the system prompt's first byte was per-turn-variable whenever any note was open (the common case), meaning the ~6,400-token static block got ZERO cache benefit from any provider's prefix-anchored cache, not reduced benefit. Moved to append alongside `rest_context` (already correctly dynamic-last) at the end instead. **Only the Anthropic-direct path has a confirmed, measurable benefit** — per #2985, OpenClaw's own OpenAI-compat gateway drops `cache_control` before forwarding, so an OpenClaw-origin dispatch gets no benefit from this fix regardless (the markers are inert on arrival); an OpenRouter-direct dispatch's benefit depends on that specific upstream's own passthrough behavior and isn't verifiable from this repo. Harmless on every path either way — never worse, just not universal. `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §26.4's own "Anthropic (via OpenClaw)" table row, which incorrectly claimed the same 90% savings as the direct path, is corrected in the same PR (§26.11 has the full writeup).

  **PR 7b — the OpenRouter `[CACHE]` log's field names were wrong, so cache hits were invisible.** `openrouter.rs`'s `log_cache_metrics` was a copy-paste of `anthropic.rs`'s own (for that path, correct) field names — `cache_creation_input_tokens`/`cache_read_input_tokens` — which OpenRouter's real `usage` object never carries; it reports cache accounting nested under `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`/`cache_write_tokens`, OpenAI-compat style. Every OpenRouter/Venice/OpenClaw-origin request logged `cache_write: 0 | cache_read: 0` regardless of what actually happened upstream — the log could never be used as evidence either way. Fixed to read the real nested keys; no change to what's enforced, sent, or billed.

  **Ruling 6 — a token-budget test that assembles the prompt from the real code, plus a per-turn log line with real totals.** `tests_3036_pr3_token_budget::test_static_prompt_assembled_from_real_code_stays_under_token_budget` (`commands.rs`) calls the real `build_messages_with_context` (richest "anthropic" runtime), counts tokens with Pane's own `TokenEstimationRatio`, and fails loudly past a 10,000-token budget (real measured size at write time: ~22.5k chars / ~6,400 tokens) — per the #2995 lesson, it has no hand-written copy of the prompt to drift against, since both the text and the token count come from the same production functions every real dispatch uses. A sibling test, `test_static_prefix_is_byte_identical_across_requests_with_different_notes`, directly pins PR 7's fix (builds the real prompt twice with two different `db_context` values and asserts the shared static prefix is byte-identical). `ai_chat_stream` now also logs `[PROMPT-SIZE] system_chars={} system_tokens_est={} (chars_per_token={})` right after the existing `[CHAT] Sending request with {} tools` line, read from the real, fully-assembled system message (not a smaller separately-computed estimate the way `apply_budget`'s own T1 tier reads) — lets a before/after comparison be read directly off the logs.

No version bump, no DMG build. Out of scope (parked): #3020, #3022, #3023, #3025, #3030, #3033, #3041, #3045. (Relates to #3036)

Screen enumeration:** `CanvasRenderer.svelte` renders 14 `CanvasViewType` screens; 5 declared values (`welcome`, `today`, `tag`, `tags-manage`, `task_detail`) have no render branch at all and are not agent-reachable by design. Of the 14, `home`/`project_list`/`all_tasks`/`calendar`/`trash`/`kanban` are already reachable via their own dedicated `navigate_*` tools (not duplicated into `show_view`); `note_editor`/`note_list` are contextual/aliases of `notes_browser`; `search_results` needs live query state no bare navigation call can populate. That left `task_list` (#3022's confirmed gap — advertised by `navigate`'s old prose, never implemented anywhere), `settings`, `project_config`, and `dashboard` reachable by **no** AI tool at all — all four added to `show_view`'s new `view` param (`SHOW_VIEW_SCREENS`, `tools.rs`). **2. `navigate`'s drift removed, not repaired:** the `view`/`tab` params (dead `folder_detail`/`project_detail` enum values, removed from the frontend in v10.13.0) are gone — `show_view` owns screen-switching now; the schema's literal duplicate `"project_id"` key is gone too. **3. The real bug:** bare `navigate({project_id})` silently did nothing, every time — the backend defaulted the emitted view to the dead `"folder_detail"`, which `ChatSidebar.svelte`'s view-only switch couldn't match, and that switch returned unconditionally on no match, so the branch that would have opened the project correctly was never reached. Fixed on both ends: the backend now emits the live `"notes_browser"`; the frontend's navigation decision (`src/lib/utils/navigationDispatch.ts`'s new `decideNavigationAction`, called by `ChatSidebar.svelte`) checks bare-project navigation before any view-only switch, so it can never again be shadowed. **4. Never silent:** `decideNavigationAction` has no bare `return` on "nothing matched" anywhere — every input resolves to a concrete action or an `{ kind: 'error' }` `ChatSidebar.svelte` surfaces as a visible, dismissible banner in `ChatPanel.svelte` (reusing `connectionError`'s styling, minus its connection-specific action button). **5. Parity test:** `ShowView.viewParity.test.ts` (`canvas.showViewParity.test.ts`) reads `tools.rs`'s `SHOW_VIEW_SCREENS` and `canvas.ts`'s mirror of the same name directly via regex and asserts the two declared SETS and ORDER are identical — following the `refreshEvent.mirrorParity.test.ts`/`ShHeaderMenu.columnTypesParity.test.ts` precedent, plus (new, addressing that precedent's two named weaknesses) a sanity assertion on the EXACT expected extraction length (not just non-empty, so a quote-style/whitespace regex break can't silently compare two wrong-but-equal sets and pass) and explicit injection tests proving the set-equality check actually fails when a dead name is injected on either side alone. States plainly: this proves the two DECLARED lists agree, not that `CanvasRenderer.svelte` has a working render branch for each one — that reachability claim is covered separately, by direct inspection (this PR's screen enumeration) and by `tests_3036_pr2_navigate_and_show_view` (`commands.rs`), which builds the real per-screen `navigate_action` JSON through a real project (`create_project_internal`), never a raw `INSERT`. **Tests:** 8 new backend tests (schema shape, the bare-project bug fix proven via `build_bare_project_navigate_action`/`build_show_view_navigate_action` against a real created project, the `SHOW_VIEW_SCREENS` constant and its schema-enum mirror); 4 `ChatPanel.navError.test.ts` mounting the real component and asserting the error banner actually renders in the DOM, dismisses, and omits the connection-specific action button). `cargo check` clean (same 2 pre-existing, unrelated warnings). `cargo test` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2505 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored, 11 filtered out (base, run separately on this same checkout: 2497/0/5/11 — exactly +8, zero regressions; `crsql_internal_sync_bit` (`ai::commands::tombstoning_tests::test_upgrade_from_v85_fixture_migrates_cleanly_to_v86`, NOT under the skipped `test_backup` module) and the TLS cert tests ran and passed this invocation — known flakes, did not reproduce this run). `pnpm vitest run`: 2997 passed, 1 skipped (base 2964+1 — exactly +33, zero regressions). `smoke-fresh-db`: PASS, 0 violations. `smoke-upgrade-db`: PASS, 2 allowlisted pre-existing violations (Memory.md backfill temp-file-creation failures for two fixture projects) — unchanged baseline. `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.8.3 (new) documents the final `navigate`/`show_view` split, the enumeration, and the parity test's scope. **This is lane 2 PR 2 of 3.** Out of scope: #3036 PRs 3/5/7/7b; lane 1's items C–G (separate Stia, `ai/commands.rs` overlap expected, diff kept tight); #3020/#3023/#3025/#3030/#3033/#3041 (parked). - Fixed the folder pill's sheet-move crash, a new project's invisible default folder, and five agent tools emitting the wrong (or no) refresh event (1.0.60 live-test-failures scope items 2/C, 4/D, and 5/E, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-16-scope-1060-test-failures.md`, plus the scope comment on #2874). **Lane 1 PR 4 — ships in 1.0.61.** Tracked on #2874.

  **Item C — the folder pill couldn't move sheets:** `update_note_internal`'s move branch (`notes.rs`) was a second, drifted copy of `move_note_internal`'s relocation logic that called `relocate_note_file` unconditionally, with none of `move_note_internal`'s existing `current.file_path.is_empty()` guard — a sheet's `file_path` is always `""`, so moving one via the folder pill always failed with "Invalid file path." **Deleted the second implementation, per Matt's ruling, rather than copying the guard into it:** the branch now calls `move_note_internal` directly (same `enforce_system_guard: true` it already had via its own `reject_system_note_move` call, now made internally by `move_note_internal` itself). `move_note_internal` re-reads the note fresh from the same open connection/transaction, so a title-rename immediately before a move in the same `update_note` call still chains correctly with no separate file-path-tracking variable needed.

  **Item D — a new project's default folder was invisible until a second folder existed:** `create_project_internal` creates the project AND its default folder in the same transaction, but `create_project` (both the Sidebar's Tauri command and the AI agent's tool, which both call it) emitted only ONE `pane-data-changed` event — for the project's own id — so the sidebar's single-entity patch handler never learned the folder's id existed. **New shared helper, `projects::emit_project_created_events(app, project_id, default_folder_id)`**, used by BOTH callers: emits the project's `created` event, then (if a default folder exists) the folder's own `created` event — §34's existing `entity_type`/`reason` values only, no new ones invented. The agent path routes through this exact same function via a new special case in `ai::commands::emit_entity_change_for_tool` (`create_project` can't use the ordinary single-tuple `tool_entity_change` path, since one call now needs to fire two events).

  **Item E — agent refresh events carried the wrong id, or none at all (two defects):** (1) `edit_note`, `append_to_note`, `set_status`, `set_priority`, and `delete_note` all accept a `note_id` param that may be a UUID or a title (`resolve_note_id`, which the executors themselves already call) — but the event-emission code read the RAW, unresolved param, so a title-based call emitted an `entity_id` no UUID-keyed listener could ever match (silently dropped, no error). **Fixed via a new shared `resolve_note_entity_for_event`**, which calls the exact same `resolve_note_id` the executor uses and tags `entity_type` as `sheet`/`note` from the resolved row's own `note_type` column, never a guess. (2) `move_note`, `move_folder`, and `star_project` (the AI agent's own tool versions, distinct from the Sidebar's `move_note`/`move_folder` Tauri commands, which already emitted) fired no event at all — fixed the same way, each resolving its own target via the shared resolver its own executor uses (a new `resolve_folder_id_by_id_or_name`, now also used BY `execute_move_folder` itself instead of a second inline copy; the existing `resolve_project_id`, which also replaced `execute_star_project`'s own ad hoc, unvalidated "does this string look like a UUID" heuristic).

  **The real deliverable of item E, per Matt's instruction:** a new test, `test_every_write_tool_fires_an_event_on_success`, walks every tool marked `ToolAccess::Write` or `ToolAccess::HomeOnlyWrite` in the tool registry itself (`tools::write_tool_names()` ∪ `tools::home_only_tool_names()`, #3038's existing marks — not a hand-typed `Vec` of tool names, which #2995 already ruled proves nothing) and fails if a successful call for any of them emits no `pane-data-changed` event. A write tool with no fixture in this test's match hits an explicit panic naming the tool, forcing one to be added; a tool with a fixture that forgets its own emit wiring fails the "an event fired" assertion. Either gap fails the build — this is the test that would have caught `move_note`/`move_folder`/`star_project`'s total silence automatically.

  **Tests, every one through real commands, never a raw `INSERT`:** `notes.rs`'s new `folder_pill_move_tests` (the folder pill moves a sheet — confirmed FAILING at base with exactly "Invalid file path" by temporarily reverting the fix and re-running; and a plain note, confirmed already passing at base, honestly noted as a control rather than a new bug) — both checked for DB/disk consistency (folder_id updated, sheet's `file_path` stays empty, the note's real file physically relocated with byte-identical content). `projects.rs`'s new `emit_project_created_events_tests` (the precondition that `create_project_internal` always sets a real `default_folder_id`; both events fire with the right id/type/reason; a defensive no-default-folder case emits only the project event) plus a source-scan proving the `create_project` command wrapper calls the new shared helper exactly once and no longer calls `emit_data_changed` directly. `ai/commands.rs`'s new `test_agent_create_project_tool_fires_both_project_and_default_folder_events` (confirmed FAILING at base by temporarily disabling the new special case — zero events instead of two) and the new `item_e_agent_event_resolution_tests` module: one test per affected tool proving a TITLE-based call emits the RESOLVED uuid (all 10 of these confirmed FAILING at base by temporarily reverting the resolver — each asserted the title string leaked through instead of the uuid), a sheet-targeted `set_status` call proving the `sheet`/`note` tag comes from the row not a guess, `move_note`/`move_folder`/`star_project` each proven to emit now, and the registry-walking test itself. **Screen test** (`Sidebar.projectCreateDefaultFolder.test.ts`, new): simulates the real two-event sequence a project creation now produces and asserts the sidebar shows the new project AND its default folder from ONE creation, with the single-entity patch handler (not a full reload) doing the work — `Sidebar.svelte` itself needed zero changes, since its existing `handleDataChangedEvent` already patched in any announced `project`/`folder` row correctly; the gap was entirely that the backend never announced the folder.

  `cargo check` clean (same 2 pre-existing, unrelated warnings — `unused import: Manager` in `notes.rs`, `ENTITY_CATEGORY` unused, both confirmed present at base too). `cargo test` (`--test-threads=1 --skip tests::test_backup::`): **2514 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored, 11 filtered out** — base re-run myself at `049d6c08` for this PR (not inherited): **2497 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored, 11 filtered out** — exactly +17 new tests (2 + 4 + 11, matching every new test named above), zero regressions. `ai::commands::tombstoning_tests::test_upgrade_from_v85_fixture_migrates_cleanly_to_v86` (the real location of the long-running `crsql_internal_sync_bit` flake — confirmed NOT under the skipped `tests::test_backup::` module, so this filter does not exclude it) ran and passed this run; the TLS-cert-pinning tests (`gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::*`) also ran and passed — no flake reproduced in either full run, reported as observed for this run specifically, not claimed as fixed or permanently flake-free. `pnpm vitest run`: **2965 passed, 1 skipped** (base-merged count at #3040 was 2964+1 — exactly +1 new test file/test, zero regressions). `smoke-fresh-db`: PASS, ready signal detected. `smoke-upgrade-db`: PASS, ready signal detected (v90→v91).

Out of scope: items F, G, and the Kanban collapse (next lane 1 PR); all of #3036 (lane 2 owns it — `ai/commands.rs` overlap expected, diff kept tight to this item's own match arms/functions); #3020, #3022, #3023, #3025, #3030, #3033, #3041 (parked). `docs/spec/data-refresh.md` §34 updated directly in this PR (the `create_project` bullet corrected for item D; a new §34.7A documents item E's two defects and the registry-walking test) — no `spec-covered-by:` needed, since this PR's own diff touches `docs/spec/`. - Fixed the agent stopping mid-task with no explanation at all — Matt's live test stopped at 390 of 750 rows and said nothing (1.0.60 live-test-failures scope item 8, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-16-scope-1060-test-failures.md`; rule-6 removal from `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-16-scope-agent-instructions.md` PR 4). **Lane 1 PR 2 — ships in 1.0.61.** Tracked on #2874 and #3036. **The bug:** the tool-iteration-cap/wall-clock-timeout exit path was already designed to make one follow-up "summarize what's done/remaining" LLM call when it fired — but if THAT call itself failed, the failure was swallowed to a server-side `eprintln!` only, and the turn ended with `done:true` and whatever (often empty) `accumulated_text` already existed. **Every early-exit path in `ai_chat_stream`'s agentic loop, enumerated by hand, not sampled** (`src-tauri/src/ai/commands.rs`): Exit A — iteration cap (`if iteration > max_iterations`, :14676); Exit B — clean completion, no tool calls (`tool_calls.is_empty()`, :15191, inline `done:true` emit at :15215); Exit C — provider error (`Err((e, stream_partial))`, :15902, inline `done:true` emit at :15984); Exit D — wall-clock timeout (`loop_start.elapsed() >= loop_timeout`, :14687); Exit A/D share one post-loop `done:true` emit site (:16201) after the optional summary-call follow-up. (The `"done": true` literals at commands.rs ~32813+ are mock Ollama test fixture JSON, not a fourth real exit path — checked and ruled out.) An existing source-scan test (`tests_2604_stream_done_agent_attribution`) already asserted exactly these 3 real emit sites exist — confirms the enumeration rather than needing a new counting mechanism. **One shared function builds the stop message for ALL of them:** `build_stop_fallback_message(exit_kind: &AgentExitKind, completed: &[String]) -> String` (:11540) — `AgentExitKind` has exactly the four variants above (`CleanCompletion`, `ProviderError`, `IterationCap`, `WallClockTimeout`); `completed_tool_names`/`describe_completed_tools` extract what actually ran from the turn's own accumulated tool-call list. **Built entirely from facts Pane already has — no model call, by design:** this is the actual fix for the bug, since a fallback that itself needs the model to run can fail the exact same way the thing it's falling back for failed. At the post-loop site, the deterministic message now engages unconditionally whenever `accumulated_text` is still empty after the summary-call attempt — covering both the `Err` (call failed) and the rarer `Ok("")` (call "succeeded" with nothing) cases uniformly — and is additive, never appended on top of a summary call that actually produced real text. Exit B/C also route through the same function, gated on "only when there's genuinely nothing to show," so neither path can regress into carrying real model/error output. **Rule 6 removed in the same PR, only because a stop can no longer be silent:** the "Use at most 5 tool actions per response" line (ABSOLUTE RULES, previously a duplicate-numbered "6." alongside the unrelated "NEVER narrate..." rule 6) is deleted outright — the ABSOLUTE RULES block already had duplicate/non-sequential numbering before this change (two "4."s, two "6."s, a missing "22") so no renumbering was needed or performed; every other rule's text and number is untouched, confirmed by test. **300-cell sheet-row guidance (`RECOMMENDED_CELLS_PER_ADD_SHEET_ROWS_CALL`) deliberately untouched** — separate question, out of scope per this PR's own instructions. **14 new backend tests, all built against the real production functions** (`build_stop_fallback_message`, `completed_tool_names`, `describe_completed_tools`, `AgentExitKind`, `build_messages_with_context` — the same function `prevention_rule_tests_2874_60_pr4` already uses to test rule 28's prompt text), not mocks or hand-copied restatements: `build_stop_fallback_message` tested directly for all four exit kinds, including a zero-completed-tools case and a message naming the actual provider error text; a control test proves the fallback does NOT engage (and does not duplicate) when a summary call succeeds with real content; two state-machine simulations (matching the established `done_emit_guard_tests` pattern, since `ai_chat_stream` itself needs a live `AppHandle` + network provider stack unavailable in a unit test) prove the exact post-loop control flow leaves `accumulated_text` non-empty after both a summary-call `Err` and an `Ok("")`; rule 6's removal is proven against the live system prompt (`build_messages_with_context`), confirming the text is gone, the sibling rule 6 and rule 7 survive untouched and adjacent, and no "5 tool actions" phrasing remains anywhere in the prompt. ### Fixed
- Fixed `scripts/build.sh`'s DMG packaging: the final `hdiutil create` hand-wrapped `Pane.app` directly, producing a DMG with no `/Applications` shortcut (nowhere to drag the app), and only the app itself got stapled — never the DMG (`stapler validate` on the DMG reported "does not have a ticket stapled to it"), and the DMG shipped `-rw-------` (600, owner-only), so anyone but the building user got "The disk image couldn't be opened. Permission denied." A staple failure (`xcrun stapler staple ... || echo`) also only warned and still shipped the DMG — how an unnotarized artifact landed in `~/Shared/ExampleApp/builds/`. **Packaging now reuses Tauri's own DMG layout** (Applications shortcut, background, window position) instead of hand-wrapping: Tauri's macOS bundler has no standalone `bundle_dmg.sh` to invoke in this Tauri version (compiled into the `@tauri-apps/cli` native binary), and re-running `tauri build --bundles dmg` after stapling risks Tauri re-copying/re-signing the `.app` and silently discarding the staple — so the already-produced Tauri DMG is mounted, its pre-staple `Pane.app` is swapped for the real signed+notarized+stapled copy, and repacked, keeping Tauri's layout byte-for-byte while guaranteeing the app inside is the stapled one. **The DMG itself is now notarized and stapled too**, then `chmod a+r`'d. **Fails closed:** every notarize/staple `|| echo` warning on the signing/notarizing/packaging path is now fatal when credentials are present (app notarization, app stapling, DMG notarization, DMG stapling, and a tightened dylib-signing loop — `find -exec` doesn't propagate a failing `codesign`'s exit status on macOS). The script builds to a hidden staging path and only `mv`s to the real `~/Shared/ExampleApp/builds/` name after `stapler validate`, a readability check, and an Applications-shortcut check all pass, so a mid-pipeline failure can never leave a half-made DMG at the real name. The `--allow-branch` UNOFFICIAL dev path is unchanged — notarization/stapling are skipped (not fatal) when Apple credentials are absent, same as before. **Docs updated** (`docs/INVARIANTS.md`, `docs/dev-hygiene-playbook.md`, `docs/spec/testing.md`, `docs/SPAWN-CHECKLISTS.md`, `README.md`) to state DMGs come only from `scripts/build.sh`, never a raw `tauri build`; public releases still follow the separate CI-driven `docs/release-runbook.md` process, untouched. No build was run as part of this change; verified via `bash -n`/`shellcheck`. (Relates to #2874)

### Fixed
- Fixed trash destroying a note's file on soft delete instead of only on Delete Permanently (#2874 item 1, PR A of 10 from the 1.0.60 live-test-failures scope, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-16-scope-1060-test-failures.md`, `docs/spec/file-system.md` §2A.2, rewritten). **The bug:** `delete_note`/`force_delete_note` (both soft deletes, despite the second name) called `delete_note_file` — which moves the file to the OS trash — immediately on soft delete, instead of only on permanent delete. `purge_note_internal` then failed on the missing file (Delete Permanently on an already-trashed note errored), `restore_note` had no recovery logic at all, and the watcher's own "already imported" dedup check additionally re-imported any trashed note whose file *was* left in place. **Matt's five rulings, implemented exactly: (1)** the file now stays exactly where it is while a note sits in Pane's own Trash — soft delete is DB-only (`UPDATE notes SET deleted_at = ...`), full stop; the `delete_note_file` calls are removed from both `delete_note` and `force_delete_note` entirely. **(2)** Delete Permanently (`purge_note_internal`) is now the ONLY path that moves a note's file to the OS trash — unchanged in shape, just no longer redundant with an earlier trash that shouldn't have happened. **(3)** a trashed note whose file is already gone purges cleanly: `purge_note_internal` now calls a new `delete_note_file_tolerating_missing` (`database.rs`), which tolerates a confirmed-`NotFound` failure (not a blanket `.ok()` — a real permission/policy-violation failure still surfaces as a hard `Err`) and treats it as "already purged." Needed a real fix two levels deep in `filesystem_policy.rs`: `FsPolicyError` gained a `NotFound`/`Other` kind (`is_not_found()`), set from a confirmed `io::ErrorKind::NotFound` at BOTH the site that actually fires for the common case — `walk_beneath_root`'s per-component inspection, which `authorize_existing` calls with `allow_missing: false` and which therefore fails on the final (or an intermediate) missing component before `authorize_existing`'s own later check ever runs — and that later check itself, for defense in depth. **(4) The watcher's real cause, found and fixed, not papered over:** Matt's citation ("a `deleted_at IS NOT NULL` check at watcher.rs:358") didn't match the live code, which actually read `AND deleted_at IS NULL` — EXCLUDING trashed notes from "already imported." That exclusion was harmless only because, at base, a trashed note's file was always already gone (the old bug trashed it immediately) — this exact branch never ran against a trashed note's still-present file. Now that soft delete leaves the file in place, the fix drops the `deleted_at` filter entirely for this dedup purpose (`process_new_file`, `watcher.rs`): "does any row, trashed or not, already own this `file_path`" is exactly "already imported, don't reimport" — a purged note's row no longer exists at all, so a genuinely-free path still correctly reports re-importable. **(5) No recovery tool — rebuild from `note_versions`, or say so plainly:** `restore_note` now always clears `deleted_at` (the DB row is always restorable) and, when the file is missing, tries to rebuild it from the note's most recent `note_versions` snapshot (written only on an edit, never on creation — a note trashed without a single edit afterward has zero snapshots and is genuinely unrecoverable). The command's response is now `{ meta, content_warning: Option<String> }` instead of a bare `NoteMeta` — `content_warning` names either the snapshot's timestamp ("rebuilt from a saved version from {timestamp} — any edits made after that version are not included") or states plainly "the content was lost before this fix"; `Trash.svelte`'s `handleRestore` surfaces it via `alert`, never a silent, normal-looking restore. `api.ts`'s `restoreFromTrash` and `entityService.ts`'s `restoreNote` both updated to the new response shape. **13 new tests, every one built through the real `#[tauri::command]` entry points (`create_note`, `delete_note`, `restore_note`, `purge_note`) plus `update_note_internal` (the existing AppHandle-plumbing substitute for `update_note` only) — never a raw `INSERT`, per Matt's standing testing rule:** soft delete leaves the file on disk with content intact (`notes.rs`); restore brings it back with content intact and no warning; purge sends the file to the real OS trash (**`#[ignore]`'d** — writes a real file into the developer's actual `~/.Trash` on every run, same #3024/#3027 hygiene rule, manual run command in the test's own doc comment); purge succeeds when the file is already gone, both as a raw-connection regression guard (`empty_filepath_guard_tests`, flipped from its old `is_err()` assertion — this IS the bug, now fixed) and through the full real-command stack; restore with a missing file rebuilds from the latest `note_versions` snapshot (created via a real `update_note` edit) with the rebuilt file's content asserted byte-for-byte; restore with a missing file and no snapshot returns the explicit lost-content message, asserted on the message text, not just `Ok`; the watcher does not re-import a trashed note's still-present file (`watcher.rs`, built against a real on-disk SQLite file since `process_new_file` opens its own connection to `get_db_path()` — an in-memory DB would be invisible to it). **3 new frontend tests** (`Trash.restoreContentWarning.test.ts`) proving `handleRestore` alerts with the backend's exact message on a rebuild, alerts with the exact lost-content message with no snapshot, and does NOT alert when no `content_warning` is present. `cargo check` clean (same 1 pre-existing, unrelated `unused import: Manager` warning in `notes.rs`). `cargo test` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2437 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored, 11 filtered out (base 2431/4/11 — exactly +6 new non-ignored tests [5 in `notes.rs`'s `item2874_trash_lifecycle_tests` plus 1 in `watcher.rs`] and +1 newly-`#[ignore]`'d test; the known `crsql_internal_sync_bit` flake did not reproduce this run). `pnpm vitest run`: 2954 passed, 1 skipped (base 2951+1 — exactly +3 new tests, zero regressions). `smoke-fresh-db`: PASS. `smoke-upgrade-db`: PASS. **This is PR A of 10 from the 1.0.60 scope — it gates item 3a (folder-delete-with-trashed-notes) and affects item 10 (agent empty-trash tool wiring, parked).** Items 2–10 of that scope (including the dialog half of item 3), and #3020/#3022/#3023/#3025/#3030/#3033, are explicitly out of scope for this PR. (Relates to #2874)

- Fixed the FAIL Reed's #3037 audit found in the item-1 trash fix above: `ai/commands.rs::execute_delete_note` (the AI assistant's `delete_note` tool) was a SEPARATE, undisclosed reimplementation of soft delete, never touched by the original PR's diff, that still called `delete_note_file` unconditionally on soft delete — the exact bug item 1 exists to close, surviving on one of its two live entry points — and its own hand-typed system-note list (`"soul"|"rules"|"memory"|"daily"`) was missing `identity`/`user`/`tools` entirely, meaning the AI assistant could trash IDENTITY.md/USER.md/TOOLS.md on request (`~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-16-pr-3037-trash-keeps-file.md`, item 1; `docs/spec/file-system.md` §2A.2, extended). **Matt's ruling: one function per operation.** **Soft delete:** a new `soft_delete_note_internal` (`notes.rs`) owns the system-note check — against `SYSTEM_NOTE_TYPES`, the single canonical list, never a second hand-typed one — and the `UPDATE notes SET deleted_at = ...` tombstone (plus the §19.5.1c(c) subtask-notification dismiss, which `force_delete_note` had been silently missing since it never had that block at all — now gets it for free). `delete_note`, `force_delete_note`, and `execute_delete_note` all call this one function; each caller maps its typed `SoftDeleteNoteError` to its own presentation (`delete_note`/`force_delete_note` keep their existing plain-string error; `execute_delete_note` turns the system-note case into its established `Ok("REFUSED: ...")` reply shape, carrying the note's title — presentation stays in the agent wrapper, the operation doesn't). `execute_delete_note`'s own `delete_note_file` call is removed entirely; its agent-only pre-delete `note_versions` snapshot (no other caller has this) now runs strictly after a successful shared soft-delete, so a refused delete writes no spurious version row. **Permanent delete (Empty Trash):** `empty_trash` was a second, incomplete reimplementation of the same operation `purge_note_internal` already did correctly — it called `delete_note_file` directly with a blanket `.ok()` (ignoring a failed OS-trash move and erasing the row anyway, leaving a stray file with no DB row) and skipped the `note_versions`/sheet-table cascade entirely. It now calls `purge_note_internal` once per trashed item, exactly what `purge_note` already does for one item. **Matt's ruling, implemented exactly:** an item whose file can't be moved stays in Pane's Trash — `purge_note_internal` returns `Err` BEFORE its own `DELETE FROM notes`, so that item's row/tombstone is left completely untouched, retryable later — and the user is told how many: `empty_trash` now returns `{ purged, failed }` instead of a bare count; `Trash.svelte`'s `handleEmptyTrash` alerts on a non-zero `failed`, the same non-blocking pattern `handleRestore`'s `content_warning` already established on this screen (`api.ts`/`entityService.ts` updated to the new return shape). The plain `delete_note_file` (not its missing-file-tolerant wrapper) now has zero callers left anywhere in the crate — kept, not deleted, as the strict primitive its wrapper builds on. **`docs/spec/ai-integration.md`'s `delete_note` tool entry re-verified against the code** (its "sets `deleted_at` only" claim is now actually true for this tool, not assumed); `docs/spec/file-system.md` §2A.2 gains a new ruling 6 for Empty Trash, written the same way rulings 1–5 already are. **5 new backend tests, every one through the real command/tool entry points, never a raw `INSERT` for the thing under test** (direct note-row inserts remain only for seeding a note of a given system `note_type` — no command exists to create one any other way, the identical precedent `system_note_move_guard_tests` already established and passed review): `notes.rs`'s `item2874_trash_lifecycle_tests` gains 3 (`empty_trash` on a sheet clears `sheet_cells`/`sheet_rows`/`sheet_columns`; `empty_trash` tolerates an already-missing file; `empty_trash` leaves a symlink-blocked item's row/tombstone untouched and reports `{purged:1, failed:1}` — the symlink forces a real, deterministic `authorize_existing` rejection, same already-reviewed technique `projects.rs`'s folder-delete leftover tests use, never dependent on the real OS Trash's own success/failure); `ai/commands.rs`'s new `execute_delete_note_system_guard_tests` gains 2 (the agent's `delete_note` tool leaves a plain note's file on disk content-intact; refused on all seven `SYSTEM_NOTE_TYPES`, table-driven, including the three — `identity`/`user`/`tools` — the old hand-typed list missed). All 4 of the bug-confirming scenarios (file trashed by the agent tool, `identity` not refused, sheet tables left behind, row erased despite a failed move) were reproduced via disposable throwaway tests in a scratch worktree checked out at this branch's own pre-fix head first, each confirmed actually failing/buggy there (and removed afterward, never committed) before being written up as the shipped, passing tests above. `cargo check` clean (same 2 pre-existing, unrelated warnings — `unused import: Manager` in `notes.rs`, `ENTITY_CATEGORY` unused). `cargo test` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2442 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored, 11 filtered out (this branch's own stated baseline before this fix: 2437/0/5/11 — exactly +5 new tests, zero regressions; the known `crsql_internal_sync_bit` flake, `test_upgrade_from_v85_fixture_migrates_cleanly_to_v86`, passed this run). `pnpm vitest run`: 2954 passed, 1 skipped — unchanged (no new frontend tests this fix). `smoke-fresh-db`: PASS, 0 violations. `smoke-upgrade-db`: PASS, 2 allowlisted pre-existing violations (Memory.md backfill temp-file-creation failures for two fixture projects) — same documented baseline, no change. ### Added
- internal: #3036 lane 2 PR 1 of 3 (shipping in 1.0.61) — registers the three real-but-unregistered read tools (`read_note`, `read_project_memory`, `read_project_chat`), generates the AI system prompt's `## Available Tools` section directly from the real tool registry, restructures the project-scoped write guard to derive its tool set from each tool's own mark, and (PR #3038, folded into this same branch/PR per instruction) adds a third `ToolAccess` value for the one tool that mark restructure exposed as mis-classified: `create_project`. **This entry replaces an earlier, now-superseded description of this branch** — the two paragraphs below describe what actually shipped on `93433f5e`, not an allowlist-based schema test or a `PROJECT_SCOPED_TOOLS` constant, both of which were removed by this branch's own second commit before `create_project`'s re-classification (its third commit) ever started (Reed's audit, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-17-pr-3038-read-tools-generated-prompt.md`, §8's blocking FAIL on the stale version of this entry).
- **Registry/prompt generation:** `tools::generate_tools_section(runtime_type)` renders name/description/params (required/optional, type, enum) straight from `get_pane_tools_for_runtime()` — the exact function that decides what's natively offered — so there is exactly one copy of each tool's facts; sequencing rules and usage conventions that aren't schema fields stay hand-written in `build_messages_with_context`'s ABSOLUTE RULES block, threaded a new `runtime_type` parameter so the generated section correctly withholds `web_fetch`/`web_search` for non-allowlisted runtimes. **`read_project_notes`, a fourth ghost tool, is dropped entirely per Matt's ruling** (`list_notes` already covers it) — its dead executor and dispatch arm are deleted, not just left unregistered; ABSOLUTE RULES rule 23's nonexistent `list_tasks` reference and rule 24's `read_project_notes` reference are corrected to real tool names.
- **The write guard, restructured to derive from the registry, not a second hand-typed list:** every `ToolDef` now carries a required `access: ToolAccess` field (compile error if omitted — not `Option`, no default). `project_scoped_tools()` (`commands.rs`) derives its membership live from `tools::write_tool_names()` — every `ToolAccess::Write`-marked tool, `OnceLock`-cached — replacing the old local array a new write tool had to be remembered and added to by hand. **A real project-isolation hole found and closed:** `star_project` carries `project_id` directly but had zero cross-project check at all — a project-scoped chat could star/unstar ANY project by ID; now marked `Write` with a matching `check_cross_project_write_permission` arm. **Both allowlists this branch previously shipped with are gone, not relocated:** the schema-completeness test (`test_schema_property_gaps_are_empty_no_allowlist`) now asserts `found_gaps.is_empty()` with zero allowlist — the three gaps it used to pin as "fix later" (`edit_note`+`priority`, `create_project`+`description`/`color`/`category`/`first_folder_name`, `star_project`+`unstar`) are fixed directly in this same branch: `create_project`'s schema gains all four missing fields, `star_project`'s schema gains `unstar`, `list_notes`'s and `create_subtask`'s status enums both now read the shared `VALID_STATUS_VALUES` (closing `create_subtask`'s pre-existing hyphenated-`"in-progress"` data-integrity bug, now validated at the executor too), and `edit_note`'s schema drops `priority` entirely (never had a matching executor read — priority-setting is `set_priority`'s job alone). `set_priority` itself, previously a fully orphaned executor+dispatch arm with no schema and zero validation, is now a registered `ToolDef` (`Write`-marked, project-scoped) whose executor validates against the shared `VALID_PRIORITY_VALUES` instead of writing any string straight to the DB. No `KNOWN_SCHEMA_PROPERTY_GAPS`-style constant, and no `PROJECT_SCOPED_TOOLS` constant, exist anywhere in the final code — both derive from the registry.
- **`create_project` is Home-only, not `Read` (PR #3038, Matt's ruling):** marking it plain `Read` — this branch's own original choice — made the tool look deliberately exempt from the write guard, when the real rule is narrower: only the Home session may create a project at all; a project agent cannot, regardless of which project it would target. A third `ToolAccess` value, `HomeOnlyWrite`, carries that rule directly on the mark (no separate "exception" doc comment needed) — `create_project` is its first member. `tools::home_only_tool_names()` derives the checked set the same way `write_tool_names()` already does for `Write`; a new guard, `check_home_only_tool_permission` (`commands.rs`), is called unconditionally from `execute_single_tool`, before the cross-project guard, and refuses a project-scoped session's attempt with exactly `"Projects can only be created from Home."` — Home chat is unaffected. **Tool-list filtering by session was investigated, not assumed:** the offered tool list (both the generated prompt section and the native wire-schema tools passed to the provider) is filtered ONLY by `runtime_type` today — there is no Home-vs-project session filter anywhere in that pipeline — so `create_project` is still offered to a project-scoped session; the guard refusal above is the sole enforcement, not a backstop behind a tool-list filter. Building that filter is a separate, larger change (`build_messages_with_context` and the native-tools call site in `ai_chat_stream` are both `runtime_type`-only today) and is left for a later PR if wanted; `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4A.5 is updated to describe all three access values, the cross-project guard, and this new Home-only guard as two distinct mechanisms answering two distinct questions. `test_every_registered_tool_is_marked_read_or_write` is extended to assert all three values (not just two), so a future Home-only tool shipped unmarked or mismarked still fails the build the same way an unmarked Read/Write tool already did. **Verified through real commands, not just unit assertions on the guard function:** Home creates a project → `execute_create_project` succeeds and the row exists in the DB; a project-scoped session's attempt → refused, and the DB is asserted to have created NO second project (not just that an `Err` came back).
