## [1.0.60] - 2026-10-16

### Added
- internal: Added a parity test pinning `ShHeaderMenu.svelte`'s hand-typed `TYPES` dropdown array to `sheets.rs`'s `VALID_COLUMN_TYPES` (#2874 item 64, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-12-scope-2874-item64-column-types.md`) — item 62 (#3002) deduplicated every Rust-side copy of the 6-value column-type list onto the one canonical constant, but its own follow-up sweep flagged `ShHeaderMenu.svelte:131-137`'s `TYPES` array (the type-change dropdown's data source) as the same defect class in the frontend: a hand-typed `[id, label]` mirror with no check tying it back to `VALID_COLUMN_TYPES`, so a 7th backend type could land with no corresponding dropdown entry and nothing would fail. **No production code changed** — order and membership already matched at base (scope §4); the defect was the absence of an enforced check, not a current divergence. **Mechanism (scope §2):** a Tauri command and a build-time Rust→TS generator were both considered and rejected — the data is `const` and never changes at runtime, so IPC buys no freshness and either needs a loading state or a synchronous fallback array (defeating the single-source goal), and no codegen tooling exists in this repo at all today for six strings that change once a year; also fails to solve the label problem (Rust has no display labels) without inventing a second hand-maintained mapping anyway. Instead, a new test (`ShHeaderMenu.columnTypesParity.test.ts`) follows the exact precedent `refreshEvent.mirrorParity.test.ts` (#2972 Stage 4) already established: `readFileSync` both `sheets.rs` and `ShHeaderMenu.svelte`, extract the ids from each via regex over the literal source text, and compare the two EXTRACTIONS — never a hardcoded list restated from memory (the #2995 lesson). **Labels (scope §3) stay in TypeScript**, in the existing `Array<[id, label]>` tuple shape — the tuple shape already makes "id present with no label" structurally impossible, so the parity test closes the only gap that mattered ("id silently absent from one file"). **Four assertions:** (1) both extractions are non-empty (sanity — catches a regex that silently stops matching and would otherwise make two empty sets compare equal and pass while guarding nothing); (2) the set of ids matches between the two files; (3) the order of ids matches (scope §4: order is currently identical and is part of the contract, not an accident); (4) every id in `TYPES` has a non-empty label. **Negative control:** added a 7th id (`"url"`) to `sheets.rs`'s `VALID_COLUMN_TYPES` only (`ShHeaderMenu.svelte` left untouched) — confirmed assertions 2 and 3 both fail (set/order mismatch, Rust side has the extra `"url"` the Svelte side doesn't), while assertions 1 and 4 still pass, exactly as expected; reverted, `git diff` on `sheets.rs` confirmed clean before committing. **Spec (`docs/spec/sheets.md:102-103`, §33.3.1):** the `col_type` enumeration sentence gains a parenthetical naming the two sites that must agree — "(canonical list: `VALID_COLUMN_TYPES`, `sheets.rs`; UI mirror: `ShHeaderMenu.svelte`'s `TYPES`, kept in sync by a parity test)" — so a future reader is pointed at the real source instead of discovering it the way this scope did. The five per-type `switch` statements (scope §6 — `Card.svelte`'s `sheetTypeGlyph`, `sheetCellRender.ts`'s `typeGlyph`, `sheetView.ts`'s three switches, `SheetGrid.svelte`'s `mismatchExplanation`, `ShHeaderMenu.svelte`'s own `typeGlyphMarkup`) are explicitly out of scope — tracked separately, not touched here. `cargo check`/`cargo test` unaffected (no Rust files changed); `pnpm vitest run`: base 2937 passed + 1 skipped on `main` at this PR's base — +4 for this PR's new test file, 0 regressions. (Relates to #2874)

### Fixed
- Fixed the sibling gap #3031's non-blocking WARN flagged as out of that PR's scope: a system-managed note (`note_type` ∈ `SYSTEM_NOTE_TYPES`) could still be MOVED — project or folder — even though #3031 already blocked renaming one (#2874, tracked on #2874, `docs/spec/file-system.md` §2A.6b, extended). **Matt's ruling, implemented exactly: hard reject, same shape as #3031's title guard** — a clear error, checked before any mutation, so the file and the DB row are both left completely untouched. Reproduced against base commit `b1aeadb6` with a throwaway test calling `move_note_internal` directly: confirmed the move actually succeeded (`Ok(true)`) on a `note_type = 'soul'` note before this fix. **The actual check lives in exactly one new function, `reject_system_note_move` (`notes.rs`), called from all three USER- or AI-initiated move entry points:** the `move_note` command (via `move_note_internal`'s new `enforce_system_guard` flag, `true`), `update_note_internal`'s project/folder-move branch, and the AI move tool (`execute_move_note`, `ai/commands.rs`). **Deliberately not a single unconditional guard inside `move_note_internal` itself**, even though that's the one function every one of those paths funnels through (directly, or via `relocate_note_file`) — `delete_folder_internal` (#2874 item 65) also calls `move_note_internal` to relocate every note out of a folder being deleted, and that forced relocation-to-safety must keep succeeding even for a system note a pre-this-fix move already left sitting in a now-doomed folder on an already-upgraded install (reachable: no guard existed on moves before this PR, so historical data can already have a system note outside its usual location). An unconditional guard there would make such a folder permanently undeletable. `move_note_internal` therefore takes an explicit `enforce_system_guard: bool` — `true` from `move_note`, `false` only from `delete_folder_internal`'s forced relocation, with a comment at both call sites explaining why. **6 new backend tests, each table-driven over all 7 `SYSTEM_NOTE_TYPES` internally (every type actually exercised, not just asserted about in the abstract):** `notes.rs`'s `system_note_move_guard_tests` (`move_note_internal` rejects every type with file+DB untouched; `update_note_internal`'s move branch does the same; a plain note still moves via both, folder move and project move, with file content verified at the new path); `ai/commands.rs`'s `execute_move_note_system_guard_tests` (same rejection proof for the AI tool, plus its own plain-note-still-moves control); `projects.rs`'s `folder_delete_moves_content_tests` gains `test_delete_folder_relocates_every_system_note_type_to_default_folder` — seeds one note of every system type plus one plain note into a folder, deletes it, and proves every single one lands in the default folder with byte-identical content, confirming the bypass flag actually keeps folder deletion working. `cargo check` clean (same 2 pre-existing, unrelated warnings). `cargo test` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2431 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored, 11 filtered out (base ~2425/4/11 per #3031 — exactly +6 new tests, zero regressions; the known `crsql_internal_sync_bit` flake did not reproduce this run). `pnpm vitest run`: 2951 passed, 1 skipped — unchanged from base (no frontend files touched by this fix). `smoke-fresh-db`: PASS, 0 violations. `smoke-upgrade-db`: PASS, 2 allowlisted pre-existing violations (Memory.md backfill temp-file-creation failures for two fixture projects) — exactly the documented baseline, no change. (Relates to #2874)
- Fixed the cause of duplicate `.pane/system/` files instead of papering over the symptom: `update_note_internal`'s title-rename had no `note_type` guard, and a self-colliding rename could orphan a daily log's real content under a `-N` suffix, which the now-removed cleanup function then deleted — keeping the empty stub (#3029, tracked on #2874, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-12-scope-3029-system-duplicates.md`, `docs/spec/file-system.md` new §2A.6b). **The traced chain:** a title-rename on a daily-log note slugifies to the SAME filename it already has (e.g. a trailing-whitespace-only edit) → `generate_unique_slug` (`notes.rs`) didn't exclude the note's own current file from its collision check, so it treated its own file as a clash and bumped to `{date}-1.md` → the next "find today's log" lookup, keyed on the now-stale `title`, missed the renamed row and created a fresh, empty `{date}.md` → the next sync pull's `cleanup_pane_system_duplicate_files` (pure filesystem scan, zero DB correlation) deleted `{date}-1.md` — the file with the real content — keeping the empty stub. Reproduced against base commit `67044319` with a throwaway test calling base's own functions directly; confirmed FAILING with the sentinel content actually destroyed (quoted in the PR body). **Matt's rulings, implemented exactly: (1) Hard reject, not a silent no-op** — `update_note_internal` now rejects a title change on any system-managed `note_type` with a clear error, checked before any mutation, so the file and DB row are both left completely untouched. **The system note-type list now has exactly one Rust-side source** (`SYSTEM_NOTE_TYPES`, `notes.rs`) — there was none before; the frontend's `Editor.svelte` had the only copy, already hand-duplicated into two test files with nothing tying any of them together. Per #3026/item-64's established precedent, a true single source across the Rust/TypeScript boundary isn't achievable (this data is `const`, so IPC buys no freshness and no codegen tooling exists in this repo) — so the frontend keeps one mirror, but consolidated: a new `src/lib/constants/systemNoteTypes.ts` is now the ONE hand-typed TypeScript copy, imported by `Editor.svelte` and both test files instead of each re-declaring it, kept honest by a new `systemNoteTypes.parity.test.ts` (reads both files' literal source via regex, fails on drift — the exact #3026 mechanism). **(2)** `generate_unique_slug` (`notes.rs`) now excludes the note's own current filename from its collision check; `update_note_internal` skips the actual file-rename syscall when the resolved new path equals the current path (renaming a file onto itself isn't a real rename — the lower-level `pane_fs.rename` treats an already-existing destination as a collision regardless of whether it's a different file or this exact one). **(3)** the daily-log "today" lookup (`ai/commands.rs`) now resolves by the immutable per-date filename encoded in `file_path` (`LIKE '%/{date}.md'`), not by the editable `title` column — extracted into its own `find_or_create_todays_daily_note` function so it's unit-testable directly, zero behavior change on the real dispatch path. **(4)** `cleanup_pane_system_duplicate_files` and all three callers removed (`sync/commands.rs`'s post-sync-pull call and its now-unused import, the `cleanup_duplicate_files` Tauri command and its `lib.rs` registration, `Onboarding.svelte`'s `invoke('cleanup_duplicate_files')`) — a new source-scan test proves the retired names are completely gone from `src-tauri/src/`+`src/`. **The separate DB-level dedup (`dedup_pane_system`/`dedup_folders_and_notes`) stays, untouched** — it guards a different legacy bug in a scheme whose only creator was deleted in March 2026; a real-install data check for whether any such legacy rows still exist is out of this scope's budget, so its removal is filed separately as **#3030, parked**. **No one-time cleanup of existing `-N` files** — Matt's call; they persist. **Two ride-alongs:** `docs/INVARIANTS.md`/`docs/spec/default-project.md` corrected — both still claimed the `remove_dir_all` fallback #3028 already removed; `attachments.rs`'s `delete_attachment` gains a `[CRITICAL]` log for the trash-succeeds-then-DB-delete-fails divergence window (#3028 audit residual finding — the file is already gone/trashed while the DB row still claims it exists, previously logged as an ordinary command failure with no distinguishing severity). **New spec section** `docs/spec/file-system.md` §2A.6b states plainly: system filenames are fixed by role, never derived from title, never get a `-N`, and title edits on system notes are rejected server-side. **6 new backend tests** (`notes.rs`: self-collision no longer bumps to a suffix — byte-identical content re-verified at the original path; every one of the 7 system `note_type`s rejects a title rename with the file byte-identical and the DB row untouched. `ai/commands.rs`: the retired-function source scan; `find_or_create_todays_daily_note` finds the existing row by file-path even with a deliberately-corrupted stale title and is idempotent across two calls in a row ("running sync pull twice"); the same idempotency starting cold (create then immediately rerun); `write_system_file` called twice with different content ("running onboarding twice") — last write wins, zero `-N` files, honestly noted as already passing at base, included as a legitimate regression guard per the scope brief, not a found bug) **plus 3 new frontend tests** (`systemNoteTypes.parity.test.ts`). `cargo check` clean (2 pre-existing, unrelated warnings). `cargo test` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2425 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored, 11 filtered out (base 2418/1(known flake)/4/11 — the known pre-existing `crsql_internal_sync_bit` flake happened to pass this run, plus exactly +6 new tests). `pnpm vitest run`: 2951 passed, 1 skipped (base 2948+1 — exactly +3 new tests, zero regressions). `smoke-fresh-db`: PASS, 0 violations. `smoke-upgrade-db`: PASS, 2 allowlisted pre-existing violations (Memory.md backfill temp-file-creation failures for two fixture projects) — exactly the documented baseline, no change. (Relates to #3029)
- Fixed `delete_project_internal` falling back to a permanent `remove_dir_all` whenever moving a top-level project's directory to the OS trash failed — the same destructive-fallback shape Matt just ruled out for folders in #3024, but for an entire project's directory this time: every note, sheet, and attachment the user ever put in that project was destroyed for good, with no OS trash step and no error saying what actually happened (#3027, `docs/spec/file-system.md` §2A.6a, new — §2A.9's pre-existing "Disk full during delete" row already specified this in general terms; this is the first place that row is actually implemented, not just aspirational). **Matt's ruling, implemented exactly: (1)** a trash failure now stops the delete unconditionally — **no `remove_dir_all` fallback exists anywhere on this path anymore** — and the caller gets an `Err` naming Trash specifically (`"Could not move project '{name}' to Trash (...). The project was not deleted."`), never a generic failure message. **(2) Disk and DB never diverge — ordering and every failure branch stated:** the `attachments` cleanup and the `projects` row delete (CASCADE handles notes/folders) now run inside one SQL transaction that stays **uncommitted** while the directory trash is attempted. Trash fails → the function returns before `commit()`, the transaction drops uncommitted and rusqlite rolls back every DB write automatically (the row is restored exactly as it was) — disk is untouched since `trash()` never completed; nothing happened on either side. Trash succeeds → commit. The one residual risk this ordering cannot remove — `commit()` itself failing after a successful trash, since the `trash` crate exposes no "undo" to call instead — is logged as CRITICAL; this ordering was chosen specifically because it is the only one that can satisfy point 1 (committing the row's deletion before attempting trash would mean a failed trash still left the row gone). **Sweep of the rest of the codebase for the same shape (ruling 3), full table in the PR:** the identical destructive-fallback bug was also found and fixed in `database.rs`'s `delete_note_file` (used by every note delete/purge path — not on Matt's own list, found during the sweep) — removed the same `trash()`-fails-so-`remove_file()` fallback; every caller already treats the resulting `Err` correctly (soft `delete_note`/`force_delete_note` log it and leave the file in place rather than destroying it; `purge_note_internal` calls it before its own DB delete, so a failure there now stops the purge with row and file both intact, matching ruling 1's shape). A second category — permanent delete of user content with **no trash attempt at all**, not a fallback — was found in `projects.rs`'s own legacy pre-v67 attachment cleanup (switched `remove_dir_all` → `trash()`, kept non-fatal) and in `attachments.rs`'s `delete_attachment` command (switched both `remove_file` call sites to `trash()`). Internal/system-owned paths (`ai/commands.rs`'s sync-rollback cleanup of directories it had just created and its dedup/orphan-cleanup of its own agent-workspace files, `sync_client.rs`'s identical rollback cleanup, `backup.rs`'s DB backup rotation, `sync/`'s session/keystore files, `.pane/tasks/` legacy migration cleanup) were reviewed and are a different category — Pane's own state, not user content — and left as-is. **Real-trash test hygiene (ruling 4):** #3024's `test_delete_folder_trashes_untracked_leftover_file_instead_of_deleting_it`, which writes a real file into the developer's actual `~/.Trash` on every run including CI, is now `#[ignore]` with its manual run command documented in a doc comment; its symlink-based sibling test (fully deterministic, never touches the real OS trash) stays always-on, matching this PR's own two new tests, neither of which touches the real OS trash either. **2 new backend tests** in `projects.rs` (`test_delete_project_trash_failure_leaves_project_and_files_intact` — the project directory itself is swapped for a symlink to real content living outside `Projects/` entirely, so `PaneFs::authorize_existing`'s unconditional symlink rejection fires before `trash::delete` is ever reached; confirmed failing against the pre-fix code first — the old code's fallback-chain error, `"Failed to delete project directory: symlink path component rejected: ..."`, says nothing about Trash, while the fix's error explicitly does, and the project/note rows and file content are asserted present and byte-identical either way; `test_delete_project_removes_from_db`, pre-existing, confirmed still passing unchanged — the ordinary successful-delete path through the new transaction). `cargo check` clean (2 pre-existing, unrelated warnings). `cargo test` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2418 passed, 1 failed (`ai::commands::tombstoning_tests::test_upgrade_from_v85_fixture_migrates_cleanly_to_v86` — independently reproduced identically against a clean `origin/main` checkout in a separate worktree, `no such function: crsql_internal_sync_bit`; confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to this PR's diff, not the previously-documented gateway-cert flake), 4 ignored (base 3 + the 1 newly-`#[ignore]`'d real-trash test), 11 filtered out. `pnpm vitest run`: 2948 passed, 1 skipped (no frontend files touched by this PR — the task's stated base of 2944+1 differs from what was actually observed on this checkout by +4; reported as observed per instruction, not reconciled). `smoke-fresh-db`/`smoke-upgrade-db`: see PR body. (Relates to #3027)
- Fixed `delete_folder` sending a non-empty folder's notes and sheets to the OS trash, silently orphaning any note still pointed at the now-gone folder (#2874 item 65, `docs/spec/file-system.md` §2A.6, which this PR rewrites — it previously specified refusing to delete a non-empty folder, now wrong). **Matt's ruling, implemented exactly:** deleting a folder moves every note and sheet in it — including items already in Pane's own trash (`deleted_at IS NOT NULL`, so restoring one afterward still lands correctly) — into the project's default folder (`default_folder_id`, §1.7.1, found by ID, never by matching "General"), through the EXACT SAME `move_note_internal` path (`notes.rs`, now `pub(crate)`) every other note move in the app already uses — no parallel move implementation. Only the resulting EMPTY directory is removed from disk, non-recursively (`remove_dir`). **Filename-clash decision: rename-with-suffix, never refuse, never overwrite** — `relocate_note_file`'s new `unique_destination_file_name` probes the destination directory and appends " (2)", " (3)", ... before the extension until it finds a name nothing on disk is already using; the pre-existing file at the original name is never touched. Chosen over an outright refusal because ruling 1 is unconditional ("every note and sheet... moves") — a single unrelated same-named file in the default folder shouldn't be able to block an entire folder delete. **All-or-nothing (ruling 2):** every DB write (each note's move, the `ai_settings` collapse-state cleanup, the folder row delete) is now inside ONE SQL transaction in `delete_folder_internal`, committed only at the very end. The filesystem half (which a SQL transaction can't cover) is tracked by hand — each note's `(old_path, new_path)` is recorded the moment `move_note_internal` relocates it; on ANY later failure (another note's move, the cleanup, the folder delete, or `commit()` itself), every recorded rename is undone in reverse order by a direct rename straight back to the original path (deliberately bypassing the DB and `move_note_internal` for the undo itself — by the time it runs, the DB side already reads its original values again via the transaction's own automatic rollback, so a second `move_note_internal` call would see `current == target` and no-op, stranding the file). Proven with a REAL injected failure, not a simulated boundary: a second note's on-disk file is deleted out from under Pane before the delete call, so its own move hits a genuine `authorize_existing` I/O error mid-loop — the first note, already relocated by that point, is confirmed rolled all the way back (DB AND disk, exact original path and content) and the folder itself still exists. **`create_folder_internal` now refuses any parent that isn't a top-level project** ("Parent must be a top-level project — folders cannot nest") — folders never nest, closing a gap `move_folder_internal` already guarded but `create_folder_internal` did not. **The delete confirmation dialog now says where content goes**, e.g. "3 notes and 2 sheets will move to Overview" — a new `get_folder_delete_preview` command reads the live note/sheet counts and the default folder's REAL, current name (by ID, never hardcoded "General") fresh at display time; Sidebar.svelte's new `formatFolderDeleteMessage` (`src/lib/folderDeletePreviewMessage.ts`) builds the exact string. **§34 events (data-refresh.md), exact counts (ruling 7):** `delete_folder`'s command wrapper (via the new, testable `emit_delete_folder_events` helper) fires exactly one `moved` (`entity_type: "note"` or `"sheet"`, matching each item's real type) per note/sheet actually relocated, plus exactly one `deleted` (`entity_type: "folder"`) for the folder itself — using §34's existing constants, nothing new invented. The default folder's own undeletability (§1.7.1 ruling 4, pre-existing) is unchanged and re-confirmed with a new test against the updated `delete_folder_internal` return type. **`docs/spec/file-system.md` §2A.6 rewritten** to this ruling and marked **BUILT (v1.0.59, #2874 item 65)**, following §34.9's status convention — it previously specified the refuse-on-non-empty behavior this PR replaces. **9 new backend tests** (`notes.rs`: the clash-avoidance probe directly, and an integration test through `move_note_internal` proving both the pre-existing and the incoming file's content survive intact at two different paths; `projects.rs`'s new `folder_delete_moves_content_tests` module: the full move — notes, a sheet, and a trashed note — landing in the default folder on disk AND in the DB with content asserted (not just paths), restoring a trashed note after its folder was deleted lands it in the default folder via the real `restore_note` command, the filename-clash rename-not-overwrite proof, the real-injected-failure rollback proof, folders-never-nest, the default-folder-still-refused regression guard, and the exact §34 event-count proof driven through the real `emit_delete_folder_events` against a live `tauri::test::mock_app()` listener, not a source-text call-count proxy) **plus 7 new frontend tests** (`folderDeletePreviewMessage.test.ts` — the ruling's own example string verbatim, the real-name-not-"General" proof, singular/plural note and sheet phrasing, the zero-count empty-folder fallback). `cargo check` clean (2 pre-existing, unrelated warnings). `cargo test` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2415 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out (base 2406/0/3/11 — exactly +9 new tests, zero regressions). `pnpm vitest run`: 2944 passed, 1 skipped (base 2937+1 — exactly +7, zero regressions). `smoke-fresh-db`: PASS, 0 violations. `smoke-upgrade-db`: PASS, 2 allowlisted pre-existing violations (Memory.md backfill temp-file-creation failures for two fixture projects) — exactly the documented baseline, no change. **Amended post-merge-review (Reed's WARN closure, 2026-10-12 audit, Matt's sign-off "fix before merge"):** the above shipped with a disclosed, non-blocking WARN — `fs_policy.remove_dir_all` on the folder directory is unconditionally recursive; it never verified the directory was actually empty before deleting, so a file a user dropped into that on-disk folder via Finder (anything Pane never tracked with a `notes` row) was destroyed permanently alongside it, with no OS trash step. **Matt's ruling: "nothing Pane didn't move is ever permanently deleted."** Fixed in the same commit sequence, one more commit on this branch before merge: every entry still in the directory after the move loop is now handed to the OS trash via the existing `PaneFs::trash` path (`filesystem_policy.rs` — the same call `database::delete_note_file` already uses for a single note's trash; no parallel trash implementation added) — recoverable, never a raw `remove_file`/`remove_dir_all`. Only once the directory is confirmed actually empty is it removed, and only via a new, genuinely non-recursive `PaneFs::remove_dir` (`std::fs::remove_dir`, which itself refuses on a non-empty directory — it is structurally impossible for this call to take an untracked file down with it). Stays best-effort throughout: a failure trashing one leftover, or removing the directory afterward, is logged and leaves that leftover/directory in place — it never fails the overall delete and never rolls back the already-committed note moves (ordering: this cleanup step runs strictly after the DB transaction commits). **4 new tests** (3 in `projects.rs`'s `folder_delete_moves_content_tests`, 1 in `filesystem_policy.rs`): an untracked leftover file is moved to the OS trash rather than destroyed (drives the real, unmocked `trash()` call end-to-end — not pre-removed to dodge it — alongside a tracked note that still moves correctly); a folder with nothing left behind has its empty directory removed non-recursively; and, proven deterministically without depending on the real OS Trash's own success/failure (a symlink leftover, which `PaneFs::authorize_existing` rejects outright before ever reaching the real `trash::delete` call) — confirmed FAILING against the pre-fix code first (the symlink and the whole directory were both destroyed by the unconditional `remove_dir_all`), then passing after the fix (the symlink and the directory are both left in place, logged, the already-moved tracked note unaffected). One sub-claim — "landed in the OS Trash with byte-identical content" — is deliberately NOT asserted by any committed test: the `trash` crate's `os_limited` listing/read API is `#[cfg]`-excluded on macOS entirely (Windows/Freedesktop-Trash only), direct `~/.Trash` filesystem access is denied in the verification sandbox even from a plain compiled binary, and Finder/AppleScript automation — while confirmed capable of it manually during development — hung indefinitely on a necessary "purge the one-off test file from Trash" follow-up call in that same sandbox, so it was not embedded in the suite. `cargo check` clean (same 2 pre-existing, unrelated warnings). `cargo test` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2419 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out (prior 2415/0/3/11 — exactly +4 new tests, zero regressions). `pnpm vitest run`: 2944 passed, 1 skipped — unchanged (no frontend files touched by this fix). `smoke-fresh-db`: PASS, 0 violations. `smoke-upgrade-db`: PASS, 2 allowlisted pre-existing violations — unchanged baseline. (Relates to #2874)
- internal: #2972 stage 4 (tracked on #2874, `docs/spec/data-refresh.md` §34) — the final stage: full cross-screen inventory, the remaining listener gaps it found, verification repros, dead-file deletion, §34 → **BUILT**. **Inventory (§34.12, now thirteen screens, not nine):** swept every `.svelte` file under `src/lib/components/`/`src/routes/` for actual reachability (not just an import), beyond the six Matt named (`ProjectsView`, `TaskList`, `Trash`, `Search results`, `Home/Dashboard`, `TaskFullPage`). Found: `TaskList.svelte`'s `task_list` canvas view and `CanvasRenderer`'s inline `search_results`/`dashboard` views are **unreachable** — zero `navigateTo({view: ...})` call anywhere in `src/` ever targets any of the three (the one call site that could have, `ChatSidebar.svelte`'s `handleCanvasCommand`, is itself dead — never called); `TaskFullPage.svelte` is imported by `CanvasRenderer.svelte` but never instantiated there, and its only real `<TaskFullPage>` usage was inside the now-deleted `ProjectAggregateView.old.svelte` — effectively dead too, flagged for a follow-up deletion decision, not acted on here (not on Matt's explicit deletion list). **Four genuinely live, unmigrated screens closed:** `ProjectsView.svelte` gains a `note`/`sheet`/`folder` listener patching ONLY `getProjectNoteCounts()` (never a full `listProjects()`/`listCategories()` refetch) — #3018/#3019 gave this view `category`+`project` only and explicitly flagged the rest as "a future issue," with none opened; this stage is that issue, no separate tracking issue, per Matt's ruling. `Trash.svelte` gains a `note`/`deleted` listener (`loadTrash()` re-read — no per-item trash read exists, same "tiny, deliberate" full-list-reread shape Sidebar/ProjectsView already use for `category`). `Settings.svelte`'s Categories tab and `ProjectSettings.svelte`'s Category dropdown each gain a `category` listener re-reading just the category list/dropdown — `ProjectSettings` deliberately does NOT patch its own `category`/`projectName`/`projectBrief` form fields from an incoming event, since silently overwriting mid-edit dirty-form state would clobber unsaved input, a worse regression than the staleness bug being fixed. **Verification:** item 46's repro (agent creates/edits a sheet → board updates without navigating away) and item 50b's repro (agent-created sheet's folder appears in the sidebar without a restart) both pass as-is against current code — named, permanent regression guards added honestly as such, not presented as new fixes, since Stages 1-3 already closed both gaps. **Reed's full-loop gap closed:** a new backend test runs five different mutating tool calls (`create_folder` → `create_sheet` into it → `set_sheet_cells` on it → `create_note` → `edit_note` on it) in one simulated turn and asserts all five `pane-data-changed` events fire, in order, each carrying the entity_id belonging to its OWN call — proving the existing per-call-independent emit design doesn't cross-contaminate ids across a multi-tool turn (passes as-is; new coverage, not a fix). **Reed's two remaining test gaps closed:** a mirror-parity test reads BOTH `refresh_event.rs` and `refreshEvent.ts` via `fs.readFileSync`, extracts every `ENTITY_*`/`REASON_*`/`EVENT_DATA_CHANGED` constant via regex from each, and asserts the two sets match — verified to actually catch a drift (temporarily mismatched `ENTITY_CATEGORY`'s value in one file, confirmed the test fails, reverted) rather than restating either file's contents as a hardcoded expectation; category names with embedded quotes, an emoji (multi-byte UTF-16 surrogate pair), forward slashes, backslash+mixed-quotes, a 500-char string, and embedded newline/tab are proven to survive both the app `CustomEvent` channel and a real backend `app.emit()`+`Listener::listen()` round-trip unmangled and un-truncated. **Dead files deleted, each confirmed zero-importer first (grep proof in the PR body):** `FolderView.svelte.before_patch`, `TaskFullPageDesign5.svelte` (Matt's list), `dashboard/TasksModule.svelte` (explicitly checked — zero `<TasksModule`/import hits; the file's only two references anywhere are an unrelated `hasTasksModule` variable in `api.ts` and a "Future:" comment in `HomeDashboard.svelte`), plus `AllTasksView.old.svelte`/`ProjectAggregateView.old.svelte`/`TaskFullPage.original.svelte` — near-identically-named `.svelte`-suffixed files to three items Matt's list said were absent at base (`AllTasksView.old`/`ProjectAggregateView.old`/`TaskFullPage.original`, no `.svelte` suffix — correctly absent as those exact literal filenames, re-confirmed), re-confirmed dead by the same zero-importer standard before deletion. **Spec wording fixes:** §34.6's `NoteList.svelte`/`pane-refresh-notes` deletion bullets, written as a pending imperative, corrected to past tense (both were actually deleted in Stage 2, #3015 — re-verified zero references anywhere in `src/`); - internal: Fixed two bugs in the spec-first CI gate (`.github/workflows/spec-first.yml`) that had bitten three PRs (#2967, #3002, #3014). **Bug 1:** `spec-covered-by:` was only read inside the `spec-skip:` branch, so a code-only PR correctly citing a merged spec PR failed unless it ALSO carried a dummy `spec-skip:` line, even though the gate's own error message said `spec-covered-by:` alone is enough — now read independently of `spec-skip:`. **Bug 2:** the top-level docs check matched ANY `docs/` change (`^docs/`), so a PR touching core behavioral files plus, say, a `docs/audits/` file passed with no spec update at all — core behavioral files now specifically require a `docs/spec/` change (or a verified `spec-covered-by:`); `spec-skip:` alone still never passes for them (the #604/#605 incident protection is unchanged). Non-core `src/`/`src-tauri/src/` changes keep the original relaxed rule (any `docs/`, or `spec-skip:`, or a verified `spec-covered-by:`). The decision logic moved out of the workflow into `scripts/check-spec-first.sh` (changed-file list via stdin, PR body via env `PR_BODY`) so it's unit-testable; `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` calls are the test seam, satisfied by a fake `gh` shim prepended to `PATH` in the test suite, `scripts/tests/check-spec-first/run-tests.sh`. **Follow-up fix (Reed audit of #3015):** the workflow's own `PR_BODY="$PR_BODY_ENV"` reassignment was missing `export`, so once the decision logic moved into the `scripts/check-spec-first.sh` subprocess described above, `PR_BODY` was never actually inherited by it in real CI — Bug 1's fix did not work in production, failing closed for a new reason (no `spec-skip:`/`spec-covered-by:` ever read). Fixed by exporting it (`export PR_BODY="$PR_BODY_ENV"`); no other variable the script consumes has the same gap (`CHANGED` is piped via stdin, not env). `run-tests.sh` grew 3 cases (12 total, all passing; `shellcheck`-clean) that extract the actual `run:` block out of the live workflow YAML and execute it exactly as GitHub Actions does (`bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`, env wiped except `PATH`/`PR_BODY_ENV`/`GH_TOKEN`) — this is what the original 9-case suite didn't exercise, since it exported `PR_BODY` per-invocation rather than through the workflow's own assignment. The CHANGELOG check and `changelog-skip:` handling are untouched. CI-only change — no `src/`, `src-tauri/`, or `docs/spec/` files touched.
- Fixed category changes in Settings (add, rename, recolor, delete) not refreshing the sidebar — rename/delete had regressed in #2972 Stage 2/3 (`renameCategory`/`deleteCategory` kept their old bare, payload-less `pane-data-changed` dispatch, which Stage 3's `subscribeDataChanged()` silently no-ops on since it has no `detail`); recolor never refreshed anything at any stage (`setCategoryColor`'s color-only-update path dispatched nothing at all) (#3018, relates to #2972/#2874, `docs/spec/data-refresh.md` §34). **`category` is a fifth `entity_type`** (Matt's ruling): `entity_id` is the category name; the same four `reason` values apply unchanged — add = `created`, rename/recolor = `edited`, delete = `deleted`, no fifth reason. Both mirrors (`src-tauri/src/refresh_event.rs`, `src/lib/refreshEvent.ts`) gain the `ENTITY_CATEGORY` constant together, plus the `EntityType` union type on the frontend side. **`api.ts`'s three category functions migrated:** `setCategoryColor()` (`:1542`) now takes an optional `reason` (defaulting to `"edited"`) so it can back both Settings.svelte's add flow (`reason: "created"`) and its color-only-update flow (`reason: "edited"`, the default) with one function, and dispatches the `category` event itself. **Bulk project updates return their IDs (Matt's ruling 2):** `rename_category` (`projects.rs:1145`) and `delete_category` (`projects.rs:1199`) both already changed `projects.category` in bulk across every affected project — each now returns those projects' IDs from the **same transaction** that changed them (read before the UPDATE/clear, inside one `BEGIN`/COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`; `delete_category` previously ran as two bare sequential `execute()` calls with no transaction wrapping at all — now atomic too). `renameCategory()`/`deleteCategory()` (`api.ts`) dispatch one `category` event (`"edited"`/`"deleted"`) plus **one `project`/`"edited"` event per returned ID — zero if none affected, not skipped** — so every screen that groups/colors projects by category regroups without a restart. **Listeners re-read the whole category list on a category event** (§34.5: "tiny, no per-item read, deliberate, unlike the single-entity reads elsewhere"): `Sidebar.svelte` gains a `entity_type === "category"` branch in its existing `handleDataChangedEvent`. **`ProjectsView.svelte` finding:** this view shows categories (a `.category-indicator` dot per project, colored via `project.category` looked up against the `categories` list) but had **zero** `pane-data-changed` listener of any kind before this fix — not migrated by any of #2972's three prior stages, for any entity type. Gains a listener scoped to what this issue needs: `category` events re-read the category list, `project` events patch the one affected project via a single-entity read (`api.getProjectOrFolder`) — not the broader note/sheet/folder migration every other screen already has, which remains a gap, out of this issue's scope. **Spec (`docs/spec/data-refresh.md`):** §34.1's payload schema and entity_type bullet list gain `category` as the fifth; §34.1.2's `setProjectCategory`/`renameCategory`/`deleteCategory` bullet is split and corrected (it previously described Stage 3's intended-but-unimplemented plan, not what Stage 3's code actually shipped); §34.2 gains rows for the three category senders plus the new Sidebar/ProjectsView category listener rows; status line → `IN PROGRESS — 3 of 4 stages (#3017)` (sprint work, not a stage — credits #3017 as the last completed stage). **Tests — 17 new** (5 Rust: `refresh_event.rs` gains 1 for the `ENTITY_CATEGORY` constant; `projects.rs` gains 4 proving `rename_category`/`delete_category` return exactly the affected project IDs, each with its own explicit zero-affected case. 12 TypeScript: `refreshEvent.test.ts` gains 1 new "identical shape" case for `category`; `api.categoryRefresh.test.ts` (6) proves exact event counts per reason — add/recolor/rename/delete, each with an explicit zero-affected-projects case asserted via `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(0)`, not skipped; `Sidebar.categoryRefresh.test.ts` (3) and `ProjectsView.categoryRefresh.test.ts` (2) prove the new listener branches), each confirmed failing against pre-fix code first (exact before/after call counts documented in each file's own docstring). `cargo check` clean (pre-existing `unused import: Manager` warning in `notes.rs`, plus a new `unused` warning on `ENTITY_CATEGORY` itself — expected, since no Rust command emits a `category` event; category mutations are app-side only, same as `setProjectCategory`). `cargo test` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2403 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out (base 2397 passed/1 failed(known flake)/3 ignored/11 filtered + 5 new Rust tests, and the known flake — `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert` — happened to pass this run, since it's flaky, not deterministic). `pnpm vitest run`: 2900 passed, 1 skipped (base 2888 passed/1 skipped + 12 new — exact, zero regressions). `smoke-fresh-db` and `smoke-upgrade-db` (run locally): both PASS — ready signal detected in both modes; upgrade mode's 2 flagged lines are the same pre-existing allowlisted `[CRITICAL] Memory.md backfill failed` entries prior stages found, unchanged by this PR. (Relates to #3018, spec-covered-by: #3012)

Replaces Stage 2's backend-only `listen(EVENT_DATA_CHANGED, ...)` registration in all seven of its sites (`KanbanBoard.svelte`, `AllTasksView.svelte`, `NotesBrowser.svelte`, `Sidebar.svelte`, `CalendarView.svelte`, `SheetGrid.svelte`, `Editor.svelte` — the last of which also had its own Stage-2-era hand-rolled DOM listener, `handleDataChangedDom`, removed as the literal double-registration this item targets) plus the new `+page.svelte` bridge and `syncStore.ts`. **One shared app-sender helper — `dispatchDataChanged()`:** the one place every app-initiated mutation above builds its payload from, mirroring the backend's `emit_data_changed` (`refresh_event.rs`) field-for-field. **One event per change (item 5) — two duplicates deleted, not converted:** `api.ts`'s `createFolder()` keeps its existing zero-dispatch behavior permanently (the backend `create_folder` command already emits unconditionally since Stage 1 — an app-side dispatch here would be a second event for one mutation); a "first reader consumes it" design would give the second reader a false negative). `Editor.svelte`'s `updateEditorMeta()`/`saveContent()`/`saveSheetTitle()` all register a tag before their save starts and pass it through to the migrated `api.ts` senders; No sibling screen (Kanban/NotesBrowser/AllTasksView/Sidebar/CalendarView/SheetGrid) checks `origin_tag` at all — per §34.4's rule, only the listener that IS the save's own origin may suppress; every other listener always updates regardless of whose tag it carries. **Tests — 30 new, each shown failing against the pre-fix code first (full method documented per-test in each file's own docstring/comments):** `refreshEvent.test.ts` (8 — origin-tag mechanics, `subscribeDataChanged`'s both-channel delivery, and the "identical shape, both senders" cross-channel structural-equality assertion); - internal: Spec-only PR for #2972 (tracked on #2874) — Matt's rulings on the single data-change refresh point written into a new `docs/spec/data-refresh.md` (§34, registered in `docs/spec/README.md`'s file table and §34 stub), ahead of the implementation PR. **The event:** one `pane-data-changed` carrying `entity_id`/`entity_type`/`reason` (`created`/`edited`/`moved`/`deleted`) for every note/sheet/folder/project change, replacing `pane-note-created`, `pane-note-changed`, `pane-project-changed`, and `pane-task-meta-changed` outright; `pane-reload-editor` is the only other surviving event name. **Two senders, one shape** (backend Tauri `emit()` for agent/background changes, app DOM `CustomEvent` for the frontend's own successful `invoke()` calls). **Origin-tag echo suppression**, scoped to the save call rather than the entity, so a note's own editor skips its own save's echo but still refreshes on an independent edit to the same note (both halves required in one test, per the spec's own acceptance criteria). **Every screen patches/inserts/removes in place, never reloads** — enumerated across all nine verification screens (Kanban board, Editor note/sheet, Sheet grid, Sidebar, Calendar, All-tasks view, Notes browser, Chat/AI sidebar), with the 7-named-in-the-ruling-vs-9-verified discrepancy explicitly accounted for (Editor splits into note/sheet variants; Chat sidebar added as a sender-only verification row). **`mutating_tools` allowlist (`ai/commands.rs:15039`, 15 entries, re-verified at this PR's base) is specified for deletion**, replaced by the tool loop's single unconditional, entity-identified emit — including its own source-scanning test (`test_mutating_tools_contains_all_six_sheet_tools`, `ai/commands.rs:6733`), which is specified for deletion rather than update, since the binding it scans for ceases to exist. **Dead code specified for deletion, confirmed dead first:** `NoteList.svelte` (imported by `CanvasRenderer.svelte:19`, never instantiated anywhere — confirmed via `<NoteList` grep) and `pane-refresh-notes` (zero senders anywhere in `src/`, only `NoteList.svelte`'s own listener). **Stale scope-doc references corrected** (the background scope doc, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/research/2026-09-24-scope-refresh-point.md`, dates from v1.0.57/#3011's merge-base and two things changed under it): `resolve_folder_id_or_create`'s silent auto-create-on-miss path no longer exists at all — #2874 item 50b (#3011) replaced it with refusal-on-miss `resolve_folder_branch_a`/`resolve_folder_branch_b`; and the sheet-tool list grew from five/six to eight (seven mutating + `get_sheet_data` read-only) with #2970's `add_sheet_rows`/`add_sheet_columns` batch tools, re-enumerated directly from `tools.rs`/`commands.rs` rather than trusting the stale doc. Event-usage counts in the spec's migration table (`pane-data-changed` 16, `pane-note-created` 9, `pane-note-changed` 6, `pane-project-changed` 4, `pane-task-meta-changed` 4, `pane-reload-editor` 5, `pane-refresh-notes` 1 — files referencing, across `src/` + `src-tauri/src/`) were re-verified directly against this PR's base and match exactly. `sheets.md` §33.11 and `toolbar.md:143` cross-references both verified to resolve at this PR's base; §33.11's six-sheet-tools sentence is flagged as stale (now eight) for the implementation PR to fix alongside its own pending items 35/40 status line, not changed here. **Stage plan (ruling 10):** (1) backend emit, (2) all nine screens' listeners in one PR — honoring Matt's standing "no separate point fixes" ruling — (3) senders + echo suppression, (4) verification. Tests carried forward unchanged in substance from the scope doc's §7, mapped onto each stage as acceptance criteria. Docs-only; no `src-tauri/` or `src/` files touched. (Relates to #2874)
- Implemented #2874 item 50b's agent folder-resolution contract for `create_note`/`create_sheet` (ai-integration.md §4.1, spec-covered-by: #3003, #3004) — the old auto-create-on-miss folder resolver (which silently created a brand-new folder from any unmatched `folder_id`/context name, with no project scoping on its ID branch at all) is retired outright and replaced by three explicit branches. **Branch A — explicit `folder_id`** (`resolve_folder_branch_a`, shared by `execute_create_note` and `execute_create_sheet`): an empty string behaves as omitted (ruling 7); a folder ID is scoped to the target project — an ID belonging to a different project is refused outright, never silently remapped (ruling 10, closing the old unscoped `SELECT id FROM projects WHERE id = ?1` gap); failing that, a case-insensitive name match against the project's visible (non-hidden, non-system, ruling 9) folders — one match uses it, two-or-more is refused listing the colliding IDs (ruling 8's "retry by ID" shape, reused), no match is refused listing the project's real folders (ruling 5). **Both refusal paths create nothing** — no folder, no note, no sheet. **Branch B — context-derived folder name** (`resolve_folder_branch_b`, `execute_create_note`'s `ctx.folderName` fallback only; `execute_create_sheet` takes no viewing context, so this branch is dormant for sheets): a miss OR an ambiguous (two-or-more) match both degrade gracefully to the project's default folder (ruling 6, deliberately reused — the user never typed the name, so there's no "retry by ID" to send them to), and the result reports `folder_fallback: "default_folder_used"`. **This is the asymmetry the spec is explicit about: an agent-chosen `folder_id` gets a hard refusal it can retry by ID; a context-derived name degrades and says so.** **Branch C — nothing given at all**: resolves `projects.default_folder_id` directly (§1.7.1), never a name lookup against `"General"`/`DEFAULT_FOLDER_NAME`. Tool results are plain text, not literal JSON for `create_note` — `folder_fallback` is surfaced as an explicit `[folder_fallback: default_folder_used]` suffix there; `create_sheet` already returns JSON and gains a real `folder_fallback` key when applicable (dormant today, since sheets have no context branch to miss on). **Also fixed, #2874 item 50b, ai-integration.md §4.1 `:164`:** `execute_create_folder`'s duplicate-name rejection (previously just propagating the sidebar's internal `DUPLICATE_FOLDER:{single_id}:...` shape verbatim to the agent) now uses a dedicated `check_folder_name_unique_for_agent`, which lists **every** colliding sibling by ID (not just one via the sidebar check's `LIMIT 1`), so the agent retries the surrounding operation by ID, never by trying another name. **Also fixed, #2874 item 50b, core-data-model.md §1.7.1:** `move_folder_internal` (`projects.rs`) gains a guard mirroring `delete_folder_internal`'s existing default-folder guard exactly (same error-message style) — moving a project's default folder is refused unconditionally, including a move that keeps it within its own project; §1.7.1 gains a new "Not movable either, not even within its own project" paragraph documenting it. **Spec statuses flipped to BUILT (v1.0.59):** `ai-integration.md:35`, `:43`, `:164`, `:280`, and the "Folder resolution for `create_note` and `create_sheet`" section at `:306` (all previously TARGET — NOT BUILT); `core-data-model.md` §1.7.2's "still TARGET" agent-facing-shape note. **No hardcoded folder name:** every default-folder reference goes through `projects.default_folder_id` or the existing `DEFAULT_FOLDER_NAME` constant (#2874 item 50a) — nothing retypes `"General"`. **17 new backend tests**, each demonstrated against the real migrated schema with a genuine `create_project_internal`-created project (so `default_folder_id` is always real, not a test-fixture gap): every Branch A step including a refused call creating nothing (note count asserted unchanged, not just that an error returned) — valid in-project ID, cross-project ID refused, case-insensitive name match, hidden-folder/system-folder not matchable by name but still reachable by ID, ambiguous name match refused listing both colliding IDs, no-match refused listing the project's real folders, empty-string `folder_id` treated as omitted; Branch B on a miss and on an ambiguous match, both returning `folder_fallback: default_folder_used` and landing in the real default folder, not refused; Branch C resolving the real default folder for both `create_note` and `create_sheet`, no fallback flag; the duplicate-name error naming both colliding IDs with folder count unchanged on refusal; moving the default folder refused both cross-project and within its own project, parent_id unchanged on refusal; and a repo-wide source scan (code, comments, AND tests, `.rs`/`.ts`/`.svelte`, excluding only the spec's own intentional retirement-notice prose) proving the old resolver has zero remaining references anywhere. One pre-existing test (`test_create_sheet_rejects_folder_under_system_project`) is updated to match the new, more-correct behavior its own scenario now triggers: a folder_id belonging to a different project than the one declared is refused by the new project-scoping check (ruling 10) before ever reaching the deeper system-folder guard it used to rely on. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2382 passed (2366 base + 16 new: 15 in `ai/commands.rs`'s `folder_resolution_2874_50b_tests` + 1 in `projects.rs`'s `default_folder_and_duplicate_name_tests`), 0 failed, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out. `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped (unaffected — backend-only change, no frontend files touched). `smoke-fresh-db` and `smoke-upgrade-db` (`.github/workflows/startup-smoke.yml`, run locally): both PASS — ready signal detected in both modes, 0 new severity violations (upgrade mode's 2 flagged lines are pre-existing allowlisted entries, unrelated to this change). (Relates to #2874, spec-covered-by: #3003, #3004)
- Added `projects.default_folder_id` — the default folder is now found by ID, never by matching the name "General" (#2874 item 50a, §1.7.1/§1.7.2, spec-covered-by: #3003, #3004) — **Ruling (Matt, 2026-09-24):** matching by name silently breaks the moment a user renames their default folder; a stable `parent_id`/`id` pointer never does. **Migration (v90→v91, `migrations.rs::migrate_v91`):** a plain, idempotent `ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN default_folder_id TEXT` — the same pattern as `migrate_attachments_v67`'s column add ("duplicate column name" = already-done), named as precedent in the PR; `crsql_begin_alter`/`crsql_commit_alter` are still unused anywhere in this codebase (the one historical attempt, #447–449, aborted the upgrade chain) and were not reached for here either. Backfill: every top-level project with at least one folder gets its OLDEST folder (`MIN(created_at)`, `id ASC` as a deterministic tie-break only) as its default; a project with zero folders gets a new `"General"` folder created and pointed at. **Found via the mandated `smoke-upgrade-db` run, not by inspection:** a bulk/row-level `UPDATE` against the already-CRR-enabled `projects` table tripped a cr-sqlite change-tracking-trigger argument-count mismatch after the `ALTER TABLE` (the trigger body is static SQL naming every column, generated once when `crsql_as_crr` first ran, and a plain `ADD COLUMN` doesn't regenerate it) — fixed by rebuilding the `projects` table (new-shape `CREATE TABLE` + copy + `DROP`/`RENAME` + re-`crsql_as_crr`), the same table-rebuild shape `migrate_v68` already uses for `attachments` in this file, gated so a re-run skips the rebuild once the trigger already mentions the new column. **Fix (#3006, Reed audit):** that rebuild shipped WITHOUT the `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` wrap `migrate_attachments_v68`'s own rebuild uses (`migrations.rs:4975`/`:5033`) — a crash between the new table being created+populated and the `DROP`/`RENAME` swap completing would auto-commit the `DROP` of the original `projects` table while the rename never lands, leaving the database with no `projects` table at all. No outer transaction is held around migration arms (`database.rs::init_database` calls `run_migrations` directly on a freshly opened connection), so nesting `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` here — matching v68's plain-transaction (not savepoint) shape exactly — is safe and makes the whole rebuild all-or-nothing: on a failure before `COMMIT`, SQLite's implicit rollback on connection close restores the original table exactly as it was. **New projects get a default immediately:** `projects.rs` (`create_project_internal`, lines ~80/98), `import.rs` (lines ~396/404), `watcher.rs` (lines ~422/429) all set `default_folder_id` right after creating a project's first folder. **The five by-name lookups replaced with by-ID (`SELECT default_folder_id FROM projects WHERE id = ?1`):** `notes.rs:155` (`create_note_internal`), `notes.rs:401` (`create_sheet_note_internal`), `notes.rs:3188` (`move_note_internal`), `watcher.rs:457`, `import.rs:416`. **The watcher no longer creates a "General" folder** for the no-folder-segment case — it resolves the project's `default_folder_id` instead, erroring out (not silently falling back) if a project somehow lacks one. **Delete guard (`projects.rs::delete_folder_internal`):** a new check mirroring the existing `is_system` guard's exact shape — reads the parent project's `default_folder_id` and refuses with `"Cannot delete the default folder"` if the target folder is it; renaming the default folder is still unrestricted. **One shared duplicate-name check, `projects.rs::check_folder_name_unique`** (case-insensitive, scoped to siblings under `parent_id`, `exclude_id` sentinel `""` for a create vs. the folder's own id for a rename/move), called from every create/rename/move path (§1.7.2): sidebar `create_folder` and `update_folder`, the shared `move_folder_internal` primitive (covers both the agent's `execute_move_folder` and the Tauri `move_folder` command), agent `execute_create_folder`, and import's/the watcher's folder-creation branches. Enforced going forward only — pre-existing duplicates are left as-is; the agent-facing "name both colliding folders by ID, retry by ID" error shape is #2874 item 50b, out of scope here. **No hardcoded "General":** a new `projects::DEFAULT_FOLDER_NAME` constant is the single source for the seed-time default name across all six creation/migration sites. **`docs/spec/core-data-model.md` §1.7.1 and §1.7.2 flipped to BUILT (v1.0.59).** **Tests:** 14 new backend tests. Migration (`migrations.rs`, 7): an untouched "General" folder; a renamed default folder (still picked, by age not name); a renamed default PLUS a newer stray "General" (the OLDER folder wins — the case that catches a naive find-by-name upgrade, with a sanity assertion proving the naive lookup WOULD pick the wrong one); a folderless project (gets a created "General"); unrelated rows left untouched (a folder's own `default_folder_id` stays NULL; an already-backfilled project isn't re-decided); re-running the upgrade (no duplicate "General", unchanged pointers); **and (#3006) the rebuild's own atomicity** — `test_migrate_v91_rebuild_rolls_back_cleanly_on_mid_rebuild_failure` stubs `crsql_as_crr` via `create_scalar_function` and pre-creates a dummy stale `projects__crsql_utrig` trigger so the real rebuild branch actually runs (none of the other six tests flip `crr_available` on — they're all in-memory, no cr-sqlite loaded), then uses SQLite's `authorizer` hook to deny specifically the `ALTER TABLE projects_v91_rebuild RENAME TO projects` step — after the new table is already created+populated AND the original is already dropped, the worst-case spot — and, on a real file-backed connection, closes and reopens it to simulate a crash. Confirmed failing against the pre-fix (no `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`) code first: the `projects` table is gone entirely after reopening (`BUG (crash-window data loss): projects table is GONE after a crash between DROP and RENAME`); after the fix, `projects` survives fully intact — same schema, same rows byte-for-byte, same CRR trigger — and the orphaned `projects_v91_rebuild` table left behind by the unfixed run is gone too (rolled back, not merely untouched). Delete/duplicate (`projects.rs`, 4, via `tauri::test::mock_app` + `app.manage(DbState)` on the real `#[tauri::command]` entry points, the same pattern `agents.rs`'s `upsert_agent_explicit_runtime_type_tests` established): deleting the default folder is refused with the exact message, row still exists; `create_folder` refuses a case-insensitive duplicate; `update_folder` refuses renaming into an existing sibling's name; `move_folder_internal` refuses moving into a project whose destination already has that name. Landing-after-rename (`notes.rs`, 3, full real schema via `run_migrations`): a new note, a new sheet, and a moved note all land in a project's RENAMED default folder, resolved by ID. **Also fixed, as regressions this change surfaced in the existing suite:** 6 `migration_tests.rs`/`migrations.rs` chain tests whose minimal fixtures predate `projects`/`parent_id`/`created_at` (migrate_v91 now guards both, matching the existing "older fixture schema" skip precedent used elsewhere in this file); `test_version_pair_coverage` (bumped to 91); a real-fixture test (`ai/commands.rs`) that opened a v85 fixture without loading the cr-sqlite extension — harmless before this PR since no prior migration ever wrote data into the already-CRR'd `projects` table, now fixed to load the extension like every real migration run does; one renamed sheet-folder test and 8 project-creation tests whose hand-rolled minimal `projects` table definitions were missing the new column; one existing test (`test_delete_folder_cleans_up_ai_settings_collapse_rows`) that deleted a project's auto-created (now default) folder — restructured to delete the sibling folder instead, since deleting the default is now correctly refused. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2362 passed, 1 failed (the known flake, `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert` — unrelated, see #2962), 3 ignored, 11 filtered out (2349 base + 14 new = 2363 ran, matching 2362 passed + 1 flake-failed). `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped (unaffected — backend-only change). `smoke-fresh-db` and `smoke-upgrade-db` (`.github/workflows/startup-smoke.yml`, the latter run locally against a new `tests/fixtures/upgrade-from-v90.db` fixture with a built builder script, `tests/build_v90_fixture.rs`, re-run for #3006 since the rebuild itself changed): both PASS — migration applies (rebuild included, confirmed in the upgrade-mode smoke log), backfill runs correctly for both a has-folder and a folderless seed project, ready signal detected, 0 severity violations. **A schema change ships nothing until Matt tests on the Mac Studio** — this is a local/CI verification, not a production confirmation. (Relates to #2874, #3006, spec-covered-by: #3003, #3004)
- internal: Corrected four spec errors in the #2874 items 50a/50b spec-only docs PR (#3003), which merged without its own fix commit (Relates to #2874). **core-data-model.md §1.7.2:** the sidebar's folder-rename check call site was misnamed as "the folder-rename path inside `update_project`" — it's `update_folder` (`projects.rs:654`); `update_project`'s own disk-rename branch is gated to top-level projects (`parent_id.is_none()`) and never runs for folders. **core-data-model.md §1.7.1/§1.7.2:** heading depth corrected from `###` to `####`, matching every other `X.Y.Z` subsection in the file. **core-data-model.md §1.7.2:** the one shared duplicate-name check now also covers `move_folder_internal` (`projects.rs:448`) and `execute_move_folder` (`ai/commands.rs:10345`) — reparenting a folder could create a same-named sibling the create/rename check never saw; still one backend check, just more call sites. (Today there's no live folder-move UI — `moveProject`, `api.ts:829`, is an inert v9 stub, and `src/` has zero `move_folder`/`moveFolder` references — so this closes the agent's gap, not the sidebar's.) **ai-integration.md §4.1:** added the ambiguous-lookup case Matt's ruling actually covered — the agent's folder name matching two or more existing folders — distinct from the create-collision text (left untouched). Branch A (explicit `folder_id` resolved as a name) refuses and lists the matches by ID for a by-ID retry. Branch B (context-derived folder name) treats an ambiguous match like a miss, reusing ruling 6's default-folder fallback. Docs-only; no `src-tauri/` or `src/` files touched.
- internal: Spec-only PR for #2874 items 50a (default folder) and 50b (agent folder-choice refusal) — Matt's ten rulings written into `docs/spec/core-data-model.md`, `docs/spec/sheets.md`, and `docs/spec/ai-integration.md`, ahead of the implementation PR. No `src-tauri/` or `src/` files touched. **core-data-model.md** gains new §1.7.1 "Default Folder (`default_folder_id`)" (TARGET — NOT BUILT) — a new `projects.default_folder_id` column, resolved by ID and never by matching the name `'General'` (ruling 1); the five current by-name call sites this supersedes, re-verified at `main` (`notes.rs:155`, `notes.rs:401`, `notes.rs:3188`, `watcher.rs:457`, `import.rs:416` — ruling 2, all identical to the stale 1.0.57-era scope docs' citations except line numbers, which had drifted and are corrected here); the `v90 → v91` upgrade backfill — oldest folder wins, a folderless project gets one created, no review log or tie-handling (ruling 3); the default folder is renamable but not deletable, mirroring the existing `is_system` delete guard (ruling 4); and the viewing-folder-missing fallback to the default folder with the tool result saying so (ruling 6). New §1.7.2 "Folder Name Uniqueness" (TARGET — NOT BUILT) specifies the one shared backend check (sibling-name collision, case-insensitive) covering every folder create/rename path — sidebar, agent, import, and watcher — none of which enforce this today (ruling 8's data-layer half); CRR tables can't carry a `UNIQUE` index (#493), so this is app-code-enforced, same as the table's existing name/parent_id note. **sheets.md** §33.2.1 updated to point `create_sheet`'s folder-omitted fallback at `default_folder_id` instead of a `'General'` name lookup, and to note the empty-string/omitted equivalence (ruling 7). **ai-integration.md** §4.1 gains a new `list_folders` tool entry (BUILT, previously undocumented despite being implemented and already listed in the §4.1 tool-count banner) documenting its existing hidden/system-folder exclusion; a new "Folder resolution for `create_note` and `create_sheet`" contract (TARGET — NOT BUILT) covering empty-string-as-omitted (ruling 7), hidden/system folders being unmatchable by name (ruling 9), a folder ID from another project being refused outright — closing a real gap in today's unscoped `resolve_folder_id` UUID branch (ruling 10), and the refuse-and-list-folders behavior replacing auto-creation (ruling 5) — `resolve_folder_id_or_create` (`ai/commands.rs:2290`) is specified as retired, with all three of its call sites (`:2364`, `:2372`, `:4055`) named; plus the agent-facing half of the duplicate-name collision contract (error names both colliding folders, retry by ID — ruling 8's agent-facing half) and a short pointer added to the existing `create_folder` tool entry. **Scope-doc note:** the background scope docs referenced for this build (`~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-09-24-scope-50a-default-folder.md`, `...-50b-refusal.md`) were not found on disk at that path or any fallback location searched — every ruling and line-number citation in this entry and the spec sections themselves was instead verified directly against this PR's own base commit (`2a34a988a303538bdd2d546cced24feaaccf201c`, confirmed == `origin/main`). Spec ahead of code; the implementation PR (migration, backend checks, tool contract changes) follows separately. (Relates to #2874)
- internal: Added ADR-0067 ("Explicit Agent Selection on the OC Wire") and nine amendments to `docs/spec/ai-integration.md`, `docs/spec/sessions.md`, and `docs/spec/sync.md` specifying how Pane and pane-gateway select and identify an OpenClaw agent over the wire — `openclaw/<agentId>` model-prefix selection, `ai_agents.runtime_ref` as the only identifier that crosses the wire, gateway pass-through for already agent-scoped models, gateway-4xx-as-provider-error classification, and a single stated default-agent-resolution order. Docs-only, ahead of the implementation PR — no code changed. (Relates to #2900)
- Added a `delete_sheet_column` agent tool and an optional `columns` parameter on the `create_sheet` agent tool (#2874 items 35, 40) — the AI agent can now delete a sheet column (and all its cells) in one call via `delete_sheet_column(note_id, column_id)`, with a cross-sheet leakage guard rejecting a `column_id` that doesn't belong to the given `note_id`; and can create a sheet with a caller-specified list of typed columns (`columns: [{ name, type, options? }]`) instead of always getting the 5 default "Column 1"–"Column 5" text columns. `create_sheet` with no `columns` param, or an explicit empty `columns: []`, is unchanged and still seeds the 5 defaults. Both tools are taint-withheld after web content is fetched and are project-scoped (cross-project write rejected), matching `add_sheet_column`/`set_sheet_cells`. Backend: `sheets::create_sheet_internal` gains a third `columns: Option<Vec<ColumnSpec>>` parameter (all 7 existing call sites — the Tauri `create_sheet` command, 4 sheets.rs tests, the `sheets_snapshots.rs` test helper, and the agent's own no-columns-param path — pass `None`, preserving today's behavior exactly); a new `sheets::seed_columns_from_spec` seeds the spec'd columns inside the existing creation transaction. Total agent tool count is now 31 (6 sheet tools, up from 5). (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: spec line already merged in prior docs PR)
- Added support for single-row ranges in formulas (e.g. `=SUM(A1:C1)`) (#2874 item 37) — previously only single-column ranges (`A1:A5`) were accepted; a row range now translates and evaluates the same way. Storage form for ALL ID-form ranges (column and row) is now two complete `{col_id:row_id}` cell refs joined by a colon (`{col1:row1}:{col2:row2}`), replacing the old single-column-only `{col:row1:row2}` shape (which remains readable for backward compat but is never written again). A genuinely mixed-shape range (different column AND different row, e.g. `A1:C3`) is still rejected inline, same as before. Inserting a column between a row range's endpoints extends the range automatically — this comes for free from the existing sort-order-based membership model, no new bookkeeping needed. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: spec line already merged in prior docs PR)
- Added `add_sheet_rows` and `add_sheet_columns` agent tools (#2970, spec-covered-by: #2980) — batch-append many rows/columns to a sheet in one call instead of one tool call per row/column. **`add_sheet_rows`** extends the existing ghost-row-commit batch backend, `create_sheet_rows_batch_internal` (`sheets.rs`), to accept a per-row optional `values: {column_id: value}` map instead of always creating blank rows; each value is written with `upsert_sheet_cell_no_recompute` (#2874 item 51's raw per-cell write primitive — A1 translation and formula validation still run per cell), then **ONE `recompute_and_regen` runs at the end, only if any value was written.** This deliberately differs from item 51's own style-batch call pattern, which calls `recompute::recompute_sheet` alone because style edits never touch the note body — `add_sheet_rows` writes VALUES, which do change the body, so it needs the regen half too; a values-less batch (today's ghost-row-commit shape) safely skips the call entirely, since a sparse row produces no body line and nothing to recompute. **`add_sheet_columns`** extends the column-side sibling, `create_sheet_columns_batch_internal`, to accept a `name`/`col_type`/`options` triple per column (same per-entry shape as `add_sheet_column`) instead of the previous hardcoded blank-text default; columns carry no cell values, so its one recalculation runs unconditionally, same as before. Both are **all-or-nothing**: every entry is validated (columns) or write-attempted (row values) inside the one open transaction, and any failure rolls back the whole call — the error names the failing row's index and column, or the failing column's index and reason. **Caps, checked before the transaction opens:** 500 rows, 100 columns; an over-cap call creates nothing and the error names the cap and the requested count. `position: 'end'|'start'` on `add_sheet_rows` lands the whole batch as one contiguous block (computed inline via the batch's own sort_order math, not a separate post-insert re-sort step), never interleaved with existing rows. Registered in the tool registry (`tools.rs`, 31 → 33 tools), dispatch (`ai/commands.rs::execute_single_tool`), and both `MUTATE_EXISTING_TOOLS`/`project_scoped_tools` permission lists (15 → 17 each, same taint/project-scoping posture as the existing four sheet tools). **Also added the four PRE-EXISTING sheet tools (`set_sheet_cells`, `add_sheet_row`, `add_sheet_column`, `delete_sheet_column`) to `mutating_tools`**, the allowlist that fires the `pane-note-changed` refresh event after a tool-call iteration — confirmed via `git log -S` that these were omitted since #2339, never deliberately excluded, found while auditing the same list for the two new tools. **This is a stopgap, not a live-refresh fix:** the emit already fires once per iteration regardless of row/column count (satisfying "one refresh event per call"), but `SheetGrid.svelte` has no listener for this event at all, so an open sheet still won't visually update until the refresh-point work (#2972) lands a real per-sheet refresh path. Flipped both `add_sheet_rows`/`add_sheet_columns` entries in `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.1 from PROPOSED to BUILT and bumped the §4.1 tool-count banner from 30 to 33. Tests: 20 new backend tests across `sheets.rs` and `ai/commands.rs` — one recalculation per call for a values-written batch vs. zero for a values-less batch (using item 51's production `RECOMPUTE_CALL_COUNT` counter in `formula/recompute.rs`); rollback on a bad value mid-fill, verified with a direct DB check that zero rows/cells were written, not merely that an error returned; exactly-at-cap succeeds and one-over-cap fails with zero rows/columns created, for both tools; cross-project rejection; web-taint refusal; a markdown note as target rejected; dispatch routing; and `mutating_tools` membership for all six sheet tools (source-scanned, since it's a local `let` binding, not a module-level const). `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, #2962): 2223 passed, 1 failed (the known flake, `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert` — unrelated, see #2962), 3 ignored. `pnpm vitest run`: 2839 passed, 1 skipped (unaffected — backend-only change, no frontend files touched). (Relates to #2970, spec-covered-by: #2980)

### Changed
- Replaced the `add_sheet_rows` agent tool's wire format outright (#2874 item 61, spec-covered-by: #2986) — the old shape repeated each row's 36-character column IDs (`rows: [{values: {column_id: value}}]`), capping a single call at roughly 40 rows before hitting the token budget. **Matt's ruling (authoritative): "Replace the format outright. 1.0.59 is unreleased, so nothing depends on the old shape. No back-compat, no dual-format support."** The new shape gives column IDs once via a `columns: [string]` array, then each row as a positional array of values (`rows: [[value, value, ...]]`, `row[i]` → `columns[i]`); `null` means a blank cell. Every row must have exactly `columns.length` values — a shorter or longer row is a validation error naming the row index, the expected length, and the actual length (there is no "omit a middle column" option positionally, unlike the old shape's omitted-key convention). **The backend write function, `create_sheet_rows_batch_internal` (`sheets.rs`), does not change at all** — this is a tool-boundary parse change only, confined to `execute_add_sheet_rows` (`ai/commands.rs`): parsing the new JSON shape into the exact same `Vec<RowSpec>` the backend always consumed. **The array/array collision, handled explicitly:** the row itself is a JSON array under the new format — that's the expected container, not a value. `coerce_sheet_cell_value` is called on each row ELEMENT individually, never on the row; calling it on the row would reject every row as "an array value", since a row is always a `serde_json::Value::Array`. **All validation runs before any row is created, same as the existing 500-row-cap/all-or-nothing posture:** an empty `columns` array; an unknown column ID in `columns` (naming the ID and its position, checked against the sheet's real column set up front instead of discovered per-cell mid-transaction the way the old shape found it); a duplicate column ID in `columns` (naming the ID and both positions); a row whose length differs from `columns` (naming the row index, expected, and actual length); a value that is itself an array or object (naming the row index and the column ID, looked up via `columns[i]`); and more than 500 rows (naming the cap and the requested count, unchanged from #2970). `tools.rs`'s schema now requires `columns` (array of string) alongside `note_id`/`rows`, and `rows`' items are schema'd as arrays, not objects with a `values` map. `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.1's `add_sheet_rows` entry status flipped to BUILT, and its coercion-preamble sentence (shared by `set_sheet_cells`, `add_sheet_row`, and `add_sheet_rows`) corrected to stop citing an `add_sheet_rows`' `values` parameter that no longer exists under this format — `add_sheet_row` (singular) still has one, and that half is untouched. **Tests rewritten to the new shape:** #2970's `add_sheet_rows` happy-path, position-start, exactly-at-cap/one-over-cap, and project-scoped/taint/markdown-note-target tests; the `tools.rs` schema test; and item 58's `add_sheet_rows` integer/decimal/boolean/null/object/array coercion tests — the object and array cases now put the bad value INSIDE a row element (`rows: [["Good"], [[1,2,3]]]`) rather than passing the row itself as the thing-that's-an-array, the exact collision this change must not reintroduce. The former column-not-found rollback test (`test_add_sheet_rows_bad_value_rolls_back_whole_call_verified_via_direct_db_check`) is repointed to an unparseable-formula value, since an unknown column_id can no longer surface at write time now that `columns` is validated up front. **Five new tests added**, each confirmed failing against current main first (fed the new-shape payload, the old parser never reads `columns` at all and treats any array-shaped row entry as a valueless blank row, silently returning `Ok({"written_cells":0})` with ONE blank row created instead of erroring): an unknown column, a duplicate column, an empty `columns` array, a row shorter than `columns`, and a row longer than `columns` — each also verified directly against the database that zero rows were created on failure. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, migration/backup-writing tests in `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962, known flake `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert` excluded): 2235 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored, 12 filtered out (2231 base + 5 new tests = 2236; the flake run separately shows the same 2235 passed / 1 flake-failed / 3 ignored / 11 filtered, confirming it's unrelated to this change). `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped (unaffected — backend-only change, no frontend files touched). (Relates to #2874, spec-covered-by: #2986)
- Moved "Insert column left" from the sheet grid's right-click cell context menu (`ShCellContextMenu.svelte`) to the column header's ⋯ menu (`ShHeaderMenu.svelte`) (#2874 item 31) — grouped with Rename and Type above the divider that precedes Sort ascending, matching where the grid's other column-level structural operations (Type, Sort, Filter, Delete column) already live. Removed entirely from the cell context menu, not duplicated; the same insert-column SVG icon is reused verbatim in its new home. `ShGhostCellContextMenu.svelte` keeps its own independent insert-column row, untouched. No backend changes — the underlying `insertColumn(referenceColumnId, 'before')` mechanism is unchanged, just wired from a new door. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: UI rearrangement, no spec change)

### Removed
