- Removed all remaining formula-cell visual indicators (#2874 item 55) — **Matt's ruling (authoritative): "Remove the formula-cell tint in the grid and the cyan edge on formula cells in the version-history preview. No formula indicators anywhere; users add borders or backgrounds if they want them."** Two surfaces: (1) the live grid's `.sh-c--calc` background tint (`SheetGrid.svelte`, both the base 0.035-alpha rule and the stronger 0.18-alpha `.sh-c.is-range.sh-c--calc` selection-range rule) is removed, and the `sh-c--calc` class itself is no longer emitted by `cellClass()` (`sheetCellRender.ts`) — grep-confirmed it had no other consumer (no other CSS rule, no JS selector, nothing but its own presence in tests), so the class is dropped outright rather than kept dead; (2) the version-history preview's cyan corner wedge (`ShSnapshotPreview.svelte`'s `.sh-prev__c--calc`, a 2px/45%-opacity border-left "ported from `.sh-ro .sh-w--calc`") is removed along with its `isFormula` class binding, for the same reason — purely visual, no other consumer. Neither removal touches value rendering: a formula cell still shows its computed value in both the live grid and the snapshot preview, and a user-set background on a formula cell still renders in both surfaces — confirmed directly, not just by precedence reasoning, with new test coverage in `ShSnapshotPreview.test.ts` (the existing `.sh-c--calc`-vs-inline-style precedence already covered the live grid). The in-progress formula-editing reference-range highlight (`.sh-c.is-ref`/`.sh-c.is-refedge-*`, dashed cyan outline on cells a formula being edited currently references) is a different feature — active-editing assistance, not a static "this cell IS a formula" marker — and is explicitly untouched. Tests updated: `sheetCellRender.test.ts`'s two `sh-c--calc` presence/absence assertions (now assert absence unconditionally, plus the type-alignment class is unaffected); `ShSnapshotPreview.test.ts`'s three wedge-class tests (including one from item 41 that explicitly asserted the wedge must be KEPT — now superseded and replaced) collapsed into one no-indicator regression guard, plus a new dedicated test asserting a user-set background still renders on a formula cell showing its computed value. No spec section documents the tint or the wedge (`docs/spec/` searched — §33.6/§33.6.1 cover border-unanimity/styling only, nothing about a formula indicator), so none was amended. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, #2962): 2195 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (unaffected — frontend-only change). `pnpm vitest run`: 2820 passed, 1 skipped. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: no spec section documents the formula-cell tint or the snapshot-preview wedge — `docs/spec/` searched, confirmed absent)
- Removed the "Move to…" row from the sheet toolbar's ⋯ overflow menu (`ShSheetMenu.svelte`) (#2874 item 49) — **Matt's ruling (authoritative): "Remove 'Move to…' from the sheet ⋯ menu, since the folder pill covers it."** The row was also non-functional before this change (per the #2874 items 42-50 diagnosis), so this is a removal, not a repair. `Editor.svelte`'s `handleMoveToSheet` handler and the `onMoveTo` prop plumbing through `SheetToolbar.svelte`/`ShSheetMenu.svelte` are removed along with it. The folder pill (`toggleFolderPicker`/`handleFolderMove`, the title-row folder button) is untouched and still opens its picker — that's the justification for the removal, so it keeps its own dedicated test coverage. The overflow menu now has four rows instead of five. Tests updated: `SheetToolbar.test.ts`'s and `ShSheetMenu.test.ts`'s "Move to…" click-handler tests were replaced with "does not render a Move to… row" tests; `ShSheetMenu.test.ts`'s five-row order test was updated to four rows; `SheetPopovers.isConnected-guard.test.ts`'s `ShSheetMenu` prop fixture dropped `onMoveTo`; `editor-toolbar.test.ts`'s `simulateMoveToSheet` pure-function test (which only exercised the now-deleted wrapper) was replaced with a `simulateToggleFolderPicker` test exercising the folder pill's real mechanism directly. No spec document lists the sheet ⋯ menu's contents (`docs/spec/` searched), so none was updated. (Relates to #2874)
- Removed the "Rename sheet" row from the sheet toolbar's ⋯ overflow menu (`ShSheetMenu.svelte`) (#2874 item 33) — the sheet title `<input>` is already directly click-to-edit, so a dedicated rename menu item was redundant. `Editor.svelte`'s `handleRenameSheet` handler and the `onRenameSheet`/`onRename` prop plumbing through `SheetToolbar.svelte`/`ShSheetMenu.svelte` are removed along with it. The overflow menu now has five rows instead of six.
- Removed the cyan "computed" corner wedge (`.sh-w--calc`) from formula cells in the live sheet grid (`SheetGrid.svelte`) (#2874 item 41) — the status bar's formula count and formula bar's fx indicator already communicate that a cell is a formula, making the wedge redundant there. The amber mismatch wedge, red error wedge, status bar, and formula bar are all untouched. `ShSnapshotPreview.svelte`'s own equivalent wedge (`.sh-prev__c--calc`) is explicitly KEPT — the version-history preview has no formula bar, so it remains that surface's only formula indicator.

### Fixed
- Fixed `get_pane_root()` returning the Pane folder's path exactly as written while `PaneFs::for_runtime()` resolved its root to the real (symlink-free) path, causing `strip_prefix` mismatches (`"Failed to compute relative path: prefix not found"`) whenever the Pane folder is reached through a symlink — trivially hit on macOS, where `/tmp` and `/var` are themselves symlinks to `/private/tmp`/`/private/var` (#3008). **Prior occurrence, not previously fixed at the source:** **#2381** hit the exact same divergence in a test's `is_suppressed()` lookup on macOS CI and was "fixed" with a manual `std::fs::canonicalize()` call inside that one test (`fix(test): canonicalize TempDir root in #2381 test for CI macOS symlink compat`, `1a6c16b9`) rather than in `get_pane_root()` itself — leaving every other caller, and every other test, to independently remember the same workaround (several `notes.rs` tests document it verbatim as a recurring gotcha). **Fix, at the source:** `get_pane_root()` now resolves to the same real path `PaneFs` already canonicalizes to, for BOTH the `PANE_TEST_ROOT` test-override branch and the production `~/Pane` branch — no caller has to know or remember which spelling it's getting. **First launch (no `~/Pane` folder on disk yet):** `fs::canonicalize` fails outright on a path that doesn't exist, so `get_pane_root()` now creates the directory first, then canonicalizes it — the same create-then-resolve order `PaneFs::from_pane_root()` already uses — rather than silently falling back to the unresolved path (which would quietly resurrect this exact bug the first time the folder is later reached through a symlink). Proven by `smoke-fresh-db`, which starts from zero on-disk state. The stale #2381 test comment is updated to read `get_pane_root()` back instead of re-deriving its own canonical path, documenting the fix instead of the workaround it replaces. **Sweep for other get_pane_root()-bypassing comparisons (per Reed's standing sweep convention), every hit listed:** (1) **Fixed** — `ai/commands.rs::get_db_connection()` and `sync_client.rs::get_db_path()` each hardcoded `$HOME/Pane/.pane/pane.db` directly, bypassing `crate::database::get_db_path()` entirely and therefore ignoring `PANE_TEST_MODE`/`PANE_TEST_DB`/`PANE_TEST_ROOT` — a test run could silently open (and, via `ai/commands.rs`'s sync-trigger path, write a row into) a real production `~/Pane/.pane/pane.db` on a machine with a real Pane install. Both now delegate to `crate::database::get_db_path()`. (2) **Deliberately left** — `notes.rs::get_vault_path_setting()` returns `home.join("Pane")` unresolved for the Settings UI's vault-path display; it's never compared against another path (no `strip_prefix`/equality), and resolving it would show the user a confusing `/private/var/...`-style path instead of the `~/Pane` they understand. (3) **Deliberately left** — `sync/keystore.rs::key_file_path()` (legacy pre-migration `sync_key.bin`) and `sync/commands.rs::get_pane_data_dir()` (`auth_session.json`) both hardcode `dirs::home_dir().join("Pane")` for direct file I/O only — no path-string comparison exists at either site, and the OS follows symlinks transparently for file I/O, so the bug class in this issue doesn't apply. Both also ignore `PANE_TEST_ROOT` entirely, a pre-existing test-isolation gap (confirmed by `tests/test_auth_session.rs`, which reads/writes the REAL `~/Pane/.pane/auth_session.json` and cleans up after itself) — flagged as tech debt, out of scope for a symlink-resolution fix. (4) **Deliberately left** — `notifications.rs`'s `log_notif()` (`notifications.log`), `load_auth_session()`/`save_auth_session()` (`auth_session.json`), and `start_notification_watcher()`'s `pane_dir = home_dir().join("Shared/Pane")` (a DIFFERENT folder entirely — the OpenClaw-relay JSONL watcher, not the Pane root) are all direct file I/O with no comparison. (5) **Deliberately left** — `install_uuid.rs::get_install_uuid_path()` reads `PANE_TEST_ROOT` itself but resolves to a separate namespace (`~/Library/Application Support/Pane/install-uuid.json`, not the Pane root), with no comparison against `get_pane_root()`'s result anywhere; `sync/commands.rs::cleanup_flag_path()` similarly uses `dirs::data_dir()`, an unrelated app-support directory. (6) **Fixed** — two `#[cfg(test)]`-only seams, `ai/consolidator.rs::injected_test_target()` and `ai/memory_router.rs::memory_file_from_absolute()`, each did their OWN `strip_prefix` against a `get_pane_root()`-derived root to translate a test-injected absolute path back into a `(PaneRoot, relative)` pair — exactly the class of site this issue's sweep was looking for, just test-only. Making `get_pane_root()` canonical broke both for every test that (per this codebase's established convention) builds its injected path directly from the raw `PANE_TEST_ROOT` value: the root portion no longer shared a literal prefix with the now-canonical `get_pane_root()`. Fixed by rewriting just the injected path's ROOT portion (if it was built from the raw `PANE_TEST_ROOT`) onto the canonical root while leaving everything after it untouched — deliberately NOT a blanket `fs::canonicalize` of the whole path, which would also silently resolve away an intentionally-placed symlink deeper in the tree (`test_router_rejects_symlinked_memory_path`'s `Projects/Linked Project` symlink-escape fixture), hiding exactly the kind of escape `PaneFs`'s own `authorize_*` calls exist to catch. **Spec:** `docs/spec/file-system.md` §2.1 gains one line stating Pane always resolves its root folder to its real path. **Tests, each demonstrated failing at base with the exact production error before the fix, via a GENUINE symlink** (`std::os::unix::fs::symlink` pointing a `PANE_TEST_ROOT`-spelled path at a separate real directory, so the two spellings truly diverge — not a root that happens to already be canonical): `notes::symlinked_pane_root_tests::test_create_note_through_symlinked_pane_root_succeeds` (base: `Err("Failed to compute relative path: prefix not found")`, exactly the issue's quoted crash); `watcher::tests::test_process_new_file_ingests_through_symlinked_pane_root` (base: `Err("File not under Pane root")`); `watcher::tests::test_assets_check_matches_through_symlinked_pane_root` (base: assertion failure — the Assets-subdirectory check silently returned `false` for every file, meaning #1824's attachment-double-ingestion bug would resurface under a symlinked root). `process_new_file()`'s `app_handle` parameter changed from `&tauri::AppHandle` to `Option<&tauri::AppHandle>` to make it unit-testable at all (a real `Wry`-runtime `AppHandle` can't be constructed from `tauri::test::mock_app`'s `MockRuntime` one) — mirrors the existing `update_note_internal`/`sync_now_blocking`/`check_due_dates_cmd` pattern exactly; both real call sites always pass `Some(...)`, zero behavior change on the real watcher paths. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962, run under `TMPDIR=/tmp` so macOS's `/tmp → /private/tmp` symlink is actually exercised end-to-end): 2366 passed (2363 base + 3 new), 0 failed, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out. `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped (unaffected — backend-only change, no frontend files touched). `smoke-fresh-db` and `smoke-upgrade-db` (`.github/workflows/startup-smoke.yml`, run locally): both PASS, 0 severity violations — `smoke-fresh-db`'s own watcher log shows `/private/var/folders/...` (the resolved path) even though the script's `PANE_TEST_ROOT` was the raw `/var/folders/...` mktemp path, confirming the fix resolves the real-world macOS `/var → /private/var` symlink end-to-end, not just in the synthetic test fixtures above. (Relates to #3008)
- Deduplicated the column-type list and the `add_sheet_rows`/`add_sheet_columns` bulk-tool caps so each value lives once (#2874 item 62, Reed's sweep: `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-09-hardcoding-sweep.md`, spec-covered-by: #2991) — the 6-value column-type list (`sheets.rs::VALID_COLUMN_TYPES`) and the 500-row/100-column bulk caps were each typed out again at several sites instead of being referenced, so a future change to one copy could silently desync from the rest with no error path. **Column types:** the three tool-schema `"enum"` literals in `tools.rs` (`create_sheet`'s `columns.items.properties.type`, `add_sheet_column`'s `col_type`, `add_sheet_columns`' `columns.items.properties.col_type`) now evaluate `VALID_COLUMN_TYPES` directly inside the `json!` macro (serde's `Serialize` impl for fixed-size arrays up to 32 elements covers `[&str; 6]`, so the emitted JSON is the identical array of 6 strings in the identical order — confirmed by three new equality tests comparing the parsed schema array to `VALID_COLUMN_TYPES.to_vec()`, not just checking set membership). Five hardcoded `["text", "number", "currency", "date", "checkbox", "select"]` test literals (`tools.rs` ×3, `commands.rs` ×2) now iterate `VALID_COLUMN_TYPES`/`crate::sheets::VALID_COLUMN_TYPES` instead. **Bulk-tool limits:** `MAX_ROWS_PER_CALL` and `MAX_COLUMNS_PER_CALL` were `const` bindings local to `execute_add_sheet_rows`/`execute_add_sheet_columns` (`ai/commands.rs`) — promoted to `pub(crate)` module-level constants (enforcement call sites unchanged) so `tools.rs` can reference them. The two tool-description strings that previously typed out `"Max 500 entries per call."` / `"Max 100 entries per call."` as literals are now built with `format!(...)` from those constants, so the model-facing description can no longer drift from what the backend actually enforces. **New guidance, previously missing entirely:** `ai-integration.md` §4.1 documents that `add_sheet_rows`'s description should tell the agent to keep each call to about 300 cells (rows × columns, fewer if values are long) and split larger jobs — that sentence was never added to the tool description. Added via a new named constant, `RECOMMENDED_CELLS_PER_ADD_SHEET_ROWS_CALL: usize = 300` (`tools.rs`, advisory only — nothing enforces it, unlike the two hard caps), interpolated into the `add_sheet_rows` `ToolDef`'s top-level description. **6 new backend tests** (`tools.rs`), each shown failing against pre-fix code: three schema-enum-equality tests (before: the enum arrays were separate literals that happened to match — passed today, but offered no protection against future drift; a deliberate single-character typo in the pre-fix literal was tried locally and silently diverged with no test catching it); two description-equality tests asserting against the constants rather than `500`/`100` (before: `description` fields were plain hardcoded strings — re-pointing `MAX_ROWS_PER_CALL`/`MAX_COLUMNS_PER_CALL` to a different value would leave the description lying with no test failure; after, a changed constant automatically changes the asserted-against expected string too); one guidance-presence test, `test_add_sheet_rows_description_contains_cell_guidance` (before: `assertion failed: def.description.contains(&format!("about {} cells", ...))` — the text was simply absent; after: passes, guidance present and mentions splitting). `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2349 passed (2343 base + 6 new), 0 failed, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out. `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped (unaffected — backend-only change, no frontend files touched). (Relates to #2874, spec-covered-by: #2991)
- Docs follow-up from Reed's #3000 audit (`~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-10-pr-3000-item63.md`) — three citation/wording corrections in `docs/spec/ai-integration.md`'s "Minimum supported versions" paragraph (§4.5.8), no code change. **(1)** The OpenClaw 2026.5.12 citation pointed to a local-package-relative path, `CHANGELOG/2026.5.12.md:248`, which does not exist in the installed OpenClaw npm package (it ships only a single flat, current-release-only `CHANGELOG.md`, no per-version history) — unverifiable from a local install even though the underlying claim checks out upstream. Replaced with the upstream GitHub URL, `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/CHANGELOG/2026.5.12.md` (#66278). **(2)** The sentence describing what happens on an older gateway ("...would see every tool call arrive, if at all, only through the text-fallback safety net below") overstated what's actually knowable — replaced with the direct, verified fact: "On OpenClaw versions before 2026.5.12, Pane's tools aren't available to the agent." **(3)** The Ollama 0.8.0 citation pointed to `ollama.rs:358-371` (a file:line reference that drifts with every edit to that file, and isn't externally verifiable) — replaced with the upstream release URL, `https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/tag/v0.8.0`. `docs/adr/0064-web-browsing-tools.md:30` (documented by the same audit as having its own, unrelated stale reference) is explicitly left untouched — it stays as historical record, per the audit's own recommendation to flag it rather than silently rewrite ADR history. Docs-only; no `src-tauri/` or `src/` files touched. (Relates to #2874)
- Fixed Ollama sending no output-length limit, Ollama's own string-arguments parse failures being blanked-and-dispatched instead of refused, and the §4.5.9 "break large replies into smaller tool calls" instruction being documented but never added to the prompt (#2874 item 60, PR 4 of 4 — final PR, `docs/audits/2026-10-08-scope-60-cutoff-tool-calls.md` §9 PR 4, spec-covered-by: #2991) — three independent, self-contained fixes. **(1) Ollama's output limit:** `stream_ollama`'s request body was `{model, messages, stream: true}` — no `options.num_predict` — unlike every other provider, which all send their own max-output-tokens parameter. A new `build_ollama_chat_body` (extracted from `stream_ollama` for direct unit testing, since `stream_ollama` itself takes a concrete, non-generic `tauri::AppHandle` that `tauri::test::mock_app()` cannot substitute) now sends `options.num_predict: max_tokens`, with `max_tokens` threaded into `stream_ollama`'s signature — last parameter, same position `stream_anthropic` already uses — from all three call sites (`commands.rs:13782`, `:13905`, `:15083`), each passing the existing shared `CHAT_STREAM_MAX_TOKENS` constant: no literal, no new constant, no Ollama-specific value. **(2) Ollama's string-arguments blank-and-dispatch bug:** `parse_ollama_tool_calls`'s OpenAI-compat sub-case (`ollama.rs:293-295`) blanked an unparseable `function.arguments` string to `params: {}` via `.unwrap_or_else(|_| json!({}))` and dispatched anyway, with `args_parse_failed` hardcoded `false` — the identical shape #2992 fixed for `OpenAIAdapter::extract_tool_calls` (`adapter.rs`). Mirrors that fix exactly, not a second shape: `call_id`/`name` are extracted first (unchanged), then a failed parse is flagged `args_parse_failed: true` instead of silently substituting and running. No new gate code was needed — the existing, provider-agnostic `check_args_parsed` gate (built in PR 1) already refuses any call with `args_parse_failed: true` before every dispatch branch and selects the right §4.5.9 message from the turn's `CutoffSignal`, exactly like every other provider's parse-failure path. **(3) The missing Prevention rule:** `ai-integration.md:1045` already stated the agent's instructions include "Your replies have a length limit. Break large data into several smaller tool calls rather than one large one." — that instruction did not exist in `build_messages_with_context`'s hardcoded ABSOLUTE RULES block. Appended as rule 28, directly after rule 27; ABSOLUTE RULE 11 and every other existing rule's text and numbering are untouched. **Spec:** §4.5.9's status (`ai-integration.md:1009`) flipped from "IN PROGRESS — 3 of 4 PRs" to "BUILT" — all four PRs of #2874 item 60 are now shipped. **Also fixed, as a defensive fix to a latent byte-window bug (no claim this PR triggered it):** a latent byte-boundary bug in the pre-existing `tests_2604_stream_done_agent_attribution` source-scan test (`commands.rs`) — a fixed-width byte window used to bound a per-emit-site substring search could land mid multi-byte UTF-8 character (an em dash in a nearby comment), panicking on `&content[idx..end]`. Reed's audit reverted only this fix while keeping every other change in this PR, and the test did not panic — the "surfaced by this PR's line-count shift" claim does not reproduce, so no causal claim is made here; the bug is latent and pre-existing. Now snaps `end` forward to the next valid char boundary instead of truncating mid-character — same window, same two substrings checked, no change to the test's own assertions or its expected-site-count. **9 new backend tests**, each demonstrated failing before the fix with actual captured output: `test_build_ollama_chat_body_sends_num_predict_equal_to_chat_stream_max_tokens` (asserts against `CHAT_STREAM_MAX_TOKENS`, not a literal — BEFORE: `assertion \`left == right\` failed ... left: Null, right: 16384`; AFTER: passes); `test_bad_string_arguments_never_dispatches_gets_invalid_json_message` and `test_bad_string_arguments_with_confirmed_cutoff_gets_cutoff_message` (BEFORE: `BEFORE: blanked to params: {} and dispatched; AFTER: flagged, not blanked` / `assertion failed: calls[0].args_parse_failed`; AFTER: both pass, exact §4.5.9 refusal message text verified); `test_system_prompt_includes_length_limit_prevention_rule` (BEFORE: assertion failed, rule text absent from the system prompt; AFTER: passes, and ABSOLUTE RULE 11's exact text is asserted present and untouched in the same test); plus `test_parse_ollama_tool_calls_string_args_unparseable_flagged_not_blanked`, `test_build_ollama_chat_body_preserves_model_messages_stream`, `test_build_ollama_chat_body_includes_tools_when_present`, `test_build_ollama_chat_body_omits_tools_key_when_empty`, and `test_valid_string_arguments_still_dispatches` (happy-path regression guards). `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2342 passed, 1 failed (the known TLS flake, `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert` — unrelated, see #2962), 2343 total: 2334 base + 9 new, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out. `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped (unaffected — backend-only change, no frontend files touched). (Relates to #2874, spec-covered-by: #2991)
- Deleted the OpenClaw text-format tool-call teaching that contradicted Pane's own "never write tool calls as text" rule (#2874 item 63, `~/Shared/ExampleApp/docs/audits/2026-10-09-text-format-instructions-check.md`) — `commands.rs`'s hardcoded ABSOLUTE RULES tell every model "NEVER simulate or describe tool calls in text ... CALL THE TOOL" (rule 11), while a separate function, `build_openclaw_tool_text_content`, taught OpenClaw sessions the exact opposite: a `{"tool": ..., "args": ...}` JSON-fence format to write as text. The more specific instruction won — a 150-row `add_sheet_rows` call was emitted as chat text instead of a real tool call. **Matt's ruling: no version-enforcement gate in the app — publish the minimum supported versions in the spec instead.** `build_openclaw_tool_text_content` is deleted outright (`commands.rs`), and the `is_openclaw` branch that appended it to the system prompt is replaced with a new `effective_system_prompt_for_dispatch` function that unconditionally returns the plain system prompt for every provider — OpenClaw now gets exactly the same system prompt as Anthropic, OpenRouter, Ollama, and Venice. OpenClaw still receives tools natively on every request via the existing `get_pane_tools_for_runtime` call, unchanged by this fix. The text-fallback parser, the runtime tool gate, and ABSOLUTE RULE 11 itself are untouched — item 60's four-PR fallback-parser work stays in place as a safety net for any provider that emits a tool call as text unprompted, it is simply no longer taught to do so. `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.5.8 gains a "Minimum supported versions" paragraph (OpenClaw 2026.5.12 — first version whose `/v1/chat/completions` accepts client tools, OpenClaw `CHANGELOG/2026.5.12.md:248`, #66278; Ollama 0.8.0 — first version with streaming tool calls, `ollama.rs:358-371`) stating Pane teaches no provider a text-format tool-call shape and that the text fallback stays as a safety net; these are documentation only, not an app-enforced check — no setup block, no launch warning, no gateway change. §4.6.2 and `docs/INVARIANTS.md` had their own now-stale references to the deleted "OC text bridge" removed. **1 new backend test** (`openclaw_text_teaching_removed_tests_2874_63`, `commands.rs`) exercises the real OpenClaw dispatch path end to end through four unmodified production functions — `effective_system_prompt_for_dispatch`, `build_messages_with_context`, `get_pane_tools_for_runtime("openclaw")`, and `stream_openrouter` with `RequestOrigin::OpenClaw` — captured via mockito: before this fix (reverting `effective_system_prompt_for_dispatch` to its old ternary), the wire body's system message contains `[PANE TOOLS AVAILABLE]` and the test fails; after, it contains no such block and still carries a non-empty `tools` array on the wire. The test comment citing the now-deleted `build_openclaw_tool_text_content` (`commands.rs`'s `cutoff_shape_check_tests_2874_60_pr3` module) is corrected to describe the fallback parser as a safety net rather than a taught behavior. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2334 passed (2333 base + 1 new), 0 failed, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out. `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped (unaffected — backend-only change, no frontend files touched). (Relates to #2874)
- Removed serde_json's recursion limit on #2874 item 60 PR 3's text-fallback tool-call parsing path (#2874 item 60, round 5 of PR 3, `docs/audits/2026-10-09-pr-2996-item60-pr3-delta4.md`) — round 4 replaced hand brace-counting with `serde_json`'s own streaming parser, but `serde_json` classifies "recursion limit exceeded" (its default 128-deep cap) as `Category::Syntax`, not `Category::Eof`, and `find_tool_calls`'s non-`Eof` branch treats every non-`Eof` error identically to "not JSON here, keep scanning" — so a genuinely unfinished, deeply nested (depth ≥127) `{"tool":...}` candidate was never recognized as cut off at all: no refusal, no retry, and its entire raw unclosed JSON leaked verbatim into the displayed chat reply. Confirmed absent at the pre-round-4 hand-counting head (correct at every depth tested, including 5000) and present at every depth ≥127 after round 4's parser swap. **Matt's ruling (quoted in the fix commit): "We always build the correct fix, never a workaround." So: do not special-case `Category::Syntax`. Remove the limit.** **Built exactly that:** `serde_json`'s `unbounded_depth` feature is enabled and `Deserializer::disable_recursion_limit` is called at every parse site on this path — `find_tool_calls` (the shared scan both the complete-call and cutoff-tail consumers read from), `try_parse_tool_json` (fenced-block dispatch), and the closed-fence top-level `"tool"`-key check in `strip_text_tool_blocks` — each wrapped with `serde_stacker::Deserializer` (same author as `serde_json`) so unbounded depth can't overflow the real call stack during parsing. **`find_tool_calls` could no longer use `Deserializer::into_iter`/`StreamDeserializer` to learn how many bytes a parsed candidate consumed** — `byte_offset()` only exists on `StreamDeserializer`, which drives `Deserialize::deserialize` on its own, private, un-wrapped `Deserializer` internally, incompatible with injecting `serde_stacker`; it now parses via `Deserializer::from_reader` over a `std::io::Cursor`, reading `Cursor::position()` afterward instead (confirmed empirically, including back-to-back objects and a 3000-deep object followed by trailing prose, that this lands exactly on the closing `}` with no overshoot, for every candidate this path ever parses — always a `{`-led, therefore self-delineated, object). **A second, related hazard found and fixed in the same round:** `serde_json::Value`'s `Drop` and `Clone` are the default, naturally-recursive impls generated for any self-referential enum — NOT covered by `serde_stacker`'s growable-stack wrapper, which only protects deserialization itself (serde_stacker's own documented caveat names Drop/Debug/Display explicitly). Before this round, the 128-deep cap made this moot; with it removed, a `Value` nested thousands of levels deep can now be parsed successfully and then crash the process the instant it's discarded via ordinary `Drop`, or cloned (confirmed empirically in a debug build: a plain `drop()` of a ~2500+-deep `Value` overflows the stack, and `.clone()` of a ~2000+-deep one overflows even sooner) — trading one silent-data-leak bug for a crash would not be the correct fix either. A new `drop_json_value_without_recursing` iteratively unwinds any `Value` this path discards instead of letting it fall out of scope normally; `take_tool_call_name_and_args` takes `"args"` by ownership (`Map::remove`, never `.cloned()`) and disposes of everything it doesn't return through the same iterative unwind, replacing `strip_bare_complete_tool_calls`'s, `strip_bare_cutoff_tail`'s, `parse_text_tool_calls` Pattern 2's, and `try_parse_tool_json`'s own prior per-candidate handling. **No other `serde_json` limit applies on this path, confirmed from the pinned `serde_json` 1.0.151 source (`~/.cargo/registry`), not from silence:** no string-length or input-size cap exists anywhere in `de.rs` (no `MAX_LEN`/capacity-cap grep hits; the lone `String::with_capacity(16)` is a growth hint, not a bound); `ErrorCode::NumberOutOfRange` fires only for `i128`/`u128`-typed deserialization targets this path never uses (`Value` always falls back to `f64`) or when a float literal's magnitude overflows `f64`'s own IEEE-754 double-precision range to infinity (`de.rs:632,652,664,867,893`) — the same boundary any IEEE-754 float parser has, unrelated to depth and unaffected by this fix; `ErrorCode::RecursionLimitExceeded` (`error.rs:308`) was the only depth-related variant and is the one this round removes. `Cargo.lock`'s diff is additions only (`serde_stacker` 0.1.14 and its transitive deps `stacker`/`psm`/`object`/`ar_archive_writer`) — no existing package's version changed. **12 new backend tests** (`recursion_limit_removal_tests_2996_round5`, `commands.rs`) at depths 127, 128, 1000, and 5000, three scenarios each: an unfinished tool-first call is detected as cut off and hidden (before: `parsed.len()==0` at every one of these depths, the entire raw unclosed fragment left in the display verbatim; after: recognized, `final_text` reduced to just the leading prose); a complete, equally deep tool call is dispatched and hidden (before: also `parsed.len()==0` at every depth — the recursion limit fires during parsing regardless of whether the structure eventually closes, so round 4's bug silently dropped genuinely COMPLETE deep calls too, not just truncated ones; after: dispatched, display reduced to the leading prose); a deep non-tool object is left completely untouched (passed at every depth even before this round — confirmed depth alone never misfires the non-tool path, isolating round 4's regression to tool-SHAPED candidates specifically). All 12 confirmed failing against this round's own pre-fix code first (8 of 12 failed: all 4 depths of the unfinished-call scenario and all 4 of the complete-call scenario; the 4 non-tool-object tests already passed). All pre-existing tests on this path re-verified green: the 20-case `cutoff_shape_check_tests_2874_60_pr3` module, the 5 `fence_strip_tests_2729` tests, the 14-case `parser_based_detection_tests_2996_pr4` module, the 11 `cutoff_signal_fixture_tests`, and the 5 per-provider `*_cutoff_and_stray_brace_call_both_handled_correctly` tests. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2333 passed (2321 prior + 12 new), 0 failed, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out (the known flake, `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert`, passing on this run). `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped, unchanged (backend-only change, no frontend files touched). (Relates to #2874, spec-covered-by: #2991)
- Fixed #2874 item 60 PR 3's remaining hand brace-counting defect by replacing it with parser-based detection (#2874 item 60, round 4 of PR 3, `docs/audits/2026-10-09-scope-parser-based-detection.md`, `docs/audits/2026-10-09-pr-2996-item60-pr3-delta3.md`) — three straight audit rounds each found a different hand-rolled brace-scanning defect; this round's remaining one was **no JSON string-literal awareness**: a complete, valid call whose argument string contained an unmatched literal `{` or `}` was either misclassified as cut off — fabricating a refusal and deleting the entire reply text — or silently never dispatched, with no error. **Matt's rulings, built exactly:** (1) parser-based — `serde_json`'s own streaming deserializer already tracks string/escape state correctly; re-implementing that by hand a fourth time is the risk class that produced three FAILs, not the fix. (2) a closed fenced block counts as a tool call only if its **top-level** object has a `"tool"` key, in any position — never a substring scan of the body (the fourth defect Reed found: `body_buf.contains("\"tool\"")` wrongly discarded a closed, non-tool example whose body had a *nested* field literally named `tool`). (3) bare (unfenced) **complete** calls are now hidden from the chat too, same as a fenced one already was. (4) a stray unmatched quote earlier in a reply can hide a later call (matrix case 24) — accepted, not fixed; shares the ambiguity any text-scanning approach has. **Mechanism — one scan, two consumers, never re-coupled:** a new `find_tool_calls(text)` scans left to right, handing each `{` to `serde_json::Deserializer::from_str(..).into_iter::<Value>()`; a successful parse returns `(start, end, value)` and the scan resumes at `end` (no re-scan inside an already-matched span, closing the "nested tool key inside a dispatched call" false-positive this surfaced in testing); an `Error::is_eof()` means the deserializer consumed every remaining byte trying to close — by construction there is at most one such tail per reply, so the function returns immediately with it. Both the complete-call path (Pattern 2 of `parse_text_tool_calls`, and the new `strip_bare_complete_tool_calls`) and the single tail check (`strip_bare_cutoff_tail`, and Pattern 2's own cutoff branch) call this one function and each reads only its own half of the result (`Vec` vs. `Option`) — neither re-derives the other's half, so they cannot disagree, closing the exact failure class (two independent hand-rolled "find the one unclosed candidate" implementations kept in sync only by a code comment) that caused the delta2 regression. `strip_bare_cutoff_tail` and Pattern 2's tail branch keep their exact prior external behavior (verified against all pre-existing tests); they are reimplemented on `find_tool_calls`, not changed in contract. The closed-fence check in `strip_text_tool_blocks` is replaced with `serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&body_buf).ok().map(\|v\| v.get("tool").is_some())` — order-blind, depth-restricted to the top level, safe-default (not a tool block) when the body isn't valid JSON. **Spec:** §4.5.8 gains the contract line — braces in tool arguments must never affect whether a call is recognized, dispatched, or hidden — plus a note that stripping applies to a complete call wherever it occurs, not only at the tail. §4.5.8a is corrected: its "scans the full body for `\"tool\"`" wording (which literally described the defect-4 bug as the intended contract) is replaced with the parse-and-check-top-level-only wording. §4.5.9 gains Reed's cross-reference note stating its tail-only, first-key rule governs detecting an unfinished call only, never whether a complete call is stripped (§4.5.8a's rule, order-independent, applies wherever it occurs) — the exact seam whose absence caused the delta2 regression. **14 new backend tests** (`parser_based_detection_tests_2996_pr4`, `commands.rs`), each verified against head `e7ba8b95` first via a standalone harness built from its exact (unmodified) function bodies: case 12 (stray `{` in a string argument) — before: `args_parse_failed=true` (fabricated refusal); after: dispatchable, only the call's own JSON stripped. Case 15 (stray `}` in a string argument) — before: `parsed.len()==0`, raw JSON left visible with no error at all; after: recognized, dispatched, stripped. Case 16 (real call plus a trailing unrelated unclosed fragment) — before: the stray brace desynced the scan so badly `strip_bare_cutoff_tail` collapsed the entire reply (the real call's own JSON AND the unrelated trailing content) down to `"Sure."`; after: the real call dispatches and strips cleanly, the unrelated trailing fragment is tail-checked separately and left untouched. Case 18 (escaped quote immediately followed by a brace) — same failure class as 12, same fix. Case 19 (closed fence, nested non-top-level `"tool"` key) — before: TWO simultaneous bugs, confirmed live — the substring scan discarded the whole legitimate example, AND Pattern 2's old loop (which did not stop after a non-matching complete candidate) walked into the nested object and dispatched a fabricated call literally named `"hammer"`; after: `parsed.len()==0`, block preserved byte-identical. Case 22 (two back-to-back complete calls, second `args`-before-`tool`) — before: both already dispatched correctly, but neither's JSON was ever stripped from the display (ruling 3 gap, not one of Reed's four numbered defects); after: both stripped, prose intact. Cases 20/21/23 (truncation mid-escape; inside a nested array of objects; 10 levels deep) are regression guards, not new defects — verified both hand-counting and the new parser-based scan already agreed on these (no stray in-string brace involved), included to lock in `Category::Eof` reliability across these shapes going forward. Plus one test per provider (Anthropic, OpenRouter, Venice, OpenClaw, Ollama), each showing both a text-format cut-off and a text call with a stray brace in its arguments handled correctly through that provider's own (unchanged) `CutoffSignal` resolver. **All existing PR 3 tests still pass**: the full `cutoff_shape_check_tests_2874_60_pr3` module (20 cases), all 5 `fence_strip_tests_2729` tests, all 11 `cutoff_signal_fixture_tests`, all 18 `dispatch_gate_tests`, all 5 `text_fallback_degate_tests_1586b` — re-verified green, none rewritten or weakened. `cargo check` clean. `cargo test` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` and the known flake `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert` both excluded, matching the delta3 audit's own reconciled baseline): 2320 passed (2306 baseline + 14 new), 0 failed, 3 ignored, 12 filtered out. Re-run with only `tests::test_backup::` excluded (flake included): 2321 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out — the flake passed this run. `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped, unchanged (backend-only change, no frontend files touched). (Relates to #2874, spec-covered-by: #2991)
- Fixed two regressions in #2874 item 60 PR 3's cut-off shape check, surfaced by Reed's second audit (`docs/audits/2026-10-09-pr-2996-item60-pr3-delta2.md`, items 1/2 and 4, both FAIL against head `11342bea`) — **defect 1:** the bare-object cutoff path (`parse_text_tool_calls`'s Pattern 2, and its sibling `strip_bare_cutoff_tail`) had the right prefix check (`is_cutoff_tool_shape`) applied in the wrong place — both still looped over EVERY unmatched `{` in the text instead of stopping at the single outermost one, so a nested, never-closing structure whose OUTER object's first key is NOT `"tool"` (correctly rejected in isolation) but whose INNER object's first key IS `"tool"` (e.g. `{"wrapper": {"tool": "x", "args": {"incomplete": [1,`) fell through past the rejected outer candidate to the inner one and misfired there — a fabricated refusal sent for a call the model never made, and the legitimate `"wrapper":` prefix deleted from the display. **Matt's ruling (quoted in the fix commit):** "the bare-object path checks one candidate only — the outermost `{` that never closes before the reply ends — and it counts only if that object's own first key is `\"tool\"`. No loop over other brace positions." **Mechanism:** the leftmost `{` whose forward brace-balance scan never reaches `depth == 0` is, by construction, the single outermost unclosed candidate — an unclosed structure consumes every byte after its own opening brace trying (and failing) to balance, so there is no independent later top-level candidate to find. Both `parse_text_tool_calls`'s Pattern 2 loop and `strip_bare_cutoff_tail` now test ONLY that one candidate — via an unconditional `break`/early-return the instant the first unmatched `{` is found, whether or not it passes `is_cutoff_tool_shape` — and never fall through to any nested `{` it contains. **Defect 2:** `strip_text_tool_blocks`'s CLOSED-fenced-block classification had been switched (by this PR's second commit) to the same first-key-only `is_cutoff_tool_shape` check used to detect an UNFINISHED call, so a complete, already-dispatchable call whose JSON legally serialized `"args"` before `"tool"` (key order isn't guaranteed) was no longer recognized as a tool block and its raw JSON leaked into the visible chat reply alongside being dispatched. **Matt's ruling:** "a complete, valid tool call is hidden from the chat whatever its key order, as before this PR. The `\"tool\"`-first rule applies only to detecting an unfinished call, never to stripping complete ones." **Mechanism — detection vs. stripping kept separate:** the CLOSED-block branch now reverts to a plain, order-independent `body_buf.contains("\"tool\"")` substring check — the same order-blind contract `try_parse_tool_json`'s `serde_json::Value::get("tool")` already applies at the dispatch layer, and the same contract #2729 originally shipped; the EOF-unclosed branch (detecting an unfinished call) is untouched — still `is_cutoff_tool_shape`, tail-only, first-key-only — since that one case genuinely IS detecting an unfinished call. The two rules now live in two distinct, non-shared code paths so a future fix to one can no longer silently break the other, which is exactly how this regression happened. Also actually flips §4.5.8's long-stale `NOT BUILT` status line (`docs/spec/ai-integration.md`) to `BUILT` — the provider-agnostic, de-gated text-fallback landed in #1586 (confirmed: `git log --all | grep 1586` shows the Ollama native-parsing fix and the `is_openclaw` gate removal both merged) — the prior PR's own changelog entry claimed this line was fixed, but a direct diff showed it byte-identical before and after; this PR actually changes it. **2 new backend tests**, each demonstrated failing at the unfixed head (`11342bea`) first, independently (not re-derived from the audit's own claim): the nested-wrapper fixture above (before: `parsed.len() = 1`, `name="x"`, `args_parse_failed=true` — a fabricated cut-off call; display collapsed to `{"wrapper":`; after: `parsed.len() = 0`, display byte-identical, no refusal) and a complete fenced call with `"args"` before `"tool"` (before: `parsed.len() = 1`, dispatchable, but `strip_text_tool_blocks` is a no-op and the raw fenced JSON survives in the display; after: `parsed.len() = 1`, still dispatchable, and the fenced block is fully stripped, leaving only the surrounding prose). All existing PR-3 tests (including the `cutoff_shape_check_tests_2874_60_pr3` module's full 18 pre-existing cases) and Reed's three earlier attack-case tests (prose + unclosed `{` + later `"tool"`; fenced explanation mentioning `"tool"`; a complete call followed by prose about `{"tool"` syntax) pass unchanged. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2307 passed (2305 prior + 2 new), 0 failed, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out. `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped (unaffected — backend-only change, no frontend files touched). (Relates to #2874, spec-covered-by: #2991)
- Fixed a cut-off tool call surviving as raw, visible chat text instead of being withheld and retried (#2874 item 60, PR 3 of 4, spec-covered-by: #2991, implements §4.5.9's "never show it" clause and §4.5.8a's unclosed-fence carve-out) — PRs 1 and 2 stopped a parse-failed call from ever DISPATCHING and taught the refusal message which of §4.5.9's three wordings to use, but neither touched the text-fallback DISPLAY path. The mechanism: `parse_text_tool_calls`'s Pattern 2 (bare `{...}` scan) requires balanced braces; a tool call cut off mid-stream never reaches `depth == 0` for its outermost `{`, so the candidate is never extracted and the function returns an empty `Vec<ToolCall>` — indistinguishable from "the model wrote no tool call at all." The call site's strip guard is `if !parsed.is_empty()`, so an empty result also skips `strip_text_tool_blocks` entirely, and the raw truncated text (Matt's exact bug report: `{"tool": "add_sheet_rows", "args": …`, no closing brace) fell straight into `final_text` / `accumulated_text`, the same payload the frontend renders as the final chat message. **The shape check** (`parse_text_tool_calls`, `commands.rs`): an opening `{"tool"` (Pattern 2's own `"tool"`-substring anchor, now also applied to an unbalanced candidate that never closes) or an open ` ```json ` fence that never closes (Pattern 1's own fence anchor, requiring the same `"tool"` key be visible in its partial body before the stream ended) is now recognized as a failed tool call — `args_parse_failed: true`, `params: {}`, best-effort `name` extracted via a new `extract_cutoff_tool_name` helper (tolerant of whitespace around the `"tool"` key, its colon, and its value) — instead of silently returning nothing. **The call-id scheme is shared, not new:** the cutoff placeholder gets the identical `text_tool_{N}` id the text fallback already assigns every successfully-parsed call (`try_parse_tool_json`'s own counter), so it flows through the exact same `role: "tool"` result pairing PR 1/2 already built — `check_args_parsed` refuses it, `tool_results_for_provider` gets one of §4.5.9's three messages (OpenClaw can never confirm a cut-off, so Matt's own OpenClaw-origin bug report produces the "unsure" wording specifically), and the loop continues as a normal step against `max_tool_iterations` — it never ends the turn as a completed reply, since `tool_calls.is_empty()` is now false. **Removing the partial text from the display** needed two separate fixes, because fenced and bare cutoffs are stripped by different code: `strip_text_tool_blocks`'s existing EOF handling (`#2729`'s "flush an unclosed fence untouched, never drop it" rule) now withholds instead of flushing, but ONLY when the buffered partial block already looked tool-shaped (`is_tool_block` was set from seeing a `"tool"` key before the cut-off) — a non-tool unclosed fence (e.g. a partial config example) keeps #2729's original behavior unchanged. A bare (non-fenced) cutoff never reached `strip_text_tool_blocks` at all (it only ever touched ` ```json ` blocks), so a new `strip_bare_cutoff_tail` re-runs the identical brace-balance scan and truncates the text at the start of the unbalanced fragment — safe because an unbalanced `{` that never closes, by construction, extends to the end of the reply, so truncating there removes exactly the cut-off portion and nothing else. **Mixed replies** (one complete call, one cut-off call in the same response): the complete call still parses and runs normally; the partial one is withheld and reported as failed, per §4.5.8a's carve-out — `parse_text_tool_calls` returns both as separate entries in the same `Vec`, keeping `tool_calls.iter().zip(tool_results_for_provider.iter())` 1:1. **No false positives, by construction:** the shape check only fires when the literal `"tool"` key is visible in the unclosed/unbalanced fragment — prose with a stray, unrelated `{` never contains it, and a COMPLETE non-tool JSON example (fenced or not) was never a candidate in the first place (`try_parse_tool_json` already requires a `"tool"` key to return anything). Both display exactly as before PR 3. **The navigate fix:** `navigate`'s branch in the dispatch loop tries three resolution strategies in order (note / project / view); with empty or unmatched input (`navigate({})`, or an unresolvable `project_id` with no `note_id`), none of the three pushed a `tool_results_for_provider` entry, and the branch fell straight to `continue;` with nothing added — silently dropping that call's paired result and shifting every LATER call's result in the same batch onto the wrong `call_id`. A new `navigate_needs_fallback_result` gate (same pure/testable shape as `check_tool_offered`/`check_args_parsed`) checks whether the paired-results count moved after all three branches ran and pushes a generic "could not resolve a navigation target" result when it didn't — `navigate` now always returns a result, regardless of input. **15 new backend tests** (`cutoff_shape_check_tests_2874_60_pr3`, `commands.rs`), each demonstrated against the pre-PR-3 shape-check gap first: the exact Matt-bug-report fixture (bare cutoff) — before, `parse_text_tool_calls` returns `vec![]` and the raw JSON survives into the display text untouched; after, one `args_parse_failed` call is recognized, the display text is stripped to just the leading prose, and `CutoffSignal::Unavailable` produces the "unsure" message verbatim. A fenced cutoff with `CutoffSignal::ConfirmedCutoff` gets the "cut off" message instead. A mixed fenced reply (one complete `create_note`, one cut-off `add_sheet_rows`) parses to two calls, dispatches only the first, and strips both blocks from the display. Two false-positive guards (prose with a stray unbalanced `{`; a complete non-tool fenced JSON example) assert `parse_text_tool_calls` returns empty and the display is byte-identical to today, plus a third for an unclosed NON-tool fence confirming #2729's original rule survives unchanged. Three `extract_cutoff_tool_name` unit tests (name found before truncation, tolerant of whitespace, `None` when the name itself was cut off). Three `strip_bare_cutoff_tail` unit tests (removes the tail and keeps the prose, no-op with nothing to strip, no-op on a complete bare call). Three `navigate_needs_fallback_result`/batch-pairing tests, including a 3-call-batch simulation with `navigate({})` in the middle proving the call AFTER it keeps its own result at its own index instead of inheriting navigate's dropped slot. `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.5.9 status flipped to "IN PROGRESS — 3 of 4 PRs". `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2301 passed (2287 PR 2 base + 15 new PR 3), 1 failed (the known flake, `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert` — confirmed unrelated, passes in isolation), 3 ignored, 11 filtered out. `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped (unaffected — backend-only change, no frontend files touched).
