- Fixed a false-positive hole in #2874 item 60 PR 3's cut-off shape check (same PR, same files — Reed's audit, `docs/audits/2026-10-09-pr-2996-item60-pr3.md` item 2, FAIL) — the shape check anchored `"tool"` containment to "anywhere in the remaining text after the unmatched `{`" instead of to the candidate's own span, so it could misfire three ways, all reproduced live against the unfixed code: (1) ordinary prose with an unrelated unclosed `{`, followed much later in the same reply by the model quoting the word `"tool"` (e.g. explaining its own tool-call format), silently deleted the legitimate remainder of the sentence and pushed a fabricated "couldn't run" refusal for a call that was never made; (2) the fenced path's `is_tool_block` had the identical weakness one level down — a per-line `.contains("\"tool\"")` scan flagged a genuinely non-tool fenced example whenever ANY line's string *value* happened to contain the word, not just a real `"tool"` *key*; (3) a COMPLETE call followed by prose discussing `{"tool"` syntax also tripped it, because Pattern 2's scan never `break`s after a successful match and kept looking. Matt's ruling (quoted in the fix commit) replaces the earlier "any key order, anywhere in the remainder" check with a tail-only one: a bare object counts only if it starts with `{`, has `"tool"` as its literal FIRST key (whitespace tolerant around the brace, the key, and the colon that must immediately follow it), and never closes before the reply ends; a fenced block counts only on the same terms, judged by its own buffered body. **Implementation, both paths:** a new `is_cutoff_tool_shape(fragment) -> bool` helper is a pure prefix check — `strip_prefix('{')`, `trim_start().strip_prefix("\"tool\"")`, then requires `:` — consulting only the start of its own argument, never scanning elsewhere. `parse_text_tool_calls`'s bare-object cutoff branch and fenced-cutoff branch, `strip_bare_cutoff_tail`, and `strip_text_tool_blocks` (whose `is_tool_block` is now a single `is_cutoff_tool_shape` check against the block's own buffered body — computed once, at close time or end-of-stream, replacing the old per-line accumulation) all now call this one helper; `.contains("\"tool\"")` is gone from all four call sites. Requiring a trailing colon (beyond what Matt's examples alone show) is what specifically closes case (3): `{"tool" when quoted this way` has no colon after the key, so it is correctly not a candidate. `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.5.9's "Never show it" clause is reworded to match (tail-only, first-key, never-closes-before-end, nothing earlier ever removed). **3 new backend tests** (`cutoff_shape_check_tests_2874_60_pr3`, `commands.rs`) reproduce Reed's three breaking cases, each run against the unfixed PR head first: prose with a stray unclosed `{` and a later quoted "tool" (before: 1 false-positive call, display collapsed to the sentence fragment before the brace; after: 0 calls, display byte-identical); a fenced non-tool example whose body mentions "tool" as a value (before: 1 false-positive call, the whole example collapsed to just the leading line; after: 0 calls, display byte-identical); a complete call followed by prose about `{"tool"` syntax (before: 2 calls — one fabricated — display lost the trailing sentence; after: 1 call, dispatchable, trailing prose intact). All 15 existing PR-3 tests and all 5 pre-existing #2729 fence-strip tests pass unchanged. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2305 passed (2301 prior + 3 new tests + the known flake, `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert`, passing rather than flaking on this run), 0 failed, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out. `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped (unaffected — backend-only change). (Relates to #2874, spec-covered-by: #2991)
- Fixed every provider's tool-call parse-failure message always reading as "possibly cut off" (#2874 item 60, PR 2 of 4, spec-covered-by: #2991, implements §4.5.9's detection table and its three messages) — PR 1 added the `args_parse_failed` gate but read no provider signal, so every refusal used §4.5.9's "no signal available" text regardless of what actually happened. **Signal plumbing, per provider:** **Anthropic** — `stream_anthropic`'s SSE loop now captures `delta.stop_reason` off the `message_delta` event (previously read for `usage` only, at the exact same match arm) and `chat_with_tools`'s non-streaming path reads the response body's top-level `stop_reason` field; both feed a new `anthropic_cutoff_signal(stop_reason)` function. **OpenRouter/Venice** — `stream_openrouter_inner`'s SSE loop now captures `choices[0].finish_reason` from the same per-chunk `data` object `usage`/`delta` already read (adjacent field, same chunk), fed to a new `openai_cutoff_signal(finish_reason, origin)`. **Ollama** — `stream_ollama`'s NDJSON loop now captures `done_reason` off the terminal `done:true` line, fed to a new `ollama_cutoff_signal(done_reason)`. Each stream function's return tuple grew one element (`CutoffSignal`) carrying the resolved signal out to the agentic dispatch loop in `commands.rs` (`stream_anthropic`/`stream_ollama`: 2-tuple → 3-tuple; `stream_openrouter`'s `StreamOpenrouterOk`: 3-tuple → 4-tuple) — every one of the ~24 call sites across the primary dispatch, smart-route retry, provider fallback, and summarization branches was updated to match, including the Anthropic/Ollama `.map(|(t, tc)| (t, tc, None::<String>))` normalization shim, now `.map(|(t, tc, sig)| (t, tc, None::<String>, sig))`. `check_args_parsed` (`commands.rs`) now takes this `CutoffSignal` and picks §4.5.9's exact verbatim message: a confirmed cut-off (`stop_reason: "max_tokens"` / `finish_reason: "length"` / `done_reason: "length"`) gets the "cut off... split it into smaller calls" message; a confirmed normal stop with unparseable arguments gets the "arguments weren't valid JSON... re-send it" message; no usable signal gets the original "possibly cut off... try a smaller version" message PR 1 always produced. **The OpenClaw trap, and how it's distinguished:** OpenClaw routes through this SAME shared OpenRouter-shaped parser (confirmed: `AiProvider::OpenClaw` dispatches via `stream_openrouter` with `RequestOrigin::OpenClaw`, the identical function bare OpenRouter and Venice use with `RequestOrigin::Other`/`RequestOrigin::Venice`), but OpenClaw's own OpenAI-compat HTTP translation layer collapses every non-`tool_calls` stop reason — including a real length cutoff — to the literal string `"stop"` before Pane's HTTP client ever sees it (confirmed against the installed OpenClaw gateway package's built `openai-http` response builder: `resolveStopReasonAndPendingToolCalls` reads the real underlying value, but every consumer of it branches only on `=== "tool_calls"`, and both the streaming `requestFinalize()` helper's default parameter and the non-streaming response body's catch-all hard-code `"stop"` for everything else — `openai-http-BNmNRauy.js:182` et al., traced file:line in the #2874 item 60 scope audit). A length-truncated OpenClaw turn and a normally-completed one are therefore wire-identical on this field. **The discrimination mechanism is `RequestOrigin`** — already the exact enum `select_openrouter_client` uses to pick the TLS client and the wire-model sentinel, so no new plumbing was needed: `openai_cutoff_signal` checks `origin == RequestOrigin::OpenClaw` FIRST, before looking at the string at all, and returns `Unavailable` unconditionally in that case, regardless of what `finish_reason` says — trusting OpenClaw's collapsed `"stop"` as a real normal stop would tell the agent "your JSON was invalid, re-send it" when the actual problem was length, which is worse than saying nothing. `RequestOrigin::Other` and `RequestOrigin::Venice` both trust `finish_reason` normally. **Anthropic fixture replaced, not extended, per PR 1's audit WARN** (`canonical_format.rs`'s `cutoff_replay_shape_tests`): PR 1's hand-authored SSE transcript was missing `message_start`, `input: {}` on `content_block_start` (Anthropic's own documented example always includes it), `content_block_stop`, and `stop_sequence` alongside `message_delta`'s `stop_reason` (Anthropic always pairs the two) — harmless for PR 1 since nothing read those fields yet, load-bearing now that this PR reads `stop_reason` from exactly that shape. The replacement transcript includes all of them in the documented order, and the test-only `accumulate_sse_transcript` helper now mirrors every SSE match arm `stream_anthropic` itself has (not just the three PR 1 needed), including the new `message_delta` → `stop_reason` capture, and asserts the fixture resolves to `CutoffSignal::ConfirmedCutoff` through the real `anthropic_cutoff_signal` function before asserting on the replayed wire shape. OpenRouter/Venice and Ollama fixtures in the new tests below likewise use each provider's real documented terminal-event shape (an OpenAI-compat `choices[0].finish_reason` SSE chunk; an Ollama NDJSON line with `done_reason`/`done:true`), parsed with `serde_json` rather than hand-passed enum values. **27 new backend tests**, each demonstrated failing against pre-PR2 code first (every one would have produced the "possibly cut off" message instead of the signal-specific one): 4 `anthropic_cutoff_signal` unit tests, 7 `openai_cutoff_signal` unit tests (including the two OpenClaw-gate tests proving `"stop"`/`"length"` both resolve to `Unavailable` under `RequestOrigin::OpenClaw`), 3 `ollama_cutoff_signal` unit tests, 2 new `check_args_parsed` message-selection tests (confirmed-cutoff, confirmed-normal-stop — the existing "no signal" test and mixed-batch-pairing test were updated to pass `CutoffSignal::Unavailable` explicitly, not removed), 1 `canonical_format.rs` fixture-replay update, and 10 end-to-end fixture tests (`commands.rs`'s new `cutoff_signal_fixture_tests` module) covering every provider's cut-off case and normal-stop-with-invalid-JSON case plus the OpenClaw-origin-cutoff-picks-"unsure"-not-"invalid" case by name. PR 1's 24 tests all still pass unmodified (the 2 message-selection tests above were extended with explicit signal args, not deleted/rewritten). `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.5.9 status flipped to "IN PROGRESS — 2 of 4 PRs". `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2287 passed (2260 PR 1 base + 27 new), 0 failed, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out. `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped (unaffected — backend-only change, no frontend files touched). (Relates to #2874)
- Fixed three tool-call parsers dispatching or silently dropping a tool call whose arguments were cut off (by the output-length limit) or otherwise failed to parse as JSON (#2874 item 60, PR 1 of 4, spec-covered-by: #2991, implements §4.5.9's "never run it"/"tell the agent" clauses) — **Anthropic streaming** (`anthropic.rs`): the parse-at-stream-end step used to substitute blanked `params: {}` on a parse failure and dispatch the call anyway (`add_sheet_rows` with no `rows`/`columns` would then fail its own `.ok_or(...)?` with a confusing, unrelated error, having actually run). **OpenRouter/Venice/OpenClaw streaming** (`openrouter.rs`, one shared function for all three): the parse-at-stream-end step had no `else` branch at all on a parse failure — the whole entry, `call_id` and tool name included, was silently discarded, which is what let a cut-off tool call's raw, truncated JSON fall through to the §4.5.8 text-fallback and surface as the final chat message. **Non-streaming adapter** (`adapter.rs`, both `OpenAIAdapter` and `AnthropicAdapter`): an all-or-nothing `if let (Some, Some, Some)` tuple pattern dropped `call_id` and tool name along with the arguments the moment any one of the three was missing or unparseable. All three now preserve `call_id` and tool name through a parse failure (added `ToolCall.args_parse_failed: bool`, `#[serde(default)]` for backward-compat) instead of dispatching or dropping; a new `check_args_parsed` gate (`commands.rs`, same shape and call-site position as `check_tool_offered`) refuses a flagged call before any special-case branch (`navigate`/`web_fetch`/`execute_single_tool`) can see it, returning §4.5.9's "no signal available" message verbatim as that call's `role: "tool"` result (PR 2 wires in the per-provider `stop_reason`/`finish_reason`/`done_reason` signal to pick between §4.5.9's three messages — until then every failure uses the one "possibly cut off" message). The refusal counts as a normal step against `max_tool_iterations`, same as `check_tool_offered`. Pairing stays 1:1 for a batch mixing a failed and a successful call — both the parser-level fix (every entry is still pushed to the returned `Vec<ToolCall>`, not dropped) and the gate's push-then-continue shape (identical to the existing dispatch-gate/taint-check pattern) guarantee `tool_calls.iter().zip(tool_results_for_provider.iter())` never desyncs. The Anthropic replay shape was verified against a hand-authored, protocol-accurate SSE transcript (not live-captured — no Anthropic API credential was available to this PR/session; extracting Pane's own production key from the OS keychain to make a live external call was judged out of scope for an unattended PR and is flagged as its own follow-up task) matching Anthropic's documented streaming format and the exact fields `stream_anthropic`'s SSE loop reads: the replayed `tool_use` block's `input` is confirmed to stay a JSON object (never `null`) even for a failed call, and its `id` is confirmed to equal the paired `tool_result`'s `tool_use_id` — Anthropic's strict same-turn matching requirement. Whether a genuine truncation can reach the separate **non-streaming** Anthropic adapter path was investigated but not live-tested for the same credential reason (the Messages API's non-streaming `input` is delivered already-parsed, never a truncatable JSON string, per Anthropic's documented behavior — confirmed from source, not from a live reproduction); the adapter was still defensively restructured to preserve `call_id`/name if `input` is ever absent. 24 new backend tests (6 `anthropic.rs`, 6 `openrouter.rs`, 7 `adapter.rs`, 1 `canonical_format.rs` replay-shape, 4 `commands.rs` gate/pairing), each demonstrated against the pre-fix code first — e.g. the OpenRouter truncated-args test returns 0 calls (silently dropped) at base vs. 1 (preserved, flagged) after; the adapter truncated-arguments test returns 0 calls at base vs. 1 after. `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.5.9 status flipped from NOT BUILT to "IN PROGRESS — 1 of 4 PRs". `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2259 passed (2235 base + 24 new), 1 failed (the known flake, `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert`, unrelated), 3 ignored, 11 filtered out. `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped (unaffected — backend-only change, no frontend files touched). (Relates to #2874)
- Fixed PR #2987's item 59 fix (directly above) rebuilding a cell's entire border set from the panel's `sides` array on every individual-sides apply, which deleted stored borders the user never clicked — #2874 item 59, round 2 (Matt's ruling, 2026-10-07, `docs/audits/2026-10-07-pr-2987-item59.md`). Concretely: a 3x3 block where the middle cell has its own Left border; select the block and click Top — the rebuild regenerated `bd` from the lit set plus the outer-edge check, and the middle cell's Left (not in that set, and not on any outer edge) was destroyed, even though the user clicked Top. The rebuild was wrong in principle, not just in that case: any stored side absent from the panel's currently-lit `sides` was at risk on every apply, whether or not the user had ever touched it. **Matt's ruling (authoritative, quoted in full): "A side click changes only that side. Turning a side on adds it to cells on the selection's outer edge. Turning it off removes it from every selected cell. Every other side on every cell stays exactly as stored, whether or not it's lit in the panel."** **Mechanism — how the apply learns which side was toggled, and in which direction:** `ShStylePanel.svelte`'s `handleSideClick` already computes both at the moment of the click (`base.has(s)` checked immediately before updating `borderState`'s own side set tells it the direction) — it now sends `{side, on, w, dashed}` directly via a new `onApplyBorderSide` callback instead of folding that information back into `onApplyBorder`'s full `sides` array. `SheetGrid.svelte`'s `applyStyleToSelection` gained a matching `patch.borderSide` branch that touches ONLY the named side on each selected cell: turning on adds it where the cell sits on that side's outer edge (unchanged outer-edge rule) and leaves every other stored entry completely unread; turning off filters just that one side out of every selected cell's own `existingBd`, also leaving every other entry untouched. `existingBd` (the cell's own real prior data) is never discarded wholesale in this path, unlike the rebuild it replaces. **One case still deliberately uses a full-array snapshot, not a delta:** leaving "All" mode via an individual side click. Item 53's ruling ("redraws the selection as an outline") makes this a genuine one-time full redraw — discarding "All"'s blanket inner-line fill is the CORRECT behavior there, since that fill was itself a blanket action, not per-cell preserved data — so `ShStylePanel.svelte` still routes that one transition through the existing full-snapshot `onApplyBorder` path; every other individual-sides click (not a transition) uses the new delta. **Kept, unchanged:** the echoing `updateSheetCellsStyleBatchMock` (it's what exposed this class of bug and the previous one); the three existing item-59 tests from PR #2987's head (re-verified passing under this fix); item 53's redraw-as-outline behavior for leaving "All" mode; "None" clearing everything absolutely; items 29/45's per-attribute weight/dashed click-only-what-you-clicked behavior; item 45's wait guard (unchanged — still defers ANY bare side click, on or off, while weight/dashed are indeterminate, exactly the same single condition as before, deliberately not carving out an asymmetric exception for "off" that this ruling never asked for). **Two new tests added** (`SheetGrid.test.ts`), each demonstrated failing against PR #2987's actual head (`4c7a457d`), not just the original pre-#2987 base, since that head is the code this fix replaces: TEST A — a 3x3 block where every cell shares a real, unanimous Left border; selecting the block and clicking Top left the middle cell (on no outer edge for either side) with `bd: undefined` at `4c7a457d` instead of its real `[{side:'left',...}]`. TEST B — a 2x3 block where only two cells (on the left edge) have a real Left border and one interior cell has an unrelated real Top border; after explicitly resolving weight/dashed (item 45's guard, confirmed as a no-op for the interior cell specifically) and then toggling Left off, the interior cell's real Top border came back `bd: undefined` at `4c7a457d` instead of its real `[{side:'top',w:2,dashed:true,...}]` — a side nobody clicked, on a cell this click should never have touched at all. Both pass after this fix. `docs/spec/sheets.md` §33.6.2 is rewritten (not merely amended) to describe the toggled-side rule — a side click changes only that side, preserving every other stored side regardless of panel lit-state — replacing the rebuild description the previous item-59 fix had written there, with a revision note explaining why. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, backup/migration-writing tests in `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2231 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out — unchanged from PR #2987's own head (no backend files touched, frontend-only change). `pnpm vitest run`: 2844 passed, 1 skipped (2842 at PR #2987's head + 2 new tests). (Relates to #2874)
- Fixed a sheet border side toggle leaving a stale entry for the side that was just turned off, instead of clearing it (#2874 item 59) — `SheetGrid.svelte`'s `applyStyleToSelection`, individual-sides branch: `let acc = existingBd.filter((b) => !sides.includes(b.side))` kept any stored `bd` entry whose side was absent from the new `sides` array (i.e. a side that had just been toggled off), and the add-back loop only ever iterated `sides` to re-add entries — never to remove one. A toggled-off side therefore survived indefinitely, contradicting this same function's own doc comment ("a directional side that's absent from `sides` is cleared for every cell"). Reproduces with a plain Top → Left → Top-off sequence on a single cell (ends `[top, left]` instead of `[left]`) — general to any individual-sides toggle-off, not limited to an All → individual-sides transition, per Reed's diagnosis (`docs/audits/2026-10-06-2874-items-59-61.md`). **Matt's ruling (authoritative): "In individual-sides mode, a side click changes only that side. Turning a side on adds it along the selection's outer edge; turning it off removes it from every selected cell. Other sides are untouched. Clicking a side while in All mode redraws the selection as an outline (per the 53 ruling)."** Fix: the branch's `acc` is now built fresh from `sides` plus the outer-edge check only, on every apply — `existingBd` is no longer consulted in this branch at all, so a side absent from `sides` can never survive, regardless of how many prior clicks it carried over from. A side that stays continuously active across clicks is unaffected (it was always recomputed fresh via `resolvedBorderSides`, same before and after). **Found in scope: the test mock hiding this bug.** `SheetGrid.test.ts`'s `updateSheetCellsStyleBatchMock` returned a generic blank-`style_json` cell for every batch entry instead of echoing the entry's own written `styleJson` back — the real backend (`sheets.rs:2517`) echoes the write verbatim, so every multi-click-in-one-test sequence's `existing` read was `[]` on every click after the first, never the real prior write, which is exactly the condition the bug needs to manifest. Fixed the mock to echo the written `styleJson`, then ran the full suite against it: **two existing tests failed, both confirmed as genuine app bugs reproducing this exact issue (not test problems)** — `#2874 item 29: removing one toggled side (clicking Top again) leaves the other side (Left) intact` (expected `['left']`, got `['top','left']`) and `TEST 3: toggling a side after "All" switches back to outline mode — the interior cell loses its fill (#2874 item 53)` (expected `[]`, got `[{side:'top',...}]`); both pass again after this fix, with no other test rewritten or weakened to hide the discrepancy. Three new regression tests added (`SheetGrid.test.ts`), each demonstrated failing against the pre-fix code with the echoing mock in place, each passing after the fix: TEST 1 (Top → Left → Top-off on one cell leaves only `['left']`, not `['top','left']`), TEST 2 (All → Bottom-off on one cell leaves `['top','left','right']`, not all four), TEST 3 (on a 2x3 block, a Left+Bottom+Bottom-off+Top click sequence leaves the bottom-left corner with `['left']` only, not a `['bottom','left']` ghost — proving a stale side cleared by one click doesn't resurface on a later, unrelated click either). `docs/spec/sheets.md` gains §33.6.2 (§33.6.1 was already allocated to #2874 item 45's border-unanimity-states clause; filed as the next free subsection, flagged in the PR per Build Standards §6 rather than silently renumbered). `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, migration/backup-writing tests in `tests::test_backup::` excluded per #2962): 2231 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored, 11 filtered out (matches base's 2242 passed + 3 ignored exactly, once the 11 excluded tests are added back: 2231 + 11 = 2242). `pnpm vitest run`: 2842 passed, 1 skipped (base 2839 + 3 new tests). (Relates to #2874)
- Fixed sheet tools silently dropping a non-string JSON cell value as a blank cell (#2874 item 58) — `v.as_str().unwrap_or("")` (two call sites originally flagged, a third found while fixing: `execute_set_sheet_cells`, `execute_add_sheet_row`, `execute_add_sheet_rows`, `src-tauri/src/ai/commands.rs`) returned `None` for any JSON number, boolean, array, or object value and silently fell back to `""`, so an agent that wrote `2400` or `true` into a cell saw no error and the cell stayed empty. **Matt's ruling (authoritative, quoted in full): "Numbers are saved as their text (`2400` → `"2400"`, `12.5` → `"12.5"`). Booleans are saved in the same format checkbox cells already use. Null stays blank. Arrays or objects return an error naming the row and column: the whole call fails for `add_sheet_rows`, the single cell fails for `set_sheet_cells`."** New shared helper `coerce_sheet_cell_value` (`ai/commands.rs`) is now the ONE place every sheet-value tool coerces a JSON value, so a future tool can't reintroduce this bug by copying the old `.as_str().unwrap_or("")` pattern: a string passes through unchanged; a number renders via `serde_json::Number`'s own `Display` (never routed through `.as_f64()`, so an integer literal stays `"2400"`, never `"2400.0"`, and `12.5` stays `"12.5"`, never a float-round-trip artifact like `"12.500000000000002"`); a boolean becomes `"1"`/`"0"` — the exact checkbox-column text form already on disk (`docs/spec/sheets.md` §33.3.1: "checkbox = '0'/'1'"; confirmed live against `sheetCellCommit.ts`'s `toggleCheckboxValue` and `formula/eval.rs`'s checkbox-coercion tests, the two places that already read/write that exact convention); null becomes `""` (the same sparse-delete-to-blank convention an empty string already uses); an array or object is rejected with `Err` naming the JSON type. **Error semantics intentionally diverge per tool, matching each one's own existing atomicity contract, and are NOT unified:** `set_sheet_cells` (Ruling 2026-09-04, §4.1: not all-or-nothing) collects a rejected value into that one cell's `errors` entry and keeps writing the rest of the batch; `add_sheet_rows` (all-or-nothing per its own spec) validates every value BEFORE building its row specs, so a rejected value fails the whole call with nothing created, naming the row index and column, matching the row-cap check's existing "checked before the transaction opens" posture; `add_sheet_row` (sequential chokepoint calls, Ruling 2026-09-04) fails the call at the first rejected value in its `values` map, naming the column, with the same non-atomic posture (earlier `values` entries in the same call already written are not rolled back) the rest of that tool already has. `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.1 gains a new "Sheet cell value coercion" subsection documenting the shared rule once, plus a per-tool side-effects sentence on each of the three tools' entries. Tests: 18 new backend tests (6 per tool — integer round-trip, decimal round-trip with no float artifact, boolean round-trip in a real checkbox column, null-stays-blank, object-rejected, array-rejected-like-object), each demonstrated against the pre-fix code first: 15 of the 18 fail at base (the silent-blank bug reproduces exactly as described); the 3 null-value tests pass at base too, by coincidence — `.as_str().unwrap_or("")` already happened to default null to `""` same as any other non-string, so there was nothing to demonstrate there, but the tests are kept as an explicit regression guard for Matt's "null stays blank" ruling. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, #2962): 2242 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored (2224 base + 18 new, no regressions, no flake hit this run). `pnpm vitest run`: 2839 passed, 1 skipped (unaffected — backend-only change, no frontend files touched). (Relates to #2874)
- Fixed clicking Top, Bottom, Left and Right one by one on a block lighting "All" and filling the inner grid lines instead of drawing an outline (#2874 item 53) — **Matt's ruling (authoritative): "The border panel tracks two modes: All (every line, inner lines included, All lit) and individual sides (outline only, using the existing outer-edge rule, All never lit, even with all four sides on). Two distinct modes in the panel's state (a tagged value), not a side flag. `onApplyBorder` carries the mode, and `SheetGrid` gates its four-side fast path on the mode, not on `sides.length === 4`. Clicking any single side switches to individual mode. Clicking All switches to All mode. None clears either. When the panel opens: All lights only if every selected cell has all four sides; otherwise individual sides show as today. For a single cell the two are the same result, so lighting All there is fine."** Item 29's original fix (commit `889b88d2`, PR #2923) deliberately treated "All" and "all four sides toggled on individually" as equivalent, since both produce the identical side list — `ShStylePanel.svelte`'s border state was a bare `Set<Side>` with no way to record *how* all four got set, and `SheetGrid.svelte`'s `sides.length === 4` fast path painted unconditionally on every cell (inner cells included) for either case. Matt's new ruling reverses that: **`ShStylePanel.svelte` now tracks a tagged `BorderPanelState = { mode: 'all' } | { mode: 'sides'; sides: Set<Side> }`** (same discriminated-union posture as item 45's `BorderSideResult` in `sheetCellStyle.ts`) instead of a plain `Set`. `onApplyBorder`'s wire payload gained a `mode: 'all' | 'sides'` field threaded straight from that state; `SheetGrid.svelte`'s `applyStyleToSelection` now gates its fill-everything branch on `patch.border.mode === 'all'` — never on a side count — so four individually-toggled sides fall into the unchanged outer-edge/outline branch like any other 1-3-side apply, even though the resulting `sides` array is identical to what "All" sends. Clicking any individual side (including from "All" mode) switches to `'sides'` mode; clicking "All" always sets `{ mode: 'all' }`; "None" clears to `{ mode: 'sides', sides: new Set() }`. Opening the panel on an existing selection now seeds `mode` from a new per-cell check in `SheetGrid.svelte`'s `panelBorder` derivation — `'all'` only when **every** selected cell individually has all four border sides present, `'sides'` otherwise — distinct from the existing per-side unanimity loop, which can report all four directions as "active" (unanimous or mixed) across a selection where no single cell actually has all four at once (an outline shape is the common example); for a single-cell selection the two checks always agree. **Item 29's comment documenting the old equivalence (`SheetGrid.svelte:549-553` at the time, inside `applyStyleToSelection`'s doc comment) was replaced, not merely deleted, with the new rule** — the replacement comment states, in part: "that original paragraph said, verbatim, that the 'all four sides' fast path fires whenever `sides.length === 4` ... explicitly treating the two as equivalent ... Matt's ruling reverses that: it is NOT identical. Four individually-toggled sides draw an OUTLINE ... with 'All' dark in the panel; only an EXPLICIT click on the 'All' button fills inner lines and lights 'All'. ... THIS COMMENT INTENTIONALLY STATES THE NEW RULE, not just the diff, so nobody reads old history and restores the `sides.length === 4` equivalence believing it's still correct." Does not touch item 45's mixed-display machinery, items 29/45's per-attribute weight/dashed click-only-what-you-clicked writes, or the outer-edge rule itself (`resolvedBorderSides` unchanged) — all three have dedicated unaffected test coverage, re-run and confirmed green. `docs/spec/sheets.md` §33.6.1 gains a new clause documenting the two modes and the panel-open seeding rule. Six new/updated tests: four component-level (`ShStylePanel.test.ts` — four individual clicks keep `mode:'sides'` with "All" dark; an explicit "All" click reports `mode:'all'` and lights "All"; toggling a side after "All" switches back to `mode:'sides'`; the pre-existing "All lights when all four sides are unanimous" test was split into an explicit `mode:'all'`-lights and `mode:'sides'`-stays-dark pair, since the old single assertion no longer holds without a mode) and two write-path/integration-level pairs (`SheetGrid.test.ts` — a 3x3 selection's interior cell stays borderless after four individual side clicks but gets all four sides after an explicit "All" click, and loses that fill again the instant a side is toggled afterward; and both cases of opening the panel, with a full-fill selection lighting "All" and an outline-shaped selection — where all four directions are individually non-absent but no cell has all four — correctly leaving "All" dark). All new behavior tests were confirmed failing against the pre-fix code before the fix landed. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, #2962): 2203 passed, 1 failed (the known flake, `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert` — unrelated, see #2962), 3 ignored (unaffected — frontend-only change, no Rust files touched). `pnpm vitest run`: 2839 passed, 1 skipped (+9 from baseline 2830, no regressions). (Relates to #2874)
- Fixed styling a selection of 50+ cells taking ~2 seconds and filling in cell by cell (#2874 item 51, follow-up to item 47) — `applyStyleToSelection`/`clearSelectedStyling` (`SheetGrid.svelte`) used to call `api.updateSheetCell` once PER CELL in the selection, and `update_sheet_cell_internal` runs a full-sheet `recompute_sheet` UNCONDITIONALLY on every call (item 47's accepted correctness cost) — so a 50-cell style apply was 50 separate transactions, each with its own snapshot check and full-sheet recompute. **Matt's ruling (authoritative): "Styling a selection saves all its cells in one batch with one recalculation, instead of one save and one recalculation per cell."** Backend: new `update_sheet_cells_style_batch_internal` (`sheets.rs`) follows `create_sheet_columns_batch_internal`'s shape — ONE transaction, ONE snapshot capture, a loop of raw per-cell writes, ONE recompute, ONE commit, no body regeneration (style-only writes already never regenerate the body; this is unchanged). **Two reusable pieces, named for #2970's reuse:** `upsert_sheet_cell_no_recompute` — the raw per-cell write (translate/validate/upsert), extracted verbatim from `update_sheet_cell_internal` (which now calls it, wrapped in its own unchanged transaction/snapshot/recompute/regen/commit — single-cell behavior is byte-identical) — and `recompute::recompute_sheet`, called directly for the "one recalculation at the end" instead of `recompute_and_regen` (`recompute_and_regen` always calls `regenerate_sheet_body` too, which would wrongly reintroduce body regen for a style-only batch; `recompute_sheet` is the recompute half on its own, with no new primitive needed since `recompute_and_regen` was always just these two existing pieces combined). Item 47 is unaffected: every returned cell still carries its A1-translated formula and live computed value via `translate_cells_for_display` (reused, not duplicated). Frontend: `applyStyleToSelection`/`clearSelectedStyling` now compute each cell's style payload exactly as before (items 29/45/53's per-attribute resolution, the outer-edge gate, and `resolvedBorderSides` are all UNCHANGED — only how the writes are delivered changed) and send them all in ONE `api.updateSheetCellsStyleBatch` call instead of N `updateSheetCell` calls; a new `applyLocalCellPatches` helper patches every returned cell into local state in one pass instead of looping the existing single-cell patcher. Tests: 9 new backend tests (`sheets.rs`, incl. a test-only recompute call counter in `formula/recompute.rs` proving a 12-cell batch recomputes exactly once, vs. 3 calls for 3 unbatched single-cell writes; a mid-batch-failure rollback test; one-snapshot-for-the-batch; no-body-regen; item 47 reply-shape compliance; cross-sheet-entry rejection; and a single-cell-path regression guard for the extraction refactor). Frontend: 21 pre-existing `toHaveBeenCalledTimes` assertions in `SheetGrid.test.ts` pinning the old per-cell call count were rewritten to assert the new one-batch-call shape instead (a new `batchEntry` test helper replaces the old `mock.calls.find(...)` per-cell lookup), plus 1 new multi-cell test proving `clearSelectedStyling` also sends one call per action, not one per cell. `docs/spec/sheets.md` §33.6 gains a new paragraph stating batched style applies recalculate once per apply. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, #2962): 2203 passed, 1 failed (pre-existing, environmental — `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert`, a loopback-TLS test that fails only under full-suite port contention and passes consistently in isolation on both this branch and origin/main; confirmed unrelated to this change), 3 ignored. `pnpm vitest run`: 2830 passed, 1 skipped. (Relates to #2874)
- Fixed flipped sheet popovers clipping off the TOP of the window at a short window height (#2874 item 57) — Reed's audit of PR #2976 (item 52) found the flip-up fix had no lower bound: at a mid-screen row, flipping a popover up from `rect.top`/the raw click `y` could still land above `y = 0` and clip off the top, since neither `openStylePanel`'s two branches nor `ShCellContextMenu`'s `posTop` ever checked the flipped result against the top of the window — only the bottom overflow (the flip trigger itself) and the horizontal overflow were clamped. Inherited from `ShCellContextMenu.svelte`'s original pattern and carried into `openStylePanel` verbatim by item 52's port; not a new regression. **Matt's ruling (authoritative): "Add a floor so neither can go above the top of the window: `Math.max(0, …)` on the flipped position, in both branches of `openStylePanel` and in `ShCellContextMenu`'s `posTop`. Same shape as the existing horizontal clamp."** Three sites fixed, each wrapping only the flipped-branch expression in `Math.max(0, …)` — the non-flipped (below) position in each is untouched, exactly mirroring how the horizontal clamp wraps only its own overflow branch: `SheetGrid.svelte`'s `openStylePanel` anchor branch (`y = flipUp ? Math.max(0, rect.top - 4 - PANEL_HEIGHT) : rect.bottom + 4`), its raw-point branch (`flipUp ? Math.max(0, point.y - PANEL_HEIGHT) : point.y`), and `ShCellContextMenu.svelte`'s `posTop` (`flipUp ? Math.max(0, y - MENU_HEIGHT) : y`). Three tests added, one per site, each demonstrated failing against the pre-fix code first: `SheetGrid.test.ts`'s anchor branch at a 600px window height with a mid-screen row (`rect.top: 300`) flips up to `-9px` at base, clamped to `0px`; its raw-point branch at the same 600px height with a mid-screen point (`y: 300`) flips up to `-5px` at base, clamped to `0px`; `ShCellContextMenu.test.ts`'s `posTop` at a 400px window height with a mid-screen point (`y: 200`) flips up to `-57px` at base, clamped to `0px` (400px rather than 600px because `MENU_HEIGHT` (257) is more than half of 600, so the flip-trigger and negative-result ranges never overlap at exactly 600px for this menu — 400px, already used by this file's own pre-existing flip-up test, is the smallest window that genuinely reproduces the unbounded-flip bug for a mid-screen rather than near-bottom point). All four of item 52's existing flip tests (anchor low/normal, raw-point low/normal) and `ShCellContextMenu.test.ts`'s own existing flip-left/flip-up tests remain green, confirming the floor does not disturb the legitimate flip cases where there is room above. No spec section covers popover positioning (`docs/spec/sheets.md` searched, confirmed absent, same finding item 52 made). `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, #2962): 2195 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (unaffected — frontend-only change, no Rust files touched). `pnpm vitest run`: 2829 passed, 1 skipped. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: pure positioning/UX fix, no data model or write path involved, no spec section covers it)
- Fixed the sheet style panel running off the bottom of the window when opened near a low row, clipping the border weight row (#2874 item 52) — **Matt's ruling (authoritative): "When the style panel would run past the bottom of the window, it flips up and opens above the cell."** `openStylePanel` (`SheetGrid.svelte`) computed the panel's vertical position as an unconditional `rect.bottom + 4` (anchor branch) or the raw click `y` (raw-point branch, opened from the right-click context menu's "Style cells…" row) with no check against `window.innerHeight` at all — only the horizontal overflow already had a clamp. Ported `ShCellContextMenu.svelte`'s own `flipUp`/`posTop`/`MENU_HEIGHT` triplet (the one existing vertical-flip pattern in the codebase, same `typeof window !== 'undefined'`-guarded, SSR-safe shape) into both branches: a new static `PANEL_HEIGHT = 305` constant, measured the same way `MENU_HEIGHT` was — the real rendered `.sh-sty` panel (all three sections plus the "Clear styling" button; none conditionally rendered, so the height is constant regardless of prop state) measured 268x304.875px via a headless-browser render of the actual component, rounded up to 305. The existing horizontal clamp (`x + PANEL_WIDTH > window.innerWidth`) is unchanged. Four tests added to `SheetGrid.test.ts` covering both doors: anchor branch low row (flips up, demonstrated failing against the pre-fix code at `top: 732px` before being fixed to `391px`) and normal row (stays below, no regression); raw-point branch low point (flips up, `700px` → `395px`) and normal point (stays put, no regression). The existing horizontal-flip test is unaffected. No spec section covers the style panel's positioning (`docs/spec/sheets.md` §33.6/§33.6.1 searched — anchoring/palette/border-unanimity only, nothing about viewport clamping), so none was amended. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, #2962): 2195 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (unaffected — frontend-only change, no Rust files touched). `pnpm vitest run`: 2826 passed, 1 skipped. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: pure positioning/UX fix, no data model or write path involved, no spec section covers it)
- Fixed a borderless sheet selection lighting the weight-1 button in the style panel alongside "None" (#2874 item 54) — **Matt's ruling (authoritative): "On a borderless selection only None lights; no weight button does. Gate the weight (and dashed) buttons' lit state on `activeSides.size > 0` in `ShStylePanel.svelte`. `borderWeight` stays seeded at 1 underneath, so clicking a side on a plain cell still applies immediately; tests must show both."** The distinction is between the ACTIVE VALUE `borderWeight`/`borderDashed` hold (seeded to `1`/`false` so a side click on a borderless cell still applies immediately at a sane default) and the LIT INDICATOR (`is-on`), which must not light off that seed when nothing is actually active. `ShStylePanel.svelte`'s weight and dashed buttons now gate `class:is-on` on `activeSides.size > 0`, in addition to the existing value-equality check; `borderWeight`/`borderDashed` themselves are untouched, so `handleSideClick`'s existing `weightDashedResolved` guard (already `true` at the seeded default) continues to apply a side click immediately with no further change. Two tests added to `ShStylePanel.test.ts` cover both halves of Matt's ruling: a borderless selection (`currentBorder: null`, and separately `sides: []`) shows only "None" lit and no weight/dashed button lit (before this fix, weight-1 and dashed both carried `is-on` too — demonstrated failing against the pre-fix code, then fixed); and clicking a side on that same borderless selection still fires `onApplyBorder` immediately with `{ sides: ['top'], w: 1, dashed: false }`, proving the seed itself was never cleared. No regression: the existing "seeds the border side/weight from currentBorder" (unanimous weight lights) and "mixed weights... show NO active weight button" (item 45 mixed-selection behavior) tests are unaffected, since both already have `activeSides.size > 0`. `docs/spec/sheets.md` §33.6.1's "Unanimous-none" clause is corrected to state the default is held as the underlying value but not shown as lit when borderless — the prior text documented the buggy lit behavior as correct. `cargo check` clean; `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, #2962): 2195 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (unaffected — frontend-only change, no Rust files touched). `pnpm vitest run`: 2824 passed, 1 skipped. (Relates to #2874)
- Fixed typing into a ghost column forcing the column-rename input open and swallowing every keystroke after the first (#2874 item 44) — **Matt's ruling (authoritative, §33.3.5 amendment, #2966): "Typing into a ghost column never opens the column rename input. After the commit, the cell editor stays open on the new cell with the typed character in it, so typing continues in the cell exactly as it does for a ghost row. The new column keeps its empty name until the user renames it from the header menu (right-click → Rename). The same applies when a row and a column are both ghosts. Supersedes PR 10's rename-on-birth for ghost typing."** `beginGhostCommit`'s `isGhostCol` branch (`SheetGrid.svelte`) unconditionally called `startHeaderRename(newColIdx)`, whose `autofocus`ed empty rename input stole keyboard focus mid-keystroke — any further characters landed in the rename field instead of the cell, so the cell kept only the first typed character and the column got silently renamed to the rest. This is PR 10's original, deliberate day-one design (`git log -S startHeaderRename` shows exactly two touches, neither of which changed this branch) — not a regression, confirmed in the 2026-09-23 items 42-50 diagnosis. Fix: the ghost-column and both-ghost cases now reopen the cell editor with the typed character, identically to the existing ghost-row-only case — all three cases share one code path. `startHeaderRename` itself is unchanged and still reachable from its two other, unaffected callers: `insertColumn()` (the toolbar/context-menu explicit "add column" action's own birth-moment rename, out of scope for this ruling) and the header menu's Rename row (right-click → Rename, the sole sanctioned rename path per §33.3.5, confirmed still working with dedicated coverage). Seven tests added/updated in `SheetGrid.test.ts`: two existing ghost-column-commit tests rewritten to assert the rename input never renders and the cell editor opens instead (case 2 offset-1, case 3 both-ghost); two header-rename-mechanics tests re-pointed from the now-removed ghost-typing entry path to the header-menu entry path; three new dedicated tests asserting each of the four §33.3.5 requirements, including one asserting the typed character's actual value and `document.activeElement` on the reopened editor (not merely "no rename input rendered"), and one confirming the new column keeps `name: ''` until a header-menu rename explicitly changes it. `cargo test` in `src-tauri/` (`--test-threads=1`, #2962): 2195 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (unaffected — frontend-only change). `pnpm vitest run`: 2821 passed, 1 skipped. (Relates to #2874, spec-covered-by: #2966)
- Fixed the date column type icon (📅) to the letter D, matching the T on text columns (#2874 item 48) — **Matt's ruling (authoritative): "The date column type icon changes from 📅 to the letter D, matching the T on text columns, on both surfaces."** Both independent duplications of the six-case glyph switch were updated: `sheetTypeGlyph` in `Card.svelte` (the card micro-grid) and the shared `typeGlyph` in `sheetCellRender.ts` (consumed by both `SheetGrid.svelte`'s live grid and `ShSnapshotPreview.svelte`'s version-history preview — no code change needed there, confirmed by re-reading both call sites). Confirmed no 📅 remains anywhere in `src/` (`grep -rn '📅' src/` returns empty). Two tests that pinned the old emoji were updated to expect `'D'`: `sheetCellRender.test.ts` and `Card.sheet-face.test.ts`. No spec section documents the glyph set, so none was updated. `cargo test` in `src-tauri/`: 2195 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (unaffected — frontend-only change). `pnpm vitest run`: 2816 passed, 1 skipped. (Relates to #2874)
- Fixed the sheet style panel showing a false unanimity ("None" and weight "1" both highlighted) for a mixed border selection (#2874 item 45) — `detectBorderUnanimity` (`sheetCellStyle.ts`) used to return `BorderUnanimity | null`, collapsing two opposite situations into the same `null`: "no cell has this side" and "cells disagree on this side" (including one cell bordered, one not). It now returns a real three-state result (`{state:'none'}` / `{state:'unanimous', w, c, dashed}` / `{state:'mixed'}`), and `panelBorder` (`SheetGrid.svelte`) includes any non-absent (unanimous OR mixed) side in the sides it reports, so the side button stays lit for a mixed side while "None" and every weight/dashed control stay dark — **Matt's ruling (authoritative, 2026-09-24, quoted in full): "When cells disagree on a side (including one bordered, one not), the side button stays lit and None and all weights stay dark. Guard against a click resetting the cells to weight 1."** `ShStylePanel.svelte`'s `handleSideClick` now defers `applyCurrentBorder()` while weight/dashed are still indeterminate (a plain side toggle no longer silently falls back to `w: 1`/`dashed: false` and clobbers real per-cell weights) — the apply proceeds only once the user explicitly resolves the ambiguity via a weight/dashed click, or via the absolute "All"/"None" actions. The already-shipped CROSS-side indeterminate-weight behavior (item 29, two different unanimous sides disagreeing with each other) is untouched. **Six existing `sheetCellStyle.test.ts` unit tests that pinned the old collapsing behavior as correct were rewritten** (not merely supplemented) to assert the new three-state shape: "returns null when cells have different widths on the same side", "returns null when cells have different colors on the same side", "returns null when one cell has the border and another does not", "respects dashed as part of the unanimity comparison", the `left`-side assertion inside "checks only the requested side, ignoring other borders on the same cells", and "returns the shared border spec when every cell agrees on that side" (shape-only, still unanimous). New coverage added at both the unit level (`sheetCellStyle.test.ts`) and the `SheetGrid`/`ShStylePanel` integration level (`SheetGrid.test.ts`): unanimous weight across multiple cells, unanimous none across a multi-cell selection, mixed weights on the same side, one cell bordered/one plain on the same side, and the click-through guard. `docs/spec/sheets.md` §33.6 gains a new §33.6.1 documenting the three unanimity states and their panel rendering. (Relates to #2874)
- Fixed the sheet style panel's border-click guard (item 45's own PR, #2963) only covering the side-toggle path, leaving a bare weight or dashed click free to silently clobber real per-cell weights — reproduced live by Reed's delta audit (`docs/audits/2026-09-24-pr-2963-item45.md`): from a same-side mixed-weight selection (item 45's own new state), clicking the dashed toggle fired `applyCurrentBorder()`'s shared `w: borderWeight ?? 1` fallback, writing `w: 1` over both cells' real, differing weights — the exact clobber Matt's original guard ruling prohibited, just reached through the other button. The same root mechanism already affected #2874 item 29's older cross-side case (Top unanimously 2px, Left unanimously 1px — clicking dashed collapsed both to weight 1). **Matt's ruling on the fix (authoritative, quoted in full): "A click in the border panel changes only what was clicked, and every cell keeps its own value for everything else. Clicking dashed on a mixed selection makes each cell dashed while keeping its own weight and color; clicking a weight works the same way for dashed. No overwrites, no dead clicks. Side-button clicks keep the wait guard as built."** `ShStylePanel.svelte`'s `handleWeightClick`/`handleDashedClick` no longer route through `applyCurrentBorder()`'s shared-value apply at all — they now fire dedicated `onApplyBorderWeight`/`onApplyBorderDashed` callbacks carrying only the one attribute actually clicked, and `SheetGrid.svelte`'s `applyStyleToSelection` resolves the write per cell, per side, preserving each cell's own existing weight/color (for a dashed click) or dashed/color (for a weight click) instead of the panel's shared, possibly-indeterminate state. `handleSideClick` (the side-toggle/"All"/"None" path) is UNCHANGED, per Matt's ruling — it still keeps its own already-shipped wait guard. Three new tests added (`SheetGrid.test.ts`): a dashed click on a same-side mix, a weight click on a same-side mix, and a dashed click on the item-29 cross-side mix — each demonstrated failing against the pre-fix code before being fixed. `docs/spec/sheets.md` §33.6.1's closing paragraph is rewritten for the per-attribute write model. (Relates to #2874, item 29 and item 45)
- Fixed a second regression in the border-click guard fix directly above (#2963) — Reed's second delta audit (`docs/audits/2026-09-24-pr-2963-delta2.md`) found that the per-attribute rewrite above dropped outer-edge geometry checking from the weight/dashed handlers' new default-creation branch entirely: on a partial-presence mixed selection (one cell bordered, one plain on the same side — the state item 45's own PR itself defines and tests), a weight or dashed click could silently create a brand-new border on a non-edge cell that never had one, something the pre-fix `patch.border` full-apply path correctly refused to do. **Matt's ruling on the fix (authoritative, quoted in full): "In the border panel's weight and dashed handlers, a new border may only be created on a cell that's on the selection's outer edge for that side. Use the same `resolvedBorderSides` check the full-apply path uses. Existing borders keep their own values regardless of position, as now. When a side is lit because only some cells have it, a weight or dashed click fills that border in along the outer edge, the same as clicking the side would. It never adds borders to inner cells and never changes values that weren't clicked."** `SheetGrid.svelte`'s `applyStyleToSelection` (`borderWeight`/`borderDashed` branches) now gates the default-creation path (a side with no existing per-cell entry) behind the same `resolvedBorderSides(...).includes(side)` check the `patch.border` branch already uses — a cell that already has a real entry for the side is still updated per-attribute regardless of position (that carve-out, and the original clobber fix, are unchanged). Two new tests added (`SheetGrid.test.ts`): a vertical partial-presence mix (weight click leaves the inner, never-bordered cell plain — demonstrated failing against the pre-fix code, then fixed) and a horizontal partial-presence mix (weight click fills the top border in on both cells, since both sit on the selection's outer edge). `docs/spec/sheets.md` §33.6.1 gains a closing paragraph documenting the outer-edge rule for newly-created borders. (Relates to #2874, item 29 and item 45)
- Fixed the sheet grid's style-only save reply (border/fill/ink apply, clear styling) returning the raw internal-ID formula string and always dropping `computed_value` to `None` for a formula cell, instead of the readable A1 formula and its live computed value (#2874 item 47) — `SheetGrid.svelte:650` compared the client's A1-translated cached form (`=SUM(B1:B5)`) against the style-write response's untranslated internal-ID form (`=SUM({714fc3ac-64…`), which never match for any formula cell, so the client-side `preserveComputedValueOnStyleOnlyWrite` guard always fell through and exposed the raw stored formula. Reproduces in plain human usage (no agent involvement needed): type a formula, let it refetch/translate to A1 form, then style any cell containing it. **Matt's ruling (authoritative): "The style-only save reply carries the readable formula and its computed value. I accept the recompute cost."** This extends item 25's rule (every save reply carries the computed value, so the grid never guesses) to the one remaining gap item 27's client-side patch only papered over, and deletes that patch outright. Backend: `update_sheet_cell_internal` (the sole cell-write chokepoint, `src-tauri/src/sheets.rs`) now runs a full `recompute::recompute_sheet` pass UNCONDITIONALLY on every write (previously gated on `value_changed`, an item 25 PR-amendment optimization this ruling explicitly reverses — computed values are never persisted, ADR-0066 D4, so there is no cheaper cache to consult instead) and translates the returned cell's `raw_value` through `translate_cells_for_display` (REUSED, not duplicated — the same function `get_sheet_data_internal` already calls for every read) before returning it, so every write's reply — style-only or value-changing — carries the same A1 display form and live computed value a subsequent read would show. Body regeneration (`notes.body`) remains gated on `value_changed` only, unchanged (Matt ruling 2026-09-03: a pure style change never touches `notes.body`/`updated_at`). Frontend: `preserveComputedValueOnStyleOnlyWrite` is deleted outright from `SheetGrid.svelte`; both call sites (`applyStyleToSelection`, `clearSelectedStyling`) now apply the backend's reply directly via `applyLocalCellPatch`, a straight trust-the-reply patch matching the shape `commitCellValue` already uses — no refetch added or needed, since a style-only write cannot affect other cells' computed values. `docs/spec/sheets.md` §33.5.2/§33.5.4/§33.6 updated in this same PR to state the uniform write-reply contract and the accepted recompute-cost trade-off explicitly. `cargo test` in `src-tauri/`: 2195 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored. `pnpm vitest run`: 2803 passed, 1 skipped. (Relates to #2874)
- Fixed pane-gateway unconditionally overwriting `body["model"]` to bare `"openclaw"` on every `/v1/chat/completions` request, discarding any agent-scoped model Pane's client sends (ADR-0067 D3, part 1 of 2; relates to #2900) — `src-gateway/src/routes/chat.rs` now passes an already agent-scoped model (`openclaw/<agentId>`, `openclaw:<agentId>`, or `agent:<agentId>`) through unchanged and rewrites to bare `"openclaw"` only when the incoming model is bare, absent, or a stale catalog id. **This alone does not fix the reported 400** — the currently-installed app still sends bare `"openclaw"` and is unaffected until the app half (part 2, a separate PR) ships the agent-scoped selector; a mandatory non-regression test (`test_non_regression_bare_openclaw_still_stamped_openclaw`, plus absent-model and stale-catalog-id siblings) locks in that an old-app request is stamped `"openclaw"` byte-for-byte identically to today, which is what makes shipping the gateway ahead of the app safe. The param-compat strip-table lookup (§4A.2.2 "Model Resolution for Stripping") also now resolves against the agent named by an incoming `openclaw/<agentId>` selector instead of always hardcoding `"main"` — verified via new tests asserting the `X-OC-Resolved-Model` response header reflects the selected agent, not main, when the two agents have different configured models (a #1323-class param-strip regression avoided from the other direction). Also replaced a 4-OC-version-stale test fixture in `src-gateway/src/agents.rs` that asserted a top-level `"defaultId"` field OC does not send and was missing a fifth agent, with a fixture matching the live OC 2026.8.2 `agents.list` capture recorded in `docs/spec/sync.md` §22C.10 (per-agent `isDefault`, five agents, no top-level `defaultId`). Gateway-only change — `src-tauri/` and `src/` untouched; the Tauri app half (client-side `openclaw/<agentId>` stamping, `runtime_ref` resolver plumbing, gateway-4xx error classification, default-agent-resolution order) ships in a separate PR per ADR-0067 D6's deployment order. `cargo test` in `src-gateway/`: 204 passed, 0 failed (18 new tests added by this PR: 10 pure unit tests for the selector-parsing helpers, 7 integration tests exercising the real `chat_completions` handler end-to-end with a mock OC backend, 1 new fixture-deserialization test). (Relates to #2900, spec-covered-by: #2956)
- Fixed the app half of ADR-0067 (relates to #2900, spec-covered-by: #2956) — Pane now stamps `openclaw/<runtime_ref>` on every OC dispatch path instead of the bare `"openclaw"` sentinel the gateway-half PR (#2957) was waiting on, and the previously-diverged non-streaming vs. streaming stamping behavior is unified behind one shared helper (`openrouter::oc_wire_model`). **`ai_agents.id` (Pane's local UUID) never reaches the wire** — `RuntimeConfig`/`AiProvider::OpenClaw` carry `runtime_ref: Option<String>` as a field distinct from `agent_id`, and every one of the six dispatch sites (`ai_chat_stream`'s 8 streaming call sites, plus consolidator/check_contradiction/`ai_synthesize_memory`/`ai_consolidate_memory`/`ai_synthesize_all_memories_impl`'s non-streaming calls) threads `runtime_ref` explicitly rather than reusing the adjacent `agent_id` field; `NULL` runtime_ref (local/AI-created agents, legacy OC rows) still produces bare `"openclaw"`, never `"openclaw/null"`. Two session-scoped internal callers (daily-narrative generation, thread compaction) source `runtime_ref` from their own already-resolved agent/session config rather than the default-agent resolver, per ADR-0067 D2. Also: gateway 4xx responses (most commonly OC's 400 "Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner" error) now classify as a new `gateway_provider_error` code — never retried, and the frontend (`streamManager.ts`) now surfaces OC's own message text verbatim instead of a generic locked string that previously discarded it; 401/402/403 keep their existing specific codes ahead of this new generic-4xx branch, and 5xx/transport errors are unaffected (`docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4A.2.5 flips from SPEC'D to BUILT). Also: the three-step default-agent resolution order (OC's reported per-agent `isDefault` → a prior Settings choice → `runtime_ref == "main"`) is now a single shared function (`sync_client::resolve_should_be_default`) used by both `sync_re_import` and `sync_initial_import`, replacing independently-hand-rolled `oc_id == "main"` heuristics; `GatewayAgent`/the gateway's `/v1/sync/initial` response now carry the `is_default` field the gateway-half PR forwards (tier 1 — correct but dormant on OC 2026.8.2, since every agent currently reports `isDefault: false`; tier 2, an existing Settings choice, remains the live production path, and tier 3 is the first-run fallback, both unchanged in observable behavior from before this fix). `cargo test` in `src-tauri/`: 2185 passed, 0 failed. `cargo test` in `src-gateway/`: 208 passed, 0 failed (untouched by this PR). `pnpm vitest run`: 2802 passed, 1 skipped. **Deployment order:** the gateway commit (#2957) already redeployed to the Studio; this app-half PR's DMG build ships second, per ADR-0067 D6.
- Fixed opening a note silently marking it dirty and triggering a spurious save + `pane-data-changed` dispatch even when the user never edited anything (#2950). Two independent triggers were found and fixed:
  1. `AttachmentImageInline.svelte`'s `handleImageLoad()` persists an inline image's natural width/height the first time it loads (when the node's `width`/`height` attrs are still `null`). That persist fires asynchronously from the native `<img>` `load` event, which can land after `Editor.svelte` has already reset its `isSettingContent` guard — so the write was tripping `onUpdate` and setting `dirty = true` exactly like a real user edit. It now passes a new `{ skipDirty: true }` option through `Attachment.ts`'s `updateAttrs`, which tags the ProseMirror transaction with TipTap's own `preventUpdate` meta key (the same mechanism `setContent({ emitUpdate: false })` uses internally) — the document still updates and the NodeView still re-renders with the persisted dims, only the dirty-marking is suppressed. Real user edits (drag-resize via `onDragEnd`, render-mode change via `handleModeChange`) do not pass this option and continue to mark the editor dirty and save normally.
  2. Separately, `Editor.svelte`'s `$effect` that syncs TipTap's editable state (`editor.setEditable(!isReadOnly)`) was calling TipTap's `setEditable` with its default `emitUpdate = true`, which unconditionally emits an `update` event (with an empty, zero-step transaction) on every single Editor mount, regardless of attachments — independently tripping the same spurious dirty/save path on every note opened. Now calls `editor.setEditable(!isReadOnly, false)` since toggling editable state is never itself a content change.
  (Relates to #2950, spec-skip: behavioral fix, no spec surface change)
- Fixed the Kanban board's note editor destroying and recreating itself on every `pane-data-changed` event (#2951) — PR #2929 (#2874 item 34) added a `pane-data-changed` listener that calls `KanbanBoard.svelte`'s `loadTasks()`, which sets `loading = true` at the top of the function and back to `false` when it finishes. The entire editor panel used to live inside `{#if loading}{:else}`, so every reload unmounted and remounted the `<Editor>` component — even though the open note's id never changed — which could itself trigger a fresh save, re-dispatch `pane-data-changed`, and loop. The `{#if loading}/{:else}` gate now only wraps the kanban columns/card list inside `.kanban-left-panel`; the editor panel renders directly off `{#if $activeNote}` as a sibling, independent of `loading`, matching the pattern `NotesBrowser.svelte` already uses for its own editor. The `pane-data-changed` listener itself is unchanged and still needed for the #2874 item 34 sheet-delete-refresh fix. (Relates to #2951, spec-skip: structural fix, no spec surface change)
- **Tests:** KeychainGuard RAII type with panic-safe teardown, `keychain_override` serial group across 189 tests, memory_router poison recovery (#2903)
- Fixed test safety: sync deadlock test no longer migrates the real production database during test runs (#2946)
- Fixed test safety: backup/restore tests now use `MockKeychain` and isolated `PANE_TEST_ROOT` temp directories — no test can touch the real `~/Pane` installation or the real macOS keychain (#2903)
- Fixed test isolation: 25 tests now use proper `#[serial]` guards and per-test temp directories, eliminating filesystem collisions during parallel test runs
- Fixed a remaining PANE_TEST_ROOT env-var race across the rest of the crate: unified all `#[serial]` usages onto a single crate-wide `pane_test_root` serial group so every test that reads or writes the `PANE_TEST_ROOT` env var is mutually exclusive with every other one, eliminating cross-test filesystem collisions that weren't already covered by the backup test safety pass above (#2903)
- Fixed checked checkbox cells in the sheet grid rendering as an empty filled box with no glyph inside (#2874 item 39) — a checked `.sh-box` now renders an inline SVG check mark (a simple tick, matching the codebase's existing inline-SVG icon convention) inside the box. The glyph uses `stroke="currentColor"`, which inherits the existing `.sh-box` / `.sh-box.is-on` `color` rules unchanged (`color: transparent` unchecked, `color: var(--accent)` checked) — no new CSS color values were introduced; these two properties were previously dead code with no text content to colorize, and are now finally functional. `ShSnapshotPreview.svelte` was checked and does not render checkbox cells via `.sh-box` (it renders raw cell text for every column type), so it needed no corresponding change. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: UI visual change, no spec change)
- Fixed currency cells in the sheet grid rendering the raw stored decimal value followed by a small ISO currency code label (e.g. `930 USD`) instead of a conventionally formatted currency string (#2874 item 38) — currency cells now render via `Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', { style: 'currency', ... })`, e.g. `$930.00`. New shared `currencyCode()`/`formatCurrencyValue()` helpers in `src/lib/utils/sheetCellRender.ts` consolidate what were previously two independent currency-lookup implementations (`SheetGrid.svelte`'s own private `currencyCode()`, and `ShSnapshotPreview.svelte`'s own private `currencyCode()`, which read the wrong `options_json` key and never actually matched) into one source of truth that both the live grid and the version-history snapshot preview (`ShSnapshotPreview.svelte`) import. The `.sh-cur` ISO-code span is removed from cells only — the column header's own `.sh-h__code` code label is unchanged. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: UI formatting change, no spec change)
- Fixed the Version History preview showing every formula cell's raw stored formula text (e.g. `=14/0`, or a formula literally containing internal `{column_id:row_id}` references) instead of the value the formula would actually evaluate to (#2874 item 32) — a user browsing version history now sees computed values (`14/0` renders as `#DIV/0!`, a `SUM` formula renders as its numeric total) matching what the live grid would show, never internal IDs. New backend: `formula::recompute::compute_envelope_values` (a DB-free sibling of `recompute_sheet`, sharing its parse/graph/cycle-detect/evaluate pipeline via a new `compute_from_snapshot` helper and `SheetSnapshot::from_parts` constructor) and `sheets_snapshots::get_sheet_snapshot_computed_values` (new Tauri command) recompute a historical snapshot envelope's formula cells for DISPLAY ONLY — nothing is ever written back to `note_versions.content` (ADR-0066 D4 fully preserved). `ShVersionHistoryPanel.svelte` fetches computed values alongside each version's raw content (with a monotonic request-token guard against out-of-order responses) and passes them to `ShSnapshotPreview.svelte`, which now renders a formula cell's computed value when present; if no computed entry exists yet (in-flight fetch, fetch failure, or genuinely missing), the cell renders EMPTY with its formula wedge indicator still shown — never the raw stored formula string, and never an internal column/row ID, under any circumstance. (Relates to #2874)
- Fixed every Sheets popover's outside-click handler being able to misjudge a detached (already-removed) click target as "outside" and incorrectly close/cancel (#2874 item 30) — when a popover's own click handler synchronously removes its clicked element from the DOM (a mode/view flip, deleting a list item, etc.), the still-bubbling click event keeps its original `e.target`, but that node's `isConnected` becomes `false` the instant it leaves the document, making any `contains()`-based inside/outside check against it meaningless. Each of the six sheet popovers' window-level `handleWindowClick` handlers (`SheetCellEditorSelect.svelte`, `ShHeaderMenu.svelte`, `ShSheetMenu.svelte`, `ShCellContextMenu.svelte`, `ShGhostCellContextMenu.svelte`, `ShStylePanel.svelte`) now bail out early with `if (e.target instanceof Node && !e.target.isConnected) return;` before their existing logic runs, rather than misreading a detached target as an outside click. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: bug fix, no spec change)
- Fixed keyboard focus silently falling off the Sheets grid after closing a cell editor (#2874 item 36) — committing an edit with Enter/Tab/Shift-Tab, cancelling with Escape, or picking/cancelling a select-column dropdown choice all unmount the currently-focused editor element; per the DOM spec that drops focus to `<body>` instead of back to the grid, so the very next arrow-key press or typed character silently did nothing until the user clicked a cell. `SheetGrid.svelte` now has a `refocusGrid()` helper (`gridEl?.focus()`) called from `handleEditorCommit` (only for the `'enter'`/`'tab'`/`'shift-tab'` causes), `handleEditorCancel`, `handleSelectCommit`, and `handleSelectCancel`. Deliberately excluded: `handleEditorCommit`'s `'blur'` cause — a blur means the user clicked somewhere else on purpose, and focus correctly stays there instead of being yanked back to the grid. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: bug fix, no spec change)
- Fixed deleting a sheet from the ⋯ menu ('Delete sheet') appearing to do nothing on the Kanban board (#2874 item 34) — the backend delete succeeded and the note-detail panel closed, but the deleted sheet's card stayed visibly stuck on the board until some unrelated action (e.g. creating a new note) happened to trigger a reload. `KanbanBoard.svelte` now listens for the `pane-data-changed` window event (already dispatched by `Editor.svelte`'s delete flow) in `onMount`/`onDestroy` and reloads via the existing `loadTasks`, matching the same pattern `NotesBrowser.svelte` and `AllTasksView.svelte` already use. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: bug fix, no spec change)

## [1.0.54] - 2026-09-13

### Removed
- Removed the New Sheet button (and its collapsed-header caret variant) from the All Tasks view (#2874 item 1) — New Sheet was never built here to begin with in the New Note pattern this view already followed for note creation; it now matches that same "no creation button" posture instead of gating an existing button behind a conditional. `AllTasksView.svelte`'s New-Sheet-only state (`sheetProjectPickerOpen`, `creatingSheet`, `headerButtonMode`, etc.), handlers (`handleCreateNewSheet`, `openSheetProjectPicker`, `handleNewSheetFromCaret`), the header-width `ResizeObserver`, and all supporting CSS are removed. `src/lib/utils/newSheetButtonLayout.ts` is untouched — KanbanBoard and NotesBrowser still use it for their own New Sheet buttons. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: UI element removal, no spec change needed)
- Removed the "Export sheet as CSV…" row from the sheet grid's right-click cell context menu (`ShCellContextMenu.svelte`) (#2874 item 11) — CSV export remains available from the sheet's "more actions" (⋯) menu (`ShSheetMenu.svelte`), which keeps its own independent Export CSV row on a separate code path. `SheetGrid.svelte`'s pass-through of `onExportCsv` into `ShCellContextMenu` is removed; the `onExportCsv` prop on `SheetGrid` itself is unchanged and still wires the toolbar's own Export CSV action. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: UI element removal, no spec change needed)

### Changed
- Sheet cell border side buttons (Top/Btm/Left/Rgt) in the styling panel are now independent toggles instead of a single-select control — clicking Top no longer discards a previously-selected Left, so a cell can have both a top AND a left border applied via two separate clicks (#2874 item 29). "All" and "None" remain absolute actions (always sets all four sides / always clears all four), not toggles. When a multi-cell selection has sides that agree on which sides are bordered but disagree on weight or dashed style, neither the weight nor dashed control highlights anything (indeterminate state) rather than guessing. No backend or stored-data changes — the underlying `bd` array already supported multiple border sides per cell.

### Fixed
- Fixed text-column sort using plain lexicographic (`<`/`>`) string comparison instead of natural numeric-aware ordering (#2874 item 24) — sorting a text column with values like `"3"`, `"7"`, `"34"` previously produced `"3" < "34" < "7"`; `compareValid` now has a dedicated `case 'text':` branch using `a.localeCompare(b, undefined, { numeric: true })`, giving natural ordering (`3 < 7 < 34`) and correctly ordering mixed alpha-numeric values (`"Item 3" < "Item 7" < "Item 34"`). `select` columns are unchanged and still use the old plain lexicographic `default` branch — only `text` moved. Number/currency/date/checkbox comparators, and all empty/null "sorts last" handling in `isValidForSort`, are untouched. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: behavioral fix on existing sort infrastructure, no spec change)
- Fixed column header left-click also opening the header menu ("one click, both effects") when it should only select the column (#2874 item 10 amendment). Per §33.3.6 (PR #2924, commit `e7e341ce`), which superseded the Sep 4 one-click ruling: left-click on a column header now only selects the whole column; right-click opens the header menu (Rename, Type, Sort ascending, Sort descending, Filter, Delete column). `handleColumnHeaderClick` no longer opens `ShHeaderMenu`; a new `handleColumnHeaderContextMenu` handler (wired via `oncontextmenu`) opens it instead, reusing the existing `openHeaderMenu`/`headerMenuAnchor` state and the unchanged `ShHeaderMenu` component. The resize grip also stops propagation on right-click so right-clicking the 1px grip sliver doesn't open the menu. No backend or stored-data changes. (Relates to #2874, spec already merged in PR #2924)
- Fixed typing into a ghost row/column more than one row/column past the last real one creating only a single new row/column and writing the typed value into the wrong (first) one instead of the one actually clicked (#2874 item 23). `beginGhostCommit` now computes how many ghost rows/columns were skipped and creates all of them in one backend transaction (new `create_sheet_rows`/`create_sheet_columns` batch commands, one snapshot and one recompute for the whole batch) via new `createSheetRowsBatch`/`createSheetColumnsBatch` API wrappers — the typed value lands in the last (Nth) row/column created; every row/column before it is an intentionally empty intermediate. Both axes ghost at once (the corner case) still runs as two independent transactions, one per axis. Existing single-row/column insert endpoints (toolbar buttons, "Insert row above"/"Insert column left") are unchanged. See `docs/spec/sheets.md` §33.3.5.
- Fixed `update_sheet_cell_internal` always returning `computed_value: None` on its `SheetCell` response, even for formula writes (#2874 item 25) — committing a formula cell briefly displayed the raw formula text (`cellKind()` saw `raw_value` starting with `=` but a null `computed_value` and classified it as `'raw'`) until a later refetch corrected it. Fixed at the source: a value-changing write now runs the existing read-only `recompute::recompute_sheet` pass and returns the resulting computed value when the written value is a formula; style-only writes (styling/clearing, `value: null`) are unchanged and still return `None`, since there's nothing new to compute.
- Fixed style-only writes silently dropping a cell's existing computed value (including a live `#REF!`/`#DIV/0!` error) in the frontend cache (#2874 item 27) — `applyStyleToSelection` and `clearSelectedStyling` now preserve the cell's prior `computed_value` when the backend response comes back `None` and `raw_value` didn't change, via a new `preserveComputedValueOnStyleOnlyWrite` helper in `SheetGrid.svelte`. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: computed_value return fix, no spec changes)

## [1.0.53] - 2026-09-12

- Replaced emoji and dingbat glyphs in sheet menus with inline SVGs matching locked design frames (#2874)
