### Removed
- Removed New Folder option from the collapsed caret dropdown in KanbanBoard, NotesBrowser, and AllTasksView (#2874 item 6)
- Removed: Cmd+B sidebar toggle shortcut (supersedes #2876)

### Fixed
- Fixed: ⌘⇧S style panel now anchors to the selected cell instead of sidebar fallback (#2874 item 21)
- Replaced the sheet toolbar's three separate style buttons (fill color, text color, border) with a single unified "Style cells" button using the bucket-with-droplet glyph (#2874 item 20, closes item 13). `SheetToolbar.svelte`'s `onFillClick`/`onTextClick`/`onBorderClick`/`fillSwatch` props, their local button-ref state, and the dead `.sh-tb__fill`/`.sh-tb__swatch` CSS are all removed; a single `onStyleClick` prop and `styleBtnEl` state replace them, wired straight through to the same `sheetGridRef?.openStylePanel(anchorEl)` call every old button already used (the popover itself already exposes fill/text/border controls in one place, so three separate entry points were redundant). Also removed the now-dead `lastUsedFill`/`onFillApplied` plumbing threaded between `Editor.svelte` and `SheetGrid.svelte` that only existed to feed the old fill button's swatch chip. The new glyph is the same bucket+droplet path data already used by `ShCellContextMenu.svelte`'s "Style cells…" row, so this also closes item 13 (the old fill button's glyph was missing the droplet detail). `SheetGrid.svelte`'s `openStylePanel()` function and the existing ⌘⇧S shortcut are unchanged — both already supported single-button anchoring. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: cosmetic fix — no spec change needed)
- Added a new `--sheet-border-styled` CSS token (`rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.31)`, same literal value in both theme blocks) and switched `SheetGrid`'s `borderColor()` to write it instead of `var(--border-strong)` for styled (solid) cell borders (#2874 item 8). Also added a read-path migration in `parseCellStyleJson` (`sheetSnapshotEnvelope.ts`) so existing sheets whose `style_json` still has borders stored with `var(--border-strong)` are remapped to `var(--sheet-border-styled)` on read, picking up the new token without a data migration. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: cosmetic fix — no spec change needed)
- Fixed task-click note selection racing a fixed 200ms `setTimeout` in `CanvasRenderer`'s `handleTaskClick` (#2874 item 18, fix 1) — replaced with an actual completion signal: `handleTaskClick` now `await`s `navigateTo()` and `tick()` before dispatching `pane-select-note` immediately, and `NotesBrowser` now queues the noteId (`pendingSelectNoteId`) when `taskNotes` hasn't finished loading yet, resolving it via a `$effect` once `loadTaskNotes()` populates `taskNotes` — no more dropped selections when the load takes longer than 200ms. Also fixed a related, previously-undiscovered bug this change surfaced: `CanvasRenderer`'s loading-spinner gate excluded `note_list`/`all_tasks`/`trash`/`calendar` but not `notes_browser`/`note_editor`, so every fresh navigation into those two views caused `NotesBrowser` to fully unmount and remount while its own `loadDataForView` data fetch was in flight — destroying local component state (including the new `pendingSelectNoteId` queue) and detaching its `pane-select-note` listener mid-flight. Added `notes_browser`/`note_editor` to the spinner gate's exclusion list so `NotesBrowser` mounts once and stays mounted across the click-to-open flow. New `CanvasRenderer.taskclick-completion.test.ts` renders the real `CanvasRenderer` end-to-end (calendar task click → real `navigateTo` → real `NotesBrowser` mount → real event dispatch/listener → real `noteService.selectNote`) with a deliberately slow (250ms, exceeding the old 200ms timer) mocked `api.listNotesByProject`, asserting no premature selection and correct note opening once the load resolves; new `NotesBrowser.pending-select.test.ts` unit-tests the queue/resolve logic directly. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: cosmetic fix — no spec change needed)
- Guarded `SheetGrid`'s `loadSheet()` against null/malformed sheet data from `get_sheet_data` (#2874 item 18, fix 2) — throws a clean `'Sheet data is missing or malformed'` error (shown via the existing `loadError` banner) instead of letting a destructure/spread inside `pivotSheetData` throw an opaque `TypeError`. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: cosmetic fix — no spec change needed)
- Fixed sheet title rename not persisting (#2874 item 17) — sheet notes have no TipTap instance, so the sheet editor's title-save path was falling through to the generic `saveNote`/`saveContent` flow and bundling a stale/regenerated `content` field alongside the title in the same `update_note` request. The #2901 sheet-body guard correctly rejects that `content` write, but its `Err` also blocked the title write bundled in the same call — collateral damage, not a guard bug (the guard is correct and stays unchanged per Matt's ruling). Fixed the caller instead: a new `isSheet` branch (in the title input's `onblur` handler and in `onDestroy`, both outside the existing `if (editor)` TipTap path) calls a new dedicated `saveSheetTitle()` (`Editor.svelte`) / `api.saveSheetTitle()` function that sends a request with ONLY `note_id` and `title` — no `content` key constructed at all — so the guard is never triggered. New frontend test (`api.saveSheetTitle.test.ts`) asserts the request object has no `content` property. New Rust test (`notes.rs`, `empty_filepath_guard_tests`) asserts a title-only `update_note` call on a sheet note succeeds and persists the title without touching the body. Required extracting `update_note`'s body into a new `update_note_internal(app: Option<&tauri::AppHandle>, ...)` so the fix could be unit-tested directly — a real `tauri::AppHandle` can't be constructed from `tauri::test::mock_app`'s `AppHandle<MockRuntime>` (different concrete runtime types); the two `AppHandle`-only side effects (`pane-badge-changed` emit, `check_due_dates_for_task`) are now guarded by `if let Some(app) = app`, with zero behavior change on the real command path (`update_note` always passes `Some(&app)`). (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: bug fix, no spec change)
- Fixed drag-select state not clearing on mouseup in sheets (#2874 item 19) — `.sh-gridwrap`'s element-scoped `onmouseup={handleGridMouseUp}` never fired for a mouseup released outside that element (over the toolbar, a popover, or outside the browser window entirely), leaving `isDragSelecting` stuck `true` so a later, unrelated `mouseenter` would keep extending the selection range. Replaced with a window-level `mouseup` listener, matching the existing resize-drag pattern (`startColumnResize`/`startRowResize` + `handleResizeMouseUp`): `handleCellMouseDown` attaches `handleDragSelectMouseUp` on `window` on every mousedown, and the handler removes itself the first time it fires (plus an `onDestroy` cleanup in case the component unmounts mid-drag). New `SheetGrid.test.ts` tests cover: a window-level mouseup outside `.sh-gridwrap` still clears the drag (the original bug's regression guard), an in-progress drag still extends normally, a later mouseenter after mouseup does not extend, and a fresh mousedown after a completed drag correctly re-arms the listener. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: bug fix, no spec change)
- Fixed: ghost-cell hover-select after single click (#2874 item 19)
- Fixed styled cell borders (weight/color) not rendering on unselected cells in sheets (#2874 item 8 reopen)
- Fixed sheet notes opening as plain text in project view — sheet grid now mounts correctly in all views (Kanban, All Tasks, Calendar, search, backlinks)
- Fixed sheets created from project view not appearing in folder view
- Added backend guard preventing direct body writes to sheet notes (body is derived from sheet tables)
- Fixed "Insert row above" and "Insert column left" in sheets — both now insert at the clicked position instead of appending at the end (§33.3.4)
- Fixed provider Disconnect confirmation dialogs in NewProviderModal and ProviderConnectionCard — native `confirm()` resolves `false` per Apple's documented WKUIDelegate default in Tauri's WKWebView, silently blocking the disconnect flow; migrated to the existing ConfirmDialog component
- Fixed cell border weights rendering too faint by switching from CSS border to inset box-shadow rendering; base hairlines suppressed on styled edges (#2874)
- Fixed New Sheet button missing cyan outline by removing competing scoped border-color (#2874)
- ShSheetMenu (sheet toolbar "More" menu) running under the chat panel when open (#2874 item 5) — the menu's `flipRight` positioning measured `anchorEl.left + MENU_WIDTH` against `window.innerWidth` to decide whether to flip its anchor edge, but `window.innerWidth` is the full browser viewport, not the editor pane's actual right edge; when the chat panel was open, the editor pane was narrower than the viewport but the measurement never accounted for that, so `flipRight` stayed `false` and the menu extended rightward past the editor pane's own boundary, running under the chat panel. The real constraint was overflow clipping from `.editor-wrapper`'s `overflow: hidden` (and, in the notes-browser overlay path, `.fv-note`'s), not a z-index loss — confirmed `.sh-pop`'s z-index (30) already safely beats the chat panel's (1) at desktop widths either way. Fix (per audit `docs/audits/2026-09-07-item5-rescope.md`, approved by Matt): since the More button is always the toolbar's rightmost item (`SheetToolbar.svelte`'s `.sh-tb__more-wrap` is the last child in the toolbar's flex row), the menu is now anchored to the button's right edge unconditionally — `MENU_WIDTH`, the `flipRight` state, and the measurement `$effect` are deleted entirely, and `.sh-pop`'s CSS just sets `left: auto; right: 0` against the already-`position: relative` `.sh-tb__more-wrap` wrapper, no markup change needed. This sidesteps the clipping ancestor by construction (the menu always opens leftward, staying within the editor pane's own bounds) rather than by fixing the ancestor. Two `ShSheetMenu.test.ts` tests that asserted the old boundary-flip behavior (`'boundary-flip positioning applies flip-right class...'`, `'does not flip-right when there is enough room to the right'`) are replaced with one test asserting the menu is unconditionally right-anchored and never applies a `flip-right` class, including at the same near-the-right-edge anchor position the old flip test used. Same latent `window.innerWidth`-measurement pattern also exists in `ShHeaderMenu.svelte` and `ShCellContextMenu.svelte`, confirmed but explicitly out of scope here — their anchors (a column header, an arbitrary click coordinate) are not guaranteed rightmost, so this same simple fix doesn't transfer; flagged for future prioritization. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: bug fix, no spec change)
- Click-to-edit on the idle formula bar (#2874 item 12) — clicking the idle formula bar (the tokenized display span or the "Empty cell" placeholder) did nothing; no click handler was ever wired to `SheetGrid.svelte`'s `barBeginEdit()`, pre-existing since PR 14. `FormulaBar.svelte` now accepts an `onBarClick?: () => void` prop, wired to both idle spans (`onclick`, plus `role="button"`/`tabindex="0"`/an Enter-Space `onkeydown` handler for keyboard accessibility) and to `sheetGridRef?.barBeginEdit()` in `Editor.svelte`. Fixing the click alone surfaced a second, previously-latent race: the bar's own rising-edge focus `$effect` (from the #2874 P0-1 fix above) saw the click's `document.activeElement` land on the bar's own idle span and misread it as "focus already elsewhere," skipping its own `.focus()` call — fixed by adding a `barRootEl` ref and a `focusInsideBar` check folded into `focusAlreadyElsewhere` so a click that lands anywhere inside the bar's own container is never treated as elsewhere. A THIRD, deeper race then surfaced once the bar could reliably open a session: `SheetGrid.svelte` mounts an in-cell editor for the SAME cell at the same time ("one formula, two places to edit it"), and that in-cell editor's own focus `$effect` (`SheetCellEditorText`/`SheetCellEditorDate`/`SheetCellEditorFormula`, all three deliberately unguarded per Matt's earlier ruling) would win the mount-order race and steal focus back from the bar. Fixed with a new `origin: 'cell' | 'bar'` flag on `SheetGrid.svelte`'s shared `EditingCell` state — `'bar'` only when `barBeginEdit` opened the session, `'cell'` (the default) everywhere else (double-click, type-to-edit, ghost-row, and the select-only `openSelectEditor` path) — threaded as a new `origin` prop to the three affected cell editors, each changing its focus effect's guard from `if (inputEl)` to `if (inputEl && origin !== 'bar')` so a bar-originated session's in-cell editor never focuses itself, letting the bar's own input win instead. `SheetCellEditorSelect` is untouched — `barBeginEdit` already no-ops for checkbox/select anchors. New Case 4 in `Editor.sheet-cell-editing-integration.test.ts` (alongside the existing #2874 P0-1 Cases 1-3) mounts the real `Editor` + `FormulaBar` + `SheetGrid` together and drives a full click-idle-bar → type 3 chars → Enter flow, asserting the bar's own input ends up focused and the typed value reaches the cell's committed display. Full `npx vitest run` suite passes (2615 passed, 1 pre-existing skip; zero regressions in `SheetGrid.test.ts`'s `barBeginEdit`/`barSetValue`/`barCommit` coverage or `FormulaBar.test.ts`'s caret-parity suite). (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: bug fix, no spec change)

- Sidebar bottom-pinning (#2881) — the global audio player (NavPlayer) and the bottom nav bar (Notifications/Settings) are now wrapped in a single persistent `.player-dock` div so they move together as one unit. After #2879 added `display: none` on `.projects-section` when collapsed, the flex-grow filler that pushed the bell/gear icons to the bottom disappeared — icons (and NavPlayer, when a track was loaded) floated up under the rail instead of staying pinned at the bottom. `margin-top: auto` now lives on the new `.player-dock` wrapper (one new CSS rule) rather than on `.bottom-section` directly, so the player and bottom bar pin together as one block regardless of whether `.projects-section` or `.ps-rail` renders. No selector or component behavior changes — `.player-dock` has no direct-child (`>`) dependents anywhere in the codebase, and NavPlayer's own four `:global(.sidebar...)` ancestor rule pairs (descendant combinators) are unaffected by the added DOM depth. (Relates to #2881, spec-skip: bug fix, no spec change)

- Sidebar duplicate category dots when collapsed — `.projects-section` had no `display: none` rule under `.sidebar.collapsed`, so it stayed visible underneath the collapsed rail (`.ps-rail`) and both rendered at once, doubling every category dot. Added `.sidebar.collapsed .projects-section { display: none; }` (`Sidebar.svelte`) — a single unconditional CSS rule, no `!important`, no template/Svelte conditional changes. `display: none` (a paint-only hide) rather than an `{#if}` guard was used deliberately so `.projects-section`'s local state (scroll position, mid-edit inputs) survives across collapse/expand. Applies in both grouped view (where `.ps-rail` already covers the gap) and flat view (which has no collapsed rail equivalent — collapsed flat view now renders blank in that region instead of leaking clipped chevron/label content at 40px; that's an accepted pre-existing design gap, not a regression from this fix). No existing test asserts on `.projects-section` visibility, so no regressions. (Relates to #2875, spec-skip: bug fix, no spec change)

- FormulaBar focus-steal bug that made in-cell sheet editing unusable — typing more than one character into a cell editor (via double-click, type-to-edit, or reopening a cell after Enter) would immediately close the editor after the first keystroke (#2874 P0-1). Root cause: `FormulaBar.svelte`'s focus/caret-restore `$effect` unconditionally called `.focus()` on its own input whenever its `editing` prop was truthy — and every keystroke in the in-cell editor re-renders `FormulaBar` (via `SheetGrid`'s `onSelectionInfo` → `Editor`'s `formulaBarInfo` `$state` → `FormulaBar` re-render), re-running the effect and stealing focus back from the in-cell editor on every single keystroke; the in-cell editor's own `onblur` handler then committed and closed it. Fixed by guarding the effect to a RISING EDGE of `editing` (`false` → `true`) only, via a plain (non-reactive) `prevEditing` closure variable, so a value-driven re-render while already editing no longer re-steals focus. On the rising edge itself, an additional `focusAlreadyElsewhere` check (`document.activeElement` is neither this bar's own input nor `<body>`) prevents the bar from still stealing focus back on the very first open — the in-cell editor's own identical (deliberately unguarded, per Matt's ruling) focus effect races this one in the same reactive flush and typically wins by DOM order, but without this check the bar would win instead on that first transition. This guard changes FormulaBar's focus/`setSelectionRange` from firing on every `selectionStart`/`selectionEnd` change to rising-edge only (`editing`: false→true). Clicking into the formula bar mid-edit is unaffected — native click focus, no rising edge fires. Four paths open bar editing: double-click, type-to-edit, ghost-row auto-advance, and bar-self-click (`barBeginEdit`) — the guard is path-agnostic, reacting to the `editing` prop transition, not the trigger. New `Editor.sheet-cell-editing-integration.test.ts` mounts the real `Editor` + `FormulaBar` + `SheetGrid` together (the level the bug lived at — two sibling components reacting to the same shared `editing` prop in the same reactive flush, which isolated component tests of either alone cannot reproduce) and covers all three regression paths: double-click then type 3 chars, single-click then type-to-edit then type 3 chars, and reopen-after-Enter then type 3 more chars — each asserting the editor stays open with the full typed string. (Relates to #2874, spec-skip: bug fix, no spec change)

## [1.0.48] — 2026-09-06

### Added
- Cell styling — live grid rendering of `style_json`, a right-click cell context menu with clear-contents/clear-styling, and a full style-picker panel with toolbar/⌘⇧S entry points and range application of new styles (#2339 PR 15d-alpha + PR 15d-beta, scope report `docs/audits/2026-09-05-sheets-cell-styling-scope.md` §3.1-3.8). Two commits on the same `sheets/cell-styling` branch, opened as one PR: alpha landed the grid-surgery and context-menu plumbing (read path — rendering and clearing EXISTING `style_json`); beta adds the actual style-picker UI, its toolbar/keyboard entry points, and the write path that lets a user apply NEW styles to a selection. **Alpha — (1) Live style rendering.** `style_json` (already parsed read-only by the version-history preview's `parseCellStyleJson`, PR 15b-beta) now also renders on the LIVE grid: a new `cellInlineStyle(styleJson, kind)` export in `sheetCellRender.ts` builds the real cell `<div>`'s inline `style` string. **Hard, dedicated-test-covered carve-out (Matt's rule):** an inline `style` attribute out-specifies any class rule, including `.sh-c--err { color: var(--status-danger) }` — so `bg` (background) and `bd` (border, any side) always apply regardless of cell kind, but `fg` (ink/text color) is applied ONLY when `kind !== 'err'`, so a user's chosen text color can never silently override the error-red contrast guarantee on a cell that's currently showing `#REF!`/`#VALUE!`/etc. Fills/borders sit behind the value and never touch text contrast, so they're unconditionally safe. Wired onto `SheetGrid.svelte`'s real cell `<div>` (ghost cells never render user styling — there's no underlying cell); `ShSnapshotPreview.svelte`'s own private `cellStyle()` duplicate (PR 15b-beta) is deleted in favor of this shared function — same behavior, one implementation. **Alpha — (2) Right-click cell context menu, `ShCellContextMenu.svelte`** — a new `.sh-pop`-shell popover (same dumb-shell-with-callback-props division of labor as `ShSheetMenu.svelte`), the first popover in the codebase anchored to a click COORDINATE (`x`/`y`, the triggering `MouseEvent`'s `clientX`/`clientY`) rather than a static button ref, with its own boundary-flip math against that coordinate. 9 rows in the design's exact order: Style cells… (⌘⇧S hint; alpha wired this row to just close the menu as a placeholder, beta below replaces that stub with `openStylePanel()`), Clear styling, a divider, Insert row above / Insert column left (calling `SheetGrid`'s own already-exported imperative methods directly, no new props needed), a divider, Export sheet as CSV… (via a new `onExportCsv` prop threaded from `Editor.svelte`, the same handler `SheetToolbar` already uses), a divider, and a danger-styled `sh-pop__danger` "Delete N cells' contents" row (singular/plural grammar driven by a new `selectionCellCount` derived value — the active selection's full rectangular cell count, 1 for a bare anchor). Right-clicking a cell outside the current selection re-selects to just that cell first; right-clicking inside an existing multi-cell range leaves the range intact so the menu's actions apply to the whole range. **Alpha — (3) Delete/Backspace clear-contents + "Clear styling."** `SheetGrid.svelte` gained a `Delete`/`Backspace` keyboard binding (added to the existing `handleKeydown` switch, guarded by the same editing/rename/open-menu checks every other grid shortcut already uses) calling a new `clearSelectedContents()` — walks every cell in the active selection (shared `selectedCellCoords()` helper, ghost coordinates skipped) and calls the existing `api.updateSheetCell(rowId, colId, '')` for each cell that currently has a value, skipping already-empty cells rather than wasting a round-trip. Per Matt's ruling, this clears VALUES ONLY — `style_json` is never touched, either from the keyboard shortcut or the context menu's identical "Delete N cells' contents" row. A separate `clearSelectedStyling()` (context-menu-only, no keyboard shortcut — "Clear styling remains its own verb") walks the same shared coordinate list and calls `updateSheetCell(rowId, colId, null, '{}')` per styled cell, leaving the value untouched (`value: null` falls back to the existing value per `update_sheet_cell_internal`'s already-shipped independent-Option contract). **62 new tests**: comprehensive `cellInlineStyle` coverage in `sheetCellRender.test.ts` (empty/null/malformed styleJson, bg-only, fg-only, bd-only, all-three-combined, and the critical error-carve-out cases — an error cell with `fg` set must never emit `color`, an error cell with `bg` set must still emit `background`), `ShCellContextMenu.test.ts` (all 9 rows present in order, the ⌘⇧S hint text, each row's callback firing then closing the menu, danger-row styling class and singular/plural grammar at cellCount 1 vs N, Escape closes, a click inside the menu does not close it, both boundary-flip directions), and new describe blocks appended to `SheetGrid.test.ts` covering live `style_json` rendering on real cells (including the error-carve-out verified against the actual rendered `<div>` style attribute), the right-click context menu's selection/re-selection behavior and cell-count accuracy, Delete/Backspace on a single cell and a multi-cell range (and the no-op-on-already-empty-cell case), and "Clear styling" (correct API call args, no-op when unstyled, value left untouched). Alpha's own suite pass: 2509 vitest tests, 151 files, 0 svelte-check errors, zero backend Rust changes. **Beta — (4) The write path: `sheetCellStyle.ts`.** A new pure, DOM-free utility module (same convention as `sheetCellRender.ts`/`sheetFormula.ts`) is the inverse of alpha's read-only `parseCellStyleJson`: `buildCellStyleJson(style: CellStyleInput)` takes structured `{bg, fg, bd}` input and serializes it back to the exact `style_json` shape the read path already parses, returning `'{}'` when every field is null/empty rather than an object with explicit null keys. **Multi-border format, decided here:** `bd` is written as an ARRAY of `BorderSpec` entries (`{side, w, c, dashed?}`, one per styled side) rather than alpha's single-object shape, since a cell can have up to 4 independently-colored/weighted borders (top/right/bottom/left) and one object can only ever hold one — `parseCellStyleJson` (`sheetSnapshotEnvelope.ts`) is updated to read BOTH shapes: it iterates every entry when `bd` is an array, and falls back to treating it as one entry when it's a bare object, so every `style_json` value alpha already wrote (or any hand-authored single-border JSON) still parses byte-identically after this change — a dedicated backward-compat regression test asserts the pre-existing single-object test case's exact output is unchanged. `expandSelection(selection)` turns the grid's existing `SheetSelectionState` (anchor + optional range) into a flat `CellCoord[]` — every cell in the inclusive rectangle when a range exists, just `[anchor]` otherwise, `[]` with no anchor — the single shared primitive both the style panel's unanimity checks and `applyStyleToSelection`'s write loop iterate over. `detectUnanimity(cells, 'bg'|'fg')` and `detectBorderUnanimity(cells, side)` implement **Matt's unanimity ruling**: the panel highlights a swatch/segment ONLY when every cell in the selection agrees on that value — any disagreement (including one cell having no style at all) returns `null`, so a heterogeneous selection shows nothing pre-selected rather than guessing from the first cell. `mergeStylePatch(existing, patch)` merges a partial style change into an already-parsed style, implementing **Matt's outer-edge border ruling**: a `top`/`bottom`/`left`/`right` border choice is resolved by the caller (see `applyStyleToSelection` below) to apply only to that edge's row/column within the selected range — never every cell — while `all` applies to all 4 sides of every cell and `none` clears every border; `bg`/`fg` patches always apply uniformly to the whole selection. The per-cell edge-resolution check itself is a new exported pure function, `resolvedBorderSides(applied, coord, range)`, in this same module — `SheetGrid.svelte`'s `applyStyleToSelection` calls it directly (one call per selected cell) instead of inlining the four-way edge comparison, and `sheetCellStyle.test.ts`'s outer-edge-ruling describe block imports and exercises this REAL function rather than a test-local reimplementation, so those unit tests now cover the exact code path the component runs. **49 new tests** in `sheetCellStyle.test.ts` cover round-tripping every field through `parseCellStyleJson`, `expandSelection` across anchor-only/range/no-anchor, unanimity with identical/differing/empty-style cells for both `bg`/`fg` and every border side, and `resolvedBorderSides`'s outer-edge resolution against a 3×3 range. 6 new tests appended to `sheetSnapshotEnvelope.test.ts` cover the new array `bd` format (all four sides in one array, a single-entry array, an empty array, malformed entries mixed with valid ones, `dashed:true`) plus an explicit backward-compat assertion for the legacy single-object shape. **Beta — (5) `ShStylePanel.svelte`** — the actual style-picker UI, a 268px `.sh-pop`-family popover built as a dumb shell with callback props (same division of labor as `ShSheetMenu.svelte`/`ShHeaderMenu.svelte`: no selection knowledge of its own, every verb an `on*` prop, its own outside-click/Escape close lifecycle). CSS ported verbatim from `docs/design/sheets/sheets.css` (`.sh-sty*`/`.sh-sw*`/`.sh-seg*`), zero new design tokens. Three sections: **Fill** (7 swatches — none/slate/cyan/green/amber/red/violet, the "none" swatch showing an ✕ icon and clearing `bg`), **Text** (7 ink swatches, each rendered as a colored "A" glyph), and **Border** (a side segment row — None/All/Top/Btm/Left/Rgt — plus a weight/dashed segment row, 1–3px + a Dashed toggle). Every swatch/segment's `is-on` state is driven by the `currentBg`/`currentFg`/`currentBorder` props the caller computes via `detectUnanimity`/`detectBorderUnanimity` — the panel itself does zero unanimity logic. Border clicks fire `onApplyBorder` immediately with the full combined `{side, w, dashed}` spec on every side/weight/dashed click (not gated behind a separate "apply" action), matching the fill/ink swatches' immediate-apply feel. A bottom "Clear styling" row reuses the same verb alpha's context menu already exposed. **27 new tests** in `ShStylePanel.test.ts`: structural counts (7+7 swatches, 6 side segments, 4 weight/dashed segments, Clear button), fill/ink/border click → callback payload correctness (including combined side+weight+dashed spec building), `is-on` highlighting seeded from all three `current*` props (and the null/heterogeneous → no-highlight case), Clear styling → `onClearStyling` then `onClose`, Escape-to-close, click-inside-doesn't-close, and `x`/`y` positioning. **One documented test gap:** genuine outside-click-closes-the-panel cannot be exercised in this suite — the shared `vitest-setup.ts` window mock's `addEventListener` is a no-op, so `<svelte:window onclick>` never actually attaches during a test render (confirmed the same gap already exists, undocumented differently each time, in `ShCellContextMenu.test.ts`/`ShHeaderMenu.test.ts`/`ShSheetMenu.test.ts` — none of this codebase's popovers can test true outside-click dispatch today); only the inverse ("click inside does not close") is verified, consistent with every sibling popover's test file. **Beta — (6) Toolbar + `SheetGrid` wiring, and Matt's ⌘⇧S ruling.** `SheetToolbar.svelte`'s three style buttons (fill/text/border), disabled since the toolbar first shipped, are un-disabled and wired to new `onFillClick`/`onTextClick`/`onBorderClick` callback props — **per Matt's callback-pattern ruling, the toolbar stays completely ignorant of the current selection**: all three buttons fire the same generic "open the style panel" signal, with zero selection-aware logic living in `SheetToolbar.svelte` itself. A new `fillSwatch` prop drives the fill button's swatch indicator color (`style:background`). `SheetGrid.svelte` gains the panel-side half of that contract: an exported `openStylePanel()` (added to the same `bind:this` imperative-method interface `insertRow`/`insertColumn`/`reload` already use) that opens the panel and closes the context menu if one is open; `panelBg`/`panelFg`/border-unanimity `$derived` values computed from `expandSelection(selection)` + the live `pivoted` grid data via `detectUnanimity`/`detectBorderUnanimity`, feeding `ShStylePanel`'s `current*` props; and `applyStyleToSelection(patch)`, which expands the selection, resolves the range's `r0`/`r1`/`c0`/`c1` bounds, and for a border patch applies **Matt's outer-edge ruling** per cell (`top` → only `row === r0`, `bottom` → only `row === r1`, `left` → only `col === c0`, `right` → only `col === c1`, `all` → every side on every cell, `none` → clear all borders on every cell) before merging via `mergeStylePatch` and writing each cell with the existing `api.updateSheetCell(rowId, colId, null, styleJson)` — fill/ink patches instead apply uniformly to every cell in the selection. Applying a fill also fires a new `onFillApplied` prop, which `Editor.svelte` uses to track `lastUsedFill` and feed it back into the toolbar's swatch. The context menu's "Style cells…" row, alpha's stub, now calls `openStylePanel()` before closing the menu. **A new ⌘⇧S keyboard shortcut opens the panel directly (Matt's ruling, 2026-09-05)** — implemented as a guard checked BEFORE `handleKeydown`'s main switch (so it can never fall through to the default printable-key/type-to-edit case and swallow a plain, unmodified `s` keystroke), and gated behind the same `editing || headerRename || openHeaderMenu` guard every other grid-level shortcut already respects, so it's a no-op mid-edit. **15 new tests** appended to `SheetGrid.test.ts`: the context menu's "Style cells…" row now opens the panel (replacing alpha's placeholder assertion that it did nothing), ⌘⇧S opening the panel and being inert both mid-edit and via the exported `openStylePanel()` method directly, a plain `s` keystroke still opening the text editor (not the style panel), unanimous-vs-heterogeneous fill highlighting, a full fill-apply round trip proving the write MERGES into (never clobbers) a cell's existing `fg`/`bd` and that `onFillApplied` fires with the applied color, and six dedicated outer-edge-ruling integration tests through the REAL, rendered `applyStyleToSelection` (`top` on a 3×1 range writes only the first row, `all` on a 2×2 range writes all 4 sides on every cell, `none` clears borders on every cell in a 2-cell range regardless of which side they'd previously had, `bottom` on a genuine 3×3 range — 9 cells, proving the row-edge resolution on an axis that also has multiple columns — writes only the bottom row, and `left`/`right` on a 1×3 range each write only their respective outer column). 6 new tests appended to `SheetToolbar.test.ts` cover the three buttons no longer being disabled, each firing its own callback, and the swatch reflecting `fillSwatch`. Full `npx vitest run` suite passes (2611 passed, 1 pre-existing skip; 153 files, 4 new — `sheetCellStyle.test.ts`, `ShStylePanel.test.ts`). `npx svelte-check` passes with 0 errors (435 warnings, same baseline as before this PR — 0 new in any touched file). **Zero backend Rust changes, zero `src-tauri/` files touched across both commits** — the whole feature builds entirely on the existing `update_sheet_cell`/`update_sheet_column`-era `api.updateSheetCell` wrapper and `style_json`'s existing untyped-JSON column; `cargo check` clean (no Rust changes to check). (Relates to #2339, spec-skip: cell styling per §33.6, `ShCellContextMenu`/`ShStylePanel` are new locked-design surfaces not yet in the spec, spec-covered-by: #2845)
- Sheet-native version history and a select-column choices editor for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 15b-beta, `docs/design/sheets/sheets-surfaces.jsx:129-247` ShHistory/SrcLabel/SNAPS, `docs/design/sheets/sheets-addendum.jsx:133-260` OptRow/OptPanel/ShOptions, `sheets.css:282-308`/`:343-373`). Two independent surfaces, landed together because both close out carry-forward gaps flagged by earlier PRs in this feature (PR 9's version-history modal, PR 11's ruling-2 choice-less `select` columns). **(1) Sheet-native version history — the safety-critical fix.** `Editor.svelte`'s existing version-history modal rendered every note's saved content as a raw markdown `<pre>` block and restored via `restore_note_version` unconditionally — for a sheet note, whose `note_versions.content` is actually a JSON snapshot envelope (`{v, columns[], rows[], cells[]}`, not markdown), this meant the preview showed unreadable JSON and, far worse, `restore_note_version` would overwrite the sheet's live cell/column tables with that raw JSON string as if it were a markdown body — silent, unrecoverable corruption. `Editor.svelte` now branches the whole version-history overlay on `isSheet`: sheet notes mount a new self-contained `ShVersionHistoryPanel.svelte`, which fetches its own version list/preview via the SAME generic `get_note_versions`/`get_note_version` commands (a sheet snapshot IS an ordinary `note_versions` row, per `sheets_snapshots.rs`'s own doc comment — no new backend needed) but restores exclusively via a new `api.restoreSheetSnapshot(noteId, versionId)` wrapper around the already-implemented, already-tested `restore_sheet_snapshot` Tauri command — this path can never reach `restore_note_version`, and a dedicated regression test in `ShVersionHistoryPanel.test.ts` proves it directly (mocked `invoke`, asserts `restore_sheet_snapshot` is called and `restore_note_version` is never called across the whole test file). The pre-existing markdown modal (`.vh-overlay`/`restoreFromVersion`, still hard-coding `restore_note_version`) is completely untouched for non-sheet notes — a second regression test (`Editor.sheet-version-history-branch.test.ts`, source-contract style per this codebase's established no-full-mount-harness convention for `Editor.svelte`) statically proves the two branches never cross: the sheet branch contains no `restore_note_version` string and no `.vh-overlay` markup, the markdown branch contains no `ShVersionHistoryPanel` reference, and `restoreFromVersion()` itself still hard-codes `restore_note_version` (and never `restore_sheet_snapshot`). A successful sheet restore fires `onRestored()`, which Editor.svelte wires to a new exported `SheetGrid.svelte` `reload()` method (wrapping the existing private `refetchSheetData()`, not the note-switch `loadSheet()` — a restore shouldn't reset the user's current selection/scroll position). **New read-only preview renderer, `ShSnapshotPreview.svelte`** — deliberately NOT a prop/mode on the live `SheetGrid`, but its own lightweight component, since a snapshot preview needs none of the grid's editing/selection/formula machinery and a shared component would mean threading a `readOnly` flag through all of it. Renders the snapshot's OWN columns/rows/values/cell styling at the design's exact 34px header / 32px row heights, with the same `typeGlyph()` header glyphs the live grid uses (extracted out of `SheetGrid.svelte` into a new shared `sheetCellRender.ts` export for this reuse — zero behavior change to the live grid). No ghost columns/rows, no selection ring, no hover state — it's a picture, not an editor. **One deliberate, documented deviation:** snapshot envelopes never persist a formula's last-computed value (confirmed via `sheets_snapshots.rs` — only `raw_value` is captured; recomputing an arbitrary historical snapshot in-memory would require a nontrivial decoupling of `recompute.rs`'s DB-coupled data-loading layer, investigated and judged out of scope for this PR's time budget), so formula cells in the preview show their raw `=...` formula text (still wedge-marked at 45% opacity, matching the live grid's `.sh-w--calc` treatment) rather than a computed value — called out explicitly rather than fabricating a number. A new pure module `sheetSnapshotEnvelope.ts` parses/validates the envelope JSON (`parseSheetSnapshotEnvelope`, versioned via `ENVELOPE_VERSION`, returns `null` — never throws — on anything malformed or unrecognized, so the preview can render its own graceful fallback), pivots it into a dense preview grid (`pivotSnapshotEnvelope`, mirroring `sheetGridPivot.ts`'s own sort-by-`sort_order`-then-`id` / width-height-0-fallback conventions, duplicated locally since envelope columns/rows lack the full live `SheetColumn`/`SheetRow` shape), and tolerantly parses per-cell `style_json` (`parseCellStyleJson` — `bg`/`fg`/`bd:{side,w,c}` only, since `docs/spec/sheets.md` §33.6 confirms `style_json` has no canonical schema anywhere in this codebase yet; returns `{}` on anything unrecognized, never throws). **Four source labels** (`ShSrcLabel.svelte`, wrapping a new pure `sheetSrcLabel.ts` classifier) render each version's origin per the design's exact glyph/color/label spec — sheet→cyan/▦/"Sheet edit", agent→violet/◎/"Agent" (forward-compatible; no `agent_edit`-shaped source is produced by any code path today), restore→amber/↻/"Before restore", manual→neutral/✎/"Manual edit" — classifying the two source strings the backend actually ever writes for a sheet snapshot (`sheet_snapshot`, `pre_restore`) plus a safe `manual` fallback for anything unrecognized (`mapSheetVersionSource` never throws). **One documented scope-down:** the design's per-label detail suffix (e.g. a changed-cell count) would require diffing each version's full envelope against its predecessor — investigated (would mean fetching and diffing up to 50 versions' full content per panel open) and judged not worth the complexity against what the task's actual test requirements check (label/glyph/color only, not a derived count); `sheetSrcLabelDetail()` deliberately always returns `null`, documented inline as "no diff/change-count data source exists" rather than fabricating a number. Preview header shows the version's timestamp, a `pivotSnapshotEnvelope`-derived "N columns · M rows · K computed" line, "Restoring takes a snapshot first," and a filled cyan Restore button — no confirmation dialog, per the design's own "Restore is confident" annotation (the backend's own pre-restore snapshot capture is what makes the action safe). CSS ported verbatim (`.sh-vh*`/`.sh-snap*` in `ShVersionHistoryPanel.svelte`, `.sh-src*` in `ShSrcLabel.svelte`) — zero new design tokens. **(2) Select choices editor.** `ShHeaderMenu.svelte` (select columns only, showing the live choice count) and `SheetCellEditorSelect.svelte`'s dropdown footer both gained an "Edit options…" row — both were explicitly, deliberately absent since PR 10/11 shipped (documented inline in each file at the time) pending exactly this PR. Both entry points open the SAME new `ShOptionsPanel.svelte`: `ShHeaderMenu` treats it as a fourth internal view-state (`'options'`, alongside the existing `root`/`type`/`filter`, swapped in-place — never a second stacked popover, matching that component's own established convention) reached via a select-only root row; `SheetCellEditorSelect` swaps its own popover body to the identical component for its footer entry point. One editor, two doors in, zero duplicated choices UI. **Six states**, all in one file per the design's single `OptPanel`: list (chips + hover-✕), add (focused empty input, Enter commits), rename (double-click a chip to swap it for an in-place input), duplicate-rejection (trimmed, case-insensitive against the OTHER choices — a rename's own current value never collides with itself — danger ring + 2px glow + a `sh-shake` keyframe restart + a `"'X' is already a choice.'"` collision message), reorder (native HTML5 drag-and-drop on each row's grip, cyan drop-line indicator, reusing `dragReorderIndex.ts`'s existing `normalizeInsertIndex` for the index math rather than duplicating it), and empty (`choices.length === 0`: "No choices yet" + one "Add the first choice" button). **Removal is provably non-destructive**: a new pure `sheetOptions.ts` module's `removeChoiceAt` is a plain array filter with no `sheet_cells` side channel whatsoever — a cell holding a removed choice starts rendering as a mismatch purely because `sheetView.ts`'s pre-existing `isTypeMismatch` classifier is re-evaluated against the shorter choices list on the next grid render; a dedicated test in `sheetOptions.test.ts` proves this exact claim at the pure-function level (the raw stored cell value string is untouched; only `isTypeMismatch`'s boolean flips). `ShOptionsPanel` itself never calls `updateSheetColumn` — it's a "here's the new choices array" emitter via `onChange`, exactly like `ShHeaderMenu`'s own existing `onTypeChange` shape; `SheetGrid.svelte`'s new `menuOptionsChange` handler owns the actual `api.updateSheetColumn(id, { optionsJson })` call + refetch (no backend change needed — `update_sheet_column_internal` already accepted `options_json` since PR 10). CSS ported verbatim (`.sh-opt*` + `@keyframes sh-shake`) into `ShOptionsPanel.svelte`'s own scoped styles. **113 new/changed tests**: 23 in `sheetOptions.test.ts` (duplicate detection incl. case/whitespace/exclude-index/empty-list, message quoting, add/rename/remove immutability, the dedicated removal-doesn't-alter-stored-values proof, reorder forward/backward/no-op/immutability), 6 in `sheetSrcLabel.test.ts` (all 4 mapped source variants across 7 raw input strings, glyph/label distinctness, `sheetSrcLabelDetail` always-null), 21 in `sheetSnapshotEnvelope.test.ts` (valid/malformed/wrong-version/missing-arrays parsing, dense pivot incl. sparse placement and both width/height-0 fallbacks, formula-cell computed-count and raw-value-only assertion, sort-order-independent ordering, style-json parsing incl. all 4 border sides and tolerant-fallback cases), 30 in `sheetCellRender.test.ts` (2 new, covering the extracted `typeGlyph` export unchanged), 23 in `ShOptionsPanel.test.ts` (all six states, drag-reorder simulated via dragstart/drop asserting index-based `onChange`), 7 new cases in `ShHeaderMenu.test.ts` (options row visible only for `select` columns with live count, opening/closing the options view, `onOptionsChange` firing, Escape stepping back to root before fully closing), 5 new cases in `SheetCellEditorSelect.test.ts` (footer row absent by default/present when `onOptionsChange` supplied, opening options, Escape from options steps back to list not full-cancel), 7 in `ShSnapshotPreview.test.ts` (envelope rendering, formula-cell raw-text-not-computed-value, malformed-envelope fallback), 6 in `ShSrcLabel.test.ts` (all 4 source variants), 10 in `ShVersionHistoryPanel.test.ts` (fetch-on-mount, per-version source labels, auto-preview newest, preview stats, version switching, empty-list state, **the critical restore-calls-`restore_sheet_snapshot`-never-`restore_note_version` regression**, `onRestored`-then-`onClose` ordering, restore-rejection doesn't fire either callback, close button never touches restore), and 5 in a new `Editor.sheet-version-history-branch.test.ts` (source-contract tests locking in the `isSheet` branch split, `restoreFromVersion()` still hard-coding `restore_note_version`, `openVersionHistory()`'s sheet short-circuit ordering, `sheetGridRef.reload()` wiring). Full `npx vitest run` suite passes (2451 passed, 1 pre-existing skip; 149 files, 11 new). `npx svelte-check` passes with 0 errors, 0 new warnings in any touched file. **Zero backend Rust changes, zero `src-tauri/` files touched** — both features build entirely on Tauri commands/columns already shipped by earlier PRs in this feature (`restore_sheet_snapshot` from the snapshots work, `options_json` support in `update_sheet_column_internal` from PR 10). (Relates to #2339, spec-skip: locked design implementation, surfaces per §33.5-§33.12, spec-covered-by: #2845)
- Error detail popover (`ShErrorPopover`), export/overflow menu (`ShSheetMenu`), and a shared `.sh-pop` popover shell for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 15b-alpha). Three independent surfaces landed together since all three either build on or feed the same `.sh-pop` shell: **(1) Shared popover shell** — the `.sh-pop*` box-model/typography CSS (panel shell, label rows, item rows + hover/disabled/is-on states, tick mark, icon slot, keyboard-shortcut label, `<hr>` divider, danger-row color, input/subtitle rows) was duplicated verbatim across `ShHeaderMenu.svelte` and `SheetCellEditorSelect.svelte`'s own scoped `<style>` blocks; both are now stripped down to ONLY their own positional overrides (`width`/`top`/`left`, `.flip-right`, `.sh-pop--cell`, `.sh-pop__chev`) and the box-model rules moved to a new global block in `src/app.css`, reusing existing CSS custom properties (`--fg-1..4`, `--surface-1..3`, `--border*`, `--overlay-hover`, `--radius-sm`, `--shadow-pop`, `--status-danger`) — zero new design tokens. Both components' existing test suites (31 tests total) pass unchanged, confirming the extraction is behavior-neutral. **(2) Error detail popover** — no such popover existed before this PR; a new `ShErrorPopover.svelte` renders under an error cell the moment it becomes the sole selection anchor (gated on `cellKind() === 'err'` AND `selection.anchor` matching the cell with no active range — a multi-cell range selection or a non-error cell never shows it), and disappears the instant the anchor moves elsewhere or Escape clears it (`sheetSelection.ts`'s existing `ESCAPE` action already clears the anchor on a single-cell selection, so dismissal needed zero new logic). Three parts, per the task's explicit no-culprit-cell-naming constraint: the raw error code in mono red (`.sh-errpop__code`), a plain-English sentence (`.sh-errpop__msg`), and the cell's raw formula verbatim (`.sh-errpop__f`) — all three sourced from a new static, backend-verified catalogue in `sheetErrors.ts` (`getErrorInfo(code)`) covering exactly the six error codes the Rust engine actually produces (`#REF!`, `#VALUE!`, `#DIV/0!`, `#NAME?`, `#PARSE!`, `#CYCLE!`, confirmed via `sheets.rs`), ported from the design's own `ERRS` array with every culprit-cell reference (e.g. "D2 holds text") deliberately rewritten out — a dedicated test asserts no message ever matches that naming pattern. Positioned with the same boundary-flip pattern as `ShHeaderMenu.svelte` (self-measures against `window.innerWidth`, flips left when it would overflow the right edge), styled with its own `.sh-errpop*` CSS ported from the design (a distinct red-tinted treatment, NOT sharing the `.sh-pop` family — the design explicitly gives errors their own visual language). **(3) Export/overflow menu** — `SheetToolbar.svelte`'s previously-disabled "More" button is now wired to a new `ShSheetMenu.svelte` popover (reusing the shared `.sh-pop` shell from part 1), showing the six rows in the exact order/grouping the task specified: Export as CSV…, Version history, a divider, Rename sheet, Move to…, a second divider, and Delete sheet styled with the shared `.sh-pop__danger` treatment. `ShSheetMenu` is a dumb popover shell only (own open/close-on-outside-click/Escape lifecycle plus boundary-flip positioning, same division of labor as `ShHeaderMenu`) — every verb is a plain callback prop, with all real behavior living in `Editor.svelte` (the file that already owns every one of these mechanisms for every other note type): **Version history** calls the existing `openVersionHistory()` unchanged — sheets are notes (`note_type: 'sheet'`), so the existing per-note version history already works for them with zero changes. **Delete sheet** calls the existing `handleMoveToTrash()` unchanged (no separate "delete sheet" backend command exists or was needed). **Rename sheet** and **Move to…** have no dedicated sheet-level backend commands, and per the task's explicit "reuse existing note-level commands — report back if nontrivial, don't improvise" instruction, none were added: Rename focuses+selects the SAME title `<input>` every note already has in its title row (`handleRenameSheet`, mirroring the existing new-note auto-focus behavior in `onMount`); Move to… calls the SAME folder-pill picker (`toggleFolderPicker`/`handleFolderMove`) already rendered in the title row for any note with a `project_id` — a new `folderPillBtn` element ref was added purely so the menu action has a button element to hand the existing picker function (which expects an anchor element), with zero changes to the picker's own logic. **Export as CSV…** calls the existing, already-implemented-and-tested `export_sheet_csv` Tauri command (`sheets.rs`, PR 5c — read-only, computes via the same `get_sheet_data_internal` path the grid itself renders from, RFC 4180 output, sanitized suggested filename), then opens the native OS save dialog (`@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog`'s `save()`, already a project dependency) defaulted to that filename, then writes the returned CSV text to the chosen path. **One blocker found and resolved, flagged here per the task's own instructions:** writing the file required `@tauri-apps/plugin-fs`'s `writeTextFile()`, but investigation found the Rust `tauri-plugin-fs` crate was already a `Cargo.toml` dependency with `fs:default` already granted in `capabilities/default.json` — yet the plugin was never actually registered via `.plugin(tauri_plugin_fs::init())` in `lib.rs`'s builder chain, and `@tauri-apps/plugin-fs` was missing from `package.json` entirely (present only as a stale transitive `node_modules` artifact, not in the lockfile). This is the one non-trivial, reported-not-improvised finding: added `@tauri-apps/plugin-fs` (~2.5.2, matching the already-pinned `plugin-dialog` version style) to `package.json`, added the single missing `.plugin(tauri_plugin_fs::init())` registration call, and added a scoped `fs:allow-write-text-file` permission to `capabilities/default.json` (the plugin's own default permission set only grants read/mkdir access to app-managed directories, not arbitrary user-chosen save-dialog paths) — no new Tauri command, no schema change, no change to any existing command's behavior; strictly completing a registration the project had already decided to make (dependency + capability were already there) but never finished wiring up. A cancelled save dialog (`path === null`) is a silent no-op, not an error; any other failure (export command rejects, or the write itself fails, e.g. permission-denied) shows the existing `showErrorToast` 5s-auto-dismiss toast already used elsewhere in `Editor.svelte`, never a silent failure. **37 new tests**: 5 in `sheetErrors.test.ts` (all six known codes, unknown-code fallback, exact-match verification, the culprit-naming-guard regex, uniqueness), 7 in `ShErrorPopover.test.ts` (all six codes render, culprit-naming guard, catalogue-fallback vs. verbatim-raw-formula-when-provided, unrecognized-code renders nothing, `.sh-errpop` shell class), 4 new cases appended to `SheetGrid.test.ts` (shows on error-cell selection with correct code/formula, absent for a non-error cell, hides when selection moves to a different cell, hides on Escape), 10 in `ShSheetMenu.test.ts` (all six rows in the correct DOM order, each row's callback-then-close behavior, the danger-row styling class, Escape-to-close, click-inside-doesn't-close, both boundary-flip directions), 10 in `SheetToolbar.test.ts` (a new test file for this component — insert-row/insert-column wiring plus the More button's enabled state, open/toggle, and all five menu-row callbacks reaching `SheetToolbar`'s own props), and 11 new cases appended to `editor-toolbar.test.ts` (pure-logic extractions of `handleExportSheetCsv`'s full guard/success/cancel/both-error-paths flow, `handleRenameSheet`'s guard/focus-then-select-order, and `handleMoveToSheet`'s guard/delegation — following this file's own established "Editor.svelte is too large to mount" pure-function-extraction convention already used for `handleMoveToTrash`). `cargo check`/`cargo test --lib` pass (2085/2086 passing; the one failure, `sync_client::tests::test_sync_push_blocking_completes_no_deadlock`, reproduces identically on a clean `git stash` of this branch — confirmed pre-existing, not a regression, same class of flake several earlier PRs in this feature have already documented). Full `npx vitest run` suite passes (2337 passed, 1 pre-existing skip; 140 files, 5 new). (Relates to #2339, spec-skip: error popover + export menu + shared popover shell per §33.5/§33.12, spec landed in #2845, spec-covered-by: #2845)
- Board card face for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 15a, `docs/design/sheets/sheets-surfaces.jsx` §4, README.md build constraint §1 + revision notes, scoping report `docs/audits/2026-09-05-sheets-pr15-surfaces-scope.md` §1). Sheet notes previously rendered through the exact same generic note-card body every task/note gets (title, 3-line body-text clamp, pills, breadcrumb) — indistinguishable from a doc note in every list. This PR forks `Card.svelte` in place on a new `data.noteType === 'sheet'` branch: a cyan grid glyph beside the title, a micro-grid (`.sh-mini`) with a type-glyph header row driven by the sheet's REAL column config (not a fixed mock — an empty 5-default-column sheet renders 5 real glyphs) plus two schematic data rows (revised down from three per the design's own revision notes), and a footer metric (`{cols} × {rows}`, `· {N} computed` appended only when `formula_count > 0`) in place of the note card's breadcrumb-only footer — the breadcrumb itself moves alongside the metric rather than being dropped. The non-sheet `{:else}` branch (title/card-body/breadcrumb) is untouched, byte-for-byte, from before this PR; the shared pill row (stage dot/label, priority pill, due-date pill) renders identically for both branches, reusing `getStageColor`/`getStageLabel`/priority-color helpers verbatim — zero duplication. **Backend, read-only, no schema changes:** new `get_sheet_card_summary`/`get_sheet_card_summaries` Tauri commands in `sheets.rs`, returning `{ note_id, col_count, row_count, formula_count, col_types }` via lightweight `COUNT(*)` queries against the existing `sheet_columns`/`sheet_rows`/`sheet_cells` tables — deliberately NOT reusing `get_sheet_data_internal` (which loads every cell plus a full formula recompute pass, far heavier than a card face needs). `formula_count` is `COUNT(*) ... WHERE value LIKE '=%'`, matching how `get_sheet_data_internal` already classifies a cell as a formula. The singular command explicitly errors on an unknown or non-sheet note id (checked via a `note_type` lookup); the batched command silently omits non-sheet/unknown ids from its result rather than failing the whole batch, mirroring `get_project_notes_for_kanban`'s existing `if let Ok(...) = ...` convention — callers pass a mixed list of visible note ids and only want the sheet subset back. **Compact variant below ~190px of the card's OWN rendered width** (not viewport width): a `ResizeObserver` bound to the card's root element, gated to attach only when `data.noteType === 'sheet'` (zero-cost for every non-sheet card), feeding a new pure utility module `sheetCardLayout.ts` (`resolveSheetCardMode(cardWidth)`, `SHEET_CARD_COMPACT_THRESHOLD = 190`, inclusive-full-at-190 — same DOM-free-pure-function convention as `newSheetButtonLayout.ts`) that drops the two data rows, keeping only the glyph + type-glyph header strip. **Height-only card revision, width untouched:** a new `.pane-card.sheet-card` CSS override touches ONLY `height`/`min-height`/`max-height` (auto height, replacing the note card's fixed 130px, so the compact and full variants can each size to their own content without a second override rule) — width, padding, border-radius, and border are all inherited unmodified from the base `.pane-card` rule; `.kanban-column`'s 280px `min-width` and `.kanban-columns`' gap/padding are completely untouched. **`cardNormalizers.ts`** extends `CardData` with five new optional, sheet-only fields (`noteType`, `colCount`, `rowCount`, `formulaCount`, `colTypes`) and gives `normalizeNoteMeta`/`normalizeTask` a new optional `sheetSummary` parameter — kept synchronous/pure per this module's existing contract; the base `CardData` object is built first and sheet fields are conditionally spread in only when `note.note_type === 'sheet'`, so a non-sheet note's returned object shape is provably identical to its pre-PR shape (explicit `undefined` keys are never added). Async summary fetching happens at the three real call sites instead — `KanbanBoard.svelte`, `NotesBrowser.svelte`, and `AllTasksView.svelte` each gained a `sheetSummaries` reactive `Map<noteId, SheetCardSummary>` + a `cardSummaryFor(note)` lookup helper, populated by one batched `api.getSheetCardSummaries(...)` call per load pass (best-effort — a failure never blocks the board/list from rendering, sheet cards just render without micro-grid data until the next successful load), mirroring the exact `subtaskCounts`/`api.getSubtaskCounts` batching pattern `AllTasksView.svelte` already used. **AllTasksView needed zero bespoke list-density work** — confirmed at build time (and now covered by a regression test) that it has exactly one `<Card>` usage and no separate list-rendering path; the grid glyph + `cols × rows` metric ruling from the design's All Tasks section is satisfied automatically by `Card.svelte`'s shared sheet branch. **Local, not shared, type-glyph helper:** `Card.svelte` gets its own private `sheetTypeGlyph()` (text/number/currency/date/checkbox/select → T/#/$/📅/☑/≡), a deliberate small duplication of `SheetGrid.svelte`'s own `typeGlyph()` rather than an import — the card micro-grid and the sheet grid/version-history preview (PR 15b) are independent surfaces with no shared component, per the PR's own seam boundary. **Data rows are schematic, not real cell data** (the backend only exposes counts/types, never actual cell values): two fixed-width bar placeholders per column, with two low-risk accuracy exceptions tied to real backend fields — a `currency`-typed column's bars get the cyan "calc" tint (`.sh-mini__bar--calc`) when `formula_count > 0`, and the due-date pill on a sheet card gets a new gold `.sh-due` tone (ported from `docs/design/sheets/sheets.css`'s `.sh-due`, remapped onto Pane's real `--status-gold`-equivalent literal, since overdue's existing red treatment still wins when both apply). **New Rust struct `SheetCardSummary`** (`note_id`, `col_count`, `row_count`, `formula_count`, `col_types: Vec<String>`), registered in `lib.rs`'s `invoke_handler!` list under a new "Sheets board card face" section; new frontend `SheetCardSummary` TS interface (`types.ts`) plus `api.getSheetCardSummary`/`api.getSheetCardSummaries` thin wrappers. `Task.note_type?: string` added to the `Task` interface (`types.ts`) and populated in both `api.listTasks()` and `api.listNotesForKanban()`'s Task-construction — the one real wiring gap found: `AllTasksView`/`NotesBrowser` already flowed `note_type` through `NoteMeta`/`normalizeNoteMeta`, but `KanbanBoard`'s `Task`/`normalizeTask` path was dropping it before this PR. **6 new backend Rust tests** in `sheets.rs` (correct col/row/formula counts against a real 3-column/2-row/1-formula sheet with column-type ordering verified, an empty freshly-created sheet returns the seeded default-column count with zero rows, a non-sheet note id errors, an unknown note id errors, a read-only assertion — `notes.updated_at`/`notes.body` byte-identical before and after the call — and a batched multi-sheet call that silently skips a mixed-in non-sheet note and an unknown id while still returning correct per-sheet counts). **29 new frontend tests**: 5 in `sheetCardLayout.test.ts` (both threshold boundaries, the design's own 176px compact-demo width, negative-width defensiveness, purity/constant-value checks), 19 in a new `Card.sheet-face.test.ts` (real `@testing-library/svelte` mounts, matching `AttachmentCard.test.ts`'s house convention for lighter components — glyph presence, header-row glyph-per-real-column-type, exactly-two-data-rows at full width, both footer-text variants with/without a `computed` suffix, the empty-sheet `N × 0` case with seeded glyphs still shown, shared pill-row/due-chip-tone rendering, the compact-variant `ResizeObserver` boundary at 190/189px including the header-row-stays-visible assertion, and a byte-identical-innerHTML regression proving an explicit `noteType: undefined` and an omitted `noteType` key produce the exact same non-sheet render), 6 in a new `Card.board-width-regression.test.ts` (source-text/regex assertions against `Card.svelte`'s and `KanbanBoard.svelte`'s real CSS, confirming `.pane-card`'s padding/border-radius/border and `.kanban-column`'s 280px min-width/24px gap are untouched, and that the new `.pane-card.sheet-card` override rule touches only height properties), and 4 in a new `AllTasksView.sheet-card-face.test.ts` (confirms the single-`<Card>`-usage/no-bespoke-renderer claim, the batched-fetch + `sheetSummary` wiring, and the non-sheet-returns-`undefined` guard in `cardSummaryFor`). Full `npx vitest run` suite passes (2292 passed, 1 pre-existing skip; 137 files, 4 new). `cargo test --lib sheets::` passes (55/55, including all 6 new). `cargo test --lib` full run: one pre-existing unrelated flake (`sync_client::tests::test_sync_push_blocking_completes_no_deadlock`), reproduced identically on a clean `git stash` of this branch — not a regression, same class of flake several earlier PRs in this feature have already documented. `npx svelte-check` passes with 0 errors (0 new warnings in any touched file). `grep -r 'assert!(true)\|assert!(false)\|unimplemented!()\|todo!()' src-tauri/tests/ src-tauri/src/tests/` returns zero matches.
