- New Sheet button polish for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 15c, addendum frame A, `docs/design/sheets/sheets-addendum.jsx` lines 7-30 + NOTES.md §A + README.md addendum ruling 7). PR 9 shipped a minimal New Sheet button (a small grid glyph, static, no responsive behavior, inverse-styled) at three host call sites (`KanbanBoard.svelte`, `AllTasksView.svelte`, `NotesBrowser.svelte`); this PR replaces it everywhere with the locked addendum design: the SAME plus glyph New Note already uses (reused verbatim, not reimplemented — both buttons now carry the identical `M7 2V12M2 7H12` 14px path), a new global `.btn--outline` CSS class (transparent background, `var(--accent)` text/border, `var(--accent-soft)` hover fill — fill-only, geometry stays local to each site's own existing button box model since the app has no prior shared `.btn` geometry system to normalize against), and a three-step responsive collapse keyed to the HOST HEADER's own width (not viewport width) via a `ResizeObserver` bound directly to each site's header element (`.kanban-header`, `.tasks-header`, `.grid-folder-header`): ≥900px both buttons fully labelled, 720–900px New Sheet drops to an icon-only 32px square box, <720px New Sheet folds into a caret popover beside New Note. New Note's own button is untouched by any of this — it keeps its label unconditionally at every width and stays the rightmost, filled/primary control per the addendum's own ruling that the primary action never moves from where people reach for it; New Sheet was reordered to sit to its left at every site (previously reversed at two of the three). **New shared pure-utility module `src/lib/utils/newSheetButtonLayout.ts`** (DOM-free, same convention as `sheetResize.ts`/`sheetView.ts`): exports `HeaderButtonMode` (`'full' | 'icon' | 'menu'`), the two named breakpoint constants (`HEADER_WIDE_THRESHOLD = 900`, `HEADER_NARROW_THRESHOLD = 720`), and the pure `resolveHeaderButtonMode(headerWidth)` resolver — imported identically by all three host components rather than each reimplementing its own threshold logic inline, so the breakpoints can never drift out of sync between sites. **Caret popover** (New Sheet + New Folder rows, in that order, matching the addendum mock's literal JSX ordering) is genuinely functional, not decorative: New Sheet's row delegates straight to each site's existing sheet-creation handler (`handleCreateNewSheet`/`openSheetProjectPicker`/`handleNewSheet`, zero duplicated creation logic), and a new New Folder action (`handleNewFolderFromCaret`/`handleNewFolderForProject`, minimal `window.prompt()`-based naming mirroring `Sidebar.svelte`'s existing `submitNewFolder` pattern but without its own inline input row) calls the pre-existing `api.createFolder` and refreshes the relevant folder list — KanbanBoard and NotesBrowser use their own ambient project context (`$canvasState.context.projectId` / `$activeProject`), both a no-op if that name prompt is cancelled/empty. **One documented deviation:** AllTasksView is a cross-project aggregate view with no ambient New Note button and no single ambient project to create a folder into, so (a) its "New Note stays rightmost" rule doesn't apply — the caret simply occupies the New Sheet button's own slot, and (b) its caret's New Folder row reuses the SAME lightweight project-picker dropdown the view already built for New Sheet creation, rather than assuming a project; both are called out inline in the component's own source comments, not silent. **Build-time overflow/kebab-menu collision check** (the addendum's own flagged open item, resolved not deferred): all three host headers were checked for an existing overflow/kebab menu before adding the caret; NONE of the three (`.kanban-header`, `.tasks-header`, `.grid-folder-header`) had one, so a brand-new caret was added at each site rather than joining an existing menu — finding stated in the PR body per the CI requirement, not just here. **Naming normalization:** NotesBrowser's button class, previously the only one of the three with a different name (`.new-sheet-btn`), is renamed to `.add-sheet-btn` to match KanbanBoard/AllTasksView. **112 new tests**: 6 in `newSheetButtonLayout.test.ts` (all three mode boundaries at both named thresholds, purity, negative-width defensiveness, exact constant values), and 29/23/25 respectively in new `KanbanBoard.new-sheet-button-polish.test.ts` / `AllTasksView.new-sheet-button-polish.test.ts` / `NotesBrowser.new-sheet-button-polish.test.ts` (all following this codebase's established source-text-extraction/regex convention for these three heavy, store/context-dependent components — see `KanbanBoard.folder-assignment.test.ts`/`NotesBrowser.collapse-rails.test.ts`'s own precedent — rather than full component mounts): plus-glyph presence and grid-glyph absence, `.btn--outline` applied (never `.btn--ghost`, which the addendum explicitly rejects, and never `.btn--primary` on New Sheet), New Sheet-before-New-Note DOM ordering (or the documented AllTasksView exception), New Note's label rendering unconditionally at every width, the `ResizeObserver` wiring (ref binding, ×observe×, ×disconnect on destroy), the label-drop and icon-only-class breakpoints, caret-menu presence/absence and its New-Sheet-above-New-Folder row order, and — the CI-required "click still creates a sheet" coverage — confirming the full/icon-mode button AND the caret's New Sheet row both still call each site's real, unmodified creation handler. Full `npx vitest run` suite passes (2258 passed, 1 pre-existing skip; 132 files, 4 new). `grep -r 'assert!(true)\|assert!(false)\|unimplemented!()\|todo!()' src-tauri/tests/ src-tauri/src/tests/` returns zero matches. **Zero backend Rust changes, zero `src-tauri/` files touched.** (Relates to #2339, spec-skip: UI polish to locked addendum design, no spec changes, spec-covered-by: #2845)
- Formula bar and formula editing (`ShFormulaBar`) for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 14, §33.5, scoping report `docs/audits/2026-09-05-sheets-pr14-formula-bar-scope.md`). Closes the `ReferenceMapper` gap PR 6/7/16 all flagged as an explicit interim gap: until now, typing `=A1+B1` into a cell parsed and stored successfully but silently computed to nothing forever, because the stored formula text carried literal `"A"`/`"1"` strings that never matched a real column/row UUID. **Eight rulings from Matt (2026-09-05) applied on top of the scope report:** (1) string tokens (`.sh-t-str`) render in `var(--status-success)` green, not the "receding" gray the design prose calls for — the shipped `sheets.css` itself gives strings the green token, and CSS-as-authored wins over the prose; cited inline everywhere the token color is set (bar, in-cell editor). (2) formulas are disallowed on the human entry path for `checkbox`/`select` columns for v1 — neither type gains a `=`-triggered escape hatch (checkbox keeps its Space/click-only toggle, select keeps its dropdown-only entry); a pre-existing formula value in either column type (however it got there) still renders through the existing computed-value classifier unchanged. (3) an out-of-bounds A1 reference (e.g. `=Z99` on an 8-column sheet) rejects the WHOLE formula inline at write time, with the same UX surface as a syntax parse rejection — never partially translated or stored. (4) the paused-mode bar stays fully editable (matching the backend's own already-existing behavior of storing/validating-but-not-recomputing past the 500-formula soft limit); the `ShPaused` banner and `SheetStatusBar`'s previously-unused `formulas`/new `paused` props are bundled into this PR rather than split out. (5) the toolbar's `fx` button stays `disabled` — no locked frame defines behavior for it, no improvisation. (6) the error-detail popover (`.sh-errpop`) is explicitly deferred to a later PR — not built here. (7) the `.sh-fbar__x` chevron's three-line expand is a REAL interaction (not static decoration) — toggles the bar between single-line and an up-to-three-line auto-collapsing scroll height, collapsing itself automatically once editing ends. (8) the `ReferenceMapper` is a **Rust function at the backend write chokepoint**, not frontend JS — both human bar/cell writes AND AI-tool writes (`set_sheet_cells`, since it also calls `update_sheet_cell_internal`) get identical A1↔stable-ID translation; only the `apply_changesets` sync-replay path is untouched (architecturally can't route through the chokepoint), left to degrade to `#PARSE!`/silent-`Empty` per existing §33.5.3 behavior. **New backend module `formula/reference_mapper.rs`**: a heuristic (column part all-ASCII-letters + row part all-ASCII-digits = A1-shaped; a real stable UUID can never match that shape, making both translation directions safely idempotent on already-translated input) distinguishes A1-form from ID-form input at the same chokepoint, so both human A1 entry and machine/sync ID-form writes pass through unchanged relative to their own shape. Write path: parses the formula, walks the AST's `CellRef`/`Range` nodes, resolves each A1 token against the sheet's live `sort_order`-ordered column/row ID lists (column letter `A`/row number `1` = position 0, etc.), rewrites to canonical `{column_id:row_id}` / `{column_id:from_row_id:to_row_id}` form (single-column ranges only, per v1 grammar §33.5.2), and re-serializes via a new precedence-aware serializer (avoids a brute-force fully-parenthesized round-trip; non-commutative `Sub`/`Div` force an extra paren on a same-precedence RHS to preserve left-associative grouping) before handing the rewritten string to the existing `validate_formula_on_write`. An out-of-bounds token aborts translation and returns a descriptive error (e.g. `"'Z99' is out of bounds — this sheet has no column Z"`) before anything is written. Read path: the inverse walk, translating stored ID-form refs back to current A1 text using the same live ordering — a stored reference whose ID no longer matches any current column/row (its referent was deleted) is left in raw ID form rather than erroring, since evaluation-side deleted-referent handling (`#REF!`) already exists in `recompute.rs`; this is a display-only fallback. **`update_sheet_cell_internal` restructured** (`sheets.rs`) so the `note_id`/column-note-match lookup now happens BEFORE formula translation and validation (translation needs `note_id` to load the ordered column/row ID lists) — the mapper runs immediately before `recompute::validate_formula_on_write`, so both succeed or both fail together, atomically, inside the same write. New `load_ordered_column_ids`/`load_ordered_row_ids`/`translate_cells_for_display` helpers; the last is wired into `get_sheet_data_internal` so every cell's `raw_value` reaching the frontend is already in A1 display form — the frontend never does its own ID↔A1 translation (kept strictly backend-only per ruling 8). **`formula_count`/`formulas_paused` added to the backend `SheetData` struct** (and the frontend `SheetData` TS interface, `types.ts`), computed from the already-loaded `cells` list inside `get_sheet_data_internal` (no second query) using the exact same `> recompute::FORMULA_CELL_SOFT_LIMIT` comparison `recompute_sheet` itself uses internally, so the two can never disagree. **New frontend pure-utility module `sheetFormula.ts`** (DOM-free, same convention as `sheetCellRender.ts`/`sheetCellCommit.ts`/`sheetView.ts`/`sheetResize.ts`): `tokenizeFormula` (mirrors the design's own `Formula` tokenizer regex/classification order exactly, for pixel-parity — classifies into `sh-t-ref`/`sh-t-fn`/`sh-t-str`/`sh-t-num`/`sh-t-op`), `a1ColLettersToIndex`, `extractFormulaRefRanges` (regex-scans an ALREADY-A1-translated formula string — confirmed the backend's `translate_cells_for_display` guarantees `raw_value` never carries stable-ID form to the frontend — for every ref/range token, returning 0-indexed rectangular regions against the REAL, sort_order grid), `isCellInAnyRefRange`/`refRangeEdges` (per-cell membership/edge-detection driving the dashed outline classes). This module does ZERO A1↔ID translation itself — purely a display/highlight utility, keeping ruling 8's backend-only translation boundary intact. **New `FormulaBar.svelte`**, mounted in `Editor.svelte` between `SheetToolbar`/the new paused banner and `SheetGrid` (design's own `Toolbar → ShPaused → FormulaBar → SheetGrid → StatusBar` flex-column order): `.sh-fbar__ref` cell-address slot, static (non-button) `.sh-fbar__fx` label, tokenized formula/value display or `.sh-fbar__empty` fallback, `is-editing` state with a real `<input>`, inline `.sh-fbar__err` rejection display, and the chevron three-line expand (ruling 7) with auto-collapse-on-editing-end. Reads/writes `SheetGrid`'s selection anchor and shared edit buffer via a new `onSelectionInfo` callback prop (pushes a `FormulaBarInfo { cref, value, editing, error, editable }` shape reactively on every selection/editing/error change) plus four new `bind:this`-exported imperative functions — `barBeginEdit()`, `barSetValue(value)`, `barCommit(cause)`, `barCancel()` — extending the exact `insertRow`/`insertColumn` pattern PR 10 already established; `editable` is `false` for checkbox/select anchors (ruling 2), giving the bar nothing to drive for those two types. **New in-cell formula editor, `sheetEditors/SheetCellEditorFormula.svelte`**: the standard "highlight-behind-transparent-input" technique — a `pointer-events:none` colored token overlay (same `tokenizeFormula` output, same `.sh-t-*` classes as the bar) sits under a real `<input>` with `color:transparent; caret-color:accent`, giving a genuine synced caret with live-colored text as you type, rather than a static color preview. **`SheetGrid.svelte` wiring**: a new `EditingCell.isFormula` flag is decided ONCE, at editor-open time (from whichever buffer the edit session opens with), rather than re-derived reactively from the live buffer on every keystroke — deliberately, since re-deriving it live would swap the rendered editor COMPONENT out from under an in-progress edit the instant a `=` appears anywhere in the buffer mid-type, tearing down the underlying `<input>` DOM node; this still satisfies "typing `=` as the first character opens formula mode" exactly, since the type-to-overwrite entry path (existing ruling from PR 10) already opens the session with a buffer of exactly `"="`. New `formulaEditRanges`/`cellRefEdges` derived values extract every range the CURRENTLY-EDITING formula references (real sort_order coordinates) and map them through the existing `rowOrder` real→display permutation before applying the new dashed `is-ref`/`is-refedge-{t,b,l,r}` CSS classes to the rendered grid — deliberately DASHED, distinct from the pre-existing SOLID `is-redge-*` selection outline, so the two states can never be visually confused (design annotation, directly informing ruling 7's surrounding context). **New `ShPaused` banner** in `Editor.svelte`, between the toolbar and the formula bar: clock glyph, bold live formula count, "computation paused for size" / "Cells show what you wrote" copy, neutral `surface-1` background (a size fact, not a warning — no action button, matching the design's own explicit "v1 isn't aimed at users who reach 500 formulas" ratification). `SheetStatusBar.svelte` gains a `paused?: boolean` prop rendering a `.sh-status__paused` “computation paused” segment alongside its existing (now finally wired) `formulas` count segment. **87 new/updated backend Rust tests**: 38 in the new `formula::reference_mapper` test module (heuristic A1-vs-ID detection idempotency both directions, single/multi-letter column translation, single-cell and range references, unary-minus-on-ref, nested function-call multi-ref formulas, lowercase-A1 normalization, out-of-bounds column/row rejection — both whole-formula-not-partial — unparseable-formula passthrough, and full write→read round-trips including a precedence-mix regression), plus 3 renamed/restructured and 2 new tests in `sheets.rs` covering the restructured `update_sheet_cell_internal` (A1→ID translation on write, ID-form passthrough idempotency, out-of-bounds rejection, and body-regen against a real grid resolving correctly through the mapper). **57 new frontend tests**: 26 in `sheetFormula.test.ts` (tokenizer classification incl. a realistic multi-token formula and the empty-string edge case, column-letter arithmetic incl. case-insensitivity, ref/range extraction incl. reversed-range normalization and function-name non-matches, cell-in-range membership, edge detection for both a 1×1 cell and a multi-row range), 9 in `SheetCellEditorFormula.test.ts` (variant/overlay rendering, ref/string token classes, all four commit causes, double-commit guard, live overlay updates as the bound value changes), 17 in `FormulaBar.test.ts` (all three idle states, tokenized display, the fx-is-a-label assertion, editing-state input wiring and all three commit/cancel/input callbacks, inline error rendering and its absence, and 5 dedicated chevron-expand tests — starts collapsed, toggles both directions, `aria-pressed` reflects state, auto-collapses when editing ends), 5 in `SheetStatusBar.test.ts` (formulas segment presence/absence, paused segment presence/absence, both together), and 14 new integration cases appended to `SheetGrid.test.ts` (typing `=` opens the formula editor not the plain-text one, double-click into an existing formula cell reopens the formula editor, a plain double-click still opens the ordinary text editor, `=` is a no-op in a checkbox column with no editor opening, a select column whose stored value happens to start with `=` still opens its dropdown never the formula editor, `onSelectionInfo` publishes cref/value/editable/editing/error correctly across selection moves, typing, commit, and a rejected out-of-bounds commit, dashed ref-range outlines appear on referenced cells during an in-progress formula edit and disappear on cancel, and the three `barBeginEdit`/`barSetValue`/`barCommit`/`barCancel` imperative-API tests including the checkbox no-op case). `cargo check --lib` and `cargo test --lib` pass (`sheets::` 49/49, `formula::reference_mapper::` 38/38, `formula::recompute::` unchanged and green); a full parallel `cargo test --lib` run shows 8 unrelated failures (`ai::memory_router::tests::*`, `sync_client::tests::test_sync_push_blocking_completes_no_deadlock`) that all pass individually/under `--test-threads=1` and reproduce identically on a clean `git stash` of this branch — confirmed pre-existing parallel-execution/timing flakes, not regressions from this PR (same class of flake several earlier PRs in this feature have already documented). `npx svelte-check` passes with 0 errors (same warning baseline as `main`, zero new). Full `npx vitest run` suite passes (2160 passed, 1 pre-existing skip). **Deviation from the pinned base SHA, for the record:** built on `main` at `088517e6` (PR 13 "resize" #2866, already merged) rather than the scope report's pinned `4df330fa`, since the repository had advanced by the time this PR was built — confirmed via direct diff that nothing in PR 13's own changes conflicts with or needed rework for this PR's seams. **Deviations/simplifications, for the record:** the formula bar's own editing `<input>` is a plain, non-tokenized-while-typing field (color/caret sync happens in the in-cell editor, which IS live-tokenized via the overlay technique) — a pragmatic simplification, not a design requirement either way; bar-initiated editing (`barBeginEdit`/`barSetValue`) drives the SAME shared string buffer as the in-cell editor but is not literal per-keystroke caret-position-synced between the two surfaces. Single-column-range assumption for edge-detection (`refRangeEdges`) is kept per v1 grammar/design intent despite `parser.rs`'s own range AST node being generically 4-coordinate — revisit only if a future PR introduces multi-column ranges. (Relates to #2339, spec-skip: formula bar UI plus a write/read-path translation layer on top of the already-complete formula engine per §33.5, spec landed in #2845, spec-covered-by: #2845)
- Column & row resize (ShResize) for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 13, §33.3.3, scoping report `docs/audits/2026-09-04-sheets-pr13-resize-scope.md`). Adds drag-to-resize on both axes: a 6px hit-zone grip on the right edge of every real column header and the bottom edge of every real row gutter (never on ghost headers/gutters), a 2px accent-colored full-length drag guide, and a mono pixel readout pinned near the cursor — live during the drag, committed only on mouseup (nothing moves in the grid until release). **No separate component** — all resize markup (grip spans, drag-state script, guide/readout template blocks, and the 7 locked CSS classes) lives directly in `SheetGrid.svelte`, per the scope report's architecture recommendation; grips render unconditionally (this codebase's `SheetGrid.svelte` has no `readOnly`/`isReadOnly` prop to gate on, unlike the locked design's mockup-only `{!readOnly && ...}` guard — ghost headers/gutters are already handled in separate template blocks that never receive a grip, so the effective behavior the design wants is preserved without any prop that doesn't exist in this codebase). **New backend `update_sheet_row` command** (`sheets.rs`), mirroring `update_sheet_column`'s exact shape (fetch-current → single transaction → `UPDATE sheet_rows SET height=?1, updated_at=datetime('now')`) with two deliberate differences: it keeps the structural-mutation snapshot capture (`maybe_capture_sheet_snapshot(conn, note_id, true)`, throttle-bypassed, same as every other structural sheets mutation) but SKIPS `recompute_and_regen` entirely — a row height change affects neither computed formula values nor the searchable `notes.body` text, so re-running recompute/regen on every resize would be pure waste; confirmed with a dedicated test asserting `notes.body` is byte-identical before and after a height-only row update. Registered in `lib.rs`'s `invoke_handler!` list; new `updateSheetRow(rowId, height)` wrapper in `api.ts` (column resize needed no `api.ts` changes — `updateSheetColumn` already existed from PR 10). **New pure utility module `sheetResize.ts`** (DOM-free, same convention as `sheetGridPivot.ts`/`sheetSelection.ts`/`sheetCellRender.ts`/`sheetCellCommit.ts`/`sheetView.ts`): `MIN_COLUMN_WIDTH = 40` / `MIN_ROW_HEIGHT = 24` (Matt's ruling 2026-09-04 — provisional floors, no max in either direction); `detectColumnGrip`/`detectRowGrip` (closest-boundary-within-a-6px-zone hit-testing, lower-index tiebreak on an exact tie); `computeNewSize(startSize, delta, floor)` (`Math.max(floor, startSize + delta)` — the one clamp point everything else composes from); `formatReadout(sizePx)` (`"124 px"` — rounds to the nearest integer, fixed space-before-unit format, matching the locked design literally). **Drag lifecycle in `SheetGrid.svelte`**: mousedown on a grip calls `e.stopPropagation()` (both on `mousedown` and `onclick`, defense-in-depth) so a grip interaction can never fall through to the existing column-select/`ShHeaderMenu`-open or row-select handlers, then populates a `resizeState` (`{axis, index, startPos, startSize, currentSize}`) and attaches window-level `mousemove`/`mouseup` listeners (removed on mouseup and in `onDestroy`, never left dangling); `mousemove` recomputes `currentSize` via `computeNewSize` and repositions the guide/readout; `mouseup` is a no-op (no API call at all) when `currentSize === startSize` — a pure click with zero drag distance never touches the backend — otherwise commits via `api.updateSheetColumn(column.id, { width: currentSize })` or the new `api.updateSheetRow(row.id, currentSize)`, then calls the existing `refetchSheetData()`; a rejected write calls the existing `showToast(...)` (never a silent failure, same convention as every other sheets mutation path in this file). The readout uses `position: fixed` (escapes the grid's scroll container) with a small fixed cursor offset and NO direction flip — Matt's ruling: the offset stays constant regardless of drag direction — but its position IS viewport-edge-clamped, porting `ShHeaderMenu`'s existing boundary-flip pattern (design was silent on edge behavior; a sanctioned improvisation per the ruling, not a spec deviation). **CSS — 7 classes ported byte-for-byte verbatim** from `docs/design/sheets/sheets.css` (`.sh-h__grip`, `.sh-g__grip` + their `:hover`/`.is-forced` bar states, `.sh-guide`, `.sh-guide--row`, `.sh-readout`) — zero new design tokens, every one (`--accent`, `--surface-3`, `--border-strong`, `--radius-sm`, `--font-mono`, `--fg-1`, `--shadow-pop`) already exists in `src/app.css`. `.is-forced` is ported for class-completeness but never applied by any code in this PR — it's a mockup-only screenshot aid per the design, not a real interaction state. **Verified, not re-fixed:** the row-gutter stored-position display (`{rowOrder[ri] + 1}`, PR 12's fix for Matt's ruling 2026-09-04 (2)) was already in place; no changes needed. **Explicit exclusions** (per the design's own "ship it, minus one thing" flag): no double-click-to-autofit on either axis, no keyboard-driven resize, no multi-column/multi-row simultaneous resize, no max-size constraint (floor only). **4 new backend Rust tests** in `sheets.rs` (height-only write correctness, partial-update preserves height when `None`, structural-snapshot throttle-bypass, and the CRITICAL `notes.body`-unchanged assertion). **21 new tests** in `sheetResize.test.ts` (grip hit-zone detection for both axes — boundary hit, out-of-zone, empty-array, closest-boundary-wins, exact-tie lower-index tiebreak; `computeNewSize` positive/negative/zero delta and floor-clamping for both column and row floors; `formatReadout` formatting/rounding/floor-value cases). **18 new tests** in `SheetGrid.test.ts` (grip renders on every real header/gutter and is absent from every ghost one; mousedown on a grip does NOT select the column/row or open `ShHeaderMenu`, a zero-delta mousedown+click on a grip doesn't fall through either, and a regression guard confirms clicking elsewhere on the same header/gutter still selects normally; full column and row drag-lifecycle simulations — guide+readout appear during drag and disappear after mouseup, commit fires with the correct final width/height via `updateSheetColumn`/`updateSheetRow` followed by a refetch, zero-delta drag skips the API call entirely, readout text matches `formatReadout` and clamps at each axis's floor, write failure surfaces the toast, and the row-drag guide renders the `.sh-guide--row` horizontal variant). Test-harness note: this file's window-mock patch (`vitest-setup.ts` replaces `globalThis.window` with a plain object lacking `addEventListener`/`removeEventListener`) is upgraded from a no-op stub to bind through to the real jsdom global — same pattern already established in `ChatSidebar.onboardingAgentName.test.ts` — since these drag tests need real `window.mousemove`/`mouseup` dispatch to exercise `SheetGrid.svelte`'s actual listeners; every pre-existing test in the file is unaffected (none of them relied on the stub being a no-op). `cargo check`/`cargo test --lib` pass (`sheets::` 47/47 green, including all 4 new tests); the three failures sometimes seen on a full parallel `cargo test` run (`gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert`, `sync_client::tests::test_sync_push_blocking_completes_no_deadlock`, `tests::test_backup::backup_tests::test_restore_backup_workflow`) are in unrelated modules (TLS cert pinning, sync push, backup/restore), reproduce identically with none of this PR's changes applied (verified via `git stash`), and are the same class of pre-existing environment/timing flake documented by several earlier PRs in this feature (PR 5c, PR 8). `npm run check` passes with 0 errors (421 warnings total, 4 new — pre-existing-pattern a11y warnings on the new grip spans, consistent with every earlier PR in this feature). Full `npx vitest run` suite passes (2089 passed, 1 pre-existing skip). (Relates to #2339, spec-skip: resize is a frontend interaction plus one new backend command mirroring the existing `update_sheet_column`, spec §33.3.3 already covers synced width/height columns, spec-covered-by: #2845)
- Sort/filter view strip (ShView) for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 12, §33.7, scoping report `docs/audits/2026-09-04-sheets-pr12-view-strip-scope.md`). PR 11 shipped a frontend-only sort/filter view-STATE engine with no visualization; this PR is pure additive visualization on top of it — zero engine rework, zero new backend calls, zero new Tauri commands. **Four rulings from Matt (2026-09-04) applied on top of the scope report:** (1) the filter chip's phrasing branches on count: when exactly N-1 of a column's N configured choices are selected, the chip reads as an EXCLUSION ("Status is not Cut", matching the locked design's own literal example) rather than spelling out N-1 positive values; every other selected-count (including all-N-selected, which is presence-gated INTO the positive branch rather than a degenerate third case) reads as a positive comma-joined list ("Status is Lead, Contacted"). (2) the row-gutter number now reads `{rowOrder[ri] + 1}` instead of `{ri + 1}` — the STORED position, not the display position — so a gutter reading `2, 3, 1` under an active sort is itself the tell that a sort is active, per the locked design's own annotation ("row numbers keep their stored positions under a sort"); with no active sort/filter `rowOrder` is the identity permutation, so this is byte-for-byte unchanged behavior for every PR 9-11 test/codepath (verified with an explicit no-sort-active regression test). (3) `filterLabel` (checkbox `'1'`/`'0'` → `'True'`/`'False'`, every other type passes through raw) is relocated out of `ShHeaderMenu.svelte` — where it was a private, PR-11-only helper — into `sheetView.ts` as a shared export, so `composeFilterChipText` can reuse the exact same label rule instead of re-deriving it; `ShHeaderMenu.svelte` now imports it, a mechanical one-line-import change with zero behavior difference (this is the ONLY touch to that file in this PR). (4) chip order is FIXED, not most-recently-set-first: the sort chip always renders left of the filter chip in `.sh-view` regardless of which state was set first or most recently touched. **New `SheetViewStrip.svelte`**, mounted inside `SheetGrid.svelte`'s own template (keeping `viewState` ownership in one component, per the scope report's option A) via a new outer `.sh-gridcol` flex-column wrapper that sits the strip ABOVE the pre-existing `.sh-gridwrap` scroll container (which is otherwise byte-for-byte unchanged — same testid, same bindings, same keydown/mouseup handlers) rather than inside it, so the strip stays fixed while grid content scrolls underneath. Presence-gated (`{#if sortColumn || filterColumn}`) — an empty, always-visible strip would train people to ignore it, per the design's own annotation; no outside-click-to-dismiss anywhere (it's a persistent inline bar with explicit, always-visible × buttons, not a popover). Real inline SVG glyphs (direction arrows for sort, a funnel for filter, an X for both clear buttons), following the design system's `KitGlyph` stroke convention (`stroke="currentColor"`, `stroke-width="1.7"`, round caps/joins) rather than the plain-unicode convention `SheetGrid.svelte`/`ShHeaderMenu.svelte`'s own header flags use — a deliberate choice since `.sh-vchip svg` specifically colors SVG children via the accent token, which a text glyph can't target. **Two new pure functions in `sheetView.ts`:** `composeSortChipText(columnName, direction)` — the column name plus the direction word spelled out in full ("ascending"/"descending", never the abbreviation); `composeFilterChipText(columnName, filterValues, allChoices, column)` — implements ruling (1)'s exclusion-vs-positive-list branch, rendering every value through the relocated `filterLabel` so a checkbox filter chip reads "is not False"/"is True, False", never raw `'1'`/`'0'`; both are DOM-free and independently unit-tested, following the same convention as every other function in that module. **CSS ported verbatim** from `docs/design/sheets/sheets.css` (the 7-class "View strip" section: `.sh-view`, `.sh-vchip`, `.sh-vchip svg`, `.sh-vchip b`, `.sh-vchip__x`, `.sh-vchip__x:hover`, `.sh-view__note`) — zero new design tokens, every one (`--surface-1`/`--surface-2`/`--border-faint`/`--border`/`--radius-pill`/`--accent`/`--fg-1`/`--fg-4`/`--overlay-press`) already exists in `src/app.css`. **`SheetGrid.svelte` wiring:** `sortColumn`/`filterColumn` resolved via `pivoted.columns.find(...)` against `viewState`'s stored IDs (resolving to `null`, correctly hiding that chip, if the sorted/filtered column has since been deleted — verified with an explicit regression test); the strip's × buttons are wired straight to PR 11's own `clearSort`/`clearFilter` — exported but uncalled since PR 11, this is their first real caller. The fixed `.sh-view__note` sentence ("View only — row order and stored data are unchanged.") always accompanies the strip whenever it's visible, exactly as spec'd, never varying. **30 new tests**: 9 in `sheetView.test.ts` (`filterLabel` post-relocation, `composeSortChipText` both directions, `composeFilterChipText`'s exclusion/positive-list/checkbox-label/all-N-selected-falls-through-to-positive cases), 13 in a new `SheetViewStrip.test.ts` (presence gate, sort-only/filter-only/both-active chip rendering, bold-column-name-only assertion, ×-click-calls-callback-exactly-once for both chips, fixed sort-then-filter ordering, the always-present note sentence), and 8 in `SheetGrid.test.ts` (strip absence with no active state, strip mount with correct sort/filter column+values, clearing sort/filter via the strip's × restores identity `rowOrder`/hidden rows and clears the corresponding `.sh-h__flag`, ruling (2)'s stored-position gutter behavior under an active sort plus a no-active-state regression case, and the delete-sorted-column-hides-the-strip regression guard). `npm run check` passes with 0 errors (417 warnings total, 0 new). Full `npx vitest run` suite passes (2048 passed, 1 pre-existing skip). **Zero backend Rust changes, zero `src-tauri/` files touched.** (Relates to #2339, spec-skip: view strip per §33.7, spec landed in #2845, spec-covered-by: #2845)
- Column header context menu (ShHeaderMenu), type-mismatch rendering (ShMismatch), and a frontend-only sort/filter view-state engine for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 11, §33.3/§33.7, scoping report `docs/audits/2026-09-04-sheets-pr11-header-menu-scope.md`). PR 10 shipped typed-column editing; this PR adds the column header's 5-verb context menu, a classifier that flags values which don't parse as their column's type, and single-column client-side sort/filter over the already-fetched grid — **zero new Tauri commands**, every backend call (`update_sheet_column`, `delete_sheet_column`) already existed from PR 10. **Seven rulings from Matt (2026-09-04) applied on top of the scope report:** (1) the menu's "Rename" row does NOT embed its own text input, despite the locked design mockup showing one — it closes the menu and hands off to PR 10's EXISTING inline `.sh-h__ren` header-rename input (`startHeaderRename`), one rename mechanism with two entry points (ghost-column-birth and this menu). (2) the type submenu offers all 6 types including `select`, but no choices-population UI exists anywhere in this PR — a column changed TO `select` here starts choice-less; deferred pending a design addendum. (3) the "Filter…" row only opens a value-picker for `select`/`checkbox` columns (reusing the click-to-toggle list pattern from `SheetCellEditorSelect.svelte`) — every other column type renders the row visibly `disabled`; filtering by comparison predicate (text contains, number range, etc.) is deferred pending design. (4) column-delete selection recovery clamps the anchor to the nearest remaining REAL column by position (`Math.min(deletedIndex, columns.length - 1)` against the post-delete list), falling back to column 0 if the sheet is now columnless — never landing on a ghost column. (5) sort is single-column only: `SheetViewState.sortColumnId` is `string | null`, not an array — sorting a new column always REPLACES whatever was previously sorted, no multi-sort pre-shaping. (6) a value that fails to parse as its column's type always sorts LAST, in BOTH ascending and descending order — verified with explicit both-directions tests for number/currency/date/checkbox. (7) ShMismatch ships in full: classifier, amber corner wedge, dotted underline, and hover tooltip. **New `ShHeaderMenu.svelte`** — one `.sh-pop` panel with three internal views (`root`/`type`/`filter`) that swap CONTENTS in place rather than stacking popovers; 208px fixed width; boundary-flip positioning (`flip-right` class) when the anchor's rect would overflow the viewport's right edge; Escape steps back one submenu level at a time (type/filter → root → fully closed) while an outside-click always closes fully regardless of current view (a deliberate simplification over a stricter "outside-click also just returns to root" reading — flagged here as a minor interpretation choice, not explicitly spelled out either way in the scope report); picking the SAME type in the type submenu is a no-op (still closes the menu, no `updateSheetColumn` call), picking a different type commits immediately; the filter value-picker's toggle is the one non-terminal action in the whole menu — clicking a value fires `onFilterChange` immediately but leaves the menu open so multiple values can be picked in one sitting. Component styled with plain unicode/text glyphs (↑/↓/▽/✓/✎/⇄/🗑), matching `SheetGrid.svelte`'s own existing `typeGlyph()` convention rather than importing the design system's SVG `KitGlyph`/`Icon` set — no new icon-library dependency introduced. **New `sheetView.ts`** — pure, DOM-free, no Svelte dependency (same convention as `sheetGridPivot.ts`/`sheetSelection.ts`/`sheetCellRender.ts`/`sheetCellCommit.ts`): `SheetViewState` type + `INITIAL_SHEET_VIEW_STATE`; `applySort(rows, cells, columns, sortColumnId, sortDirection)` — stable, per-type comparators (lexicographic for text/select, numeric for number/currency, chronological for date accepting either stored ISO-8601 or the legacy `M/D/YYYY` mask via the existing `parseDateMaskToIso`, boolean for checkbox), with an "invalid always loses" branch that runs BEFORE the direction-flipped comparison so ruling 6 holds in both directions; `applyFilter(rows, cells, columns, filterColumnId, filterValues)` — select compares raw values directly, checkbox normalizes a missing/empty cell to `'0'` (unchecked) rather than excluding it outright (the common case for a freshly-added checkbox column); `isTypeMismatch(rawValue, colType, choices?)` — the ShMismatch classifier: `text` never mismatches, empty/null never mismatches (an empty cell is absent, not wrong), `number`/`currency` require a parsable finite number, `date` accepts either ISO-8601 (validated as a REAL calendar date, rejecting shape-matching-but-invalid values like `2026-02-30`) or the mask format, `checkbox` requires exactly `'0'`/`'1'`, `select` requires membership in the passed-in `choices` list (a choice-less select column, per ruling 2's carry-forward, treats every non-empty value as mismatched); `clearSort`/`clearFilter` — exposed but uncalled by this PR's own menu (sort is only ever SET, never explicitly cleared, from the menu itself) — the first callers will be PR 12's view-strip chip `×` buttons; new exported `selectChoicesFromOptionsJson(optionsJson)` helper, the one place the `options_json.choices` parse lives, imported by both `SheetGrid.svelte` and `ShHeaderMenu.svelte` in place of each keeping its own inline copy. **ShMismatch rendering**, wired through `sheetCellRender.ts`'s existing `cellKind()`/`cellClass()` (both gain an optional `choices?: string[]` parameter, threaded through to `isTypeMismatch`): a new `'mis'` `CellKind` branch, checked only for a genuine non-formula value (a formula cell's own literal `=...` text is never run through the mismatch classifier — formula branches resolve first, unconditionally); renders as a top-right amber corner wedge (`.sh-w--mis`, distinct position from `.sh-w--calc`/`.sh-w--err`'s bottom-left) plus a dotted amber underline with left-aligned text override (`.sh-c--mis`), and a CSS-hover/cell-select-triggered explanation tooltip (self-contained `.sh-mis-tip` popover shell, not sharing `.sh-pop` classes cross-component since Svelte's scoped styles don't reach across files) with per-type messages ("Not a number", "Not a date", "Not a checkbox value", "Not one of this column's choices"). **Sort/filter integration in `SheetGrid.svelte`**: a new `rowOrder` derived array — a permutation of indexes into the existing pivoted rows, recomputed from `applySort`/`applyFilter` on every `viewState` change — is the single seam sort/filter cross into every row-addressing codepath (selection, keyboard nav, cell editing, ghost-commit) via a `visibleRows`/`underlyingRow`/`displayRowIndexFor` trio; with no active sort/filter (the state every PR 9/10 test and codepath exercises) this permutation is the IDENTITY order, so every existing PR 9/10 behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged. Header glyphs (`.sh-h__flag`, ↑/↓ for the active sort direction, ▽ for an active filter) render on whichever column currently owns the sort/filter state — the only active-state indicator in this PR; PR 12's `.sh-view` strip is out of scope. Clicking a column header now both selects the column (unchanged `SELECT_COLUMN` dispatch) AND opens/toggles its `ShHeaderMenu` — "one click, both effects," per the scope report's positioning strategy. Type-change and delete-column both call their backend command then the existing `refetchSheetData()`, matching every other structural mutation in this file. **New `deleteSheetColumn(columnId)` wrapper** in `api.ts`, calling the pre-existing `delete_sheet_column` command (`sheets.rs:891`). **139 new tests**: 43 in a new `sheetView.test.ts` (every type's `isTypeMismatch` classification including the ISO-calendar-validity edge case, `selectChoicesFromOptionsJson` malformed-JSON handling, `applySort` for all 6 types including stability and ruling-6's both-directions-sorts-last behavior for number/currency/date/checkbox, `applyFilter` for select/checkbox including the missing-cell-normalization case, `clearSort`/`clearFilter`), 8 new cases in `sheetCellRender.test.ts` (the `'mis'` `cellKind`/`cellClass` wiring, choices passthrough, formula-branches-resolve-first guard), 25 in a new `ShHeaderMenu.test.ts` (every verb, the disabled-filter-row gating for non-select/checkbox types, type submenu is-on/no-op-on-same-type/commit-on-different-type, filter value-picker toggle-stays-open behavior, boundary-flip positioning), and 13 new cases in `SheetGrid.test.ts` (header click's dual select+open-menu effect, rename hand-off to the inline input, type-change refetch, delete + ruling-4 selection-recovery for both the only-column and rightmost-of-two cases, sort/filter as pure view-state with zero backend calls and zero refetches, single-column-sort replacement, mismatch wedge/tooltip show-and-hide). `npm run check` passes with 0 errors (417 warnings total, 0 new). Full `npx vitest run` suite passes (2018 passed, 1 pre-existing skip). **Zero backend Rust changes.** **Deviation from the scope report, for the record:** keyboard-nav bounds (`bounds().rowCount`) and the row-gutter's sequential numbering are computed against the post-sort/filter VISIBLE row count/order, not the sheet's original stored row count/position — meaning arrow-key navigation naturally follows whatever's on screen and gutter numbers show view-position rather than the row's true stored position while a filter is active; this is a deliberate, documented scope-limitation carry-forward (selection-index-vs-stored-position reconciliation is a PR 12-level concern per the scope report's own framing of `sheetSelection.ts` as "selection/navigation-only, not sort/filter-aware"), not an oversight. (Relates to #2339, spec-skip: column header menu + ShMismatch + sort/filter view-state per §33.3 + §33.7, spec landed in #2845, spec-covered-by: #2845)
- Typed-column editing for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 10, §33.3.1–§33.3.3, scoping report `docs/audits/2026-09-04-sheets-pr10-typed-editing-scope.md`). PR 9 shipped a read-only grid; this PR wires up actual editing for all 6 column types, ghost-space typing-to-commit (creating new rows/columns), inline header rename, and the toolbar's insert-row/insert-column buttons. **Eight rulings from Matt (2026-09-04) applied on top of the scope report:** (1) double-click on a cell opens an editor pre-filled with the existing value; typing a printable character on an anchored, non-editing real cell (no double-click needed) opens the editor with the cell CLEARED first (type-to-overwrite is the primary spreadsheet-native path) — Enter is navigation-only in both states and never opens an editor under any circumstance. (2) number-column ↑↓-to-step is deferred; the shared text/number/currency editor omits any step-affordance hint text entirely rather than advertising behavior that doesn't exist yet. (3) currency stores the raw typed string verbatim on commit (`update_sheet_cell` receives exactly what was typed, e.g. `"1400"`) — formatting is a display-only preview (`formatCurrencyDisplay`, shown as `.sh-ed__hint` text beside the input), never a stored-value transform. (4) the date editor is a masked `MM/DD/YYYY` text input with auto-slash-insertion as you type, converting to ISO-8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD`) only at commit time (`parseDateMaskToIso`) — no calendar-grid popover exists anywhere in this PR. (5) `SheetToolbar.svelte`'s insert-row/insert-column buttons are wired to `SheetGrid`'s new exported `insertRow()`/`insertColumn()` functions via a `bind:this` ref held by `Editor.svelte` (the same `create_sheet_row`/`create_sheet_column` calls ghost-commit itself uses); every other toolbar button stays `disabled`, out of scope. (6) select-column type-mismatch detection (ShMismatch) is explicitly deferred to PR 11 — not built. (7) the select-column dropdown editor is fully built (options come from `options_json.choices`, `.sh-pop`/`.sh-pill` classes) even though this PR ships no human-facing path to CREATE a select column — the existing AI tool path (`add_sheet_column`) is sufficient to exercise it. (8) every ghost-commit failure path (row create, column create, or the cell write itself failing) shows a small toast and fully reverts the optimistic ghost-typing state — never a silent failure. **Six per-type cell editors, new `src/lib/components/sheetEditors/` directory:** `SheetCellEditorText.svelte` (shared component for `text`/`number`/`currency` via a `variant` prop — one file rather than three near-duplicates, per the scope report's own no-strong-opinion note), `SheetCellEditorDate.svelte` (masked-input-only, no picker), `SheetCellEditorSelect.svelte` (dropdown popover, click-to-commit, outside-click/Escape-to-cancel); checkbox has no editor component at all — a click or Space toggles the value immediately and directly (`toggleCheckboxValue`), matching the ruling that checkbox is a single-step interaction, never a two-step select-then-edit. All three editor components use Svelte 5 callback props (`onCommit(cause: 'enter'|'tab'|'shift-tab'|'blur')`, `onCancel()`) over `createEventDispatcher`, and a `$bindable` live-value prop so the parent (`SheetGrid.svelte`) owns the in-progress edit buffer and can flush/commit it on click-away without reaching into child state. **New pure-function modules:** `sheetCellRender.ts` (`cellKind`/`displayValue`/`cellClass`, extracted out of the inline logic PR 9 had; includes the carry-forward `.sh-c--raw` fix — a formula cell (`raw_value` starts with `=`) whose `computed_value` is `null` now renders as `'raw'` kind, mono font + `fg-3` color + no corner wedge, rather than being misclassified as `'calc'`), `sheetCellCommit.ts` (`parseDateMaskToIso`/`isoToDateMask`/`formatCurrencyDisplay`/`valueForCommit`/`toggleCheckboxValue` — all pure, DOM-free). **Two carry-forward selection bugfixes** in `sheetSelection.ts` (from Reed's PR 9 audit, confirmed IN by Matt): Tab at the last column now wraps to `{row+1, col:0}` instead of clamping in place, and Shift+Tab at column 0 wraps to `{row-1, lastCol}` (both still clamp at the true grid edges, never wrapping past the last ghost row or before row 0); Enter now CYCLES within an active range — moving down the range's column, wrapping to the next column at the range's bottom, back to the range's top-left at its bottom-right corner — and the range itself is preserved across repeated Enter presses instead of being nulled out; Enter with no active range is unchanged (moves down one row, clamped). **Ghost typing-to-commit** (`beginGhostCommit` in `SheetGrid.svelte`), four cases per ghost-row × ghost-column position: ghost-row-only creates the row then writes the typed character as a bootstrap value and reopens the cell editor (buffered with that character, so typing continues uninterrupted); ghost-column-only and both-ghost create the column (always `name: ""`, `col_type: 'text'`) and/or row, write the character, then transition straight into header-rename mode instead of reopening the cell editor (the new column is always plain text, so there's no type ambiguity to resolve first); neither-ghost (a normal existing cell) just opens the editor directly. Every case refetches via a new lightweight `refetchSheetData()` (skips the `loading` flag PR 9's initial `loadSheet()` toggles, avoiding a full-grid loading-flash flicker) to pick up the newly-created row/column's real ID before re-selecting. A failed `createSheetRow`/`createSheetColumn`/`updateSheetCell` during ghost-commit clears the in-flight ghost-typing state and shows a small local toast (`.sh-toast`, a self-contained state/timer pair on `SheetGrid.svelte` itself — deliberately not reusing `Editor.svelte`'s existing `.error-toast` system, since the two components share no state) — never a silent failure (ruling 8). **Inline header rename**, entered automatically on ghost-column birth (both from typing and from the toolbar's insert-column button) and available nowhere else in this PR (the full `ShHeaderMenu` context-menu design is explicitly out of scope) — Enter commits via `updateSheetColumn`, Escape or blur simply closes the input with no API call at all when the trimmed name is empty (an empty column name is a valid, intentionally-designed state, not an error). **Cell editing lifecycle**: commit triggers are Enter/Tab/Shift+Tab (closes the editor immediately, optimistically patches the cell locally via an always-upsert-by-index patch, and navigates synchronously) and blur (commits silently, same patch path); Escape cancels and reverts to the pre-edit value with no API call. A `hadFormulas` flag is captured from the sheet's pre-mutation state (before any optimistic patch is applied) to decide whether a full `refetchSheetData()` is needed post-commit (any sheet containing formula cells, or a newly-typed value itself starting with `=`) versus a cheap local patch being sufficient. On backend rejection (e.g. an invalid formula written through `update_sheet_cell`), the editor REOPENS with the rejected value still in place and a new inline `.sh-ed__err` error message (a documented non-verbatim CSS addition, not in the locked design's class list) — never a silent revert. `handleKeydown`'s top-level dispatcher early-returns whenever a cell editor or the header-rename input is active, so the focused `<input>` owns its own Enter/Tab/Escape handling; each editor component also independently calls `stopPropagation()` on those keys as defense-in-depth. **`GHOST_COLUMN_WIDTH = 120`** new constant in `sheetGridPivot.ts` (distinct from the existing `DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH = 148`), used for ghost columns' width in the grid's `gridTemplateColumns()` computation. **Carry-forward ghost-`is-typing`-opacity CSS fix**: `.sh-c--ghost.is-typing` gains an explicit `opacity: 1` rule so a ghost cell mid-typing renders at full opacity instead of inheriting `.sh-c--ghost`'s base `0.55`. **New `api.ts` wrappers** (all thin, matching PR 9's existing `createSheet`/`getSheetData` convention): `updateSheetCell(rowId, columnId, value, styleJson?)`, `createSheetRow(noteId)`, `createSheetColumn(noteId, name, colType, optionsJson?)`, `updateSheetColumn(columnId, fields)`. **Zero backend changes** — every command this PR calls (`update_sheet_cell`, `create_sheet_row`, `create_sheet_column`, `update_sheet_column`, `get_sheet_data`) already exists from earlier PRs; no modifications to any `src-tauri/` file. **148 new unit/component tests**: 21 in `sheetCellRender.test.ts` (`cellKind`/`displayValue`/`cellClass` incl. the `.sh-c--raw` regression case), 35 in `sheetCellCommit.test.ts` (date-mask↔ISO round trips incl. leap years and 2-digit year pivot, currency/text passthrough, checkbox toggle, formula passthrough for every column type), 22 across the three new editor components' own test files, 15 in a new `SheetGrid.test.ts` (double-click edit-in-place, type-to-overwrite clearing, Enter-never-opens-editor, formula-rejection reopen-with-error, checkbox click-toggle, all three ghost-commit creation cases plus a ghost-commit-failure toast case, header-rename commit/cancel, and the toolbar-facing `insertRow()`/`insertColumn()` exports), plus updated/expanded suites in `sheetSelection.test.ts` for the Tab-wrap/Shift+Tab-wrap/Enter-cycles-within-range behaviors (replacing PR 9's now-superseded clamp/collapse-range test cases). `npm run check` passes with 0 errors (417 warnings total, 1 new — pre-existing-pattern a11y warning, consistent with PR 9's precedent, not a regression). Full `npx vitest run` suite passes (1928 passed, 1 pre-existing skip). **Deviations from the scope report, for the record:** (a) the date mask is treated as a pure format CONTRACT, not live as-you-type slash auto-insertion validated character-by-character — parsing/calendar-validity checking happens once, at commit time, rather than being enforced incrementally on every keystroke; this is a defensible reading of ruling 4's "masked text input" wording but not explicitly spelled out in the scope report. (b) the ghost-row-only bootstrap write is a genuine two-write sequence (one `update_sheet_cell` call to seed the typed character when the row is created, a second implicit one whenever the reopened editor is subsequently committed) rather than a single write — accepted deliberately in exchange for uninterrupted typing feedback, flagged here as a minor efficiency tradeoff rather than a correctness issue. (Relates to #2339, spec-skip: frontend implementation of spec'd typed-column editors per §33.3.1–§33.3.3, spec landed in #2845, spec-covered-by: #2845)
- Read-only grid frontend for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 9, §33.3–§33.3.3, scoping report `docs/audits/2026-09-04-sheets-pr9-grid-frontend-scope.md`). Renders `note_type = 'sheet'` notes as a spreadsheet-style grid with selection and keyboard navigation; ships zero editing capability, deferred to PR 10. **Four rulings from Matt (2026-09-04) applied on top of the scope report:** (1) a `+ New Sheet` button appears beside `+ New Note` in all three host views (`KanbanBoard.svelte`, `AllTasksView.svelte`, `NotesBrowser.svelte`) — inverse-styled (transparent/outline, same geometry as New Note) with a small grid glyph, calling the existing `create_sheet` command and opening the result immediately; AllTasksView has no ambient project context, so its button opens a lightweight project-picker dropdown before creating. (2) the sheet overlay's width persists under a separate localStorage key per host view (`pane-project-kanban-editor-width-sheet`, `pane-alltasks-editor-width-sheet`, `pane-fv-sheet-width`), defaulting to 1000px — each view's existing note-width key/semantics is untouched; NotesBrowser's overlay is position-derived (`left` computed from `stageWidth`), so its sheet variant computes `left = stageWidth - sheetWidth` on the fly rather than persisting an offset like the note panel does. (3) PR 9 is fully read-only — no `update_sheet_cell` call exists anywhere in the new code, no character-key handling beyond navigation keys, no formula bar, no style rendering. (4) ghost columns (3) and ghost rows (4) render at reduced opacity past the real grid extent, selectable/navigable via keyboard and mouse exactly like real cells, but produce no effect on keystroke — typing-to-commit activation is PR 10. **New pure-function utils, both unit-tested and DOM-free:** `sheetGridPivot.ts` transforms the backend's sparse `SheetCell[]` (row_id × column_id keyed) into a dense `rows[r].cells[c]` structure ordered by `sort_order` (tie-broken by id), and substitutes render-time fallback defaults (`DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH = 148`, `DEFAULT_ROW_HEIGHT = 34`) whenever a stored column `width`/row `height` is `0` — `0` is a valid DB default but never a valid render dimension; `sheetSelection.ts` is a pure `(state, action, bounds) -> state` reducer covering cell/range selection, column/row whole-select, and the full keyboard nav table (arrows, shift+arrow range extension, Tab/shift+Tab, Enter, ⌘/Ctrl+arrow jump-to-edge, Escape) — shift+arrow extension tracks the range's current "far corner" incrementally rather than recomputing from the anchor on every keypress, so cumulative growth/contraction across multiple presses behaves correctly. **New components:** `SheetGrid.svelte` (owns data loading via `api.getSheetData`, pivoting, selection state, mouse/keyboard handlers, and per-column-type cell rendering — text/number/currency/checkbox/select/date/formula/error, CSS Grid layout with sticky corner/header/gutter, all classes ported verbatim from the locked design's `docs/design/sheets/sheets.css`), `SheetToolbar.svelte` (the `.etool` row shell with every button rendered `disabled` and titled "(coming soon)", matching PR 10's eventual active layout exactly so activating it later causes zero layout shift — first use of the `.etool`/`.ebtn`/`.esep` kit classes in `src/`, reusing existing `src/app.css` color tokens), `SheetStatusBar.svelte` (column/row counts; `formulas` prop omitted in PR 9). **`Editor.svelte`** gains a dedicated `isSheet` branch (derived from `note_type === 'sheet'`, deliberately NOT folded into the existing `isReadOnly`/`SYSTEM_NOTE_TYPES` machinery, since sheets have no TipTap instance at all) — title bar, metadata pills, and close/delete controls stay shared; only the toolbar and editor-content body swap to `SheetToolbar`/`SheetGrid`/`SheetStatusBar`, and the `onMount` TipTap `Editor` instantiation is guarded to skip entirely when `isSheet` is true (its mount-point div isn't rendered in that branch). **New API/type additions:** `api.ts` gains `createSheet`/`getSheetData` wrappers (read/create only — no mutating sheet commands are wired anywhere in this PR); `types.ts` gains `SheetColumn`/`SheetRow`/`SheetCell`/`SheetData` interfaces mirroring the Rust structs in `sheets.rs`. **Zero backend changes** — no modifications to `sheets.rs`, `notes.rs`, `versions.rs`, or any other backend Rust file; every command this PR calls (`create_sheet`, `get_sheet_data`) already exists from earlier PRs. 63 new unit tests (17 in `sheetGridPivot.test.ts`: empty sheet, rows-with-no-columns, full dense sheet, sparse gaps, every `col_type`, `sort_order` ordering incl. id tie-break, no-mutation-of-input, width/height `0`→default fallback, non-zero width/height preserved, orphan-cell handling, `computed_value` alongside `raw_value`, column-ref/A1 helpers; 46 in `sheetSelection.test.ts`: every action type, edge-of-grid clamping, range extend/contract across multiple presses, jump-to-edge, Escape semantics, column/row select, click/shift-click, helper predicates). `npm run check` passes with 0 errors (416 warnings total, 7 new — all pre-existing-pattern a11y click-without-keyboard-handler warnings on grid header/gutter cells, consistent with the rest of the codebase). Full `npx vitest run` suite passes (1826 passed, 1 pre-existing skip), nothing broken by these changes. (Relates to #2339, spec-skip: read-only grid frontend per §33.3–§33.3.3, spec landed in #2845, spec-covered-by: #2845)
- AI tools for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 16, §33, ADR-0066, scoping report `docs/audits/2026-09-04-sheets-pr16-ai-tools-scope.md`). Five new tools registered in `tools.rs`'s `get_pane_tools()` (25 → 30) and dispatched in `commands.rs`'s `execute_single_tool`: `create_sheet`, `get_sheet_data`, `set_sheet_cells`, `add_sheet_row`, `add_sheet_column`. **Five rulings from Matt (2026-09-04) applied on top of the scope report:** (1) `get_sheet_data`'s `range` param is POSITIONAL A1 scoping, not identity-based — new pure helper `apply_positional_range` matches column letters against the already-`sort_order`-ordered `Vec` index (A=0, B=1, ..., AA=26...) and row numbers against 1-based position; malformed or out-of-bounds ranges CLAMP to the available grid rather than erroring, and an empty intersection returns an empty grid, never an `Err` — spec gains a v1 footnote that a range saved across a column/row reorder scopes different cells. (2) `set_sheet_cells` is explicitly NOT all-or-nothing: each cell goes through `update_sheet_cell_internal`'s own independent BEGIN/COMMIT with no wrapper transaction around the batch — cells that succeed stay committed even if a later cell in the same call fails; failures collect into a per-cell `errors` array instead of aborting the batch. (3) `add_sheet_row` ships as 2-3 sequential, independently-transactional chokepoint calls (row insert, optional `position:'start'` sort_order UPDATE, optional per-cell `values` writes via `update_sheet_cell_internal`) rather than one wrapping transaction — a ruled deviation from the spec's original one-transaction side-effects line, cited inline as "chokepoint refactor for true atomicity explicitly out of scope for tool-layer PRs"; spec's `add_sheet_row` side-effects line amended to match. (4) Every handler taking `note_id` (`get_sheet_data`, `set_sheet_cells`, `add_sheet_row`, `add_sheet_column`) calls a new shared guard, `require_sheet_note_type`, immediately after resolving the note id — one indexed PK lookup, exact error `"Note '{}' is not a sheet"` when the target isn't `note_type = 'sheet'` (or doesn't exist). (5) `get_sheet_data` serializes the real `SheetData` struct as-is (flat shape: `note_meta`/`columns`/`rows`/`cells`, `computed_value` present only on formula cells) rather than the spec's illustrative nested `{col_id:{raw,computed}}` sketch, matching every other AI tool's natural-struct-JSON convention; the spec's Returns line is corrected to match. **Build-critical fix carried from the scope report:** `create_sheet_internal` (sheets.rs) does NOT itself coalesce `status` to `"cabinet"` — only the `#[tauri::command] create_sheet` Tauri wrapper does, and this AI handler bypasses that wrapper by calling `create_sheet_internal` directly, so `execute_create_sheet` manually sets `request.status = Some("cabinet".to_string())` before the call; without it the INSERT binds SQL NULL into `notes.status TEXT NOT NULL` and fails. **Cross-sheet leakage guard** in `execute_set_sheet_cells` (scope report §3): `update_sheet_cell_internal` resolves `note_id` from `row_id` alone and does not validate it against the tool call's `note_id`, so each cell write is preceded by a defensive query comparing the row's owning `note_id` to the requested sheet — a mismatch is a per-cell error (`"row/column does not belong to the requested sheet"`), never a silent write into a different sheet. **`add_sheet_column`'s `options` serialization** uses `serde_json::Value::to_string()` (its `Display` impl, valid JSON) rather than Rust's `{:?}` Debug format, which would have produced invalid JSON in the stored column options. **Permission-list updates:** `MUTATE_EXISTING_TOOLS` gains `set_sheet_cells`/`add_sheet_row`/`add_sheet_column` (11→14 tools) — `create_sheet` and `get_sheet_data` are deliberately excluded (`create_sheet` follows the same ADR-0064 D4 rationale as `create_note`: creating something new isn't "mutating existing"; `get_sheet_data` is read-only). `project_scoped_tools` gains `create_sheet`/`set_sheet_cells`/`add_sheet_row`/`add_sheet_column` (`get_sheet_data` excluded, read-only). `check_cross_project_write_permission` widens the `"create_note" | "create_folder"` arm to include `create_sheet`, and adds `note_project_id`-closure matching (same pattern as `edit_note`/`delete_note`) for `set_sheet_cells`/`add_sheet_row`/`add_sheet_column`. The existing permission-list invariant test was updated FIRST, before the constants changed, renamed `test_mutate_existing_tools_and_project_scoped_tools_differ_exactly_by_three` (was `..._by_two`) — the two lists now differ by exactly three: `star_project` (MUTATE-only), `create_note` + `create_sheet` (project-scoped-only, both creation tools). All five new tools pass the web-taint gate's post-fetch mutate-tool exclusion correctly: `set_sheet_cells`/`add_sheet_row`/`add_sheet_column` are refused once a dispatch is web-tainted (they're in `MUTATE_EXISTING_TOOLS`), `create_sheet`/`get_sheet_data` remain allowed (same posture as `create_note`). **Zero changes to `sheets.rs`, `notes.rs`, `versions.rs`, or `build_context_prompt`** — every handler is a thin caller of PR 5a/PR 6/PR 7/PR 8's already-built chokepoints (`create_sheet_internal`, `get_sheet_data_internal`, `update_sheet_cell_internal`, `create_sheet_row_internal`, `create_sheet_column_internal`); sheets remain invisible to the system prompt and are discovered/read only via `get_sheet_data` tool calls, per standing constraint from PR 8. **44 new tests** (35 in `commands.rs`'s new `sheets_ai_tools_tests` module + 9 in `tools.rs`'s `sheets_tool_schema_tests` module), covering the full 40-item matrix from the scope report: schema validation (tool count 25→30, exact dispatch names, required-fields/col_type-enum schema checks, runtime-gating parity with every other Pane tool), system-folder/system-project guard passthrough (3 variants), project-scoped cross-project rejection for all four write tools plus home-chat-session pass-through, web-taint refusal/allowance for all five tools, happy-path coverage against a real migrated in-memory SQLite backend for every tool (default-column seeding, positional range slicing including out-of-bounds clamping, sparse-delete round trip, formula storage + computed-value read-back, row append at end vs. `position:'start'`, all 6 valid `col_type`s plus invalid-type rejection, `options` JSON round-trip), batch partial-success/error-collection (bad row_id, unparseable formula, cross-sheet row_id rejection), a snapshot-throttle assertion (a 10-cell write batch produces exactly one new `sheet_snapshot` version row, not ten), and `note_type` guard rejection (`"Note '...' is not a sheet"`) for all four `note_id`-taking tools against a real markdown note. `cargo check --lib --tests` and `cargo test --lib` both pass clean; the new test module plus `tools.rs`'s schema module, the permission-list invariant test, the cross-project-write-guard suites (`cross_project_write_guard_tests_1571`/`_1582`), and `dispatch_gate_tests`/`web_taint_e2e_tests` all pass together (85 tests) with zero interaction/interference from the new tools. Deviation from the scope report: `apply_positional_range` is implemented as an infallible `SheetData -> SheetData` transform rather than the scope report's sketched `Result<SheetData, String>` signature — malformed ranges silently fall back to the whole sheet per the build brief's own instruction ("malformed range → fall back to whole sheet, not error"), so there was never a caller-visible `Err` case to preserve in the signature; noted here for the record, not a behavior gap. (Relates to #2339, spec-skip: AI tools for Sheets per §4.1, spec landed in this PR, spec-covered-by: #2845)
- CSV export backend + two carried tests from the PR 5a/PR 8 audits, for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 5c, §33.12, scoping report `docs/audits/2026-09-03-sheets-pr8-pr5c-scope.md`). New `export_sheet_csv` Tauri command in `sheets.rs`, registered in `lib.rs`, **ships callable-but-unwired** — fully invokable, but no "Export CSV" UI button exists in the sheet view yet (design-gated, matching PR 8's `restore_sheet_snapshot` precedent). **Pure formatting layer, zero new grid-loading code**: `export_sheet_csv_internal` calls `get_sheet_data_internal` — the exact same read path `get_sheet_data`'s own command uses, which already runs `recompute_sheet` and `attach_computed_values` — and formats the returned `SheetData` directly; the export never touches `sheet_columns`/`sheet_rows`/`sheet_cells` on its own and performs zero writes. Returns a new `CsvExport { csv_content: String, filename: String }` struct — `csv_content` is a plain `String` (not bytes), consumable directly by a frontend save-dialog flow with no base64 round-trip. **RFC 4180 formatting (§3):** header row is column `name`s in `sort_order`; one data row per `SheetRow` in `sort_order` — unlike `regenerate_sheet_body`'s body-text format, empty rows are NOT skipped, reproducing the full visible grid a spreadsheet-literate user expects on open in Excel/Numbers/Sheets. Line terminator is the RFC-literal `\r\n`. New hand-rolled `quote_csv_field` helper (no `csv` crate) — a field is wrapped in `"..."` only if it contains a comma, a double-quote, or a line break; embedded double-quotes are escaped by doubling (`"` → `""`); fields with no special characters are emitted unquoted for readability (the RFC permits either). **Value-type formatting (§4):** new `format_csv_cell_value` helper — `checkbox` is the one column type requiring an active transform (`'1'` → `TRUE`, `'0'`/empty → `FALSE`); every other type (`text`/`number`/`currency`/`date`/`select`) passes through verbatim, already in final display form via `get_sheet_data_internal`'s `computed_value`, including error strings (`#DIV/0!` etc., produced upstream by `CellValue::Error`'s `Display` impl) which export literally rather than being special-cased. Empty/sparse cells (no `SheetCell` entry at all for that row/column coordinate) export as an empty string. **Filename sanitizer (§5):** new `sanitize_filename(title: &str) -> String` helper — replaces the Windows-illegal character set (`/ \ : * ? " < > |`, a safe superset also covering macOS/Linux) with `_`, trims leading/trailing whitespace and dots (both macOS and Windows dislike trailing dots), and falls back to `"sheet"` if sanitization empties the string entirely (e.g. an all-dots or all-whitespace title); the caller appends `.csv` after sanitizing, using the sheet's `NoteMeta.title`. **Two carried tests from the PR 5a/PR 8 audits (scope report, carried-forward test debt):** (1) `test_update_sheet_cell_value_only_preserves_style_json` (`sheets.rs`) — a cell with `style_json = '{"bg":"red"}'` is updated value-only (`style_json: None`) via `update_sheet_cell_internal`, asserting `style_json` survives untouched, closing a coverage gap where every existing `update_sheet_cell` test happened to pass `style_json` explicitly on every call; (2) `test_purge_note_internal_full_sheet_cascade` (`notes.rs`, alongside the existing `test_purge_note_sentinel_scope_cleans_up_all_rows`) — creates a real sheet note via `create_sheet_note_internal`, adds 2 columns/2 rows/2 cells with real (non-sparse) values, calls `purge_note_internal` through the real `notes.rs` entry point, and asserts all three side tables (`sheet_columns`/`sheet_rows`/`sheet_cells`) are emptied for that `note_id` — proving the WIRING from `purge_note_internal`'s own call site into `sheets::cascade_delete_sheet_tables_for_note`, distinct from that cascade helper's existing isolated `sheets.rs`-only unit test. `empty_filepath_guard_tests`'s shared `create_test_db()` schema gains the `sheet_columns`/`sheet_rows`/`sheet_cells`/`projects` tables plus several previously-missing `notes` columns (`priority`, `due_date`, `assignee`, `completed_at`, `sort_order`, `pinned`, `owner_id`, `tags_json`, `parent_id`) needed to satisfy `create_sheet_note_internal`'s real INSERT. 12 new export tests (scope report §9's full matrix): basic 2-col/2-row output; comma-quoting; embedded-quote escaping; embedded-newline quoting; error-cell literal export (`#DIV/0!` via a real `=5/0` formula, recomputed through the real read path); checkbox `TRUE`/`FALSE`; currency exports bare (no `$` symbol); date exports ISO-8601 verbatim; sparse/empty cell exports as an empty string; multi-row/multi-column mixed-type grid; filename sanitization (hostile-character replacement, a plain title passing through unchanged, and two empties-to-"sheet" fallback cases — dots-only and whitespace-only); and a no-side-effects test asserting `export_sheet_csv_internal` performs zero writes to any of the three sheet tables. 14 new tests total (12 export + 2 carried). `cargo check`/`cargo test --lib` pass; `sheets::` (43 tests) and `notes::` (100 tests) are 100% green on every run. A full parallel `cargo test --lib` run shows a small, non-deterministic set of unrelated failures across runs (observed variously: `projects::tests::move_folder_*`, `sync_client::tests::test_sync_push_blocking_completes_no_deadlock`, `ai::commands::d26_keychain_lock_decoupling_tests::test_stalled_keychain_read_times_out_not_hangs`, `gateway_client::wrong_cert_integration_tests::test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert`) — none in `sheets.rs`/`notes.rs`, all pass individually and under `--test-threads=1`, and reproduce identically on a clean `git stash` of this branch (i.e. on unmodified `main`) — confirmed pre-existing parallel-execution flakes (temp-dir/global-state/timing contention under full-suite thread load), not regressions from this PR.
