- Snapshot capture/restore backend for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 8, §33.9–§33.9.3, scoping report `docs/audits/2026-09-03-sheets-pr8-pr5c-scope.md`). New `sheets_snapshots.rs` module, one new Tauri command (`restore_sheet_snapshot`) wired in `lib.rs`. **Three rulings from Matt (2026-09-04) applied on top of the scope report:** (1) `reorder_sheet_columns`/`reorder_sheet_rows` are STRUCTURAL, not grid-tier — snapshot-before + throttle bypass, same as add/delete/type-change. Rationale: range membership (SUM/AVERAGE) is computed by row order between endpoints, so a reorder can silently change formula results — consequence-heavy enough to warrant a guaranteed pre-capture, resolving the scope report's "borderline" flag. (2) The pre-restore capture (§33.9.3 step 1) reuses the EXISTING `pre_restore` `note_versions.source` tag — no sheet-specific `sheet_pre_restore` variant, per Reed's recommendation (the JSON-vs-markdown `content` distinction is already resolved by `note_id` lookup at read time, `source` doesn't need to encode it too). (3) The manual-edit throttle constant is extracted exactly once: `notes::MANUAL_EDIT_THROTTLE_SECS: i64 = 60` (previously a bare literal inline in `maybe_save_manual_version`), read by both that existing function and this PR's new grid-mutation throttle — one source of truth, no broader refactor. **Versioned JSON envelope (§33.9.1):** `{ "v": 1, "columns": [...], "rows": [...], "cells": [...] }`, built fresh from live `sheet_columns`/`sheet_rows`/`sheet_cells` rows on every capture. Raw values and formula strings only — never computed values (ADR-0066 D4, restated for snapshots). IDs stored verbatim (load-bearing for ID-preserving restore). Sparse cells — only real `sheet_cells` rows are included, never a dense matrix. No `created_at`/`updated_at` in the envelope (DB-lifecycle metadata, not restorable grid state) and no `note_id` (redundant with `note_versions.note_id`, would be a footgun if a snapshot were ever copied cross-note). Unknown `v` values fail the restore cleanly (`Err`), never silently misparse. **Capture hooks (§33.9.2):** new `maybe_capture_sheet_snapshot(conn, note_id, bypass_throttle)`, called inside every existing mutation's own transaction, immediately after `BEGIN TRANSACTION` and before the mutation's first write — a capture failure rolls back the whole mutation (capture is not best-effort, unlike `maybe_save_manual_version`'s fire-and-log-only pattern for regular notes). Wired at all 9 chokepoints: `create_sheet_column`/`update_sheet_column`/`delete_sheet_column`/`reorder_sheet_columns`, `create_sheet_row`/`delete_sheet_row`/`reorder_sheet_rows` (all structural — throttle bypassed), `update_sheet_cell`/`delete_sheet_cell` (grid — throttled). Throttle check is scoped to `source = 'sheet_snapshot'` specifically (a `pre_restore` row never suppresses the next grid-edit snapshot and vice versa); no content-equality dedup (a snapshot captures PRE-mutation state, so dedup would rarely fire — the throttle alone satisfies "a burst of cell edits produces one snapshot, not fifty"). Style-only cell edits DO still capture (distinct from the separate body-regen gate, which skips style-only — two different gates for two different concerns). Zero schema changes — `note_versions.source` is unconstrained TEXT, `'sheet_snapshot'` is just a new string value. Prune inheritance is automatic and required zero new code: `save_version`'s existing 50-row all-sources DELETE is keyed on `note_id` only, so both `sheet_snapshot` captures and the `pre_restore` restore-time call ride the same prune. **Restore (§33.9.3):** new `restore_sheet_snapshot_internal`, one transaction (bare-SQL `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`, matching `sheets.rs`'s existing idiom): (1) unconditional pre-restore capture (`source = 'pre_restore'`, throttle-bypassed — restore is itself undoable); (2) `get_version` + parse the JSON envelope, reject any `v != 1`; (3) diff-apply in load-bearing order — columns, then rows, then cells (column/row deletes cascade their cells first, so cell diff-apply only ever sees still-valid coordinates, no double-deletes or stray cells); (4) `sheets::recompute_and_regen` (PR 7's existing chokepoint, reused verbatim — no new recompute logic, now `pub(crate)` for this call site); (5) `COMMIT`. Any failure at any step — including a malformed envelope — rolls back the ENTIRE transaction, including the pre-restore capture itself, so a failed restore leaves the grid and version history completely unchanged. Diff-apply upserts by stored ID (`ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`), always bumping `updated_at` to `datetime('now')` regardless of the snapshot's (nonexistent) timestamps; a cell whose live `value`/`style_json` already match the snapshot is skipped entirely, avoiding a needless CRR changefeed entry for cells the restore didn't actually change. **No formula validation on restore** — `validate_formula_on_write` is never called; a since-invalid-syntax restored formula degrades to `#PARSE!` at recompute time exactly like a sync-arrived one does (§33.5.3's documented asymmetry), never blocks the whole restore. `get_note_versions`/`get_note_version` (`versions.rs`) are reused as-is for listing/fetching sheet snapshots — a sheet snapshot is still an ordinary `note_versions` row, `content` just holds JSON instead of markdown. `versions::restore_version` is untouched (zero diff, verified by a dedicated test) — it's the markdown-specific general-note path; sheet restore is this PR's new, separate command. **Ships callable-but-unwired:** `restore_sheet_snapshot` is registered in `lib.rs` and fully invokable, but the version-history UI panel that lists/triggers sheet restores is design-gated — no frontend wiring in this PR. 18 new backend Rust tests in `sheets_snapshots.rs` (16 from the scope report's test matrix §7, plus 2 additional structural-bypass tests for the two reorder commands per Matt's ruling 1): capture on cell-value change (content is pre-mutation state), style-only edit still captures, throttle blocks a second grid mutation within the window, capture fires again after the window elapses, five structural-bypass tests (column add, row delete, column type change, column reorder, row reorder — each firing twice within the throttle window and both capturing), envelope shape (parses as `v:1`, raw formula string preserved not a computed value), restore preserves IDs, restore deletes a column/row added after the snapshot (with cascade verified at the DB level), restore creates exactly one `pre_restore` row, restore recomputes and regenerates `body` (stale post-snapshot value gone, restored value present), restore is one transaction (a malformed envelope rolls back everything, including the pre-restore capture, leaving the grid byte-identical), unparseable restored formula degrades to `#PARSE!` without failing the restore, and 50-row prune inheritance (51 direct `sheet_snapshot` captures cap at 50). `cargo check`/`cargo test --lib` pass; the handful of failures seen on unrelated full-suite runs (`projects::tests::move_folder_*`, `sync_client::tests::test_sync_push_blocking_completes_no_deadlock`, `tests::test_backup::backup_tests::test_restore_backup_workflow`, an AI keychain-timeout test) reproduce identically on a clean `git stash` of this branch — confirmed pre-existing environment/timing flakes, not regressions from this PR. (Relates to #2339, spec-skip: snapshot capture/restore backend per §33.9, spec landed in #2845, spec-covered-by: #2845)
- Dependency graph + recompute engine for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 7, §33.5.2–§33.5.4, scoping report `docs/audits/2026-09-03-sheets-pr6-pr7-formula-scope.md`, PR 6 audit `docs/audits/2026-09-03-sheets-pr6-formula-audit.md`). This is the PR that WIRES the formula engine into the live app — PR 6 was a pure, inert library. **PR 6 audit FAIL-tier fix (landed first, before any write-path wiring):** the recursive-descent parser (`parser.rs`) gains a `MAX_PARSE_DEPTH = 128` recursion guard (a `depth: usize` counter on the `Parser` struct, incremented/decremented around the two genuinely-recursive call sites — `parse_expr` for parens/function args, `parse_unary` for chained unary minus), returning `FormulaError::Parse` past the ceiling instead of risking a stack overflow on a pathological/malicious deeply-nested formula. **PR 6 audit WARN resolutions:** (1) `CellResolver::resolve_range`'s empty-`Vec` contract is now documented on the trait method — either endpoint missing/unresolvable returns an empty `Vec` (SUM treats as 0, AVERAGE as `#DIV/0!`), distinct from a per-member `Some(Error(Ref))` sentinel for an existing-but-deleted single cell within an otherwise-valid range; (2) `evaluate()` gains a `visited: &mut HashSet<(String, String)>` parameter threaded through every recursive call site (binary ops, comparisons, function calls, unary minus) — a cell reference already in `visited` returns `CellValue::Error(FormulaError::Cycle)` instead of infinitely recursing; this is defense-in-depth only (the primary, real multi-cell cycle detection is the graph-level DFS below, which pre-marks every cycle member `#CYCLE!` before `evaluate()` ever touches it) but closes the theoretical gap for a resolver implementation that recurses into `evaluate()` itself. `eval_formula` (`mod.rs`) initializes a fresh `HashSet` per top-level call. **New module `formula/recompute.rs`:** dependency graph construction (walks each formula cell's AST extracting `CellRef`/`Range` dependencies into a `HashMap<CellId, Vec<CellId>>`, `CellId = (column_id, row_id)`); three-color DFS cycle detection collecting ALL cycle members (not just the two endpoints of one back-edge) into a result set, deterministic and idempotent — rerunning on unchanged data produces the same `#CYCLE!` set; Kahn's-algorithm topological sort over the non-cyclic subgraph; a `LiveCellResolver` (`CellResolver` impl) that resolves formula-cell dependencies from the in-progress computed-value map (never a live re-evaluation — topological ordering guarantees every dependency is already computed) and non-formula cells via raw-string coercion, returning `#REF!` when a referenced column or row no longer exists at all (distinct from a valid-but-empty/sparse cell, which resolves as `Empty`); single-column range expansion (v1 grammar) against the sheet's row-sort-order list. **Full-graph rebuild per mutation** (Matt ruling 2026-09-03): every value-mutating command rebuilds the ENTIRE sheet's dependency graph and recomputes every formula cell, not just a dirty subgraph — a deliberate v1 simplicity tradeoff, documented inline, deviating from §33.5.4's dirty-subgraph wording; revisit if perf requires targeted invalidation. **Guard rail** (Matt ruling 2026-09-03): a provisional soft limit of 500 formula cells per sheet — past it, recompute is skipped entirely (formulas keep storing and displaying as raw strings, exactly like pre-PR-7 behavior) rather than ever attempting a computation heavy enough to freeze the UI; a warning is logged. **In-memory-only computed-value store:** `recompute_sheet(conn, note_id) -> Result<HashMap<CellId, CellValue>, String>` returns a fresh map on every call, consumed immediately by body regen in the same transaction and never persisted — confirmed against the real `sheet_cells` DDL (`migrations.rs`) that no `computed_value` column exists or is needed; computed values live only in memory, matching ADR-0066 D4 (documented in `sheets.rs`'s module comment). **Body regen integration, closing the PR 5a interim gap:** `regenerate_sheet_body` now takes a `&HashMap<CellId, CellValue>` parameter — a formula cell's body line renders its computed value (via a new `Display` impl on `CellValue`) instead of its raw `=...` string; falls back to the raw string only in the defensive case of a missing computed entry. **Fixed the PR 5a comment-ordering bug** (Matt ruling 2026-09-03): every one of the nine `sheets.rs` `§33.5.4` placeholder comments (create/update/delete/reorder for columns, rows, and cells) is replaced with a live `recompute_sheet` call immediately followed by `regenerate_sheet_body` — recompute MUST run before body regen (several PR 5a comments had the order backwards) so body text reflects fresh computed values, not stale/raw ones. **Parse-on-write validation (§33.5.3):** `update_sheet_cell_internal` — the sole cell-value write path — now calls `recompute::validate_formula_on_write` before any DB write; a syntactically invalid local formula edit (including a pathologically deep one, exercising the new recursion guard through the real write path) is rejected inline with an error, never stored. Sync- and AI-originated formulas bypass this (already committed by cr-sqlite by the time this code runs) and instead surface `#PARSE!` at recompute time — documented asymmetry. **Post-sync recompute hook** (`sync/engine.rs`): a new `recompute_all_sheets_post_sync`, called immediately after the existing orphan sweep inside `receive_sync_payload`'s sheet-table-touched gate, recomputes EVERY `note_type = 'sheet'` note (Matt ruling 2026-09-03: broad scope over precision-scoping to the touched primary keys — simple over surgical, revisit at perf) so an LWW-losing formula on this device recomputes from the just-arrived WINNING formula string, never stale pre-sync state; per-sheet recompute/regen failures are logged and skipped, never abort the batch or block other sheets. **Known, documented scope gap:** PR 7 does not build an A1-notation → stable-ID `ReferenceMapper` (PR 6's parser already accepts both syntaxes structurally, but the actually-merged PR 6 never added ID translation) — formulas authored with A1-style letters (e.g. `=SUM(A1:A5)`) against real UUID-keyed columns/rows safely degrade to an empty-range/zero result rather than crashing or silently resolving wrong data, but only stable-ID-syntax formulas (`={col_uuid:row_uuid}`) actually resolve against real grid cells; flagged as a follow-up. **Test count (audited claim — count the delta, not the running total; commit and CHANGELOG must agree, Matt ruling 2026-09-03):** 38 new tests added by THIS PR's diff, verified by counting `#[test]` functions added in this branch vs. `main` file-by-file: 20 in the new `formula/recompute.rs` module (dependency-graph/cycle-detection/topological-sort/guard-rail coverage), 4 in `formula/parser.rs` for the depth-guard, 5 in `formula/eval.rs` for the visited-set cycle guard (0 in `formula/mod.rs`), 5 in `sheets.rs`, 3 in `sync/engine.rs`, 1 in `test_p2p_sync.rs`. The `formula::` module alone (parser.rs + eval.rs + mod.rs + recompute.rs) sits at 116 `#[test]` functions post-PR — 87 pre-existing from PR 6's parser.rs/eval.rs base + this PR's 29 new (the 20 in recompute.rs plus 4 in parser.rs plus 5 in eval.rs). Across all 7 touched files (formula/ plus the sheets.rs/sync/engine.rs/test_p2p_sync.rs integration tests this PR also adds to), the total is 155 tests (117 pre-existing from PR 6's base + this PR's 38 new). An earlier draft of this entry claimed ~113/~116 new tests for this PR — that figure was PR 6's pre-existing base miscounted as this PR's delta; corrected here to the real diff-counted number, 38. Coverage areas: parser depth-guard boundary/over-limit/nested-unary-minus, `resolve_range`/`evaluate()` visited-set cycle unit tests, and a full `recompute.rs` suite: linear/diamond dependency chains, value-change recompute, direct/indirect/self-reference/mixed cycles, cycle-detection idempotency, `#REF!` vs. sparse-but-valid-cell distinction, guard-rail at-limit/over-limit behavior, parse-on-write accept/reject, unparseable-formula-doesn't-block-other-cells, empty-range SUM/AVERAGE semantics, plus 5 new `sheets.rs` tests (computed-value body rendering replacing the old raw-string-interim test, A1-style-against-UUID-columns safe degradation, parse-on-write accept/reject/style-only-skip/deep-nesting-rejection through the real write path) plus 3 new `sync/engine.rs` tests (post-sync multi-sheet recompute, one-bad-sheet-doesn't-block-others, no-sheets-is-a-noop) plus 1 new `test_p2p_sync.rs` LWW-race regression test (`test_lww_race_loser_recomputes_from_winning_formula` — two real cr-sqlite-backed DBs, a formula cell loses a sync race, recompute on the loser's device must produce the WINNING formula's value, never its own stale pre-sync value). No `assert!(true)`, no `todo!()`, no `unimplemented!()` — every test exercises real parser/evaluator/recompute/write-path code. - Formula engine core: parser + evaluator for the Sheets feature (#2339 PR 6, §33.5.1–§33.5.3, scoping report `docs/audits/2026-09-03-sheets-pr6-pr7-formula-scope.md`). New `src-tauri/src/formula/` module (`mod.rs`, `parser.rs`, `eval.rs`) registered in `lib.rs` behind `#[allow(dead_code)]`. **Pure library — zero touches to `sheets.rs` or `engine.rs`.** Formulas continue to be stored as raw strings with no validation (PR 5a behavior unchanged); nothing in the runtime calls this module yet — PR 7 wires it in. **Parser (`parser.rs`):** hand-rolled tokenizer + recursive-descent parser (no crate, no Pratt-parser machinery) for the v1 grammar — numeric/string/boolean literals, cell references in both A1-style (`A1`, `AB123`) and stable-ID form (`{col_uuid:row_uuid}`, §33.5.2), ranges (`A1:A5`, `{col_uuid:row1:row2}`), parentheses, `+ - * /`, `SUM`/`AVERAGE`/`IF`, and comparison operators (`= != < > <= >=`) for `IF` conditions. **Unary minus included in v1 grammar** (Matt ruling 2026-09-03, overriding the scope report's ambiguity flag) — `-A1`, `-(1+2)`, and double-negative `--5` all parse, as the highest-precedence prefix operator. Operator precedence: unary minus > `*`/`/` > `+`/`-` > comparisons. Malformed formulas never panic — every failure path returns `FormulaError::Parse` with a descriptive message; unknown function names parse successfully as `FnName::Unknown` and only fail at evaluation time (`#NAME?` is an eval-time error per §33.5.3, not a parse error). **Evaluator (`eval.rs`):** tree-walking `evaluate(ast, resolver) -> CellValue` plus the `CellResolver` trait — the PR6/PR7 seam (`resolve_cell`, `resolve_range`), letting PR 6 be fully tested against a mocked resolver with zero database dependency. `CellValue` enum: `Number`/`Text`/`Boolean`/`Error`/`Empty`. Type coercion: text→number attempts `str::parse`, `#VALUE!` on failure; number→text formats without a superfluous `.0`; boolean→number is `true→1.0`/`false→0.0`; empty→number is `0.0` in arithmetic. **Checkbox coercion ruling:** `'0'`/`'1'` (and parsed `Boolean` values) coerce to `0.0`/`1.0` in arithmetic — this explicitly OVERRULES the scope report's `#VALUE!` recommendation per Matt ruling 2026-09-03 (checkbox stores `'0'`/`'1'` per §33.3.1, coercion is natural, counting checks is a core tracker use case; documented inline at the coercion site in `eval.rs`). **AVERAGE counts non-empty cells only** (Matt ruling 2026-09-03): sum of non-empty values divided by count of non-empty values, NOT total range size — an `AVERAGE` over 5 cells with 3 populated divides by 3; empty cells are skipped entirely rather than contributing zero (distinct from `SUM`, which also skips empties but this only matters for `AVERAGE`'s denominator); zero non-empty values → `#DIV/0!`. `SUM` sums all numeric values across ranges/literal args, coercing booleans, skipping empties, `#VALUE!` on non-numeric non-empty text. `IF(condition, true_val, false_val)` accepts boolean or numeric (`0`=false, nonzero=true) conditions; wrong arity or a text condition is `#VALUE!`. **Error propagation (§33.5.3):** any operand evaluating to `CellValue::Error` short-circuits the enclosing operation to that same error, through arithmetic, comparisons, and `SUM`/`AVERAGE`/`IF` alike. Full §33.5.3 error taxonomy implemented: `#REF!` (invalid referent, signaled by a `CellResolver` implementation), `#VALUE!` (coercion failure), `#DIV/0!` (division by zero or empty-range `AVERAGE`), `#NAME?` (unknown function), `#PARSE!` (parser failure, carries a message). **`#CYCLE!` variant exists for completeness only** — per Matt ruling 2026-09-03, cycle detection is explicitly PR 7's concern; PR 6's evaluator never produces this error, it only has the capacity to propagate one if a future `CellResolver` implementation (PR 7's) hands one back as an already-resolved cell value. **`mod.rs`** re-exports the full public API (`parse_formula`, `evaluate`, `AstNode`, `CellValue`, `FormulaError`, `CellResolver`) plus a convenience `eval_formula(input, resolver)` that parses and evaluates in one call, short-circuiting to `FormulaError::Parse` on a parse failure without reaching the evaluator. 87 new backend Rust tests (43 parser, 44 evaluator) covering the full matrix from the scope report §6.1: every operator-precedence combination, unary minus including the double-negative edge case, parenthesized expressions, both A1-style and stable-ID cell/range reference forms, all three function calls, string/number/boolean literals, malformed-input parse failures (unbalanced parens, trailing garbage, empty input, unterminated strings/stable-id braces, invalid characters), case-insensitive function names and booleans, whitespace tolerance, basic arithmetic and precedence via the real evaluator, cell reference resolution against a mocked `CellResolver` (populated, missing/sparse, and explicitly-invalid `#REF!` coordinates), `SUM` over ranges with sparse gaps and mixed numeric/boolean/empty values, `AVERAGE`'s non-empty-only denominator (including the empty-range `#DIV/0!` case), `IF` with boolean and numeric conditions, checkbox coercion in both `Boolean` and raw `'0'`/`'1'` text-cell forms, division by zero, text-in-arithmetic `#VALUE!`, unknown-function `#NAME?`, error propagation through arithmetic/`SUM`, nested function calls (`SUM(...) + AVERAGE(...)`), numeric-string coercion, text-equality comparison, and direct unit tests on the `to_number`/`to_text` coercion helpers and `FormulaError`'s `Display` impl. No `assert!(true)`, no `todo!()`, no `unimplemented!()` — every test exercises real parser/evaluator code paths. Verified inert: `cargo check`/`cargo test` pass identically to pre-PR main (one pre-existing unrelated flaky test, `sync_client::tests::test_sync_push_blocking_completes_no_deadlock`, reproduces identically on main without this PR's changes). (Relates to #2339, spec-skip: formula engine parser + evaluator per §33.5.1–§33.5.3, spec landed in #2845, spec-covered-by: #2845)

New `sheets.rs` module, 11 Tauri commands wired in `lib.rs`. **`create_sheet`** — the public creation entry point: wraps PR 4's `create_sheet_note_internal` + seeding of `DEFAULT_SHEET_COLUMNS` (5, all `text` type, provisional pending design-phase sign-off) + an initial body regen, all in ONE `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` transaction (bare-SQL idiom, matching `reorder_notes_internal`, not `rusqlite::Connection::transaction()`). Returns full `SheetData` (columns/rows/cells + `NoteMeta`) so the frontend renders immediately, no second round-trip. **Column/row/cell CRUD**: `create_sheet_column`/`update_sheet_column`/`delete_sheet_column`/`reorder_sheet_columns`, `create_sheet_row`/`delete_sheet_row`/`reorder_sheet_rows`, `update_sheet_cell`/`delete_sheet_cell`, `get_sheet_data` (read). Two on-disk DBs with the live cr-sqlite extension loaded, real `sheet_cells` DDL; both diverge on the same non-PK column for the same composite-PK row, bidirectional sync, asserts single-row convergence (no PK duplication), same winning value on both sides, and that the OTHER untouched non-PK column (`value`) survived independently — proving true per-column resolution, not row-level LWW. ## [1.0.46] - 2026-09-02

### Infrastructure
- Fixed nightly workflow: pinned pnpm version to prevent build-script drift, switched failure reporting to single pinned issue (#2827) instead of per-failure duplicates

### Fixed
- Wire-level body logging + production-path retry test for the embeddings token-retry mechanism (#2776 Round 3, trace `docs/audits/2026-09-02-2776-closure-trace.md`). Reed's full closure trace refuted the hypothesis that `embed_fn` captures an outer `content` variable instead of its own parameter — both closure arms in `build_http_embed_fn` (`lib.rs`) correctly use their `text: &str` parameter, and `embed_with_token_retry` (`embeddings.rs`) correctly re-slices its own `content` parameter for the retry, not an outer/module-level original — but production logs still showed the server reporting the exact same 513-token count for a 1224-char body AND a 1099-char retry, which is impossible if the wire genuinely carried shorter content on the second attempt. Two changes close the gap between "source looks correct" and "prove what's on the wire": (1) both `build_http_embed_fn` closure arms (OpenRouter and Ollama) now `eprintln!` immediately before `.send()`, reporting the serialized JSON body's actual byte length alongside the closure parameter's own char count (`[EMBEDDINGS] Wire: sending {body_bytes} body bytes, input text {char_count} chars`) — visible in production logs on every embed call, not just retries; (2) a new test, `test_build_http_embed_fn_wire_body_shrinks_on_retry`, closes the coverage gap every existing retry test shared: they all hand-write a parameter-honoring `attempt` closure directly in the test, which can never catch a closure-capture/lifetime/serialization bug in the REAL production constructor because the test's own closure is definitionally correct. This test instead builds `embed_fn` via `build_http_embed_fn` itself (the actual production constructor, wired through the Ollama arm's configurable `embeddings_endpoint` so a mockito server can stand in for the real HTTP target), routes it through the real `embed_with_token_retry`, and asserts on the ACTUAL bytes mockito's server received via `Request::body()` — not on what the test's own code thinks it sent. **Result: the test PASSES** — the second wire body (1694 bytes) is strictly shorter than the first (1882 bytes), confirming the wire genuinely carries the truncated content end-to-end through the real production closure. This refutes a wire-level bug and points the remaining #2776 Round 3 symptom at the `chars_per_token = 4.0` truncation ratio being too generous for embedding models (bge-base tokenizes closer to 2-2.5 chars/token) — addressed in the following entry. (Relates to #2776, spec-skip: diagnostic instrumentation + test coverage, no spec-visible behavior change)
- Tightened `truncate_to_token_budget`'s char/token ratio for embedding-model truncation from `4.0` to `2.2` chars/token (#2776 Round 3). With the wire invariant confirmed intact (previous entry — `test_build_http_embed_fn_wire_body_shrinks_on_retry` passes, proving the wire genuinely carries the shorter retry content end-to-end through the real production closure), the residual production symptom — first-attempt embed calls still landing over a model's token limit despite a truncation pass having already run — is a ratio problem, not a mechanism problem: `4.0` chars/token matches GPT-family tokenization (`TokenEstimationRatio::for_model`'s chat-model default), but bge-base-en-v1.5's real WordPiece tokenizer (the TEI backend behind OpenRouter's bge-* embedding models) runs meaningfully denser on real content, so the existing 10% safety margin wasn't enough headroom to absorb the gap. `2.2` chars/token (still with the existing 10% margin and `floor_char_boundary` UTF-8 safety pass, both unchanged) is conservative enough that first attempts land under budget for the dense content shapes seen in production (`max_tokens=512` now truncates to 1013 chars, down from 1843), at the cost of retaining less content per truncated chunk than the old ratio allowed. `embed_with_token_retry`'s adaptive retry mechanism (unchanged) remains the backstop for any content shape this static ratio still misses. All existing truncation tests updated for the new byte counts (`test_truncation_applies_10_percent_safety_margin`, `test_larger_max_tokens_allows_more_content`, `test_facts_subpass_truncates_long_fact_strings_same_as_notes_and_chats`) — no new test-shape gaps, since every UTF-8-boundary-safety and larger-budget test already exercised this code path structurally and only their expected byte counts changed. (Relates to #2776, spec-skip: internal truncation-ratio tuning, no spec-visible behavior change)

## [1.0.45] - 2026-09-02

### Added
- TEI error wording recognition + retry logging (#2776 follow-up 2, diagnosis `docs/audits/2026-09-01-2776-retry-diagnosis.md`). Follow-up 1's `embed_with_token_retry` mechanism (below) was correctly wired to all three notes/facts/chats sub-passes, but `parse_token_limit_from_error` only matched OpenAI chat-completions phrasing (`"You passed N input tokens"`) — wording `baai/bge-base-en-v1.5` never actually produces, since it runs on a TEI (HuggingFace Text Embeddings Inference) backend whose real 400 body reads `"Input validation error: \`inputs\` must have less than 512 tokens. Given: 513"`. The regex never matched real bge-base-en-v1.5 traffic, so `embed_with_token_retry` always fell to `_ => return Err(e)` — **zero retries fired for any content type**; notes/facts happened to stay under budget from the truncation heuristic alone, but chats (denser content) still failed outright with no second attempt. `parse_token_limit_from_error` now tries a new regex (`must have less than \d+ tokens\. Given: (\d+)`) matching TEI's real wording first, falling back to the original OpenAI-style pattern for other provider/model families — a plain substring/regex match, so it recognizes the pattern whether it arrives flat or nested inside OpenRouter's `error.metadata.raw` JSON-escaped envelope. Separately, `embed_with_token_retry` previously had zero `eprintln!` calls anywhere in its retry branch — a fixed regex alone still wouldn't make a retry visible in the console. It now logs the retry attempt (server-reported actual tokens vs. the model's limit, retry content length vs. original) before re-attempting, and logs success or the second failure afterward. 4 new backend Rust tests: `test_parse_token_limit_recognizes_tei_wording` (the real OpenRouter-wrapped TEI error body resolves to `Some(513)`), `test_parse_token_limit_still_recognizes_openai_wording` (regression proving the original OpenAI-style wording still parses via the fallback), `test_embed_retry_on_tei_wrapped_token_limit_400` (mockito 400-then-200 using the real TEI-in-OpenRouter envelope body — retry sends shorter content, succeeds, exactly 2 requests made), and `test_embed_retry_logs_on_success` (exercises the success-branch retry path end-to-end, confirming it's reached rather than short-circuited; exact `eprintln!` text is verified by source inspection, not stderr capture). (Relates to #2776, spec-covered-by: #2817)
- Adaptive retry on embedding token-limit 400s + read-path seed-table resolution (#2776 follow-up, v1.0.43 retest). PR #2817's token-aware truncation dropped Matt's failure count from 31 to 22 but left two gaps. **Gap 1 — adaptive retry:** the 4.0 chars/token estimate with its 10% safety margin can still overshoot on dense content — Matt hit 1843 chars of markdown estimating under budget but tokenizing to 513 against bge-base's 512 limit. Rather than re-tuning the ratio (which can never be perfect for every content type), a new `embed_with_token_retry` (`embeddings.rs`) wraps each of the three `run_embedding_pipeline` embed-call sites (notes/facts/chats): on an embed call's HTTP 400 whose body matches OpenRouter's `"You passed N input tokens"` wording (`parse_token_limit_from_error`, regex-matched, also requires `"HTTP 400"` in the error text so any other status is never mistaken for a token-limit error), the content is re-truncated ONCE using the server's actual token count as ground truth (`new_char_limit = current_chars * (model_max_tokens / N)`, then the existing 10% safety margin applied on top) and the embed call retried exactly once. A non-token 400 (e.g. an auth failure surfaced as 400) fails immediately with no retry; a second token-limit 400 on the retry also fails cleanly with no further attempt — this is a targeted retry at the embed call site, not a global retry loop. **Gap 2 — read path skips the seed table:** `read_embeddings_max_tokens` previously only checked the stored `ai_settings.embeddings_max_tokens` value before falling to the 512 floor, skipping the same `embedding_model_seed_lookup` static table the WRITE path (`switch_embedding_engine`/`resolve_embeddings_max_tokens`) already consults — Matt's boot log proved it: "unknown model, using conservative floor" for `baai/bge-base-en-v1.5`, which IS in the seed table. This is harmless for bge-base (512 == the floor already) but a bge-m3 user (8192 tokens) with no persisted setting — fresh install, or an engine configured before #2776 landed — would silently boot into 512, a 16x over-truncation. `read_embeddings_max_tokens` now resolves via a three-tier chain: (1) the stored value if present/parseable, (2) **new** — `embedding_model_seed_lookup` keyed on the current `ai_settings.embeddings_model`, the same standalone function the write path already uses (no duplicated table), (3) the `EMBEDDINGS_MAX_TOKENS_FALLBACK` floor, still always logged. 6 new backend Rust tests: `test_embed_retry_on_token_limit_400` (proves the retry sends proportionally shorter content, succeeds, exactly 2 requests made), `test_embed_no_retry_on_non_token_400` (a non-token 400 body like "Invalid API key" fails on the first attempt, exactly 1 request), `test_embed_second_token_400_fails_cleanly` (both attempts hit a token-limit 400, fails cleanly with exactly 2 requests, no infinite loop), `test_read_embeddings_max_tokens_resolves_seed_table` (a bge-m3 model with no stored `embeddings_max_tokens` resolves 8192, not the 512 floor), plus `test_read_embeddings_max_tokens_prefers_stored_value_over_seed_table` and `_no_settings_at_all_falls_through_to_floor` covering the tier-1 precedence and full-fallback edge cases. (Relates to #2776, spec-covered-by: #2817)
- Token-aware truncation for the embeddings chunker (#2776, scope audit `docs/audits/2026-09-01-2776-embeddings-chunker-scope.md`). **Root cause:** the pipeline (`embeddings.rs`, notes/facts/chats sub-passes) truncated content to a flat 2000-character cap, not a token count — for English text (~4 chars/token) that's routinely ~500-570 estimated tokens, exceeding bge-base-en-v1.5's 512-token limit and producing OpenRouter HTTP 400 ("You passed 513 input tokens... context length is only 512") on every over-limit chunk. The facts sub-pass had **zero truncation at all**, so any long fact string always failed. Nothing had been indexed since Aug 29; 31 items were permanently stuck in a failed state. **Fix — 5a, persist the real limit:** `switch_embedding_engine` (`ai/commands.rs`) gains an optional `max_tokens: Option<u64>` param, sourced from OpenRouter's `fetch_openrouter_embedding_models`/`ModelInfo.context_length` (already fetched, now threaded from `Settings.svelte`'s model picker through the `switch_embedding_engine` invoke as `maxTokens`). A new `resolve_embeddings_max_tokens` helper resolves, in order: (1) the caller-supplied OpenRouter `context_length`, (2) a new static seed table for Ollama (`embedding_model_seed_lookup`, `embeddings.rs`, mirrors `ai/context_budget.rs`'s existing `seed_lookup()` pattern) — each entry verified against its model card: `bge-m3`→8192, `bge-base`→512, `bge-large`→512, `nomic-embed-text`→8192, `mxbai-embed-large`→512, `all-minilm`→256, (3) a documented last-resort floor, `EMBEDDINGS_MAX_TOKENS_FALLBACK = 512` (Matt's ruling: no bare magic numbers — the 512 limit is always read or derived, never hardcoded inline at a call site), always logged as "unknown model, using conservative floor" so a missing/unmatched model is diagnosable from terminal output, never silently treated as authoritative. The resolved value is persisted to `ai_settings.embeddings_max_tokens` alongside `embeddings_engine`/`embeddings_model`. **Fix — 5b, token-aware truncation:** `run_embedding_pipeline` gains a `max_tokens: usize` parameter; all three truncation call sites (notes, facts, chats) now call a new `truncate_to_token_budget(content, max_tokens)` using the app's existing `TokenEstimationRatio` heuristic (`ai/context_budget.rs`, already used for chat context budgeting — no second estimator invented) with a 10% safety margin (`(max_tokens * chars_per_token * 0.9).floor()` chars) to absorb the gap between this char-based estimate and the model's real server-side tokenizer, then the existing `floor_char_boundary` UTF-8 safety pass. The facts sub-pass now truncates for the first time (Matt's ruling: facts get the same treatment as notes/chats). **Fix — 5c, caller wiring:** all three callers of `run_embedding_pipeline` now supply a token limit — `switch_embedding_engine` passes the just-resolved/persisted value directly; `run_integrity_check` (`ai/commands.rs`) and the `lib.rs` startup pipeline both read the persisted `ai_settings.embeddings_max_tokens` via a new `embeddings::read_embeddings_max_tokens` helper, falling back to `EMBEDDINGS_MAX_TOKENS_FALLBACK` (logged) for installs that configured their embedding engine/model before this setting existed. **Retry path for the 31 stuck items:** no manual data fix was needed — the fix rides the pipeline's existing failed-item retry, triggered by any of: the next app startup, `run_integrity_check`'s periodic background pass, or clicking "Save & Test" on the Semantic Search settings card. 16 new backend Rust tests cover: the seed table (known models, case-insensitivity, unknown-returns-`None`), the fallback constant, `truncate_to_token_budget` directly (under-budget unchanged, a 3000-char string at 512 max tokens stays under limit, the 10% safety margin's exact byte count, a larger budget allowing more content, a zero-max-tokens edge case, and UTF-8 boundary safety across emoji/CJK/accented-Latin content), a facts-sub-pass regression test proving long fact strings now truncate identically to notes/chats (previously untruncated), and three integration tests (mockito-simulated OpenRouter 400 response confirmed not misclassified as an auth error; the old 2000-char cap reproduced as exceeding 512 estimated tokens under the codebase's own conservative token ratio; a sweep of content lengths confirming the fix's `truncate_to_token_budget` output always estimates ≤512 tokens). (Relates to #2776, spec-covered-by: #2808)
- Venice as a Smart Features internal provider (#2795, ADR-0065 Supplement S1, spec `docs/spec/smart-routing.md` §27.6.2, `docs/spec/onboarding.md` §6.4.1/§6.4.5): Venice can now power the three background AI features (extraction, Smart Routing, Rerank) as the internal provider, not just as a primary/chat runtime. Backend: `get_internal_provider` (`commands.rs`) gains a `"venice"` arm in both resolution steps — Step 1 (explicit `internal_provider = "venice"`) reads the key via `read_venice_key` (keychain account `ai_venice_key`, ADR-0065 D4 — deliberately NOT `read_internal_key`, the shared OpenRouter/Anthropic slot, since Venice has no plaintext fallback and a wrong-account read would either break Venice or leak a key into the wrong slot), and Step 2 (Venice-primary with `internal_provider` unset, the back-compat fallback for Tier 1/2 installs) now resolves instead of hard-erroring (`Err("Unsupported provider for internal calls: venice")`) — this broken fallback state was the original motivation for #2795. Both arms construct `AiProvider::Venice { api_key, include_system_prompt: false }` unconditionally: extraction/classification/rerank are background machinery with no user-facing conversational turn, so Venice's install-wide "Use Venice system prompt" toggle (ADR-0065 D3, chat-scoped) never applies on this path, matching the existing `call_llm_from_config` background-worker precedent. `fetch_internal_provider_models`'s previously-hardcoded Venice rejection is replaced with a call to the existing `fetch_venice_models` fetcher (already used by the primary-provider model list). No generalized provider-enumeration mechanism was built here — Venice is a 4th hardcoded arm at each of the 9 census sites, matching the existing per-provider pattern (a generalized enumerator is filed separately as #2810). Frontend: Settings → AI → Smart Features dropdown gains a Venice option with its own key-entry field (masked-status display via `venice_key_status`, since Venice has no raw-key round-trip) and save path (`validate_venice_key` → `save_venice_key`, never the shared `internal_api_key` slot); onboarding's §6.4.1 Smart Features picker gains a 4th Venice card (name + "Your Venice API models" descriptor, matching #2792's card convention) routing to a new `smart-features-venice-setup` sub-flow screen mirroring the existing OpenRouter/Anthropic credential-entry + three-model-picker shape. Ride-alongs clearing #2808 audit debt: ADR-0065 D8's "Out of this PR" note now points at Supplement S1 as superseding the Smart-Features-exclusion bullet; `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §28's stale "All primary providers (OR, Anthropic, Ollama)" model-picker line now includes Venice; `docs/spec/agents.md` §24.6's "+ New agent" gate description now names Venice among the API providers it admits, with a verification note that `AgentCreateOverlay`'s connected-runtime filter is already runtime-agnostic and required no code change. Backend: 4 new unit tests (`test_get_internal_provider_venice`, `_venice_missing_key`, `_venice_fallback_from_primary`, `_venice_fallback_missing_key`) plus 1 integration test exercising the real `set_ai_setting`/`get_ai_setting` Tauri command round-trip through to `get_internal_provider`'s Venice resolution (`dual_provider_tests.rs`). Frontend: `Settings.venice-smart-features.test.ts` (11 tests, source-level assertions matching this file's established DOM-render-unavailable pattern) and `Onboarding.venice-smart-features.test.ts` (3 tests, full component render/interaction) cover the dropdown, key-entry field, save-path command routing, picker card, and sub-flow routing. - Venice live-test blocker fixes (#2777, Relates to #2455, Closes #1630, spec `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §28.2 status note): a live smoke test of the just-shipped Venice runtime (ADR-0065) surfaced several key-change/validation/visibility bugs, fixed here as one PR. **Fix 1a** — `ai_configure_and_save`'s `venice` arm now reactivates any deactivated Venice agents (`is_active = 0 → 1`) on a successful reconnect and promotes a new default agent if none exists, matching the reconnect behavior other runtimes already had. **Fix 1b** — the agents-integrity safety net (`verify_agents_integrity_with_path`) no longer force-overwrites `role` to `'main'` when promoting a default agent, and its promotion candidate query now explicitly excludes imported subagents (`role = 'sub' AND runtime_ref IS NOT NULL`, per B5/#2567) — the safety net could previously promote an imported subagent to default and silently relabel it. **Fix 1c** — the `migrate_v83` `"openclaw-pending"` model sentinel is now rewritten to `"openclaw"` upstream in `call_llm`'s `AiProvider::OpenClaw` arm, before `ChatRequest` construction, so both the streaming and non-streaming dispatch paths get the fix from one call site (previously only the streaming path rewrote it; the consolidator, memory extraction, synthesis, and classifier all leaked the placeholder onto the wire on the non-streaming path). **Fix 1-UX** — the provider Disconnect confirm-dialog copy (`ProviderConnectionCard.svelte`, `NewProviderModal.svelte`) no longer implies a later reconnect "restores" agents; it now reads "This will deactivate all agents on this provider and delete the saved key. You can reconnect later through New Provider." **Fix 2 / §28.2 (closes #1630)** — Save/Add connection for all three key providers (Venice, OpenRouter, Anthropic) now validates the key (`validate_venice_key`/`validate_openrouter_key`/`validate_anthropic_key`) before calling `ai_configure_and_save`, in both `ProviderConnectionCard.svelte`'s `saveConnection()` and `NewProviderModal.svelte`'s `handleAddConnection()` — previously Save/Add fired the instant a key was typed, entirely independent of whether Test was ever clicked or what it returned. A failing validator aborts the save with an inline error and never calls the backend. **Fix 3** — Provider Connection Cards (`ProviderConnectionsPanel.svelte`) now render only for providers where `configured_this_install` is true (the "+ New Provider" button stays always visible); the backend command (`ai_list_runtime_connections`) is unchanged and still returns all five runtime types, so any other consumer wanting the full roster still gets it. New one-time schema migration `migrate_v88` (SCHEMA_VERSION 87→88) backfills `{runtime}_configured_at` for anthropic/openrouter/venice on upgrade when a real, working keychain credential exists with no marker — deliberately a one-time migration rather than a per-request check, so #2631's "stale keychain leftover ≠ configured_this_install" contract stays a stable signal rather than flipping true on every list-connections call against an old leftover key. ADR-0065 D8 and ADR-0063 D8 gain correction notes pointing at this new `configured_this_install` gating (superseding their prior "always render all cards" text). **Ride-alongs**: (4) the Venice card's display-name/logo maps (`RUNTIME_LABELS`/`RUNTIME_LOGOS` in `ProviderConnectionCard.svelte`) were missing a `venice` entry, showing raw `"venice"`/`"??"` instead of "Venice"/"VE" — added. (5) `stream_openrouter_inner` (Venice's streaming dispatch path) now logs `[VENICE] stream body keys: [...]` — top-level JSON keys only, never values — right after `venice_parameters` is set on the request body, for execution-evidence debugging without leaking key/content data. (6) the show/hide API-key toggle on `ProviderConnectionCard.svelte` was investigated and found already fully wired and functional (toggles the input's `type` between `text`/`password`); no code change was needed. (7) key-provider cards (Venice/OpenRouter/Anthropic) now always render a Test button, matching OpenClaw/Ollama parity, instead of only showing it once a key was typed; clicking Test with an empty key now shows a clear "Enter an API key to test." error instead of doing nothing. Backend: 9 new/updated Rust tests (`migrate_v88` backfill/no-invent/idempotent/no-overwrite/table-absent coverage, plus `configured_this_install` card-visibility gating). Frontend: `ProviderConnectionCard.test.ts` gains a failing-validator-aborts-save test; `ProviderConnectionsPanel.test.ts` and `Settings.agents-tab-refresh-after-oc-import.test.ts` updated for the new card-visibility filter. - Refactored base_url predicates in openrouter.rs to explicit AiProvider variant-keying (RequestOrigin enum), eliminating URL-inference for OpenClaw detection. Behavior-preserving for OpenRouter and OpenClaw sessions. (#2455)
- SSRF guard extraction to `net_guard.rs` + `og_fetch.rs` hardening (#2751, spec `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.6.5 status note): the §4.6.5 SSRF guard (scheme allowlist, hostname pre-check, IP blocklist, DNS resolve-and-pin, pinned client builder) is extracted from `web.rs` into a new shared module, `src-tauri/src/ai/net_guard.rs`, consumed by both `ai::web` (`web_fetch`/`web_search`) and `og_fetch.rs` (link-preview og: tag fetch, ADR-0049 Decision 2) as their single SSRF enforcement point — no more parallel copies of the blocklist to keep in sync. Each caller keeps its own redirect-hop cap (`web.rs`'s `MAX_WEB_REDIRECTS = 5`, renamed from the former bare `MAX_REDIRECTS` to avoid ambiguity with `og_fetch.rs`'s own `MAX_REDIRECTS = 3`) and its own `USER_AGENT`/timeouts, passed into `net_guard::build_pinned_client`. As part of the extraction, `og_fetch.rs`'s blocklist — previously a separate, narrower copy — is brought up to the full §4.6.5 list, adding `0.0.0.0/8` and `100.64.0.0/10` (CGNAT/Tailscale), both previously missing from `og_fetch.rs`'s SSRF coverage. `og_fetch.rs`'s redirect loop also now builds a fresh pinned `reqwest::Client` per hop via `net_guard::build_pinned_client` instead of reusing a single non-pinned client across all hops — the previous implementation re-validated each `Location` target's resolved address (SSRF re-check was already correct) but connected with a client that was never pinned to those checked addresses, leaving a narrow DNS-rebinding gap between the per-hop check and the per-hop connect; it's now closed on every hop, matching `web.rs`'s existing pinning discipline. All 61 of `web.rs`'s existing tests pass unchanged (test names, assertions, and behavior untouched — only the underlying blocklist/pre-check/resolve functions moved, now reached via `net_guard::` imports). 26 new `net_guard` unit tests cover the blocklist (one test per §4.6.5 blocked range, matching `web.rs`'s original per-range coverage), hostname pre-check, scheme allowlist, and `resolve_and_pin`/`build_pinned_client` (including a DNS-failure classification test). `og_fetch.rs` gains 6 new tests: `0.0.0.0/8` and `100.64.0.0/10` unit coverage on `is_blocked_ip` plus end-to-end `fetch_og_inner` integration tests for both ranges via a mocked redirect, a `10.0.0.0/8` redirect-rejection integration test (explicit private-range case, sentinel-body-never-leaks assertion, mirroring `web.rs`'s existing redirect-to-private-address test shape) — bringing `og_fetch.rs`'s own suite to 51 tests, all passing. (Relates to #2751)

- Extraction guard, PR A (#2745, #2750, spec `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.6.9 status note): memory extraction was saving too aggressively — PR-scoped procedural instructions, task assignments, and test requirements were being captured as if they were durable facts. `build_extraction_prompt` (`commands.rs`) gains an explicit rule against extracting instructions/task assignments/test requirements/process steps scoped to a specific PR, issue, build, or test run, with three negative examples pulled from real over-saves (a spec-delta-location note, a test-count/test-shape instruction, and a review-sequencing instruction). The `PROJECT DECISION RECOGNITION:` block is tightened to distinguish decisions that change how future work is done (extract, `decision` category) from what happens next in the current thread — task sequencing, who does what next (do not extract); `decision` stays a single category, no schema change. Two new filter-only fields, `source` (`"user"` | `"assistant"` | `"web"`) and `scope` (`"durable"` | `"episodic"`), are added to the LLM response schema and `RawEntry`/`MemoryEntry` (mirroring the existing `attribution` pattern) — captured on the extracted entry, consumed by the worker's output filter, never written to the `ai_memory` INSERT and no migration required. `filter_assistant_origin_facts` (`extraction_worker.rs`) gains two new mechanical drop signals alongside the existing attribution-origin signals: any fact tagged `source == "web"` is dropped regardless of the exchange-level `used_web_tools` flag (the §4.6.9 prompt warning stays a hint; this tag is the mechanical backstop for the residual paraphrase-gap risk accepted under ADR-0064), and any fact tagged `scope == "episodic"` is dropped. 15 new backend Rust tests cover: the three real over-save examples dropped end-to-end via the filter, a Tampa/Florida fixture proving a `source: "web"` fact is dropped while a `source: "user"` fact in the same batch survives, an episodic-tagged fact removed from filter output, `source: "web"` dropping independent of any exchange-level flag, durable/user-sourced facts passing through untouched, missing-field defaults (`"user"`/`"durable"`) passing through, a combined-multi-signal single-drop case, and 9 prompt-text assertions pinning the new negative examples, decision-tightening language, and source/scope field instructions in `build_extraction_prompt`'s output. Dedupe and confidence-threshold observability findings noted in #2745 were not actioned in this PR; escalation path filed as #2761. (Relates to #2745, #2750)
- Web Browsing Tools, Part 1 (#2591, ADR-0064, spec `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.6): the assistant can now fetch a specific web page via a new `web_fetch` tool. New `src-tauri/src/ai/web.rs` owns the full pipeline: a 6-step SSRF guard (scheme allowlist, hostname pre-check for `localhost`/`.local`/`.internal`, DNS resolution, an IP blocklist covering private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10, deliberately blocking Tailscale-reachable addresses per ADR-0064 D7)/multicast/reserved ranges with IPv4-mapped and NAT64 IPv6 addresses unwrapped and re-checked, a DNS-pinned client via `resolve_to_addrs` that connects to the exact addresses just checked (defeating DNS-rebinding TOCTOU), and a manual redirect loop that re-runs the full guard on every hop, capped at 5), a 5 MB streamed body cap, a content-type allowlist (HTML/XHTML/plain-text/Markdown only), readability extraction (`readabilityrs`) to Markdown with an empty-extraction gate for JS-heavy pages, and character-based truncation (`max_chars`, default 8000, clamped 1000-20000). Extracted content is always wrapped in `<<<EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT>>>` delimiters before being returned to the model, with an explicit instruction not to follow directions found inside it. `web_fetch` is offered only to `anthropic`/`openrouter`/`ollama`-runtime dispatches (`get_pane_tools_for_runtime`, never `openclaw` — OC sessions browse through OC's own tools) and is dispatch-gated so a text-fallback-parsed tool name that was never offered for a given dispatch cannot execute regardless of runtime. Successfully returning any external content taints the rest of that dispatch: `MUTATE_EXISTING_TOOLS` (edit/delete/move/status/priority/star, kept as a separate constant from the pre-existing `project_scoped_tools` — the two differ by exactly `star_project`/`create_note`) are withheld from the very next tool-call batch onward, so a page's content can never directly drive an edit to existing user data without the user's next message; `create_note` deliberately stays available so the assistant can still save what it found. A per-dispatch cap (`WEB_TOOL_CALLS_PER_TURN = 5`) limits total web-tool calls regardless of outcome. The background memory-extraction worker (`extraction_worker.rs`) now detects `web_fetch`/`web_search` usage on an extracted exchange (`load_extraction_pair`, reading the `chat_messages_local.tool_calls` column) and appends a warning line to the extraction prompt so fetched page content is never captured as if it were the user's own stated fact. 79 new backend Rust tests cover the SSRF guard (every blocked IP class including CGNAT/Tailscale and IPv4-mapped/NAT64 unwrapping, blocked hostnames, scheme allowlist, redirect-to-private-address rejection at the hop, and a 6-hop-rejected/5-hop-succeeds redirect chain), the DNS-pinned client, content-type rejection, the 5 MB body cap, Markdown extraction, truncation end-to-end through `execute_web_fetch` with the exact marker text, the taint/dispatch-gate refusal paths end-to-end (both the non-tainting-error half and the successful-fetch → taint → refused-edit → unchanged-note half), the per-turn cap end-to-end (sixth call refused with no HTTP request made), extraction-worker web-tool detection, and the extraction-pair query's exclusion of `tool_results` from `assistant_response`. `web_search` (Brave-backed) and its Settings UI are Part 2, not in this PR. (Relates to #2591, spec-covered-by: #2747)

- Web Browsing Tools, Part 2 (#2591, ADR-0064 D5, spec `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.6.8): the assistant can now search the web via a new `web_search` tool, backed by the user's own Brave Search API key or a self-hosted SearXNG instance. `web.rs` gains a backend-selection wrapper (`execute_web_search`) plus two independent client functions — `brave_search` (`GET https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search`, `X-Subscription-Token` header, reads `web.results[].{title,url,description}`) and `searxng_search` (`GET {endpoint}/search?q=<query>&format=json&count=<n>`, reads `results[].{title,url,content}`). SearXNG overrides Brave when both are configured (self-hosted, so it's presumed more trusted/intentional than a fallback API key). Neither client reuses Part 1's SSRF-pinning machinery (`build_pinned_client`/`resolve_and_check_host`) — Brave's endpoint is a fixed literal and the SearXNG endpoint is user-configured and explicitly exempt from the 4.6.5 address check (self-hosted instances are commonly on the LAN); result URLs still go through the full SSRF check when the model later calls `web_fetch` on them. With neither backend configured, `execute_web_search` returns the exact not-configured text with zero HTTP calls. Results are wrapped in the same `<<<EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT source="web_search">>>` delimiter convention as `web_fetch`, taint the rest of the dispatch identically, and share the same `WEB_TOOL_CALLS_PER_TURN = 5` per-turn cap counter with `web_fetch` (both tools combined, not tracked separately). Zero results returns a plain, undelimited `No results for "<query>".` (nothing external was returned, so no taint). `tools.rs` adds `web_search_tool_def()` (query required, count optional/clamped 1-10, default 5) to the same runtime allowlist gate as `web_fetch`. `commands.rs` adds a `web_search` dispatch branch mirroring `web_fetch`'s shape exactly, plus five new Settings-card Tauri commands — `save_brave_key`, `brave_key_status`, `remove_brave_key`, `save_searxng_endpoint`, `clear_searxng_endpoint`, `test_web_search` — deliberately NOT routed through `ai_configure_and_save`, which owns an unrelated 4-card provider-connection contract. **Credentials:** the Brave key is a new keychain-only account, `ai_brave_key` (`credential_migration::read_brave_key`/`write_brave_key`/`delete_brave_key`, added to `ALL_AI_KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNTS` for backup export) — it postdates ADR-0044 entirely, so unlike every other credential helper in that module it has no migration-flag branch and no plaintext `ai_settings` fallback; a keychain miss means not-configured, full stop. The SearXNG endpoint is a plain `ai_settings.searxng_endpoint` value (not a credential), Clear sets it to `""` (the codebase's existing clear idiom). **New "Web Search" Settings card** (Settings → AI, next to Semantic Search, above Link Embeds): a masked-key field (Save/Remove, reusing the existing `mask_secret` presentation), a collapsible "Advanced" SearXNG endpoint field (Save/Clear), a Test button that runs a live 1-result query against whichever backend is configured, and a status line covering all seven §4.6.8 states (not configured / Brave configured / SearXNG configured / SearXNG-only / test passed Brave / test passed SearXNG / test failed). Two deliberate copy rulings apply here, per Matt: the card's Brave link points to `https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com/` (where keys are actually created) rather than spec §4.6.8's `brave.com/search/api` marketing page, and the not-configured status line reads "Web search is off. Reading pages by URL still works." (design wording) rather than spec's chat-tool-facing "web_fetch still works with direct URLs" phrasing — the chat-side §4.6.7 tool-result text is unchanged either way. 18 new backend Rust tests cover: not-configured with no HTTP request (including a blank-string-treated-as-absent variant), SearXNG-overrides-Brave backend selection (and the Brave-only path), Brave's exact 401/403/429/other-non-2xx error texts, SearXNG's non-2xx text, zero-results (no delimiter, no taint), the `count` clamp, the `web_search` tool definition schema, all six runtime-gating tests updated to assert both web tools together, the shared-cap-counter proof (3 `web_fetch` + 3 `web_search` calls, capped on the 6th regardless of which tool it is), the full Brave-key keychain round-trip (write → read → delete, plus `ALL_AI_KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNTS` membership and the no-migration-fallback guarantee), and (post-audit, #2591) `test_web_search`'s returned error text having neither a leading "Web search failed: " prefix nor a trailing "Check ... in Settings" clause — the Settings card's own "Test failed: " wrapper already supplies the former, verified end-to-end against a mocked Brave 401 response. (Relates to #2591, spec-covered-by: #2747)

- Venice AI provider runtime (#2455, ADR-0065): Venice is now a standalone fifth AI provider. New `AiProvider::Venice` variant with its own `RequestOrigin::Venice` discriminant, plain system-root TLS client (never the gateway-pinned client), `venice_parameters: { include_venice_system_prompt: false }` body injection on every request (D2/D3), temperature always omitted (D5 — Venice's `/models` returns no `supported_parameters`), model name passed through verbatim (never rewritten to `"openclaw"`), and HTTP 402 error messaging updated to name Venice explicitly. New `validate_venice_key` Tauri command validates via `GET /api_keys/rate_limits` (not `/models`, which returns 200 for any key). Venice key is keychain-only (`ai_venice_key` account, ADR-0065 D4) — no legacy plaintext fallback matching `read_brave_key`'s posture. Venice is added to the `WEB_TOOL_RUNTIME_ALLOWLIST` (D6). Frontend: Venice card in Settings provider list, NewProviderModal picker row, AgentCreateOverlay runtime picker, and `PROVIDER_LABELS`/`RUNTIME_TYPE_LABELS` display maps. `ModelInfo.tier_label` carries Venice's per-model `model_spec.privacy` field verbatim for the picker's tier tag (None for all other providers). (Relates to #2455, spec-covered-by: #2769)
- Stateful echo suppression — tombstoning (#2410, §30.11 addendum, refined per Reed's scope audit `docs/audits/2026-08-24-tombstone-scope.md`). **Root problem:** the existing content-match backstop (`is_recent_local_assistant_echo`) is stateless — it only ever compares against the SINGLE most-recent local assistant row, so once a caught echo's own insert (or any subsequent genuine insert) becomes the new "most recent" row, the ORIGINAL echo stops matching on the next poll tick and silently resurrects as a duplicate insert 1-2 ticks later (the "tick-3 leak"). Migration v86 adds `chat_oc_tombstones` (`thread_id, oc_message_id, reason, tombstoned_at`, PK on `(thread_id, oc_message_id)`, per-device — NOT in `CRR_TABLES`, matching `chat_messages_local`'s own per-device scope) and `idx_chat_local_thread_role_ts` on `chat_messages_local(thread_id, role, created_at DESC)`, the index the new containment queries below scan against. Two new checks run **unconditionally** on every poll tick — including `suppress_ingest=true` ticks, since both checks only ever resolve messages that are ALREADY permanently settled one way or another, never a genuinely deferred message: (1) **Rule 1, the permanence pre-filter** (`is_already_classified`) — before anything else, drops any incoming message whose `(thread_id, oc_message_id)` is already either a real `chat_messages_local` row OR a prior tombstone; this is what makes classification permanent, since a tombstoned/ingested id can never reach the drifting single-row comparison again. The existing backstop loop now also writes a tombstone (`reason='backstop_echo'`) on every hit, closing the tick-3 leak at its source. (2) **Rule 2, refined stale-at-first-sight with content-containment** (`check_stale_echo`) — for messages surviving the pre-filter, a three-step gate: staleness (skip entirely if the message's own claimed `timestamp` is under 15 minutes old — fresh messages never touch this path), a 20-character content-length floor (short boilerplate like "Done." is never trusted enough to tombstone, even if stale — fails toward inserting), then a ±5-minute containment query anchored on the incoming message's OWN `timestamp` (never wall-clock `now`, avoiding the exact stateless-drift bug this feature fixes) against local assistant rows — a substring match tombstones as `stale_echo`; no match means a genuine late delivery (e.g. app closed 40+ minutes, agent finished while away) and the staleness gate is overridden, proceeding to the existing backstop/ingest path unchanged. Every tombstone write logs `[OC-PULL-TOMBSTONE] thread=... oc_msg_id=... reason=... content_preview="..."` (plus `matched_local_created_at` for `stale_echo` hits), matching the file's existing `[OC-PULL]` observability convention. `OcPullResult` gains two new counters, `already_classified_count` and `stale_echo_tombstoned_count`, alongside the existing `content_match_skipped_count`. 14 new backend Rust unit/integration tests (`tombstoning_tests`) cover: the pre-filter's three classification states (never-seen / real-row / tombstoned) and per-thread scoping; the tick-3 leak scenario end-to-end (backstop tombstones at tick 2, pre-filter alone catches it at tick 3, zero spurious inserts — the regression this feature closes); resurrection-via-content-match tombstoning both as a unit test and end-to-end through the full pipeline; genuine late delivery inserting both as a unit test and end-to-end; the length-floor bypass (short stale content with an otherwise-matching local row still inserts); the repeated-content rescue case (identical content outside the ±5min anchor window inserts, not tombstones — proves legitimate boilerplate re-sent later isn't falsely suppressed); migration idempotency (fresh install, a live re-run at current version, and a simulated v85→v86 re-run with pre-existing data surviving); a real `tests/fixtures/upgrade-from-v85.db` fixture migrating cleanly; and pre-filter unconditionality during `suppress_ingest=true`. (Relates to #2410, spec-covered-by: #2687)
- Echo suppression for the proactive delivery pipeline: live-turn dispatch no longer produces duplicate assistant messages via the 60s OC transcript poll (#2410, §30.11.4 PR 4). **Root cause:** OC's own internal (server-side) tool loop can expand a single Pane `ai_chat_stream` request into multiple assistant-role transcript segments (confirmed via a required pre-step correlating the `f16e623a` transcript's 7-segment turn against `tools.rs::get_pane_tools()` — Pane's client-side tool registry excludes `exec`, so the segments were produced server-side within one HTTP/SSE connection, not by 7 separate Pane-side loop iterations); meanwhile Pane's own `stream_openrouter_inner` SSE parser concatenates every `delta.content` chunk from that connection into one locally-saved row with `oc_message_id = NULL`, which the poll's dedup index can't match. **Two layered mechanisms, one PR:** (1) primary — `ChatSidebar.svelte`'s 60s poll now suppresses *ingestion* (not the fetch — "defer, don't skip") while a thread is actively streaming or within a 90s grace period after its last `done:true`, using a new per-thread `streamManager.getLastDoneAt(threadId)`/`isStreamingThread(threadId)` check (not the component-scoped `isStreaming` var, which doesn't reset on thread navigation and would be stale after switching sessions) — a new `suppress_ingest: Option<bool>` parameter threads through `pull_oc_transcript_for_session_cmd`/`pull_oc_transcript_for_session` so the gateway fetch still runs every tick (telemetry/dedup-discovery continues) but the mapped batch is withheld from `ingest_external_messages_impl` until suppression lifts — since this adapter has no cursor state (§30.11.3), a deferred message is simply re-fetched and normally ingested on the next eligible tick, never dropped; (2) defense-in-depth — a new `is_recent_local_assistant_echo` backstop in `commands.rs` catches the residual case where a poll tick lands just outside the frontend grace window: before insertion, it checks whether an incoming OC segment's content is a SUBSTRING of this thread's single most-recent local assistant row (not exact-equality — per the pre-step finding, Pane's local row is a concatenation of OC's segments), scoped to a 150s trailing window and a `datetime('now', '-N seconds')` SQL check (matching existing precedent elsewhere in this file) — reported via a new `content_match_skipped_count` field on `OcPullResult`. Both mechanisms are per-session scoped (keyed by `thread_id`), so one session's dispatch/grace window never suppresses a different session's cron/proactive delivery. 9 new backend Rust unit tests (`echo_suppression_tests`) cover content-match hit/miss, the 150s window boundary, per-thread scoping, a multi-segment-turn integration test (zero echoes ingested, a genuine same-batch cron message still lands), and the `suppress_ingest` defer-then-resume contract; 4 new frontend tests (`ChatSidebar.echoSuppression.test.ts`) cover the streaming gate, the 90s grace window boundary, and that the fetch still fires every tick during suppression (defer, not skip). (Relates to #2410, spec-skip: echo suppression is internal poll/ingest plumbing, no user-facing behavioral change, spec-covered-by: #2687)
- OC transcript pull now baselines on first poll (no backfill insertion) and filters to assistant-role text messages only (#2410, §30.11). Migration v85 (`src-tauri/src/migrations.rs`) adds `chat_sessions.oc_baseline_done_at TEXT` (idempotent, pragma-checked before `ALTER`, matching the `migrate_v84` pattern). `pull_oc_transcript_for_session` (`src-tauri/src/ai/commands.rs`) now checks this column immediately after fetching the raw OC transcript: if unset (the session's first-ever pull), it stamps `oc_baseline_done_at = datetime('now')` and returns a skip result (`skip_reason: "first pull: baselined N message(s), none ingested"`) without mapping or inserting anything — the existing 20-message history a session already has is no longer re-inserted as if newly arrived. Subsequent pulls proceed as before. Separately, `map_oc_message_to_external` now rejects any non-`"assistant"` role (closing the leak where OC's own user-role echoes of Pane-originated cron/proactive payloads were being ingested as if Matt had typed them) and rejects messages whose flattened content is empty after trimming (closing the leak where pure-toolCall assistant turns, which have no text block, inserted as blank rows). Both guards are early returns in the existing mapper — no new function, no gateway changes. (Relates to #2410, spec-skip: ingestion filtering is internal plumbing, no user-facing behavioral change, spec-covered-by: #2687)
- External message ingestion command (`ingest_external_messages`, `src-tauri/src/ai/commands.rs`) for proactive message delivery (#2410, §30.11). Provider-neutral: accepts a batch of `ExternalMessage` records (target session, dedup key, role, content, timestamp, source agent for binding) and writes them directly to `chat_messages_local` via `INSERT OR IGNORE` against a new partial unique index (see Migration v84 below) — deliberately not `save_chat_message`'s `INSERT OR REPLACE`, which is keyed on local `id` and would never catch a same-content replay. Per-message skip-not-abort: one message's dedup hit or binding mismatch never blocks the rest of the batch. A `target_session_id` with no matching `chat_sessions` row is treated as a binding mismatch (`binding_mismatch_count`), the same skip bucket as an agent-id mismatch — not a distinct DB-error failure class (correction, #2410: PR 2's original PR body described a missing session as a separate "DB error" case; the implemented code has always treated it as `BindingMismatch`, which is more conservative, not less — still skip-not-abort, just counted under the mismatch bucket rather than `errors`). Reports split skip counts (`inserted_count`, `dedup_skipped_count`, `binding_mismatch_count`, `errors`) rather than a single opaque total, so callers can distinguish deliberate no-ops from real failures. Does not bump `chat_sessions.last_active_at` (matching existing user-message behavior) and structurally never calls `ai_chat_stream` or any streaming/dispatch path — append-only, no dispatch coupling. Backend-only this PR; no frontend caller yet.
- Migration v84 (`src-tauri/src/migrations.rs`): adds `chat_messages_local.oc_message_id TEXT` and a partial unique index `idx_chat_local_oc_dedup ON chat_messages_local(thread_id, oc_message_id) WHERE oc_message_id IS NOT NULL`, the dedup key `ingest_external_messages` inserts against (#2410, §30.11.2). Idempotent (pragma-checked before `ALTER`, `IF NOT EXISTS` on the index), matching the `migrate_v79` pattern.
- OpenClaw transcript pull adapter (`pull_oc_transcript_for_session`, `src-tauri/src/ai/commands.rs`) fetches a session's recent OC transcript (`GET /v1/sessions/{session}/messages?limit=20`, no `since`/`before` cursor — OC has none; over-fetches a small recent page and lets dedup discard already-seen messages) and feeds it through `ingest_external_messages`. Derives the composite OC session key (`agent:{runtime_ref}:openai-user:pane-{session_id}`) fresh on every call rather than caching it, since the underlying OC session key can rotate. Gateway/transport failures (502, timeout, malformed JSON) are handled gracefully — logged and returned as a clean skip result, never a panic or propagated error, so the next poll tick simply retries. New helper `session_uses_openclaw_runtime` gates which sessions are eligible for polling; unlike `check_bound_agent_active`, it does not check `is_active` — per ADR-0062 Amendment (2026-08-23), a locked/inactive agent's session still receives proactive messages even though dispatch stays refused. Both remain internal-only (no Tauri command registered) — wiring the frontend poll loop is PR 3's scope.
- Frontend 60-second proactive-message poll (`ChatSidebar.svelte`, #2410, §30.11.4) wires PR 2's backend to the UI. Two new thin `#[tauri::command]` wrappers (`pull_oc_transcript_for_session_cmd`, `session_uses_openclaw_runtime_cmd`, `src-tauri/src/ai/commands.rs`) expose the existing internal functions to `invoke()`. A `setInterval(..., 60_000)` runs inside an `$effect`, gated on three conditions simultaneously: the session is open (`$activeChatThreadId` non-empty), the app is focused (`document.visibilityState === 'visible'` and `tauri://focus`, reusing `+page.svelte`'s existing focus-tracking pattern), and the session is bound to an openclaw-runtime agent (checked once per session-open/switch via `session_uses_openclaw_runtime_cmd`, not every tick — the binding is immutable per ADR-0062 D1). The interval is cleared (not just skipped) on session switch, app blur/background, or a non-OC session, and restarts when focus returns to an eligible open session. Each tick calls `pull_oc_transcript_for_session_cmd` for the current thread; when it reports `inserted_count > 0`, the existing `loadMessages(threadId)` reloads the message list from the DB — reusing the ordinary DB-backed load path rather than duplicating the greeting pattern's manual `allMessages` append. A `skip_reason` or `inserted_count === 0` result is silent — no error toast, matching the poll's designed-graceful-skip contract. Structurally cannot trigger dispatch: the poll only ever calls `pull_oc_transcript_for_session_cmd`, which internally reaches `ingest_external_messages`'s `INSERT OR IGNORE` — no `ai_chat_stream` call site anywhere in the poll path.

### Fixed
- OpenClaw disconnect-arm promote gap + keychain-ordering hazard + Venice disconnect promote gap + dead-code removal (#2793, scope audit `docs/audits/2026-09-01-2793-openclaw-disconnect-promote-scope.md`, spec correction `docs/spec/sync.md` disconnect invariant block rule 2). Same structural bug class Reed previously found and fixed for Venice's *save* path in #2796, found here on OpenClaw's (and, latently, Venice's) *disconnect* path. **Bug 1 (PRIMARY) — OC disconnect promote gap:** `ai_disconnect_runtime_impl`'s `"openclaw"` arm demotes and promotes a fallback default on disconnect, but its demote UPDATE only clears `is_default` on OC's own rows (`WHERE runtime_type = 'openclaw'`); a foreign provider's default row (Anthropic/OpenRouter/Ollama/Venice) is untouched and may still hold `idx_ai_agents_default`'s single global `is_default = 1` slot. The prior unconditional promote query then either silently no-oped or attempted a second `is_default = 1` write, hitting the partial UNIQUE index and rolling back the entire disconnect transaction. A global existence guard (`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM ai_agents WHERE is_active = 1 AND is_default = 1)`), taken inside the same transaction immediately before the promote query and mirroring #2796's Venice-save fix, now gates the promote — it only ever fills an empty seat, never contests an occupied one. **Bug 2 (CRITICAL, Matt's ruling) — keychain-vs-transaction ordering:** the OC gateway token's keychain deletion previously ran *before* `BEGIN`, outside the DB transaction. If the transaction later rolled back (exactly the Bug 1 collision, pre-fix), the credential was already gone from the OS keychain while every DB-side effect rolled back — a partial-failure state (DB still says "connected", credential needed to actually talk to the gateway is gone, no way to retry short of re-pairing from scratch). The keychain delete now runs only after a successful `COMMIT`; a rolled-back transaction leaves the keychain token fully intact and OC connected, so the user can simply retry. **Bug 3 — Venice disconnect had zero promote logic:** unlike OC (and unlike Venice's own *save*/reconnect path, #2796), Venice's disconnect arm deactivated and demoted Venice's rows but never attempted to promote a replacement default — if Venice held the global default, disconnecting it left the seat permanently empty until the user manually picked a new default agent. Venice's disconnect arm (previously not wrapped in any transaction) now runs inside `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`, matching the OC arm's structure, with the identical global-guard + conditional-promote logic added after the demote step. **Item 4 — dead code removal:** `agents::deactivate_agent` (a `#[tauri::command]` with zero frontend `invoke()` call sites, and which had the same latent same-family promote gap — it flips `is_active = 0` without touching `is_default` or promoting a replacement) is removed from `agents.rs`, along with its registration in `lib.rs`'s `invoke_handler!` list; per Matt's ruling, removed rather than fixed since it has no live caller. An existing raw-SQL test that exercised the same `is_active` toggle shape (never the removed command itself) is renamed, not removed, to reflect that it was never actually testing `deactivate_agent`. **Spec:** `docs/spec/sync.md`'s disconnect invariant block (rule 2, added #2647/#2648) described demote-then-promote without noting the demote's per-runtime scope; a correction note is appended in place documenting the global-guard requirement this fix adds and naming it as the pattern now shared by every disconnect arm that promotes a fallback default. **Tests:** 5 new backend Rust tests — `test_disconnect_openclaw_does_not_steal_foreign_default` and `_when_newest_row` (the second seeds the foreign default as the newest-`created_at` row, the exact naive pick the pre-fix promote query would have made, proving the guard blocks the promote structurally rather than by row-ordering luck), `test_disconnect_openclaw_tx_failure_leaves_keychain_intact` (forces a transaction failure independent of Bug 1's guard by dropping `ai_settings` mid-transaction, asserts the keychain token and the OC agent's `is_active`/`is_default` state are both untouched by the rollback), and `test_disconnect_venice_promotes_fallback_when_venice_was_default` (Venice held the default; after disconnect, the other active agent is promoted and exactly one `is_default = 1` row exists system-wide). (Relates to #2793)

- Venice provider-dispatch gaps + Smart Features UX (#2795 follow-up, sweep `docs/audits/2026-09-01-venice-unsupported-sweep.md`).
