Reed's post-#2811/#2812 sweep of every `AiProvider`/provider-name match site in the codebase found 4 remaining gaps where a *second*, *local* `AiProvider -> (provider_name, api_key, endpoint)` conversion match — downstream of `get_internal_provider`/`resolve_runtime_config_for_default_agent`, both of which already build `AiProvider::Venice` correctly per #2795 — was missing its Venice arm, silently dropping Venice into that match's `_` catch-all. All 4 fixes are the identical additive shape (`AiProvider::Venice { api_key, .. } => ("venice".to_string(), api_key.clone(), None)`, mirroring `commands.rs`'s 8 other existing Venice arms) — no new plumbing, since every downstream sink (`call_llm_from_config`, `stream_openrouter` + `RequestOrigin::Venice`) already accepts Venice. **Gap 1 (CRITICAL, confirmed broken in the v1.0.41 build log — `[EXTRACTION] Unsupported internal provider variant for extraction`):** `extraction_worker.rs`'s internal-provider dispatch match for the background extraction-job queue now has a Venice arm — Venice-primary/Venice-internal installs' extraction jobs no longer silently fail. **Gap 2 (HIGH):** `ai_chat_stream`'s internal-provider single-retry-on-transient-error block (`commands.rs`) was missing the Venice arm present on its sibling primary-dispatch and fallback-retry blocks — a transient error (429/timeout) on a Venice stream fell into `_ => Err(("Streaming not supported"...))`, discarding the real error and masking it with a misleading message instead of retrying. Now retries via `stream_openrouter` + `VENICE_API_BASE` + `RequestOrigin::Venice`, identical to the sibling arms. **Gap 3 (MEDIUM):** both consolidator trigger paths in `lib.rs` (the router-triggered `trigger-consolidator` event listener and the one-time startup staleness-check pass) were silently no-oping (`eprintln!` + `return`) for Venice-primary installs — background note consolidation now runs for Venice the same as every other provider. **Gap 4 (LOW):** `ai_chat_stream`'s daily-log narrative generation trigger (`commands.rs`) silently skipped Venice (`_ => return None`) — Venice-primary installs now get the auto-generated daily narrative instead of falling all the way through past the mechanical entry-count fallback. `notes.rs::ai_save_config` was confirmed dead code (no live caller) and intentionally left unfixed per the sweep's ruling. **UX fix 1 — per-feature Smart Features config false-gating:** the Extraction/Smart-Routing/Rerank model pickers under Settings → Smart Features previously rendered only when `internalConnectionStatus === 'success'`, which always starts `'not-tested'` on mount (§28.1 invariant) — a returning user with an already-stored Venice (or OpenRouter/Anthropic) key saw no model pickers until re-saving, the same false-gating shape as the earlier Test-button bug (#2631). A new `internalHasConfiguredKey` derived value (checks `internalVeniceKeyMasked` for Venice, `internalApiKey` for OpenRouter/Anthropic, always-true for Ollama) now OR-gates the picker section alongside the existing fresh-success path. **UX fix 2 — Semantic Search provider clarity:** the embeddings/Semantic Search provider dropdown's sublabel now states "Only providers with embedding support are listed," explaining why Venice (and any other non-embedding provider) doesn't appear there — no provider-list change, description text only. Backend: 4 new source-scan tests (`dual_provider_tests.rs::venice_dispatch_gap_tests`) mechanically assert each fixed match block carries its `AiProvider::Venice` arm — each site is unreachable from a plain unit test without a live `AppHandle` (spawned worker loop, `app.listen` event handler, or a closure buried inside `ai_chat_stream`'s streaming loop), matching the existing `tests_2604_stream_done_agent_attribution` source-scan precedent; all 4 were test-the-tested (reverted, confirmed red, restored, confirmed green) per the dev-hygiene playbook. Frontend: 6 new tests (`Settings.smart-features-config-gate.test.ts`) cover the `internalHasConfiguredKey` derivation, the OR-gate on the model-picker block, and the Semantic Search description text; all were test-the-tested via a full revert/restore cycle. (Relates to #2795, spec-covered-by: #2811)

- Onboarding sender label stuck on "Pane" after the first agent is created (#2794, provider card Show/Hide disabled while empty (#2783), formal diagnosis `docs/audits/2026-08-31-2794-2783-formal-diagnosis.md`). **Fix 1 (#2794) — root cause:** `ChatSidebar.svelte`'s Home bound-agent-name resolution only ran inside an `$effect` keyed on `$activeChatThreadId`/`isHomeSurface`. On a fresh install, `navigateTo()` sets `$activeChatThreadId` at app boot — BEFORE onboarding has created the first `ai_agents` row — so the effect resolved once to `homeBoundAgentName = null` / `homeAgentsLoaded = true` against an empty agent roster and never re-ran, because `$activeChatThreadId` never changes again across the entire onboarding flow. `resolveSenderName()` (`ChatPanel.svelte`) then fell through to the literal `'Pane'` for every assistant message in that session-open — greeting and streaming placeholder included — until a reload/thread-switch re-fired the effect. The resolution logic is extracted into a standalone `resolveHomeBoundAgent()` function, called both from the original `$effect` (thread/surface change, unchanged trigger) and from a new `'pane-onboarding-complete'` window-event listener (cleaned up on component destroy) that re-invokes it once `Onboarding.svelte`'s `ensureMainAgent()` creates the first agent and dispatches that event — no `$activeChatThreadId` change required. **Diagnostic visibility (#2794, required per task):** `resolveSenderName()`'s existing `[2604-PROBE]` console diagnostic for the `'Pane'` fallback hit is gated behind `localStorage['pane-debug'] === '1'`, invisible in a production log capture. A new backend echo, `log_sender_name_fallback_cmd` (`src-tauri/src/ai/commands.rs`), is invoked (fire-and-forget, unconditional `eprintln!`, no DEBUG gate) every time `resolveSenderName()` reaches the `'Pane'` fallback with `sessionAgentsLoaded === true`, logging the thread id and resolution state — so the fallback hit is visible in any process log capture (e.g. live tests) without requiring the localStorage flag. **Fix 2 (#2783):** `apiKeyInput` always starts empty — `masked_credential` is only ever wired into the input's `placeholder`, never its `value` (no raw-secret round-trip to the renderer, by design). Placeholders render identically under `type="password"`/`type="text"` (no dots either way), so toggling Show/Hide with nothing typed genuinely has no visible effect, reading as broken. `ProviderConnectionCard.svelte`'s Show/Hide button is now disabled (greyed out, matching the existing `.pcc-btn-ghost:disabled` pattern) while `apiKeyInput.trim() === ''`, re-enabling the instant the user types a character — UX-only, no backend change, no stored-secret round-trip. **Tests:** 4 new frontend tests (`ChatSidebar.onboardingAgentName.test.ts`) cover the fresh-install repro end-to-end (thread opens before the agent exists → 'Pane' → `pane-onboarding-complete` fires → re-resolves to the new agent name), the streaming placeholder carrying the re-resolved name via `sessionBoundAgentName`, a no-agent-created no-op/no-crash case, and listener cleanup on unmount; 6 new frontend tests (`ProviderConnectionCard.test.ts`, group E2) cover the disabled/enabled states across empty/stored-key/typed/cleared/whitespace-only inputs; 3 new backend Rust tests cover `log_sender_name_fallback_cmd`'s always-Ok contract. (Relates to #2794, Relates to #2783, spec-skip: non-architectural UX fixes (sender label timing, button disable state))

- Certificate pinning bypass on non-streaming OpenClaw calls (#2775, scope audit `docs/audits/2026-08-31-cert-pinning-scope.md`). **Root cause:** five call sites reaching `select_openrouter_client` for non-streaming OpenClaw dispatches passed `db: None` even though a `DbState` handle was available one or two frames up the call stack, forcing every one of these calls onto the pre-pairing `danger_accept` TLS fallback (no SPKI pinning, no cert validation) instead of the pinned client a paired install's stored `gateway_tls_cert_pem` should have selected. **Fix — Option A, thread `&DbState` through 5 gaps + 1 ruled case:** (1) `check_contradiction` (`commands.rs`) gains a `db: Option<&DbState>` param, threaded from its only caller, `ai_save_memory`. (2) `call_ai_no_stream` (`commands.rs`) gains the same param, threaded into `call_llm_from_config` and both its callers — `generate_daily_narrative` (which now takes an owned `DbState` clone into its spawned task, mirroring `ai_synthesize_all_memories`'s existing `db_clone` pattern) and `maybe_compact_thread` (whose `db_state` param was already in scope, just never passed through). (3) `consolidator::consolidate_file` now passes `Some(db_state)` instead of `None` — `db_state` was already a direct parameter, one line from the call site; the false "db (not available in this context)" comment is corrected. (4) `ai_synthesize_all_memories`'s spawned per-project closure now wraps its existing `db_clone` (already cloned for the DB write-back) into a `DbState` and passes it to the LLM call too, instead of `None`; same false-comment correction. (5) `ai_extract_memory` (the Tauri command, ruled a required fix rather than an intentional gap) gains a `db: State<'_, DbState>` param matching every sibling command, passing `Some(&db)` through to `ai_extract_memory_with_db` — the prior comment declaring the gap "intentional" was not backed by any mechanism; no frontend caller needed updating since Tauri injects `State` params automatically. The legitimate pre-pairing `danger_accept` fallback for fresh (unpaired) installs is untouched — `build_gateway_client_with_cert`'s `_ =>` arm (empty/missing stored cert) is unchanged; this fix only changes whether the DB handle **arrives** at that branch point, not what happens when there's genuinely no cert yet. **`ai_synthesize_all_memories`/`consolidate_file` `_impl` split:** both were also refactored into a thin `#[tauri::command]`/public wrapper (keeps the `tauri::AppHandle` for its `pane-note-changed`/`pane-reload-editor` emit) and an inner `_impl` function taking only `db_state`/`db` — `tauri::test::mock_app()`'s `App<MockRuntime>` cannot satisfy a literal `tauri::AppHandle` (`AppHandle<Wry>`) parameter, so this split (matching the existing `ai_disconnect_runtime`/`_impl` precedent) was required to unit-test the DB-threading fact without a real Tauri runtime; behavior is unchanged, the wrapper still emits on every path the original function did. **Tests, three tiers per the scope audit:** Tier 1 — a `#[cfg(test)]` stamp mechanism (`ClientPathStamp` enum, `LAST_CLIENT_PATH` thread-local, `test_take_last_client_path()`) added to `gateway_client.rs`, since `reqwest::Client` doesn't expose its TLS config for inspection and log-text matching was explicitly ruled out; `test_select_client_openclaw_origin_with_db_and_cert_uses_pinned_client` (`openrouter.rs`) proves `db: Some(..)` + a stored cert selects the pinned path, alongside the pre-existing pre-pairing-fallback counterpart. Tier 2 — one threading test per gap (`check_contradiction`, `call_ai_no_stream`, `consolidate_file`, `ai_synthesize_all_memories`), each asserting the stamp reads `Pinned` when a paired `DbState` is passed through, using an unreachable/plain-HTTP endpoint since only client **selection** (which happens before any network I/O) is under test, not the network call's outcome. Tier 3 — a real local TLS listener (`rcgen` + `tokio-rustls`, since `mockito` is HTTP-only and can't exercise pinning) presenting a deliberately mismatched SPKI cert against a paired client's stored pin: `test_pinned_client_rejects_mismatched_spki_cert` asserts the request fails with a TLS/certificate error (a successful response would mean `danger_accept` is silently swallowing the mismatch — exactly this bug class), with `test_pinned_client_accepts_matching_spki_cert` as the sanity counterpart proving the harness itself isn't just broken. **Ride-along fix (found during Tier 1/2 test-writing, pre-existing on `main`, unrelated to the #2775 gaps themselves):** two existing `gateway_client.rs` tests (`test_build_gateway_client_no_cert`, `test_build_gateway_client_with_valid_cert`) called `database::init_database(None)` without setting `PANE_TEST_ROOT` first, which resolves to the real production `~/Pane` install rather than a test fixture — every `cargo test` run on `main` was silently overwriting the live `gateway_tls_cert_pem`/`ai_settings` config on disk. Both are now isolated via a `tempfile::TempDir` + `PANE_TEST_ROOT`, and all new tests in this PR follow the same isolation discipline from the start. (Relates to #2775, spec-skip: security fix to existing plumbing — DB-handle threading through call sites that already had the handle available, not new architecture)

- AgentCreateOverlay's `RUNTIME_LABELS` map was missing an `openclaw` entry (#2771, found by Reed during the Venice build-scope census, `docs/audits/2026-08-29-venice-build-scope.md` §6 #18) — OpenClaw agents rendered their raw `runtime_type` string ("openclaw") in the runtime/model-step labels instead of "OpenClaw". Added the missing `openclaw: 'OpenClaw'` entry, matching the other five display-label maps already covering it. **Ride-along (#2794):** `ChatSidebar.svelte`'s `resolveGreetingAgentName()` now logs a `[GREETING]` diagnostic `console.warn` at the final `'Pane'` fallback, naming which of the two lookup steps missed (bound-agent lookup: skip because no `agent_id` was bound vs. a miss because the bound agent wasn't found or had an empty name; `get_main_agent`: a miss because it returned an agent with an empty/whitespace name vs. a miss because it returned `null` or threw) — the fallback chain itself is unchanged, this only adds observability so a future "greeting says Pane" report (like #2794's Venice-onboarding repro) can be triaged from the console instead of re-deriving the fallback chain from scratch. 5 new frontend tests added to `ChatSidebar.greetingAgent.test.ts` cover all four diagnostic-message permutations plus two negative cases confirming the warning never fires on a successful bound-agent or default-agent resolution. (Relates to #2771, Relates to #2794, spec-skip: map entry completeness fix + diagnostic log, not new architecture)

- Venice save no longer steals the default-agent seat from a foreign provider (#2791, scope audit `docs/audits/2026-08-31-venice-default-promote-scope.md`). **Root cause:** `ai_configure_and_save`'s Venice arm gated its "does anyone already hold the default seat?" guard (`has_default`) on `runtime_type = 'venice'`, so it evaluated `false` on every Venice save until Venice itself had a default row — even when a different provider (Anthropic, OpenRouter, Ollama, OpenClaw) already held the single global `is_default = 1` seat enforced by `idx_ai_agents_default`'s table-wide partial UNIQUE index. The promote branch then ran unconditionally, demoting whoever currently held the seat and handing it to Venice on every save/reconnect. **Fix:** the `has_default` guard query (`commands.rs:4288`) drops the `runtime_type = 'venice'` filter and checks globally (`WHERE is_active = 1 AND is_default = 1`) — a one-line scope fix. No other change to the venice arm: the reactivate step, the promote-candidate eligibility filter, and the demote/promote UPDATE pair were all already correct per the audit. The existing regression test (`commands.rs`, previously `test_venice_save_promote_does_not_violate_unique_constraint_with_foreign_default`) asserted the buggy behavior as correct; it is renamed to `test_venice_save_must_not_steal_default_from_foreign_provider` and its assertions flipped — an active foreign (Anthropic) default now survives a Venice save unchanged, and the reactivated Venice agent is confirmed NOT promoted, while still asserting exactly one `is_default = 1` row system-wide. A new test, `test_venice_save_promotes_when_no_default_exists_anywhere`, covers the legitimate F3 case: with no active default row anywhere in the table (fresh install), a Venice save still correctly promotes a reactivated Venice agent to fill the empty seat. **Ride-along (ADR-0065 D5 copy cleanup):** the onboarding Venice card and the New Provider modal's Venice descriptor both made an implicit privacy claim ("Private, uncensored models" / "Privacy-focused AI on Venice") that ADR-0065 D5 forbids — Pane makes no privacy claims of its own for Venice anywhere in product. Both are reworded to neutral, non-privacy-claiming copy: "Your Venice API models." A repo-wide grep for "private"/"uncensored"/"anonymous" on Venice-related rows/strings found no other instances. (Relates to #2791, spec-skip: bug fix to existing logic, not new architecture)
- v1.0.36 live-test round 2 — six findings scoped and fixed (#2455, audit `docs/audits/2026-08-30-venice-livetest-v2-scope.md`). **F1 — Ollama has no card and can't be added:** new one-time migration `migrate_v89` (SCHEMA_VERSION 88→89) backfills `ollama_configured_at` on upgrade when `ollama_endpoint` is already set (the v82 grandfather case) but the v88 backfill's keychain-only design structurally couldn't cover Ollama (it has no keychain account). `NewProviderModal.svelte`'s `isProviderConfigured` predicate is realigned from `connected === true` to `configured_this_install === true`, matching `ProviderConnectionsPanel.svelte`'s card-visibility gate — the two predicates had diverged onto different fields, so a grandfathered Ollama install (reachable, `connected: true`, but never `configured_this_install`) showed no card AND was hidden from "New Provider" as if already connected. Cross-reference comments added at both sites so a future card-visibility change can't re-diverge them. **F2 — Test button ignores stored key:** `validate_anthropic_key`/`validate_openrouter_key`/`validate_venice_key` (`system_files.rs`, `commands.rs`) now accept `Option<String>`; when `None` (empty input), they read the already-saved keychain credential via the existing `read_provider_key`/`read_venice_key` helpers before validating, instead of unconditionally erroring "Enter an API key to test." on an untouched, already-configured card. `ProviderConnectionCard.svelte` passes `null` when its input field is empty rather than always sending the raw (often blank) string. **F3 — Venice save promote UNIQUE constraint failure:** `ai_configure_and_save`'s Venice reconnect arm now globally demotes any existing default agent (`UPDATE ai_agents SET is_default = 0 WHERE is_default = 1`) before promoting a reactivated Venice agent to default — the prior check only asked whether *Venice* held the default seat, so reconnecting Venice while a different runtime's agent already held `idx_ai_agents_default`'s table-wide partial-unique `is_default` slot hit a raw UNIQUE constraint violation and failed the whole save. New regression test seeds a non-Venice (Anthropic) default agent before a Venice reconnect and asserts the save succeeds, Venice becomes the sole default, and the prior default is demoted. **F4 — Venice agents invisible to rosters / Venice missing from several enumeration surfaces:** `DefaultAgentPickerModal.svelte` gains `venice` in both `groupOrder` and `RUNTIME_LABELS` (previously Venice agents were silently dropped from the Default-agent picker's grouping entirely). A follow-up grep sweep for hardcoded 4-runtime (`openclaw`/`openrouter`/`anthropic`/`ollama`) lists across the codebase found and fixed two further gaps: `AgentCreateOverlay.svelte`'s forced-create Step 0 provider-picker button row and `handleTestProvider` dispatch were missing a Venice option entirely (button + `validate_venice_key` call added), and `ReadOnlySessionNotice.svelte`'s `PROVIDER_LABELS` map (ADR-0062 D5's read-only-session notice) was missing a `venice: 'Venice'` entry, which would have shown the raw string "venice" instead of "Venice" if a Venice-bound session ever went read-only. The sweep also confirmed several near-miss sites are already correct (`api.ts`, `types.ts`, `Settings.svelte`'s `RUNTIME_TYPE_ORDER`/`RUNTIME_TYPE_LABELS`, `ProviderConnectionCard.svelte`'s `RUNTIME_LABELS`/`RUNTIME_LOGOS`, `agents.rs`'s runtime-type validators, `ai/tools.rs`'s `WEB_TOOL_RUNTIME_ALLOWLIST`, `credential_migration.rs`'s `ALL_AI_KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNTS`) and one intentionally-frozen exception (`migrations.rs`'s historical `migrate_v79`, a point-in-time migration correctly left untouched). `RuntimeConnectionInfo`'s doc comment (`commands.rs`) is also corrected to mention `venice`/`validate_venice_key` alongside the other runtimes. The Smart Features internal-provider screen's Venice gap (`get_internal_provider`'s internal-provider arms, and `list_available_models`'s Venice model-search fallback) is out of scope for this PR — it needs its own design pass, tracked separately. **F5 — Sync reassertion / Stia-in-picker:** `sync_client.rs`'s initial-import role-reassertion path already correctly re-applies the B5 subagent-exclusion predicate (`role = 'sub' AND runtime_ref IS NOT NULL`) on every sync pull; confirmed correct and documented in place, no code fix needed. **F6 — No validation log on Venice save:** `validate_venice_key` gains `[VENICE_VALIDATE]` log lines at entry, the no-key/stored-key-fallback branch, failure, and success — matching the existing `[OPENROUTER_VALIDATE]`/`[ANTHROPIC_VALIDATE]` convention used by the other two key-based validators. New backend Rust tests cover F1 (`migrate_v89` backfill/idempotency), F3 (the foreign-default UNIQUE-constraint regression above), and F2's `Option<String>` stored-key fallback for all three validators — 9 new tests (3 per validator: `None` input falls back to a stored key and reaches the mocked HTTP call rather than short-circuiting, `None` input with no stored key returns the exact "No API key provided and no stored key found" error with zero HTTP calls, and a typed `Some(...)` key wins over a stored key, proven by asserting on the actual Authorization/x-api-key header the mock server received) — added post-review (Reed's 2026-08-30 delta review flagged that the PR's initial claim of F2 test coverage did not match the diff at review time; `validate_openrouter_key`/`validate_anthropic_key`/`validate_venice_key` gained new `#[cfg(test)]` thread-local URL overrides so these command-level tests can run against a real `mockito` server instead of the hardcoded production endpoints). `NewProviderModal.test.ts` gains coverage for the realigned `configured_this_install` predicate. Onboarding's provider picker (`Onboarding.svelte`, `docs/spec/onboarding.md`) is updated to include Venice as a selectable provider option end-to-end. Two documentation nits from the same review are also fixed: `Onboarding.svelte`'s entry-point census comment misnamed `NewProviderModal.svelte`'s `PROVIDER_ROWS` constant as `PROVIDER_OPTIONS`, and a CSS comment cited a nonexistent `docs/spec/06-ai-providers.md` file instead of the actual `docs/spec/onboarding.md` ruling note. (Relates to #2455, spec-skip: live-test fixes scoped by Reed)
- Fixed Brave wrong-key detection: Brave returns HTTP 422 (not 401) for invalid keys; now parses error.code to show the friendly rejection message. Added body logging on all non-2xx Brave/SearXNG responses (#2759, live-evidence audit `docs/audits/2026-08-27-brave-422-scoping.md`).
- Identity-based own-turn tombstoning closes the short-live-reply duplicate-note gap that content-length-based echo suppression structurally cannot catch (#2738). **Root problem:** §30.11.7's content-length floor (20 chars) means a short live reply Pane's OWN dispatch produces (e.g. a 4-character reply like "Gold") can echo back through the 60s OC transcript poll as if it were a genuinely new proactive message — there is no length threshold that admits a genuine short delivery while excluding an own-reply echo of the same length, since both look identical by content alone. **Fix:** a third, identity-based check layered on top of §30.11.7's existing content checks (which remain untouched as fallback), relying on a confirmed OC guarantee (source-scope audit: `docs/audits/2026-08-26-issues-2738-2739-source-scope.md`) that OC serializes all turns per session — two independent OC-side mechanisms (`beginSessionWorkAdmission`'s scoped admission lock, `replyRunRegistry`'s one-active-run-per-key guard) plus a structural backstop (transcript-append FIFO queue + write lock, from which `chat.history`'s `__openclaw.seq` is assigned) together guarantee all `seq` values one turn produces are strictly less than the next turn's. New `fetch_oc_latest_seq` (`src-tauri/src/ai/commands.rs`) records this session's max `__openclaw.seq` as a baseline immediately before `ai_chat_stream`'s first outbound OC call (OpenClaw-runtime dispatches only); new `tombstone_own_turn` re-fetches `chat.history` at **every** terminal `done:true` emit site (success, reconnect-budget-exhausted error, and iteration-cap/timeout fallback — all three, not just the happy path, so an aborted/errored turn's partial output is still tombstoned) and writes a `chat_oc_tombstones` row (`reason="own_turn"`, via the existing `write_tombstone` helper) for every assistant-role message whose `seq` exceeds the baseline. Both functions re-derive the OC session **key** fresh from `runtime_ref`/`session_id` on every call, matching §30.11.3's existing never-cache convention, which also makes mid-turn OC session-id rotation transparent (each call simply resolves the gateway's current state for the stable key). Storage is in-memory only, scoped to the dispatch's own spawned-task closure (`own_turn_baseline_seq: Option<i64>`) — not a DB column, not a cross-dispatch cache; a baseline's entire lifetime is exactly one in-flight dispatch. Best-effort throughout: any failure to resolve gateway context or reach the gateway is logged and swallowed, never propagating into `ai_chat_stream`'s own response — a dispatch whose tombstone pass fails simply falls back on §30.11.7's pre-existing content-based checks for that turn's own messages. 4 new backend tests (`own_turn_tombstone_tests_2738`) cover: the exact bug-report reproduction ("Gold", 4 chars, tombstoned and confirmed never re-inserted via a full round-trip through `pull_oc_transcript_for_session`); a genuine cron/proactive delivery arriving after a dispatch's tombstone pass (higher `seq`, never evaluated by that pass) still inserting normally; session-id rotation mid-turn producing a correctly fresh baseline on re-fetch rather than a stale cached one; and the reconnect-budget-exhausted error path still tombstoning its own partial output exactly like the success path. (Relates to #2738, spec: `docs/spec/sessions.md` §30.11.9 added)
- Fixed: Streamed replies no longer lose JSON fence openers (#2729). **Root cause:** `strip_text_tool_blocks` (`src-tauri/src/ai/commands.rs`) had an asymmetric fence state machine — the ` ```json ` opener line was discarded unconditionally the moment a fence was seen, before the block was classified as tool vs non-tool, while the closer ` ``` ` was only discarded once a block was confirmed a tool block. Every non-tool fenced JSON block (e.g. cron-job config the model echoed back) lost its opener but kept its closer, corrupting the saved local row so a later containment check (`.contains()`) against the same content arriving intact from OC failed, causing the segment to insert as a duplicate instead of being tombstoned. Fixed with two changes, both required: (1) the function now buffers each fenced block (opener + body + closer) and defers the emit/discard decision until the block's body has been fully scanned for a `"tool"` key — non-tool blocks emit byte-identical, tool blocks are still fully stripped; an unclosed fence at end of stream is flushed untouched rather than dropped; (2) the call site (`commands.rs`, the text-fallback tool bridge, §4.5.8) now only invokes the stripper when `parse_text_tool_calls` actually found at least one call — previously it ran unconditionally on every zero-native-tool-call response, including replies with no tool calls whatsoever. Also switched the function's final trim from `result.trim()` to `result.trim_end_matches('\n')` to avoid eating leading whitespace that may be semantically part of non-tool content. 5 new regression tests (`fence_strip_tests_2729`) cover: non-tool block byte-identical survival, tool block still-fully-stripped (no regression), a mixed tool/non-tool reply, an end-to-end containment regression using the real 1164-byte `fcfedbbb` segment fixture from the reported incident, and an unclosed-fence-at-end-of-stream edge case. Does not touch the echo-containment path (`is_recent_local_assistant_echo`, `check_stale_echo`) or backfill previously-saved rows with missing openers — that residue is cosmetic and self-healing on new replies. (Relates to #2729, spec: `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §4.5.8a added)
- Mirrored the 150s backstop echo check's (`is_recent_local_assistant_echo`) missing length floor with Rule 2's (`check_stale_echo`) existing `CONTENT_LENGTH_FLOOR: usize = 20` guard (#2730). **Root cause:** the backstop only ever guarded against empty incoming content, with no minimum length — a short first-sight message (e.g. a 4-character cron delivery like "Blue") could be false-suppressed/tombstoned purely because it happened to be a substring of an unrelated recent local assistant row (e.g. "...Blue..." inside a longer unrelated reply), the exact class of false-positive Rule 2's length floor already guards against on its own path. The backstop now mirrors the identical 20-character floor and posture: content below the floor skips the containment check entirely and returns `Ok(false)` (fail toward inserting, §5). New regression test replays today's exact failure case — a 4-char "Blue" incoming message that IS a genuine substring of a recent local row within the 150s window — and asserts it now inserts rather than tombstones. Scope is deliberately narrow: `check_stale_echo` (Rule 2) and the backstop's substring-matching semantics are both untouched. (Relates to #2730, spec-covered-by: #2708)
- Echo suppression dead band — assistant segments aged 150s–15min are now correctly classified by the anchored containment check (#2725). **Root cause (Reed's scope audit, `docs/audits/2026-08-26-echo-dead-band-scope.md`):** `check_stale_echo`'s Step A age gate (`if age_secs < STALE_THRESHOLD_SECS { return Ok(None); }`, 15min) short-circuited the ±5min anchored containment check for any first-sight message younger than 15 minutes — but the 150s backstop (`is_recent_local_assistant_echo`) only compares against a local assistant row written within the last 150s. A first-sight message aged strictly between 150s and 15min satisfied neither gate's entry condition, so it reached neither check's actual comparison logic and inserted as a genuine new message even when it was a verbatim re-ingest of an already-saved local turn. Step A's early-return is removed — the length floor (Step B) and ±5min anchored containment check (Step C) now run on every first-sight message regardless of age, closing the dead band. `STALE_THRESHOLD_SECS` (900s) is retained, now used only to label a tombstone's catch-class (`dead_band` for age < 900s, `resurrection` for age >= 900s) in the tombstone-write log line and reused in two new regression test assertions — no behavior depends on it anymore. The 150s backstop is kept exactly as-is (belt-and-suspenders, per the audit's (a) subsumption analysis: the anchor check is a practical but not a strict mathematical superset of the backstop, so both stay). Two new tests: a dead-band echo fixture (a ~180s-old first-sight message matching a local row within ±5min, now correctly tombstoned as `stale_echo` — today's production leak as a regression test) and a "moving reference" fixture (the anchor check finds the correct matching local row even when it isn't the thread's most-recent assistant row, unlike the backstop's single-row `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1`), plus end-to-end pipeline variants of both. All existing tombstoning/echo-suppression tests pass unchanged. (Relates to #2725, spec-skip: bug fix closing classification gap in existing echo suppression machinery, no behavioral change to spec)
- [2604-PROBE] console markers gated behind debug flag, no longer pollute production output (#2682). The `[2604-PROBE]` diagnostic markers added by #2604's agent-name-fallback-race fix (`ChatPanel.svelte`'s first-token probe, `SessionDropdownHeader.svelte`'s `agentsLoaded`-resolved and suppressed-null-emission probes, `ChatSidebar.svelte`'s Home-surface mirror probe) shipped as unconditional `console.log` calls, polluting production console output on every session's first stream token and every session-header mount. All four call sites are now gated behind the existing `pane-debug` localStorage flag (the same runtime debug flag already used by `ChatSidebar.svelte`, `Editor.svelte`, `KanbanBoard.svelte`, `NoteList.svelte`, `Sidebar.svelte`, `CanvasRenderer.svelte`, `NotesBrowser.svelte`, and `noteService.ts`) — off by default, enabled via `localStorage.pane-debug=1`. No new debug flag mechanism introduced; no behavioral change to the underlying #2604 fallback logic. 5 new frontend tests (`ChatPanel.probeDebugGate.test.ts`, `ChatSidebar.probeDebugGate.test.ts`) drive the real load-order race that fires all four probe call sites and assert markers are absent by default and present only with the flag enabled. (Relates to #2682, spec-skip: debug/observability cleanup, no behavioral change to spec)
- Security hardening for the v1.0.28 production promotion (#2717): migration backup recovery now enforces the centralized `PaneFs` boundary and rejects symlinked/external candidates; OpenClaw pairing is HTTPS-only, redirect-free, response-bounded, and pinned to the user-reviewed origin with explicit two-way workspace-sync disclosure; v82 credential splitting now retries transient keychain failures and never deletes a legacy credential without exact destination confirmation.
- OC-ingested messages now render in true send order instead of poll-tick insertion order (#2690, §30.11)
- Compaction cutoff keys off rowid instead of created_at, preventing silent content loss for origination-stamped rows
- Clock-skew floor clamp prevents assistant replies from sorting above their trigger messages
- Fixed: OC transcript polling now sends the derived composite session key instead of the bare UUID, surviving gateway restarts. `pull_oc_transcript_for_session` (`src-tauri/src/ai/commands.rs`) already derived the correct composite key (`oc_session_key = agent:{runtime_ref}:openai-user:pane-{session_id}`, per §30.11.3) but built the poll URL from the bare `session_id` instead — a one-line divergence between the derived value and the value actually sent. After a gateway restart, `session_mappings` is empty, so the gateway's `messages` handler passes the URL path value straight through to OC as `sessionKey`; the bare UUID caused OC to synthesize the wrong key and return zero messages. Fixed by using `oc_session_key` (already in scope) in the URL construction instead of `session_id`. Both happy-path integration tests (`test_oc_pull_happy_path_200_ingests_messages_end_to_end`, `test_pull_oc_transcript_for_session_cmd_happy_path`) updated to assert the mocked gateway route matches the percent-encoded composite key path, locking the contract. (Relates to #2410, spec-skip: one-line URL fix, no behavioral/architectural change)
- Fixed: Gateway `chat.history` call now uses correct `sessionKey` parameter and resolves OC session key correctly, preventing 502 errors on message retrieval. Root cause (two independent bugs): (1) the `messages` handler (`src-gateway/src/routes/sessions.rs`) sent OC's `chat.history` a `"key"` field, but OC's `ChatHistoryParamsSchema` requires `"sessionKey"` and declares `additionalProperties: false`, so the call was rejected outright; (2) the handler also unconditionally included `"before"`/`"since"` fields (serialized as JSON `null` via `serde_json::json!` when absent), neither of which exists in OC's schema at all — a second independent rejection cause. Both are now dropped from the outgoing OC call entirely for this slice; OC has no native since-by-message-id cursor, so callers over-fetch the most recent page and dedup client-side. Separately, `session_mappings` was storing whatever OC returned as `sessionId` at session-creation time (with `key` only as a fallback) — but OC's own session model treats the **key** as the stable identifier and `sessionId` as a field on the resolved entry that can rotate (e.g. OC mints a fresh `sessionId` under the same key on an out-of-turn send that finds no live entry). `create()` now prefers `"key"` over `"sessionId"` when populating `session_mappings`, fixing key resolution for every handler that reads the map (`messages`, `send_message`, `abort`, `delete_session`), not just the one that surfaced the 502. Extended `sessions.rs`'s existing test suite: `test_messages_remaps_pagination_casing` is retained (pagination-field remapping is unrelated and still correct), and new tests (`test_messages_sends_session_key_param_not_key`, `test_messages_uses_stored_key_from_session_mappings`, `test_create_prefers_key_over_session_id`, `test_create_falls_back_to_session_id_when_key_missing`) assert the corrected param shape and key-resolution behavior. (Relates to #2410, spec-skip: Gateway route bug fix — no behavioral change to Pane's core systems, purely fixing param name and key resolution to match OC's documented schema)
- Fixed ADR-0040 workspace migration rejecting all 107/107 files on every startup with "Workspace is not canonically beneath PaneRoot::System" (#2674). Root cause: `migration_workspace_policy()` in `sync_client.rs` ran a redundant, incorrectly-scoped `std::fs::canonicalize(supplied)` on the raw bare-UUID `workspace_path` (canonicalized relative to the process cwd, not `PaneRoot::System`) in addition to the correct `PaneFs::authorize_existing()` check — the redundant check always failed for the bare-UUID shape `ai_agents.workspace_path` actually holds, rejecting every file regardless of the correct check's result. `migration_workspace_policy()` now relies solely on `authorize_existing()`. Compounding bug: `apply_migration_files()` unconditionally stamped `workspace_resolution_migration_complete = "true"` regardless of `err_count`, permanently masking a 100%-failure run. The completion flag is now gated on `err_count == 0` — any error leaves it unset so the migration retries on the next startup. The flag key is renamed to `workspace_resolution_migration_complete_v2` at all 5 call sites, so installs already stamped `true` under the old key by the pre-fix bug get a fresh, unset key and self-heal via automatic retry (no manual DB intervention required), following the same versioned-flag precedent as `sync_master_key_v1`. Added two regression tests: one asserting `migration_workspace_policy` succeeds for a bare-UUID `workspace_path` resolved against a real `.pane/system/<UUID>` directory (deliberately bypassing the `#[cfg(test)]`-only `legacy_test_workspace_policy` shim that masked this exact bug shape in CI), and one asserting the completion flag stays unset when every file in a migration batch is rejected. (Relates to #2674, spec: ADR-0040 supplement added documenting the v2 flag semantics)
- Fixed `WorkshopReview.svelte`'s `<ChatPanel>` mount (first-run onboarding and agent-creation's shared Memory/Soul review chat) never passing the new `agentsLoadedProp` introduced by #2604's race fix (delta audit finding, PR #2681). `agentsLoadedProp` defaults `false` and nothing in `WorkshopReview`'s lifecycle ever set it `true` (it has no `SessionDropdownHeader` mount and no `getAgents()` call of its own), so the speaker label for every onboarding/agent-creation assistant message was permanently stuck on the `.chat-sender--loading` pulsing treatment instead of the correct `'Pane'` literal (the genuine ADR-0059 D5 nothing-to-attribute case — WorkshopReview's messages are locally-synthesized workshop-chat turns with no real backing agent or session binding). `WorkshopReview.svelte` now passes `agentsLoadedProp={true}` explicitly at its `<ChatPanel>` call site, since there is no real agent roster for this surface to ever wait on. Added a regression test asserting the initial assistant message renders `'Pane'` (not `.chat-sender--loading`) for a `WorkshopReview`-shaped `ChatPanel` mount. (Relates to #2604, spec-skip: same display-layer fallback-timing fix as the parent #2604 change, extended to a third call site missed in the original PR — no behavioral/dispatch/schema changes, spec-covered-by: #2675)
- Fixed the speaker label showing the hardcoded "Pane" literal during streaming for the FIRST message sent after opening a chat session, self-correcting only once the stream completed or the agent roster happened to finish loading (#2604). Root cause (confirmed by audit, format-mismatch hypothesis killed): a pure frontend load-order race, not a dispatch/attribution bug — `activeSession` (session store) can resolve on a faster tick than `allAgents` (`getAgents()`, async) finishes its fetch on session-open, so `SessionDropdownHeader`'s bound-agent `$effect` (and `ChatSidebar`'s identical Home-surface mirror) fired a FALSE `null` before the roster had loaded, which `ChatPanel`'s fallback chain (`message.agent_name ?? sessionBoundAgentName ?? 'Pane'`) then rendered as the literal 'Pane' for the first stream token. Both effects now track an `agentsLoaded` boolean (true once `getAgents()` has resolved at least once) and suppress the null emission until then; the flag is surfaced to `ChatPanel` via a new `onAgentsLoadedChange` callback (project surfaces) / `agentsLoadedProp` (Home). `ChatPanel`'s speaker-label render now distinguishes "still loading" (renders the neutral `chat-sender--loading` treatment, reusing the existing thinking-pulse animation) from "genuinely no bound agent" (renders the literal 'Pane', reserved for the true ADR-0059 D5 case). Console timing probes (`[2604-PROBE]`) ship enabled on the null-suppression, `getAgents()` resolution, and first-token render paths for live-repro verification. (Relates to #2604, spec-skip: Display-layer load-order race fix — no behavioral/dispatch/schema changes. Agent name fallback timing only., spec-covered-by: #2675)
- Fixed `Onboarding.svelte`'s `processUpload`/`processQuestions` calling `ensureMainAgent()` and `createWorkshopSession()` as bare awaits with no surrounding try/catch (#2676). A throw from either call was an unhandled promise rejection that left the user stranded on the `'processing'` screen indefinitely — no error message, no Back button, no recovery path, and a silent failure in the console. Both functions now wrap the entire remaining function body (from `ensureMainAgent()` through the existing `screen = 'workshop'` transition) in one outer try/catch, mirroring `AgentCreateOverlay.svelte`'s `handleUploadConfirm`/`handleInterviewFinish` shape. On catch, a new `processingError` state var is set to the error message and `screen` resets to the originating screen (`'upload'` or `'questions'`) so the user can see what went wrong and retry. The error renders inline via the existing `.connect-error-msg` class (already used 9+ other places in this file) on both screens, and is cleared when the user clicks Back. The pre-existing inner try/catch around `streamAndCollect` (which already produces graceful fallback content) is untouched. (Relates to #2676, spec-skip: UX error-handling improvement using established pattern — no new behavioral contract, spec-covered-by #2675)
- Fixed `ai_list_runtime_connections` and `connected_runtime_providers` (used by `fetch_available_models`/`populate_model_registry_from_provider`) holding `db.0.lock()` for their entire duration while looping all four runtime types' OS keychain reads, which could stall `ai_chat_stream` and every other `db.0`-dependent command indefinitely if any single keychain read blocked at the OS level (e.g. a stale code-signature re-triggering an unattended macOS Keychain Access authorization prompt after a rebuild) (D26, #2673 PR-A). Both call sites are split into a DB-only phase (reads the `ai_agents` roster and relevant `ai_settings` keys into an owned snapshot, then drops the lock) and a keychain-only phase (runs entirely without `db.0` held, each keychain read wrapped in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` + `tokio::time::timeout` bounded to 2-5s), mirroring the existing #1347 precedent in `sync/commands.rs:324-333`. A stalled read now degrades to a bounded per-card/per-provider error instead of hanging the whole command or the shared mutex. `ai_list_runtime_connections` is now `async fn`; no frontend change needed (`invoke()` was already Promise-based). Added `CredentialDbSnapshot`/`RuntimeSettingsSnapshot` snapshot structs (`credential_migration.rs`/`runtime_resolution.rs`) so keychain-only helper variants never need a live `&Connection`. (Relates to #2673, spec: `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` new §28.4 added)

### Changed
- Onboarding provider cards (`Onboarding.svelte`, both §6.2 "Connect Your AI" and §6.4.1 "Connect Smart Features" pickers) now render at a fixed 52px height instead of a variable, oversized one (#2792). **Root cause:** the component's single `<style>` block contained two conflicting `.provider-card` rule definitions — the intended `flex-wrap` row layout, and a second, later-in-source-order block (a leftover merge artifact) that silently won the CSS cascade on every provider-card instance in the file, forcing a full-width `flex-direction: column` layout with no height cap. That duplicate block, along with its dead `.provider-card.selected` state selector (no markup in this file ever applies a `selected` class — `class:active` is what every card button uses), is removed; the surviving `.provider-card` rule gains an explicit `height: 52px` plus `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis` on `.provider-name`/`.provider-desc`, so name/descriptor truncate with an ellipsis rather than wrapping and growing the box — the mechanism that keeps every card the same height regardless of text length. **Smart Features descriptors:** the §6.4.1 "Connect Smart Features" cards (OpenRouter/Anthropic/Ollama) previously rendered provider name only, with no `.provider-desc` span at all, unlike §6.2's "Connect Your AI" cards. They now carry the same one-line descriptor text as §6.2 for the same provider (OpenRouter — "Access multiple models"; Anthropic — "Claude direct"; Ollama — "Local models") so the two pickers can't describe a provider two different ways. Venice's §6.2 descriptor ("Your Venice API models") is unchanged — decision D5 (no privacy/uncensored copy) is untouched, and Venice is not offered on the §6.4.1 Smart Features picker. 13 new frontend tests (`Onboarding.cardHeight.test.ts`) assert against the real component source: exactly one `.provider-card` rule definition exists (RED-ON-REVERT on reintroducing the duplicate block), the dead `.provider-card.selected` selector stays removed, `.provider-name`/`.provider-desc` both declare ellipsis truncation, a short-text and long-text card compute the identical 52px height in jsdom (RED-ON-REVERT on removing the `height` declaration), every Smart Features provider button renders the matching `.provider-desc` text, and the two pickers' descriptor text for OpenRouter/Anthropic/Ollama stays in sync. All 18 pre-existing `Onboarding.test.ts`/`Onboarding.processingError.test.ts`/`Onboarding.synthesisOrdering.test.ts`/`Onboarding.workshopSession.test.ts` tests pass unchanged; `npm run check` reports 403 warnings (one fewer than main's 404 — the removed dead-selector warning), zero new errors. (Relates to #2792, spec: `docs/spec/onboarding.md` §6.2 and §6.4.1 updated, new "Provider card fixed height + Smart Features descriptors (#2792)" section added, spec-covered-by: this PR's own spec diff)
- Provider cards (Anthropic, OpenRouter, Ollama, OpenClaw) and the Smart Features status dot now use a three-state grey/green/red color system, replacing the old binary connected/disconnected treatment (#2641). Grey means the provider was never configured *this install* — fixing #2631, where a credential left behind in the OS keychain by a previous install painted a card green before the user had ever touched that provider. **Backend:** `ai_configure_and_save` writes a new `{runtime}_configured_at` timestamp to `ai_settings` (`anthropic_configured_at`, `openrouter_configured_at`, `ollama_configured_at`) immediately after a successful credential/endpoint save; `ai_disconnect_runtime_impl` clears it on disconnect. `ai_list_runtime_connections` returns a new `configured_this_install: bool` field on `RuntimeConnectionInfo`, computed from that key (OpenClaw reuses the existing `gateway_paired_at` marker rather than a new key). No live reachability probe is added — `connected` stays a presence check; red only fires from an `info.error` populated by an explicit Test/Save/dispatch failure. **Frontend:** `ProviderConnectionCard.svelte`'s binary `unconfigured` check is replaced by a single derived `cardStatus: 'unconfigured' | 'active' | 'failed'`, driven by `configured_this_install` for the three key/endpoint runtimes. OpenClaw is the one exception to that generic formula — its color derives from `hasOcAgentRows` (already fetched for the Pair/Re-pair button label), not `ocUnpaired` (which conflates "never paired" with "disconnected but was paired"): a user-initiated OC disconnect (paired, not connected, no error) now renders grey "Paired, disconnected", never red — red is reserved for `hasOcAgentRows === true && info.error`, a genuine failure. The red attention border (`.pcc-card--attn`) now keys off `cardStatus === 'failed'` only. Smart Features gains a matching three-state status dot next to its section title (`internal_configured_at`, same write/clear pattern, tracked via a new `internalConfiguredAt` state var in `Settings.svelte`) and the pre-existing on-load auto-success (which set `internalConnectionStatus = 'success'` whenever a saved key/endpoint existed, independent of whether it was actually tested this install — the same #2631 shape) is removed; fresh loads now stay `not-tested` until an explicit Test/Save, matching the pre-existing Ollama-only invariant in `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §28.1. (Relates to #2641, #2631, spec: `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §28.3 added)
- Architecture reversal: the New Provider modal now owns the full OC pairing ceremony end-to-end (#2642, #2630). The ProviderConnectionCard becomes manage-only (disconnect, test connection, sync, status display). Card's Pair/Re-pair button opens the modal via a `startCeremony` prop-based deep link, replacing the prior `driveOcCard()` DOM-hack in `ProviderConnectionsPanel`. The modal uses `runOcPairingExchange` + `runOcImportPhase` separately (retry-on-import-failure without consuming a fresh pairing code), `confirmCollision` is always shown on re-pair (D20 unconditional), and `lastImportError` is threaded back via `onConnectionSaved` for the card's badge. Card label now driven by `oc_agent_row_exists` instead of `info.agents.length`/`info.connected`, fixing the post-disconnect regression where soft-deactivated rows made the button incorrectly show "Pair" instead of "Re-pair". (Relates to #2642, #2630)

### Fixed
- Fixed create-agent/onboarding synthesis (`streamAndCollect`, `src/lib/onboarding/seedGeneration.ts`) dispatching through the WRONG agent's runtime, confirmed via live logs (e.g. an existing OpenClaw-runtime agent's synthesis call was observed dispatching through a stale "Brit Freed" OpenClaw session instead of the newly created Anthropic-runtime agent it was meant to seed) (D26/PR-B, #2673). Root cause: `streamAndCollect` took only a `prompt: string` with no session identity, so `ai_chat_stream`'s dispatch fell back to whichever session happened to be active in that project scope (`context.projectId` fallback resolution) rather than the just-created agent — the exact hazard `WorkshopReview.svelte`'s later review-chat step had already been fixed for (#2618) but the earlier synthesis step never was. `streamAndCollect` now takes a **required** `sessionId: string` second argument, threaded into `ai_chat_stream` as a top-level `sessionId` field (matching `WorkshopReview.svelte`'s existing pattern) — not nested in `context`. Both callers (`AgentCreateOverlay.svelte`'s `handleUploadConfirm`/`handleInterviewFinish`, and `Onboarding.svelte`'s `processUpload`/`processQuestions`) now call `createWorkshopSession(agent.id)` **before** `streamAndCollect(...)`, reusing the one resulting session for both synthesis and the subsequent review chat, instead of creating it afterward as a separate step. Rider: `context.currentView` literal renamed `'onboarding'` → `'agent-seeding'` at both call sites — confirmed cosmetic (display/logging-only; never a backend branch gate) via `is_workshop_session`'s actual gating logic (`noteId`/`projectId`, not `currentView`). (Relates to #2673, spec: `docs/spec/sessions.md` new §30.7.1a added, `docs/spec/onboarding.md` "Agent-before-synthesis ordering invariant (#2634, D10)" amended, `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §29.1 row 1 annotated)
- Fixed the Settings default agent block (and Agents tab) not refreshing after an OC disconnect promoted a new default agent backend-side (D25, #2649). The Agents tab refresh fixed in D24 covered only the OC-import path (`handleConnectionSaved` → `onAgentsChanged`); disconnect (and any other card-level mutation) goes through a separate path — the `onChange` prop passed to every `ProviderConnectionCard` — which was still wired straight to `loadConnections` and never called `onAgentsChanged`, so Settings' `agentsLoaded` flag stayed `true` and neither the Agents tab nor the default agent display re-fetched. `ProviderConnectionsPanel.svelte` gains a `handleCardChange` wrapper (`await loadConnections(); onAgentsChanged?.();`) now passed as every card's `onChange`, replacing the bare `loadConnections` reference. (Relates to #2649, spec: `docs/spec/agents.md` data loading discipline paragraph updated with the `onChange`/card-mutation note)
- Fixed Home chat header showing "Pane" during streaming instead of the bound agent's name (#2643). **Follow-up (D22/#2643 session-resolution fix):** the original D22/#2643 fixes computed the Home lock banner and bound-agent name off `$sessionStore.activeSession`, which is `undefined` on a real Home launch when `ChatSidebar.svelte`'s Home `$effect` first fires — nothing on Home writes to `sessionStore` (`SessionsDrawer.svelte` keeps its own local session list; only the project-surface-only `SessionDropdownHeader` calls `sessionStore.loadSessions`). The thread only resolves after mount, via the NAV event (`pane-navigation-complete`, `navigation.ts`) setting `$activeChatThreadId` — the effect wasn't subscribed to that resolution, so on real Home it never re-ran and both the lock banner and the bound-agent name silently stayed unset. The Home effect is now keyed off `$activeChatThreadId` instead of `$sessionStore.activeSession`, and resolves the session via `sessionStore.getActiveSession('workspace')` (the same `'workspace'` surface constant `loadOrCreateThread`/`navigateTo` already use for Home), with a staleness guard against rapid re-navigation. This also fixes `isFreshSession` and `resolveGreetingAgentName`'s bound-agent lookup elsewhere in `ChatSidebar.svelte`, which read the same `$sessionStore.activeSession` and shared the identical undefined-on-Home root cause. Both `ChatSidebar.homeLockBanner.test.ts` and `ChatSidebar.homeAgentName.test.ts` are updated to start with an empty session store and set `$activeChatThreadId` post-mount, matching real Home instead of the previously pre-populated fixture that masked this gap. (Relates to #2643, spec: `docs/spec/sessions.md` §30.1.3 Home-surface resolution note updated with the thread-id-based lookup)
- Fixed the Agents tab in Settings not refreshing after OC pairing imports new agents — the newly-imported roster only appeared after navigating away from and back to the tab (D24, #2649). Root cause: `handleConnectionSaved` (`ProviderConnectionsPanel.svelte`) called `loadConnections()` (refreshes provider cards only) but never signaled `Settings.svelte` to re-fetch its own `agentsList`; `loadAgents()` is gated on `agentsLoaded === false`, which is set `true` on first load and never reset. `ProviderConnectionsPanel` gains an `onAgentsChanged?: () => void` callback prop, called from `handleConnectionSaved` right after `loadConnections()` resolves; `Settings.svelte` passes `onAgentsChanged={() => { agentsLoaded = false; }}`, which the existing Agents-tab `$effect` picks up and re-fetches from. (Relates to #2649, spec-skip: reactivity bug fix — Agents tab not re-fetching after OC import, no behavioral change, no spec surface)
- Fixed the lock banner (`ReadOnlySessionNotice`) never rendering on the Home surface when the active session's bound agent was deactivated (D22, #2649). The backend's dispatch guard (`agents::check_bound_agent_active`) correctly refused to dispatch, but on Home the composer stayed fully enabled and no lock notice ever appeared, because `SessionDropdownHeader` — the only component that computed the read-only/lock state — never mounts on Home (`showHeader` is gated on `$activeProject !== null`, which is always `false` there). Per Matt's ruling, the header/dropdown bar itself is NOT added to Home (the clean look stays); instead, the read-only/lock computation (bound-agent lookup + `is_active`/runtime-connectivity check) is extracted from `SessionDropdownHeader.svelte` into a new shared helper, `src/lib/services/sessionReadOnlyCheck.ts` — both `SessionDropdownHeader` (project-scoped surfaces) and `ChatSidebar` (Home) now call the same function, so the two surfaces can never disagree on whether a session is locked. `ChatSidebar` calls the helper directly on Home and passes the result into `ChatPanel` via a new `readOnlyState` prop (used only when `showHeader` is `false`; `SessionDropdownHeader`'s own `onReadOnlyChange` callback remains the source of truth when the header is mounted) — `ReadOnlySessionNotice` renders and the composer disables on Home exactly like any project-scoped locked session. Also fixed `handleSendMessage`'s catch block (`ChatSidebar.svelte`), which previously classified the backend's deactivation error message as a generic failure (`⚠ Something went wrong: <raw error>`) because the `isGateway` regex only matches network-ish terms; it now recognizes the deactivation message shape (checked before the gateway check, since the guard's own copy — "reconnect the agent's provider" — would otherwise false-match the gateway regex's "connect" term) and surfaces the backend's own clear lock message instead. Also removed a hand-rolled duplicate of `check_bound_agent_active` inline in `ai_chat_stream` (`commands.rs`, its own SQL/error string) — it now calls the canonical `agents::check_bound_agent_active` (`agents.rs:366-403`) directly, so there is exactly one place that decides what "bound agent is inactive" means and one error message for it. (Relates to #2649, spec: `docs/spec/sessions.md` §30.1.3 updated with the lock-banner-renders-on-every-surface note)
- Fixed OpenClaw disconnect (D21, #2649) NULLing `chat_sessions.agent_id` for every session bound to a deactivated OC agent (via `null_out_chat_sessions_for_deactivating_runtime`, `ai_disconnect_runtime_impl`'s `openclaw` arm), which routed the next dispatch attempt through the NULL self-heal path (`resolve_and_selfheal_session_agent`) — silently rebinding the session to whatever agent was currently `is_default = 1`, not the agent the user actually selected. Per `docs/spec/sessions.md`'s "Unavailable bound agent" rule (ADR-0062 D5), a session bound to a deactivated agent must render read-only and error explicitly naming the agent — never silently re-bind. Disconnect now leaves `chat_sessions.agent_id` completely untouched; `null_out_chat_sessions_for_deactivating_runtime` is deleted entirely (its one call site was the disconnect path itself). A new guard, `agents::check_bound_agent_active`, runs in the dispatch path (`resolve_runtime_config_for_session`, `runtime_resolution.rs`) BEFORE self-heal gets a chance to run: it checks the session's *existing* non-NULL `agent_id` against the bound agent's `is_active` flag and errors with an explicit lock message naming the agent (`"Session is bound to agent '{name}' which is currently inactive. Start a new session or reconnect the agent's provider."`) when the bound agent is deactivated. NULL `agent_id` rows (legacy migration backfill) are unaffected — the guard is a no-op for them and self-heal proceeds exactly as before. The existing lock banner (`ReadOnlySessionNotice.svelte`, `SessionDropdownHeader.svelte`) needed no changes — it was already correctly built and checks `is_active`, but was dormant because disconnect raced ahead of it by NULLing the binding before the banner ever saw a non-NULL, `is_active=0` row. **Intentional behavior reversal:** the existing test `test_disconnect_nulls_chat_sessions_bound_to_openclaw_agents` is rewritten as `test_disconnect_preserves_chat_session_agent_bindings`, now asserting `agent_id` is unchanged after disconnect (previously asserted it was NULLed) — this is a deliberate spec-driven reversal of PR2's (#2647/#2648) prior behavior, not a stale-test cleanup. (Relates to #2649, spec: `docs/spec/sessions.md` §30.1.3 updated with the disconnect-preserves-binding note)
- Fixed OpenClaw re-pair (D20, #2649) never actually reimporting agents: both re-pair callers (`Onboarding.svelte`'s `runOcSync`, `ProviderConnectionCard.svelte`'s `completePairing`) passed native `confirm()` as the shared ceremony module's `confirmCollision` callback, and `confirm()` does not render in Tauri's WebView — it resolves synchronously to `false`, so every re-pair with a detected collision silently declined without any dialog ever appearing, and `reimport_oc_agents` never ran. The shared module (`src/lib/services/ocPairingCeremony.ts`) reported that decline as `{ ok: true }`, structurally indistinguishable from a genuine 0-agent success. Three coordinated fixes: (1) `runOcImportPhase`'s `check.collisions.length >= 1` gate is removed — `confirmCollision` is now called unconditionally on every re-pair, including with an empty collisions array; (2) `ImportPhaseOutcome` (and `PairingCeremonyOutcome`) gained an explicit `declined?: boolean` discriminant, set `true` only when the user explicitly declines — structurally distinct from a successful reimport, even one with zero imported agents; (3) both callers replace their native `confirm()` with a `ConfirmDialog.svelte` instance, Promise-wrapped following the existing OC-disconnect-confirmation pattern already in `ProviderConnectionCard.svelte` (`showDisconnectConfirm`/`confirmOpenClawDisconnect`/`cancelOpenClawDisconnect`). A declined re-pair now renders a dismissable, non-error notice ("Re-pair cancelled, nothing changed") in both callers, deliberately styled apart from the existing `pairSyncError`/`ocSyncError` error banners — declining is a user choice, not a failure. Updated `ocPairingCeremony.test.ts`: the zero-collision test now asserts `confirmCollision` **was** called with `[]` (previously asserted `not.toHaveBeenCalled`), and a new/updated decline test asserts `outcome.declined === true` with `reimport_oc_agents` never called. Also updated `ProviderConnectionCard.test.ts`'s D18 re-pair-routing suite to interact with the rendered `ConfirmDialog` instead of spying on `window.confirm`. No changes to `sync_initial_import`/`sync_re_import` Rust commands or the shared module's pairing phase (phase 1). (Relates to #2649, spec: `docs/spec/sync.md` re-pair section updated with the unconditional-prompt / `declined` discriminant contract)

### Removed
- Removed same-machine OpenClaw topology support entirely. OpenClaw is confirmed split-machine only — same-machine was never an allowed topology and is a security risk (running OC on the same machine as Pane violates the isolation boundary that makes split-machine deployments secure), and no live install ever carried `same_machine` state. Deleted `src/lib/components/AgentDiscovery.svelte` and its usages in `Onboarding.svelte` (`proceedFromOpenClawDetect()`, the `openclaw-detect` and `oc-agent-discovery` screens, and their `Screen` type entries). Removed the `SameMachine` variant from `sync_client.rs`'s `SyncTopology` enum; the `"same_machine"` string value read from `ai_settings` still maps to `SplitMachine` (with a log warning) for backward compatibility with any pre-existing DB value. Removed the now-dead `is_same_machine`-gated startup-reconciliation call in `watcher.rs`. Cleaned up related same-machine comments in `notes.rs` and `ai/commands.rs`. Added a regression test (`agents.rs`) proving `upsert_agent` provides no `runtime_type='openclaw'` guard of its own and documenting that the real protection is structural: no live caller reaches it with `runtime_type='openclaw'` post-deletion — OC agent rows are created exclusively via `sync_initial_import`/`sync_re_import`, which set `runtime_ref` directly and never pass through `upsert_agent`. (Relates to #2649, spec: `docs/spec/sync.md` §22C.11 and §22C.1-§22C.3 updated with removal notice; `docs/spec/onboarding.md` §6.5.3 updated with split-machine-only note)

### Fixed
- Fixed onboarding's OpenClaw pairing flow (`Onboarding.svelte`'s `exchangePairingCode()` + `runOcSync()`) lacking the first-pair/re-pair routing, `gateway_paired_at` write, and structured error handling that the Settings inline pairing flow (`ProviderConnectionCard.svelte`'s `completePairing()`) already had since #2647/#2648 — the two ceremonies had drifted after being implemented independently. Extracted a shared module, `src/lib/services/ocPairingCeremony.ts`, exporting `runOcPairingExchange` (pairing-code exchange + TLS/topology settings + `ai_configure_and_save` + `gateway_paired_at`, steps 1-6 per `docs/spec/sync.md` §22C.22.4), `runOcImportPhase` (the `oc_agent_row_exists` first-pair/re-pair branch: `sync_initial_import` vs. `check_oc_agent_collisions` → caller-supplied `confirmCollision` → `reimport_oc_agents`), a convenience `runOcPairingCeremony` wrapper composing both phases (used by Settings, which has no retry-only-sync UX to preserve), and a shared `parseGatewayError`. Both callers now share one implementation instead of two independently-drifting ones. Onboarding-specific fixes as a result: it now does the same `oc_agent_row_exists` re-pair routing Settings already had (previously always called `sync_initial_import`, which would have minted a duplicate agent on any re-onboard after a disconnect); it now writes `gateway_paired_at` (previously never written from this path); the redundant second `ai_configure_and_save` call and the redundant `fetchOcModels()` call that `runOcSync()` made after the initial sync are removed (the shared ceremony already did this work in phase 1); and the dead `set_ai_setting('provider_state', 'configured_verified')` write is deleted (zero readers found codebase-wide). `ensureMainAgent` and the same-machine onboarding paths (`proceedFromOpenClawDetect`, `openclaw-detect`/`oc-agent-discovery` screens, `AgentDiscovery.svelte`) are untouched — out of scope. Added two Rust round-trip tests in `sync_client.rs` exercising a real `ai_disconnect_runtime_impl("openclaw", ...)` followed by a real `sync_re_import` against a mocked gateway: the agent's UUID and `workspace_path` are identical before/after, `is_active` is restored to `1`, and the `model` column (deliberately absent from re-import's overwrite-in-place `UPDATE ... SET` list) survives untouched — plus a second variant with a foreign default agent present, confirming the OC agent reactivates without stealing `is_default` back (the #2644 invariant, now proven through a real disconnect+re-pair sequence rather than only a hand-seeded collision state). (Relates to #2649, #2647, #2648, spec: `docs/spec/onboarding.md` §6.6.3 and `docs/spec/sync.md` §22C.22/§22C.22.5 status markers updated)
- Fixed OpenClaw disconnect only clearing 3 of the 7 OC-related `ai_settings` keys and never deactivating the OC agent rows themselves, leaving stale `ai_agents` entries (`is_active = 1`, `is_default` sometimes still `1`) fully visible to every picker/roster surface after a "disconnect" the user reasonably expected to actually disconnect. `ai_disconnect_runtime_impl`'s `"openclaw"` arm is rewritten as one transaction (keychain deletion stays outside it, being an OS call): all 7 settings keys (`endpoint`, `gateway_tls_fingerprint`, `gateway_tls_cert_pem`, `gateway_paired_at`, `tier3_topology`, `last_sync_push`, `api_key` — previously only 3 were cleared) are set-emptied via the existing `set_ai_setting` idiom (not `DELETE`, matching the rest of the settings-clearing convention in this function); every `runtime_type = 'openclaw'` row gets `is_active = 0, is_default = 0` in a single UPDATE (unconditional demote, regardless of prior default status); `chat_sessions.agent_id` bound to a deactivated OC agent is NULLed via a new sanctioned helper (`agents::null_out_chat_sessions_for_deactivating_runtime`, keeping the ADR-0062 D1 single-write-path gate intact) so every subsequent reader routes through the proven NULL self-heal path instead of resolving a dangling reference; and, if another active non-sub agent exists, one is promoted to `is_default = 1` (`ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1`, same-transaction ordering after the demote so the partial unique index never sees two `1`s at once) — if none exists, no default is set, which every downstream consumer already handles correctly. This is a soft-deactivate ("unpair"), never a `DELETE` — agent directories and files on disk are untouched, and re-pairing reactivates the same rows rather than creating new ones. Two supporting reactivation fixes close the loop: `sync_re_import`'s overwrite-in-place UPDATE and `sync_initial_import`'s `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` both now include `is_active = 1` in their SET clause, so a re-pair after disconnect actually reactivates the existing (same-UUID, same-directory) rows instead of leaving them permanently `is_active = 0` and invisible to every picker forever. The native browser `confirm()` for OC disconnect (`ProviderConnectionCard.svelte`) is replaced with the shared `ConfirmDialog.svelte` component, naming the exact number of agents that will become unavailable and stating plainly that their files stay on the machine. (Relates to #2647, #2648, spec: `docs/spec/sync.md` updated with the disconnect-is-unpair / demote-then-promote / reactivation invariants)
- Fixed OpenClaw pairing leaving the `main` agent's `model` column NULL after a first pair via Settings (D17), and re-pairing an already-paired OC gateway minting a duplicate UUID agent directory instead of updating the existing one (D18), plus a related default-status-stealing bug newly reachable once re-pair is wired up (#2644). Three coordinated fixes, unified in one PR: (1) `sync_initial_import`'s INSERT now includes a `model` column, resolved via `fetch_oc_agent_model` for the `oc_id == "main"` agent BEFORE the DB transaction begins (subagents have no gateway-side model concept exposed by `/v1/agents`, so they never get one); the `ON CONFLICT(runtime_type, runtime_ref)` clause self-heals a NULL model from a prior pre-fix import (`model = CASE WHEN ai_agents.model IS NULL THEN excluded.model ELSE ai_agents.model END`) while never clobbering a real, already-set model. If the gateway is briefly unreachable for `/v1/agents` specifically (even though `/v1/sync/initial` just succeeded), the import still completes with `model = NULL` for the affected agent rather than aborting — a genuinely actionable warning (not a log-only soft-fail) is now surfaced in `ImportedAgentsModal.svelte`, naming the affected agent(s) and pointing to Settings → AI. `ai_configure_and_save`'s `openclaw` branch no longer writes `ai_agents.model` directly (that UPDATE ran before the row existed and could never have worked) — it still calls `fetch_oc_agent_model` unconditionally as connectivity validation (#1446), just no longer uses the result for a DB write. (2) `completePairing()` (`ProviderConnectionCard.svelte`) now calls the new `oc_agent_row_exists` command (a DB-only existence check on `runtime_type='openclaw'` rows — deliberately not `info.connected`, which requires a live keychain token and would misroute a paired-but-token-revoked install back onto the first-pair path) to branch: no existing rows → `sync_initial_import` as before; existing rows → `check_oc_agent_collisions` + (on any collision) a confirm-gated warning, then `reimport_oc_agents` (delegates to the already-implemented-but-previously-UI-unreachable `sync_re_import`, which overwrites agent rows/files in place instead of minting a new UUID directory). `completePairing()` also now writes `tier3_topology='split_machine'`, matching `Onboarding.svelte` — Settings-paired installs previously never got this topology marker, silently skipping the ADR-0040 one-shot workspace-migration gate. (3) `sync_re_import`'s two demotion blocks (overwrite-in-place and fresh-import) now gate the DB `is_default`/role write on a new `land_as_default` flag — ported from D13's `default_agent_exists` pre-flight pattern — instead of the bare `oc_id == "main"` check: re-importing the OC main agent no longer steals default status from an existing foreign default agent (e.g. an OpenRouter-onboarded default). This gate ships in the same PR as (2) specifically because wiring re-pair to `sync_re_import` is what makes that function UI-reachable for the first time — shipping (2) without (3) would have been a new regression. (Relates to #2647, #2648, #2644, spec-skip: sync_initial_import model column addition + re-pair routing + default gate — scoped by Reed E2E audit, no spec section exists for OC pairing internals)
- Fixed `sync_initial_import` rolling back an entire OpenClaw agent import batch whenever a default agent already existed (e.g. an OpenRouter-onboarded default agent created during onboarding, before OC was ever paired). The imported OC main agent's INSERT unconditionally set `is_default = 1` when `oc_id == "main"`, colliding with `idx_ai_agents_default` (a partial UNIQUE index the INSERT's `ON CONFLICT(runtime_type, runtime_ref)` clause does not name) and rolling back all N agents in the batch — the exact `UNIQUE constraint failed: ai_agents.is_default` error from the bug report. Added a pre-flight `default_agent_exists` check inside the same transaction as the per-agent INSERT loop; `is_default` is now gated on `runtime_type == 'openclaw' && oc_id == "main" && !default_agent_exists`. When a default already exists, the imported OC main agent now lands as non-default with `role = 'local'` (not `'sub'` — keeps it pickable in the agent picker per `DefaultAgentPickerModal.svelte`'s `role !== 'sub'` filter); the pre-existing default agent is never touched. This is a one-directional check, not a demote-then-promote — `sync_re_import`'s demote-then-promote pattern (a separate, pre-existing behavior for the explicit provider-switch re-import path) is out of scope here and is tracked separately as #2644. Also ported `sync_re_import`'s `claimed_slugs` collision-avoidance pattern into `sync_initial_import` to close the same root-cause class on the `slug` UNIQUE constraint (suffix-increment on collision, e.g. `assistant` → `assistant-1`), and added success-path logging to the rollback cleanup loop (previously only failures were logged). Also added a collapsed-card-header error indicator to `ProviderConnectionCard.svelte`, driven off `pairSyncError`, so a failed post-pair agent import is visible without expanding the card. (D13, Relates to #2640, spec: `docs/spec/sync.md` updated with the is_default collision-avoidance invariant)
- Fixed onboarding's upload and questions paths (`processUpload`/`processQuestions`, `Onboarding.svelte`) invoking synthesis (`streamAndCollect()` → `ai_chat_stream`) BEFORE the main agent existed, on every fresh install. `ai_chat_stream`'s session→agent resolution (`resolve_and_selfheal_session_agent`, `agents.rs`) hard-fails with `Err("No agent is set up yet...")` when zero `ai_agents` rows exist — exactly the state before `ensureMainAgent()`/`upsert_agent` runs. `processUpload`'s catch block logged the real error to console but showed the user a fabricated "Processing took too long" message regardless of cause; `processQuestions`'s catch block didn't even log it, silently substituting raw form-field text with no synthesis and no visible failure. Fixed by moving `ensureMainAgent()` above the synthesis call in both functions, mirroring the already-correct `AgentCreateOverlay.svelte` pattern (agent created first, synthesis second). `processUpload`'s fallback message now surfaces the real error (`Synthesis failed: <message>`); `processQuestions`'s catch block now logs to console. Verified the reorder introduces no duplicate-agent risk: the later agent-rename step calls `update_agent` on the existing row (never a second `upsert_agent`), and `createWorkshopSession(agent.id)` still binds to the exact id `ensureMainAgent()` returned — no id drift. (Relates to #2634, spec: `docs/spec/onboarding.md` updated with the agent-before-synthesis ordering invariant)
- Fixed OpenClaw gateway pairing done via Settings/"New Provider" (`ProviderConnectionCard.svelte`'s `completePairing()`) never being detected by the sync client, even though pairing itself reported success and correctly stored the endpoint, token, and TLS cert. Root cause: `ai_configure_and_save`'s `openclaw` branch only UPDATEs an existing `ai_agents` row keyed on `runtime_type='openclaw' AND runtime_ref='main'` - it never INSERTs one - and the only code path that INSERTs that row (`sync_initial_import`) was called exclusively from the onboarding wizard, never from this pairing ceremony. `sync_client::has_active_openclaw_agent()` (and therefore `get_gateway_url()`) gate on that row's existence, so a Settings-paired gateway silently never engaged sync. `completePairing()` now calls `sync_initial_import` after `ai_configure_and_save` succeeds, mirroring what `Onboarding.svelte` already does; a `sync_initial_import` failure surfaces as a distinct, non-blocking warning (pairing itself is unaffected, since the token/endpoint/cert are already durably stored by that point) rather than reopening the pairing-code step, with "Sync now" as the retry path. Added `ImportedAgentsModal.svelte`, a lightweight popup shown when agents are imported this way, so the user sees which agents came in - mirroring (but not duplicating) onboarding's own agent-import review step. Also corrected a misleading `detect_topology` log line that claimed "no endpoint configured" when the function only ever checks `ai_settings.tier3_topology`. Teaching `ai_configure_and_save` to INSERT rows itself remains explicitly out of scope for this fix. (D11, Relates to #2635, spec: `docs/spec/sync.md` §22C.11A.5 updated with the new invariant note)
