- Fixed onboarding creating the main agent with the wrong `runtime_type` and no `model` — a fresh install with both Anthropic and OpenRouter keychain entries present (e.g. a customer who tried one provider, backed out, then connected the other) would have `ensureMainAgent`'s `upsert_agent` call silently defer to ambient keychain inference (`resolve_runtime_type_for_new_local_agent`, which tie-breaks to `openrouter` when both keys exist) instead of the provider the customer actually just connected and validated (`connectProvider`), while the chosen model was written only to the retired `ai_settings.model` scalar (dead since #2585/D8 — dispatch reads `ai_agents.model` only) and never landed on the new agent row at all. `CreateAgentRequest` gained a new `runtime_type: Option<String>` field; `upsert_agent`'s INSERT branch now honors an explicit, validated `Some(value)` directly (skipping ambient inference entirely) and falls back to the original inference behavior only when `None`, preserving every other existing caller unchanged. `ensureMainAgent` (`Onboarding.svelte`) now passes `runtime_type: connectProvider` and `model: connectModel`/`selectedComplexModel` directly on the `upsert_agent` request, and the now-dead `set_ai_setting('model', ...)` call in `proceedFromModelSelect` is removed. (Relates to #2629, spec: `docs/spec/agents.md` updated with the fix note)
- Fixed onboarding's "Choose Your Model" step (`Onboarding.svelte`) blocking every non-OpenClaw provider on a fresh install with "No primary provider configured" — a chicken-and-egg bug: `fetchPrimaryModels()` called `fetch_primary_provider_models`, which derived the connected provider from `ai_agents` rows (`derive_active_provider_label`), but model selection happens *before* the first agent is created, so a fresh install has zero `ai_agents` rows and the call always errored (Retry re-ran the same broken call; Back was the only exit). `fetchPrimaryModels()` now calls `fetch_available_models` (credential-based, agent-independent — same command `AgentCreateOverlay.svelte`'s `loadModelsForRuntime()` already uses) and filters the merged, provider-namespaced response down to `connectProvider` client-side, mirroring that component's pattern exactly. Added a distinct empty-after-filter message so a real per-provider fetch failure doesn't look identical to a generic error — and split that message itself into two cases: `fetch_available_models` (commands.rs) only returns `Err` when *every* connected runtime's fetch fails, so if `connectProvider`'s own fetch failed silently while another connected runtime succeeded, the merged response resolves `Ok` with `connectProvider` simply absent from it, which previously looked identical to "connected but genuinely has zero models" (e.g. a real-but-empty Ollama instance). Checking whether `connectProvider` appears in the *unfiltered* merged list can't actually distinguish these — that predicate is the exact filter that just produced the empty result, so it's always false at this point (a tautology, not a real signal). `fetchPrimaryModels()` instead re-probes `connectProvider` itself via the same live commands `testConnection()`/`probeOllama()` already ran moments earlier with the same credentials (`validate_anthropic_key`/`validate_openrouter_key`/`ollama_probe_two_step`, new `probeConnectProviderReachable()` helper): reachable-now renders `No models available for <Provider>.`; unreachable renders `Could not reach <Provider>. Check your connection and try again.` `fetch_primary_provider_models`/`fetch_primary_provider_models_impl` (and their `lib.rs` registration and unit test) were dead code once this call site was fixed — removed in the same PR. `derive_active_provider_label` itself is untouched — it remains correct for its other callers (settings/status surfaces where an agent already exists). Relates to #2617.
- Fixed "Session __workshop__ does not exist" crashing the Memory→Soul refinement chat (`WorkshopReview.svelte`) for every brand-new agent, in both the first-run onboarding flow and Settings → Create Agent. Root cause: `WorkshopReview.svelte` called `ai_chat_stream` with `context.projectId = WORKSHOP_SCOPE_ID` (`"__workshop__"`, a DB-only-notes sentinel) but never passed a `sessionId`. Post-ADR-0062, `ai_chat_stream`'s dispatch is session-first — with no explicit `sessionId`, its fallback path in `commands.rs` resolved (and then treated as a literal session id) the string `"__workshop__"`, which never existed as a `chat_sessions` row, so `agents.rs::resolve_and_selfheal_session_agent` threw before the AI could respond at all. `WorkshopReview.svelte` now takes a required `sessionId` prop, threaded straight into `ai_chat_stream`'s top-level `sessionId` arg (same pattern `ChatSidebar.svelte` already uses) — bypassing the buggy fallback path entirely rather than patching it. Both callers (`Onboarding.svelte`, `AgentCreateOverlay.svelte`) now call a new shared `createWorkshopSession(agentId)` helper (`src/lib/onboarding/workshopSession.ts`) right before mounting `WorkshopReview`, which creates a real, disposable `chat_sessions` row via `api.createSession(WORKSHOP_SESSION_SCOPE_ID, agentId)` — explicitly bound to the just-created/just-resolved agent (not `getActiveSession`, which would silently leave a pre-existing session's `agent_id` binding unchanged, refining the wrong agent's memory in the create-agent-from-Settings flow). `WORKSHOP_SESSION_SCOPE_ID` is a new, separate sentinel from the pre-existing `WORKSHOP_SCOPE_ID` (that one still scopes the workshop's DB-only notes; conflating the two would misuse a notes-only concept as a session id again). No backend changes — `ai_chat_stream` and `resolve_and_selfheal_session_agent` already worked correctly given a real session id; the gap was entirely the frontend never creating/passing one. (Relates to #2618, spec: `docs/spec/onboarding.md` and `docs/spec/agents.md` updated with the workshop-session contract)
- Fixed both canned greeting templates (`ChatSidebar.svelte`'s home greeting and project greeting) resolving the app-wide **default** agent's name (`get_main_agent`) instead of the session's own **bound** agent. Matt's repro: Biff is the default agent, he creates a session bound to Blue — the canned welcome says "I'm Biff." Because that greeting text sits in the conversation context from then on, Blue then believes it IS Biff until challenged — same RC-B family (name resolved from default instead of binding) as the speaker-label and onDone attribution fixes below. New `resolveGreetingAgentName()` helper resolves `$sessionStore.activeSession?.agent_id` against the agent list (`api.getAgents()`) first, falling back to `get_main_agent` only when the session is unbound (or the bound agent can't be resolved), and finally to the literal `'Pane'` — matching the existing fallback chain's shape at both call sites. (Relates to #2604, spec-skip: greeting template agent resolution fix — same RC-B family, no new behavioral surface)
- Fixed the chat speaker label showing the app-wide default agent's name instead of the session's own bound agent whenever a live-streamed (not-yet-DB-reloaded) message rendered — e.g. a session permanently bound to "Biff" would label its own live messages "Blue" the moment Blue became the default agent elsewhere in the app, and switching the default mid-session would silently relabel every open, un-reloaded message. Root Cause A (which agent/model actually *dispatches*) was investigated and closed as working-as-configured; this was purely a **display** bug (Root Cause B, `docs/audits/2026-08-20-c8-session-binding-investigation.md`). Two coordinated fixes: (1) the backend's stream-done event (`ai_chat_stream`, `commands.rs`) now resolves and includes `agent_id`/`agent_name` for the actual dispatching agent (new `resolve_agent_name_for_dispatch` fn), threaded through `streamManager.ts`'s `onDone` callback so `ChatSidebar.svelte` can set `agent_id`/`agent_name` on the live message object immediately, the same way `model` is already set there; (2) `ChatPanel.svelte`'s speaker-label fallback chain changed from `message.agent_name ?? mainAgentName` (the ambient app-wide default) to `message.agent_name ?? sessionBoundAgentName ?? <legacy-NULL copy>`, where `sessionBoundAgentName` is sourced from the session's own bound agent (`SessionDropdownHeader.svelte`'s existing `boundAgent` derivation) — and `ChatPanel` no longer listens to `pane-agent-switched` for relabeling purposes at all. Model-badge behavior (which model actually answered a smart-routed message) is unchanged — this is the receipt for Root Cause A's sanctioned divergence and was deliberately left untouched. (RC-B, Relates to #2604, spec-skip: spec note added in this PR)
- Fixed the session-picker popover (`AgentPickerPopover.svelte`, shared by both the Home surface's Sessions drawer and each project's session header dropdown) rendering off-screen at certain window sizes/trigger positions. The popover previously positioned itself purely from the trigger element's own coordinates with no viewport awareness; it now computes a viewport-clamped `top`/`left` (`recomputeClampedPosition()`, `VIEWPORT_MARGIN = 8`) on open and on window resize (`<svelte:window onresize>`), so it always stays fully on-screen regardless of where its trigger sits. Since the fix lives entirely in the shared popover component, neither `SessionDropdownHeader.svelte` nor `SessionsDrawer.svelte` needed any changes. (Relates to #2590, spec-skip: positioning fix only, standard popover viewport-clamping behavior, no redesign)
- Fixed the New Provider modal's Step 1 provider list always showing all four providers (Anthropic, OpenRouter, Ollama, OpenClaw) regardless of which were already configured/connected — a user who'd already set up a provider would still see it in the "add new provider" list, letting them re-select something already live. Step 1 now filters to `visibleProviderRows`, a `connections`/`ocConnectionInfo`-derived list that excludes any provider already connected (or, for OpenClaw specifically, already paired); if every provider is already configured, Step 1 shows an empty-state message instead of an unusable list. (Relates to #2590, spec-skip: filtering fix only, no behavioral changes to connection/pairing logic)
- Added a "Test connection" button to the OpenClaw provider card (`ProviderConnectionCard.svelte`) for parity with the other three provider cards, which already had one. Reuses the existing `gateway_fetch_fingerprint` backend command (the same reachability probe the pairing ceremony's own Step 1 health check already calls) rather than adding new backend surface — confirms the paired gateway URL is still reachable, with no credential sent (matching the pairing ceremony's own unauthenticated health check). Only shown once paired; an unpaired OC slot has no connection to test. (Relates to #2590, spec-skip: UI parity fix reusing an existing backend command, no new backend surface)
- Replaced the "wall of cards" model picker in the agent creation flow (`AgentCreateOverlay.svelte`'s Step M) with the same searchable dropdown (`SearchableModelSelect.svelte`) Settings' "Smart Routing Model" picker already uses — search-at-top, single reusable component instead of a bespoke card grid. Onboarding's model picker (`Onboarding.svelte`) was already using `SearchableModelSelect` prior to this change; no changes were needed there. (Relates to #2590, spec-skip: UI component consolidation, reuses an existing shared component, no new behavioral surface)
- Fixed a tokio panic ("Cannot start a runtime from within a runtime") that crashed any chat mid-response when memory search ran with LLM rerank enabled. `execute_search_memory` (`ai/commands.rs`) is a sync fn reached from inside the async tokio runtime during chat dispatch (`ai_chat_stream` → `execute_single_tool` → `execute_search_memory`), but its optional rerank step called `tokio::runtime::Handle::current().block_on(...)` directly — illegal from a thread already inside a runtime. The call is now wrapped in `tokio::task::block_in_place`, which is legal from a tokio worker thread on a multi-threaded runtime (the kind Tauri and this crate both use). Rerank failures still degrade gracefully to the original result order (unchanged `Err(e)` fallback) rather than losing the chat response. (C9, Relates to #2603, spec-skip: spec note added in this PR (one-line §5.15.4 async fix note))
- Fixed `connected_runtime_providers` (`ai/commands.rs`) deriving "connected runtime" status from `SELECT DISTINCT runtime_type FROM ai_agents` instead of actual connection config — a chicken-and-egg bug: a runtime with a valid key or endpoint configured but zero `ai_agents` rows (the exact state right after saving Anthropic/OpenRouter credentials, before the first agent exists) was invisible to `fetch_available_models`, so the model picker for first-agent creation stayed empty until an agent already existed for that runtime. `connected_runtime_providers` now iterates all four runtime types and calls `build_provider_for_runtime_type` for each — the same connection-config derivation `ai_list_runtime_connections_impl` already uses — so connection status depends purely on credentials/endpoint/pairing, never on agent-row count. Also added `[RUNTIME-PROVIDERS]`/`[DEDUP]` `eprintln!` logging to several previously-silent `Err(_) => Vec::new()` swallows in the same file (`commands.rs`) that were masking real SQL/prepare failures behind an empty-result fallback. (Relates to #2598, spec-covered-by: #2541)
- Fixed `migrations.rs` missing match arms for schema versions v72/v73/v74 — match arms jumped straight from v71 to v75, so any DB stamped at v72/v73/v74 (a real, reachable state: a v73→v74 migration arm was briefly added then reverted with no replacement, and no released build leaves users there but an interrupted/rolled-back upgrade could strand an install here) hit the `SCHEMA_MISMATCH` fallthrough with no path forward. Added three new arms (`"72"`, `"73"`, `"74"`) chaining `migrate_v76` through `migrate_v83` + `verify_crr_tables`, following the same pattern the existing `"75"` arm already uses. (Relates to #2598, spec-covered-by: #2541)
- Fixed deactivated legacy agents (`ai_agents.is_active = 0` — e.g. the Bob/Murphy-style rows `migrate_v83` deactivates on the retired `runtime_type IS NULL` population) still rendering on the Settings → Agents tab. That population was already excluded from every picker surface (`filterConnectedAgents`'s `is_active` gate, #2588 B5/C4), but the Agents tab itself read straight off the raw agent list with no `is_active` filter — the last surface where a deactivated row could still appear. A new `activeAgentsList` derived (`Settings.svelte`) filters on `is_active` before the roster is grouped by runtime_type or counted in the section header. Separately, the Agents tab no longer shows a model string for subagents (`role === 'sub'` with a real OC `runtime_ref` — Lane, Reed, Stia, Pane Support): D9's post-dispatch write-back (`write_back_agent_model_if_changed`) never fires for them since their dispatch is gateway-side, so their `model` column would otherwise show the `migrate_v83` `'openclaw-pending'` sentinel forever instead of a real value. "Brit Freed" (the main OC agent) and any Pane-dispatched non-sub agent are unaffected and keep showing their real model string. (Relates to #2587, spec-skip: display-only filtering, no behavioral changes, spec-covered-by: #2541)
- Fixed `migrate_v82_keychain_slot_split` (`migrations.rs`) unconditionally deleting the legacy shared `ai_provider_key` keychain slot right after writing the new per-provider slot, without ever confirming the write actually stuck — a bare `Ok(())` from `store_password` is not proof the item is durably persisted and queryable (real-world keychain-lock transitions, ACL/trust-store races, and first-unlock-after-boot windows can all produce a write that reports success but doesn't stick). This was a data-loss bug: once the legacy slot was cleared with no confirmed copy anywhere, the credential was gone. The write path now mirrors `migrate_one_credential`'s existing ADR-0044 Decision 2 pattern exactly — write, read back, assert the read-back value matches byte-for-byte, and only then delete the legacy slot; any other outcome (`Ok(None)`, a value mismatch, or `Err`) aborts the split for that slot, preserves the legacy slot intact, and logs a retry-next-launch line instead of a false "cleared" success (the migration was already idempotent-by-design for this case — this fix makes the retry path real instead of theoretical). Separately, `read_provider_key`, `read_gateway_token`, and `read_internal_key` (`credential_migration.rs`) stopped discarding a real keychain `Err` via `.ok().flatten()`, which collapsed ACL-denied reads, a locked keychain, or any other genuine failure into the exact same "not configured" log message and return value as a confirmed-absent credential — making the two cases indistinguishable in the logs. All three reads now match explicitly and log a distinct `"keychain READ ERROR: ... — unavailable, not 'not configured'"` line for a real `Err`, never falling through to the generic miss message for that call. `MockKeychain` gained per-account, per-operation failure injection (`fail_get_for`/`fail_store_for`) so this exact write-succeeds-but-readback-fails shape — previously structurally unreachable by the all-or-nothing mock — is now covered by regression tests and stays testable going forward. (Relates to #2584, spec-skip: keychain migration safety fix — adds read-back confirmation and error-path distinction to existing v82 migration, no new behavioral surface, spec-covered-by: #2541)
- Fixed `fetch_primary_provider_models` (Onboarding model-select) and `get_internal_provider`'s Step 2 fallback still gating on the retired `ai_settings.provider` scalar (deleted for real by #2564/B1 #2574) — both always failed with "No primary/AI provider configured" before ever reaching a keychain read or HTTP call, since B1 deleted the writer but explicitly deferred these two readers as fast-follow items. Both now resolve via `derive_active_provider_label` (`runtime_resolution.rs`), the same retarget B1 already applied to `list_available_models` — reading the live per-agent `ai_agents.runtime_type` roster instead of the dead global scalar. (Relates to #2586, spec-skip: mechanical retarget to existing resolver, same pattern as prior B1 fix, no new behavioral surface, spec-covered-by: #2541)
- Fixed OpenClaw agents left with a permanently empty `ai_agents.model` after v79's D8 dissolution deleted the global `ai_settings.model` key without ever backfilling the new per-agent column — this silently broke dispatch for any OC agent created (or re-imported) before the backfill existed, since `resolve_model_for_message`'s Step 3 hard-fails on an empty model. New `migrate_v83` (`SCHEMA_VERSION` 82→83) backfills `model = 'openclaw-pending'` for every `runtime_type = 'openclaw'` row with a NULL or empty model — a self-healing placeholder, not a real model name: the D9 post-dispatch write-back (`write_back_agent_model_if_changed`) corrects it to the agent's real resolved model on its very next successful dispatch, and it's safe on the wire in the meantime because `stream_openrouter_inner` (openrouter.rs) unconditionally rewrites the outgoing model to `'openclaw'` for every OC-routed request regardless of what `ai_agents.model` says (both sites carry a cross-reference comment tying this safety argument together — if that rewrite is ever made conditional, the placeholder could leak onto the wire). Unlike `migrate_v81`'s role-label repair, this backfill **does** bump `updated_at` — a model value is dispatch-relevant, not a cosmetic label, so it counts as a real data change. `ai_configure_and_save`'s OC pairing write is also retargeted from the same D8-retired `ai_settings.model` key to `ai_agents.model` for the `runtime_type='openclaw' AND runtime_ref='main'` row — call-site tracing confirmed the old `ai_settings.model` write was already dead for every non-OC provider (anthropic/openrouter/ollama agents get their `model` written directly at agent-creation time via `create_local_agent_impl`, never through this path), so the retarget is OC-only by necessity: OC is the only runtime with one structurally unique target row per install, and the dead write for other providers is simply removed rather than resurrected elsewhere. The Settings roster now masks the sentinel in the UI — `ProviderConnectionCard.svelte` renders `'openclaw-pending'` as "resolves on first message" instead of the raw placeholder string. Same migration also rides C3 (below). (Relates to #2585, spec-skip: migration backfill + retarget write path — no new behavioral surface, spec-covered-by: #2541)
- Fixed legacy-unpinned agents (`ai_agents.runtime_type IS NULL` — the pre-v79 population Stage 6 stopped minting) still appearing as selectable, active rows and still triggering the one-time `LegacyProviderPrompt` interception flow in `AgentPickerPopover`. That population is closed — v79's migration was the only path that could ever produce a NULL `runtime_type` row, and every current agent-creation path pins one — so the rescue-UI is no longer justified. `migrate_v83` also runs `UPDATE ai_agents SET is_active = 0 WHERE runtime_type IS NULL`, deactivating any remaining legacy-unpinned rows; `LegacyProviderPrompt.svelte`, its wiring in `AgentPickerPopover.svelte`, and its test file are deleted outright rather than left dormant. (Relates to #2587, spec-skip: deactivate legacy rows + delete now-unreachable rescue UI — no new behavioral surface, spec-covered-by: #2541)

### Changed
- Changed: Replaced the placeholder "P" text glyph on the auth/onboarding surfaces (`AuthScreen.svelte`'s loading/email/password/no-account states, `S8TakeOver.svelte`, `S7SubscriptionBlock.svelte`) with the actual Pane logo (`static/pane-logo.png`) inside the existing `.auth__glyph` container — same 44×44 size, border-radius, and placement, just an `<img>` (`object-fit: contain`) instead of a styled letter. `Onboarding.svelte` was not touched. (Relates to #2616, spec-skip: visual-only logo swap, no behavioral change)
- Changed: Provider Settings visual polish. Unconfigured/disconnected provider cards now render neutral grey instead of red (§12's grey-not-red ruling, applied panel-wide) — red is reserved for a provider that was configured and is now genuinely failing; every runtime type gets a "Not configured" (or, for OpenClaw specifically, "Not paired") badge in the never-connected case, and the failure strip is recolored to match. API key / Base URL fields in `ProviderConnectionCard.svelte` now pick up the dark-theme input/button styles they were missing (the component referenced `.input`/`.btn`-family classes without ever defining them, so they rendered as unstyled tiny white browser-default fields). The "Default agent" row in Settings → AI now names the current default agent and its runtime (e.g. "Brit Freed · OpenClaw") instead of showing only a "Change default" button. The New Provider modal gets a standard X close button, and picking an already-connected Anthropic/OpenRouter/Ollama provider now shows a read-only connection summary (masked credential or endpoint, agent count, Update connection / Disconnect) instead of a blank config form — generalizing the existing already-paired OpenClaw pattern. The Ollama card's Disconnect button now shows a brief "Disconnect requested" acknowledgment on click; this is presentation-only feedback, not new backend semantics (`ai_disconnect_runtime`'s "ollama" arm remains an intentional no-op — B3: Disconnect semantics TBD). Visual/frontend only — no `.rs` files touched, no changes to connected-derivation or credential logic. (Relates to #2522, spec-skip: visual polish only, no behavioral changes)
- Provider credentials now stored in separate per-provider keychain slots (Anthropic and OpenRouter no longer share a single entry). New `migrate_v82` (`SCHEMA_VERSION` 81→82) performs the one-time keychain split for existing installs: the legacy shared `ai_provider_key` value is format-sniffed (`sk-ant-`/`sk-or-` prefixes) and routed to the correct new per-provider slot, falling back to inferring from an active `ai_agents.runtime_type` row when the prefix is unrecognized, and leaving both new slots empty (requiring re-entry) as the last resort. (Relates to #2565)
- Ollama connection requires explicit user configuration — reachable-but-unconfigured instances show as detected, not connected. `build_provider_for_runtime_type`'s ollama arm now requires `ai_settings.ollama_endpoint` to have been written (by the Save flow, or by `migrate_v82`'s grandfather backfill for pre-existing installs) rather than assuming any reachable localhost Ollama instance is "connected". The same `migrate_v82` migration backfills `ollama_endpoint` for any install with a pre-existing active `runtime_type = 'ollama'` agent, so it doesn't silently go non-dispatchable the moment this ships — from the legacy `ai_settings.endpoint` value if it's Ollama-shaped, else the standard local default. The legacy `endpoint` key itself is left untouched (`openclaw`/sync client/system files still read it directly). (Relates to #2565)
- Changed: **role='local' at birth** — locally-created agents (`create_local_agent_impl`, `upsert_agent`'s default-role fallback, and the filesystem-recovery INSERT path in `ai/commands.rs`) now write `role='local'` at creation instead of `role='sub'`. Per Matt's ruling: a user-created agent is never a subagent, structurally — the `role='sub'` literal (since #2264) was a birth mislabel that B5 (#2577) had already worked around at every predicate site via a `runtime_ref IS NULL` conjunct, without retiring the underlying mislabel. `sync_client.rs`'s three OC re-import demotion UPDATEs (pre-flight normalization, overwrite-path, fresh-import) now conditionally preserve the demoted row's correct class (`CASE WHEN runtime_ref IS NULL THEN 'local' ELSE 'sub' END`) instead of blanket-writing `role='sub'` — previously, a locally-created default agent losing default status to an incoming OC agent would be silently re-mislabeled as a subagent on every re-import. The OC-agent INSERT/UPDATE sites (which always set a non-NULL `runtime_ref` in the same statement) are unchanged — they correctly label real OC subagents. New `migrate_v81` (`SCHEMA_VERSION` 80→81) performs the one-time data repair for existing installs: `UPDATE ai_agents SET role = 'local' WHERE role = 'sub' AND runtime_ref IS NULL`, idempotent by its own self-exhausting predicate, role-only (does not bump `updated_at` — data repair, not a user edit, per Matt's explicit ruling). The B5-era defense-in-depth predicates (`agents.rs` `set_default_agent_impl`, `Settings.svelte`'s subagent-label and rename-icon conditionals, `DefaultAgentPickerModal.svelte`'s eligibility filter) are left unchanged — they remain correct post-migration and simply stop being load-bearing, matching Matt's "stop being load-bearing" framing exactly (they stop being *necessary*, not *present*). (Relates to #2567, spec-skip: spec already landed in prior PR, spec-covered-by: #2541 (merged, touched docs/spec/agents.md — per-session agent binding + runtime-per-agent))

### Fixed
- Fixed subagents (Lane, Reed, Stia, Pane Support — `role='sub'` with a non-null `runtime_ref`) still appearing as selectable options in the New Session picker (session header dropdown, Sessions drawer) and the New Project agent picker. Matt's ruling: subagent sessions are always-no. `filterConnectedAgents` (`agentDisplay.ts`), the one shared utility feeding `SessionDropdownHeader.svelte`, `SessionsDrawer.svelte`, and `ProjectSettings.svelte`'s pickers, now applies the same `role === 'sub' && runtime_ref != null` exclusion `DefaultAgentPickerModal` and the backend `set_default_agent_impl` guard already enforce (#2567/#2577 B5) — locally-created agents that happen to share `role='sub'` (pre-#2567 birth-mislabel cases, `runtime_ref` null) are unaffected. (#2588, spec-skip: extends existing B5 subagent filter to remaining session pickers — same predicate, no new behavioral surface, spec-covered-by: #2541)
- Saving an OpenRouter API key no longer makes Anthropic show "Connected" with the same masked key (#2565)
- Disconnecting one key-based provider (Anthropic or OpenRouter) no longer disconnects both — each now reads/writes/clears its own per-provider keychain slot instead of a single shared one (#2565)
- Ollama Disconnect button now clears the connection (previously a silent no-op — there was no `ollama_endpoint` signal for it to clear) (#2565)
- Fixed subagents (Lane, Reed, Stia, Pane Support — `role='sub'`) rendering as selectable options in the "Default agent" picker (`DefaultAgentPickerModal.svelte`). The old per-agent "Set as Main" buttons carried a `role !== 'sub'` filter (#2271); it was dropped when those buttons were replaced by the cross-provider picker (#2522 Stage 5). Sub-role agents are now excluded from the eligible-agent list entirely (absent, not disabled), and `set_default_agent_impl` (the shared implementation behind the `set_main_agent` command) now rejects any `role='sub'` target at the command level with "Subagents cannot be set as default" — a UI filter alone isn't enforcement since `set_main_agent` is reachable from other callers. (Relates to #2567)
- Retired legacy `ai_settings.provider` scalar — all provider resolution now uses per-agent `runtime_type` (#2564)
- Fixed v79 migration orphaning gateway connection for OpenClaw users (#2564)
- Fixed consolidator silently falling back to localhost when gateway endpoint missing (#2568)
- Fixed three frontend attribution surfaces (session header binding line's New Session picker call, the read-only banner's trigger + label, and the New Project picker) still reading the retired `ai_settings.provider` global scalar via `aiLoadConfig().provider` after PR #2574 removed it from every backend reader — caused the read-only banner and New Session/New Project pickers to disagree with the header's own agent-identity label, and to wrongly exclude OpenClaw-bound agents from pickers whenever the stale global scalar drifted from an agent's own `runtime_type`. `agentDisplay.ts`'s `agentProviderLabel` now derives a label purely from the agent's own `runtime_ref`/`runtime_type` identity (no second parameter); `filterInClassAgents` is retired in favor of a new `filterConnectedAgents`, which filters against live per-runtime connectivity from `ai_list_runtime_connections` (the same mechanism `DefaultAgentPickerModal` already used) instead of a client-side XOR against the global scalar. The read-only banner's trigger (`SessionDropdownHeader`'s `bindingUnavailableReason`) now implements ADR-0063 D6 directly: read-only fires only when the bound agent is inactive, or its own runtime is genuinely disconnected — replacing the retired D5 "out-of-class XOR". (Relates to #2563, spec-covered-by: #2541)

## [1.0.5] - 2026-08-18

### Added
- New Provider modal — 2-step flow to add a provider connection: pick runtime (Anthropic, OpenRouter, Ollama, OpenClaw), then configure (API key + Base URL for API providers, pairing handoff for OpenClaw unpaired, connection summary for OpenClaw paired) (#2522)
- `+ New Provider` ghost button in Provider Connections section header for discoverability (#2522)
- OpenClaw pairing ceremony re-homed to Provider Connection card (3-step flow: URL entry → fingerprint verification → pairing code exchange) with three entry points (Pair gateway, Re-pair, New Provider) and comprehensive error states (#2522)
- Sync Now button on paired OpenClaw card — triggers gateway file sync on demand, updates timestamp on success (#2522)
- `sync_now` Tauri command wrapping `pull_pending_changes_blocking` + `flush_sync_queue_blocking` for frontend-invokable gateway sync (#2522)
- Legacy provider prompt — one-time modal for pre-migration agents with no `runtime_type`, asked on first selection (#2522)
- Added: ADR-0063 Stage 6 — Agents page rework + creation flow. Backend: `create_local_agent` now accepts an explicit `runtime_type` parameter instead of inferring it via the `resolve_runtime_type_for_new_local_agent` stopgap fallback added in an earlier stage — every newly created local agent is pinned to the runtime the user actually picked, no inference required. Agents tab: the roster is now regrouped by `runtime_type` (Anthropic / OpenRouter / Ollama / OpenClaw), replacing the old local-vs-OC-imported split that predated per-agent runtimes. Creation flow: `AgentCreateOverlay.svelte` gets a new runtime picker (lists connected runtimes only) that feeds into the model picker before naming, and every remaining `provider === 'openclaw'` creation gate — the disabled-button/tooltip machinery added for #2392 — is retired, since agent creation is now always available regardless of the active provider. New test suites cover `AgentCreateOverlay` (12 tests: runtime picker, model picker, gating removal). (Relates to #2522, spec-skip: spec already landed in PR #2541, spec-covered-by: #2541)
- Added: ADR-0063 Stage 5 — Settings dissolution + runtime connections UI. The Settings chat pane is removed entirely (#2536): Settings is now a single-column layout, content measure widened from 600 to 860 and kept centred, with nothing added in the pane's place (per README-group-b.md's ruling — a help rail, health summary, or shortcuts panel would all be things nobody opened Settings to read, and connection health already lives on the cards). Settings › AI gets per-runtime provider connection cards (ADR-0063 D8): a new `ProviderConnectionsPanel.svelte` fetches `ai_list_runtime_connections` and renders one `ProviderConnectionCard.svelte` per runtime type — always all four (OpenClaw, OpenRouter, Anthropic, Ollama), connected or not — as a flat list with no concept of an "active" provider; every connected provider is live simultaneously, matching D8 ("every connected provider is live at the same time"). Each card shows identity, config rows (key providers + Ollama only; OpenClaw is read-only — pairing ceremony is Stage 7 scope), a read-only agent roster (name, model, Default badge — no create/set-default/provider-switch controls on the card itself), and a failure strip when disconnected. A new cross-provider `DefaultAgentPickerModal.svelte`, wired into Settings › AI behind a "Default agent" trigger below the provider connection cards, handles "Set as default" as a comparison across every provider's agents; the two per-agent "Set as Main" buttons that used to live inline in the Agents-tab roster are retired, keeping roster rows (both the provider cards and the Agents tab) read-only so the same choice isn't offered three ways. The old dark-provider-gate predicate (`is_default && provider === 'openclaw'`) that hid OpenClaw-specific UI behind the previous single-active-provider model is removed along with the single-provider `ai_settings` fields it depended on — superseded by the fixed four-runtime-card contract. Smart Features (ADR-0061 D6) stays a standalone connection-config block below a visual rule beneath the provider cards, with its own single provider dropdown, unchanged — it's a Pane subsystem, not a conversation, and is deliberately not folded into any provider card. (Relates to #2522, spec-covered-by: #2541)
- Added: ADR-0063 Stage 3+4 — concurrent streams and `StreamManager` demolition. `src/lib/services/streamManager.ts`'s singular `streamId`/`callbacks`/`buffer`/`streamThreadId`/`pendingResult`/`capturedContext` fields — shared by every in-flight stream regardless of thread — are replaced by a `Map<threadId, StreamState>`, so each thread now owns its own stream state entirely. This fixes the bug the new dual-provider test harness (`streamManagerConcurrency.test.ts`) was built to prove: previously, starting a second stream (e.g. a different agent/thread) unconditionally cancelled whatever stream was already in flight, because `startStream()` called a global `this.cancel()` first; now `startStream()` only supersedes a prior stream for the *same* threadId, and event dispatch matches each incoming `ai-stream-chunk` payload's stream id against the live entry in the map instead of a single stored id. `cancel(threadId)`, `isStreamingThread(threadId)`, `reattachCallbacks(threadId, callbacks)`, `getBuffer(threadId)`, `getCapturedContext(threadId)`, `setPendingResult(threadId)`, and `consumePendingResult(threadId)` all take an explicit threadId now; `cancel()` with no argument still cancels every thread (used by tests/full-reset callers). `ChatSidebar.svelte`'s call sites are updated accordingly. On the backend, Stage 3 verification confirmed `ai_chat_stream` already has no shared mutable state post-Stage 2 (`resolve_runtime_config_for_session` resolves fresh per dispatch, DB lock scopes never cross an `.await`, each stream gets its own `uuid::Uuid::new_v4()` id carried through every `ai-stream-chunk` emit) — no backend dispatch-path changes were needed; a new backend test (`runtime_resolution::tests::test_two_concurrent_runtimes_resolve_independently_no_shared_state`) pins this. Separately (D7.3), `fetch_available_models` and the startup `populate_model_registry_from_provider` now enumerate every connected runtime (every distinct `ai_agents.runtime_type` among active agents with valid credentials, via a new `connected_runtime_providers` helper) and merge each runtime's model list into the already provider-namespaced `ModelRegistry`, instead of only ever resolving the single default agent's runtime — a user with e.g. both an Anthropic and an Ollama agent configured now sees both providers' models. (Relates to #2522, spec-covered-by: #2541)
- Added: ADR-0063 Stage 2 — `AiConfig`/`AiStateWrapper` singleton demolition and per-dispatch runtime resolution. The startup-configured, mutex-shared `AiConfig` (provider + model + a de-facto constant system prompt) and its `AiStateWrapper` Tauri-managed wrapper are removed entirely. Every dispatch and background-command call site that used to lock the singleton now resolves runtime + model fresh from the database on every call via a new `ai::runtime_resolution` module: `session_id → chat_sessions.agent_id → ai_agents.runtime_type/model` for chat dispatch (self-healing a NULL agent binding to the designated default per ADR-0062), and "designated default agent" (ADR-0062 D5) for sessionless background work — memory save/synthesis/consolidation, the consolidation-trigger listener, the startup consolidation-staleness sweep, and eager `ModelRegistry` population. Because nothing is cached in memory anymore, the async-race class of bug the old singleton was exposed to (#1460's pending-marker guard, #1485's `ProviderRestoreGuard` drop-guard) no longer has a class of state to race on — both mechanisms, and their now-inapplicable regression tests, are removed rather than ported. `ai_configure_and_save` is narrowed to a pure connection-config writer (`ai_settings` + keychain) — it no longer mutates any in-memory dispatch state, since dispatch doesn't read any. `ai_configure` (a dead duplicate of `ai_configure_and_save` with no in-memory-only behavior worth preserving) is deleted. D9's post-dispatch model write-back now targets the answering agent's own `ai_agents.model` column (write-on-change only) instead of the retired global `ai_settings.model` key. (Relates to #2522, spec-covered-by: #2541)
- Added: ADR-0063 Stage 1 — runtime-per-agent schema rename and v79 migration. `ai_agents.oc_agent_id` is renamed to `runtime_ref`, `is_main` is renamed to `is_default`, and a new `runtime_type` column (`'anthropic'` | `'openrouter'` | `'ollama'` | `'openclaw'`) tracks each agent's own runtime independent of the global active-provider setting. The `migrate_v79` migration backfills `runtime_type` on upgrade: OC-imported agents (`runtime_ref IS NOT NULL`) become `'openclaw'`; locally-created agents inherit the active `ai_settings.provider` at migration time if it's an API-class provider, or are left `runtime_type = NULL` (legacy-unpinned) if the active provider was OpenClaw — resolved by a one-time picker in a later stage. The composite unique index `idx_ai_agents_runtime_unique(runtime_type, runtime_ref)` replaces the old single-column `oc_agent_id` unique index, and the four now-superseded global `ai_settings` keys (`provider`, `endpoint`, `api_key`, `model`) are deleted. This is schema/rename scope only — dispatch, Settings/Agents UI, and gateway wire contracts are unaffected and land in later stages. (Relates to #2522, spec-covered-by: #2541)
- Added: Per-session agent binding (ADR-0062 phase 1): every session is permanently bound to one agent at creation; agent picker on New Session and New Project, session header shows binding, read-only state for unavailable agents (#2522)
- Added: ClawHub skill package (clawhub/pane/) with CI drift-detection gate for gateway API changes
- Added: Tagged Pane releases now build and publish Linux DEB, RPM, and AppImage packages with SHA-256 checksums alongside the macOS DMG. Linux bundles are built from the exact release tag on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu, and release publication waits for both platform builds to succeed. (Relates to #2340)
- Added: New `scripts/build-gateway-dmg.sh` — builds, signs, notarizes, and packages the standalone `pane-gateway` CLI binary (`src-gateway/`) as a DMG and publishes it as a GitHub release, mirroring the existing Tauri build/release flow (`scripts/release.sh`) but for the gateway rather than the full app. Signs the release binary with hardened runtime (`--options runtime`, required for notarization) using the `Developer ID Application: Matthew Carano (FL493VAUAL)` identity, packages it into a plain-binary DMG (no `.app` bundle — it's a CLI tool) via `hdiutil`, signs and notarizes the DMG itself (`xcrun notarytool submit --wait` + `xcrun stapler staple`), copies the result to `~/Shared/ExampleApp/builds/`, and creates a GitHub release under the `gateway-v*` tag prefix (kept distinct from the main app's `v*` tags per the existing release-pipeline convention, #2340). Supports `--version <x.y.z>` (defaults to the version in `src-gateway/Cargo.toml`), `--skip-build` (reuse an already-built binary), and `--dry-run` (run the full build/sign/notarize pipeline but skip the GitHub release upload). Apple notarization credentials load from environment or fall back to `~/Projects/example-app/.env`, with an explicit presence check before any build work starts. Script not yet run — first build to be executed manually by Matt/Brit. (Relates to #2340)

- Changed: **#2379** — All Tasks view now matches Project (Kanban) view's layout and behavior, per Matt's ruling (exception: no Cabinet column). `AllTasksView.svelte` columns now grow via `flex:1`/`min-width:280px` (was a fixed non-growing `width:220px`), matching `KanbanBoard.svelte`'s column sizing; `overflow-x:auto` is kept on the container as a narrow-viewport fallback. The editor-panel resize mechanism adopts Kanban's full `#2331`/`#2336` machinery: a `splitViewRef` bound to `.tasks-body`, a dynamic max-width (`splitViewRef.clientWidth`, replacing the hardcoded `800`), and an `isEditorResizing` guard (set before listener attach, cleared via a deferred `setTimeout(...,0)` in mouseup) consumed as the first check in the close-handler. The close-handler itself is relocated off `.all-tasks-view` (the view root, a shared ancestor of both the card columns and the editor mount) onto a new wrapper around the card-columns only — sibling of `.editor-panel`, closing the same class of bug #2329 fixed in Folder View (a checklist click inside a task opened from All Tasks could previously have unexpectedly closed the note); `handleCloseEditor`'s body is unchanged. Drag-and-drop now updates the local task list optimistically (mutate → API call → revert-via-reload on error) instead of always reloading after the API call. `onUpdate` is now a no-op relying on a new `pane-task-meta-changed` listener for partial-field patches, replacing a 300ms full-reload `setTimeout`. Wiki-link clicks inside a task opened from All Tasks now navigate (`onNavigate` wired to the shared `navigateWikiLink` helper, `folderId`/`projectId` left undefined — navigation-only; create-on-miss stays inert per Matt's ruling) — previously a dead no-op. `<StatusBar>` now renders below the editor. The header gains sticky positioning matching Kanban's; header content (title, task count, priority filter) is unchanged. **Two deliberate divergences from the donor, per Matt's ruling:** (1) every column is collapsible, unconditionally — supersedes Kanban's Done-only/`>5`-task gate; Done still defaults collapsed on mount, not persisted; (2) All Tasks keeps its existing `dragleave`-clears-highlight behavior rather than adopting Kanban's dragleave-is-a-no-op quirk. Task sorting, the priority filter, the context menu, and the no-new-note-affordance are all unchanged — out of scope per the audit. (Relates to #2379, spec-skip: parity per Matt's behavior ruling 2026-08-07, audit §6)

### Added
- Added: **#2392** — Voluntary-create-on-OC gate (Settings → Agents). When the active provider is OpenClaw, the "+ New agent" button is **disabled** (visible, not hidden) rather than opening the local create flow. Tooltip reads: *Agent creation is managed by OpenClaw*. An explanatory note renders directly below the button: *Agents are created in OpenClaw and imported here automatically. To create a Pane-local agent, switch to an API provider in the AI tab.* The "Locally created" group's empty-state message changes to: *No local agents. Pane-local agents are created under an API provider.* Under any API provider (Anthropic / OpenRouter / Ollama) all three surfaces revert to their pre-#2392 defaults — button enabled, no note, original empty-state copy — behavior is identical to before. This completes the provider-usability matrix (ADR-0059 §2026-08-03 supplement): voluntary creation while OpenClaw is active is now defined — disabled with explanation — rather than undefined. The forced-create flow reached via a provider switch (§24.5.5) is completely untouched. (Relates to #2392, spec-covered-by: #2395)
- Added: **#2334** — Cabinet Drag-to-Reorder. Cabinet notes (`status IS NULL OR 'cabinet'`) can now be manually reordered by dragging cards within the Cabinet column, in both `NotesBrowser.svelte`'s folder view and `KanbanBoard.svelte`'s project kanban — previously only column-level status-change drops existed; there was no per-card drag target anywhere. New per-card drag handlers (`cabinetDragStart`/`cabinetDrop`/etc. in NotesBrowser, `handleCardDragStart`/`cabinetCardDrop`/etc. in KanbanBoard) follow the existing `ChecklistNodeView.svelte` splice-and-renumber pattern and persist via `entityService.reorderNotes` (its first production caller). Event-propagation contract: card-level handlers `stopPropagation()` so a drop on a card never double-fires the column-level status-change handler (#2325 lesson); drag *source* determines reorder-vs-status-change mode, so a task card dropped directly onto a Cabinet card still correctly changes status to `'cabinet'` instead of being swallowed. `get_project_notes_for_kanban`'s `ORDER BY` is now conditional per status: Cabinet notes order by `sort_order ASC, created_at DESC` (user-arranged); task columns (todo/in_progress/review/done) keep the pre-existing `priority, due_date` system order, completely unaffected — computed in one query via per-branch `CASE WHEN` expressions, no post-query re-sort. New Cabinet notes place above the existing shelf via gap-based `COALESCE(MIN(sort_order), 0) - 1000` in both `create_note_internal` and `import_note_file` (mirrors the existing `templates.rs` `COALESCE(MAX(...), -1)` precedent). `reorder_notes` hardened with an explicit `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` transaction and single-scope validation (a batch spanning two different folders/projects, or mixing folder-scoped with bare-project-scoped notes, is rejected outright with zero writes). Fixed an incidental bug in `import_note_file` where an explicit SQL `NULL` bound for `status` violated the `notes.status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'cabinet'` constraint (was previously unreachable in tests; blocking for the new sort_order work in that exact function) — now inserts the literal `'cabinet'` string, which the rest of `notes.rs` already treats identically to NULL. A pre-existing, narrower version of the same bug in `create_note_internal` (reachable only if a caller explicitly passes `status: None`, which no current frontend call site does) is left as a documented, pinned-by-test known issue, out of scope for this PR. Also deleted the entire dead `showKanban` block in `NotesBrowser.svelte` (state var, stale drag handlers, markup, and its associated orphaned CSS) — a second, unused kanban implementation that predated the live Cabinet/Tasks folder-view columns. New spec section `docs/spec/core-data-model.md` §1.11 documents ordering semantics, the persistence model, the drag interaction surface (full event-propagation contract), sync behavior (last-writer-wins on concurrent reorders, accepted risk, no ticket), and backward compatibility (pre-existing notes at `sort_order=0`, cold-start order unaffected). (Relates to #2334)
  - **Fixed (follow-up):** the original `(project_id, folder_id)` reorder-scope validation was too strict — both aggregated Cabinet views this feature targets (the project Kanban board, and the folder view's Cabinet column when viewing a project with no folder selected) construct drag batches spanning *every* folder in the project by design, so nearly every real-world drag was rejected with "mixed-scope batch rejected." `reorder_notes_internal` (`notes.rs`) is now relaxed to `project_id`-only scoping — `folder_id` is free to vary within a batch; cross-project batches and unknown note_ids are still rejected outright, and the transaction/rollback wrapper is unchanged. For coherence, the gap-based new-note-on-top placement (`create_note_internal` and `import_note_file`) is also re-scoped from per-folder to project-level `MIN(sort_order)`, so a new note tops the entire project's Cabinet list — matching the aggregated views it's meant to appear at the top of — rather than only topping its own folder's subset while landing mid-list everywhere else. `docs/spec/core-data-model.md` §1.11.1/§1.11.2 updated to record project-global ordering as the ruled semantics, superseding the original per-folder scoping language. (Relates to #2334)
  - **Fixed (follow-up):** the reorder drop handler was on per-card `.cabinet-drag-wrap` elements (130px, card-sized), but the visual "insert here" indicator rendered at the seam/gap between cards — territory owned by the parent list container, not any card. Users aiming for the seam had their drop event bubble past the (non-existent) card-level handler straight to the column-level status-change handler, which silently no-op'd on its status-unchanged guard. The reorder path had never executed successfully. Drop handling is now moved to the list CONTAINER level in both views — `.folder-card-list` in `NotesBrowser.svelte`, `.column-content` in `KanbanBoard.svelte` — so the entire column surface, including every seam between cards, is a valid reorder target. New shared `src/lib/utils/dragReorderIndex.ts` (`resolveDropIndex`/`normalizeInsertIndex`/`cardRectsFromElements`) resolves the drop index from the pointer's Y position relative to the rendered card boundaries — one source of truth used by both the actual drop resolution and the drop-indicator's render position (previously per-card hover state, `is-drag-over` border; now a `.cabinet-drop-indicator` rendered by the container at the resolved slot). Mode disambiguation is relocated, not redesigned: the container-level handler still branches on `cabinetDragSourceId` (Cabinet-origin → reorder) vs. its absence (falls through to the existing `handleColumnDrop`/`handleDrop` status-change path), and `stopPropagation()` on the container handler still prevents the column-level handler from double-firing during a reorder (#2346 contract preserved). Per-card `cabinetDrop`/`cabinetCardDrop` handlers and their `ondrop`/`ondragover`/`ondragleave` bindings on `.cabinet-drag-wrap` are deleted entirely — `.cabinet-drag-wrap` now exists only as the drag *source* wrapper (`ondragend` only; drag start stays on `Card`'s own `ondragstart`). Also fixed a second defect: the column-level status-change handlers' status-unchanged early-return guard (`handleColumnDrop` in NotesBrowser, `handleDrop` in KanbanBoard) now logs `console.debug('[Cabinet] drop: status unchanged, no-op', {...})` before returning, so a silent no-op on a real user drag gesture is visible at debug level instead of producing zero console output. **DMG-gated:** the real `getBoundingClientRect()` → pixel-Y → resolved-index pipeline against genuinely laid-out cards cannot be exercised in jsdom (no layout engine) — covered by unit tests against synthetic `CardRect[]` input (fully DMG-free) plus real-DOM event-dispatch/bubbling tests proving the container is wired and receives drops on gap-only targets; the end-to-end "drop lands where the indicator shows, with real pixels" claim needs manual/DMG verification. (Relates to #2334)
- Added: **#2340** — Release pipeline mechanization. New `.github/workflows/release-publish.yml` triggers on any `v*` tag push and enforces the build-source rule with no skip mechanism: bare `vX.Y.Z` tags (public GitHub Releases, `--latest`) may only build from a commit already promoted to the protected `release` branch; `vX.Y.Z-test.N` tags (tester prereleases, `--prerelease`) may only build from `main`. The `guard-tag-branch` job checks commit ancestry via `git merge-base --is-ancestor` against both branches before any build step runs, so a mis-tagged push fails fast without wasting a self-hosted-runner build cycle. New `docs/release-runbook.md` documents the full pipeline: test-build flow (tag on `main`, Discord delivery since the repo is private and testers can't reach GitHub links), public-release flow (tag on `release` only, first one will be `v1.0.0`), and the hotfix path (`main` → Matt promotes via PR → `release` → new public Release). The existing 71 GitHub Releases (all bare `v0.68.x` tags, all built from `main` prior to this pipeline) are left untouched — repo is private, no external consumers to protect. Auto-updater (`updates.paneapp.ai`) is explicitly out of scope; the runbook notes it must publish the updater manifest alongside the DMG once auto-update ships, but no implementation lands here. (Relates to #2340, spec-skip: CI workflow, runbook, and release-pipeline infrastructure — no behavioral code changes)
- Added: **#2252** — Folder-view column collapse rails (PR C of #2180). Cabinet and Tasks columns in `NotesBrowser.svelte` each collapse independently to a 46px slim rail (`--fv-rail`) showing icon, vertical label, and count — all four combinations (both open, either alone, both collapsed) supported, matching the `folder-view-screens.jsx`/`folder-view.css` design spec's `RailCol` pattern. Distinct from the pre-existing kanban `doneCollapsed` pattern, which is unpersisted and icon-only. Collapse state persists per-folder via the existing `ai_settings` SQLite KV table and `get_ai_setting`/`set_ai_setting` Tauri commands (zero new Rust commands, zero new migrations) — keys `folder:{folder_id}:cabinet:collapsed` / `folder:{folder_id}:tasks:collapsed`, loaded on folder mount/switch and written immediately on toggle. When both columns are collapsed and a note panel is open, the panel's left anchor moves to 92px per the design. `delete_folder` now cleans up its folder's orphaned `ai_settings` collapse rows on deletion. `docs/spec/ui-layout.md` §3.2 rewritten to document the built SQLite/per-folder persistence, superseding the prior stub that incorrectly specified `localStorage`/global-scope keys per Matt's ruling. **Note: #2252 closes only on Matt's DMG test, not on merge.** (Relates to #2252)
- Added: **#2311** — "What should I upload?" help link on both upload screens (onboarding's Upload Documents screen and create-agent's Add context files screen), opening `https://paneapp.ai/system-files-creation` in the system browser via the shared `openExternalUrl` helper (Tauri `plugin-shell` `open()`, same pattern as `AuthScreen.svelte`/`ChatPanel.svelte`). Identical link text and visual treatment on both screens. Note: the target page 404s until built — accepted by Matt. (Relates to #2311)

Added reproducible 32/64/128/256/512px freedesktop hicolor assets so desktop shells can select a native resolution instead of scaling the old 256px maximum. macOS `.icns` and Windows `.ico` assets are unchanged. - Fixed: **#2379** — All Tasks view's editor-panel resize handle was ungrabbable at the visible divider. `.editor-resize` is `position: absolute; left: -2px`, resolved against its nearest positioned ancestor — but `.editor-panel` (its intended containing block) had no `position` declaration, so the handle escaped up to `.all-tasks-view` (`position: relative`, wraps the entire view) and rendered ~600px+ off from where users could click. Added `position: relative; /* Anchor for drag handle */` to `.editor-panel`, mirroring `KanbanBoard.svelte`'s `.kanban-editor-panel`, which already carries the identical declaration and comment. One-line CSS fix; handle element and `onmousedown`→`startEditorResize` wiring were already correct on both sides. (Relates to #2379, spec-skip: one-line CSS fix per Reed's diagnosis 2026-08-07, no behavioral spec change)
- Checklist and other in-note component clicks no longer close the note in Folder View. `NotesBrowser.svelte`'s click-outside-to-close handler previously lived on `.fv-stage`, the shared ancestor of both the card columns and the note editor overlay, relying on a `closest()` denylist (`.fv-note`, `.pane-card`, `.fv-collapse`, `.fv-railcol`) that did not reliably exclude clicks inside NodeView-mounted components like the checklist. The card columns are now wrapped in a new `.fv-cards-panel` element that carries the close-handler, structurally scoped off `.fv-stage` so the note editor (`.fv-note`) is a sibling, not a descendant — mirroring `KanbanBoard.svelte`'s `.kanban-left-panel`/`.kanban-editor-panel` sibling split, which is why Project View was never affected. `.fv-void` gets its own direct click handler to preserve click-outside-to-dismiss. (Relates to #2329)
- Fixed: **#2438 re-land** — Re-lands #2443 (search_notes returns project_id/folder_id + wiki-link fallback), which was merged, shipped as v0.68.93, then reverted after causing a nav lockup: every wiki-link click wrote `canvasState.view = 'notes_browser'` via a separate `navigateFn` call, then `noteService.selectNote()`'s own `canvasState.update()` unconditionally overwrote it back to `'note_editor'` ~20–25ms later — a confirmed double-write flip-flop that snapped every navigation back (see `docs/audits/2026-08-05-nav-lockup-diagnosis.md`). The backend half (`SearchResult.project_id`/`folder_id`, `search_notes_internal`'s SQL SELECT) ships unchanged from #2443. The frontend fix (§7 Option 2, single-writer, scoped): `navigateFn` is removed entirely from `wikiLinkNavigation.ts`; `noteService.selectNote()` gains an optional `contextOverride?: { projectId?, folderId? }` parameter, and only the exact-match wiki-link branch passes one (using the target note's own `project_id`/`folder_id`, resolved via the existing `getNoteRawFn` defense-in-depth fallback when the search row lacks them) — making `selectNote()`'s single `canvasState.update()` the ONLY write for a wiki-link navigation. Caller enumeration (all 6 call sites of `selectNote()`) confirmed this override is opt-in per call site, so none of `NoteList.svelte`, `NavPlayer.svelte`, `ChatSidebar.svelte`, `TasksModule.svelte`, or `NotesBrowser.svelte`'s own card-click path change behavior — `NotesBrowser.svelte`'s `selectProjectNote()` in particular was found to have real folder_id-contamination risk under unconditional (Option 2, unscoped) threading, which the opt-in override design avoids. Separately, `CanvasRenderer.svelte`'s `lastLoadedProjectId` reload guard is hardened (fix 3): a transient `notes_browser`→`note_editor` pass-through to the same note/project no longer resets the guard and forces a redundant note reload/remount — the guard now also tracks `lastLoadedNoteId` and only clears when the departing transition's context matches neither the last-loaded note nor project. (Relates to #2438, spec-skip: ordering fix per nav-lockup diagnosis §7, no behavioral decision)
- Wiki-link clicks now navigate fully to the target note's project and folder, not just open its content in place (#2438)
- Wiki-link picker now searches by title prefix instead of full-content FTS (typing [[D finds "Define Target Customer") — query construction moved server-side (`search_notes_internal`, gated by a `title_prefix` request flag) after a delta audit found the original frontend-built FTS5 syntax was being corrupted by the existing query re-quoting logic, returning zero results for every query
- Wiki-link picker no longer shows "No notes found" on bare [[ with no query
- Inline formatting (bold, italic, code, links, wiki-links) no longer lost on save when directly inside a paragraph or list item
- Fixed: **#2419 follow-up** — `search_notes` (Rust, `notes.rs:552-636`) now excludes system-scope notes from all search results: workshop-sentinel-scoped notes (`project_id = '__workshop__'`), `daily`/`memory`/`soul`/`rules` note types, and notes belonging to an `is_system` project or folder. Per Matt's ruling (2026-08-05), a user's manual search, the wiki-link picker, task search, and QuickSwitcher should never surface an agent's daily log, a project's Memory.md, or a Soul/Rules note — all four live consumers of `search_notes` were confirmed to not need system-scope results. Filter only — no schema change, no migration. (Relates to #2419, spec-skip: implements Matt's system-scope search ruling 2026-08-05, note-linking spec tracked in post-launch spec issue #2420)
- Fixed: **#2419 follow-up** — `api.searchNotes` now remaps the backend `note_id` field to `id`/`slug` before transforming results (`transformNoteMeta` expects `.id`; `search_notes`'s Rust `SearchResult` struct only ever returns `note_id`). This was the root cause of the wiki-link click-through phantom editor: clicking a wiki-link opened an empty editor with `get_note missing required key noteId` in the console, because `noteService.selectNote` received a note object with `id: undefined` and `slug: undefined`. Fix is scoped to `searchNotes` only (api.ts:250-253), following the existing donor pattern in `QuickSwitcher.svelte:67-68`; the shared `transformNoteMeta` mapper and `searchNotesByTitle` (wiki-link picker autocomplete, confirmed unaffected) are untouched. Wider blast radius fixed for free: `NoteList.svelte` and `CanvasRenderer.svelte` search-results clicks shared the same latent `note_id`→`id` mismatch and would have hit the identical phantom-editor bug once exercised. (Relates to #2419, spec-skip: field-mapping fix per QuickSwitcher donor pattern (QuickSwitcher.svelte:67-68), no behavioral decision)
- Wiki-link picker search now returns results (was silently failing due to wrong invoke parameter shape); link-click navigation opens matching notes or creates new ones with project/folder context in both folder and Kanban views (first time this subsystem has worked) (#2419)
- Calendar task creation now prompts for project/folder instead of silently failing (#2405)

- Wiki-link note creation now respects active folder context (was using bare project name) (#2405)
- Fixed: **#2377** — New notes created via the +New Note button in folder view now land in the currently-open folder (`$activeFolder`) instead of always being assigned to the alphabetically-first non-system folder. Previously, `NotesBrowser.svelte`'s `handleNewNote` ignored `$activeFolder` and always picked `nonSystemFolders[0]`, so opening "Test" and clicking +New Note still created the note in "General". The fix validates `$activeFolder.id` against the non-system folder list (pattern from `+page.svelte:450-452`) before using it, with fallback to alphabetical first. Separately, `KanbanBoard.svelte`'s `handleCreateNewTask` was picking `folders[0]` from an unsorted `listFolders` result — non-deterministic by DB insert order. Kanban-created notes now omit `folder_id` entirely, letting the backend's auto-assign in `create_note_internal` deterministically resolve to the project's General folder. (Relates to #2377, spec-skip: behavior ratified by Matt 2026-08-04 (folder view → active folder, project view → default folder), spec formalization tracked in #2406)
- Fixed: **#2378** — Status and Priority pill dropdowns in Project view (KanbanBoard) and All Tasks view were rendering off-screen. The `position: absolute` CSS overrides in `KanbanBoard.svelte` and `AllTasksView.svelte` negated the `position: fixed` positioning contract established by PR #2208, causing dropdowns to be displaced 200–500px off-viewport (handlers fired, DOM element existed, but nothing visible to the user). Both overrides removed; Editor.svelte's `position: fixed` now applies correctly in all three view contexts. (Relates to #2378)
- Fixed: **#2381** — `rename_note_file()` (`database.rs:965`) was the only note-file write path that never called `crate::watcher::suppress_path()` before touching disk. Every other write path (`atomic_write` for create/save, `delete_note_file` for delete) already suppressed correctly; renames were the one gap. Because a title-changing save renames the `.md` file *before* the DB's `file_path` column is updated, the file watcher's 2-second debounce could race the DB commit, see the new filename as an untracked external file, and import a duplicate note (titled with the filename slug, not the real title). Wired `suppress_path()` onto the rename destination path inside `rename_note_file()`, immediately before `PaneFs::rename()` — same suppress-before-write pattern already used at `file_ops.rs:135` and `database.rs:952`. Confirmed from `watcher.rs:148,196` that the watcher unconditionally discards all `EventKind::Remove(_)` events before they ever reach the debounce queue, so the *old* (source) path needs no suppression — only the destination. This is one root function with five call sites, all now covered: title rename (`notes.rs:765`), folder/project moves (`notes.rs:665` via `relocate_note_file`), and all rollback-on-error rename paths (`notes.rs:774`, `notes.rs:810`, `notes.rs:2324`). New integration test (`test_2381_rename_note_file_suppresses_destination_before_disk_write`, `database.rs`) exercises the real function against a real filesystem and asserts against the real `SUPPRESSED_PATHS` set; removing the `suppress_path()` call flips it red. `docs/spec/file-system.md` §2A.3's stale `NOT BUILT` status is corrected to reflect that the suppression set is built and in active use, and §2A.8's `rename_note` checklist item is checked off. Out of scope (per audit): the title-slug dedup-check bug (#2390) and any DB-lock/watcher-connection coordination redesign — this PR closes only the suppression gap. (Relates to #2381)
- Fixed: folder view layout bounce when clicking between cards with a column collapsed (#2335). `CanvasRenderer.svelte`'s `note_editor` reload guard (originally shipped in #2380, then reverted in #2384 after Reed's audit found it compared against the wrong reference point) now compares `context.noteId` against `$activeNote`'s current id instead of a component-local `lastLoadedNoteId` bookkeeping var. `noteService.selectNote()` always sets `$activeNote` to the just-clicked note *before* firing its `canvasState.update()` echo, so by the time that echo reaches `CanvasRenderer`'s `$effect`, `$activeNote` already matches — the redundant `loadDataForView('note_editor', ...)` call (which set `isLoading = true` and fully unmounted/remounted `<NotesBrowser/>` on every single card click, not just same-note re-selection) is now correctly skipped for every genuine card-to-card transition, not only for re-selecting the currently-open note. `lastLoadedProjectId` is kept (project membership isn't tracked by `$activeNote`) so cross-project switches and view-away-and-back still force a real reload. (Relates to #2335, Relates to #2370, spec-skip: runtime fix — corrected guard comparison per Reed audit of #2380, no architectural change)
- Fixed: **#2335** — Added a `selectSeq`-style monotonic counter guard (`collapseLoadSeq`) to the collapse-load `$effect` in `NotesBrowser.svelte`, mirroring the existing pattern in `noteService.ts`. Previously the effect's two `get_ai_setting` reads (for `cabinetCollapsed`/`tasksCollapsed`) had no sequencing: on a rapid scope change (e.g. folder A → folder B in quick succession), an older/slower `Promise.all` resolve from folder A could land after folder B's own resolve, silently overwriting folder B's just-loaded collapse state with stale folder-A values. The guard captures a `mySeq` snapshot before each async read and discards the resolve (success or error path) if `collapseLoadSeq` has since advanced. Reed's trace confirmed the effect's `lastCollapseLoadScopeId` memo guard is correctly string-compared and churn-immune on the card-click path — this fix closes a distinct async-race gap, correctness-positive regardless of whether it fully explains the reported rail-bounce symptom (see PR body for full honest-note contingency). (Relates to #2335, spec-skip: selectSeq guard on async collapse-load reads — behavioral hardening, no spec-covered domain change)

- Fixed: **#2252** — Three collapse-rail bugs found during the DMG pass on #2320 (bugfix, not a spec change — spec was already updated in #2320): **(1, LAUNCH-BLOCKING)** Clicking a Cabinet/Tasks collapse button (`.fv-collapse` header buttons and `.fv-railcol` rail buttons, all 6 click sites) closed the currently-open note. Root cause: the click bubbled up to `.fv-stage`'s click-outside handler, whose exclusion list checked only `.fv-note`/`.pane-card` and never `.fv-collapse`/`.fv-railcol`. Fixed both ways: `toggleCabinetCollapsed`/`toggleTasksCollapsed` now take the `MouseEvent` and call `e.stopPropagation()` first (all 6 existing `onclick={...}` bindings pick this up automatically, no binding changes needed), and the `.fv-stage` exclusion list is widened to also exclude `.fv-collapse`/`.fv-railcol` as defense-in-depth. **(2)** `set_ai_setting` had zero unconditional logging (unlike its `get_ai_setting` sibling, which logs every call), so the collapse-state SQLite write was firing correctly but invisible in terminal output — this cost a full diagnosis cycle during the DMG pass, since the save looked like it wasn't happening at all. Added an unconditional `eprintln!("[SET_AI_SETTING] key=... value=...")` (credential keys redacted) at the top of the command wrapper in `notes.rs`, matching `get_ai_setting`'s pattern. **(3)** The collapse-state load `$effect` in `NotesBrowser.svelte` was already correctly scoped to `$activeFolder`/`$activeProject` only, but upstream store-reference churn on note navigation (separate issue #2324) reassigns those stores to new object references with the same `.id`, re-triggering the effect on every note open/close. Added a `lastCollapseLoadScopeId` identity-memo guard that compares the resolved scope *id* (not object reference) and no-ops when unchanged, without needing to chase down every upstream reassignment site. Test-layer note: Bug 1's DOM-bubbling reproduction is covered by a real jsdom click-dispatch test against the `.fv-stage` exclusion list (Option B); it cannot independently verify the `stopPropagation()` call inside `toggleCabinetCollapsed`/`toggleTasksCollapsed` (Option A) since that requires the full Tauri window context per this test file's existing house pattern — Matt's DMG re-test gates Bug 1 regardless of test coverage. (Relates to #2252, spec-skip: bugfix for existing feature shipped in #2320, spec already updated in that PR, spec-covered-by: #2320)
- Fixed: **#2308** — Onboarding finish failed to persist the workshop transcript. `Onboarding.svelte`'s `saveAndComplete` transcript-save block called `invoke('save_chat_message'/'load_chat_messages')` directly with the wrong argument shape (`{ projectId, role, content }` / `{ projectId, limit }`), omitting the `threadId` key `save_chat_message` requires and the `sessionId` key `load_chat_messages` requires — every save/verify call failed silently (`invalid args threadId for command save_chat_message: missing required key threadId` / same for `sessionId`/`load_chat_messages`). Fixed by routing through the shared `api.ts` wrappers (`getActiveSession`, `sendChatMessage`, `saveAssistantMessage`, `getChatMessages`) that every other chat-persistence call site (`ChatSidebar.svelte`) already uses, which resolve a real thread via `getActiveSession` and pass the correct keys. Checked `AgentCreateOverlay.svelte` for the same pattern — it has no transcript-save calls at all (its `handleReviewFinish` writes SOUL/MEMORY and purges workshop notes but never persists chat messages), so no fix was needed there. Note: `save_chat_message` takes `threadId` while `load_chat_messages` takes `sessionId` for the same underlying thread/session concept — flagged as a two-lists naming smell but intentionally NOT renamed on the Rust side in this PR (param-fix only). (Relates to #2308)
- Fixed: **#2309** — Create-agent workshop AI refused to edit its own Memory draft. `build_messages_with_context` gated the Memory-edit permission on the global `ai_settings.onboarding_completed` flag, which is already `true` by the time the create-agent workshop runs — so the AI always got the strict "Memory is append-only via the pipeline" instruction and refused direct edits to the workshop's sentinel-scoped Memory note. Replaced with a backend-derived `is_workshop_session` check (`ai/commands.rs`): resolves `context.noteId` against the `notes` table and tests whether that note's own `project_id` is the sentinel `WORKSHOP_SCOPE_ID`, not a frontend-trusted flag. Workshop sessions now get the permissive sentinel-scoped-only instruction; every normal chat context (including post-onboarding chat) keeps the strict append-only protection per INVARIANTS §5. Also stopped injecting the main agent's real SOUL.md/IDENTITY.md/USER.md/TOOLS.md/AGENTS.md/MEMORY.md into workshop context (previously loaded unconditionally off `is_main = 1`) — workshop context now comes only from the workshop's own notes; intentional consequence (ruled by Matt): the workshop assistant loses main-agent knowledge of the user for the duration of the workshop. Wired the previously-dead `context.navigationContext` param (`WorkshopReview.svelte`'s "ONBOARDING MODE" hint, silently dropped by the Rust backend) into the system prompt as an informational hint. This narrows but does not close #2310 — persona-quality verification on the DMG build is separate. (Relates to #2309)
- Fixed: **#2302** — `update_note`, `execute_append_to_note`, and `purge_note` all unconditionally called `write_note_content`/`delete_note_file` (which route through `note_policy_path`) on sentinel-scope workshop notes with empty `file_path`, crashing with `"note path must be under Projects/ or .pane/system/: "` on second-save, append, or purge of a workshop note (Memory/Soul during create-agent or onboarding). Added the same `file_path.is_empty()` DB-only guard `execute_edit_note` already had (#2294) to all three sites. Also fixed `AgentCreateOverlay.svelte`/`Onboarding.svelte` silently swallowing `purge_note` failures via a bare `.catch()` — both now `console.error` so a failed purge is visible instead of vanishing. Does NOT claim to fix #2303 (separate onboarding silent-edit bug, still open pending repro). (Relates to #2302)
- Fixed: rust-tests push-to-main cascade skip that silently disabled post-merge test runs since April (#2291)
- Fixed: **#2277** — Context read-path vs. written-file mismatch. `build_messages_with_context` no longer reads the global `~/Pane/.pane/ai/soul.md` and `ai/workspace-memory.md` files, which contaminated every agent's prompt with whoever's personality/memory was onboarded or saved last. Per-agent `SOUL.md`/`MEMORY.md` under `.pane/system/{UUID}/` (already read via the §24 block) are now the sole source. When a per-agent `SOUL.md` is empty or missing (e.g. a freshly created "Just Start Chatting" agent's skeleton file), the §24 read path falls back to the same hardcoded default personality string the global read used to provide, so new agents no longer get a blank personality. Also unified the `"rules"` note-type resolver: `database.rs`'s `get_system_note_from_agents` now maps `"rules"` to `AGENTS.md` (was `RULES.md`), matching `edit_note`/`load_system_notes`/the §24 read block, which have always used `AGENTS.md` for the "Rules" slot — fixing a bug where `edit_note("rules")` and the prompt-pipeline read resolved to two different files. (Relates to #2277, spec-skip: spec amendment PR #2285 covers this work (pending merge); this PR adds a status note to docs/spec/ai-integration.md for the CORE_BEHAVIORAL gate, spec-covered-by: #2285 (pending merge — ADR-0060, §24.10.1a; this PR also touches docs/spec/ directly))
