(Relates to #993)
- §28 (ai-integration.md): new "Settings — Provider Configuration & Connection Status" section. Specifies the Settings AI-tab internal-provider Ollama probe — on-load not-tested default (no assumed success, #1627), `ollama_probe_two_step` reuse with no raw fetch, three `error_class` inline states (unreachable / no_models / tags_failed, #1628), and the not-tested INVARIANT. Probe trigger: on-tab-open when internal=ollama + on-demand Test. Mirrors onboarding §6.4.4. Known gap flagged: primary-provider Ollama path uses raw fetch, future §28.2. (Relates to #1627, #1628)
- §4.5.8 (new): provider-agnostic tool-call handling — native-first parsing for every provider with a guarded text-fallback that fires only when native returns zero calls; removes the `is_openclaw` gate; formalizes Ollama native tool-call parsing requirement. ADR-0046 overturns §4.3's "skip text parsing entirely" stance (#1586 launch-blocking; Phase 3).
- §22C.12.4 (new): reconnect behavior for the chat/SSE path on OC topology — state machine (Idle/Attempting/Reconnecting/Failed), passive "Reconnecting…" indicator that does not block input, carry-forward of the 1s→30s backoff curve and 5-retry budget from §22C.4.1 + §22C.12.1, with ±10% jitter added to prevent thundering-herd on gateway recovery; mid-stream disconnect re-sends original message (no Last-Event-ID resume, no partial-result splicing); explicit out-of-scope for sync paths, Settings "Save & Test", and pairing exchange; sequential handoff to §22C.12.3 on budget exhaustion (#945 launch-blocking; Phase 3; sibling to #946).
- §22C.12.3 (new): client-facing error categories for OC-topology gateway calls — four codes (gateway_unreachable, gateway_auth_failed, gateway_cert_mismatch, gateway_connection_failed) with locked user-facing copy and a structured backend/frontend contract; closes the single-regex collapse identified in the 2026-06-22 Phase 3 scope audit (#946 launch-blocking; Phase 3).
- §22C.11A.5 (sync.md): formalized `gateway_version` as a required field in the `PairResponse` wire contract (#1508). The gateway already emits it (`CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, post-#1461) and Pane discards it; this makes Pane's dependence contractual — gateway MUST emit the semver string on every 200 `PairResponse`, Pane MAY reject a response lacking it. Supports shipped Pane/Gateway version-skew detection (the two ship as independent DMGs and can run mismatched). No protocol change — the field is already on the wire and test-pinned. The floor value, comparison logic, warn-vs-block behavior, and version storage are Pane-side implementation (#1508), deliberately NOT part of the wire contract. Spec lands before the #1508 code fix cites it via `spec-covered-by:`. (#1508)
- §22C.8.1a (sync.md): stale `pane_gateway_token` / `pane_gateway_url` row cleanup (#1499). #1167 stopped reading/writing these keys but left any pre-existing `ai_settings` rows orphaned; a one-time migration copies `pane_gateway_token` → `api_key` only where `api_key` is absent/empty (never overwrites — `api_key` is authoritative post-#1167), then deletes the row; `pane_gateway_url` is deleted outright (only ever written empty, no data to preserve). Spec invariant: #1499 runs BEFORE #1008's credential-to-keychain migration, so no `keychain_migration_v1` flag-clear is needed (sequencing eliminates the trap rather than patching it). No live installs carry these rows yet — this closes the gap before anyone hits it. Spec lands before the #1499 code fix cites it via `spec-covered-by:`. (#1499)
- ADR-0044 Addendum A + ADR-0004 key-storage update: the sync master key (Argon2id-derived, encrypts all synced changesets/files/notifications) moves from `~/Pane/.pane/sync_key.bin` into the OS keychain (account `sync_master_key`), under ADR-0044's credential-storage contract (#1498). Adopts ADR-0044 Decisions 2–5 in full — copy-then-clear with read-back confirm, DB migration flag (`migration_flags` table, same mechanism as ADR-0044), no plaintext fallback post-migration, backup enumeration. The only difference from the AI credentials is the migration source: a file (`sync_key.bin`) instead of a DB field. `delete_master_key()` post-migration deletes the keychain entry, not the file; `get_known_keychain_accounts()` adds `sync_master_key`. config.json redaction / shared-field split / apiKeyRef are N/A (no config.json mirror, no conflation). Spec lands before the #1498 code fix cites it via `spec-covered-by:`. (#1498)
- ADR-0044 (new) + `ai-integration.md` / `sync.md` §22C / `file-system.md` §2.3C: keychain credential storage contract for #1008. The three AI credentials — primary provider key, OC gateway token (the conflated `api_key` field, split per #1167 history), and Smart Features internal key — move from plaintext `ai_settings` + `config.json` mirror into the OS keychain (accounts `ai_provider_key` / `ai_gateway_token` / `ai_internal_key`). Migration is copy-then-clear with read-back confirmation, idempotent across launches, never clearing DB plaintext on a failed keychain write. config.json redaction is normative: `apiKeyRef` becomes a non-secret sentinel and an aiSettings dump blocklist excludes credential keys. Backup keychain-export adds the three fixed accounts. Post-migration keychain miss = "not configured" (no plaintext fallback). Rollback yields non-functional AI — accepted PRE-LAUNCH ONLY, flagged as a launch-blocking revisit. Spec lands before the #1008 code fix cites it via `spec-covered-by:`. (#1008)
- §6.3.3 (onboarding.md): add `tags_failed` row to Ollama probe routing table — `/api/version` 200 + `/api/tags` non-200 routes to custom-endpoint screen (Step 3). Relates to #997.
- **#999 — Ollama model picker no longer shows `:latest` suffix in the dropdown.** `ollamaModels` is now `{ id: string; display: string }[]`; `id` holds the raw model name (sent to the Ollama API unchanged) and `display` strips the `:latest` suffix for the label. Non-latest tags (e.g. `llama3:8b`) are shown verbatim. The list is sorted alphabetically by display name per §6.3.3 step 2. (`spec-covered-by: onboarding.md §6.3.3 step 2`, `Relates to #999`)
- **#1586 (Fix A) — Ollama now sends tools in the request body and parses native tool calls from the response.** `stream_ollama` gains a `tools: &[ToolDef]` parameter; when non-empty the tools array is serialized into the Ollama `/api/chat` request body using the OpenAI-compatible format Ollama expects (`{"type":"function","function":{...}}`). On the `done: true` NDJSON chunk, `message.tool_calls` is extracted as a complete block (no delta accumulation needed) via the new `parse_ollama_tool_calls` helper, which handles both object-valued and JSON-string-valued `arguments` fields and synthesises a call_id when Ollama omits the `id` field. Both `stream_ollama` call sites in `commands.rs` now forward the active `tools` slice. Previously `ollama.rs:375` returned `Ok((full_text, vec![]))` unconditionally; tool calls from Ollama models are no longer silently dropped. (`Relates to #1586`, `spec-covered-by: #1613 (§4.5.8 provider-agnostic tool-call handling)`, `spec-skip: spec already landed in PR #1613`)
- **#1586b — Text-fallback tool-call parsing is now provider-agnostic per §4.5.8.** The `is_openclaw` gate on the text-fallback branch in `commands.rs` has been removed; the empty-result guard (`tool_calls.is_empty()`) is preserved as the §4.5.8 INVARIANT ensuring native-first, single-fire behavior. Models on OpenRouter, Anthropic, or Ollama that emit tool calls as fenced or bare JSON in their response text will now have those calls extracted and executed, instead of being silently dropped. The `call_id` prefix for text-parsed calls is renamed from `openclaw_text_` to `text_tool_` (provider-neutral). No downstream pattern-matchers on the old prefix exist. (`spec-covered-by: #1613 (§4.5.8 provider-agnostic tool-call handling)`, `spec-skip: spec already landed in PR #1613`, `Relates to #1586`)
- **Test:** Pin typo-tolerance contract — wrong pairing code preserves active slot (#965)
- **#946 — Gateway error states now render structured, action-oriented copy per §22C.12.3.** `streamManager.ts` replaces the single regex collapse with `getGatewayErrorMessage(errorCode, errText)` that returns locked copy for all four gateway error categories: `gateway_unreachable` (gateway not running), `gateway_auth_failed` (token expired), `gateway_cert_mismatch` (TLS fingerprint changed), and `gateway_connection_failed` (both machines reachable but connection failed). Non-OC providers without a structured `error_code` fall back to the previous regex heuristic. `ChatPanel.svelte` shows a **Re-pair** button (navigates to Settings) instead of **Settings** when `gatewayErrorCode === 'gateway_auth_failed'`, directing users to the re-pair flow. Completes the chat-resilience trio: #1312 (timeout bounds) → #945 (auto-reconnect) → #946 (error copy). (`spec-covered-by: #1599 (§22C.12.3 client-facing error categories)`, `Relates to #946`)
- **#945 — Chat/SSE path now auto-reconnects with exponential backoff on transient gateway errors.** When a chat completion request to the gateway fails with a retryable error (`gateway_unreachable`, `gateway_connection_failed`), Pane retries up to 5 times using the §22C.12.4 backoff curve (1s → 2s → 4s → 8s → 30s, ±10% jitter) before surfacing a final error. Hard-fail errors (`gateway_auth_failed` on 401/403, `gateway_cert_mismatch` on TLS fingerprint mismatch) skip the retry loop and surface immediately. A passive "Reconnecting…" banner appears near the input area during backoff; the input field remains editable but Send is disabled until the retry succeeds or the budget is exhausted. On budget exhaustion, a structured §22C.12.3 `error_code` is emitted for #946 frontend copy rendering. Mid-stream disconnect discards partial responses (no partial splicing). New `chat-retries` in-memory counter (distinct from `ws-reconnects` per §22C.14) exposed via `get_chat_retry_count` Tauri command. (`spec-covered-by: #1603 (§22C.12.4 reconnect behavior contract)`, `Relates to #945`)
- **#1312 — Reduce blocking gateway client timeouts to bound UI hang on unreachable gateway.** `build_gateway_client_blocking_with_cert` previously used 30s connect + 300s total timeout — values inherited from reqwest defaults, never tuned for Pane's LAN/Tailscale gateway topology. All sync operations through this client (push, pull, initial import, agent fetch) send small payloads (KB-scale markdown/config files) and have no need for 5-minute total timeouts. Reduced to 5s connect + 30s total. Worst-case user-visible stall on Settings save now ≤30s (was ≤300s). Background thread worst case also bounded proportionally. Audit: `docs/audits/2026-06-22-1312-blocking-client-scope.md`. (`spec-skip: timeout tuning; no new behavior contract — values are implementation detail, not spec'd`, `Relates to #1312`)
- **#1553 — Agentic loop now truncates large tool-call arguments from prior iterations in outbound requests (§4.5.7), preventing context bloat that caused oversized request bodies.** Large argument payloads (> 1024 bytes) in prior-iteration assistant tool-call messages are replaced with `{"_truncated": "<N> bytes omitted"}` in the request copy before each provider dispatch. Canonical history is never mutated. The transform runs once pre-dispatch (single site, all providers covered), producing a JSON-object placeholder valid on both sides of the §29 OpenAI/Anthropic dual-provider boundary. Failed-call arguments and current-iteration tool calls are never truncated. (`spec-covered-by: #1590`, `Relates to #1553, #1407`)
- **#1007 — Backup rotation now removes all sidecar files (_install-uuid.json, _keychain.json, _metadata.json) alongside the .db and _system.tar.gz. Previously only the .db and tar were cleaned up, leaving orphaned credential and metadata files past their retention window.** Introduced `SIDECAR_SUFFIXES` constant as the single source of truth for sidecar enumeration; `delete_backup_and_sidecars()` loops over it so future sidecar additions can't reintroduce this bug. (`spec-skip: internal backup behavior, no spec contract exists for rotation cleanup`, `Relates to #1007`)
- **#1582 — `create_note` and `create_folder` now reject absent `project_id` at the cross-project write guard, not downstream in executor validation.** Previously, if a model omitted `project_id` for these tools (despite it being `required` in the schema), the guard's `_ => Ok(())` arm passed silently and the executor returned a generic `"project_id required"` error — giving the model no security-aware guidance and a nudge to supply any project ID on retry. The new `create_note | create_folder` arm in `check_cross_project_write_permission` rejects absent `project_id` fail-closed with `"project_id is required for X; use the session project ID"`. The redundant inline project_id check in `execute_single_tool` is removed; all validation now lives in the guard. Home agent (session_project_id=None) is unaffected. (`spec-skip: spec note added to §4A.4 in this PR`, `Relates to #1582`)
- **#1571 — Project-scoped AI chats now correctly reject writes to notes/folders in other projects per §4A.4.** Previously only `create_note`/`create_folder` were guarded; `edit_note`, `append_to_note`, `delete_note`, `set_status`, `set_priority`, `create_subtask`, `move_note`, and `move_folder` bypassed the cross-project write check because they use `note_id`/`folder_id` instead of `project_id`. Added `check_cross_project_write_permission` guard that resolves the owning project from the DB for note_id/folder_id-based tools and rejects cross-project writes. Fail-closed: unresolvable IDs are rejected, not skipped. Home agent (session_project_id=None) is unaffected — writes everywhere as designed. (`spec-skip: enforcement of existing §4A.4 spec guarantee, already marked BUILT v0.17.61`, `Relates to #1571`)
- **#1572 — Active project chat context now injects the project's own Memory.md per ADR-0020, instead of the agent's home memory.** The `load_system_notes` closure in `build_context_prompt` iterated soul/rules/memory via `database::get_system_note` for all three. On post-§24 installs, `get_system_note` ignores `project_id` and returns agent workspace files — meaning every project's chat context was injected with the agent's home MEMORY.md instead of the project's own Memory.md. Fixed by extracting `load_project_memory_for_context` (ADR-0020 canonical path) and routing `note_type == "memory"` through it inside the closure; soul and rules remain on the agent-level path (correct). (`spec-skip: bug fix aligning context builder to existing spec (ADR-0020 canonical project memory path)`, `spec-covered-by: #801 (ADR-0020 canonical project memory path, merged, touched docs/spec/memory-pipeline.md)`, `Relates to #1572`)
- **#1568 — Home-screen project index now shows each project's own memory preview per ADR-0020, instead of repeating agent memory across all projects.** The preview builder in `build_context_prompt` previously called `database::get_system_note` per-project, which on post-§24 installs ignores `project_id` and returns the agent's workspace MEMORY.md. Replaced with `get_project_memory_preview` helper (extracted for testability) that calls `notes::get_project_memory_impl` — ADR-0020 canonical path. Filter and truncation logic unchanged. (`spec-skip: bug fix aligning preview builder to existing spec (ADR-0020 canonical project memory path)`, `spec-covered-by: #801 (ADR-0020 canonical project memory path, merged, touched docs/spec/memory-pipeline.md)`, `Relates to #1568`)
- **#1565 — AI `read_project_memory` tool now reads from canonical project path (`Projects/{name}/Memory.md`) per ADR-0020, instead of returning agent's home memory.** `execute_read_project_memory` previously called `database::get_system_note` which on post-§24 installs routes through `get_system_note_from_agents`, ignoring `project_id` entirely and returning the agent's workspace MEMORY.md. Fixed by replacing the `get_system_note` call with `notes::get_project_memory_impl`, which resolves the project name and reads from `Projects/{name}/Memory.md` — the canonical path per ADR-0020. (`spec-covered-by: #801 (ADR-0020 canonical project memory path, merged, touched docs/spec/memory-pipeline.md)`, `Relates to #1565`)
- **#1415 — Project memory panel now reads from canonical path (`Projects/{name}/Memory.md`) per ADR-0020, ignoring stale `file_path` in notes table.** `get_project_memory` previously used the `file_path` column from the notes table to locate and load memory content. On installs with legacy rows whose `file_path` still pointed to a pre-#470 path (e.g. `Projects/{name}/AI/Memory.md`), this returned empty or wrong content. The function now ignores `file_path` entirely: it queries the project name, computes the canonical path as `Projects/{name}/Memory.md` (ADR-0020), and reads from there. The DB row is still used for `note_id` and `word_count`. (`spec-covered-by: ADR-0020 (canonical project memory path is Projects/{name}/Memory.md, merged in PR #803)`, `Relates to #1415`)
- **#1557 — Gateway SSE stream no longer drops mid-run during OC tool execution (§22C.4.1.1).** The gateway's `streaming_idle_timeout_secs` timer previously watched only HTTP SSE bytes. During OC tool execution, no SSE bytes are emitted regardless of how busy OC is internally — causing a silent 60-second timeout to fire and kill healthy connections (observed: connection dropped 20 ms before the run finished, #1407). Fix: the idle deadline is now correlated with the gateway↔OC WebSocket channel. `OcClient` records the timestamp of every received WS message (Text, Ping, Pong) in a shared atomic. When the HTTP SSE deadline fires, the chat proxy checks the WS age: if the WS was active within `idle_timeout_secs`, the deadline is extended; only when **both** channels have been silent does the timeout fire. The 30-second WS ping cycle (§22C.4.2) provides the liveness signal during tool runs. Dead connections (OC crash / WS drop) are still detected within `idle_timeout_secs + ~30s`. Gateway-only change; no OC or Pane-client modifications. Also removes the temporary `GATEWAY_STREAMING_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS=300` override from the launchd plist — the 60-second default is correct and safe now that WS correlation is in place. (`spec-skip: spec already landed in PR #1558 — §22C.4.1.1 streaming-proxy idle deadline contract`, `spec-covered-by: #1558`, `Relates to #1557, #1407`)
- **#1407 — Raise `/v1/chat/completions` body limit from 1 MiB to 8 MiB.** Agentic loops that re-echo tool-call content across multi-turn sessions were producing request bodies in the 1–5 MiB range, exceeding the previous 1 MiB `DefaultBodyLimit` and returning 413 with no retry. Limit raised to 8 MiB (consistent with `MAX_BUFFERED_BYTES = 50 MiB`; headroom below sync-push at 10 MiB). Session message limit (`/v1/sessions/:id/messages`) unchanged at 1 MiB. Spec table §22C.13 updated in the same PR to document the chat completions limit. (`Relates to #1407, #1553`)
- **#1546 — `sync_re_import` UPDATE path now sets `is_main=1` on OC main agent (collision provider-switch fix).** The overwrite-in-place branch of `sync_re_import` was updating `name`, `slug`, and `updated_at` but omitting `is_main` and `role`. After a provider switch (OC→OR→OC), the demotion guard correctly set the OR agent to `is_main=0`, but the UPDATE never promoted the OC agent to `is_main=1`, leaving zero `is_main=1` rows until the next app restart. Added `is_main=?5, role=?6` to the UPDATE SET clause; parameters bound identically to the INSERT path (`1i64`/`"main"` for main agents, `0i64`/`"sub"` for sub-agents). The demotion block already runs first within the same transaction, satisfying the partial unique index constraint. (`spec-skip: spec already landed in PR #1529`, `spec-covered-by: #1529 (ADR-0045 D2 / §24.7A — demote-then-promote contract for is_main selection)`, `Relates to #1546, #1495, #1492, #1527`)
- **#1495 — Chat header no longer shows stale agent display name after provider switch.** `ChatPanel.svelte` was only refreshing `mainAgentName` on `pane-agent-renamed` and `pane-onboarding-complete` events. When the user switched providers (OC→other or other→OC), the main agent changed via `restore_non_oc_main` / `reimport_oc_agents` but no event was dispatched to ChatPanel. Added a new `pane-agent-switched` custom event dispatched from all four provider-switch call sites in `Settings.svelte` (`confirmCascadeAndSave`, `handleTestConnection`, `handleSaveAi`, `confirmReimport`). ChatPanel listens for it alongside the existing events and re-runs `loadMainAgentName()`. (`spec-skip: undocumented UI behavior — chat header refresh not spec'd`, `spec-covered-by: N/A`, `Relates to #1495, #1534`)
- **#1539 — Crash-recovery INSERT now skips non-UUID directories (§24.2 guard).** `verify_agents_integrity_with_path` was iterating all folders under `.pane/system/` and inserting any directory containing a `SOUL.md` into `ai_agents`, including non-UUID legacy or stale directories. Added a 32-char hex UUID format check (matching the guard already in `upsert_agent`) between the skip-list block and the DB existence query: non-UUID folders emit a warning and are skipped, preventing bad `workspace_path` values from entering the DB. Secondary fix: changed `source = 'filesystem'` to `source = 'recovered'` in the recovery INSERT to match §24.10's specified value. (`spec-skip: spec already covers this — §24.2 + §24.10`, `spec-covered-by: §24.2, §24.10 (workspace_path invariant already requires UUID for all insert paths including recovery)`, `Relates to #1539, #1535, #1534`)
- **#1535 — Onboarding no longer writes agent display name as `workspace_path`.** `Onboarding.svelte` was passing `workspace_path: agentName` to `upsert_agent`, creating `.pane/system/Bill/` instead of the required UUID folder. Removed the field from the frontend call; the backend UUID fallback in `agents.rs` now always fires. Added a server-side guard that rejects any `workspace_path` value that is not a 32-char uppercase hex UUID, enforcing the §24.2 invariant for all callers. (`spec-covered-by: #1536 (§24.2, §24.10)`, `Relates to #1535`)
- **#1492 — Fix: `restore_non_oc_main` wired to correct call paths.** The restore call was placed in `handleSaveAi`, which is unreachable on OC→OR switch (Save button dispatches to `handleTestConnection` when `provider !== 'openclaw'`). Moved to `confirmCascadeAndSave` (cascade-warning path) and `handleTestConnection` (no-cascade path). Existing backend logic unchanged. (`spec-covered-by: ADR-0045 / §24.5.5`, `Relates to #1492`)
- **#1492 + #1527 — Auto-restore main agent on provider switch away from OpenClaw + single-main normalization.** Switching away from OpenClaw now re-promotes the prior non-OC main agent (`oc_agent_id IS NULL`) via a single demote-then-promote transaction (ADR-0045 D4). OC-native installs (no non-OC agent) correctly no-op. Additionally, `sync_re_import` now normalizes to one `is_main = 1` row before processing: a pre-flight `SELECT COUNT(*)` assertion demotes stranded non-OC mains, and a demotion guard on the overwrite-in-place UPDATE path ensures the OC main agent always holds `is_main`. (`spec-covered-by: ADR-0045 / §24.5.5`, `Relates to #1492, #1527`)
- **#1508 — Pane/Gateway version-skew detection.** Pane now reads `gateway_version` from the PairResponse on pair, logs it, and stores it in `ai_settings`. If the gateway is below `MIN_GATEWAY_VERSION` (0.2.1), Pane shows a non-blocking warning: "Your Pane Gateway is out of date. Download the latest from paneapp.ai." Pairing always completes — warn only, never block. CI guard (`scripts/check-gateway-version-floor.sh`) fails the build if the gateway version advances past the floor without a floor bump. (`spec-covered-by: #1512`, `Relates to #1508`)
- **#1008 — Complete keychain backup enumeration: add `supabase_access_token` and `supabase_refresh_token`.** `get_known_keychain_accounts()` now includes both Supabase session-token accounts written by `save_auth_session` / legacy migration. Re-login-recoverable, but included for backup completeness so a restored machine retains an active session. (`spec-skip: trivial backup completeness fix, no architectural change`, `spec-covered-by: #1500 (ADR-0044 Decision 4 — backup enumerates all known keychain accounts)`, `Relates to #1008`)
- **#1499 — Clean up stale `pane_gateway_token` / `pane_gateway_url` rows.** One-time schema migration (v64→v65, §22C.8.1a) clears the two `ai_settings` orphan rows left by #1167. `pane_gateway_token` is copied to `api_key` only when `api_key` is absent or empty (`api_key` is authoritative post-#1167 — never overwritten on divergence); the row is then deleted. `pane_gateway_url` is deleted outright (only ever written as an empty string; no data to preserve). Combined migration arms extend v62→v65 and v63→v65. 5 new migration tests covering all spec-enumerated cases. (`spec-skip: code implementation of already-landed spec`, `spec-covered-by: #1505 (§22C.8.1a stale pane_gateway_token cleanup)`, `Relates to #1499`)
- **#1498 — Move sync master key to OS keychain (ADR-0044 Addendum A).** The Argon2id-derived sync master key (encrypts all synced changesets, file blobs, and notifications) migrates from `~/Pane/.pane/sync_key.bin` into the OS keychain (`sync_master_key`, service `com.threelane.pane`). Migration is idempotent across 6 enumerated states (A–F) with copy-then-clear and read-back confirmation. Post-migration: `load_master_key()` is keychain-only; a keychain miss returns `None` — never a silent file fallback (Decision 5). State F (flag set, file present, keychain absent) deletes the stale file without re-adopting it. `delete_master_key()` post-migration targets the keychain entry only; migration flag is preserved. `store_master_key()` post-migration writes directly to keychain. `get_known_keychain_accounts()` adds `sync_master_key` for backup export. DB schema bumped v63→v64 (`migration_flags` table). 17 regression tests (9 migration states + 8 keystore unit tests). (`spec-skip: code implementation of already-landed spec`, `spec-covered-by: #1503 (ADR-0044 Addendum A — sync master key keychain contract)`, `Relates to #1498`)
- **#1008 — Move AI credentials to OS keychain (ADR-0044).** Three credentials (primary provider key, OC gateway token, Smart Features internal key) migrate from plaintext `ai_settings` + `config.json` to OS keychain (`ai_provider_key` / `ai_gateway_token` / `ai_internal_key`). Migration is copy-then-clear with read-back confirmation, idempotent (6 states A–F). `config.json` redaction: `apiKeyRef` becomes sentinel `"keychain"`, aiSettings dump blocklist excludes credential keys. Post-migration keychain miss = "not configured" (no plaintext fallback). Backup export includes three new accounts. 8 regression tests. (`spec-covered-by: #1500`, `Relates to #1008`)
- **#1444 — Settings: add `gateway_hostname` substitution to `startPairing()`.** When the OC gateway URL is an IP address, `gateway_fetch_fingerprint` returns the Tailscale hostname in `gateway_hostname` so TLS hostname verification succeeds. `Settings.svelte:startPairing()` now widens the `invoke` return type to include `gateway_hostname?: string` and rewrites `openclawUrl` to the hostname-based URL before proceeding, mirroring the pattern already present in `Onboarding.svelte:probeGatewayUrl()`. Substitution logic extracted into a shared helper `src/lib/utils/gateway.ts:substituteGatewayHostname()` to prevent future divergence. (`spec-covered-by: #1311`, `Relates to #1444`)
- **#956 — Frontend: Provider-switch agent re-import UI (§24.5.5).** `handleSaveAi()` now triggers the re-import flow when switching to OpenClaw from another provider. On collision, a warn-and-confirm modal pauses the save; the user can Overwrite (runs `reimport_oc_agents`, then completes the full save) or Cancel (reverts dropdown and fields, zero DB mutation, no error). Collision-free switches import silently and fall through to save. Implemented via `confirmReimport`/`cancelReimport` handlers and a state-gated modal following the `.modal-overlay` pattern. (`spec-covered-by: #1476`, `Relates to #956`)
- **#956 — Backend: Provider-switch agent re-import (§24.5.5).** When a customer switches the AI provider to OpenClaw in Settings, Pane now discovers and imports the gateway’s agents. Three new backend primitives in `sync_client.rs` and `ai/commands.rs`:
  - `fetch_gateway_agents(url, token, cert_pem)` — reusable helper that extracts the HTTP fetch + 3-attempt retry loop from `initial_sync`; `initial_sync` refactored to call it internally (zero behavior change on the onboarding path).
  - `sync_re_import(conn, url, token, cert_pem)` — executes the provider-switch import in a single transaction. Existing agents (matched by `oc_agent_id`) are overwritten in place via UPDATE (including `IDENTITY.md` — deliberate divergence from `sync_initial_import`’s `!exists` guard); new agents are fresh-imported (INSERT + new UUID dir). Slug collision on UPDATE → full rollback. `workspace_path` always sourced from the pre-queried DB row, never the gateway payload.
  - `check_oc_agent_collisions(url, token)` Tauri command — read-only; returns `{ collisions, new_agents }` with zero DB mutations or file writes.
  - `reimport_oc_agents(url, token)` Tauri command — mutating; self-contained (re-fetches and re-queries at execution time; shares no state with `check_oc_agent_collisions`). 12 unit tests. (`spec-covered-by: #1476`, `Relates to #956`)
- Settings: removed OC model auto-population from gateway catalog; model now sourced exclusively from agent registry (#935)
- Settings: removed orphaned OC model reactive effects and dead model-picker onboarding screen (#882)

- **#956 — `is_main` UNIQUE constraint collision during provider-switch reimport.** When switching from OpenRouter to OpenClaw, `sync_re_import` now demotes any existing agent holding `is_main=1` (e.g. an OR-onboarded agent with `oc_agent_id=NULL`) before inserting the OC main agent. The demotion runs inside the existing transaction, so it rolls back atomically if the INSERT fails. OC gateway is authoritative on who is main. Regression test T13 added (`test_reimport_demotes_or_main_on_oc_main_import`). (`Relates to #956`)
- **#1485 — Re-pair completion signal never reaches frontend.** Four-facet fix for a bug that left Pane's pairing UI frozen and chat blocked after a failed gateway re-pair:
  - **Fix 3 (backend, load-bearing):** `ai_configure_and_save` now captures `state.provider` before setting the pending-marker (`AiProvider::None`) and restores it on every error return path via a `ProviderRestoreGuard` drop-guard (Rust has no `finally`). Previously, any failure in `fetch_oc_agent_model` left the in-memory provider permanently as `AiProvider::None`, triggering the #1460 chat guard indefinitely until restart. Restores the ACTUAL previous provider (not unconditionally OpenClaw). Three regression tests added.
  - **Fix 1 (frontend):** `submitPairingCode()` now resets `pairingStep = 0` in both the `catch` block and the "0 models" else branch. Previously only the success path reset it, leaving the Step 3 spinner frozen on any failure.
  - **Fix 2 (frontend):** Step 3 of the pairing flow now renders `pairingError` if set and shows a Cancel button, matching the pattern of steps 0–2. Previously the step 3 block had no error display and no escape hatch.
  - **Fix 4 (frontend):** `savedConnectionStatus` is now reset to `'not-tested'` on re-pair failure, preventing the Gateway Status dot from showing stale green “Connected” from a prior successful pairing. (`Relates to #1485, #1445, #1460`)
- **#1481 — Slug-collision coexist + disambiguate in `sync_re_import` (§24.5.5).** When an incoming OC agent has no `oc_agent_id` match but its slug collides with an existing `ai_agents` row (including `oc_agent_id IS NULL`), the two agents now coexist: existing row is kept entirely untouched (no UPDATE, no file overwrite, no `oc_agent_id` adoption), and the incoming OC agent imports as its own new row with a disambiguated slug (numeric-increment-until-free: base → `-2` → `-3` → … until unused). A slug collision is a handled, expected condition and does **not** roll back the transaction. Intra-batch slug probe uses an in-memory `HashSet` (pre-populated from all existing DB slugs) so multiple agents in the same batch with the same base slug each receive a unique disambiguated slug. Replaces the prior rollback-on-collision behavior shipped in #1477. (`spec-covered-by: #1479 (§24.5.5)`, `Relates to #1481, #1480, #956`)
- **#956 — Backend test robustness (WARN-11A).** `sync_re_import` now accepts an optional `system_dir_override: Option<&Path>` parameter; production callers pass `None` (zero behavior change). T2 (`test_reimport_fresh_import_new_uuid`) and T7 (`test_reimport_slug_collision_rolls_back_all`) now use `tempfile::tempdir()` and pass `Some(dir.path())`, preventing spurious failures in sandboxed CI from attempting writes to `$HOME/Pane/`. All other test call sites updated for the new signature.
- Settings: Re-pair now validates gateway URL before attempting pairing — prevents flash on bad URL (#1446)
- Settings: renamed OC Test Gateway button to 'Save & Test' for clarity (#1442)
- Settings: added URL-format validation before saving OpenClaw gateway URL (#1446)
- Settings: handleTestConnection now validates empty/malformed URL on cascade-confirm path (#1442)
- Fixed false-green: ai_configure_and_save now always validates OC gateway connectivity even when model is pre-populated (#1446)
- Settings: 'Save & Re-pair' on OC URL change now actually triggers re-pairing instead of saving with stale token (#1445)
- Fixed async race in ai_configure_and_save where chat dispatched during OpenClaw model fetch could read stale credentials (401) (#1460)

- Settings: Re-pair button now surfaces gateway_fetch_fingerprint errors (#1450). Previously the error was set but never rendered because the display lived only in pairingStep=1/2 blocks.
- **#1453: OC model sync — sentinel-on-wire + reverse-channel propagation.** Pane's `ai_settings.model` cache drifted from OC's truth when a customer edited `openclaw.json` between Pane saves (the only prior refresh path was `fetch_oc_agent_model` at save time). Fix: (1) Pane's `stream_openrouter_inner` now forces `body["model"] = "openclaw"` on the OC gateway path before sending — wire-format hygiene, matches the gateway rewrite anyway; (2) the gateway emits `X-OC-Resolved-Model` on every 2xx `/v1/chat/completions` response, sourced from `agent_registry.get_agents()` (already computed for PARAM_COMPAT, zero extra lookups); (3) Pane reads that header after successful stream completion and writes the value to `ai_settings.model` + runtime `state.model` if it differs from the cached value. Invariants preserved: `ai_settings.model` is a display cache only and is never read in dispatch decisions; per-message chat badges are unchanged (#1448 invariant); `handleSaveAi` direct-synthesis path is untouched (#1449). (#1453, #1456, spec-covered-by: #1455 [§22C.6.7 + §27.6.1d])
- §22C.11A.2 + §22C.22.5 (sync.md): removed dead SameMachine spec residue. §22C.11A.2 loses its two `same_machine` error-state rows; §22C.22.5 loses its `Value at SameMachine completion` persistence column. SameMachine topology was removed in #1108; code residue was cleaned in #1441; this is the spec-side cleanup of the two sections that still carried SameMachine references. Deletion only — no contract change. Remaining `split_machine` rows/column intact. (#1122)
- §24.5.5 amendment (agents.md): provider-switch re-import slug-collision rule. When an incoming OpenClaw agent has no `oc_agent_id` match but its slug collides with any existing `ai_agents` row (including `oc_agent_id IS NULL` — the default path for every non-OC provider, since onboarding always creates one NULL-`oc_agent_id` main agent), the two agents now **coexist**: the pre-existing row is untouched, and the incoming OC agent imports as its own new row with a disambiguated slug (numeric-increment-until-free: base, then `-2`, `-3`, … until unused). The prior "slug collision → rollback" rule is **rewritten out** of every occurrence in §24.5.5 (transaction prose and, if present, the WARN-7A note) — rollback now applies only to genuine unexpected failures (DB/file-write/network), never to a slug collision. Precedence: `oc_agent_id` match → overwrite-in-place (unchanged); else slug collision → coexist + disambiguate (new); else → fresh import (unchanged). Closes a Reed-found gap in §24.5.5; supersedes the shipped #1477 rollback-on-collision behavior (T7 rewrites). Spec lands before the code fix cites it via `spec-covered-by:`. (#956)

- §24.5.5 (agents.md): Provider-switch agent re-import — when the AI provider is switched to OpenClaw in Settings (not onboarding), Pane discovers and imports gateway agents via a two-phase read-then-mutate command split (`check_oc_agent_collisions` read-only; `reimport_oc_agents` mutating). Existing agents are updated in place (same `id`, same UUID `workspace_path`, all files including `IDENTITY.md` overwritten from the gateway — deliberate divergence from `sync_initial_import`'s `!exists` guard, since the gateway is authoritative on switch-back); new agents are fresh-imported. `notes.agent_id` references are never broken — rows are UPDATEd, never DELETE+INSERTed. A warn-and-confirm modal fires on collision (Cancel aborts the entire switch and reverts the provider dropdown with zero DB mutation); net-new-only imports run silently. Spec lands before the #956 code fix cites it via `spec-covered-by:`. (#956)

- `docs/spec/smart-routing.md` §27.6.1b intro reframe + new §27.6.1d + `docs/spec/sync.md` §22C `X-OC-Resolved-Model` header contract + `docs/INVARIANTS.md` Smart Routing (§27) new cache-not-authoritative bullet: spec coverage for #1453 (OC model cache drift between Pane and OC after `openclaw.json` edits or provider switching, caused by `ai_settings.model` having only a save-time refresh path via `fetch_oc_agent_model` and no continuous-refresh channel). The normative contract is the **sentinel-on-wire + reverse-channel propagation** fix shape (Matt's locked decision 2026-06-11, on Reed v2's cost analysis): Pane sends `body["model"] = "openclaw"` on the OC chat path (matches the gateway rewrite — wire-format hygiene); gateway emits `X-OC-Resolved-Model` response header sourced from `agent_registry` (zero new lookups); Pane reads the header on successful stream completion and updates `ai_settings.model` if drifted — the continuous-refresh channel the cache was missing. §27.6.1b's "decorative at dispatch" intro framing replaced with "display cache, kept in sync via reverse channel" to match the contract. INVARIANTS.md bullet locks "stored OC model is a cache, never authoritative for dispatch" against future refactor pressure. No behavior change in this PR; spec lands before the #1453 code fix cites it via `spec-covered-by:`.

## [0.67.0] - 2026-06-10

### Added

- Compaction trigger now uses the override-aware context-window resolver instead of the seed-only `context_window_estimate` (#1405-G, Relates to #1324). With `context_window_override=1_000_000` and `compaction_trigger_pct=0.80`, compaction fires at 800K tokens — previously it incorrectly fired at ~102K (80% of the 128K seed floor). The trigger now uses the same three-input resolver path as the downstream `apply_budget` call.

- Eager `ModelRegistry` population on app startup via background async task spawned from Tauri `.setup()` immediately after `app.manage(ai_state)` (#1410, sub-issue of #1324). Returning users who reopen Pane and chat immediately (without visiting Settings) no longer hit seed-table fallback on every first turn — registry pre-warms within the first ~500ms of launch. New `populate_model_registry_from_provider` in `commands.rs` dispatches to existing inner fetch helpers by `AiProvider` variant; `AiProvider::None` returns `Ok(())` silently (first launch, no provider configured). `AiProvider::Ollama` values are stored as `None` per ADR-0043 §4 (on-demand fetch). Two `[startup]` log lines for DMG verification. Existing Settings/ProjectSettings panel-mount `fetch_available_models` invocations preserved (in-session refresh still needed).
- User context-window override UI in Settings AI Health tab (#1404-E, sub-issue of #1324). Non-OC setups get an editable numeric input (floor 50,000) pre-filled with the resolved context window value, an explicit "Clear override" button, and an "(estimated)" badge when the resolver fell back to the static seed table or 128k floor. OC setups remain read-only with the `.openclaw-locked-label` lock pattern ("Set in OpenClaw"). Backend: additive `is_estimated: bool` field on `BudgetResult`, populated via new `resolve_context_window_with_source()` wrapper that classifies the resolver's source tier without touching `get_context_window`, `apply_budget`, or `BudgetResult`'s existing logic. Per Matt's locked answers: Q1=A (pre-fill with resolved value, no extra invoke on mount), Q2=A (additive `is_estimated` field), Q3 (explicit Clear override button). Compaction trigger override-awareness deferred to #1405-G per scope. Implements spec §27.11.
- Percentage-based compaction trigger and `BudgetResult.tokens_demanded` field (#1403-D, sub-issue of #1324). Replaces the fixed `+12` message-count heuristic in `maybe_compact_thread` with a token-percentage check gated on `compaction_trigger_pct` (default 0.80, seeded in `database.rs`). Two-value design per Reed §2.5: coarse pre-budget estimate drives the trigger in `commands.rs`; precise `tokens_demanded` (full scan including excluded messages) lives on `BudgetResult` for Health dashboard / observability only — never crossed. Latency trigger untouched. References #1403, #1324.
- `get_context_window` async resolver with 5-level precedence chain (OpenClaw wire → user override → provider API → seed table → 128k floor), `Backend` enum, `ModelRegistry` per-session state, and cold/unknown registry-miss log markers (#1402-C, sub-issue of #1324). Migrates all `apply_budget` call sites to accept a pre-resolved `context_window: u64`; `apply_budget` remains sync.
- `ModelInfo.context_length` field captured from OpenRouter `/api/v1/models` (#1399, sub-issue of #1324). First of three independent deserializer fixes (#1399 OpenRouter, #1400 Ollama, #1401 Pane client) feeding the resolver refactor #1402.
- `get_ollama_context_window` sibling helper fetches per-model window via `/api/show` lazily (on first use), cached in-memory for the session (#1400, sub-issue of #1324). Second of three independent deserializer fixes (#1399 OpenRouter merged, #1400 Ollama — this PR, #1401 Pane client parallel) feeding the resolver refactor #1402-C.
- Pane client deserializes `context_window` from Pane Gateway `/v1/models` and maps to `ModelInfo.context_length` (#1401, sub-issue of #1324). Third of three independent deserializer fixes feeding the resolver refactor #1402-C.

### Fixed

- Anthropic billing errors (HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error` with "credit balance" message) now surface a clear billing CTA ("Insufficient Anthropic credits. Add credits at console.anthropic.com/settings/plans to continue.") instead of a cryptic API error string. Affects all four Anthropic call sites: `chat`, `chat_with_tools`, `stream_anthropic`, and `validate_anthropic_key`. (#968)
- #1145 — Onboarding: error messages no longer crowd Continue button (added `margin-bottom: 8px` to `.connect-error-msg` shared across onboarding screens)
- Gateway: gated `AgentRegistry::seed_agents` test seam behind `cfg(test)` / `test-utils` feature so it cannot be reached from production code (#1323 follow-up to Reed F1).
- Gateway PARAM_COMPAT now resolves real downstream model from agent_registry unconditionally, eliminating wrong-model strip when Pane's cached model string differs from OC config (#1323). Previously, the common path trusted Pane's `body["model"]` directly; if Pane's cache was stale (e.g. `claude-opus-4-6` while OC ran `claude-opus-4-7`), deprecated params slipped through to Anthropic, causing 422 errors. Gateway-only change; deploys via gateway rebuild + restart on the Studio — no Pane DMG required.

### Security

- Hardened sync ingest to reject path-traversal filenames via centralized `file_ops::safe_path_join` (#1300). Previously protected only incidentally by the allowlist filter; now explicit and enforced at every ingest call site (`pull_pending_changes_blocking`, `initial_sync`, `apply_migration_files`). Removes the old `contains("..")` check in `initial_sync` (subsumed by the helper). New INVARIANT §22C.18 #15 documents the filesystem sandbox requirement. Spec §22C.8.5 status table corrected to BUILT (ingest filter was already live since PR #1372 but the spec still said MISSING).

### Specification

- `docs/spec/ai-integration.md` §27.8–§27.11 amendment + ADR-0043 (#1324): Dynamic context window sourcing (resolver replaces hardcoded substring table; precedence: OC gateway → provider API → user override → static seed) and percentage-based compaction trigger (`tokens_demanded / window ≥ 0.80`, replaces `+12` message-count gap). Adds invariants 7–10 to §27.8. New backend keys `context_window_override` (global, non-OC only, floor 50k, clamp-to-max-when-known) and `compaction_trigger_pct` (global, default 0.80). OC gateway `/v1/models` dependency (§27.9.1) confirmed NOT emitted today — sub-issue #1324-F covers the gateway-side change; until landed, OC falls to 200k seed labeled "estimated".
- `docs/spec/onboarding.md` §6.6.3 amendment (#1295, #1341): error table network-error row updated to document real error passthrough + fallback copy; sync-screen text documents `[← Back]` alongside `[Retry]` with state-clearing semantics (clears `ocSyncError`, `ocSyncing`; preserves `ocFingerprint`, `ocCertPem`, `ocToken`).
- `docs/spec/onboarding.md` §6.3.1 Step 3 amendment (#1295): documents `[Retry] [← Back]` for model-fetch failure on BYOK flow, Back navigates to provider connect screen.
- ADR-0042: LWW tie-break resolves to Pane (source of truth), honoring the Pane-PRIMARY / OC-REPLICA model (ADR-0012, §0.3.3). Supersedes the inherited bridge behavior (gateway-wins on tie) that entered §22C.8.2 as one line in commit `57dab52da` without a decision artifact (#1299).
- §22C.8.2 amendment (sync.md): tie-break rule flipped from "Ties resolve to the gateway" to "Ties resolve to Pane"; heading updated from "LWW with gateway tie-break" to "LWW with Pane tie-break"; closing paragraph updated to document the inversion and cite #1299 + ADR-0042.
- §22C.11.2a amendment (sync.md): cross-reference flipped from "LWW with gateway tie-break" to "LWW with Pane tie-break" with citations to §22C.8.2 + ADR-0042.
- §22C.15 amendment (sync.md): test category 2 assertion flipped from "Tie-case asserts gateway wins" to "Tie-case asserts Pane wins" with citations.

### Fixed

- **Onboarding error screens now have a Back button (#1295).** The OpenClaw sync-error screen previously trapped users with only a Retry button — if Retry kept failing, the only escape was to quit and relaunch. Back now navigates to the pairing-code entry screen and clears the sync error state (pairing state is preserved). Same fix applied to the model-select error state, which Backs to the provider connect screen.
- **Pairing failures now show the real error instead of "Connection lost." (#1341).** Previously every non-classified pairing error (network failure, malformed response, gateway down) collapsed to the literal string `"Connection lost."`, hiding what actually went wrong. The catch block now passes through the real gateway error (e.g. `"Pairing failed: error sending request..."`) via a new `mapPairingError` helper. Empty errors fall back to actionable guidance.
- **Cross-machine sync no longer waits for app restart; pull now runs every 5 minutes via the same background thread that previously only ran flush (#1370).** The pull subsumes flush — one thread does both directions.

### Refactor

- `pull_pending_changes_blocking` signature now accepts `Option<&tauri::AppHandle>` and forwards it to the internal `flush_sync_queue_blocking` call. This preserves the `sync-failure` banner emission path that the frontend listens for at `src/routes/+layout.svelte:14`. (#1370)

### Fixed

- **LWW tie-break now applies on the live pull path — ADR-0042 real fix (#1299):** PR #1366 patched the shared `conflict_resolution` module (ADR-0042 compliant) but `pull_pending_changes_blocking` — the only function called from `lib.rs:945` on every app startup — had its own inline timestamp match that explicitly set `should_ingest = true` on tie ("gateway wins"). This PR routes `pull_pending_changes_blocking` through the shared module and deletes the dead async `pull_pending_changes` that had no callers. After this fix there is exactly one conflict-resolution path. spec-covered-by: ADR-0042.

- **LWW tie-break direction inverted to Pane-wins (#1299):** When `local_modified == remote_timestamp` to the millisecond, the conflict resolver now returns `KeepLocal` instead of `AcceptRemote`, preserving Pane's version on tie. Honors the Pane-PRIMARY / OC-REPLICA model (ADR-0012, §0.3.3). The original gateway-wins rule was inherited from the bridge plugin without a decision artifact (commit `57dab52da`); ADR-0042 (PR #1365) codifies the corrected direction. Matching unit test `test_case_5c_both_exist_timestamps_equal` flipped to assert `KeepLocal`. spec-covered-by: #1365.

- **UI freeze — periodic flush deadlock on shared DB mutex (#1180):** Two-part fix for the pinwheel-of-death freeze that appeared after extraction completed and triggered sync. Root cause: the periodic flush thread (`lib.rs:967`) held the shared `db.0` mutex across the entire blocking HTTP flush, while the startup sync path (`sync_client.rs:882`) tried to acquire the same mutex via `build_gateway_client_blocking(db)` — producing a deadlock logged as four stacked `[GATEWAY_CLIENT] Building blocking gateway client...` lines with no completion. Fix A: `pull_pending_changes_blocking` now uses `build_gateway_client_blocking_with_cert(cert_pem)` (cert pre-read from `conn`) instead of `build_gateway_client_blocking(db)`, eliminating the redundant mutex re-acquisition. Fix B: the periodic flush thread opens a fresh WAL-safe connection via `database::open_connection(None)` per iteration instead of locking the shared `db.0` across blocking HTTP — the shared mutex is never held during network I/O. Reed audit: `docs/audits/2026-06-02-freeze-cluster-1347-1180.md`.

- **Smart-route retry destructively overwrites partial streamed content (#1358):** When a long stream error mid-flight triggered the smart-route fallback (Fix 3 from PR #1359), the fallback provider completed successfully and its `onDone` overwrote the user's partially-streamed content in the DB via `saveAssistantMessage(same msgId)`. Fix A's partial persistence never ran because `onError` never fired. Reed's Option A (audit `2026-06-02-120s-cap-and-destructive-retry.md`): gate the smart-route retry with `partial_text.is_empty()`. Decode errors with non-empty partial text now fall through to the error path so Fix A's partial persistence runs and the user sees their partial content + error banner instead of a silent replacement.

- **Long OC streaming responses fail with decode error and partial-text loss (#1358):** Three coordinated fixes targeting the same failure chain:

  1. **Gateway idle timeout (Fix 1):** The gateway's reqwest client for streaming requests previously applied a 120-second *total* wall-clock timeout via `.timeout(120s)`. A 5,000-word Opus response with `max_tokens=16384` routinely exceeds 120 s even when bytes are flowing normally (confirmed by 118 s gap in Matt's log). The 120 s total timeout was replaced with a **per-chunk idle timeout**: the stream now lives as long as any byte arrives within the threshold; only a genuine stall (no bytes for N seconds) drops the connection. The threshold is configurable via `GATEWAY_STREAMING_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default: 60 s). Non-streaming requests retain the previous 60 s total timeout unchanged.

  2. **Persist partial text on stream error (Fix 2, end-to-end):** When a stream terminated with an error, partial text was lost on reload. Two-part fix: (a) **Backend** — `stream_openrouter_inner` now returns the partial text accumulated before the failure alongside the error (return type changed from `Err(String)` to `Err((error_message, partial_text))`). The agentic loop in `commands.rs` appends this partial to `accumulated_text` before emitting the error event, so `fullText` in the error payload contains real content rather than an empty string. (b) **Frontend** — `streamManager.ts` `onError` callback forwards `fullText`, `toolCalls`, and `tool_results` from the error event. If `fullText` is non-empty, `ChatSidebar.svelte` displays it as `{partial}\n\n---\n⚠ {error}` and persists the message to the database via the same `saveAssistantMessage` path used by successful streams. Empty `fullText` retains the banner-only behaviour. Display logic extracted to `$lib/utils/streamErrorContent.ts` so component and tests call the same implementation.

  3. **Classify decode error as transient (Fix 3):** The error string `"error decoding response body"` (reqwest's representation of a TCP stream closed mid-body) was not matched by `is_transient_error()` in `commands.rs`, so the smart-route fallback path never fired for this error class. Added `"error decoding response body"` to the transient set so the fallback-to-primary-provider logic is eligible when this error occurs.

- **Chat streaming UI freeze — keychain blocking call (#1347):** `auth_check_entitlement` (the Tauri command invoked at launch and on-focus) was calling `get_auth_session()` synchronously on the tokio async executor thread. `get_auth_session` reads the macOS Keychain via `security_framework::get_generic_password`, a blocking syscall. When a chat stream was active, this blocked the executor thread, stalling SSE delta emission and producing the macOS beachball. Fix: wrapped the `get_auth_session()` call inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` so the blocking Keychain I/O runs on a dedicated blocking thread, freeing the executor to continue streaming. Identified in Reed's audit `docs/audits/2026-06-02-freeze-cluster-1347-1180.md`.

- **Onboarding URL hotfix (#1345):** `fetch_oc_agent_model` no longer produces `/v1/v1/agents`. The resolver from PR #1340 was fetching `https://{host}/v1/v1/agents` — a doubled path — because `normalize_api_endpoint` had already appended `/v1` to the stored `base_url`, and `fetch_oc_agent_model` then appended `/v1/agents` on top. Fix: (1) new `oc_agents_url()` helper strips any trailing `/v1` before appending `/v1/agents` — defence-in-depth for user-entered URLs and future callers; (2) `ai_configure_and_save` now passes the raw user endpoint to `fetch_oc_agent_model` instead of the `/v1`-normalised `base_url`. Unit test `test_oc_agents_url_no_double_v1` covers bare, trailing-slash, already-suffixed `/v1`, and `/v1/` inputs.

- **Sync push deadlock (#1350):** In-app autosave edits now reach the gateway immediately.
  The autosave path had been silently dead since commit `7776bd4d` (May 4 cert-pinning refactor).
  Root cause: `trigger_sync`'s background thread wrapped its fresh `rusqlite::Connection` in a
  `DbState(Mutex::new(conn))`, immediately locked it, then passed `&db_state` to
  `sync_push_blocking`, which called `build_gateway_client_blocking(db)`, which tried to
  re-lock the same non-reentrant `std::sync::Mutex` on the same thread — hanging forever.
  Fix (Option 2): extract `gateway_tls_cert_pem` before locking, add
  `build_gateway_client_blocking_with_cert(cert_pem: Option<String>)` that takes no `DbState`,
  update `sync_push_blocking` to accept `cert_pem` directly. The background thread now reads
  all config from its plain `Connection`, never wraps it in a mutex, and calls the `_with_cert`
  variant. No lock is held during the HTTP call. Local autosaves push immediately.

### Fixed
- **Root-cause fix for opus-4-7 onboarding failure (v0.65.74):** In OC mode, Pane now reads the AI model from `GET /v1/agents` on the gateway instead of falling back to a hardcoded `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6` literal. The hardcoded default caused onboarding to route requests through the wrong model (one the gateway had no strip-rule for), letting `temperature` pass through to Anthropic, which rejected it. Now the stored model matches the gateway's real agent model (e.g. `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7`), the gateway's existing strip rule fires, and onboarding completes successfully. Zero fallback strings — if the gateway can't provide a model, onboarding fails with a clear error rather than silently completing with a wrong model. CI guard G3 flipped from report → fail mode as the regression guard. (#1322)

### Fixed
- **Launch-blocking (gateway v0.2.1):** Gateway now negotiates the OC WebSocket protocol using a broad range declaration (`minProtocol: 3, maxProtocol: 99`) instead of the exact `3,3` that caused handshake rejection after OC bumped to protocol v4. This is the durable fix: OC's server uses an inclusive range check, so `max=99` continues to work when OC bumps to v5, v6, etc. without further code changes. Named constants `OC_PROTOCOL_MIN = 3` and `OC_PROTOCOL_MAX = 99` replace the three inline literals in `oc_client.rs`. (#1336)
- **CI guard G6:** Forbids `minProtocol`/`maxProtocol`/`protocol` integer literals in `src-gateway/src/` at `fail` mode, **including test modules** (a test that hardcodes `"protocol": 3` is a blind spot when the production constant bumps). Prevents regression to the same outage class. Two unit tests added to `scripts/ci-guards/tests/run-tests.sh` (14/14 total). (#1336)

### Fixed
- **Build determinism:** `src-tauri/Cargo.lock` is now tracked in git (previously gitignored), preventing Cargo from silently upgrading Tauri crates between builds on the same commit. `@tauri-apps/cli` exact-pinned to `2.10.0` in `package.json` (was `^2.10.0`); prevents contaminated-install builds from pulling 2.11.x CLI which enforces stricter minor-version parity. `@tauri-apps/api` bumped to `2.11.0` and `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog` to `2.7.1` to align with Rust-resolved `tauri 2.11.2` + `tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.1`. Both Rust crates now exact-pinned in `Cargo.toml` (`=2.11.2`, `=2.7.1`). Version-parity rule documented in Dev Hygiene Playbook Appendix F. Eliminates the drift class that caused v0.65.71 and v0.65.73 build failures. (#1318)

### Fixed
- **Launch-blocking (gateway):** Gateway now strips `temperature` and `top_p` from requests to models that reject them (e.g., `claude-opus-4-7`) before forwarding to OC. Completes the opus-4-7 onboarding fix: PR #1326 raised the token cap; this PR (#1323) removes the sampling params that Anthropic deprecated. Both are required — neither alone is sufficient. Gateway bumped to v0.2.0. (#1323)
- New module `src-gateway/src/param_compat.rs` owns the strip table, loaded from `~/.pane-gateway/param-compat.json` at startup (no gateway rebuild needed to add a new model). Bundled default covers `claude-opus-4-7` (exact) and `claude-opus-4-8+` (prefix) for both bare and provider-prefixed model IDs. Strip happens BEFORE the §22C model-overwrite so the real model name is still visible. (#1323)

### Fixed
- **Launch-blocking:** Streaming paths (`stream_openrouter`, `stream_anthropic`) now honor `temperature` and `max_tokens` from the request struct instead of hardcoded literals. Fixes the `claude-opus-4-7` onboarding failure (`LLM request rejected: temperature is deprecated for this model`) and removes the 4096-token silent truncation cap on all streaming responses. New cap: 16384 tokens. (#1321)
- 12 call sites across `openrouter.rs`, `anthropic.rs`, `commands.rs`, `consolidator.rs`, and `openclaw.ts` refactored: all sampling params now live in named constants at the caller/policy layer — never hardcoded in the provider layer. G1 (temperature literals) and G2 (max_tokens streaming literals) CI guards flipped from report → fail. (#1321)

### Added
- CI guards G1–G5: mechanical enforcement against hardcoded model strings, sampling parameters, and context-window literals. All five guards land in report-only mode (build never fails); downstream PRs #1321, #1322, #1324 flip their guards to blocking as violations are cleaned up. Guard runner: `scripts/ci-guards/run-guards.sh`. 12 unit tests in `scripts/ci-guards/tests/run-tests.sh`. Documented in Dev Hygiene Playbook Appendix E. (#1320)

### Fixed
- Sync no longer re-pushes files immediately after pulling them from the gateway — ingest writes now use `WriteOrigin::Remote` which suppresses `trigger_sync`, breaking the ping-pong loop (ingest → re-push → ingest) that caused 224 re-push attempts per full sync (#1298)
- TLS hostname mismatch no longer causes chat failures or UI freezes — Pane now reads the Tailscale hostname from the gateway's /v1/health response during pairing and rewrites the gateway URL to use it, so all subsequent calls use the correct hostname for TLS verification (#1305)
- Gateway TLS handshake now succeeds with Let's Encrypt certificates — built-in system roots re-enabled alongside pinned cert so the full LE chain (leaf → E8 → ISRG Root X1) can validate (#1305)
- Embedding pipeline no longer blocks the UI — uses its own DB connection instead of the app's shared mutex (#1306)
- Onboarding sync no longer freezes the UI — `sync_initial_import` converted from blocking to async (#1296)
- Sync allowlist enforced on all four sync surfaces (ADR-0041): gateway push-receive rejects non-allowlisted files; gateway read uses role-based filter; Pane initial-sync and incremental-pull ingest both enforce allowlist; push enforces depth-1 for memory/ and logs/
- BOOTSTRAP.md added to IDENTITY_WHITELIST
- Sub-agents sync only 6 files (SOUL, MEMORY, IDENTITY, AGENTS, USER, TOOLS) — no memory/, logs/, HEARTBEAT, BOOTSTRAP, or RULES
- ADR-0040 (#1278): Gateway `get_agent_workspace()` no longer uses hardcoded `~/.openclaw/workspaces/{tenant}/{agent}` path. Workspace paths are now resolved from OC's `agents.list` response `workspace` field via the agent registry. Missing or empty workspace returns HTTP 500. Both `/v1/sync/push` and `/v1/sync/initial` use the same mechanism. Sub-agents resolved identically.
- ADR-0040 migration (#1278): On first launch with `provider=openclaw` + `split_machine` topology, Pane runs a one-shot migration that overwrites stub files (created by the old placeholder) with real content from the gateway.

- Memory Settings delete propagation: deleting a routed fact now immediately removes its bullet from the memory file via the router's remove-bullet path (#674)

- Memory Router: deterministic file-based routing of unrouted facts to agent MEMORY.md or project Memory notes per §5.5.1 routing table - no LLM, millisecond latency, idempotent appends, per-file mutexes, word-count-triggered consolidator, remove-bullet path for inactive facts (#670)
- AI greeting: first-time users receive personalized introduction from AI after onboarding (#568)
- CI: skip rust-tests on docs-only PRs - workflow now uses path filter to prevent unnecessary test runs (#651)
- CI: label gate - `reed-reviewed` (and future matt-only labels) auto-removed if applied by anyone other than Matt, with comment explaining why (#627)
- Spec: §27 Context Budget State - full spec section documenting budget allocation, cache-aware change detection, window state preservation, and invariants (#658)

- Spec: §5.6 rewritten per ADR-0010 - append-only invariant, audit-entry markers (`[saved]`, `[memory edited]`, `[memory deleted]`), pattern-based extraction filter, end-of-day agent locked (3-6 sentence header, exact-match dedup, mechanical fallback, no pruning)
- Spec: §5.7/§5.12 rewritten per ADR-0010 - writer ownership table, read-only editor for memory/daily notes, Memory Settings as write surface, `goal` in manual save picker, edit/delete propagation across staged/routed/consolidated stages

- Extraction filter: lines containing audit markers (`[saved]`, `[memory edited]`, `[memory deleted]`) are filtered before LLM extraction to prevent circular re-extraction (#673)
- Extraction threshold lowered from 8 to 5 words per §5.4A (#647)
- Editor: read-only banner now displays type-specific write-surface guidance per §5.7.2 - "Edit in Memory Settings" for memory notes, "Managed by the memory pipeline" for daily logs, "Created during onboarding. View in Agents settings." for soul/rules/identity/user/tools (#675)

- Reed Gate now covers `.github/workflows/` - CI gate files require Reed review to modify, closing the self-referential gap. (#612)

- Fix model input validation: trim whitespace, strip trailing punctuation, validate format (#579)
